Members clean and re-cut the lettering themselves rather than employing crews, an arrangement defended on principle and complained about constantly. Vaelris walks it often and can explain what a marker meant when it was set. Residents slow down as they pass, a habit taught so early that most no longer notice doing it.

Orvantis Family Hall.description: The formal seat of the house, a layered compound hall used for receptions, internal councils and the ceremonies that mark a competitor's entry into the bracket. Its furnishings are old and repeatedly restored rather than renewed. The hall is heavy stone with bronze-black fittings, its upper gallery open to the wind on one side, and the floor carries the scuffing of generations of the same gatherings. Bostarix works the procedural side from here, preparing registration papers, medical disclosures and challenge language well before anyone at the Arena asks for them. Guests are seated by relationship to the house, and everyone present understands the seating.

Weathered Training Court.description: The quarter's main training floor, its surfacing marked by decades of impact and patched in visibly different materials. Instruction here emphasizes form and endurance over spectacle, in the style the house has always taught. The court is open to the sky with a low stone parapet and a windward baffle that does not quite do its job, and the oldest rig mountings have been re-anchored so many times the stone around them is a mosaic. Sessions start early, run to a fixed order and finish with the floor swept by whoever trained last. Younger members complain the court is outdated; nobody has been permitted to resurface it.

Ancestor Stone Gallery.description: A sheltered gallery of inscribed stones recording Orvantis competitors, their results and the terms of their defeats as carefully as their wins. Losing cleanly earns a stone here, which explains a great deal about the house. The gallery is cut back into the terrace, out of the wind, lit dimly and lined floor to ceiling, with the oldest inscriptions worn to the point of argument about what they say. Vaelris keeps the records that explain them, is willing to admit the house's failures, and will show a visitor an entry the rest of the family would rather discuss less. Members bring children through it before their first bracket appearance. Visitors are usually surprised by how many of the inscriptions commemorate losing.

Quiet Recovery Garden.description: A sheltered planted court behind the training floor, screened from the wind and used for slow rehabilitation and slower conversations. Injured members recover here rather than in the public yards when the house can arrange it. The planting is old, the benches are stone with worn wooden slats, and the screening walls cut the noise of the quarter down to something distant. Melqara spends time here when she is not on the practice platform, and the conversations that happen on these benches tend to be the ones the house cannot have in the hall. It is the one part of the quarter that was never built to be seen.

Sophira’s Practice Platform.description: A private training deck extended out over the terrace edge, in near-constant use. Sophira works here on approaches the family hall would call unorthodox, against an inherited standard she has no interest in meeting quietly. The platform is newer than anything around it, braced underneath with plain storm-metal that nobody has troubled to finish in house colors, and it is exposed to the wind on three sides because she prefers it that way. Melqara trains here under her, pushed hard and pushed deliberately, and the two of them disagree about whether the house should be restored or become something else. The rig mountings have been replaced twice in a year.

Hasdrovex’s Corner Table.description: A fixed table at the junction of the honor walk and the hall approach, occupied nearly every day. Much of what the house actually decides is settled here, in conversation, without record. The table is old stone with a bench on the sheltered side, positioned where everyone entering the quarter passes within speaking distance, and Hasdrovex holds it through most of the day with food, company and no apparent agenda. He softens conflicts started by pride or intensity elsewhere in the house, and has stopped arguing with Sophira about whether peace is surrender. Anyone hoping to reach Orvantis leadership is usually told to speak at this table first.

Hannovar’s Viewing Balcony.description: An elevated balcony overlooking the training court and the drop toward the Arena traffic beyond it. Hannovar watches from here most days, commenting rarely and precisely. The balcony is cut from the same old stone as the hall, fitted with a single heavy chair and a rail that has been repaired rather than replaced, and it faces the court squarely so that nothing on the floor happens outside his view. He appears in the weekly bracket as a matter of family and civic obligation, never misses a week, and never rewrites a loss into an excuse. Younger members have learned to read his silences, which is not the same as agreeing with them.

Zelvaris Quarter.name: Zelvaris Quarter
Zelvaris Quarter.basicInfo: Zelvaris Quarter feels like a district converted into a training engine, set into Korrvane's lower-middle civic layers where ordinary flight traffic and the nearby Lower Descent Routes keep training and recovery infrastructure close at hand. Walls, platforms, schedules, food routines and sleep spaces are all organized around closing the Genesis gap. The tone is focused, dense and exhausting, and the house is respected for it. The building stock is dark, reinforced and instrumented, stone frames filled with storm-metal and fitted with measuring equipment wherever a load can be recorded, and the district reads as a single working facility rather than a set of separate buildings. Losses are treated as information, which produces admirable discipline and a culture where rest can feel like failure. The Recovery Grind Benches connect directly through to the Zelvaris Recovery Annex in the Recovery Yards, so rehabilitation is part of the daily geography rather than an afterthought. Ordinary life continues around the training: families cook and eat on the posted schedule, children do homework beside a metrics display, and residents with unrelated occupations walk past a session they have watched a hundred times. The house has come closer to pressuring the Genesis ladder than any other, and the quarter is built around the belief that the distance is measurable.
Zelvaris Quarter.hiddenInfo: Zelvaris measures everything, and the measuring is both the house's strength and its danger. The Combat Data Archive holds match analysis on competitors across every district, which other houses find useful, unnerving and occasionally worth acquiring by less than honest means. Recovery is built into the quarter's geography rather than treated as an afterthought: the Recovery Grind Benches connect directly to the Zelvaris Recovery Annex in the Recovery Yards, and Eshmunar moves between the two. That integration is what keeps the house's brutal training loads survivable, and the arguments about where the line sits are constant. Magara's platform pushes contenders past what trainers elsewhere would allow, and Barcavon's method court is where that approach is defended in front of anyone who questions it. Hamilvar observes and records more than he says. The house's ambition is genuine and its evidence is real, but nobody in the quarter has yet produced a result that proves the method works at the top, and everyone here knows exactly how many weeks it has been.

Barcavon’s Method Court.description: The quarter's central training floor, where Barcavon's system is taught, defended and revised in front of whoever is watching. Sessions are structured to the minute and posted in advance. The court is enclosed on three sides by instrumented walls, its floor divided into marked working zones, and the schedule board at the entrance carries the day in order with names against each block. Barcavon runs sessions personally, rebuilds his methodology when the results say to, and treats a defeat as the start of the next revision rather than as an ending. Abdesara trains here under him while studying someone else's patience more closely. Visitors expecting brutality find something closer to a laboratory with impact damage.

Impact Metrics Hall.description: An instrumented hall where strikes, landings and flight loads are measured against recorded baselines. Displays render a fighter's week as curves that do not flatter anyone. The equipment is mounted into structural stone so the readings stay honest, the hall is lit evenly and coldly, and the noise is a repeating sequence of impact and recorded tone that residents outside have long stopped hearing. Trainees book slots, run their sets and take the output to whoever is going to argue with them about it. Civilians from the quarter use the hall too, for conditioning that has nothing to do with a bracket. Trainees argue with the numbers and then, almost always, adjust to them.

Magara’s Burn Platform.description: An exposed conditioning deck built for loads that other houses' trainers would refuse to supervise. Magara runs it personally and her sessions end when the measurements say so, not when anyone asks. The platform stands out from the quarter's face on heavy bracing, fully open to the wind, with the loads racked along the sheltered side and nothing else on the deck at all. Magara treats almost every contender in the city as a personal rival and would attempt the ladder far more often than anyone thinks wise. Eshmunar has removed people from this deck, and she resents him most when he turns out to be right. The platform's edge railing is one of the few in Korrvane that people actually use.

Hamilvar’s Observation Room.description: A glassed room overlooking the method court and metrics hall, fitted with recording equipment and a wall of running analysis. Hamilvar watches from here and says considerably less than he writes down. The glass is the heavy reinforced kind used on the outer balconies, the room is deliberately dim so the displays read clearly, and the notes covering the wall are organized by opponent rather than by date. Hamilvar studies a rival for weeks before entering a bout and prefers being underestimated, since reputation only gives an opponent usable data. Tannivar works beside him often, and the two of them agree that preparation beats spectacle. Being asked up to this room is either a promotion or a problem.

Recovery Grind Benches.description: Rehabilitation benches worked into the quarter's daily schedule rather than kept apart from it, connecting directly to the Zelvaris Recovery Annex in the Recovery Yards. Recovery here is treated as training, with its own loads and its own measurements. The benches sit in a half-sheltered bay with the loads racked overhead and the schedule posted alongside the training board, so a rest block appears in the day exactly the way a session does. Eshmunar oversees the floor, blunt about what he did to his own body trying to close the gap too quickly, and willing to end someone's week outright. Nobody is allowed to skip it, including the people who want to.

Combat Data Archive.description: A dense records chamber of match analysis, opponent profiles and historical bracket data covering every district in the city. Access is controlled and the controls are the subject of ongoing suspicion elsewhere. The chamber is cut back out of the wind, cool and quiet, its shelving and slate racks running deeper than the room first appears, with a reading table at the center that is never entirely clear. Tannivar works here, tracking footage, timing, flight paths and recovery rates, and may understand Alcandrus's public habits better than Alcandrus does. What the archive holds on Genesis ladder attempts is the collection's real centerpiece.

Challenger Sleep Barracks.description: Shared sleeping quarters built to a schedule, with rest treated as a measurable input like any other. Lighting and noise are controlled and the rotations are posted alongside the training board. The room is plain, warm, screened against the wind and fitted with bunks set far enough apart that one person's schedule does not wreck another's. Abdesara keeps to the rotation with a discipline the older contenders admire and do not always match, and the argument about whether the system produces recovery or merely records it never entirely stops. Outsiders find the arrangement bleak; the residents find the alternative slower.

The Rebuild Table.description: A long working table where a fighter's approach is taken apart and reassembled after a defeat, with the archive and the metrics both open. The conversation is unsparing and nobody leaves it without a revised plan. The table is heavy stone with a scarred working surface, set where the archive and the method court both open onto it, and the seating puts the fighter where everyone can see the record as clearly as they can. Sessions run long and arguments get loud, and the house admits openly that progress is incremental and costly rather than sudden. Food arrives partway through because nobody is leaving. It is the most feared and most valued fixture in the quarter.

Caelthorn Quarter.name: Caelthorn Quarter
Caelthorn Quarter.basicInfo: Caelthorn Quarter is the cleanest district in Korrvane, set into the mid-level civic band near formal tournament and civic traffic but outside the institutions that govern either. Nothing appears out of place and nothing is technically wrong. The tone is polished, pleasant and exact, and most visitors leave more suspicious than they arrived. The facings are polished black and ivory with silver detailing, the proportions are deliberately slightly asymmetric, and the banners are tensioned so they move less than anyone else's in the same wind. Maintenance happens before damage is visible, which means the quarter shows none of the impact marks that read as ordinary everywhere else in the city. The house does not describe itself as dishonest: its members find exact boundaries, exploit allowances, control wording and weaponize social expectation, and the tournament has reviewed those methods repeatedly and left the house eligible, which frustrates the city more than a clear verdict would. Business here runs through reception, filing and quiet conversation rather than through the training floor, though the house competes and wins. Caelthorn is sometimes simply correct, and that is the part rivals find hardest. Everything requested is logged, acknowledged and answered, and nobody leaves with quite what they came for.
Caelthorn Quarter.hiddenInfo: The quarter sits beside the procedures it studies and exploits rather than inside them, which is the entire design. Adherix's archive holds every version of every Arena rule, including the superseded language that can still be argued from, and the Legal Challenge Office turns that reading into filings that arrive at the Judges' Dais already complete. Caelthorn regularly challenges seeding language, and the running debate in The Ascent over whether the house should remain tournament-eligible is not idle. Giscara's reception hall converts civic access into obligation without ever naming a price, and the Quiet Agreement Rooms exist so that the resulting arrangements leave no public trace. Favor trading and blackmail both operate here in forms that stay carefully inside the rules. The visible fracture is Sophavel, whose discomfort with the house's methods is genuine and whose quiet connection with Vaelris Orvantis crosses a line his family would not sanction. The most difficult cases involving this quarter are the ones where Caelthorn is technically correct and still clearly awful.

Polished Rule Court.description: The quarter's central court, immaculate and precisely proportioned, used for formal receptions and demonstration sparring conducted strictly by the book. The surfacing shows no impact marks at all, which in Korrvane is a statement. The stone is polished black with ivory inlay marking the legal boundaries of a declared space, the lighting is even from every angle, and an official from elsewhere in the city is usually invited to observe so that the correctness is witnessed. Demonstrations stop precisely on the stated condition, and the house points this out afterward. Everything about the space is correct and slightly cold.

Giscara’s Reception Hall.description: A warm, expertly arranged hall where Giscara receives officials, rivals and anyone who might one day be useful. Hospitality here is genuine in execution and instrumental in purpose. The seating is grouped for conversations that can be overheard selectively, the refreshments are excellent, and Giscara never raises her voice or arrives without an account of where she has been. Tanithra works the same room, remembering who owes a favor, who attended which gathering and who needs something they cannot ask for publicly. Guests leave feeling well treated and faintly indebted, without being able to point to the moment it happened.

Adherix’s Rule Archive.description: A tightly organized archive of Arena rules, civic ordinances and every superseded revision of both, cross-indexed for argument rather than for history. Adherix can produce the governing language on any dispute within minutes. The room is lined with slate racks and reading stands, silent, precisely lit, and organized on a scheme that only makes sense once someone explains that it is arranged by use rather than by date. Adherix builds strategies from what is permitted rather than what is expected, has never technically broken a rule, and finds the city's frustration genuinely funny. Magozra works here beside him, already brilliant and already irritating to officials. The superseded shelves are the ones that matter most.

Legal Challenge Office.description: A working office that drafts objections, eligibility challenges and formal protests for filing at the Judges' Dais. Submissions leave here complete, correctly worded and difficult to dismiss quickly. Baalrix runs the office, handling challenge language, sponsorship conditions and match conditions, and is polite enough about all of it to make people furious. Drafts are checked against the archive before they go anywhere, filings are timed to land when the officials have room to consider them properly, and the office turns tactics into durable procedure rather than temporary tricks. Clerks from other houses have been known to come in and quietly ask for help.

Witness Balcony.description: A viewing balcony with clear sightlines over the rule court and the civic routes beyond, used to observe proceedings and to be observed observing them. Statements made from here carry weight because they were made in the open. The balcony is narrow, railed in silver-finished metal and positioned where anyone below can see exactly who is standing on it, which is the whole of its design. House members come out to be present at a moment they intend to reference later, and the timing of an appearance is understood by everyone watching. Other houses have learned to check the balcony before saying anything on the court below. Nothing said on this balcony is ever accidental.

Quiet Agreement Rooms.description: Small, sound-isolated rooms where arrangements are reached that neither party wishes to place on record. The furnishings are comfortable and entirely unremarkable by design. There is nothing on the walls, nothing to identify one room from another, and no record kept of who used which and when. Tanithra uses them for favors that would embarrass someone if requested in the reception hall, and terms leave as an understanding rather than as a document. The doors are heavy, the ventilation is quiet, and the corridor outside is arranged so that two arrivals never meet. Guests are shown in separately and leave by different routes, which everyone involved understands as courtesy.

Sophavel’s Side Garden.description: A small planted court off the main approach, kept deliberately informal and largely unvisited by the rest of the house. Sophavel is usually here when she is not required elsewhere. The planting is untidy by the quarter's standards, the seating is mismatched, and the wind reaches it, which is the first thing a visitor notices after the rest of the district. She competes because she is Caelthorn and wins because the methods work, and she remains uncomfortable with the way those victories are engineered. Her quiet respect for Vaelris Orvantis points at a different definition of dignity. It is the only place in the quarter where a conversation can be genuinely off the record.

The Courtesy Desk.description: The quarter's public front counter, staffed at all hours by attendants who are unfailingly helpful and unfailingly precise about what they can and cannot do. Requests are logged, routed and acknowledged in writing. The counter is ivory stone with a silver rail, the ledgers are kept in plain view, and an attendant will read back the exact wording of a request before accepting it. Complaints receive the same careful treatment as inquiries, and arrive back later phrased in a way that makes them difficult to repeat. Nobody is ever refused here; they are simply directed somewhere that will refuse them properly.

Aevon Quarter.name: Aevon Quarter
Aevon Quarter.basicInfo: Aevon Quarter barely touches the ground. It occupies the open space between Korrvane's major city layers, a lattice of suspended terraces, drift rings and marker gardens that expresses the city's vertical design more clearly than any other district. The tone is beautiful, exposed and fast, and it is frankly inconvenient for anyone who cannot fly. The structures are pale stone and bronze-trimmed storm-metal shaped to shed wind rather than block it, hung on cables and bracing that read as deliberate rather than temporary, with almost nothing enclosed and very little railed. The house turned the city's three-dimensional design into a complete combat and social identity, and its members read altitude, descent, wake pressure and traffic flow better than anyone else in Korrvane. That mastery is justified in open sky and vulnerable the moment an opponent forces them onto the ground. Ordinary life happens at height too: families live here, deliveries arrive in the air, children are taught to hold position before they are taught anything else, and couriers stage out of the terraces between jobs. The quarter is reachable by lift for visitors, deliveries and residents who need it, which some members treat as basic hospitality and others as a concession they resent. The wind markers are checked before every launch, by everyone.
Aevon Quarter.hiddenInfo: The quarter's aerial superiority is real and so is the cost of it. Aevon seating at the Arena sits on high open-air platforms that non-fliers struggle to reach, and the same logic shapes the district itself, which means the house is constantly negotiating its relationship with the two-thirds of Korrvane that stays on decking. The Non-Flier Waiting Lift exists as a concession and is treated by some residents as an apology they never agreed to make. Yadira's courier work gives the house detailed knowledge of routes across the entire city, including cuts that officially do not exist, and that knowledge is worth more than most of the quarter's visible assets. Elissara's speed run and Magonex's drift ring host informal contests whose results circulate faster than any bracket. The Sky Etiquette School teaches lane courtesy to visitors and locals alike, and its instructors privately regard that teaching as the quarter's real civic defense: every serious lane obstruction investigation raises the question of whether Aevon's routes are safe for the people flying beneath them.

Open-Sky Terrace.description: The quarter's main gathering terrace, a broad platform with no walls and very little railing, open to the wind on every side. Residents land and launch from it continuously without breaking conversation. The decking is pale stone over storm-metal bracing, warm underfoot in the afternoon, with landing marks worn into the most-used approaches and seating arranged so nobody's descent path crosses a table. Yadira Aevon stages her courier teams from here, handing out urgent runs and bracket notices and leaving a conversation halfway through when a route calls. First-time visitors tend to stand near the middle and stay there.

Spiral Descent Court.description: A helical arrangement of stepped platforms descending through the open gap between city layers, used for controlled descents and as the quarter's main route downward. The spiral is lit at each turn so fliers can judge the pitch at speed. The platforms are narrow, cantilevered and staggered so that a descent has to be flown rather than simply fallen through, and observation points at the outer turns let instructors watch a student take it in stages. Couriers use it as a working route between the layers, and the emergency descent path alongside is kept clear regardless of what else is happening. Watching a practiced Aevon take it is a local entertainment.

Bomilvar’s High Platform.description: The highest fixed platform in the quarter, from which Bomilvar oversees the district's traffic and its reputation. Approaches are steep and deliberately unforgiving. The platform is small, finished in bronze-trimmed pale stone and set where the wind is least predictable, with a single seating group facing outward across the whole vertical district. Bomilvar treats open-sky movement as an art, controls angle, altitude and timing with calm precision, and has declined repeated invitations to ground-based refinement sessions without ever quite saying no. Being received here means having flown the approach correctly, which is the first half of the conversation.

Elissara’s Speed Run.description: A marked straight-line course threading the quarter's structures, timed by beacon and run constantly by anyone with something to prove. Elissara holds the standing time and shows no interest in surrendering it. The course markers are set through gaps that punish a wide line, the timing beacons are mounted where a runner has to commit before seeing the next one, and attempts are logged on a board at the start that is amended more often than it is cleaned. Elissara wins through velocity rather than elegance, has been corrected on her form many times, and has not changed it because she keeps winning. Challengers announce themselves by simply appearing at the start marker.

Magonex’s Drift Ring.description: A circular training volume exploiting the standing updraft between two city layers, used for control work rather than speed. Magonex teaches sustained drift and precise positioning here, skills that win aerial matches slowly. The volume is defined by suspended beacons and by the updraft itself, which residents can feel long before they can see where it begins, and sessions run at a pace that looks like nothing at all from the terraces above. He denies approach angles, controls spacing and lets opponents exhaust themselves chasing him, and he is the member most willing to work with a trainee on grounded patience. The ring is marked by suspended beacons that shift with the wind.

Wind-Marker Gardens.description: Planted terraces set with long streamers and drift indicators that read the shifting air across the quarter. They are functional instruments and genuinely beautiful, which Aevon considers the same achievement. The terraces step down through the open gap in shallow tiers, each set of markers calibrated to a different band, so a glance across them gives the state of the air at several altitudes at once. Children are brought here to learn what the markers mean before they are allowed to launch from anywhere, and older residents sit among them simply because it is the quietest place in the district. Residents check them by reflex before every launch.

Non-Flier Waiting Lift.description: The single reinforced lift serving visitors, deliveries and residents who cannot make the quarter's approaches on their own. It is slow, well maintained and frequently crowded. The housing is heavy storm-metal anchored back into the nearest city layer, the waiting bay is sheltered and benched, and the maintenance record is kept where anyone can read it because the house will not be accused of neglecting the one route in. Hannoq is regularly stationed here and resents the association, being a legitimate aerial prospect whose objection is to ground work rather than to the lift. Some residents treat it as basic hospitality and others as a standing concession they resent, which says a good deal about the house.

Sky Etiquette School.description: A teaching platform where visitors and local children learn lane courtesy, merge discipline and the difference between confidence and a civic incident. Instruction is patient and the examples are drawn from real accidents. Gisqon runs the school, teaching that slower traffic keeps to the outer bands, that emergency descent takes precedence over everything, that a challenge belongs in a challenge lane, and that deliberate wake disruption is hostile conduct rather than a joke. He is patient until a mistake becomes rude, and identifies poor flight posture on sight. Its staff regard this work as the quarter's most important contribution to the city.

Luxaryn Quarter.name: Luxaryn Quarter
Luxaryn Quarter.basicInfo: Luxaryn Quarter proves that standing in Korrvane is not built only through victories. Set in the mid-to-lower transition toward the Commerce Layer, it sits naturally along the broad post-match flow leaving the Arena without controlling the civic routes that carry it. Away from tournament traffic it remains a lived-in residential district of family homes, practice spaces, guest balconies, food and ordinary neighborhood life. The quarter is warm-lit and generously proportioned, wine-red and cream against bronze fittings, with wide flightways, deep balconies and stalls built into every approach, and the smell of cooking reaching the lane above it at most hours. Feeding people, hosting rivals, keeping relationships alive and controlling the city's post-match social rhythm create genuine influence, and the house does not apologize for having built its standing that way. Winners and losers arrive together after a bracket and are fed the same way, which is the method rather than the decoration. The house competes seriously as well, and its contenders resent being read as an extension of the party. On an ordinary week the district runs on deliveries, neighborhood kitchens, children underfoot, music in the evening and a great deal of invisible work by the people who arrange who sits where. A guest list here is a political document nobody calls one.
Luxaryn Quarter.hiddenInfo: Feeding people, hosting rivals, keeping relationships alive and controlling the city's post-match social rhythm create genuine political influence, and Luxaryn understands exactly what it holds. Qartessa's food routes reach through the Commerce Layer and the Arena's street ring, which is why Luxaryn vendors occupy the best positions without ever having taken them by force. Salambor's control of access to the feast hall handles guest lists and rival spacing, and an invitation withheld is a message the whole city can read. Cross-house diplomacy happens here in a way it cannot at the Judges' Dais, because a shared table permits conversations that a tribunal forbids. The quarter's private frustration is Didobara, whose combat ambition is serious and who is persistently taken less seriously than the party around her; reducing her achievements to an excuse for a celebration is the fastest way to insult this house. Hannix carries the opposite reputation and is equally capable in both directions. Celebrating after a defeat is a genuine Luxaryn practice, not a consolation.

Hadavar’s Feast Hall.description: A warm, rearrangeable hall with a main feast floor, a family seating edge, a serving pass, a reception point for announced events and a working kitchen behind it. It handles celebrations, cross-house gatherings and ordinary neighborhood dining with equal seriousness. Hadavar receives here, universally liked and entirely aware of it, turning genuine friendship into political weight without pretending otherwise, while Salambor arranges who sits with whom, who needs distance and how to redirect a rematch before the furniture suffers. The floor is re-set between an event and an ordinary evening meal in the time it takes to clear the passes. Slow-roasted Korrin shoulder is the hall's prestige dish, though nobody has to eat heroically to belong.

Festival Flightway.description: A broad ceremonial flight route through the quarter, hung with banners and lit for announced events and processions. On celebration nights it carries slow formation flying rather than fast transit. The lane is wider than the traffic needs, its banner lines strung between the terraces on either side and re-tensioned before any announced event, and the balconies along it are treated as seating by everyone living behind them. Families fly it together at low speed, children included, and the etiquette shifts accordingly: no overtaking, no wake games, nothing that would make a slower flier uncomfortable. The rest of the week it is an ordinary, generously proportioned lane home.

Didobara’s Practice Yard.description: A serious working training yard set back from the celebration spaces, in use at hours when the rest of the quarter is asleep or recovering. Didobara's combat ambition is genuine and the yard's condition proves it. The floor is worn through to the bedding in the working lines, the rigs are maintained rather than decorative, and the yard is screened from the flightway so nothing about it reads as part of the entertainment. She is a capable contender who wants to be recognized for her results, has considered competing under another name, and remains loyal anyway. Treating her results as a pretext for a party is the local definition of an insult.

Hannix’s Party Court.description: An open court with a main gathering floor, a music position, a drinks-and-snacks edge, conversational seating and a kept-clear arrival zone that separates landings from dancing. The equipment is modern and maintained, not improvised. Hannix hosts here, seeing no contradiction between fighting seriously in the afternoon and hosting immediately afterward, and arrives dressed as though the celebration has already started. Rival houses mix on this floor because the arrival zone keeps the entrances from becoming confrontations. An evening can open with an energetic set and end with friends talking long after the music stops.

Street Food Crown.description: A ring of stalls and carts crowning the quarter's main approach, serving portable food continuously from midday into the night. Vendors here supply the Arena's food ring as well and know the bracket schedule better than most competitors. Qartessa Luxaryn holds the route, knows what everyone orders and rather more of their private business than they realize, and fighters, officials, families and visitors talk freely around her counters. Queues form along the approach rail, orders are called across the ring, and a stall that runs out of something gets loudly and publicly mocked by the stall beside it. The smell reaches the flight lane above it.

House Guest Balconies.description: Guest accommodation balconies looking out over the quarter, kept ready for visiting houses, sponsors and cross-house friends. Placement on these balconies communicates standing precisely, which is why Salambor assigns them personally. The balconies are deep, sheltered on the windward side and furnished for people who intend to stay a while, each with its own landing step so a guest never has to arrive through anyone else's. Milkon works this part of the quarter hardest, wanting Luxaryn's informal popularity converted into explicit leverage, which Hadavar appreciates and others distrust. Rival guests are spaced with a care that looks accidental.

After-Match Commons.description: The wide open commons where post-match traffic from the Arena settles into food, argument and company. Winners and losers arrive together and are fed the same way, which is the quarter's actual political method. The commons is open paving ringed with serving points and long shared tables, sheltered enough to hold a crowd in wind and large enough that nobody has to sit where they do not want to. Salambor works the room, separating people who should not be adjacent and steering an argument toward a table rather than a lane. A fighter who celebrates after losing is not thought unserious here. It is fullest on the nights when Luxaryn's own competitor lost.

Music Steps.description: A terraced run of open steps where musicians play and audiences arrange themselves by how closely they want to listen. It remains open air and unenclosed, distinct from the party court next to it. The steps are broad stone treads cut into the terrace face, warm from the day, with the lower runs taken by people who came for the music and the upper ones by people who came to talk over it. Players work in rotation without any formal arrangement, and residents on the balconies above listen without ever coming down. Late in the evening the playing gets quieter and the steps fill with people who have stopped dancing.

Vorreth Quarter.name: Vorreth Quarter
Vorreth Quarter.basicInfo: Vorreth Quarter challenges Korrvane's obsession with measurement. The district is real, functional and inhabited, sitting on the eastern slope away from the legible civic spine, but its records, routes, occupancy and public behavior never settle into a stable pattern. The tone is quiet and occupied rather than sinister, and it is genuinely difficult to map. The building stock is muted plum and gray over bronze-black trim, well kept and deliberately unremarkable, with fewer banners than any other district and none that announce anything. Wind moves through the terraces the way it moves through the rest of the city, and the quarter is no darker, no colder and no emptier than its neighbors. People live here ordinarily: food is delivered, children are raised, repairs are made, residents work occupations across the city and come home. The house has competed in Korrvane for years and its representatives appear in the bracket like anyone else, yet its tactics, records and public roster resist confident interpretation, and its results are the reliable weak point in every prediction the city makes. Statements from the house are clear enough to be useful and vague enough to resolve nothing. Nothing here is concealed so much as unlabeled, and no visit produces quite the same account as the last one.
Vorreth Quarter.hiddenInfo: Nobody can say for certain whether the quarter's inconsistency is deliberate method, accumulated accident or a bit of both, and the house has never clarified. Vorreth results regularly damage the Arena's prediction models and the betting stands price them at a permanent discount, which is either a disadvantage or a very old advantage. Bomivex's record wall holds house history in a form that contradicts the civic archives on several points, and each side maintains its own version is correct. Magovar's platform stands empty often enough that its emptiness has become a subject in itself. Azrubara receives visitors in a hall where conversations are pleasant, unhurried and afterward surprisingly hard to summarize. Residence rows shift occupancy between visits, guest rooms appear where there was no door the previous day, and the misdirection walk sends the unfamiliar in circles without anyone obstructing them. The quarter is on the map, pays its civic obligations and fields its bracket competitor every week. It simply demonstrates that Korrvane cannot measure everything, which the city finds harder to forgive than deception.

Unmarked Entry Court.description: The quarter's main entrance, a plain court with no house marker, no directory and no obvious onward route. Residents pass through it without hesitation and visitors stop dead. The paving is well maintained, the walls are clean, there is nothing broken and nothing hidden, and the exits lead in several directions without any of them being signed. Sufeta meets arrivals here when the house expects them, answers questions courteously and at some length, and leaves the visitor holding no more than they came with. Deliveries arrive and are accepted without anyone asking where they are going next. Nothing here is hidden; it is simply not labeled, which turns out to be sufficient.

Shifting Residence Rows.description: Terraced housing rows whose occupancy, door arrangements and connecting stairs do not match anyone's previous visit. Families genuinely live here and can say which home is theirs today. Washing hangs on the balconies, food smells carry between the levels, and children play on the stairs exactly as they do in every other residential quarter in the city. Bomqara is associated with these rows, and other houses disagree about whether she has already competed under another identity, a disagreement Vorreth has never troubled to correct. Civic surveyors have produced four incompatible plans of this area and stopped producing more.
paths: Guest Room That Was Not There Yesterday

Azrubara’s Quiet Hall.description: A low, comfortable receiving hall where Azrubara meets guests without ceremony or evident agenda. The conversation is unhurried and genuinely pleasant, and visitors have trouble reconstructing it afterward. The room is warm, plainly furnished and quieter than the wind outside should permit, with seating arranged so that nobody is at the head of anything. Azrubara has been part of Korrvane tournament history longer than most active contenders, wins impossible fights, occasionally loses straightforward ones, and appears quietly amused by other houses' attempts to understand her. Sufeta is often present and says a great deal. Nothing in the room suggests it is the seat of anything.

Bomivex’s Record Wall.description: A long inscribed wall holding Vorreth match histories, house events and dates, several of which contradict the civic archive outright. Bomivex maintains it personally and declines to reconcile the differences. The inscriptions are cut cleanly, kept legible and arranged in an order that does not correspond to any sequence an outsider can name, and Hamilqa keeps the fuller records behind it in a system nobody outside the house fully understands. Bomivex himself is friendly, easy to talk to and perfectly willing to discuss a result he cannot explain, which makes his record more frustrating rather than less. Both versions are consistently defended, and neither side has produced anything decisive.

Magovar’s Empty Platform.description: A maintained training platform that is almost never in use, swept clean and evidently ready. Magovar is associated with it and is rarely on it. The surface is bare stone with the rigs stowed at the edge, the anchor points show wear that nobody has seen being made, and the wind crosses it without anything to catch. Magovar has competed publicly only twice, winning once in a way nobody could explain and losing once in a way that made less sense, and she has clarified neither result. Bomqara is sometimes seen here and sometimes not. The city has generated several theories about the emptiness, none of which the house has bothered to address.

Misdirection Walk.description: The quarter's connecting route, whose turns, sightlines and step counts make an unfamiliar walker arrive somewhere other than intended. No barrier, sign or guard is involved. The walk is ordinary underfoot, well lit and perfectly maintained, with the same muted facings on both sides and views that close off just before they would orient anyone. Residents carry deliveries through it at speed, children run it without looking, and a visitor who asks for directions is given them clearly and still ends up elsewhere. Residents navigate it without thought and are politely unhelpful about explaining how.
paths: Guest Room That Was Not There Yesterday

Guest Room That Was Not There Yesterday.description: Visitor accommodation that reliably exists whenever a guest requires it and reliably cannot be located when they return. The room is comfortable, prepared and entirely ordinary while occupied. There is bedding, water, a window with a view of the slope and a door that locks from the inside, and the hospitality is unforced enough that most guests sleep well. Staff arrive when expected and not otherwise. Nobody who has stayed reports anything unusual about the night, only about the morning after, and accounts of where the room actually was differ in every particular. Guests who ask about it are answered courteously and learn nothing.

Silent Viewing Deck.description: An overlook facing the slope out of the city, where residents watch the eastern approach and the traffic below without comment. Conversation on the deck is minimal by custom rather than rule. The deck is bare stone with a low parapet, exposed to the wind, furnished with nothing that would encourage anyone to settle, and it faces away from the Arena, the compound and every other thing the city considers worth looking at. People arrive, stand for a while and leave, and nobody records who was present or when. Visitors are welcome on it and find the silence harder to keep than residents do. Whatever the quarter observes from here does not appear in any public record.

Quilrath.name: Quilrath
Quilrath.basicInfo: The polished inner city of the Dravon empire: black star-glass towers, red command-light grids and gold status inlays along elevated avenues. The avenues run above sealed transit corridors and open into angular civic plazas, and every surface is kept clean enough to show a fingerprint. Surveillance pylons, automated checkpoint bridges and silent patrol drones sort everyone who moves here by rank, family and loyalty standing. The sorting is quiet. A gate reads a citizen and opens, or reads a citizen and does not, and the queue behind has learned not to comment either way. Projection banners of approved Dravon history hang over the main routes, and the ordinary sound of the place is engineered: dampened corridors, measured footsteps, announcements that arrive at one fixed volume and stop when they are finished. Officers, couriers, clerks and approved households cross it on errands with a recorded start and a recorded end. Comfort is real in the Inner Circle, and it is issued rather than owned. Rank-gated residences, reserved tables, unhurried service and warm interiors all exist here, and every one of them rests on a standing that can be reviewed. Visitors are processed before they see any of it and escorted if they cannot move alone. Damage is repaired fast: a scuffed inlay is replaced before most residents notice it was scuffed.
Quilrath.hiddenInfo: The Inner Circle is beautiful because the suffering has been pushed outward. Movement runs on Access Levels 0 through 9, and access is a social weapon as much as a technical one: it can be quietly lowered after a relative's bad audit, temporarily raised to bait someone into a room, or revoked mid-errand so a citizen discovers their new standing at a rank gate in front of witnesses. The Red Ledger Intake Office is where that machinery first shows a seam. Citizens arrive with travel-status problems, summons and record corrections, and a few of them are actually holding the edge of the disappearing-records scandal that runs to Red Ledger Prime in the Nivarek Compound. Names are going missing from the system entirely, and nobody in the intake queue is told that. The Victory Walk's edited conquest reliefs contradict the chronicle Maelra Dravon is supposed to be curating, and the vandalism that occasionally appears there is not random. Helvyra is absent from every route board: the Dravon Disconnection is absolute, and the city's one gate reaches Relstaris only.

The Command Spine.description: The elevated avenue running through inner Quilrath toward the Ascendant Keep - part parade route, part command artery, part surveillance corridor. It runs broad and hard underfoot, black star-glass panels set with gold lines marking where formation traffic takes priority, a red command-light grid burning overhead. Officers, couriers and approved citizens move along it beneath projection banners of approved Dravon history, and the patrol drones overhead never quite leave the edge of hearing. Most days it carries errands rather than parades: escorts collecting visitors, clerks crossing between compounds, a supply crew keeping to the outer lane. At the joins, the inlay is worn pale where couriers have cut the same corner for years.

The Inner Compliance Gate.description: The controlled entrance from the wider city into inner Quilrath. Every arrival is scanned, logged, ranked and assigned movement permissions before the checkpoint bridge releases them, and escorts are issued to anyone who cannot move alone. The approach is a long channel of black composite under white processing light, lined by a rail that keeps arrivals in single file, and the bridge extends only once a permission has cleared. The queue is orderly because everyone in it has watched a denial happen. Gate staff work from scripts and do not improvise; a question about a delay gets the same sentence each time. Past the barrier there is a waiting bay of fixed benches where the escorted sit until the officer assigned to them arrives.

The Rank Gates.description: Smaller inner checkpoints dividing movement by clearance, rank mark, escort authorization and loyalty standing. Each one reads a citizen silently and opens, or does not. They are set into ordinary walls at the ends of ordinary corridors, narrow enough for one person, a red reader plate at shoulder height and a light above it that changes without any sound. This is where people learn their status has changed: no announcement, no explanation, just a gate that used to work and a crowd pretending not to look. Anyone refused steps aside and waits, because arguing with a gate is a worse record than being refused by one. The plates are wiped down on a schedule, and the fingermarks accumulate again within the hour.

The High Civic Rings.description: Elite residential rings for command families, ranking administrators and officer households, terraced in black star-glass with gold status inlay. The terraces step back from the avenue behind their own rank gates, with private landings, quiet interior courts and windows that show a warm interior light rather than anything happening inside. Children are raised here to impossible standards, and reformist conversations happen at ordinary volume behind private doors. The comfort is genuine and entirely conditional. Household staff, tutors and couriers come and go on standing permissions of their own. The inlay along each frontage is renewed when a household's standing changes, which is how a street learns of a promotion before the family announces one.

The Victory Walk.description: A public avenue lined with red-lit star-glass reliefs, holographic conquest records and official history projections. The reliefs are cut deep into black glass and lit from within so the carved conquests read from the far side of the walk, and the projections between them cycle campaign records on a fixed loop. School tours pass through weekly and citizens can recite the approved account on request. What the displays leave out of the Dravon conflicts is more interesting than what they show. Guides move groups along at a measured pace, pausing at the same panels every time. Maintenance crews polish the lower panels often, because the lower panels are the ones people touch.

The Civic Watch Plazas.description: Open angular plazas fitted with surveillance pylons, rank scanners, public address systems and automated crowd-routing barriers. The paving is hard black composite, the barriers sit flush until they rise, and the pylons stand at the corners with their sensor heads turning slowly and continuously. Loyalty announcements and public corrections happen here, before crowds the barriers have already arranged. People choose their words carefully and praise promptly. Between announcements the plazas are simply the fastest way to cross between avenues, and they are used that way constantly. The address speakers carry a short tone before every message, and conversation drops on that tone before anyone decides to stop talking.

Red Ledger Intake Office.description: The public-facing branch of the Red Ledger. Travel-status problems, missing paperwork, summons and record corrections are handled at its counters by quiet Nivarek clerks who never hurry anyone. The hall is low-ceilinged and evenly lit, with a numbered waiting bank facing a run of counters and red data readouts recessed into the desk surfaces. It feels like ordinary bureaucracy, which is the point; the files that decide anything are not kept in this building. Citizens bring documents in folders, rehearse their question while they wait, and are answered in the same unhurried register whatever they ask. Nobody at the counters can say when a referral will come back, and they have been trained not to guess aloud.

The Gilt Setting.description: A formal restaurant in the High Civic Rings: an arrival-and-reservation room, the dining floor, small booked rooms, a serving passage and the preservation kitchen behind. Dark polished finishes, understated gold, seating and service order arranged by rank. Arrivals give a name at the front room and wait while it is confirmed; the dining floor beyond is quiet enough that cutlery is the loudest thing in it. Successive preparations come out on a timed service, and a booked room reduces interruption without promising privacy from anything else. A reservation buys a beautiful evening and no access whatsoever. Diners here do sincerely enjoy the food, and some of them are marking a family occasion.

The Ascendant Keep.name: The Ascendant Keep
The Ascendant Keep.basicInfo:
House Dravon's central seat is a command fortress rather than a palace: black star-glass walls, red tactical light, sealed elevators and holographic battle maps above panoramic windows overlooking the districts it controls. The approach is severe and deliberately legible, the interior a sequence of halls, chambers and courts connected by corridors that carry sound badly and sightlines well. War planning, ceremony, advancement and family power all converge in the same building. A declaration made in one chamber is recorded in another before the speaker has left the floor. Elite guards stand in exact formation and the corridors are quieter than they should be. Movement inside runs on sealed lifts and rank-gated doors, so most people who work here only ever see the part of it their standing reaches. Officers, adjutants, ceremonial staff, household attendants and Nivarek observers all keep to their own routes through it. Natural light reaches only the outer windows, and everything inward of them is lit red. Visitors are escorted throughout, held between appointments in bare anterooms, and told plainly that waiting is part of the process. The stonework equivalent is not here: nothing is carved, everything is cast, fitted and replaced when it wears.

Work on offer here: House Dravon — Walk the Gates Unknown (ask Orvane Dravon).
The Ascendant Keep.hiddenInfo: The Red War Room is where Dravon's next move actually lives — Ignivex pressure, Dustfall containment, Contair and Relstaris files, and the early shape of off-world expansion routes. Anything stolen from it is worth a house. Kaldor Dravon remains the active head, fully in command and dangerous; he delegates daily operations to Sorin and Vaelen deliberately, and permits the succession pressure between them because sharpened heirs and guessing rivals both serve him. Kaldor's War Gallery frames the First Dravon Conflict as noble resistance to disorder and stays quiet about Ark Genesis and the Castro power that ended the campaign; the Second Conflict's treatment is even more selective. The gaps between the gallery's version and the true chronology are traceable, and the Correction Archive across the city in the Nivarek Compound holds the revisions before release. The Oath Courts look ceremonial and function as surveillance: Nivarek observes every vow, and advancement trials are where loyalty is proven or quietly lost.

Ascendant Hall.description: The main command chamber of House Dravon: raised command platforms, tactical displays, house banners and rank stations under panoramic windows overlooking the controlled districts. The platforms step up toward the windows so that anyone addressing the room does it with the city behind them, and the rank stations line the floor in fixed positions nobody mistakes for interchangeable. Major decisions, command ceremonies and high-level negotiations happen here. Between them the hall is worked rather than admired: adjutants updating displays, couriers arriving at the lower stations, a duty officer holding the floor. The view is part of the argument, every single time. Delegations are brought in facing the windows, and never seated higher than the platform they are answering.

The Iron Assembly.description: A vast ceremonial chamber for declarations, rank advancements, loyalty ceremonies and state addresses. It is built as a bowl of tiered seating around a speaking floor, the tiers black and unornamented, the floor lit hard from above so whoever stands on it is the brightest thing in the room. It is not a senate; it is a performance of unity, and the seating quietly publishes who is currently trusted. Attendance is by summons, places are assigned, and everyone present reads the arrangement before the first word. Accusations delivered from its floor have ended families between one speech and the next. Ceremonial staff rehearse entries and exits beforehand, because the choreography is part of the message.

The Red War Room.description: The restricted strategic chamber where Dravon watches Ignivex, Dustfall, Contair and Relstaris on live campaign maps. The maps stand as projected volumes over a central table, updating continuously, and the walls carry secondary displays officers turn to without leaving their positions. Access is tightly held and the room is swept constantly. Officers speak in clipped ranges and timings, and the red light makes everyone in it look like they have already decided. Sessions run long and nothing leaves on paper. Entry is by name against a list held at the door, and a name can be on the list one week and absent the next without anyone in the room remarking on it.

Kaldor's War Gallery.description: A curated history chamber staging Dravon's official account of past wars in holographic relief. The reliefs stand in sequence along a walking route, each with its own lighting and commentary cue, the room kept cool and dim so the projections carry. Guides frame the First Dravon Conflict as noble resistance to disorder; the Second is handled more carefully still. Anyone who knows the real chronology can watch the edits happening in front of them. Officer candidates, visiting delegations and school groups are all brought through, each with a version of the tour pitched to them. One relief near the end of the route has a noticeably shorter commentary, and the guides move groups past it without pausing.

The Inner Obsidian Yard.description: The elite training yard for Dravon heirs, command candidates and approved officers, black composite underfoot and instrumented for measurement rather than spectacle. Sensor arrays ring the floor at waist height, readouts run along the wall for anyone qualified to read them, and there is seating only for assessors. This is command preparation, not sport: controlled duels, advancement trials and affinity demonstrations, watched by people whose job is to score them. Bouts are stopped on a called figure rather than on a finish, and the results go into a record before anyone has caught their breath. The composite is scuffed in a wide band through the centre of the floor and clean at the edges.

The Oath Courts.description: Formal courtyards used for vows, promotions, loyalty renewal and rank confirmation, open to the sky and ringed with recording positions. The paving is plain and the surrounding galleries are narrow, so a voice carries clean across the court and is captured from several angles at once. Obedience is proved in public here. Nivarek observers attend every session, and the pause before a vow is timed as carefully as the words that follow it. Families attend when invited and stand where they are placed. Ceremonies run back to back on busy days, with the next party waiting in the gallery while the previous one finishes. The wording of each oath is issued in advance so that nobody has an excuse for hesitating, and the ones who hesitate anyway do it in front of everybody who matters to them.

Private Dravon Strategy Suites.description: Restricted meeting rooms for Dravon family leadership: small, sealed, and unrecorded by anything the family does not control. Each is little more than a table, fixed seating, a single display surface and a door that reports only that it was opened. The light in them is lower than anywhere else in the Keep, which is deliberate and which visitors notice before they can say why. Succession friction, reform-versus-expansion arguments and emergency war planning all happen at these tables. Attendance is by summons and the summons carries no agenda. The sound damping is good enough that a raised voice never leaves the room, so a family argument ends with everyone walking out at the same measured pace.

Nivarek Compound.name: Nivarek Compound
Nivarek Compound.basicInfo: House Nivarek makes conquest permanent by recording it, and its compound is the legal-memory engine of Dravon rule: black archive towers, red data columns, glass-floor record chambers and sound-dampened corridors. The towers are narrow and windowless above their lower floors, and inside them the data columns stand floor to ceiling in ranks, shedding a red working light that never changes with the hour. Loyalty standing, family classification and citizenship status are all decided here. What arrives as a person's difficult year leaves as a classification, a grade and a file reference. Clerks move in exact routes and nobody raises their voice. Hearings run to timetable in chambers built for it, testimony is taken in sealed rooms, and gold-lined legal panels mark the doorways where a decision becomes binding. Citizens summoned here wait in corridors with benches along one wall and nothing else, and are called by reference rather than by name. The air is cool and dry throughout, kept that way for the records rather than the people. Nothing in the building hurries, and the effect of that on anyone waiting is well understood by the staff who designed the waiting.
Nivarek Compound.hiddenInfo: Nivarek is terrifying because it is precise. People are broken through procedure rather than violence: a loyalty audit can reduce a family's standing, a sealed testimony session can produce a confession nobody struck anyone for, and the Conquered-Family Registry Wing quietly assigns inherited suspicion marks to children who have done nothing. Red Ledger Prime holds the files that matter — elite family records, erased identities, military assignments, hidden political risk — and records are disappearing out of it. The Erased are the same mystery seen from the other end: people Dravon now claims never existed. The Unbroken Accord's Archive believes it has a friend inside this record system and does not know who; Myrra Nivarek quietly helps people in the intake queues and has never been confirmed as anything more. The Correction Archive stores altered records and revised histories before release, which makes it the one room in Quilrath where the official past and the real one are held side by side.

Nivarek Record Court.description: The central administrative hall of House Nivarek, a glass-floored chamber of red data columns where legal status, family classification and loyalty standing are processed. The columns rise in ranks from a floor that shows the working levels below, so the whole machinery of the place is visible and entirely inaudible. Disputes are heard without raised voices and settled in writing. A representative states a case from a fixed position, an adjudicating clerk answers from another, and the result is issued as a document rather than announced. Clerks cross the floor along fixed routes and do not look up as they pass. Family representatives wait at the margin for their reference to be called. The glass is cleaned nightly and still shows the faint tracks of the routes most used.

Red Ledger Prime.description: The restricted high-security branch of the Red Ledger, behind biometric archive gates. The gates open onto a short sealed passage and then a chamber of shelved data cores standing in their own field, with handling stations set at intervals and nothing on any wall that names what is held where. Elite family files, erased identities, military assignments and state secrets are held here. The air is cold, the light is red, and the number of people cleared to stand in the room is small enough to list by name. Retrieval is logged at the gate, at the station and on the core itself. Nobody works here alone, and nobody working here discusses the work outside. A single chair sits at the reading station and there is no second one.

Loyalty Audit Courts.description: Formal hearing chambers where citizens, officers, elite families and conquered-house members are reviewed. Each chamber is a plain room with a raised examiner's desk, a single seat facing it and recording positions along the side wall. No violence is used and none is required: an audit can lower a grade, strip an access level, or open a review of everyone the subject is related to. Proceedings run to a posted list, subjects are called in one at a time, and the finding is issued afterwards rather than delivered in the room. Families wait outside on benches designed to be uncomfortable. The corridor outside the chambers is the quietest part of the compound, and people who have waited there before bring nothing to read.

Conquered-Family Registry Wing.description: Record halls for absorbed minor families, relocated populations, work assignments and inherited suspicion marks, displayed as holographic family trees branching into classifications. The trees hang in the aisles at working height, pale red against the dark, and a clerk can rotate a whole lineage with one hand to find the branch that matters. Children appear on them already carrying a standing they were born into. Requests to view a line are taken at a desk at the head of the wing and answered in the order they were logged. Missing entries are commoner than the staff will admit. A gap in a branch is shown as a gap, unlabelled, and the display offers no explanation for it because the display has not been given one.

Sealed Testimony Rooms.description: Private deposition, interrogation and confession rooms where silence is part of the pressure. Sound-dampened walls, one table, a recording field and an examiner with unlimited time. The rooms are small and evenly lit, with no clock, no window and a door that closes without any sound at all. A session begins when the examiner begins it and continues through long stretches in which nothing is said. People walk out of these rooms having agreed to things they came in fully intending to deny, and cannot always say when that turned. Nothing is written by the subject; the record is made by the field and read back at the end. Water is provided on request, which is the only thing in the room that can be asked for.

The Correction Archive.description: A restricted archive holding altered records, revised histories and corrected public narratives before release. The shelving is ordinary and the handling is not: each item is stored in a pair, the version in circulation and the version replacing it, with the working copy issued only against a countersigned request. It is the one place in Quilrath where the official past and the real one sit on adjacent shelves. Staff work in silence at low tables under directed light, comparing, amending and closing files that will be public in a month. Access is severely limited, and the wing does not appear in the compound's public directories. Nothing here is destroyed, which is a working principle and not a mercy.

Balrath Bastion Barracks.name: Balrath Bastion Barracks
Balrath Bastion Barracks.basicInfo: House Balrath makes conquest physical. The compound - Balrath Barracks to most, the Gate-House to outsiders - builds and maintains the walls, gates, drones, transit locks and issued equipment that let Dravon control who moves through Quilrath. Armored machine halls, red-lit gate machinery, drone racks and heavy transit lifts run loud beneath a disciplined surface. The halls are stacked and connected by black alloy walkways, the repair bays seal for testing, and the maintenance pits below the floor line are open working spaces rather than hidden ones. Shifts change on a horn and the crews move in formation until they reach their stations. Engineers, wall technicians, gate operators, drone-line supervisors, quartermasters and rapid-response troops all work the same site and rarely mix outside their own halls. Gold-coded command lines run along the walls to mark authority and route, and the equipment depots issue nothing without a name attached. Above the upper tiers are the aerial patrol launch slots, which fire off at intervals all day. It is a working industrial compound first, and its discipline is visible in how quickly a mess is cleared rather than in how little mess is made.
Balrath Bastion Barracks.hiddenInfo: Everything that makes the city a cage is manufactured here, which means everything that makes it a cage can be reached here. Gate lockdowns, rank-gate behaviour and surveillance pylon coverage are all set from the Inner Wall Control Yards, and a single sabotage in the Gateworks changes what the Inner Compliance Gate will accept. The Labor Transit Systems Office is the uncomfortable one: it moves classified conquered-house populations out to the Camp Belt, and the engineers who route those transports know exactly what their work supplies. Lurani Balrath has begun asking about it. The Prototype Gate Lab exists because Dravon wants Lunar Gates of its own and cannot build them without Contair; Namar Balrath's admiration for the technology he is supposed to replace shades into illegal study of captured equipment, and the lab does not add a gate or change the city's one Relstaris link. Border Infrastructure Command's corridor plans are third-conflict preparation, not contingency.

Balrath Gateworks.description: The main engineering hall for Quilrath's gates, walls and access-control systems, full of red-lit gate machinery and heavy transit lifts. The hall runs tall, with gantries at two levels, test frames standing in the open floor and lifts hauling assemblies up through it continuously. Lockdown protocols are written and tested here, and repairs after unrest run around the clock. A test cycle is called, the frame drives a barrier through its full travel, and the whole hall hears it. Crews work in rotation with supervisors tracking faults on boards at the hall's end. The noise is constant, and the crews have learned to shout everything twice. Hand signals cover the rest, and a newcomer is taught them before being taught anything else.

Inner Wall Control Yards.description: The control center for inner walls, automated barriers, surveillance pylons and rank-gate systems, banked with wall-control stations and live district feeds. The stations face a wall of feeds in fixed grid order, each operator holding a set of sectors, and the room is kept dim so the displays read. A citywide lockdown begins as one confirmed instruction at one of these desks. Drone response launches from the slots overhead within seconds of it. Ordinary shifts are hours of watching nothing change, punctuated by barrier faults, a pylon losing a feed, or a rank gate reporting a reader error that someone has to go out and touch. Confirmations are spoken aloud and repeated back. The chairs are worn through at the armrests.

Drone Assembly Tiers.description: Stacked production and maintenance tiers turning out Dravon state drones: reliable, intimidating, ugly and completely standardized. The tiers run one above another with racks of frames along the outer wall, assembly benches down the middle and test cages at the end of each line where a finished unit is put through its paces before it is signed off. Shifts run against quotas under supervisors who count failures. Parts arrive in numbered crates and every unit leaves with the same profile as the one before it. Balrath engineers compare the output to Contair's elegance in private and defend it loudly in public. The scrap bins at the line ends are emptied twice a shift, and nobody on the floor is told where the contents go.

Military Equipment Depots.description: Storage and inspection halls for issued armor, weapons, field kits, gate hardware and rapid-response equipment, racked in numbered aisles under gold-coded command lines. The aisles run long and identical, the racking is heavy, and an inspection bench sits at the head of each run where kit is checked, logged and either passed back or pulled. Quartermasters check every item out against a name. Nothing leaves on a promise, and an item returned damaged generates a report before it generates a replacement. Dravon does not win through brilliance here; it wins through scale, and the aisles prove it. The end of one aisle carries a board of outstanding returns, and the names on it stay up until the items come back.

Border Infrastructure Command.description: The strategic engineering office for Ignivex pressure, Dustfall containment and the old Contair invasion scars, its walls carrying siege corridor plans and border maps. It is a working office rather than a command chamber: plan tables at standing height, map surfaces that can be marked and cleared, and engineers arguing over a corridor profile with the drawings between them. The planning assumes a third conflict rather than fearing one. Projects here are measured in seasons of construction and are revised constantly as the frontier situation changes. It is also where the reasons Dravon has not moved on Dustfall directly are written down. The oldest drawings in the room are the Contair scar surveys, and they are consulted more often than anyone here says aloud.

Labor Transit Systems Office.description: A restricted infrastructure office routing outer-city labor movement, conquered-family transport and work-camp logistics. It is a quiet room of scheduling stations, well away from the machine halls, with the whole system rendered as flows and timings on the wall displays. Transit schedules scroll past as abstract load figures on the wall displays. Staff work to clearing times and reroute around delays, and the work is genuinely difficult in the way any large scheduling problem is difficult. Engineers here can trace exactly how inner comfort is supplied by outer control, and some have started doing that arithmetic. The figures are held at a level of abstraction that makes the arithmetic possible only if somebody chooses to do it, and most of the time nobody does.

Prototype Gate Lab.description: A smaller experimental lab where Balrath tries to improve gate and access systems without Contair equipment. It is one room of test rigs behind a sealed bay door, with containment around the working frame and instrumentation banked along the wall to catch what happens in the fraction of a second that matters. Test rigs fail loudly and expensively; the successes are incremental and heavily reported. A working session is mostly waiting, then a burst of noise, then hours of reading what the instruments caught. Captured technology occasionally appears on the benches, and no paperwork explains where it came from. Nobody in the lab asks about it, and the pieces are gone again within a few days.

The Gray Rings.name: The Gray Rings
The Gray Rings.basicInfo:
Ring 2, the compliant middle city: administrative blocks, standard housing, state commerce and industry in gray composite instead of star-glass, under red command-lights older and dimmer than the Inner Circle's. The composite is patched where it has been repaired and the repairs do not quite match, which is the ring's most honest visual detail. Assigned work, standardized goods of famously adequate quality and civics instruction fill the day under the Civic Standing Grades. Mornings run on shift horns and queue boards; the streets fill twice a day and are unremarkable in between. This is where the regime looks most like a functioning state. Counters are staffed, permits issue, clinics treat people, classes are taught, and a household with clean paperwork can live an entire ordinary life inside the system as designed. Nivarek assesses Standing here and Kathvar administrators process what that Standing means at the counters, the queues and the gates. Many residents believe in the order they live under, keep decent and careful lives, and file honest reports. The pressure is procedural rather than dramatic: a grade that moves on a relative's audit, a permit that takes three days instead of one, a stock board that is shorter this week than last.

Work on offer here: Quilrath — A Day at the Permit Counter; Quilrath — The Corrected File (ask Odrin Kathvar).
The Gray Rings.hiddenInfo: Standing decides housing, work assignment, movement radius, queue speed and audit frequency, and Nivarek decides Standing — Kathvar administrators at the counters only process what has already been determined, which does not stop people begging the wrong clerk. Ferrik Nivarek audits from the Standing Office believing precision is mercy; his files are immaculate and his sleep is not. Torbek Karn works a Provision Hall counter and moves extras through the tolerated gray market with perfect paperwork, useful to the same officials who periodically raid it — everyone's quiet friend, nobody's informant so far. Merron Talvek teaches the official history in the Civics Classrooms, believes about half of it, and polices which half he says aloud; a pupil recently asked him about a name he remembers and the records do not. Olna Bresk runs a floor in the Works, files honest reports and has never been audited, which is the regime's best argument in one decent person. The horror here is procedural, not theatrical: what the ladder quietly does to people who love someone on a lower rung.

Standing Office.description: The Nivarek office where Civic Standing is assessed and audited for this ring: a waiting hall, numbered assessment rooms, and files that are always more current than the people sitting in front of them. The waiting hall has fixed bench seating facing a call board, and the assessment rooms open off it in a numbered run. Grades rise on service and fall on association. Sessions are scheduled and subjects attend at a stated time, sometimes with a relative, more often alone.
