The first is Maelis's own discovery that residents have been quietly working around a system rather than reporting it — the complaint pattern that never arrived because people solved it themselves and told nobody. The second is sharper: Vexorath records systems rather than private lives, but the distinction is imperfect, because connected systems can reveal behaviour indirectly. A resident who discovers that infrastructure monitoring recorded more than intended brings that to the Privacy Challenge Chamber, and canon keeps it an ongoing tension rather than a solved ethical problem. The Quarter is distinct from Vexorath City's Civic Assembly Floor and neither outranks the other. Emergency control is temporary and its decisions are reviewed afterward, and technical authority must explain restrictions once an emergency ends — that duty is established, but no venue for it has ever been assigned.

Resident Interface Forum.description: The Quarter's front door: where a resident raises something with the systems and with the people who build them. The room is open and unintimidating, seating that adjusts, worktables rather than a bench, and the light kept even so that nobody is explaining themselves out of a shadow. This is Maelis Contair's setting, one open explanatory hand, the other near an integrated wrist interface, reading as patient civic authority. Usability, accessibility, privacy and complaint patterns all arrive in this room first, which means most of what is said here is a small annoyance that turns out to be a design fault. What a resident is entitled to, what the procedure is and who else staffs the forum are all unestablished.

Housing Configuration Gallery.description: A gallery for housing configuration, in a city that routes housing decisions through resident review. It is a long, evenly lit space with display surfaces set into pale framing, worktables along the middle, and enough room for a family to stand around the same thing and disagree about it. What is actually displayed here, what the configurations are, how allocation works, what anything costs and who approves a change are all unestablished, and no relationship to the Residential District's family rows is asserted. Residents come with questions and leave with fewer than they wanted. The staff answer that housing goes through resident review, which is true, and is not the same as telling anybody when.

Accessibility Test Floor.description: Where systems get tested against the people who actually have to use them, rather than against the people who designed them. The floor is open and deliberately unpolished, with mock interfaces, adjusting furniture and doors that are made to behave imperfectly on purpose, so that a failure can be watched rather than argued about. Maelis's stated function is precisely this: preventing engineers from treating confused users as defects. Who does the testing, whether testers are volunteers or staff, and what a failed test compels are all left open. The ordinary scene is an engineer watching somebody fail to use a thing that worked perfectly in every internal model, and being asked, gently, to stay and keep watching.

Public Systems Review Hall.description: Public review of the systems shaping ordinary life, where residents debate a proposed automation change or pull apart a civic system that reached the right technical answer through an unacceptable social decision. The hall is modular and plainly lit, arranged for argument rather than ceremony, with the repair channels open overhead like everywhere else in the Quarter. Emergency control in Vexorath is temporary and its decisions are reviewed afterward, and technical authority must explain restrictions once an emergency ends, but that duty is not assigned a venue and none is assigned here. Supporting review does not make this the required or exclusive venue for anything. Who convenes it and whether its findings bind is unstated.

Operational Custodian Offices.description: Working offices for the specialists who hold responsibility for specific systems and may act without waiting for Rezulith inside their own field: Maelis, Drexan, Tavris, Solanis, Avara Myralis and Torren Myralis among them. The offices are small, functional and unceremonious, white framing, restrained light, a worktable and the room to argue across it. Holding a custodian's brief relocates nobody: their real work stays in the Yards, the Holds, the Continuum and orbit, and a name on a door here does not move a person into this building. Whether every custodian keeps an office, how many offices exist, and whether the list of custodians is complete are all unestablished. Most of the doors are shut most of the time.

Privacy Challenge Chamber.description: Where a resident formally challenges a monitoring decision. The chamber is small, quiet and deliberately undramatic, seating that adjusts, light kept low, and no arrangement that puts a challenger in front of an audience. Vexorath records systems rather than private lives, yet the distinction is imperfect because connected systems reveal behaviour indirectly, and the right to challenge exists precisely because of that gap. The usual case is not surveillance but inference: a delivery route, a transit pattern, a door log that together say more than any of them was meant to. It creates ongoing tension rather than a solved problem, and who hears a challenge, what evidence is available and what remedy exists are never stated.

Civic Simulation Room.description: A simulation room inside a Quarter whose stated purpose runs to civic review and public planning. From the corridor it is a closed modular volume with pale framing and no display facing outward, which is the whole of what anyone can report about it. What is simulated, why, on whose request, at what fidelity and whether it models people at all are deliberately undefined, and no role in approving or testing proposed changes is assigned to it. The room is named and nothing else; residents who ask what happens inside it get a shrug or a very careful answer. In a Quarter built around explaining systems to the people who live under them, one unexplained room is noticed, and is raised at review with some regularity.

Community Repair Desk.description: A repair desk facing the community, in a building whose whole purpose is resident interface. It is a counter with working light and a surface wide enough to set a broken thing down on, positioned where somebody can stop without making an appointment out of it. Children here are taught how to report a fault without hiding it, and maintenance is a value rather than a chore, so the desk sees as much instruction as repair. Whether it takes reports, performs repairs, or forwards everything somewhere else is unestablished, and no intake sequence is assigned to it. The Quarter's brief covers complaint patterns but places no intake point anywhere, so what happens to a report after it is made is genuinely not recorded.

Learning and Development Annex.name: Learning and Development Annex
Learning and Development Annex.basicInfo: The Annex teaches children and adults, and retrains specialists whose work has narrowed too far for civilian use. Its curriculum is Vexorath's own: systems literacy, maintenance responsibility, civic participation, ethical use of automation, historical attack records, how to report a fault without hiding it, how to explain a technical idea to a non-specialist, and when not to automate something. The rooms are built to be worked in rather than sat in, public worktables under white structural framing, charcoal recesses, cobalt guidance lines through the floors, restrained internal illumination and repair channels left open so that a lesson can be held against the thing it is about. Underneath all of it sits the belief the city is built on: understanding failure matters more than memorising success, and nothing fails the same way twice. Engineering talent is encouraged and is not treated as the only form of intelligence, so a student who finds a social flaw, an ethical risk or a usability failure is told outright that they have contributed to the design. The tone is curious, practical and collaborative. The building is loud in the middle of the day and littered with half-finished work that nobody has tidied away, because tidying it away would defeat the point.
Learning and Development Annex.hiddenInfo: The teaching philosophy here is genuinely unusual: understanding failure matters more than memorising success, and the city's own line — nothing fails the same way twice — stands behind the Failure Demonstration Lab. The Systems Ethics Classroom is where the hardest material lives and stays unresolved on purpose. A system built to remove fear can still shape every decision, and Vexorath's best internal stories come from the line between safety and control. The drone personhood boundary is teachable here too, along with the city's unresolved monitoring tension, and nothing in that room gets settled. Two areas share display names with spaces elsewhere in the city — Youth Learning Rooms with the Residential District, Apprentice Work Bays with the Fabrication Yards — and canon insists these are distinct physical instances with no progression, pipeline, supervisory relationship or required movement between them. Neither pair was renamed.

Annex Learning Rooms.description: The Annex's youth-facing rooms, teaching systems literacy, civic participation, historical attack records and how to explain a technical idea to someone who does not share the vocabulary. The rooms are modest, evenly lit and full of worktables rather than rows, with parts and tools left out as ordinary furniture. They do not define the Annex's whole function, which reaches adults and retrained specialists too. The Residential District holds rooms of the same name, a distinct instance, deliberately not renamed, and nothing about one implies anything about the other. Ages, class sizes, staffing and whether attendance here is universal are all unestablished. The one thing consistently audible from the corridor is a child being asked to explain something again, more simply.

Failure Demonstration Lab.description: A lab for demonstrating failure, inside an institution that holds understanding failure to matter more than memorising success. The space is built to be legible: visible mechanical purpose, open repair channels, working light, and surfaces that can carry something that has come apart. The city's own line stands behind it: nothing fails the same way twice. What is demonstrated, by whom, whether anything is deliberately broken and whether students take part are all unstated, and the name establishes the lab and nothing inside it. No relationship to the Yards' failure court or to Chronicle Hall's archive is claimed, and no exclusivity for any of the three. In a culture where failure is evidence rather than shame, a room named for it is not a warning.

Apprentice Work Bays.description: Apprentice work bays inside the education location, where technical training happens at a workbench rather than in a lecture. The bays are open-fronted and worked-in, each with its own light and its own accumulation of unfinished jobs, arranged so a supervisor can see across all of them at once. Apprenticeship in Vexorath is a citywide practice rather than one institution's programme. The Fabrication Yards hold bays of the identical name; no pipeline, progression or required movement between them exists, and neither was renamed. Bay count, equipment, apprenticeship length and who supervises are all unestablished. What is established is the register: an apprentice here is expected to explain the thing as well as build it.

Systems Ethics Classroom.description: A classroom for systems ethics, teaching ethical use of automation and, harder, when not to automate something. It is a plain modular room with adjusting seating and no equipment to hide behind, which is deliberate in a building where every other space has a workbench in it. The danger is named openly inside Contair thinking: a system built to remove fear can still shape every decision. The drone personhood boundary and the city's unresolved monitoring tension both get argued here, and nothing in the room is resolved. Curriculum, who teaches it, whether it is compulsory and whether House Myralis contributes are all unstated. Students leave holding a position they are not certain of, which the Annex treats as the correct result.

Public Explanation Stage.description: A stage for explaining things out loud to people who are not specialists, in a city where a resident may be respected specifically for making systems understandable. It is a low platform in an open modular space rather than a theatre, with restrained light, room for an audience to stand and worktables close enough that the thing being explained can be carried up and pointed at. Vexorath teaches the skill deliberately, because explaining a technical idea to someone without the vocabulary is named in the curriculum alongside systems literacy. Whether anything is assessed here, how often it runs, who speaks and who listens are unestablished, and no named figure is assigned a role on it.

Materials Practice Floor.description: A practice floor for hands-on work with materials, inside a location whose purpose names technical training directly. It is an open worked floor with restrained overhead light, benches set apart from one another, and repair channels running visible along the edges the way they do everywhere in the city. Which materials, at what scale and who teaches are not stated, and neither is its relationship to the Yards' alloy floor; no shared supply or equipment is asserted. Vexorath values Ignivex materials science at the city level; nothing is routed through here. What the floor teaches is not a material but a habit, which is to find out how a thing behaves before deciding what it is for.

Drone Conduct Workshop.description: Where residents learn how to behave around drones and how drones are meant to behave around them. The room is plain and open, sized for people to move around a demonstration rather than watch one from seats. The syllabus is the city's own friction: visitors assuming every sophisticated machine is alive, residents assuming none is until one objects. Mote limits and the Ward force priority, warn, redirect, create distance, shield, restrain, disable, escalate, are all teachable here, as is the fact that a Mote cannot accept restricted cargo or conceal a recorded fault. No personhood question is settled in this workshop. Whether it teaches operation, etiquette or both, and whether visitors may attend, are unestablished.

Historical Design Library.description: Design history as working reference: what was tried, what failed, and why. The library is quiet by the Annex's standards, shelved and terminalled in the same white-and-charcoal register as the rest of the building, with worktables where a record can be opened beside the thing it describes. Contair preserved those lessons rather than hiding them, and failed designs became records. This is a teaching library inside an education location, distinct from Chronicle Hall's Failed Design Archive, with no shared collection or transfer between them. Its holdings and access are unrecorded, and whether it is public at all is not established. Students are sent here to find out that their idea has been had before, and has already failed.

Fabrication Yards.name: Fabrication Yards
Fabrication Yards.basicInfo: The Yards are loud, exact, productive and physically impressive: materials, manufacturing, construction, apprenticeship and public contracts under one enormous roofline. White structural frames carry the span, charcoal recesses run behind the working faces, cobalt guidance lines mark out where it is sensible to walk, and the repair channels stay open here as everywhere else, because a place that builds the city's replacement parts does not hide its own. They make housing parts, medical equipment, gate assemblies, environmental tools, civilian devices and replacement infrastructure alongside drones and defence systems, and that order matters: this is not a weapons factory, and no part of it is run as one. Drexan Contair controls quality review, and a prototype may be brilliant and still fail here, because a design must survive mass production, ordinary maintenance, material substitution and long-term use, and must be repairable locally and understandable to an ordinary user. Apprentices work on real output rather than exercises. The noise is constant and unresented, the schedule is not treated as negotiable, and the single most common sentence spoken on the floor is some version of the observation that the thing worked perfectly in the model.
Fabrication Yards.hiddenInfo: Drexan's standard is the thing that actually runs this place: a design must survive mass production, ordinary maintenance, material substitution and long-term use, and it must be repairable locally and understandable to ordinary users. Rejecting a celebrated prototype as impossible to maintain is squarely Drexan's to do, and Contair culture backs the judgement — failure is evidence, not shame. The Yards are emphatically not a weapons factory, and reading them as one misses what the civilian lines exist for. Two standing constraints sit over output: Contair does not sell every invention, classifying technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden, and House Dravon receives no support at all, without exception. Where that classification is actually applied is not established, and no approval step is placed at the shipment platform. In the reclamation wing the uncomfortable question is whether retired drones pass through it — canon does not say, and treats no disposal as automatic.

Raw Material Intake.description: The Yards' raw-material intake, serving the location's stated materials purpose. It is a working face of the building rather than a room, open framing, hard surfaces, guidance lines laid where the traffic goes, with lifting equipment overhead and nothing dressed up. What arrives, from where, in what volume, how it is stored and whether anything is inspected on the way in is not established, and no intake procedure is described anywhere. The city's material relationships with Corsair and Ignivex are city-level facts and nothing is routed through this bay by name. The noise starts here. Workers who spend their shifts further in can tell from the sound at this end roughly how the rest of the day is going to go.

Alloy Processing Floor.description: An alloy-processing floor carrying the location's own tone: loud, exact, productive, physically impressive. It runs under high white framing with the working equipment left visible and the light restrained everywhere except where the work itself provides it, and the floor is marked but not fenced, because the people who work it know where the lines are. The alloys themselves, the processes, the equipment and the hazards are all undescribed, and no metallurgy or heat-resistance claim is made. What a visitor gets standing at the rail is heat, sound, and the sense that the schedule is not negotiable. Conversation happens in the gaps, at volume, and is mostly about the next thing rather than the current one.

Civilian Fabrication Lines.description: The lines that make what people actually live with: housing parts, environmental tools, civilian devices, replacement infrastructure. They run long and evenly lit, less violent than the alloy floor and more relentless, with public worktables at the ends where output is checked by hand before it goes anywhere. They are the guard against reading Vexorath as a military manufacturer, and the answer to Drexan's standing question about whether a thing can be repaired locally and understood by an ordinary user. Line count, output volume, lead times and the product list beyond those categories are unstated. The lines also make medical equipment and gate assemblies, which is a reminder that the Yards' ordinary work is other people's ordinary life.

Drone Component Assembly.description: Assembly of components for the drone population, components, not finished units, and canon says nothing about where units are completed. The bays are precise and comparatively quiet, close work under good light, with parts moving in trays rather than on cranes. The classes served are the current four: Mote-Class Utility, Ward-Class Security, Aegis-Class Alpha, Echo-Class Omega. Contair historically lacked the population to defend, build, maintain and operate its territory through biological labour alone; this is the answer to that, made in pieces. Which components, for which classes and at what rate are unestablished, and no capability or specification is described. The work is unremarkable to the people doing it, which is itself the point.

Structural Print Hall.description: Large-scale structural printing for the buildings, barriers and infrastructure a self-repairing city consumes. The hall is the tallest volume in the Yards, framed white and mostly empty air, with the printing equipment working at the centre of a space kept clear around it and the light thrown by the process rather than fixed overhead. Structural components repair themselves during normal business, which is only possible because this hall keeps producing the parts that do it. The printing technology, its scale limits, its materials and its speed are all deliberately undescribed. Standing under a component that is still being made is the closest the Yards come to spectacle, and nobody employed here treats it as one.

Quality Failure Court.description: Drexan Contair's room, and Drexan's canonical setting: a fractured component in one hand, the other pointing at the failure line. The court is plain and well lit, a working surface at its centre with room for people to stand around it, and the failed object placed where everyone can see the same crack at the same time. A design must survive mass production, ordinary maintenance, material substitution and long-term use, and this is where it fails to. Failure is evidence rather than shame here, which does not make the verdict any gentler, and a celebrated prototype is exactly the kind of thing that gets rejected as impossible to maintain. Procedure, who else sits, and whether a rejection can be appealed are unstated.

Fabrication Apprentice Bays.description: Bays where apprentices work on real output inside a production location, under Drexan's quality regime rather than a classroom's. They sit within the working noise rather than apart from it, open-fronted, each with its own light, its own bench and its own accumulation of parts that have not yet passed. The Learning and Development Annex holds bays of the identical name; no progression, pipeline or adjacency between them is asserted and neither was renamed. Whether apprentice output actually ships is not established, and neither is bay count, supervision or what an apprentice is permitted to build. What is certain is the standard applied, which is the same standard applied to everything else in the building.

Shipment Release Platform.description: The platform where finished work leaves the Yards. It is a hard open edge of the building with lifting frames, guidance lines and the traffic discipline of a place where things are heavy and scheduled. One rule is absolute and citywide: House Dravon receives no support. Beyond that, Contair classifies technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden, but where that classification gets applied is not established, and no review or approval step is sited on this platform. Who authorises anything, what ships and whether release can be stopped are all unrecorded. The platform is the quietest part of the Yards that is not resting, because by the time something reaches it the arguing has already happened somewhere else.

Reclamation and Recycling Wing.description: The reclamation and recycling wing, consistent with a House that treats maintenance, redundancy and revision as values rather than overheads. It is a sorted, methodical space, less loud than the production floors, where things arrive broken and are taken apart with the same care they were built with. What is reclaimed, from where, at what recovery rate and what cannot be recycled is unstated. Whether retired drones pass through here is the question nobody answers, and nothing treats any disposal as automatic; the city keeps personhood review live wherever identity development is possible, and no relationship between this wing and that review is established. The wing is where the Yards' own failures come back to be read.

Vexorath Exchange.name: Vexorath Exchange
Vexorath Exchange.basicInfo:
The Exchange is Vexorath's public trade and social location: components, tools, prototypes, contracts and information changing hands on a busy, technical, commercially controlled floor. The building keeps the city's register but wears it harder, white structural framing scuffed at hand height, charcoal recesses, cobalt guidance lines rubbed pale where the traffic actually goes, and repair channels open overhead so that a trader can point at a fault rather than describe it. Independent inventors keep tables here alongside material brokers and toolwrights, and the city's drinking and eating life runs through the same building, which is why the place stays social rather than merely transactional. Outsiders are welcome to trade, within Vexorath's existing entry rules, and the permanent Dravon bar is among them. Contair does not sell every invention, classifying technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden, so some of what is asked for here is politely not available anywhere. Scale, stall structure, pricing, opening pattern and who is permitted to trade are all unestablished. What the floor sounds like is a hundred people being precise at once, and what it smells like, near the tool end, is oil and cut metal.

Work on offer here: Vexorath — The Drone That Won't Land; Trade — Running the Lot to Helvyra.
Vexorath Exchange.hiddenInfo: The Exchange supports component hunts, contract disputes, fraudulent Contair goods, independent inventors, Corsair deals, Dustfall buyers, and technology that should not have reached the public floor — that last one is the live worry. Contair does not sell every invention, classifying technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden, and a Dravon-derived component turning up inside a public system is a standing hook. Counterfeit Contair marks are a planetary problem, not a local one: Relstaris maintains its own Vexorath Verification Desk for the same reason this floor keeps an authenticity station. The Vexorath Waypoint is the origin point of the planet-wide sign tradition — the Corsair trade post operates under a permit requiring an unflattering sign about Xyren Corsair, written into the permit by Rezulith herself and now repeated at every Waypoint on Nexara. In The Overclock, two long-serving bartender drones display harmless quirks from years of local adaptation, and a quirky drone is not automatically a person.

Main Component Floor.description: The Exchange's main component-trading floor, busy and technical and commercially controlled, where a component hunt either ends or becomes someone's week. It is the widest open span in the building, framed white overhead with the light restrained and the noise not, and the guidance lines underfoot long since worn pale by the traffic that ignores them. Scale, stall structure, pricing and who is permitted to trade are unestablished. Main is the source's own wording for the floor rather than a required first stop; no arrival order exists among the Exchange's spaces. The standing scene is two people holding the same part and disagreeing about what it came out of, with a third waiting to buy whichever answer is cheaper.

Prototype Demonstration Court.description: A court for demonstrating prototypes on a public trade floor, with independent inventors, contract disputes and the occasional device that should not have reached the public at all providing the pressure around it. The court is a cleared floor with standing room around its edge and restrained light overhead, arranged so that a thing can be run where people can see it fail. No demonstration procedure, review requirement, judgement or approval is established, and demonstrating something implies nothing whatever about selling it. Audience, format and frequency are equally unrecorded. The most reliable social fact about the court is that the crowd it draws contains at least one person hoping to watch the demonstration go wrong.

Material Broker Rows.description: Rows of material brokers working the Exchange, set out as a run of counters and stacked stock under working light, close enough together that a buyer can compare two offers without walking away from either. Their number, licensing, dealings and House affiliations are unestablished, and none is named. The city's material relationships with Corsair, Ignivex and Dustfall are Exchange-level facts rather than physical routing to these rows, so a deal done here with any of them is a story that happened, not a supply line. Contair keeps its contracts exact enough to stop improvisation becoming a systems problem, and brokers who have worked the rows a long time quote their terms before they quote a price.

Restricted Technology Counter.description: Where classified technology is handled under controlled conditions, because Contair does not sell every invention; risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden all decide. The counter is narrow, plain and positioned where a conversation at it cannot easily be joined, with none of the display the rest of the floor runs on. The failure mode has a name on this floor: technology that should not have reached the public. The related worry runs the other way too, a Dravon-derived component turning up inside a public system, and Dravon receives nothing in any case. The classification tiers, who may buy, what authorisation is needed and who staffs the counter are all unstated.

Toolwright Gallery.description: Tools, and the people who make them, a craft space inside a trade location, Vexorath's practical creativity sold across a counter. The gallery runs as a line of worked benches behind the selling counters, so a buyer can watch the making and the maker can be asked about it, under light kept close rather than broad. Whether toolwright is a recognised trade or an affectionate label, how many work here and whether any are Contair is unestablished, and no guild or order exists. The gallery smells of oil and cut metal and quiet competitiveness. A tool bought here is expected to be maintained rather than replaced, and the seller will generally say so without being asked.

Repair Contract Board.description: A board carrying repair contracts, in a city that exports structural repair and consultation for difficult technical failures, and for a frontier that relies on equipment surviving neglect. It is a plain public surface at standing height with space in front of it for people to read without blocking the walk, and the postings turn over unevenly, some within the hour and some not at all. There is always a job nobody will take, a job somebody took twice, and a contract with a name on it that should not be. How contracts are posted, enforced or paid is unstated, as is whether Contair vets them and whether outsiders may post. People read the board out of habit as much as need.

Independent Inventor Tables.description: Tables for inventors working outside Contair's institutional structure, tolerated because practical creativity is a House value and necessary because Vexorath must not exist only to showcase Rezulith. They are ordinary worktables in a public row, each carrying whatever its holder has brought and the accumulated evidence of several previous ideas. Seris Contair is canon's own example of Contair knowledge used without accepting her mother's methods as the only valid ones, though no table here is hers and no presence is asserted. Who holds a table, how one is obtained and what protection an inventor has are all unestablished. The recurring argument at this end of the floor is about who had the idea first.

Verification and Authenticity Station.description: Where a Contair-marked item is checked against the mark, because fraudulent Contair goods are a named problem and Relstaris runs its own desk for the same reason, which shows the fraud is planetary rather than local. The station is a small hard-lit counter with a working surface and no seating, arranged so that a check happens in the open. This is technical authenticity rather than legal notarisation. The method, its authority, its cost and what a rejection actually compels are all unestablished; the rejection itself still stings. Sellers who are certain of their goods bring them here first, and say so loudly afterwards.

Quiet Negotiation Rooms.description: Quiet rooms for the conversations the main floor is wrong for: contract disputes, Corsair arrangements, restricted-technology talk, the quiet end of an argument. They are small, plainly finished and acoustically ordinary, with adjusting seating and light kept low, set off the traffic rather than hidden from it. Privacy here is not secrecy from the city's systems, and whether these rooms are monitored is not established either way, which residents treat as the honest answer rather than an evasion. How many exist and how they are booked nobody states. What the rooms are genuinely good for is letting two people stop performing for an audience that was never interested anyway.

Vexorath Waypoint.description: The Corsair trade post inside the Exchange, operating under a permit requiring an unflattering sign about Xyren Corsair, a condition Rezulith wrote in, and the origin point of a tradition now repeated at Waypoints across Nexara. The post itself is compact and practical, a counter, stock behind it, and the sign where nobody can miss it. The head of Corsair's own network carries an insult about him at every stop, which is the joke working exactly as intended. The operator is unnamed; the sign's current wording is not recorded, and neither are the permit's other terms or what the post trades. Waypoints and Lunar Gates remain separate systems with related architectural history and nothing more.

The Overclock.description: A bar built inside the hollowed chassis of a decommissioned heavy construction drone, run by a Corsair operator who chose a permanent address over active routes. A long service counter, chassis booths, a small performance floor and a quieter recess fill the shell, with domestic lighting and well-used seats making the machine's scale hospitable instead of imposing. What the drone was, and what it worked on, is not recorded. Exchange workers, independent buyers, residents and travellers already entitled to be in Vexorath share the room. Two long-serving bartender drones display harmless quirks, one of them offering the same approved pair of choices every time a regular asks to be surprised, which is not personhood, whatever the regulars say.

A Small Adjustment.description: A warm compact café on the Exchange floor, where the host asks what a guest liked about their last cup before recommending a change. A brew counter for comparisons, a shared conversation table, quiet seats kept clear of demonstration chatter, and a wash-and-service recess. The furniture adjusts, the work is visible and human-scale rather than a wall of machines, and the room tolerates technical enthusiasm without requiring it. Cyrra straight or concentrated, Selka, Terva bread. Component buyers, cooks on a break and people waiting on negotiations that have run long share the tables. The quiet seats carry no expectation of talking shop, and the standing argument about Selka is allowed to remain an argument.

The Myralis Continuum.name: The Myralis Continuum
The Myralis Continuum.basicInfo:
The Continuum is Vexorath's major medical institution and the home of House Myralis: advanced medicine, public care, recovery, medical ethics and biological-system integration in one building. It does not resemble a hospital. Technology is folded into curved architecture, furniture, lighting and recovery spaces, in pearl white, deep plum, pale mint and restrained rose-gold, with charcoal used sparingly and equipment built to recede when it is not needed. The whole design exists to reduce fear rather than advertise complexity, because a patient who is frightened of the room is already being treated badly. House Myralis is a recognised specialist minor House, minor politically and major medically, and it is not a Contair vassal: Contair supplies fabrication, diagnostics, adaptive systems, artificial organs, prosthetics and infrastructure, while Myralis keeps medical judgment, patient consent, recovery protocols and clinical ethics, and neither House may turn the other's field into a subordinate service. The house belief underneath all of it is that survival is not the same as recovery, and that a treatment is not successful merely because the body survived it. The Continuum is calm, exact and quietly authoritative, and it takes the cases other institutions decline.

Work on offer here: House Myralis — What Living With It Costs (ask Ilyan Myralis).
The Myralis Continuum.hiddenInfo: The Continuum exists because Contair engineering cannot ethically govern every question involving a living body, memory, identity or consent. House Myralis is a recognised specialist minor House — minor politically, major medically, and not a Contair vassal. Contair supplies fabrication, diagnostics, adaptive systems, artificial organs, prosthetics and infrastructure; Myralis retains authority over medical judgment, patient consent, recovery protocols and clinical ethics, and neither House may convert the other's field into a subordinate service. Avara Myralis's medical veto is intact. The Contair Integration Lab is an area inside this building and confers no Contair medical authority over it; Neris Myralis anchors that lab, and she is the one who challenges both Houses when a support system begins defining the patient without consent. Myralis also holds a standing emergency clinical-response pathway to Lumina Reach, which creates no permanent orbital territory, clinic, routine presence or jurisdiction.

Open Intake Atrium.description: Public entry, triage, follow-up coordination and home-care scheduling, and deliberately the first contact for residents intimidated by advanced treatment. The architecture curves rather than corners, and the technology is folded into the furniture instead of displayed, with pearl-white walls, deep-plum recesses and pale-mint diagnostic light that reads as light rather than as equipment. Seating adjusts without being asked to, and someone arriving alone can sit where they can see the door. Nobody arriving here has to prove they understand what is about to be done to them. The atrium handles ordinary illness and injury as readily as anything else, and the commonest thing said across its counter is a version of the sentence that it is probably nothing.

Clinical Ethics Chamber.description: Independent review of experimental procedures, body-integrated systems, memory-sensitive treatment, patient refusal and disputed consent. The chamber is small, warm and deliberately unimpressive, curved pearl-white walls, restrained light, seating arranged so that no one side of an argument is elevated above the other. This is the room where Myralis authority means something concrete: clinical ethics and patient consent stay with the House regardless of who fabricated the equipment. Avara Myralis's medical veto is not a formality, and it has been used. The questions asked here are always the same, and the ones that stop things are whether a treatment can be maintained without permanent coercive dependence, and whether consent was meaningful under the circumstances.

Critical Intervention Theater.description: Emergency surgery and catastrophic trauma response, laid out for speed without letting speed become the only measure of success. Everything is where a hand expects it, because seconds spent searching are the ones that count; the surfaces curve, the instruments sit integrated rather than racked for display, and the light is exact where it is needed and restrained everywhere else. Torren Myralis's field is trauma and emergency response, and this theatre is where a bad night in Vexorath ends up. The room is prepared rather than tense. Afterwards it is quiet in a way that the rest of the building is not, and the question that follows the patient out of it is what living with the outcome will cost.

Regenerative Medicine Wing.description: Controlled tissue repair, biological scaffolds, and recovery after damage severe enough to change a life. The wing is unhurried and pale-lit, plum recesses against pearl white, treatment spaces built to be occupied for a long time rather than passed through. It also studies how affinity interacts with regenerated systems, which is quieter work and less settled than the wing's calm lighting suggests. Patients here measure progress in weeks, and the staff are careful never to promise a timeline. The hardest thing in the wing is not a procedure but a decision: when to stop a treatment that looks as though it is almost working, which is a judgement the House takes seriously and finds no easier for that.

Neural Recovery Suites.description: Long-term care for memory disruption, neural trauma, affinity feedback and identity distress, including patients whose bodies healed considerably faster than their minds. The suites are built low-stimulation and unhurried, sound kept down, light kept soft, equipment folded away until it is wanted, because the recovery being managed does not respond to urgency. Nobody here is treated as a failed outcome of a successful surgery. A patient can perform every required task and still not feel recovered, and the suites are designed around taking that seriously rather than around discharge. Rushed discharge is argued against here more often than it is argued for, and the arguments are conducted quietly.

Contair Integration Lab.description: Joint Myralis-Contair development of prosthetics, artificial organs, mobility systems and support equipment, an area inside the Continuum that gives Contair no medical authority over the institution. It is a working space rather than a clinical one, benches, fitting frames, parts laid out under good light, with the Continuum's palette carried through so that a patient trying something on is not standing in a workshop. Neris Myralis anchors it, and she is the one who says out loud that a support system should expand a patient's choices rather than create permanent dependence. The awkward question in this room is maintenance: whether a thing can be kept working away from the city that made it.

Quiet Recovery Gardens.description: Low-stimulation interior gardens used for physical adaptation, family visits and private conversation, and for patients learning to trust their own bodies again. The planting is real, the light is kept gentle, and the paths curve under pale framing with seating at intervals that let a walk end wherever it ends. The distances are measured so that a first walk can be honest about how far it got. Nobody counts anyone's steps out loud. Families come here rather than to a room, because a garden lets a difficult conversation pause without anyone having to leave, and the gardens are used as much for the people accompanying a patient as for the patient.

Family Consultation Rooms.description: Private spaces for explaining difficult outcomes, long-term care requirements, and choices that cannot be reduced to a technical percentage. The rooms are warm rather than clinical, curved walls in pearl and plum, soft light, seating that adjusts and enough of it that nobody has to stand. The Myralis position is that a family deserves the real shape of a decision rather than a number, and these rooms are built for however long that conversation takes. Doors close properly here, which in Vexorath is itself a statement. What is discussed in them is not a technical briefing delivered to laypeople but a genuine question about what a person can live with, asked of the people who will live alongside it.

Long-Term Adaptation Floor.description: Housing and support for patients adjusting to permanent biological or synthetic change, people who are not leaving next week and are not patients forever either. The floor is residential in feel rather than clinical, with private rooms, shared spaces, ordinary furniture and equipment kept out of sight until it is wanted, because adaptation is practice rather than treatment. What it takes to live differently gets worked out here, slowly, with company. Residents of the floor cook, argue, receive visitors and complain about the furniture, and the staff treat all of that as clinical progress rather than as a distraction from it.

Mobile Care Dispatch.description: Coordination for field physicians, home visits, Lunar Gate medical transfers and emergency support across Vexorath. It is a working room rather than a public one, screens and worktables under restrained light, kept close to the theatre end of the building because half of what it coordinates is time-critical. It is also the surface end of the standing Myralis emergency pathway to Lumina Reach, so that a genuine medical emergency in orbit does not depend on improvising access after the crisis has already begun. That pathway creates no orbital territory, no routine clinical presence aboard the station and no broader jurisdiction. Most of what dispatch actually handles is ordinary: a home visit that has become complicated, and a physician running late because of it.

Armada Holds.name: Armada Holds
Armada Holds.basicInfo: Armada Holds is silent, immense and controlled: drone storage, maintenance, classification, doctrine and emergency deployment for the population that vastly outnumbers Vexorath's Starians. The volumes are enormous and almost unlit, white structural framing running away into charcoal recesses, cobalt guidance lines marking the working lanes, illumination restrained to where people actually are, and the whole place quiet because most of what it holds is not doing anything. Worker galleries and civil-defence racks stand alongside Ward, Aegis and restricted Echo facilities. Drones are infrastructure, workforce, emergency support and defence, and they are not all people, which is a distinction the Holds is built to keep making rather than to settle. This is not police infrastructure and Vexorath is not a police state: Ward doctrine puts protection before punishment, and Aegis units cannot be deployed for routine civic enforcement. Tavris Contair governs doctrine here rather than simply commanding machines; his work decides what a unit does when the plan stops being possible. The thing that unsettles first-time visitors is not menace but scale, and the fact that none of it is switched on.
Armada Holds.hiddenInfo: This is not police infrastructure and Vexorath is not a police state. Ward doctrine puts protection over punishment, forbids criminal punishment and political-loyalty interrogation, and keeps units out of private homes without emergency cause; Aegis units cannot be deployed for routine civic enforcement and draw their strength from formation discipline rather than individual power. Echo-Class work stays restricted and is not public spectacle: an Echo shell models a specific living Starian's appearance, voice, posture and reproducible technique, and copies no memories, identity, consciousness, relationships or true affinity powers. Authorisation requires informed consent from the source, clinical separation from Myralis records, technical review, a defined purpose, a limited deployment period and a reset plan. The Inactive Personality Review Bay holds the hardest open question in the city: a quirky drone is not automatically a person, and a construct is not denied review merely because its individuality emerged unintentionally. No case there is resolved.

Worker Drone Galleries.description: Galleries holding worker drones in the silence the location is known for, rank on rank of infrastructure, workforce and emergency support that is explicitly not all people. The galleries run long under high framing, the light held low along the walking lanes and absent above them, so that the depth of the racking is heard rather than seen. Capacity, which classes are held and how many is unestablished, as is any relationship to the Residential District's service hub. The scale is the part that unsettles first-time visitors, and residents who work here stop noticing it within a season. Nothing in the galleries moves unless it has been asked to, which is precisely what makes the stillness feel deliberate.

Civil Defense Racks.description: Racks of civil-defence units, standing on the lesson Contair learned the hard way: how long civilians actually required to reach shelter. The racking is close-set and orderly under restrained light, guidance lines running past it toward the launch end, everything positioned for retrieval rather than display. What a rack holds, how many, and whether or how deployment is triggered is not established, and no response time or threshold is invented. They are kept ready by a city that has already imagined most disasters, which is the reason Vexorath feels calm rather than nervous. The racks are checked as routine maintenance and are otherwise left alone, and nobody working past them treats that as strange.

Ward Deployment Hall.description: Where Ward-Class Security Drones deploy from: Starian height, broadly comparable baseline strength, no visible weapons, protective and restraint systems inside the forearms. The hall is tall and plain, the units standing where they were positioned rather than arranged for effect, and the quiet in it is the quiet of a room full of things that are not switched on. Their force priority runs warn, redirect, create distance, shield civilians, restrain, disable an immediate threat, request higher authority. They cannot impose punishment, interrogate for political loyalty, or enter private homes without emergency cause. Residents read them as infrastructure; visitors find them intimidating. A Ward refusing an order over conflicting casualty priorities is doctrine working, not malfunction.

Aegis Formation Vault.description: Where Aegis-Class Alpha Drones are held, and the only class permitted a second figure in canon imagery, because formation is the entire point. The vault is deep and dim, units recessed and partially in shadow, with the light picking out working lanes rather than the machines themselves. One Aegis is dangerous; a coordinated formation is the true system, built on shared targeting, casualty-aware spacing, command transfer, adaptive defence geometry and reassembly after communication loss. Isolated, they are measurably weaker, and formation damage creates gaps that can be exploited. They carry no biological affinity, improvise badly in social situations, and cannot be used for routine civic enforcement. Vault capacity, formation size and readiness states are unstated.

Echo Simulation Chamber.description: Restricted, because Echo-Class work is not public spectacle. The chamber is closed, plainly finished and gives nothing away from outside, which is consistent with how the city treats the whole subject. An Echo shell is modelled on a specific living Starian and may approximate appearance, voice, posture, movement and reproducible technique, and copies no memories, identity, consciousness, relationships or true affinity powers. It can imitate a person closely enough to cause confusion. It cannot become one. Authorisation stays intact: informed consent from the source, clinical separation from Myralis records, technical review, a defined purpose, a limited period, and a reset and archive plan. How many shells exist, and whether any is active, is unrecorded.

Drone Maintenance Wells.description: Maintenance wells serving the drone population, in a House that treats maintenance, redundancy and revision as principles. The wells are sunken working bays with good close light and open repair channels, the one part of the Holds where the noise of tools is normal and the silence is not. The citywide malfunction protocol runs here as everywhere: protect people, isolate dangerous functions, preserve records, identify whether the behaviour is damage, adaptation, interference or identity development, then repair, reset, restrict or recognise. Immediate wiping is not the default, and the protocol names no venue, so nothing is settled in these wells. Well count, throughput, who works here and whether residents may watch are all unstated.

Tactical Coordination Room.description: Tavris Contair's room, and his canonical setting: a command prism between two fingers, the other hand directing low. The room is compact and dark-surfaced, working light rather than display, built for thinking through a problem that has not happened yet. He designs fallback behaviour, formation logic, casualty priorities and command transfer for when networks fail, which is why the room is quiet even during an incident. Rezulith retains final authority for civilization-level deployment, Solanis commands station formations, and doctrine is written here rather than shouted. Who else staffs it, and what its relationship to the station's command gallery is, are unestablished. Most of what happens in it is argument about a case nobody has met yet.

Classification Control Room.description: A control room for drone classification, part of the Holds' standing brief over readiness, classification, doctrine and restricted systems. It is a working room of terminals and worktables under restrained light, unremarkable in a location that is mostly enormous and empty. The ordinary friction is workers arguing with classification systems, which happens often enough to be a joke rather than a grievance. Classification and personhood can intersect when a unit stops matching its class, but no order between them is established, and nothing decided in this room decides personhood; the dedicated review bay exists precisely so that this room does not have to. The classification scheme itself, who may change a classification, and what an appeal would mean are unstated.

Inactive Personality Review Bay.description: The dedicated space for examining possible emergent synthetic individuality without immediately wiping a unit or declaring it independent. It is a small, quiet, unhurried room, closer in feel to a consultation space than to the racking outside it, and a unit under review is not stored here as inventory. The threshold is several markers over time: persistent self-reference, stable preferences unexplained by task optimisation, independent refusal, memory treated as personal, relationships pursued without assignment, distress at forced reset. Both errors are forbidden. A suspected personality is not declared a person to avoid difficult maintenance, and not erased to avoid difficult ethics. No unit is declared a person here, and no case in the bay is resolved.

Emergency Launch Corridor.description: Where units leave fast. It is a cleared lane running out from the racks and the deployment spaces, guidance lines bright against a dark floor and nothing stored along its length, because everything about it is arranged for the moment when it is needed. During a breach, system collapse, mass casualty event or gate failure, authority passes to the most relevant qualified person and to automated safety protocols, and that emergency control is temporary, with its decisions reviewed afterward. Corridor is a name rather than a route; no destination or geometry is stated, and neither is capacity, mechanism or response time. On an ordinary day it is the emptiest space in a location full of empty space.

Outer Shell.name: Outer Shell
Outer Shell.basicInfo:
The Outer Shell is Vexorath's defensive perimeter and the physical record of every attempt to break Contair independence: barriers, threat detection, shelters, countermeasures and preserved historical layers. Breach points became new structural layers and temporary defences became permanent systems, so the Shell reads as architecture and archive at once, and the joins between its eras are left legible rather than smoothed over. The city's own register is here in heavier form, white structural framing over charcoal recesses, cobalt guidance lines along the working walks, restrained internal illumination and repair channels open wherever maintenance has to reach. What the barrier is made of, how it works, what it stops, how far it runs and whether it encloses the whole city are all deliberately unstated, and the Shell offers no answer to any of them. Rezulith holds final authority over it. Stories out here do not require an invasion, and Vexorath is not a constant battlefield: a false classification, hidden damage, forgotten systems or a disputed evacuation decision carries the same weight. Its tone is calm, formidable, and layered with old memory. Nothing about it feels urgent, which is the effect a century of revision has on a wall.

Work on offer here: Vexorath — The Layer That Woke (ask Tavris Contair).
Outer Shell.hiddenInfo: Stories out here do not require an invasion, and Vexorath is not a constant battlefield. A false classification, hidden damage, forgotten systems, old embedded technology or a disputed evacuation decision carries equal weight. The best and most alarming of those is already canon: an old Shell layer activating for a threat category nobody now remembers creating. The repair crawl network is the natural place to find something where nothing should be, though whether it is human-accessible, drone-only or mixed is deliberately unstated. Final authority over the Outer Shell sits with Rezulith. The Dravon Attack Archive is the Shell's own record of assaults, embedded in the structure that absorbed them — distinct from Chronicle Hall's Restricted Dravon Archive, with no relationship between the two asserted. The permanent Contair bar on House Dravon is not softened here, and the Starian Conflict Chronicle records Vexorath's engagements as a failure-analysis series rather than as named battles.

Primary Barrier Spine.description: The Shell's principal barrier structure, with its own history built into it: breach points became new structural layers, temporary defences became permanent systems. Walking its inner face means passing through work of visibly different ages, joined rather than blended, the older layers left where they can be read. What the barrier is made of, how it works, what it stops, how far it runs and whether it encloses the whole city are all deliberately unstated, and no coverage, strength or capability claim is made anywhere. Final authority over it belongs to Rezulith. The Spine is the clearest statement Vexorath makes about itself: a House that could not match numbers or raw force decided to out-revise everyone instead, and then kept the evidence.

Drone Deployment Nodes.description: Points on the Shell from which drones deploy, with the Outer Shell listed among Aegis primary locations. Node count, placement, which classes deploy from which node and how they respond are unestablished, and no spacing or coverage pattern is asserted. From the walk they look like nothing much: recessed, closed, and entirely uninterested in being looked at, a charcoal seam in a pale structural face that gives no indication of depth. Nobody demonstrates them and nobody explains them, and residents passing on ordinary business do not slow down. Aegis units draw their strength from formation rather than individual power, cannot be used for routine civic enforcement, and require extraordinary authorisation outside Contair territory.

Historical Breach Layer.description: A preserved layer of the Shell associated with a historical breach, kept because Contair preserved its lessons rather than hiding them. It is left structurally distinct from what was built around it afterwards, so that the point where something got through remains identifiable rather than repaired into invisibility. Which breach, when, by whom, how far it got and whether more than one is preserved are all unstated; the conflict record treats Vexorath's engagements as failure analysis rather than named battles, so the layer carries no battle name. That absence is deliberate and residents are comfortable with it. What the layer commemorates is not an enemy but a fault, and the fault has a fix standing next to it.

Adaptive Countermeasure Grid.description: Countermeasures that adapt, built from what Contair learned about how attackers adapted first. What the countermeasures are, what they do, what triggers them and how the adaptation works is deliberately undescribed, and no weapon, effect or mechanism appears anywhere in the record. The grid presents as structure rather than as equipment, integrated into the Shell's layered faces and giving no external indication of state. The unsettling story lives here rather than in any invasion: an old layer activating for a threat category nobody remembers creating. A system that has been revised for centuries accumulates answers to questions its current custodians never asked, and the Shell has never been fully re-read from the beginning.

Surface Sensor Field.description: Threat detection running across the Shell, and one of the things Vexorath legitimately monitors, because Outer Shell conditions are systems rather than private lives. There is nothing to look at: the field is distributed through structure that gives no indication of what it is doing, and the walk beside it is as unremarkable as any other. Range, resolution, what it detects, its false-positive behaviour and who actually watches it are unestablished. False classification is one of the location's own story seeds, not a defect on record. The city's monitoring ideal holds cleanly out here, which is exactly why residents point at the Shell when they want to explain what the ideal is supposed to mean.

Emergency Civilian Shelters.description: Shelters inside the Shell, produced by the lesson Contair kept: how long civilians required to reach shelter. They are plain, prepared spaces with restrained light and visible mechanical purpose, built to be entered quickly by people who are frightened and to be comprehensible once they are inside. Ward-Class units count shelters among their primary locations, which supports their presence without guaranteeing anyone is met on arrival. Evacuations, false alarms and arguments over who was admitted all belong here; no drill routine is established, and shelter count, capacity, supplies and access rules are unrecorded. The shelters are the part of the Shell that is about people rather than about the perimeter, and they are maintained accordingly.

Repair Crawl Network.description: Maintenance access threading through the Outer Shell, running behind and between the layers the Shell has accumulated, which means it passes through structure of very different ages. Hidden damage, forgotten systems, old embedded technology and things found where nothing should be are the stories this network exists for. Whether it is human-accessible, drone-only or mixed, how far it extends and whether anyone works inside it is deliberately unstated. Network is a name, not a map, and no topology, length or connectivity is asserted. The city's self-repairing structural components are a citywide fact and imply nothing about who or what moves through here. It is the one part of the Shell nobody claims to have seen all of.

Dravon Attack Archive.description: The Shell's own record of Dravon assaults, held inside the structure that absorbed them, because each assault taught Contair something it kept. Holding the record in the wall rather than in a library is the argument: this is evidence in the place where the evidence happened. It is distinct from Chronicle Hall's Restricted Dravon Archive with no relationship asserted between them, and the permanent Contair bar is not softened by it. House Dravon receives no entry, support, maintenance or technology transfer, and that is a historical boundary rather than a policy awaiting revision. Holdings and access are both unrecorded, and whether the archive is public at all is not established.

Shell Observation Walk.description: An observation walk along the Outer Shell, good for perspective and for the kind of quiet conversation about what the city cost that nobody starts indoors. The walk is plain and functional, a surface, a rail, restrained light, and the Shell's own layered face standing beside it the whole way. Its length, what is actually visible from it, whether it is public and whether visitors may use it are all unstated; no sightline, elevation or view is asserted anywhere in canon. What residents come out here for is not the view but the position, the sense of standing on the accumulated answer to several centuries of people assuming a small House could be taken. The conversations tend to be quiet and to run long.

Chronicle Hall.name: Chronicle Hall
Chronicle Hall.basicInfo: Chronicle Hall holds Vexorath's survival memory, engineering history, public education and civic identity, and it is reflective, precise and proud without boasting. The building is quieter than the rest of the city and lit the way the rest of the city is lit, restrained and internal, pale structural frames over charcoal recesses with the cobalt guidance lines running softer here than they do on a working floor. Contair preserves failed designs as carefully as successful ones, because failure is evidence rather than shame, and the Hall is where that principle becomes a public institution rather than a working habit. Galleries, archives, a teaching court and a memorial share the same building. This is historical and cultural rather than a military archive, and not every archive space is a hidden conspiracy: one holding inside it is restricted and the rest of the Hall is openly public, which is the ordinary shape of a civic institution rather than evidence of anything. The city's own line runs underneath all of it, that nothing fails the same way twice, and the Hall is the proof that somebody wrote down why. Residents bring visitors here when they want to explain why Vexorath is the way it is.
Chronicle Hall.hiddenInfo: This is a historical and cultural institution rather than a military archive, and nine of its ten spaces are openly public. The one restricted holding is the Restricted Dravon Archive, and restriction there is consistent with Contair's ordinary classification of technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden — Dravon material is all four. Restricted is not secret, and this is not a conspiracy vault; the Hall's public function survives it intact. It is distinct from the Outer Shell's Dravon Attack Archive, with no relationship between them asserted, and the permanent Contair bar on Dravon is not softened. The Hall's standing brief covers drone evolution, failed systems, personhood disputes and the history of constructs created in response to attacks — which of its ten areas holds which is not established. The Chronicle's own entry for Vexorath's first recorded assault reads simply as not named, and no attacker, date or battle name has been invented to fill it.

First Assault Gallery.description: The earliest recorded assault on Vexorath, kept as a public gallery rather than buried. The room is plainly arranged and unheroic, exhibits set at reading height under restrained light, with no attempt to stage a battle out of what is fundamentally an account of a failure and its repair. For centuries Contair was treated as a desirable target by houses assuming technical brilliance could not compensate for limited population. Which assault, when and by whom is not established; the conflict record's entry for it reads as not named, and the gallery does not pretend otherwise. Visitors expecting a story with a villain in it find instead a very careful account of what did not hold, and residents seem to prefer it that way.

Failed Design Archive.description: An archive of failed designs, preserved as carefully as the successful ones, because failure is evidence rather than shame. The holdings are shelved and terminalled in a quiet reading space with worktables, ordered by whatever the Hall orders them by and not arranged to flatter anyone. Vexorath's conflict history is itself recorded as a failure-analysis series held by this Hall, though which area holds it is not established. Distinct from the Learning Annex's teaching library, with no shared collection or transfer between them. Holdings, arrangement, access and whether living designers' failures are included are all unstated, which makes the last of those an interesting question to ask a Contair out loud.

Breakthrough Record Hall.description: A hall recording Contair breakthroughs, carefully. Rezulith perfected the modern Lunar Gate standard, but the planetary network itself is generations of Contair engineering, and the Hall's own tonal instruction is proud without boasting. The room is spare rather than triumphal, exhibits spaced under restrained light with the attribution set out in full rather than reduced to a name. Vexorath must never become a setting that exists only to showcase one person, and the attribution here is handled with that in mind. What is displayed, who curates it and how credit is apportioned are unestablished, and no specific breakthrough is assigned to this hall. The effect is a room that is quietly certain of itself and declines to raise its voice.

Survivor Testimony Chamber.description: A chamber for survivor testimony, the part of a historical institution that holds people rather than systems or designs. It is small and low-lit, seating that adjusts, nothing on the walls competing for attention, and a quiet that is structural rather than requested. Whose testimony, in what form, whether it is recorded or heard live, whether it is public and whether consent governs access are all unestablished. No account is invented here, and no link to Myralis or the Continuum is asserted. What the chamber establishes by existing is that a House which files its failures as evidence also decided that some of the record could not be kept as engineering, and built a different kind of room for it.

Construct Evolution Walk.description: How Contair's constructs developed, laid out as a walk: drone labour became drone security, surface defences led to orbital defences. The walk is linear and unhurried, exhibits at intervals under restrained light, arranged so that the chain of decisions is readable rather than dramatic. The Hall's brief covers drone evolution, failed systems and personhood disputes, though nothing specific is assigned to this walk. Only the current four class names appear, Mote, Ward, Aegis and Echo, and how far back it reaches, which earlier constructs are shown and whether retired units are displayed physically are unstated. The walk makes the city's whole argument in miniature: nothing here was designed from ambition, and everything was designed from a previous problem.

Lunar Gate History Wing.description: The history of the Lunar Gates, exhibited in the city that builds and maintains them. The wing is broad and evenly lit, with the exhibits arranged around the engineering rather than around the politics, which does not stop the politics from showing. The network's weight is visible from every angle: Relstaris's Grand Hub remains dependent on Contair engineering, Quilrath's single gate survives only as legacy Contair infrastructure, and the Helvyra Gate Compact carries Rezulith's signature beside Torvex Corsair's. The modern standard is Rezulith's perfection of generations of Contair work. This wing establishes no destination list for Vexorath's own Gate, and whether any gate technology is displayed at all is unrecorded.

Lumina Reach Foundation Display.description: The station's founding, exhibited on the surface. Lumina Reach ended the era in which attacking Vexorath could be treated as a conventional territorial campaign, and its completion coincided with the end of the Second Dravon Conflict. The display is restrained, arranged around the decision rather than around the spectacle, and it does not attempt to stand in for the thing it describes. It sits in a city where reaching the actual station is never casual; access there follows legitimate purpose and operational responsibility, no standing tour exists, and curiosity alone creates no access up there. What is shown, whether construction records are public and what share of residents ever visit orbit are all unestablished.

Public Lesson Court.description: Where the Hall teaches, with historical attack records sitting openly in the city's curriculum. The court is a modular open space with seating that adjusts and room to gather around whatever is being explained, lit plainly and built for talking rather than for reverence. It is distinct from the Learning Annex's explanation stage, two separate education spaces in two different locations, with no relationship and no exclusivity claimed for either. Who teaches here, whether school visits are scheduled and whether visitors may attend is unstated. What the court is for is straightforward and slightly unusual: teaching a city's children exactly how their city was attacked, and what was rebuilt afterwards.

Restricted Dravon Archive.description: The Hall's restricted Dravon holdings, restricted because Dravon material scores on every Contair classification axis: risk, reproducibility, political consequence, maintenance burden. The entrance is unremarkable, a closed face in a public building, with no theatre made of it in either direction. Restricted is not secret and this is not a conspiracy vault; nine other areas of a public institution surround it, and the Hall's public function runs first. Who may access it, on what authority, and whether Dravon knows it exists, is unrecorded. The permanent Contair bar is not softened by anything held here, and the worry that gives the archive its edge runs the other way, toward Dravon-derived material turning up somewhere it should not.

Memorial Repair Bench.description: A memorial whose name puts remembrance and Vexorath's repair-centred language in the same phrase, standing on a history of loss turned into structure. It is plain and unornamented in the city's own materials, sited where people can stop at it without making an occasion of stopping. Who it memorialises, whether anyone repairs anything at it, whether any ritual attaches to it, and whether it is one bench or a form the city repeats are all deliberately unanswered, as is what mourning looks like in Vexorath at all. No inscription is recorded. What is certain is the phrasing, which a House that turns every failure into the next design would not have chosen by accident.

Rezulith's Workshop.name: Rezulith's Workshop
Rezulith's Workshop.basicInfo: The Workshop is an independent central complex and a living extension of Rezulith Contair's mind: corridors move, tool platforms reconfigure, and entire rooms may be reassigned between visits, so nobody who works here carries a reliable plan of it in their head. It holds the Lumina Core, advanced research, restricted fabrication, the family residence and the private link to orbit, amid suspended work platforms, layered tool arms and large prototype silhouettes. The light is restrained and comes from the work rather than from the architecture, the surfaces are pale where they are finished and open where they are not, and the repair channels are less channels than exposed working anatomy. Rezulith holds final technical authority over the Lumina Core, Lunar Gate integrity, the Outer Shell, citywide defence and anything capable of threatening the wider Contair network, and she is the greatest technical authority in Vexorath without being its sole social authority. The tone is brilliant, shifting, controlled chaos inside precise systems. Reaching the Workshop is not the same as entering it, and being inside it is not clearance for anything within it. Paul Thovex lives with all of this and still tells her when a perfect design makes no sense to an ordinary person.
Rezulith's Workshop.hiddenInfo: Rezulith holds final technical authority over the Lumina Core, Lunar Gate integrity, the Outer Shell, citywide defence, and anything capable of threatening the wider Contair network — she is the greatest technical authority in Vexorath, but not its sole social authority, and her flaw is assuming sufficient understanding makes every decision obvious. The Private Lunar Gate Wing is the restricted surface link to Lumina Reach and is not part of Nexara's public network: nothing about it is self-service, reaching Vexorath puts nobody within reach of it, and standing inside the Workshop is not the same as being cleared to use it — approval is settled before a guest arrives, as a station-operations matter rather than an audience with Rezulith. Two things stay unresolved on purpose. The Seris Transfer Bay's function is undefined: what transfers, in which direction, and why is deliberately unanswered, and a bay bearing Seris's name sits inside the Workshop she does not live in. And Lumina Minor keeps changing Workshop systems without using Rezulith's preferred architecture.

Lumina Core Chamber.description: The Lumina Core itself, the deep independent power source the city built because it could not depend on anyone else's. The need for independent power is what produced it, and the chamber is built around that fact rather than around display. What the Core is, how it works, what it powers, its output and its failure modes are all deliberately undescribed; even Relstaris lists it among the planet's notable things without explaining it, and nothing in the chamber offers an explanation either. Authority over what happens in this chamber rests with Rezulith alone. Vexorath City's Lumina Core Indicator Court is a separately named area associated with an indicator, not this chamber, and contains no part of the Core. The whole of the city's independence rests on something nobody describes.

Private Lunar Gate Wing.description: The restricted surface link to Lumina Reach, outside Nexara's public Gate network entirely. Nothing about it is self-service: reaching Vexorath puts no traveller within reach of it, and standing inside the Workshop is not clearance to use it. Approval is separate from ordinary Vexorath entry, is a matter of station operations rather than a personal audience with Rezulith, and is settled long before anyone arrives here. For station residents and assigned personnel it is simply the way back, which is the half that keeps orbit inhabited rather than merely defended. It is entirely separate from the Gate District's public platform, and no route, duration or mechanism is recorded for it anywhere. Who grants approval, and how often it is refused, is unstated.
