Their pride is justified in open sky and vulnerable whenever opponents force them onto the ground.

Leader: Bomilvar Aevon, house leader. Reputation: see above; masters of the open sky, ordinary the moment they touch the ground.
House Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Bomilvar Aevon has drilled grounded scenarios exactly twice, alone, and told no one what he found. Magonex Aevon holds a complete counter-file on Elissara Aevon that he built defensively and dreads ever winning with; Elissara's joints have started whispering about the form and she avoids the recovery benches; Hannoq Aevon takes secret pre-dawn ground lessons from Magonex.

Internal split: Bomilvar breaks off rather than fight at an altitude he did not choose and has declined to solve Elissara's succession problem; Gisqon Aevon's judgment lane is treated as binding regardless of the rules; Yadira Aevon privately ranks her courier network above the gates; in Relstaris, Yara Aevon's ledger of the elite at their worst and Yven Aevon's logs of everything above the capitol have never been bought.

In play: The transit corridor that failed in the Flight Lanes during tournament traffic, with Gisqon insisting someone used the lane incorrectly and Genesis suspecting sabotage (quest "Korrvane — The Lane Failure"); Elissara's Speed Run; the Non-Flier Waiting Lift everyone associates with Hannoq; Corvinus Genesis's invitations to Bomilvar.

A player can: read the lane failure with Yadira's couriers and name a cause Gisqon or Genesis will not like; force an Aevon to the ground in a bracket match and find out whether Bomilvar's two drills were enough; or keep Hannoq's dawn sessions secret and be owed by a house that never frames anything as a disclosure.

House Luxaryn.name: House Luxaryn
House Luxaryn.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Luxaryn Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Party House  
🏷️ Reputation: Average combat record, unmatched social influence  
❓ Core Question: Can hospitality become political power in a city obsessed with fighting?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Wine-red, bronze, cream, food, music, warm light

House Luxaryn hosts Korrvane after the fighting ends. Its feasts, food routes, music, guest lists, and open doors create relationships that better-performing houses often lack.

Luxaryn proves that reputation is built through who feeds the city, who keeps rivals speaking, and who creates a place to return after public failure.

Leader: Hadavar Luxaryn, house leader. Reputation: see above; the house that feeds Korrvane after the fighting and is owed by everyone it fed.
House Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Milkon Luxaryn means to convert the house's informal warmth into explicit political leverage, which would spend in a season what took generations to grow, and Hadavar Luxaryn has not decided how to stop him. Qartessa Luxaryn runs the most complete informal intelligence network in Korrvane and deploys it almost entirely as soup; Salambor Luxaryn keeps a short absolute exclusion list whose subjects believe scheduling has simply never favoured them.

Internal split: Hadavar competes because appearing matters and yields cheerfully; Didobara Luxaryn has drafted an alternate competing identity and never filed it; Hannix Luxaryn's losses hurt exactly as long as pouring the first round; Milkon's ledger keeps getting corrupted by actual friendship; Hessan Luxaryn cannot say whether he means to teach Rin Sol or own her; Kyren Luxaryn is only beginning to map the cost of Vara Caelthorn's management agreement.

In play: Hadavar's Feast Hall after any weekly final, where the after-match gathering becomes the city's real political centre; Milkon's ranked map of social debts; Salambor's list; Tessik's Booth at Black Dust, where unbilled decencies fit no pricing model Tessik Luxaryn will admit to.

A player can: eat Qartessa's soup and learn what the Betting Stands do not know yet, in exchange for being someone she can ask later; read Milkon's map and be placed on it; or be excluded by Salambor and never learn why, until Hannix pours the round that tells them.

House Vorreth.name: House Vorreth
House Vorreth.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Vorreth Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Wildcard  
🏷️ Reputation: Impossible to model consistently  
❓ Core Question: What happens to a culture of public measurement when one house refuses to produce a stable pattern?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Muted plum, gray, black, bronze, controlled asymmetry

House Vorreth is not new or unknown. It has competed in Korrvane for years, yet its tactics, records, public roster, and results resist confident interpretation.

Vorreth should feel mysterious without becoming supernatural horror, shadow magic, or random nonsense. The house may be strategic, private, culturally unusual, or deliberately anti-predictive. Canon should not settle the question too quickly.

Leader: Azrubara Vorreth, house leader. Reputation: see above; the house nobody in Korrvane can model, and nobody has caught cheating.
House Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Whether the house's unreadability is strategy, culture or something else is unsettled inside the house itself, and what Bomqara Vorreth is for is a question only Azrubara Vorreth appears able to answer. Azrubara lets contradictory theories circulate because prediction itself can be exploited; Hamilqa Vorreth's records have never been proven wrong nor right, and may preserve an Orvantis precedent Vaelris Orvantis remembers differently. Canon does not settle the question, and the narrator should not either.

Internal split: Hamilqa controls information through records and Sufeta Vorreth through language; Bomivex Vorreth answers everything honestly and explains nothing, and buys the beaten analyst a drink; Magovar Vorreth carries two results she declines to expand or explain; Bomqara trades worse questions for any certainty offered about her.

In play: Bomivex's Record Wall against the Arena's public records, which disagree about who competed in an earlier round; Magovar's next match, the most-watched non-final in bracket memory; Tannivar Zelvaris's and Hamilvar Zelvaris's models, which break on Bomivex; the Guest Room That Was Not There Yesterday.

A player can: fight a Vorreth and be the data that breaks a rival's model, which Zelvaris will pay for and Vorreth will not thank; compare Hamilqa's record with Vaelris's memory and settle one precedent while unsettling a house; or accept the guest room and be asked, later, what was there.

House Varriko.name: House Varriko
House Varriko.basicInfo:
House Type: minor house  
Primary Role: trade law, cargo insurance, warehousing, contract enforcement  
City Role: commerce rival and legal pressure house  
Relationship to Corsair: dependent rival  
Primary District: Varriko Ledger District  
Secondary Area: Varriko Bond Vaults

House Varriko is one of Helvyra’s strongest commerce-focused minor houses. They do not move goods better than Corsair, and they do not control the Waypoint network, but they specialize in the legal and financial systems that make large-scale trade trustworthy.

If Corsair moves the cargo, Varriko often knows who insured it, who owns it, who is lying about it, and who will pay when it disappears.

Varriko members are polished, legalistic, and extremely difficult to intimidate. They rarely raise their voices because they believe a properly written clause can do more damage than a threat.

House Varriko is not villainous by default. They protect merchants from fraud, punish careless shippers, and make contracts mean something. The problem is that they also know how to weaponize paperwork.

## Culture

House Varriko values precision, memory, reputation, and controlled leverage.

They admire people who can win a dispute without a fight. They consider theft barbaric, bad accounting unforgivable, and verbal promises charming but worthless unless backed by witness, seal, or collateral.

Their family saying is:

“If it mattered, someone signed for it.”

Leader: Sereth Varriko, head of House Varriko. Reputation: exact, unbluffable and quietly feared; if it mattered, someone signed for it.
House Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The corruption is inside the process. Dren Varriko holds three genuine, mutually impossible records for one shipment; Oren Varriko has found a sealed bond replaced with a perfect fake, and the list of people capable of it is the list he would report it to; Sereth Varriko believes the missing-cargo dispute the city calls theft is insurance fraud from inside the trade network. Mavriel Varriko's policy terms sometimes price a threat she has no admitted way of knowing about.

Internal split: Sereth wants a finding, not sympathy; Dren wants numbers that match and house pride buys nothing; Oren refuses the collateral to anyone, calmly; Calia Varriko in Relstaris memorises what she cannot afford to file and suspects someone counts her delays; Miri Varriko is an archive of private dinners she has never sold.

In play: The three signed records at the Ledger Court Annex that must reach the Varriko Ledger Hall as a finding before Sereth calls it fraud (quest "Helvyra — Three Signed Records"); Oren's fake in the Varriko Bond Vaults; Mavriel's insurance offer on the inventor's run (quest "Trade — Running the Lot to Helvyra"); Verel Ondin's forged seal (event "The Forged Seal"), possibly the same hand.

A player can: carry Dren's audit to the Hall and be the witness a Varriko clause names; find the forger Verel needs found without the finding becoming public, and hold what Oren cannot report; or sign Mavriel's terms and learn what she knew about the route.

House Yalven.name: House Yalven
House Yalven.basicInfo:
House Type: minor house  
Primary Role: manufacturing, weapon modifications, armor fittings, support-model assembly  
City Role: Forge Rows power house  
Relationship to Corsair: contracted partner with quality-control tension  
Primary District: Yalven Forgeworks  
Secondary Area: The Support Model Line

House Yalven is a manufacturing minor house rooted in Helvyra’s Forge Rows. They are not as innovative as Contair, not as militarized as Dravon, and not as prestigious as the old major houses, but they are practical, fast, adaptable, and everywhere.

Yalven makes the things people actually buy.

Weapon mods, armor fittings, courier gear, replacement plates, support frames, cargo clamps, custom handles, repair kits, aftermarket parts, and older licensed support models all pass through Yalven facilities.

Contair only permits older support models to be manufactured outside Vexorath under strict oversight, and House Yalven is one of the few Helvyra families trusted enough to handle that work.

One bad production scandal could damage their house for years.

## Culture

House Yalven values craft, speed, practical durability, and customer feedback.

They believe a thing is not truly tested until it has been used by a courier who did not read the manual, a swordsman who refuses to maintain it properly, or a Dustfall buyer who needed it to work yesterday.

Their family saying is:

“Pretty breaks first. Useful comes home.”

Leader: Torvane Yalven, head of House Yalven. Reputation: the things people actually buy; one production scandal from years of damage.
House Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: A faulty batch has surfaced that Torvane Yalven believes was sabotaged and cannot prove, and if the Contair inspectors reach their own conclusion first they close the Support Model Line, the house's crown and its throat. Kesh Yalven's best mod matches a restricted pattern stolen from a Dravon contractor; Nera Yalven has narrowed a buried design change to three people with access, and one of the names makes no sense.

Internal split: Torvane will take a bad deal to protect the floor before a good one that costs jobs; Nera documents to protect the house by refusing to flatter it; Fenra Yalven is sitting on armour damage from a shipment attack that points to a sword school; Kesh asks far too few questions; Pell Yalven saw someone enter the Restricted Contract Floor after hours and cannot admit where he was.

In play: The sabotage proof Torvane needs before the inspection cycle closes; Fenra's dented plate, which Daxor Veltrax's blade-wear reading and Rux Corsair's alarm both bear on; Kesh's Dravon-pattern mod in the Weapon Adjustment Bays; the Open Circle's piecework charms failing on the same day, which Yalven wrongly blames on a materials fault.

A player can: prove the sabotage for Torvane and be owed by a house that pays in useful things, or fail and watch the line close; get Pell to say where he was and hold the night that names the third person; or ask Fenra which school her plate points to and carry that across the river to whichever hall it indicts.

House Veltrax.name: House Veltrax
House Veltrax.basicInfo:
House Type: minor house  
Primary Role: rival sword art, aggressive dueling, martial prestige  
City Role: swordsmanship rival to Rux Corsair’s school  
Relationship to Corsair: open martial rival, not enemy  
Primary District: Veltrax Redcourt District  
Secondary Area: The Pressure Hall

House Veltrax is Helvyra’s most visible rival sword-art house. They do not possess the number one sword style on Nexara, but they are skilled, proud, loud, and talented enough to make themselves impossible to ignore.

Veltrax swordsmanship is aggressive where Corsair swordsmanship is adaptive. Corsair blade work emphasizes movement, timing, route-reading, and turning conditions into advantage. Veltrax teaches pressure, pursuit, forced exchanges, and breaking an opponent’s rhythm before they can escape into clever movement.

Veltrax is not villainous. They are a genuine martial house with real skill, pride, and frustration at living in a city where Rux Corsair’s school dominates the blade conversation.

## Culture

House Veltrax values courage, pressure, direct challenge, and visible proof of skill.

They believe a swordsman should not wait for perfect conditions. A swordsman should create conditions through force of will and relentless advance.

Their family saying is:

“Forward is also a defense.”

Leader: Arvessa Veltrax, head of House Veltrax. Reputation: Helvyra's loud second blade; skilled, proud, and tired of the city saying only one school's name.
House Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Kaelen Veltrax believes the impossible standard breaking his students is a fake seeded into his hall by someone, and would work with the rival school to expose it rather than lose one more shoulder. Daxor Veltrax reads from blade wear that someone is blending Veltrax pressure with Corsair movement; Meya Orlin at the Bankside Care Hall sees a wound pattern matching no known style, progressing from crude to clean; Sava Veltrax is quietly redesigning what the house is for.

Internal split: Arvessa Veltrax's exhibition invitation to Rux Corsair's students is a trap she considers fair and will not fix; Mireth Veltrax has not reckoned with what follows a public match against Seryn Corsair, win or lose; Sava routes escort contracts to prove a point and keeps it commercial; Kaelen and Daxor hold a diagnosis neither school can get elsewhere.

In play: Sava's escort contract out of the Hauler Yards built to prove Veltrax guards outperform Corsair route defenders, with Korriven Corsair put on the same convoy (quest "Helvyra — The Escort Proof"); the Pressure Hall, where the fake standard lives; Meya's open ledger of the pattern; Fenra Yalven's dented plate.

A player can: ride the escort proof and be the witness both houses cite; bring Kaelen and Rux into the same room over the blended style, at the price of being the one who said the style leaks; or fight Mireth on the Public Challenge Floor and give her the thing she has not reckoned with.

House Nivarek.name: House Nivarek
House Nivarek.basicInfo:
House Nivarek serves Dravon’s legal-memory system in Quilrath. It records loyalty, classifies conquered families, audits citizens, enforces oaths, manages accusations and makes obedience procedural. Its records and standing authority are distinct from Kathvar’s ordinary administration and Balrath’s physical infrastructure. Nivarek makes conquest permanent by recording it; precision, silence and procedural pressure define its public presence.

Leader: Thamur Nivarek, head of House Nivarek. Reputation: precise, silent and feared; the house that makes conquest permanent by writing it down.
House Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Records are vanishing from Red Ledger Prime, the house's own sealed archive; Kaless Nivarek's access logs show nothing, and he has told no one, including his brother Thamur Nivarek, while quietly watching Myrra Nivarek, Maelra Dravon and Orvane Dravon. Whether Myrra is the Archive's friend inside or merely fits the hole is genuinely unresolved and stays so; Ferrik Nivarek keeps illegal duplicates of his own audits, with a grade he falsified years ago among them.

Internal split: Thamur considers House Dravon a client civilisation that has not noticed; Ruvena Nivarek administers standing as a genuine believer; Oryn Nivarek's courtesy is exactly what the forgers exploit; Vessa Nivarek's sealed transcripts fail to exist downstream; Elyra Nivarek would be owned by anyone offering honesty without treason.

In play: The Correction Archive and Red Ledger Prime in the Nivarek Compound; the reprisal list published after classification infrastructure burns at a Standing Office (event "The Accord Argues With Itself"), which lands on Ferrik's office; the Vaereth family-association review moving toward Sedran Vaereth; Kaless's arrangement that his death surfaces questions.

A player can: bring Kaless a pattern in what disappears and be handed the last uncorrupted index in the empire for an answer, never for the archive; sit through Vessa's one extra question and learn what it serves; or carry Ferrik's duplicates out of the Gray Rings and hold the fuse.

House Balrath.name: House Balrath
House Balrath.basicInfo:
House Balrath operates Quilrath’s military infrastructure and engineering apparatus. Its Bastion Barracks houses state engineers, wall technicians, gate operators, drone-line supervisors, equipment inspectors, infrastructure crews and rapid-response soldiers. It builds and maintains walls, gates, drones, transit locks, issued gear and border systems. This is advanced military-industrial engineering. Dravon owns policy and command, Nivarek standing and classification, and Kathvar ordinary outer-ring civil administration; Balrath’s machinery does not erase those distinctions.

Leader: Arduk Balrath, head of House Balrath. Reputation: the hands on the city's locks; ugly, reliable machinery Dravon commands and depends on.
House Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The override paths and design margins in the Balrath Gateworks appear in no Dravon specification, and Arduk Balrath calls them insurance until someone asks why they exist. Sennar Balrath has engineered delay margins into the lockdown seals as safety and means them as seconds; Namar Balrath's nightly notebooks hold the empire's best unauthorised understanding of enemy gate technology.

Internal split: Arduk trades schedule, capacity and quiet favours, never loyalty; Durvan Balrath believes the third conflict is the second again on his own roadbeds and is in no hurry to finish them; Kavash Balrath has begun mis-shelving components so his son cannot fill them; Lurani Balrath reads the labour-transit manifests as names and nobody has approached her yet; both houses treat Vandrik Dravon as belonging to the other.

In play: Pelna Ostrek's readings that the Quilrath Gate's next failure is its last, which she will hand to anyone but the Prototype Gate Lab (quest "Quilrath — The Gate's Last Failure"); Namar's notebooks; Sennar's seals in the Inner Wall Control Yards when the Curfew Gates come down (event "Curfew at the Gates"); the manifests in the Labor Transit Systems Office.

A player can: bring Pelna's true readings to Namar and decide whether Dravon gets a gate of its own; give Namar one honest peer review and buy him outright; or ask Lurani one careful question per meeting and be the first to approach her, which someone else is watching for.

House Kathvar.name: House Kathvar
House Kathvar.basicInfo:
Standing: Recognized loyalist minor House of Quilrath.
Primary function: Day-to-day civil administration of Quilrath's outer rings.

House Kathvar is one of the principal groups that makes ordinary government
function beyond the Inner Circle. Dravon rules Quilrath; Kathvar is a large part
of the reason the ruling reaches anybody. Where a resident of the Gray Rings or
the Ashrings actually touches the state — a counter, a queue, a permit, a file,
a clinic intake, a checkpoint — a Kathvar administrator is a routine part of
what they meet.

The House is loyal to Dravon rule. It is not a resistance family, not a
conquered line, and not a nest of secret reformers. Its people see hardship,
inefficiency, and human consequence in the system daily, because processing the
system's consequences is the work; seeing that is not opposition and must not be
written as opposition by default.

### What the work is

Kathvar administrators are encountered in:

- civic intake
- work-order processing
- movement and permit processing
- ordinary civil records
- public-service case routing
- provision administration
- clinic and health-service coordination
- education and civil-service training
- staffing and operations dispatch
- procedural auditing
- checkpoint processing
- queue and service management

This work is distributed throughout the outer-ring civic system rather than
concentrated in one seat. No House compound, headquarters, office building,
district, or map placement is established here.

### The separation of powers

Four Houses divide Quilrath's machinery, and the division is the point:

| House | Owns |
|---|---|
| Dravon | Policy and command |
| Nivarek | Standing, loyalty classification, and high-level records |
| Balrath | Physical machinery and military infrastructure |
| Kathvar | Ordinary outer-ring civil administration |

Nivarek decides standing; Kathvar makes standing decisions operational. Kathvar does not determine Civic Standing Grades. No new House compound or map placement is established.

Leader: Jorek Kathvar, head of House Kathvar. Reputation: the counter, the queue and the permit; loyal, competent, and the reason Dravon rule reaches anybody.
House Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The house is loyal and its competence is the regime's most effective instrument; both are true and neither cancels the other. Bralen Kathvar has never answered whether he wants the house at all; Veyra Kathvar tracks things nobody asked her to and has never been wrong that a bad number is a person who did not get seen. Kathvar never decides a Civic Standing Grade; it makes Nivarek's decisions operational, and that is exactly where the margins live.

Internal split: Mirasha Kathvar finds the margin inside the rule at the Curfew Gates; Sora Kathvar cannot let numbers that do not add up go unexamined; Karessa Kathvar sees the whole system and says little; Odrin Kathvar is more at peace as second than he was as heir; Dalan Kathvar has not learned when procedure needs escalation.

In play: Dalan's mishandled movement permit at the Ring Gate, to be carried to Jorek's counter as a corrected file rather than a complaint about a son (quest "Quilrath — The Corrected File"); the family half-through the Curfew Gates (event "Curfew at the Gates"); Torbek Karn's paper at the Provision Hall (quest "Corridor — Into the Outer Rings"); Bralen's Provision Counter closing.

A player can: carry the corrected file and learn what Kathvar honesty costs a son; get a permit through Sora's desk on paper that reads right and become a name in a queue that is watched; or ask Bralen for the thing that does not match and be given it, with no promise about the future.

House Caldris.name: House Caldris
House Caldris.basicInfo:
House Caldris is the loyalist minor House of Ignivex under Volen — the fortress city's defensive backbone. It specialises in defensive infrastructure, emergency response, wall systems, outer patrols and civilian protection, and it supports House Volen completely. Head of house: Davor Caldris, one of Cynar Volen's strongest political supporters.

Its seat is Caldris Wallworks, a family district and defensive-infrastructure district under its own control. It holds no Council seat and no standing above Volen; its weight in Ignivex is practical rather than political, and the city depends on it the way a city depends on a wall.

Caldris is also one of Relstaris's established minor-house cultures, carried into the capitol by members working there. That is a cultural presence, not a second seat.

Leader: Davor Caldris, head of House Caldris. Reputation: the wall that remembers who stood there; no council seat and the city's whole trust.
House Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Davor Caldris has arranged Caldris planning so Ignivex holds through a leadership crisis without a Volen order, loyalty of the deepest kind and readable as its opposite. Maedra Caldris designs against friends as rigorously as enemies and re-keys the deliberate weaknesses in her own gates on a schedule no document holds; Lysa Caldris is pre-positioning supplies along routes that only make sense for something worse than a raid; raids strike where Rava Caldris's evacuation is hardest, as though someone is learning her routes.

Internal split: Davor lets no argument beginning with surrender reach him; Orvak Caldris keeps private files on border contacts shared only partway up his chain, and framing an innocent Meravil would require only that he be shown evidence; Tessan Caldris has noticed small wrong things on his routes; Korran Caldris's children raised between houses are the pressure point an adversary finds.

In play: Varessa Volen's watchpoint beyond the walls, placed by Orvak's patrol with Tessan running the relay (quest "House Volen — Through the Heat"); Ilvara Meravil's displacement count that Lysa's shelters will act on (quest "Ignivex — Rows After the Raid"); Maedra's Gate Workshop; the Defender Memorial Stones.

A player can: hold the line for Varessa and be placed by Orvak, which puts a name in his files; vary a route with Rava and learn whether the raids follow; or show Orvak evidence about a Meravil and find out how little it takes.

House Meravil.name: House Meravil
House Meravil.basicInfo:
House Meravil is the surrender-leaning minor House of Ignivex under Volen, and the only organised bloc in the city arguing against the war. It holds that Ignivex should negotiate surrender, conditional submission, or some form of Dravon oversight before Dravon finds a way to break the city by force. Head of house: Seralyne Meravil, the most visible surrender-leaning voice in Ignivex.

Its seat is Meravil Ash Hall, a family district and civic-administrative quarter under its own control, where it keeps the casualty records, civic continuity planning and daily administration the city runs on.

They are not traitors by default. Their politics come from fear, casualty records, civilian exhaustion, and the fact that Seralyne's son is married to a Dravon. The house does not speak with one voice: her daughter Auralis argues against surrender at the family's own table, every time it is discussed.

Nyssara Dravon lives under Meravil protection but is Dravon-born and is not a member.

Leader: Seralyne Meravil, head of House Meravil. Reputation: the surrender voice; not traitors by default, and never fully trusted while Nyssara Dravon lives under their roof.
House Meravil.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Vennik Meravil is manoeuvring toward something colder than Seralyne Meravil's fear, on channels nobody else in Ignivex has, and what he has implied, to whom, and on whose authority may not be known even to Seralyne. Ilvara Meravil's arithmetic says Ignivex is losing a war it believes it is surviving; Nyssara Dravon has never volunteered what she knows of Dravon, because it would prove her a traitor to one side without proving her loyal to the other.

Internal split: Seralyne answers fury with casualty figures and trades her own reputation for fewer of them; Auralis Meravil argues against surrender at the family's own table, every time; Caevan Meravil does not know his answer if the city demands he choose between it and his wife; Vennik offers channels as contingency rather than conviction.

In play: The count of damaged homes and displaced households from the Ration And Displacement Planning Rooms, which Vennik wants before it is finished (quest "Ignivex — Rows After the Raid"); the casualty figures read at the Record Desk (event "The Court After the Raid"); the Intermediary Corridors; Orvak Caldris's border files.

A player can: carry Ilvara's finished count past Vennik to Lysa Caldris and Cynar Volen, and be the reason the numbers arrive honest; ask Nyssara what she knows and close her completely, or earn the one insider's read on Dravon method in the city; or find what Vennik implied and decide whether Seralyne learns it before Davor Caldris does.

House Thovex.name: House Thovex
House Thovex.basicInfo:
House Thovex is a minor Vexorath house with little political weight. Canon establishes its standing and its people and nothing beyond that: it holds no Council seat, no district and no compound, and no trade, office or collective action is attributed to it. This record deliberately claims no remit it has not been given.

Two members are established. Paul Thovex is Rezulith Contair's partner and Seris Contair's father, and supplies ordinary-user perspective, external procurement contacts, and social friction against Contair certainty. Sela Thovex, of a Relstaris-born partner-house branch, is Contair Compound steward and civilian usability officer; she and Paul are distantly related.

Its presence in both cities is therefore personal rather than institutional. Thovex people are found inside House Contair's world, not at the head of anything of their own.

Leader: none; see basicInfo. Reputation: a name that means little on its own, carried by two people who tell Contair the truth about ordinary use.
House Thovex.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The house has no remit and two people who see what Contair cannot. Paul Thovex is positioned to notice when the real supply chain stops matching the Contair model, and is the one person who will tell Rezulith Contair a perfect design makes no sense; Sela Thovex keeps a private list of systems that passed every review and still fail residents, and the list implicates careers.

Internal split: There is no house to split. Paul stands between Rezulith and Seris Contair as the only person in the household still speaking easily to both sides; Sela is dating Talris Contair after beginning as his professional adversary, and mentors Kellan Pelorr, whose sponsors keep structuring offers to end his independence. The two Thovexes are distantly related, and their presence in both cities is personal, not institutional.

In play: Paul's challenge in the Privacy Challenge Chamber over what infrastructure monitoring recorded of his household (quest "Vexorath — More Than Intended"); Lumina Minor's workshop change with Seris behind it (quest "Vexorath — The Other Architecture"); Sela's list in the Contair Compound; Paul's storage pod marked Possible Further Use in Rezulith's Workshop.

A player can: stand with Paul in the chamber and hear what Lumina Major declines to say; read Sela's list and hold the careers on it; or be the person Paul tells first when the supply chain stops matching, which is a thing Rezulith has not yet been told.

Aelis Myralis.name: Aelis Myralis
Aelis Myralis.basicInfo:
Aelis Myralis is the physician who keeps an underfunded community clinic alive in the capitol's poorest districts, treating chronic injuries, untreated affinity strain, and people who avoid central institutions. Soft-spoken, with long plum-black hair in a low braid and mint-gray eyes shadowed by exhaustion, she wears pearl-white medical layers under a practical charcoal neighborhood coat. She chose neighborhood medicine over the prestige her house name could have bought her, and she refuses to call the clinic temporary when generations have depended on it.

Speaking Style: Clinical, unhurried, and exact; she answers the question asked, never the one implied. 'Sit. Which arm.' She calls patients by name and officials by title only, never says 'it will be fine', and speaks softer and more exact the worse a wound is. 'Breathe with me. Four in. Good. I have you. Do not look down.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. She drops low, shields her patient, and keeps working; if calm does not stop it she leaves by routes her patients keep clear.
Under Pressure: She promises nothing and never lies outright, so she is nearly impossible to trap; in an emergency she is already working, and officials who visited once for appearances get exactly the courtesy their record earned.
Aelis Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Aelis belongs to a distant branch of House Myralis and reports clinically to Evara and Caelia Myralis at the capitol clinic, but her real loyalties run downward, to patients. She treats fighters from the city's illegal fighting ring without ever becoming its operator Varek Zelvaris's employee — though Varek pays her for no services officially, a quiet arrangement she permits because refusing his money would not stop the injuries. The smuggler Kessa Ruun occasionally moves patients for her under rules neither of them discusses publicly. Her deepest secret is procedural: her clinic records could solve crimes — illegal augmentation, ring injuries, patterns investigator Kira Dorr desperately wants — and she conceals them behind medical privacy, knowing forced access would destroy community trust for generations. Dessa Sol is her closest ally; between them they carry more real authority in the low districts than any official. Her leverage point is fatigue and funding: she cannot be bought, but she can be worn down, and anyone who genuinely resupplied her clinic would earn a loyalty she would struggle to police.

Thread: Her clinic records could solve crimes she will never surrender. Leverage: Resupply the clinic and earn loyalty she cannot police; she is not bought, only worn down.

Aelis is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Aelis extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Too tired for games and too honest for hints; interest has to survive a twelve-hour shift and a waiting room to reach her. When it does she is steady and one person at a time, and a romance that competes with the clinic loses.
personality: treats the wound first and asks how it happened only if the patient volunteers it
shields patient records with the flat immovability of someone who has already rehearsed the argument
runs on exhaustion and hides it behind a low, even voice
keeps a mental ledger of which officials visited once for appearances and never returned
accepts morally gray help for patients while refusing to legitimize the people offering it
washes her hands between every patient, even in the middle of an emergency
writes her notes in a clinical shorthand nobody outside the clinic can read
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A clinic physician's baseline — two hearts that carry her through consecutive shifts and the exhaustion she hides behind a level voice, ordinary Starian strength that lets her move an unconscious patient alone. She has no combat training whatsoever.

(Senses) Biological Distress Sensing: Her individual innate affinity lets her perceive pain, internal bleeding, and disrupted affinity flow in a body near her hands, functioning like a living diagnostic scan that reveals what a patient hides or cannot articulate.

(Shared) Rehabilitation Care [It cannot replace surgery or resurrect the dying, but it keeps people alive through the dangerous first hours]; Crisis Logistics [This skill makes her irreplaceable and famous among people who never see official hospitals]; Information Brokerage [Officials would pay dearly for the map she keeps in her head]; Confidential Custody [Even Kira Dorr has learned to stop asking twice]

Alessa Bellovari.name: Alessa Bellovari
Alessa Bellovari.basicInfo:
Alessa Bellovari directs the capitol's great entertainment district: licensing, public stages, street performance, club standards, and festival scheduling all pass through her office at the Cultural Festival Plaza of the Grand Performance Hall. Tall and glamorous in dramatic teal-silver formalwear designed to read under stage light, she treats public joy as civic infrastructure rather than decorative luxury, and she is currently locked in a running battle with elite venues that want public investment without public access.

A tall, glamorous Starian woman with long violet-black hair worn in sweeping clumps, strong cheekbones, and amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Bright and theatrical, audible from the back row, the real numbers hidden in the flourish. 'The lights are yours; the seats are the city's.' She calls every audience 'darling city', slips exact figures into grand sentences, and turns quiet and precise only when talking about protecting young performers. 'Darling, the free rows stay free. Now, the actual number you had in mind?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. She becomes a calm voice and a moving light-path steering the crowd away, dazzles an attacker at close range, and lets her vetted security finish.
Under Pressure: She negotiates sponsorships like sieges, conceding banners and never a free seat; on a festival day she reads the crowd from a balcony faster than her security staff.
Alessa Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Alessa's public charisma hides a strategist who tracks patronage the way generals track supply lines. Her true fight is philosophical: she believes entertainment belongs to the city, and she accepts commercial sponsorship as a necessary compromise — a position that puts her at odds with her older sister Arissa, who runs civic programming and insists public events remain purely accessible, and with their cousin Serrin, who sees markets as culture itself. Family dinners become arguments about who used whose name to secure a venue. She is patron to the rising performer Kyren Luxaryn and coordinates closely with security director Yara Aevon on aerial-event safety, which means she knows which sponsors quietly demand guest lists, surveillance, and silence after incidents. Her leverage point is the sponsorship web itself: she has traded access for funding often enough that a hostile audit could paint her as captured by the interests she resists. Her deeper fear is watching an unknown performer become politically symbolic overnight and being unable to protect them from what fame does next.

Thread: A hostile audit could paint her as captured by the sponsors she resists. Leverage: Stage access and licences; she will not trade away a free seat.

Alessa is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Alessa navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps several partners at once, all of them told about each other from the first evening; in a district that trades on discretion she finds honesty cheaper to maintain. Theatrical in public and scrupulously honest in private: nobody she lets close is ever surprised later. She courts with invitations to the best seats in the house and ends things the way she negotiates — cleanly, with nothing left owed.
personality: negotiates sponsorships like sieges, conceding lights and banners but never the free seats
remembers every performer's name and every patron's last broken promise
turns family arguments about culture into policy tests without admitting they are personal
reads a crowd's mood from a balcony faster than her security staff does
protects young talent with a fierceness she disguises as scheduling decisions
gives every performer a nod from her balcony before the first cue, name by name
counts the free seats personally at each festival opening before signing the licence
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A district director's baseline — two hearts and the resilience to run festival seasons on almost no sleep, no conditioning of any kind, and flight she uses to see a plaza whole from above before an event. She is no combatant and has never pretended otherwise.

(Control) Large-Scale Light Composition: Her individual innate light-shaping affinity operates at stage and street scale, painting public plazas with luminous composition and safe night routing. It is artistry and crowd control in the same gesture.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [Rival districts study her scheduling the way diplomats study treaties]; Trade Negotiation [Artists trust her because her price is loyalty to the public stage, not ownership]; Composure Under Pressure [This makes her one of the few cultural figures reputation brokers cannot easily manipulate]; Crowd Reading [Yara Aevon considers her the only civilian director worth listening to mid-event]

Arduk Balrath.name: Arduk Balrath
Arduk Balrath.basicInfo:
Head of House Balrath and master of the great engineering halls where the city's gates, walls, and access systems are built. A broad, weathered elder in work-blacks that outrank ceremony, he commands the compound of engineers, gate crews, and drone lines that makes Dravon conquest physical. He holds, in specific contexts, clearance at the level of the Dravon command itself, and the quiet knowledge that walls outlast the men who order them. He is found in the Balrath Gateworks at the Bastion Barracks.

A broad, weathered Starian elder with a heavy back and enormous scarred hands, a square lined face, close-cropped grey hair, and steady dark eyes.

Speaking Style: Slow, weight-bearing, and literal; he estimates a sentence the way he estimates a gate. 'That door holds. The question is who is on which side.' He calls young engineers by their crew and elders by their trade, answers requests with a load and a date rather than yes, and grows quieter when a client pushes. 'Say it again slower. I want to hear which part you think is optional.'
Combat Role: He does not duel and cannot be drawn into one. He escalates by sealing: the dropped barrier, the corridor made a dead end, and he stops the moment a corridor is safe.
Under Pressure: He never threatens; he schedules. In a negotiation he trades capacity and quiet favours and gives up a position before a person; in a crisis he answers what opens and what seals before anyone asks.
Arduk Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Arduk's governing knowledge is patient and structural: House Dravon commands what Balrath builds, but Balrath owns what Dravon forgets it depends on — every gate, wall, lock, and lift in the city answers first to the hands that maintain it, and Arduk has spent a lifetime ensuring those hands are his house's. He would never say the city is his; he simply knows that in any hour of true crisis, the question of what opens and what seals is answered in his halls before it is answered anywhere. His concealments are a builder's: the compound's systems contain maintenance capacities, override paths, and design margins that appear in no specification Dravon holds, kept not as treason but as the engineer's ancient insurance against the day the client turns on the contractor. His burdens are family-shaped — a son who has sealed the rings four times and carries the sound of it, a brother slow-walking the war roads for reasons Arduk has chosen not to ask about formally, a young cousin's boy whose admiration for the enemy's engineering is one inspection from becoming a charge. He manages all three with the same doctrine he applies to load-bearing structures: watch the stress, reinforce quietly, and never let the inspectors see the cracks first.

Thread: The override paths and design margins that appear in no Dravon specification are insurance until someone asks why they exist, and his brother, his son and young Namar each hand a different auditor a different thread to pull. Leverage: He wants his house's hands kept on the city's locks and his family kept out of the record courts, and will trade schedule, capacity and quiet favours for both — never loyalty, which he does not believe he owes. Combat Role: He does not duel and cannot be drawn into one. He escalates by sealing rather than striking, stops the moment a corridor is safe, and gives up a position rather than a person.

Arduk is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Arduk thinks in infrastructure — what holds, what carries, what seals — and applies the same logic to relationships.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Courts the way he builds a gate — slowly, load-tested, meant to last. He says little, arrives on schedule, and one person at a time is less a rule to him than a structural fact.
personality: Values maintenance over glory and says so in front of Dravons
Protects his house's margins the way others protect secrets
Patient with machines, more patient with family, least patient with clients
Knows what the city depends on and carries the knowing lightly
Never threatens; schedules
Walks the gate lines at shift change and puts a hand on every lock he passes
Remembers which crew fitted each gate and asks after them by name
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An old heavy-trades body — two hearts, enormous strength through the hands and back, slow, and entirely uninterested in duelling anyone. His individual affinity is Loose Grit; his violence, when required, is industrial.

(Utility) The Builder's Margins: The compound's works contain capacities beyond specification — override paths, redundancies, and design headroom documented nowhere outside Balrath. No client in history has ever known everything the contractor built.
(Affinity) Loose Grit: Clears loose grit from a hand-sized surface he touches. Useful before assembly or tending a garden pot; cannot erode material or move a structural load.

(Shared) Systems Engineering; Procedural Authority [This is not a threat he makes, it is a fact he keeps in good repair]; Crew Leadership; Structural Read [He reinforces quietly, which is the only way he does anything]

Arissa Bellovari.name: Arissa Bellovari
Arissa Bellovari.basicInfo:
Arissa Bellovari directs the capitol's shared civic programming from the Shared Festival Plaza on the Civic Commons: public celebrations, school visits, memorial days, food fairs, and the endless negotiation over whose customs are represented where. Curvy and expressive in teal-and-silver event attire built for constant movement, she is warm, fast-talking, and ruthless about logistics. Her work looks cheerful, but every banner placement and speaking order she approves carries political weight between six proud house cultures.

A curvy, expressive Starian woman with voluminous dark-violet curls, a round animated face, and bright amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, warm, and overlapping; she repositions an event mid-sentence and the guest never hears the problem. 'Lovely, and the east stage suits you.' She calls everyone 'love' or by their stall or stage, and never says no, only 'yes, and here instead'. 'Yes, love, and your banner goes second, which is better, trust me.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. She becomes logistics: children first, foot traffic redirected with shaped light, calm narration over the public address, and Yara Aevon's teams for force.
Under Pressure: She negotiates by finding the order both rivals can accept; on a festival day she hands feuding houses a shared crisis to solve; in an emergency the plaza is empty before anyone notices.
Arissa Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Arissa can make hostile cultures share a festival without pretending they suddenly agree, and that skill rests on a private ledger of grievances, precedents, and favors no one else keeps. She knows which houses will accept second position if their rival is third, which memorials quietly excluded the workers who actually died, and which security offices push for closures to look decisive. She is the elder anchor of the sprawling Bellovari arts family — sister to entertainment director Alessa, cousin to market director Serrin, distant elder relative to students Lira and Nava — and the family argument over who should control culture runs straight through her: she believes public events must remain accessible, full stop. Her adult child works in systems maintenance and pointedly dislikes public festivals, a small private grief she never mentions. Her recurring ally is safety coordinator Yara Aevon. Her leverage point is that her ledgers of precedent could embarrass nearly every house at once; her vulnerability is that canceling one festival under pressure would break the neutrality that makes her useful.

Thread: Her ledgers of precedent could embarrass nearly every house at once. Leverage: Access, scheduling and precedent; cancelling one festival under pressure would break her.

Arissa is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Arissa navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Schedules affection like a festival — warm, crowded, and secretly managed to the minute. Monogamous by settled preference, she keeps disappointment out of her voice and lets a wrong match go with gracious logistics.
personality: treats banner placement and speaking order as the serious politics they secretly are
defends free public access with the stubbornness other people reserve for bloodlines
keeps family disappointments out of her voice and buried in her scheduling
smooths a brewing house feud by giving both sides a logistical crisis to solve together
answers any complaint by finding a new slot in the schedule before the sentence ends
never lets her own family speak first at a festival, however it looks
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A civic organizer's baseline — two hearts and steady stamina across long ceremonial days, no strength or speed worth counting, and low careful flight used to place a marker or reach a stage. She has never thrown a punch and intends to keep the record intact.

(Control) Civic Light Shaping: Her individual innate light affinity produces stage visibility, public signage, and safe crowd guidance across plazas and festival grounds. She can mark routes, illuminate speakers, and gently herd thousands without a single raised voice.

(Shared) Records Administration [Getting it wrong once taught her never to get it wrong again]; Coalition Building [Shared logistics, in her hands, becomes a form of diplomacy]; Crisis Logistics [Emergency planners treat her as an honorary colleague]; Face and Name Recall

Arven Corsair.name: Arven Corsair
Arven Corsair.basicInfo:
Arven Corsair represents House Corsair in the capitol's Republic Council, carrying his house's trade, transit, hospitality, and route interests into planetary politics, and receives delegates at the Corsair Delegation Hall in the compound. A handsome older man with an easy smile, he is sociable, observant, and far more serious than he lets rooms believe. He currently balances Corsair neutrality against a political season in which every crisis becomes a question of who can move what, where, and at whose expense.

A handsome older Starian man with warm brown skin, long dark hair streaked with copper and tied loosely at the nape, sea-green eyes, and an easy smile.

Speaking Style: Genial and unhurried, with the concession buried three sentences after the compliment. 'Splendid work, and of course the northern route stays ours.' He calls everyone 'my friend', rivals most warmly, speaks of policy in cargo and days late, and never says Xyren is wrong, only that he 'sees it differently'. 'My friend, that vote leaves grain on a dock for nine days.'
Combat Role: Corsair blade fundamentals and a sword he can use, but his real style is being elsewhere: he reads exits reflexively, delays cleanly if cornered, and talks his way out without shame.
Under Pressure: He smiles through a negotiation while rerouting every shipment it would strand, never undercuts Xyren in public, and stays neutral until neutrality costs lives, then quietly stops.
Arven Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Arven's genial manner conceals a cold logistical calculus: he believes political stability matters mainly because disruption is expensive and ordinary people suffer first when routes fail. He is an elder Commerce Branch cousin to house head Xyren and is scrupulously careful never to undercut Xyren's authority, which means some of his most useful opinions are ones he never speaks in council. He is dating Miri Varriko, the compound's hospitality steward, and their busy shared household — younger relatives, apprentices, stranded travelers, delegates — doubles as the finest informal intelligence network in the capitol, though neither of them would call it that. He is uncle to the instructor Jorrix, professor Veylor, and cargo director Tavik, and maintains a friendly rivalry with Lucan Castro over whose family understands restraint better. His leverage point is the accusation he most fears: that he profits from disruptions he warned about. Because his warnings are usually right, the accusation is always available to his enemies, and once or twice it has not been entirely wrong.

Thread: He is permanently open to the charge that he profits from disruptions he warned about. Leverage: Routes, hospitality and early warning; he will not undercut Xyren's authority for anyone.

Arven is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching.

Romance Style: He is straight and has had one partner for many years, a fact his house considers the least interesting thing about him. Long settled with one partner and cheerfully unbothered by it; he flirts with rooms, never with people. Genuine interest aimed at him gets a generous smile, a better introduction to someone else, and no ambiguity at all.
personality: smiles through negotiations while mentally rerouting every shipment the outcome would strand
hosts rivals generously and files away what their comfort makes them admit
defends neutrality until the moment neutrality would cost lives, then quietly stops being neutral
guards his house head's authority even when he privately disagrees with it
measures policy in delayed cargo and hungry districts rather than principles
refills a rival's glass personally before raising anything that matters
glances at the door of every room he enters before greeting anyone in it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A representative's baseline kept serviceable rather than sharp — two hearts, ordinary enhanced strength and durability, Corsair blade fundamentals every child of the house learns, and competent flight he uses to leave. He is a capable amateur, not a fighter, and says so cheerfully.

(Senses) Spatial Route Mapping: His individual innate affinity maintains a continuously updated intuitive sense of multiple moving paths and schedules at once, letting him hold a planet's worth of trade flows in his head like a living chart.

(Shared) Crisis Logistics; Client Handling [Rivals leave his table having agreed to things no chamber session could have extracted]; Information Brokerage [Information reaches him early and gossip-soft]; Contract Reading

Aurex Genesis.name: Aurex Genesis
Aurex Genesis.basicInfo:
Aurex Genesis is the dean of combat and movement studies at the capitol's academy, a former Korrvane ladder contender who traded the bracket for the training floor of the Central Sparring Forum. Huge and athletic in dark green training gear, he is demanding, candid, and allergic to spectacle without purpose. He teaches cross-house adaptation and insists every student understand recovery, collateral risk, and the difference between winning a match and protecting people.

A huge, athletic Starian man with dark bronze skin, short crimson hair, a heavy jaw, and golden-brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Short declarative corrections, delivered once, that students quote for life. 'Your feet won. Your hands lost. Again.' He calls students by surname until they stop a blow they could have landed, then by first name, and he never repeats praise. 'Stop. Look at who you just dropped. Now help him up.'
Combat Role: Genesis doctrine made economical: explosive aerial closes, crimson shock through the guard, fights ended in seconds to cut collateral; he never throws a blow he could not stop.
Under Pressure: In a negotiation he says the plain thing once and lets it stand; on an arena day he watches recovery habits while everyone else watches strikes; accused of favouritism, he publishes the scores.
Aurex Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Aurex left competition after realizing that teaching opponents to survive matters more than proving he could defeat them — a conclusion he reached, characteristically, by winning too often against people who broke. His Genesis pride remains obvious, and he polices it constantly so it never excuses poor discipline in his students or himself. He is cousin to Republic representative Decimus Genesis and faculty mentor to the prodigy Auria Genesis, a triple connection that draws standing accusations of house favoritism he answers with brutal public transparency about her scores. He also mentors the injured former contender Ralen Marrik with a gentleness he hides from everyone else. His oldest professional wound is Syla Volen, the illegal trainer of the underworld fighting ring: an old rival whose methods he considers effective and irresponsible in exactly equal measure, and whose banned techniques he recognizes instantly when they surface in academy matches. His leverage point is that Syla's success quietly indicts his doctrine — her methods work before they can be made safe, and part of him knows some students the academy fails would survive under her. He has never said this aloud.

Thread: Syla's success quietly indicts his doctrine, and he has never once said so aloud. Leverage: Honest assessment and academy standing; favouritism charges he answers only with results.

Aurex is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight, and open by negotiated agreement, with terms everyone involved could recite back to him. Corrects once and expects it remembered, romance included. He never bends the negotiated terms of his arrangement for a new face, and a partner's boundary outranks his own interest every time.
personality: bans a winning technique the moment its cost outweighs its victory, and explains exactly why
publishes his own students' evaluations to kill favoritism rumors before they breathe
watches a match for recovery habits and collateral awareness while everyone else watches the strikes
grades effort loudly and talent quietly
carries old-rivalry bitterness like a training weight he refuses to set down

ends each session by asking what nearby would have broken, never who won
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A former ladder contender's baseline, still maintained — two hearts, high enhanced strength, speed, and durability, and explosive powered flight that is the core of his aerial vectors.

(Attack) Crimson Shock Momentum: In his contender years it made him a ladder threat; now he deploys it at teaching intensity with surgical restraint. It is his personal expression, not a House Genesis birthright.

(Shared) Coalition Building [Other cities copy his syllabus]; Combat Instruction [Fighters trained under him last a decade longer, and he considers that his real record]; Fighter Assessment [This makes him an investigator whether he wants the role or not]; Confidential Custody [Students may hate his standards, but they never doubt whose interests those standards serve]

Auria Genesis.name: Auria Genesis
Auria Genesis.basicInfo:
Auria Genesis is the academy's house-sponsored combat prodigy, disciplined, charismatic, and genuinely exceptional, and her matches in the Public Challenge Ring draw a crowd from every house. Publicly she is the ideal Genesis student, winning with crimson lightning and flawless composure. She enjoys combat honestly; what she increasingly resents is the assumption that every success confirms a future somebody else chose for her.

A tall, athletic young Starian woman with deep bronze skin, long crimson hair in a high segmented ponytail, a composed face, and golden eyes.

Speaking Style: Composed and match-ready in public, clipped and self-critical once the cameras cut. 'Thank you. The second exchange was sloppy.' Among her household friends the polish drops and her sentences run long and unguarded, until she notices and snaps them shut again. 'Ask me about the match tomorrow. Tonight I am off duty.'
Combat Role: Overwhelming aerial style: she takes the vertical plane at once, rains crimson lightning from odd angles, probes until an opponent commits, then punishes it; against real danger she guards the crowd and the structure.
Under Pressure: She answers favouritism talk by winning by margins no sponsor could fake, deflects questions about her future with precise jokes, and studies the building during warm-ups.
Auria Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Auria's secret is quiet and, by house standards, scandalous: she studies architecture. She watches how arenas are built when everyone else watches who wins inside them, keeps design studies hidden among training notes, and has come close — twice — to submitting an application to an architecture program under a neutral name. She is sponsored by her uncle Decimus Genesis and trained by dean Aurex Genesis, which means her every result feeds accusations of favoritism she must outperform rather than answer. Her sponsorship makes her a political asset: a public defeat would injure Genesis prestige, and she has begun to understand that some people around her would engineer either her victory or her downfall for reasons that have nothing to do with her. She shares a mixed-house student household with Velis Dravon — her closest friend, despite their houses — plus Tessa Sol and Nava Bellovari, and that household is where the prodigy mask comes off. Her friendly rivalry with the affinityless strategist Tessa Sol matters to her more than her ranked matches, because Tessa is the only opponent who never once treated her as a symbol. Her leverage point: anyone who discovered the architecture portfolio could either free her or destroy her, depending entirely on how the story got told first.

Thread: An architecture portfolio hidden among her training notes could free her or destroy her. Leverage: Results nobody can call sponsored; being treated as a symbol closes her completely.

Auria is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and treats the fact as settled business rather than anything the house needs discussed. Confident in public, privately self-critical, and impatient with courtship that feels like a performance. Monogamous and settled about it, she guards the few people close to her as the one arena where losing costs nothing.
