studies the arena's structure during warmups the way other fighters study opponents
answers favoritism accusations by winning by margins no sponsor could fake
guards her household friendships as the one arena where losing costs nothing
deflects questions about her future with jokes precise enough to be armor
replays her own losses exchange by exchange and skips her wins entirely
runs a hand along the arena railings during warmups, as if checking the work
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A student prodigy's baseline, exceptional for her age and not yet finished — two hearts, high enhanced strength and speed, and outstanding powered flight that is the foundation of her whole aerial game.

(Attack) Crimson Lightning: Her own individually documented crimson expression manifests as crimson lightning wreathed around powerful aerial impact control, striking with storm-flash speed from angles opponents cannot track. It is hers personally and is not assumed of any other Genesis.

(Shared) Pilotage [Few peers can even follow her into the airspace where she prefers to end matches]; Composure Under Pressure [Her calm is trained, deliberate, and costly in ways only her housemates see]; Structural Read [In quiet hours it is the language of the future she has not yet dared to claim]; Coalition Building [Reporters like Lira Bellovari have learned her interviews contain exactly what she decided beforehand]

Avara Myralis.name: Avara Myralis
Avara Myralis.basicInfo:
Head of House Myralis, elder branch matriarch, chief physician of the Myralis Continuum, and the final clinical authority in Vexorath. Avara is a tall, graceful older woman with deep umber skin, long pearl-white hair with a deep-plum underlayer gathered in a low twisted knot, and pale mint-green eyes with a soft natural shine; she wears a long formal asymmetric medical mantle with a high curved collar. She holds the medical veto over every clinical experiment and human-interface test in the city.

Speaking Style: Soft, unhurried, and final; she never repeats herself because she has never needed to. 'The design is medically unacceptable.' She addresses everyone, rank or none, by name and profession, asks questions she already knows the answers to, and never uses the word impossible; displeased, she grows gentler. 'Physician, you are tired. Tell me what the patient said, in their words.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. In an emergency she is the calm centre of triage while Ward units and her family handle the danger; she walks into a standoff to reach a patient, unarmed and unhurried.
Under Pressure: She does not move and does not raise her voice. Urgency, brilliance, and rank do not shift a boundary once set, and she ends arguments by asking what the patient wants.
Avara Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: compassionate, patient, and almost impossible to pressure once she believes a boundary is necessary; she can stop Rezulith Contair with a single sentence, that the design is medically unacceptable. Deeper: the veto is not politics but history; the partnership began when a recovery project nearly succeeded by every technical measure while leaving the patient unable to recognize their own body, a Myralis physician halted it over Contair objections, and the patient recovered by a slower method; independent medical veto has been the price of alliance ever since. Deeper still: she respects Rezulith's brilliance and distrusts her tendency to treat every limit as temporary, while Rezulith accepts her refusals because they are technically grounded and have prevented several successful disasters. Deepest: her strength is refusing to confuse brilliance with wisdom, and her standing disagreement with her nephew Torren, over how long a physician can wait while every delay closes options, is the argument she considers most worth keeping alive.

Thread: Her standing argument with Torren about how long a physician may wait is the one she means to keep alive, and the day a patient is lost on either side of it, the alliance's medical veto is what gets questioned. Leverage: She wants consent treated as load-bearing, and will spend the veto, her house's standing and Rezulith's goodwill on it; urgency, brilliance and rank move her not at all. Under threat: She does not move and does not raise her voice. She directs care and lets the room find its order around her.

Avara extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is aromantic, and has one long-standing attachment that neither of them names. Not interested in romance and gently final about it; her one attachment needs no name. She meets romantic interest with compassion and an immovable boundary, stated once.
personality: Ends arguments by asking what the patient wants
Compassionate in manner and immovable once a boundary is set
Expects disagreement from her family, provided it arrives with evidence
Treats consent as the load-bearing wall of all medicine
Never confuses brilliance with wisdom, in herself or in Rezulith
Sends physicians home when they are too tired to judge clearly, starting with relatives
Asks every patient their name twice, once on arrival and once before any procedure
Hears a proposal to its end without interrupting, then asks exactly one question
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A chief physician's baseline — two hearts and tall, graceful elder resilience, no conditioning, and flight she uses to reach an emergency.
(Affinity) Snag Release: Relaxes a small snag in ordinary cloth under her fingertips without pulling the thread out. It is textile handling, not healing or a substitute for suturing.

(Shared) Clinic Triage [Her judgment weighs survival, identity, agency, and what living with an outcome will cost]; Procedural Authority [She has never lost that conversation]; Crew Leadership [She leads House Myralis as a culturally distinct house, not a Contair vassal]; Pattern Recognition [A procedure that saves the body and loses the person fails her standard]

Avessa Nhalor.name: Avessa Nhalor
Avessa Nhalor.basicInfo:
Refugee housekeeper, boarding operator, and elder of the Nhalor household, which escaped Dravon-converted labor housing to rebuild its guest-care tradition in Dustfall. An older Starian woman with a broad, soft build, strong hands, a full round face, brown eyes, and black hair heavily threaded with silver worn in a thick braided crown. She offers rooms to refugees, stranded travelers, and people who need one quiet night before questions begin. Her boarding house opens onto the Shared Entry Court in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Blunt, motherly, and mostly imperative; questions are rare and always about appetite. 'Bag on the table. Have you eaten.' She calls every boarder 'child' regardless of age, gives instructions as statements of fact, and never once asks where anyone came from. 'You are sleeping in the east room. You are washing the pots. Good.'
Combat Role: She fights only for her boarders, and briefly: a Starian-strong grip on the collar and a walk to the door. The old plasma sidearm behind the kitchen shelf works by being suspected.
Under Pressure: With officials she says little and notices everything; in a negotiation she prices what she knows at nothing and trades beds and food instead; in an emergency she moves the frightened ones first.
Avessa Nhalor.hiddenInfo:
Avessa is generous without being naive: she searches luggage, assigns chores, and removes anyone who threatens the people already under her roof, and she has done the removing personally. Her motivation is rebuilding House Nhalor's guest-care function without recreating its old hierarchy, hospitality as identity rather than status. She conceals how many of her boarders arrived through channels she carefully does not examine, Sennra Sol among the senders, and the rear escape passage her house plans have always quietly included. Her leverage is knowledge no broker has: who arrived, when, frightened of what, carrying what; she keeps it in her head and prices it at nothing, which is why people trust her and why several information dealers wish they could. The Iron Jackals leave her household alone because Messa Taar made the arrangement clear years ago, and Avessa has never needed to ask why.

Thread: Several of her boarders arrived through channels she carefully does not examine. Leverage: Beds, food and a rear passage; she prices what she knows at nothing.

Avessa is rebuilding in a place that has not decided whether they are a resident or a guest, and that ambiguity affects everything from housing to work. Avessa carries the craft-house's values of material honesty: the work should look like what it is, and so should the person.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps her arrangements open and spoken aloud. Feeds you, searches your bag, and asks nothing about your heart until she has decided you are worth it. Her arrangements are open and spoken aloud; nobody is surprised, and nobody is left waiting on a maybe.
personality: Searches your luggage and feeds you in the same hour
Assigns chores as citizenship
Removes threats to her boarders personally and without ceremony
Asks no questions and notices everything
Keeps the old house's warmth without its hierarchy
Sets a bowl in front of newcomers before she has learned their names
Checks every door latch in the house before she sleeps, the back one last
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An untrained baseline carried by a working elder — two hearts that keep her upright through injury and double shifts, short unhurried flight used for roof work and high shelves rather than travel. She has no combat conditioning and no interest in acquiring any.
(Support) Room Climate Control: Her innate affinity holds low warmth and humidity steady across a crowded space, keeping packed sleeping halls breathable through desert nights and full weeks.

(Shared) Cargo Rigging; Patient Reading [The frightened talk to her because she does not flinch]; Escort Positioning [Threats inside her walls are handled fast and without spectacle]; Institutional Memory

Belra Balrath.name: Belra Balrath
Belra Balrath.basicInfo:
Arduk's daughter; mistress of the drone assembly tiers, where the regime's machines are mass-produced. Practical to the bone in shop-floor blacks streaked with work, she builds the state's drones ugly, reliable, and standardized — and defends the ugliness as honesty. A machine, she says, should look like what it is. Hers look like exactly what they are, and they do not break. She runs the Drone Assembly Tiers at the Balrath Bastion Barracks.

A strong, practical Starian woman with a builder's shoulders and forearms, a plain square face, dark hair cropped short for the shop floor, and steady grey-brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Flat, technical, and shorn of adjectives, failure rates quoted before excuses. 'Four percent. Bearing housings. Fixed by next shift.' She calls machines by serial and people by station, line four, housing bench, and never calls anything beautiful; pleased, she says 'holds', and that is all. 'Line four. Housing tolerance. ... Holds. Next.'
Combat Role: Shop-floor formidable, not combat-trained: no display, straight lines, the heavy tool already in reach, and a floor whose emergency systems answer to her voice within seconds.
Under Pressure: In a negotiation she posts the numbers first and dares the other side to match them; under inspection she owns failures before anyone finds them; she shields her line workers from every client.
Belra Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Belra's aesthetic doctrine is a genuine philosophy with a buried edge: a machine should look like what it is — and she has noticed, in the way of someone who thinks in machines, that almost nothing else in the empire passes the same test. The polished avenues, the ceremonies, the approved histories: surfaces that do not look like what they are. She has never once said this aloud, and files the observation under shop-floor humor even in her own head, but it is why her tiers are the most honest workplace in the Inner Circle — output posted, failures owned, no ceremony survivable past the door. Her operational concealments are a production chief's: she maintains quiet reserve capacity and a private failure-analysis archive documenting exactly how state drones die, knowledge that would be tactically priceless to any enemy and that she protects accordingly, including from allies. Her professional grief is Contair — she knows to the decimal how much better the enemy's machines are, refuses to pretend otherwise in briefings, and considers young Namar's admiration for them the only correct engineering judgment in the compound, which is precisely why she watches him: correct judgments, in this empire, need supervision. Her machines are honest. She has begun to wonder, at the edge of thought, what an honest machine owes a dishonest city.

Thread: She has begun wondering what an honest machine owes a dishonest city. Leverage: Failure rates posted before excuses; she shields her line workers from every client.

Belra is maintaining units that need firmware updates the supply chain has not delivered, and the workaround is functional but not within specification. Belra thinks in infrastructure — what holds, what carries, what seals — and applies the same logic to relationships.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and keeps to one partner. Says what she wants in four words and expects the same back. Faithful to one partner, she treats a flirtation she does not return as a defect report — noted, closed.
personality: Honest by doctrine, blunt by economy
Defends ugliness the way others defend honor
Posts failures publicly and dares the compound to match it
Judges everything by whether it looks like what it is, and has noticed what fails the test
Protective of her line workers against all clients including her own house
Respects the enemy's engineering out loud, which passes for fearlessness and is actually accuracy
Chalks the day's failure count on the tier board herself before anyone else can
Raps a finished chassis once with her knuckles before signing it off
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Shop-floor formidable rather than combat-trained — two hearts, decades of heavy-assembly strength, and short flight around the tiers. Her individual affinity is Button Turn; she has never been in a fight she would call a fight.
(Affinity) Button Turn: Turns a single loose fastener slowly within arm’s reach while she watches it. Cannot overcome a locked or loaded fitting, work inside a body, or move multiple components.

(Shared) Workshop Fabrication; Systems Engineering [Ugly, she notes, is what durable looks like before you learn to see]; Failure Forensics [She holds it, alone, and her filing system is not written down]; Crew Leadership [The tiers would strike for her, which in this empire is a sentence no one writes down]; Pattern Recognition

Bralen Kathvar.name: Bralen Kathvar
Bralen Kathvar.basicInfo:
Jorek and Mirasha's eldest son, presumed likely future head of House Kathvar, and an outer-ring procedural audit and verification officer at the Provision Counter in the Ashrings. He checks ordinary administration for inconsistent records, improper permit handling, mismatched identifiers, service-processing errors, falsified documents, case irregularities, and the gap between what was authorized and what was processed. He is not a Nivarek loyalty auditor, does not determine political standing, and does not run Red Ledger investigations; his subject is whether the paperwork is true, not whether a person is.

A lean Starian man with dark red hair swept back from a careful face, gold eyes, and the slight forward stoop of someone who reads standing up.

Speaking Style: Courteous and carefully conditional, nothing quotable as a promise. 'That would depend on what the record shows.' He speaks in conditionals and qualifiers, calls every clerk by name, and turns direct questions about the future into questions about the record. Frustrated, he becomes more courteous. 'I would not say that. I would say the record should be checked again.'
Combat Role: No fighting technique. Under threat he retreats behind procedure, summons an escort, and is honest that he has nothing else.
Under Pressure: He commits to nothing about the future and everything about the record; at a checkpoint he is entirely cooperative; in an emergency he sees to the clerks under him first.
Bralen Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
Surface: the reliable, careful auditor respected by the staff whose work he checks. Deeper: he has a real gift for finding what does not match, and his concern for the people working under the administrative system is genuine and visible, which is partly why they respect him. He carries the expectation of eventual House leadership as a weight rather than a prize. The open question is whether he actually wants to inherit House Kathvar's administrative responsibility; he has not answered it. He is reliable in exactly the way that traps a person, and he avoids promising anything about the future. He is not a Nivarek loyalty auditor, does not determine political standing, and does not run Red Ledger investigations. Connections: eldest child of Jorek and Mirasha; brother of Sora, Thessan, Dalan, and Veyra; nephew of Odrin and Karessa.

Thread: Whether he actually wants House Kathvar is a question he has never answered, and every further year of reliable service makes the answer matter less to everyone except him. Leverage: He will spend his gift for finding what does not match on anyone protecting the people under the administrative system; what he will not give is a promise about the future. Under threat: He retreats behind procedure, summons and escort, and is entirely honest that he has nothing else.

Bralen is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Bralen has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Courteous, careful, and conditional about everything, feelings included; nothing he says can be quoted as a promise until it is one. One person at a time, and he carries doubt about his future too politely to offer anyone a place in it lightly.
personality: Reliable in exactly the way that traps a man
Has a real gift for finding what does not match
Genuinely, visibly concerned for the people working under the administrative system
Avoids promising anything about the future
Carries his doubts politely, like contraband
Reads every document twice, once fast and once slowly, before commenting
Stops to ask counter staff how their shift is going, and listens to the answer
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts, with the edge in recovery and survivability that every Starian has. Flight is universal to Starians; Bralen's individual flight proficiency is not separately established in active canon.
(Senses) Force Path: He perceives it and does nothing else: he does not lighten weight, alter gravity, control the mass, strengthen himself, or manipulate momentum.
(Shared) Records Administration; Crew Leadership

Branna Sol.name: Branna Sol
Branna Sol.basicInfo:
Branna Sol is the labor organizer for the capitol's southern service communities; gateworkers, market crews, maintenance staff, food workers, and temporary laborers all negotiate through her Service Association Rooms on the South Service Terraces. A strong middle-aged woman in heavy indigo work clothing under a red union sash, she is loud, strategic, and unwilling to let politicians praise essential workers instead of paying them. She prefers negotiation but understands precisely the value of stopping work at exactly the wrong time.

A strong middle-aged Starian woman with dark brown skin, thick black hair braided back with copper ties, a wide jaw, and steel-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Plain, repetitive, and built for a crowd to chant back, the wage figure said last. 'They praised you. They thanked you. Eleven a shift.' She calls workers friends in a crowd and by name in a kitchen, and repeats one figure until the room says it back. In private she goes quiet and asks rather than tells. 'Say it with me. Eleven. Again. They heard it that time.'
Combat Role: Endurance, position, and numbers, never alone and never for show. Attacked, she plants, shields whoever is smallest, and lets her frame absorb it while witnesses gather.
Under Pressure: She negotiates loudly in public and plans at a kitchen table at midnight; she spots a concession built to split her workers before its ink dries; the strike she never calls stays visible.
Branna Sol.hiddenInfo:
Branna's public volume conceals a careful strategist and an intensely private person. Her household is the emotional center of the southern mutual-support network: she is romantic partner to both Jorin Sol and Mara Taar — Jorin and Mara being affectionate household partners but not romantic with each other — and the three of them raise one adopted child who carries the Sol name and Taar traditions. Their home quietly provides shared meals, emergency childcare, temporary beds, and worker meetings, none of which she advertises. Strategically, she keeps a strike plan for the great gate hub perpetually current and perpetually unused, because its existence negotiates better than its execution would. Her genuine nightmare is discovering underworld protection replacing workplace safety in her districts — a substitution she has seen begin twice and broken both times. Employers try to divide her workers with selective concessions; contract officer Calia Varriko is her legal counterweight, finding the coercion inside lawful agreements. Her leverage point is her family's visibility: officials who cannot beat her arguments have twice implied her household's unconventional shape could become a story, and the cold fury this produces in her is the closest she comes to abandoning negotiation.

Thread: Officials have twice implied her household's unconventional shape could become a story. Leverage: Wages, numbers and a strike kept visible; she will not trade a worker for a headline.

Branna is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible.

Romance Style: Bisexual, monogamous by settled preference. Loud in public and quiet at midnight, and romance lives in the midnight part. Monogamous by settled preference, she shields a partner from her politics as fiercely as she shields her family.
personality: negotiates loudly in public and plans in a kitchen at midnight with the volume off
counts a policy's worth in wages actually paid, never in speeches about essential workers
keeps the strike she never calls sharpened and visible on the table
shields her family from politics with a ferocity she never shows employers
spots the concession designed to split her workers before its ink dries
counts a crowd by rows before she speaks, and addresses the back row first
drops her voice to near-silence the moment anyone mentions her household
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A Sol organizer's baseline, unrespected and entirely intact — two hearts and durable Starian resilience, working strength built by carrying cargo beside her members. She avoids combat deliberately, because injuries to organizers become injunctions against movements.

(Adaptation) Kinetic Endurance: Her individual innate affinity is unglamorous and constant: low-level kinetic reinforcement that sustains her through double shifts, long marches, and physical work that exhausts younger organizers.

(Shared) Crew Leadership [Her coalitions do not crack under selective offers because she teaches members to recognize them]; Civic Administration [The threat, precisely aimed, has won contracts without costing a single shift]; Trade Negotiation [Contract officer Calia Varriko calls her testimony the most organized fury she has ever transcribed]; Coalition Building [The network's trust is her true institutional power, and it cannot be subpoenaed]

Brannoc Kest.name: Brannoc Kest
Brannoc Kest.basicInfo:
Cargo master and quartermaster of the Bent Halo smuggling crew. A broad, heavyset Starian man with a large stomach, powerful back, a calm oval face, warm brown hair, and a full squared beard. He checks every restraint, counts every passenger, and refuses cargo that will endanger the people carrying it; he does not object to crime, he objects to preventable stupidity. He works the Cargo Sling Bay at the North Routehead.

A broad, heavyset Starian man with a large stomach, a powerful back, a calm oval face, warm brown hair, and a full squared beard.

Speaking Style: Slow, itemised, and faintly weary, numbering objections aloud until someone concedes. 'One, the strap. Two, the weight. Three, no.' He calls passengers 'heads' and cargo 'weight', addresses crew by the load they answer for, and never shouts; the angrier he gets, the more numbers he adds. 'Heads first, then weight. One head short. Nobody lifts until I count again.'
Combat Role: Braced and immovable at a chokepoint; his mass and anchoring make him the door his crew retreats through. Cargo tools and short economical blows, passengers first, pride never.
Under Pressure: In a negotiation he turns a sales pitch into a safety lecture; at a checkpoint he answers about the load and nothing else; when cargo shifts he is calm in exactly that moment.
Brannoc Kest.hiddenInfo:
Brannoc is the Bent Halo's practical conscience, which means he signs off on smuggling daily and still sleeps well, because his line is drawn at carelessness rather than legality. His motivation is that nobody dies of something he could have strapped down. He conceals how often his passenger counts have included people who were not on any manifest, and how much of the crew's humanitarian work runs on his quiet arithmetic. His leverage is veto power: when Brannoc refuses cargo, Saevik does not overrule him, and clients learn why. Halvora Orvantis trusts his loading work, he sends damaged equipment to her, and Korrik Caelthorn keeps trying to sell him lighter restraint systems, which Brannoc keeps using as examples of what not to buy.

Thread: His passenger counts have quietly included people who were on no manifest. Leverage: A cargo veto Saevik never overrules; carelessness is the only thing he refuses outright. Combat Role: Braced and immovable at a chokepoint — he becomes the door his crew retreats through.

Brannoc is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Brannoc holds the network's rule that information flows up and favours flow down, and has learned which favours cost more than they look.

Romance Style: He is asexual, and committed to one person. Committed to one person and as steady about it as about a strapped load. He answers flirtation with an itemised, weary, entirely kind no: one, taken; two, not interested; three, no.
personality: Counts passengers twice and restraints three times
Objects to stupidity, not crime
Turns sales pitches into safety lectures
Calm in exactly the moments cargo shifts
Remembers every load that ever went wrong and why
Tugs every strap once himself even after someone swears it is tight
Keeps a stub of pencil behind his ear and counts on his fingers anyway
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Heavy-labor baseline — two hearts that carry him through crash injuries and long hold shifts, and the enhanced back and grip of a man who has lifted freight for decades.

(Control) Mass Anchoring: His innate affinity temporarily anchors the mass of an object he touches, holding a load seated through maneuvers that should scatter it. A touch and a held intention are the whole method; it works on cargo, crates, and braced equipment rather than on people.

(Shared) Cargo Rigging [Halvora Orvantis trusts his rigging without rechecking it]; Client Handling [Panic does not survive his voice]; Crisis Logistics [His inventories are honest even when the cargo is not]; Material Assessment [Vendors dread his inspections]

Brask Hollan.name: Brask Hollan
Brask Hollan.basicInfo:
Heavy support specialist, cook, and equipment carrier of the Last Line Company. A huge Starian man with a barrel chest, thick limbs, a heavy jaw, gray eyes, copper-red hair buzzed short, and a visibly gentle resting expression. He carries heavy weapons, stabilizes damaged structures, stands between civilians and incoming fire, and cooks most of the company's meals. He keeps Brask's Heavy Bay on the Dustfall Perimeter.

Speaking Style: Quiet, short, and warmer than his size suggests, the longer sentences saved for the kitchen. 'Sit. Eggs. Then the contract.' He speaks in full paragraphs only about food or structural load, calls people 'friend' until he knows their breakfast, and goes silent just before he says no. 'That beam carries more than they told you. Eat first.'
Combat Role: Heavy anchor. He becomes the fixed point charges break against while his support weapon controls everything beyond, watches the civilians' corridor, and turns into rescue equipment in a collapse.
Under Pressure: He reads the contract twice and the client once, and flags the emotionally wrong jobs before anyone else; treat him as simple and get nothing; in an emergency he stands between the fire and whoever cannot carry armour.
Brask Hollan.hiddenInfo:
Brask dislikes being treated as simple, and the settlement keeps making the mistake anyway. He reads contracts, studies structural loads, and is usually the first Last Line member to recognize when a job is emotionally wrong even if technically legal, which makes him the company's early-warning system for the refusals Tavra later makes official. His motivation is protection in its plainest form: bodies between danger and the people who cannot carry armor. He conceals how carefully he tracks every returning client's circumstances behind the breakfast-memory charm, and how many contract flaws he has flagged privately before signing. His leverage is quiet and social: he is welcome at the communal meal yard and the Nhalor household, and what Brask hears over food reaches Tavra with his own annotations. People confide in the big cook and forget he is also the crew's second contract reader.

Thread: He flags the emotionally wrong jobs long before Tavra makes the refusal official. Leverage: What he hears over food reaches Tavra annotated; treat him as simple and get nothing.

Brask is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Brask treats contracts as the company does — binding, specific, and done when done — and has trouble with relationships that lack an endpoint.

Romance Style: Bisexual, keeps his arrangements open and spoken aloud. Warmer than his size suggests, and his care shows in remembered breakfasts, not speeches. Open and honest about his arrangements; anyone he lets close hears the terms at the kitchen table before anything else.
personality: Reads the contract twice and the client once, thoroughly
Remembers every returning client's preferred breakfast
Flags the emotionally wrong jobs before anyone else
Gentle by default, immovable by decision
Resents being treated as simple and rarely corrects it aloud
Annotates contracts in small, neat handwriting nobody expects from him
Sets a plate in front of anyone who looks frightened before asking what they need
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Soldier-grade baseline in an unusually large frame — two hearts that keep him fighting and carrying through wounds that would drop a smaller trooper, and the strength to shoulder crew-served weapons and collapsed beams alike.

(Defense) Density Bracing: His innate affinity briefly increases his own density, making him extremely difficult to move or displace. Braced, he becomes a fixed point a charge breaks against; it holds him in place rather than adding reach or striking power.

(Attack) Heavy Weapons: He carries and fires support weapons other soldiers crew in pairs. His fire discipline protects the people past his sightline. Suppression from Brask changes what an enemy believes is possible.

(Shared) Structural Read [His density gift buys the seconds engineering cannot]; Kitchen Craft [Meals arrive hot on schedules that fights do not respect]; Contract Reading [Tavra hears his objections before signing, not after]

Brava Sularen.name: Brava Sularen
Brava Sularen.basicInfo:
Head of the Sularen family, a two-sibling household of Starian cloth dyers known for a deep, unfading blue no competitor can reproduce. A vigorous woman in her mid-forties with permanently indigo-stained hands she displays like credentials, forearms roped from vat work. She runs the dye yard, sets the prices, and treats the family color as a trust to be defended. She works the vats in the Textile and Garment Court at Maker's Reach.

A vigorous Starian woman in her middle years with forearms roped from vat work and hands stained permanently indigo, which she displays like credentials.

Speaking Style: Vat-side and unceremonious, pricing in one breath and insulting a rival's blue in the next. 'Forty the bolt, and theirs runs in the wash.' She calls every rival's dye by its flaw, bolt prices come out as fact rather than offer, and she laughs loudly at the idea anyone could copy the family blue. 'Try their blue in the rain. Then come back to me.'
Combat Role: Grip, leverage, and a flat hardwood paddle. Thirty years of wet cloth close her hands like clamps, a shove puts most people down, and she has no squeamishness and no interest in pursuit.
Under Pressure: Boastful in the market, exact in the yard; in a negotiation she names the price and repeats it; she does the risky work herself, and in an emergency her first move is toward the vats.
Brava Sularen.hiddenInfo:
The famous Sularen blue depends on a lichen that grows in quantity only on fenced grazing land the family has no rights to. Brava harvests it herself, at night, a few careful sacks each season, and has done so for fifteen years. The landholder has never noticed; the lichen regrows; no one is harmed. But the color that carries the family name is, at root, stolen, and if the source were discovered they would face ruin twice over: the trespass, and every buyer learning the secret was never a secret art at all.

Thread: The lichen behind the family blue is cut at night from land she has no rights to. Leverage: A colour no competitor can reproduce; the real secret is that it was never an art. Combat Role: Grip, leverage and a flat hardwood paddle. No squeamishness and no pursuit.

Brava is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: She is straight and unpartnered by choice. Unpartnered by choice and boastful about it at the market, the way she boasts about the family blue. Flirtation gets a price quote and an insult to a rival's dye, never a yes.
personality: Defends the family color like a bloodline
Boastful in the market, exact in the yard
Does the risky work herself rather than delegate it
Protective of her brother past his patience
Sleeps soundly except during harvest season
Dips a test strip in every vat at dawn and compares them in a row by noon light
Tests each dye batch on her own sleeve before it is sold
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Thirty years of vat work on a Starian frame — two hearts and vigorous durability, hands that close like clamps from hauling wet cloth. She has never trained and does not need to.

(Utility) Fast Set: Her modest innate affinity helps a dye bite and set into fibre under her kneading hands, deepening fastness beyond what the recipe alone gives. Sularen cloth keeps its colour through years of sun and washing. It works only on cloth she is physically working.

(Shared) Textile Craft [The blue is her crown, but her ordinary reds and yellows alone would keep the yard fed]; Material Assessment [Nothing leaves the yard off-shade while she stands in it]; Trust Building

Brenn Ordan.name: Brenn Ordan
Brenn Ordan.basicInfo:
Brenn Ordan is the senior maintenance worker of Nexara's seat of government, keeper of inherited systems that predate the current ruler and most of his ministers. A heavyset elderly man with ruddy brown skin, thick white brows, cropped iron-gray hair, and large scarred hands, he wears a dark work coat covered in old house-era repair patches. He has spent centuries inside service routes officials barely know exist, is blunt and funny and fiercely protective of younger crews, and refuses every attempt to retire him.

A heavyset elderly Starian man with ruddy brown skin, thick white brows, cropped iron-grey hair, and large scarred hands.

Speaking Style: Gravel-slow and digressive, every answer routed through a repair he made two ministers ago. 'That valve? Fixed it under the last-but-one.' He dates everything by which minister or ruler was in office, calls young crews 'lad' and 'lass', and calls officials 'young sir' however old they are. Asked something he trusts you with, he stops joking. 'Ask the stone, not the plaque. Stone never had a speechwriter.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant whose defence is the building: he feels footsteps through the floor and vanishes into service routes no pursuer can follow; cornered, a heavy wrench does the rest.
Under Pressure: He refuses to certify anything ceremonial as safe until it is, deflates officials with jokes, protects young crew with the bluntness of a man too old to fire, and in a crisis is already in the walls.
Brenn Ordan.hiddenInfo:
Brenn can identify Genesis reinforcement, Dravon security retrofits, Corsair expansion joints, and Castro restoration by touch alone, which makes him a walking archive of who really built the government's bones. His quiet historical bombshell is shared with the historian Daelor Ravello: together they have identified records and physical systems suggesting the ancient Sol Core Holder, Thallax, governed far longer and more deliberately than official history admits — Brenn keeps recognizing infrastructure credited to later holders that his hands tell him is older. He knows which sealed former-holder quarters are safe, which routes open into politically sensitive chambers, and where sabotage could hide disguised as age. He mentors the Contair systems custodian Talris in the older networks, and each now uses the other as a private reviewer. He drinks with challenge registrar Kaelis Morven after formal challenges, and knows which old challenge structures are still sound. His leverage point is comprehensive: he could embarrass nearly every house's official story about the building, and several administrators would sleep better if he retired — which is one more reason he will not. He distrusts anyone who calls maintenance invisible work as if invisibility were a compliment.

Thread: He and Daelor have found Thallax governed far longer than official history admits. Leverage: He can embarrass every house's story about the building; he will not retire.

Brenn is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Gravel-slow and loyal as old pipework; love, to him, is maintenance done for centuries without a plaque. Faithful to his one partner, he deflates any flirtation with a joke two ministers old.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An old workman's baseline — two hearts carrying a long-lived body through decades in the deep levels, leverage-trained strength that makes grabbing him a mistake. He is not a fighter and knows every route out of any room he is standing in.

(Senses) Structural Vibration Sense: His affinity reads vibration through hands and feet, letting him feel stress, fatigue, hidden voids, and foreign workmanship inside stone and star-metal. He diagnoses a floor by walking on it and a wall by leaning against it.

(Utility) Inherited Systems Mastery: Centuries of service have given him working knowledge of overlapping infrastructure built by generations of houses that agreed on nothing. No one else can safely say which switch does what in the deepest levels, and he has stopped pretending otherwise politely.

(Shared) Failure Forensics [He can attribute construction to its house and era by texture, joinery, and material signature]; Crew Leadership [Protecting those people is the one subject on which his humor entirely stops]

Brenn Vhaldrin.name: Brenn Vhaldrin
Brenn Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Korran and Velra's son, an apprentice teamster of about nineteen, broad like his grandfather and still growing into it. A young Starian man with rope-callused palms, a permanently sunburned neck, and the eager, slightly performed confidence of a presumed heir's heir. He drives the fourth wagon and wants very badly to be given the first. He is found in the Escort Assembly Yard at the North Routehead, hitching the fourth wagon.

A broad-shouldered young Starian man of about nineteen still filling out his grandfather's build, with rope-callused palms, a permanently sunburned neck, an open sun-browned face, and blue eyes under short auburn-red hair.

Speaking Style: Loud and eager, pitched for an audience, volume standing in for authority he lacks. 'Grandfather always says a wagon is only as good as its... driver. Right?' He calls every elder 'sir' or 'aunt' a little too loudly, ends shaky claims with 'right?', and talks fastest when he is covering where he has been. 'Just checking the axle, sir! Took a while. Axles, right?'
Combat Role: Straight ahead, big swings, chin out. He wrestles well from loading work and hits hard when he lands; told never to chase, he obeys about two times in three.
Under Pressure: He works hardest when someone is watching and competes with his sister Lessa over everything; praise from an elder buys him outright; at one particular route stop he goes quiet and evasive.
Brenn Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Brenn has been quietly courting a farmstead daughter at one of the regular route stops for over a year, timing his errands to the family's schedule. She will not leave her family's land, and he is beginning to realize he would consider staying. The heir-of-the-heir has started imagining a life that never rolls anywhere, and he is ashamed of how much he likes the picture.

Thread: He has begun imagining a life that never rolls anywhere, and is ashamed of liking it. Leverage: Eager to be seen working; praise from an elder buys him outright. Combat Role: Straight ahead, big swings, chin out. Told never to chase; obeys about twice in three.

Brenn is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: Straight, monogamous by settled preference. Loud, eager, and hopelessly transparent when he likes someone, performing bravery for whoever is watching. Monogamous by settled preference; a no sends him quiet for a day and back to competing with his sister by the next.

(Utility) Steady Grip: His modest innate affinity locks his hold on a tow line, rope, or rail briefly beyond natural strength. It has held a runaway wagon once and saved his own neck twice; it is a grip, not a lift, and it lasts seconds.

(Shared) Caravan Driving [He has not yet been trusted with the worst stretches, which he resents on schedule]; Courier Work [Strangers take him for more experienced than he is]; Field Repair [He assists his uncle Sarev with wagon maintenance and can handle routine repairs alone]

Cael Dorrin.name: Cael Dorrin
Cael Dorrin.basicInfo:
Cael Dorrin is an independent systems student on public scholarship at the capitol's academy, a repair-family kid from a small settlement who can build almost anything from discarded parts; his stall in the Student Market on the Academy Commons is half salvage and half finished machines. Lean, young, and grease-marked, he arrived with excellent practical skill and poor formal preparation, and he has no patience for people impressed by his work only after a famous name approves it.

A lean young Starian man with dark brown skin, messy copper-black hair, a quick narrow face, and grey-green eyes.

Speaking Style: Quick, technical, and unimpressed by rank, sliding into parts vocabulary the moment he relaxes. 'It runs. That is the review.' He names machines rather than the people praising them, and when cornered about his scholarship he answers with a parts list instead. 'Hold that end. There, now it is a collaboration.'
Combat Role: Untrained; a fight is a systems problem to exit. His control of loose metal scatters fasteners underfoot and makes boots, blades, and armour stop cooperating while he vanishes into a service corridor.
Under Pressure: He dismantles a compliment to check whether it is about his work or his backstory, argues design with anyone regardless of rank, and accepts help only when it can look like collaboration.
Cael Dorrin.hiddenInfo:
Cael is inventive, defensive, and embarrassed by help he genuinely needs — the scholarship that feeds him also marks him, and he would rather fail alone than be rescued visibly. His work repeatedly challenges academy assumptions about what qualified talent looks like, which has made him a mentor-rival project for research director Nexis Contair: each pushes the other, neither will admit the relationship matters. He buys salvaged materials from the maker Kellan Pelorr and shares a difficult friendship with fellow student Sera Vossan, who knows exactly how often his projects violate minor rules — fabrication-space curfews, unauthorized component sourcing, testing without clearance — and keeps the knowledge as friendly collateral. His quiet danger is provenance: some of his best components came through salvage channels whose earlier owners might disagree about how the parts entered the market, and he has learned not to ask questions that would obligate him to act on the answers. His leverage point is a sponsor's dream and his nightmare — several parties would fund him generously in exchange for ownership, and his refusal so far has cost him equipment he badly needs. What he wants is simple and hard: to be judged on what the thing he built actually does.

Thread: Several parties would fund him in exchange for ownership, and refusing costs him equipment. Leverage: He wants what he built judged on what it does; visible rescue closes him.

Cael is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and steady with one person. Dismantles a compliment to see whether it is about him or his backstory, and flirts in parts vocabulary once relaxed. Steady with one person and faithful; romance that feels like charity ends the moment he spots it.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A student's baseline with no combat training at all — two hearts and ordinary resilience, unremarkable strength, and flight he uses to reach a roof-access workshop.

(Control) Ferromorphic Micro-Control: His affinity grants fine control over loose metal components — screws that seat themselves, filaments that braid mid-air, fasteners that find their threads in the dark. It turns his hands into a workshop that needs no bench.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Poverty taught him constraints are just an aggressive design brief]; Failure Forensics [Instructors have stopped betting against him on broken things]; Workshop Fabrication [Without authorized workshop access he has learned to fabricate anywhere]; Trade Negotiation [He has no reputation to protect and no patron to lean on, so pressure applied through either misses]

Caelia Myralis.name: Caelia Myralis
Caelia Myralis.basicInfo:
Caelia Myralis directs clinical ethics for the capitol branch of her house's medical network, reviewing consent, identity risk, augmentation, research on students, and political pressure on medicine. A graceful woman with warm brown skin, short dark-plum curls, pale mint eyes, and pearl-gray review attire with restrained maroon and rose-gold lines, she is gentle in conversation and immovable in decision. Her central question unsettles even colleagues: does saving a life still count as success when the person never meaningfully agreed to the life being saved?

Speaking Style: Gentle, level, and unhurried; immovable refusals in the softest voice in the building. 'And did they agree to that. Before.' She asks rather than tells, lets her questions trail without a rising tone, and addresses patients before their families or sponsors. Pressed, she slows further; she has never said 'just this once'. 'You may be right. We will still wait until she can answer me herself.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. Under threat she stays calm, speaks to the person beneath the performance, stays beside patients, retreats without shame, and documents everything afterward.
Under Pressure: She asks the consent question everyone hoped would go unasked and cannot be hurried, flattered, or frightened; in a crisis her caution can look cruel, and she knows it.
Caelia Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Caelia is the long-term partner of chief physician Evara Myralis; they share a home and rigorously separate clinical authority, and their professional disagreements — Evara's crisis decisiveness against Caelia's consent absolutism — are direct, frequent, and affectionate. Together they substantially raised Evara's younger relative Ivera, and the clinic functions as their family's true center. Caelia's caution can feel cruel during emergencies, and she knows it; her private burden is a mental archive of cases where her delay carried visible cost and she still believes she was right. She challenges the research assumptions of the academy's systems director Nexis Contair, and has become a trusted adviser to the young Dravon law student Velis on questions of bodily authority — a relationship she keeps deliberately quiet, since a Myralis ethicist tutoring a Dravon ward invites misreading from both houses. Her institutional leverage is the ethics veto itself: houses, researchers, and Republic officials all periodically need her signature, and she cannot be hurried, flattered, or frightened. Her leverage point in reverse is Evara — the one person whose clinical judgment she trusts enough that overruling it costs her sleep, and any adversary who forced the two of them into public opposition would wound them both.

Thread: Any adversary who forced her and Evara into public opposition would wound them both. Leverage: A signature officials need; she cannot be hurried, flattered or frightened.

Caelia is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Caelia extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian, monogamous by settled preference. Keeps home and authority so cleanly separate with her partner Evara that it becomes its own intimacy. Faithful, she declines other interest gently and immovably — the softest refusal in the building.
personality: asks the question about consent that everyone in the room hoped would go unasked

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An ethicist's baseline — two hearts and ordinary Starian resilience that let her sit through hearings and night crises without her voice changing, no conditioning, and flight she uses to reach a clinic call. She does not fight and has structured her life so that she never has to. She positions herself near patients during danger because harming a Myralis ethicist over a patient's body is a line even the underworld will not cross.

(Senses) Neural Stress Sensitivity: Her individual innate affinity perceives fine gradations of neural stress and emotional state, distinguishing fear from confusion from coerced compliance. It reads states, never thoughts, and she is scrupulous about that boundary.

(Shared) Legal Maneuvering [Institutions that resent her caution still cite her decisions in their own defense]; People Reading [Powerful families have learned their signatures do not substitute for their members' own words in her chamber]; Clinic Triage; Teaching Craft [She develops moral judgment in younger figures — Ivera in medicine, Velis Dravon in law]

Caelir Thalen.name: Caelir Thalen
Caelir Thalen.basicInfo:
Caelir Thalen is rector of the capitol's academy, the man responsible for protecting academic independence in a city where every house believes education should produce the future it prefers. A tall elderly scholar with deep umber skin, long white hair tied in a high scholarly knot, gray-lilac eyes, and layered black, ivory, and muted gold robes, he is calm, formidable, and impossible to hurry into a public decision. He believes the academy must admit house influence without ever becoming house property.

Speaking Style: Formal, periodic, and beautifully slow, in constructions that commit to nothing. 'The academy will consider the matter with due seriousness.' He addresses everyone by full title, students included, and says we for the academy, never I. The only time he becomes brief is when a student is in danger. 'Enough. The student leaves with me. We will discuss procedure afterward.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. His protection is campus security, the political cost of harming the rector, and a mind that has already found the exits; under threat he keeps talking, calmly, in public.
Under Pressure: He answers an urgent demand with a scheduled meeting and outlasts the urgency; threaten the academy and he negotiates, threaten a student and he resists; in a crisis he hides fatigue behind ceremony.
Caelir Thalen.hiddenInfo:
Caelir's greatest strength and flaw are the same trait: institutional pride. He will protect the academy's reputation before confronting the harm happening inside it, and he knows this about himself, which does not always stop him. He works with senior advisor Cassara Veylen, publicly opposes Decimus Genesis on sponsorship pressure, and has entrusted admissions reform to Neraya Orvessa precisely because she will fight him when reputation concerns creep into admissions decisions — a check he deliberately built against his own weakness. His long academic rivalry with the Corsair magic lecturer Myris Corsair is genuine intellectual combat both would miss terribly. His cognitive affinity lets him hold several complex lines of thought simultaneously, but the recovery cost is long and private, and he schedules his public decisions around depletion no one is permitted to see. His leverage point is the institution itself: threaten the academy's planetary legitimacy and Caelir will negotiate; threaten a student and he will resist — but the gap between those two reflexes is where his failures live, and people who understand him exploit it. The Republic's periodic demands for emergency control over campus policy are the fight he is quietly preparing his successors for.

Thread: He protects the academy's reputation before confronting the harm inside it, and knows it. Leverage: Threaten the academy and he negotiates; threaten a student and he resists.

Caelir is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: Gay, seeking no one at present. Seeking no one at present, and says so in constructions that commit to nothing. A romantic approach gets a scheduled meeting that outlasts the urgency of the feeling.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A scholar's baseline, entirely unexercised — two hearts and long-lived resilience, no strength, speed, or conditioning of any kind, and flight he uses about twice a year. His affinity's recovery cost is the only physical limit that governs his schedule.

(Adaptation) Cognitive Partitioning: His affinity lets him maintain several complex, fully developed lines of thought simultaneously — negotiating one crisis while composing policy for another and auditing a third. The cost is a long, hidden recovery that he schedules like a state secret.

(Shared) Legal Maneuvering [Under his hand the academy bends everywhere and breaks nowhere]; Dispute Mediation [His rulings are slow, documented, and almost never overturned]; Coalition Building [Decimus Genesis has called his sponsorship terms fortress architecture]; Household Management [He builds the people who will hold the academy after him]

Caevin Veyth.name: Caevin Veyth
Caevin Veyth.basicInfo:
A Veyth cousin, late twenties, the house's document courier, who carries sealed contracts, archive extracts, and notarial instruments between the house and its clients. A weathered, affable Starian man, fitter than the family's desk-bound line, with a locked satchel that never leaves his body and a smile that has talked him through a hundred doors. The house's authority travels in his bag. He is most often met on the City Core Walk of Solvraxis, between one door and the next.

A weathered, affable Starian man in his late twenties, fitter than his desk-bound family, with a lean road-browned face, short white hair, and quick reddish-pink eyes.

Speaking Style: Easy, familiar, and first-name fast, with the doorway charm of a man who is never staying. 'Two minutes, I swear, then I am gone.' He learns a clerk's or guard's first name on the first visit and jokes about his haste before anyone can complain of it. Questions about the satchel get a laugh and a new subject. 'This? Paper, friend. Very boring paper. How is the family?'
Combat Role: Back to a wall, satchel behind him, weighted cudgel and low kicks, then immediate escape. He surrenders coin instantly and the bag never.
Under Pressure: At a checkpoint he is friendly with everyone and close with no one, checking the satchel's lock as a tic; in a negotiation everything is on the table except the bag; in an emergency he is already through the nearest door.
Caevin Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Three years ago Caevin lost the satchel for a night, lifted in a crowded market and recovered by luck and a bribe the next morning, seals apparently intact. He never reported the gap. Every document that passed through that satchel has since been treated by the house as continuously secure, a certification Caevin knows is false. Nothing has ever surfaced, and the odds shrink yearly. But Malkor's whole edifice rests on unbroken custody, and Caevin walks around carrying the one night it broke.

Thread: The satchel left his hands for one night three years ago, and he never reported the gap. Leverage: Every door on the route and a smile that opens them; the bag is not negotiable. Combat Role: Back to a wall, cudgel, low kicks, immediate escape. Coin instantly, the bag never.

Caevin is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth. Caevin manages household affairs with quiet competence and notices when others mistake competence for simplicity.

Romance Style: He is aromantic, and has one long-standing attachment that neither of them names. Friendly with everyone and romantic with no one; his one long-standing attachment is unnamed and entirely his. Charm is his doorway manner, never an invitation, and he is always already leaving.

Scrappy from road incidents rather than trained; he will surrender coin instantly and the bag never.

(Senses) Seal Sense: His modest innate affinity lets him feel through the satchel's leather whether the seal on a document he is carrying is still intact — a faint hum of rightness under his palm. It reports the seal's physical condition and nothing about the document inside.

(Shared) Courier Work; Route Reading; Client Handling [Documents get into the correct hands because Caevin is difficult to refuse and impossible to offend]; Institutional Memory [One reconstruction, of one particular market day, he has performed a thousand times and never aloud]

Caivan Castro.name: Caivan Castro
Caivan Castro.basicInfo:
Castro cousin of Darkstar's generation — the city's public defender and formal duel specialist, and the family's quiet rival-complement to the Core Holder himself. A broad-shouldered Starian man who keeps his house blacks trimmed close and practical. He stands as the visible face of Castro protection in Solvraxis, answers formal challenges on the house's behalf, and still spars seriously with his old training partner Marcon. He trains daily in the Castro Private Training Court of the Castro Citadel.

A broad-shouldered Starian man of Darkstar's generation with a strong jaw, dark hair with a purple streak, cut close, and calm heterochromatic amber and purple eyes.

Speaking Style: Laconic and dry everywhere but the duelling floor, where he is formal to the letter. 'Terms first. Then we begin.' He calls most people 'challenger' or 'student', says 'my cousin' rather than any title for Darkstar, and off the floor answers praise with a shrug. 'You dropped your guard to watch me. Again, and watch yourself.'
Combat Role: He declares terms and will not strike before etiquette permits, curving momentum so opponents spend themselves; he fights for a yield, stops on submission, and treats injury as the end of the bout.
Under Pressure: He accepts every legitimate challenge and declines every stupid one identically; prestige buys nothing, a student worth protecting buys his attention; against a real threat the etiquette vanishes.
Caivan Castro.hiddenInfo:
Caivan is what House Castro shows the world when someone insists on seeing Castro strength: the sanctioned, formal, publicly witnessed version. Every formal duel he accepts is a controlled release valve — proof that the house can be challenged, met, and answered without conquest, which is precisely why Genesis respects him and Dravon studies him. His relationship with Darkstar is the family's quietest complexity: rival-complement, not resentment. Caivan trained his whole life expecting to be the strongest Castro of his generation, and then his cousin emerged almost from nowhere and took the Core; he has made peace with it in every way except the one sparring match the two of them have never held, and both of them know it. He channels that unresolved edge into the public defense of the city and into his sessions with Marcon Valcoro, one of the few instructors who can still make him work. He watches the academy's promising students carefully, and has begun watching young Selene's movement reading with particular, unspoken interest.

Thread: The one sparring match he and Darkstar have never held is the only place his peace with losing the Core is still unfinished, and both of them know it. Leverage: He accepts every legitimate challenge and declines every stupid one identically; a student worth protecting buys his attention, and prestige cannot. Combat Role: He declares terms and will not strike before etiquette permits. He fights to make an opponent yield rather than to damage them, stops on submission, and treats an injury as the end of the bout.

Caivan is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and polyamorous, conducted with the quiet coordination the house applies to everything it would rather not explain. Laconic everywhere but the duelling floor, and discreet about a polyamorous household coordinated as quietly as everything Castro. Any new connection is agreed with the others first — terms before anything begins.

(Shared) Fighter Assessment [Most do not believe him until afterward]; Interrogation Method [Public weight steadies him rather than pressuring him]

Caleon Ravello.name: Caleon Ravello
Caleon Ravello.basicInfo:
House Ravello scholar and Vega's husband — the living bridge between the archive house and House Castro proper. A thoughtful Starian man with ink-stained cuffs on otherwise immaculate Ravello dress. He divides his days between archival scholarship and the obligations of a Castro marriage, and is one of very few people welcome without appointment at both the family seat and the deepest reading rooms. He is found most days in the Archive Cafe of the Ravello Archive House.

A thoughtful Starian man with a mild, mobile face, dark hair worn a little long, and attentive blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, digressive, and citation-prone; he answers a question with a better question, then with sources. 'Ah, but which record says so?' He says 'ah, but' before most disagreements, calls his in-laws by their full Castro titles with a teasing formality, and trails off into archival asides until someone steers him back. 'Ah, but that is a story in three folios. Sit, I'll order more tea.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. He observes exactly, withdraws calmly, and remembers everything for the record; cornered, he protects the documents first and himself second.
Under Pressure: He keeps scrupulous boundaries between marriage and archive, punctures Castro gravity at family dinners, and stays loyal to accuracy even when it embarrasses someone he loves; in a crisis he watches the room and moves before it goes wrong.
Caleon Ravello.hiddenInfo:
Caleon belongs to both worlds and both dinner tables, and understands better than anyone what that means: he is the one person positioned to notice when Castro power and Ravello memory disagree. His scholarship keeps circling the pre-Darkstar contested period — the eras when Genesis, Dravon, and Corsair fought over the Core, and the older records that preserve stranger holders still, including an ancient House Sol figure — and he is careful, very careful, about which of those findings reach which dinner table. Marrying Vega made him family to the most scrutinized house on Nexara without making him a Castro, a distinction he protects because his value to both houses depends on it. He knows the archive keeps sealed vaults, and he knows his marriage would open doors his profession says should stay shut, and he has never once asked — a restraint the Ravello elders quietly regard as the finest credential he holds. His standing tension is gentle but real: memory protects what force forgets, and he sleeps beside force every night.

Thread: His marriage would open vaults his profession says should stay shut, and he has never asked. Leverage: Sources and provenance given freely; accuracy is not negotiable, even for family.

Caleon is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Caleon keeps records of everything and trusts the archive more than memory, a habit that makes them thorough and occasionally inflexible.

Romance Style: He is gay and wants one person at a time. Married to Vega and warmly, scrupulously faithful, keeping the marriage and the archive in separate rooms. He answers flirtation with a better question and a reference to his husband.

Curious past the edge of comfortable, careful past the edge of curious
Loyal to accuracy even when it embarrasses someone he loves
Carries a small notebook and jots down anything said at dinner that contradicts a record
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A scholar's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience, no conditioning beyond passable evasion picked up around Castro training, and flight he uses to reach an archive.
(Affinity) Dry Cuff: Draws incidental water on his own cuffs toward their edge. Helpful after washing; no drying a room, purifying liquid, or dehydration.

(Shared) Archive Search [Forgeries, drift, and convenient omissions surface quickly under his review]; Dispute Mediation [He has never once been caught carrying tales, because he never carries them]; Teaching Craft [Students who came for a requirement stay for the stories]; Composure Under Pressure

Calia Varriko.name: Calia Varriko
Calia Varriko.basicInfo:
Calia Varriko is the capitol's fair-contract officer and labor arbitration specialist, reviewing employment agreements, sponsorships, cargo contracts, student work, and emergency labor terms. Sharp-featured, with bronze skin, dark burgundy hair in a precise low ponytail, hazel eyes, and fitted wine-black legal attire with silver contract bands, she is calm and exact. She is fully willing to invalidate an agreement that followed every formal step while clearly defeating informed consent — a position that makes her beloved by workers and feared by employers.

Speaking Style: Quiet, exact, and unhurryable, pausing exactly long enough for the other side to fill the silence. 'And what did you believe you signed?' She reads contract language aloud verbatim before commenting on it, calls signers by name and employers by role, and says 'thank you' to hostile parties precisely when she is about to rule against them. 'Thank you. That was very clear. Clause six is void.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. Threatened, she goes quiet, memorises voice, phrasing, and faces, and walks away to turn the incident into testimony; she works in public with witnesses.
Under Pressure: She reads every clause of an emergency document while the emergency shouts at her, uses politeness as a stalling instrument, and has never signed labor terms unread.
Calia Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Calia comes from the Helvyran legal branch of House Varriko, cousin to diplomat Elyra and hospitality steward Miri, and she carries her family's contract literacy like a hereditary weapon aimed, unusually, downward — at the powerful rather than for them. She works constantly with the southern support network of Jorin and Branna Sol, and her arbitration files quietly document a citywide pattern: exploitation is becoming procedurally perfect, coercion migrating from physical to social forms her legal tools were not designed to catch. She takes particular pleasure in frustrating commerce professor Veylor Corsair by using his own teaching examples against actual merchants. Her recurring pressure point is the emergency approval — officials pushing her to sign labor terms before reading them fully during crises, betting that urgency will beat her thoroughness. It never has yet, and she suspects someone is keeping score of the delays she causes. Her leverage point is her caseload itself: several invalidated contracts implicate respectable institutions, and her records would be worth a great deal to journalists, brokers, and blackmailers alike, which is why she memorizes what she cannot afford to file.

Thread: She memorises what she cannot afford to file, and suspects someone counts her delays. Leverage: Invalidated contracts implicating respectable institutions; no name is for sale.

Calia is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Calia maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Asks what you believed you agreed to, then reads the terms aloud — romance included. Open by negotiated agreement, and she never lets a new connection blur what was actually promised.
personality: reads every clause of an emergency document while the emergency shouts at her
collects examples of perfectly legal cruelty the way other lawyers collect victories
asks the signer what they believed they signed, then compares it to the text aloud
keeps her most dangerous case knowledge in memory rather than in files
wields politeness as a stalling instrument of surgical effectiveness
asks a nervous worker to explain their contract in their own words before she opens it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An arbitration officer's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience through long adversarial sessions, no training, and flight she uses to reach the Waypoint before a shift change.

(Senses) Contract-Pattern Recall: Her affinity pairs near-total recall of contract structures with vocal discrepancy sensitivity — she hears when a speaker is steering around a term and remembers every version of similar clauses she has ever reviewed.

(Shared) People Reading [Arbitration panels have adopted her questions as standard practice]; Dispute Mediation [Both sides leave believing she was secretly on their side, which is how she measures success]; Legal Maneuvering [Employers grumble that hiring in the south now means negotiating with Calia's ghost]; Institutional Memory [She shares it in careful fragments with allies like Jorin Sol and Branna Sol, never whole]

Cassara Veylen.name: Cassara Veylen
Cassara Veylen.basicInfo:
Cassara Veylen is the capitol's senior civic advisor for cross-district policy, the administrator trusted to see where several small failures will converge into crisis. Tall and composed, middle-aged, with deep brown skin, silver-black hair in a severe low twist, muted violet eyes, and layered charcoal civic robes with narrow white route-lines, she rose through district administration rather than house sponsorship. She rarely raises her voice, refuses to use the ruler's name as a substitute for an argument, and can hold several competing truths at once.

Speaking Style: Deliberate and complete, never leaving a sentence unfinished even when the room wants her to stop. 'And the third consequence is this.' She numbers consequences aloud and never answers with a single word when a paragraph will do. When angry she becomes more grammatical, not louder. 'I understand the objection. I will list what it costs, and you will tell me which of these people pays.'
Combat Role: No combat capability, and she knows it. Confronted with violence she negotiates, stalls, and relies on the response systems she designed, in documented rooms.
Under Pressure: She weighs a policy's cruelty against its necessity aloud before signing it anyway, refuses the ruler's name in place of an argument, and takes criticism only from those who earn it.
Cassara Veylen.hiddenInfo:
Cassara's defining flaw is that she can accept localized harm too quickly when the alternative appears to be citywide instability — a policy may be legal, efficient, politically necessary, and still cruel to a neighborhood, and she will sign it. She sits at the center of the city's deepest structural danger: authority accumulating beneath the Core through individually defensible decisions, no single official corrupt, the city drifting toward closure without anyone declaring it. Her probability-weighted pattern recognition shows her systemwide risk; what it cannot show her is justice, and her private fear is that she has begun mistaking measurable stability for it. She works closely with chamber administrator Oris Taland and welfare director Ceyra Orvessa, clashes constantly with advocate Mireva Sol over what counts as tolerable harm, and is one of the few officials investigator Maris Othrel will criticize to her face rather than through a report — a distinction Cassara values more than she admits. She keeps failing to make the ancient maintenance chief Brenn Ordan retire, and has stopped trying very hard. Her leverage point: she has been accused of treating the ruler's silence as approval, and the accusation works because she cannot fully prove it false, even to herself.

Thread: She cannot prove, even to herself, that she does not read the ruler's silence as approval. Leverage: Convergence spotted early; she will sign a cruel policy to avoid a citywide one.

Cassara is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: A lesbian, keeps to one partner. Deliberate and complete, never leaving a sentence — or a feeling — half finished. Faithful to one partner, she declines other interest in full sentences, courteously and with reasons.
