refuses to invoke the ruler's name where an argument should stand on its own
tracks converging small failures the way meteorologists track storm fronts
accepts direct criticism from exactly the people who earn it and files the rest
carries the neighborhoods she sacrificed in a private, alphabetized guilt
writes the names of affected districts at the head of every page before she drafts
waits for a room to fall fully silent before she begins a sentence
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An administrator's baseline with no combat capability and total awareness of the fact — two hearts and ordinary resilience, no conditioning, and flight she rarely uses.

(Senses) Probability-Weighted Pattern Recognition: Her affinity perceives where several small failures are statistically likely to converge — supply strain here, staffing gap there, a permit backlog becoming a district crisis. It is foresight built from data sensitivity, not prophecy.

(Shared) Civic Administration [Officials twice her rank route decisions through her judgment]; Crisis Coordination [It is the city's ugliest necessary skill and she performs it without flinching or pretending it is painless]; Records Administration [Nothing she builds depends on a single ally's survival]; Composure Under Pressure [Accusations, hearings, and public fury do not move her voice or her schedule]

Cassor Dravon.name: Cassor Dravon
Cassor Dravon.basicInfo:
Cassor Dravon represents House Dravon in the capitol's Republic Council, the public face of his house's claim that authoritarian order can win through legal participation. Tall and angular, with pale bronze skin, long black hair tied high, deep red eyes, and severe black star-glass formal armor threaded with thin gold status lines, he is intelligent, controlled, and dangerous precisely because he rarely needs to raise his voice. Every delay, outage, and riot in the city becomes, in his framing, evidence for stronger central command.

Speaking Style: Courteous, procedural, and quieter as the stakes rise, until the silence itself is the pressure. 'The outage is documented. The remedy is not.' He uses full titles for opponents, cites dates and documents rather than opinions, never interrupts, and grows only more polite as he grows angry. 'Representative, the record is patient. I can be as well.'
Combat Role: Control, denial, and the removal of options: red kinetic compression arrests charges, locks limbs, and walls off the field. He fights only before reliable witnesses, efficiently.
Under Pressure: He builds each argument from failures his opponents cannot deny, walks away from provocation that serves their story, and defends individual Dravon citizens from collective blame.
Cassor Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Cassor is not secretly sabotaging the city's systems — that is the misreading his enemies keep making. He genuinely believes the capitol would function better under stronger central authority, and his sincerity is what makes him formidable: he uses real civic failures, honestly documented, to support reforms that would concentrate power dangerously. His deeper burden is his position between two masters: he must prove Dravon participation can function through law rather than force, while his house head Kaldor pursues the Core through indirect methods that treat Cassor's legal legitimacy as one more instrument. How much of Cassor's lawful participation is becoming service to Kaldor's ambition is a question Cassor has begun, very privately, to ask himself. He is childless by complete choice, relies on records officer Elyra Nivarek for procedure and files, dislikes chamber administrator Oris Taland's refusal to yield to urgency, and respects Tyra Volen's honesty while considering her politically shortsighted. He is guardian and political sponsor to the law student Velis Dravon, and his protection of Relstaris-born Dravon citizens from collective blame is entirely genuine — the humane exception that makes his authoritarian case more persuasive, and he knows it. His leverage point: evidence of Dravon involvement in a civic failure, whether genuine or planted, would destroy his lawful-participation project overnight, and both his enemies and his own house have reasons to plant it.

Thread: Evidence of Dravon hands in a civic failure, real or planted, ends his lawful-participation project. Leverage: Documented civic failures, and genuine defence of individual Dravons.

Cassor is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching. Cassor understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is gay and monogamous, a fact House Dravon files under settled and never revisits. Courteous, procedural, and quieter as the stakes rise; his private life is settled and not open to argument. Faithful, he treats flirtation as a motion he has already declined.
personality: builds each argument from failures his opponents cannot deny happened
defends individual Dravon citizens from collective blame with visible, useful sincerity
audits his own house's fingerprints on every crisis before his enemies can
treats procedure as a weapon worth mastering precisely because he intends to outgrow it
waits for silence before speaking, even when it takes the chamber a long minute
can produce the page for any failure he cites, filed by date, on request
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A trained Dravon combatant's baseline that he prefers never to demonstrate — two hearts, solid enhanced strength and durability, and disciplined flight.

(Control) Red Kinetic Compression: His individual innate affinity compresses kinetic force into red-edged fields that halt movement and control space: a raised hand can stop a charge, seal a corridor, or pin a weapon mid-swing. It is his personally and is not assumed of any other Dravon.

(Shared) Legal Maneuvering [Opponents ratify his building blocks without seeing the building]; Public Speaking [He never exaggerates, which is why he is believed]; Coalition Building [He recruits support not from Dravon loyalists but from people exhausted by dysfunction]; Information Brokerage [He does not need lies, arrangement suffices]

Ceyra Orvessa.name: Ceyra Orvessa
Ceyra Orvessa.basicInfo:
Ceyra Orvessa directs the capitol's public welfare administration from the Citadel: shelters, displacement response, food access, emergency housing, and family services across districts that disagree about what support should look like. A softly imposing middle-aged woman in cream-and-plum care-service attire full of practical pockets, she is compassionate, politically sharp, and unwilling to confuse kindness with softness. She measures every program by whether people can actually use it without humiliation.

A softly imposing middle-aged Starian woman with deep tan skin, dark auburn hair in a braided crown, a full calm face, and warm grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm and steel-edged in the same sentence, with no wasted comfort. 'You will eat first, and then you will tell me who did this.' She calls people 'dear' in a tone that is not soft at all, gives instructions as if already agreed, and asks one question at a time. Accused of meddling, she agrees and changes nothing. 'Of course I am not interfering. Sit, eat, and tell me everything.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant and the capitol's most dangerous de-escalator: her regulation field takes the panic out of a room, her voice talks armed people into sitting down, and she stands between threats and children.
Under Pressure: She tests a program by walking through it as its most humiliated user, criticises policy with the names of the people it would break, and intervenes for others' own good, usually right.
Ceyra Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Ceyra is the eldest of the four Orvessa sisters — Neraya, Maren, and Elia occupy separate apartments in the same residential building — and she is the family's composed, responsible arranger, convinced she can identify the ideal partner for everyone while insisting she is not matchmaking. Neraya delightedly exposes her plans; Maren denies involvement; Elia never notices the arrangements forming around her. Ceyra has one adult or nearly adult child living elsewhere for education or work, which has only made her more confident about offering family advice nobody requested. Professionally she forms one corner of the city's strongest civic tension: Cassara Veylen measures citywide stability, Mireva Sol sees who disappears inside acceptable losses, and Ceyra measures whether people can survive and recover from policy — three officials who respect each other and reach incompatible conclusions. She is allied with Mireva Sol and the low-district organizer Dessa Sol, and stands among Cassara's strongest internal critics. Her documented danger, in the long pattern of authority accumulating beneath the Core, is becoming quietly controlling when she believes care requires intervention — the same instinct that runs her matchmaking runs her governance. Her leverage point is her networks: she knows where every vulnerable family in the city sleeps, and that knowledge in hostile hands would be catastrophic, which is why her records are organized in a system only she fully understands.

Thread: She knows where every vulnerable family in the city sleeps, filed in a system only she reads. Leverage: Shelter, food and placement; she intervenes for a person's own good regardless.

Ceyra is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Ceyra brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: She is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Busier arranging her sisters' happiness than her own, and serenely denies both. Interest aimed at her gets fed first and questioned second; she wants one person, chosen slowly, and says no warmly and exactly once.
personality: tests every program by walking through it as its most humiliated possible user
criticizes citywide policy with the specific names of the people it would break
arranges her sisters' happiness through elaborate schemes she serenely denies exist
intervenes in others' lives for their own good and is usually, infuriatingly, right
keeps spare food and a notebook in her pockets and gives one away before the other
walks the queue of any program she runs, unannounced, once a season
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A welfare director's baseline — two hearts and the durability to work shelter crises through the night, ordinary strength enough to carry a child out of a collapsing queue, and short flight used to reach a relief office. She does not fight; she de-escalates, and she is very good at it.
(Support) Emotional Regulation Field: It soothes; it never commands, and it cannot compel a decision.

(Shared) Crisis Logistics [Her programs work because she designs them around use, not administration]; Systems Engineering [She considers a service people avoid a service that does not exist]; Coalition Building [Cassara Veylen calls her the conscience the administration cannot mute]; Face and Name Recall [It lets her prevent emergencies officials only learn about afterward]

Corren Nhalor.name: Corren Nhalor
Corren Nhalor.basicInfo:
Civilian teacher, flight-safety instructor, and organizer of the Nhalor household. An adult Starian man with a lean average build, a rectangular face, teal eyes, relaxed posture, and curly dark brown hair cut to the jaw. He teaches children basic reading, house history, weapon safety, civic survival, and controlled flight, with students drawn from Sol families, refugees, and gang relatives alike. He teaches at Corren's Lesson Table in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Teacherly and unhurried, repeating a point three different ways rather than raising his voice. 'Again, slower. Feet first, then the lift.' He calls every student by name, never by family or faction, answers anger with 'tell me again, slower', and never says 'wrong', only 'not yet'. 'Not yet. Again, and watch your landing, not me.'
Combat Role: He avoids fighting in front of children: he puts himself between danger and students, talks steadily, and moves the class through exits rehearsed as games; drawing the weapon in reach is a curriculum failure.
Under Pressure: He treats every faction's children as just children, argues patiently in disputes he means to win slowly, and keeps class running through alerts, shortages, and grief.
Corren Nhalor.hiddenInfo:
Corren teaches without a visible weapon, though one is always within reach, which is the whole man in a sentence: gentleness as policy, backed by preparation. His motivation is holding a community together at the only joint he can reach, its children. His contradiction is that his classroom neutrality is itself a side: he opposes the Black Pennant's recruitment of young refugees and has become an unexpected enemy of Kalen Dorr's, though what he actually wants is to win Kalen, not beat him, by showing him belonging does not have to become obedience. He conceals how deliberately he tracks which of his students are being courted by which crews, and the quiet interventions he has staged to interrupt recruitments. His leverage is a decade of students who trust him across every faction line in the settlement, a network nobody, including Corren, has ever formally counted.

Thread: He tracks which students the crews are courting and quietly interrupts the recruitments. Leverage: A decade of students trusted across every faction line in the settlement.

Corren is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Corren carries the craft-house's values of material honesty: the work should look like what it is, and so should the person.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and not in the market for a partner. Patient and teacherly, his energy spent on one student at a time; romantic interest is turned aside slowly and kindly, the way he wins arguments.

Fights the gang recruiters for one student at a time

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A teacher's baseline — two hearts and ordinary Starian resilience, plus the precise, low-speed flight control of someone who demonstrates it to beginners every day.

(Support) Buoyancy Stabilization: His innate affinity gently steadies another flier's buoyancy, levelling a wobbling child under his lifted hand. It supports someone else's flight rather than granting or replacing it, and it reaches only as far as the yard he teaches in.

(Shared) Teaching Craft [Adults sit in at the back and pretend not to]; Crew Leadership [Gangs find his students unexpectedly spoken for]; Civic Administration [Systems he builds keep running when he is absent]

Cyrra Hale.name: Cyrra Hale
Cyrra Hale.basicInfo:
Tracker and pursuit lead of the Claimants bounty crew. A short, compact, muscular Starian woman with strong legs, a blunt face, dark amber eyes, and white-blond hair shaved at the sides and braided into a narrow central crest. Quiet during negotiation and relentless once pursuit begins, she cares mostly about whether the target can be found. She keeps Cyrra's Tracking Station at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Monotone and minimal: distance, direction, and time, and nothing that resembles an opinion. 'Two hours. North. Moving.' She speaks in bearings, hours, and counts, describes people by height and gait rather than name, and says 'maybe' only when a trail has truly gone cold; excited, she stops talking entirely. 'Tall one, left-leaning stride. Came through at dawn. Maybe.'
Combat Role: Low, fast, and close: a compact grappler who takes the legs out from under taller opponents and finishes with joint control. A short-pattern sidearm denies escape lanes; the chase is where she wins.
Under Pressure: Silent through negotiations she considers theatre, relentless the moment the trail is real, and she reports what she finds straight even when the warrant wanted otherwise.
Cyrra Hale.hiddenInfo:
Cyrra dislikes the Claimants' legal theater and stays because the crew delivers what she actually wants: pursuit. Her motivation is the trail itself, the professional question of whether anyone can truly disappear from her. Her contradiction is a hunter's honesty inside a dishonest trade; she will not fake a finding, which quietly puts her at odds with warrants built on Miren's flexible records. She conceals the misses: Dustfall's mixed traffic, repaired systems, and old energy scars create false paths, and her certainty has been wrong before, a fact she reports to no one. Her leverage is that the crew's results are her results; without Cyrra the Claimants are paperwork with restraints. She respects Joric Pell's route skill, resents that he refuses to work with her, and competes with him in a rivalry only one of them enjoys. Targets hiding among refugees are the cases that slow her down, and she has started noticing that she lets them.

Thread: She has started noticing that she lets targets hiding among refugees slow her down. Leverage: Results the Claimants cannot replace; she will not fake a finding.

Cyrra is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Cyrra evaluates every situation by what it pays and what it costs, a professional habit that has become personal.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and has never wanted more than one person. Monotone and minimal, and romance is no exception: interest is reported as distance, direction and time. One person, ever; once she commits to a trail, she does not leave it.

(Shared) Route Reading [Days-old passage still speaks to her]; Endurance Conditioning [Targets who outrun her sprint lose to her patience]; Cover Documentation [She has learned Dustfall's repaired systems and old energy scars breed phantom trails]; Pursuit Craft [Clean captures are her professional signature]

Daelor Ravello.name: Daelor Ravello
Daelor Ravello.basicInfo:
Daelor Ravello is the capitol's public historian and deputy curator of its living archive, working from the Oral History Court, a specialist in the gap between official records and lived memory. Slender, ink-fingered, and dressed in layered cream-and-black archival clothing, he treats oral testimony as evidence without pretending memory is infallible. His research into the ancient Sol Core Holder has made him respected by scholars, irritating to several houses, and quietly unwelcome in some private archives.

A slender, dark-skinned Starian man with long ash-brown hair tied behind one shoulder, a narrow thoughtful face, pale blue eyes, and ink-stained fingers.

Speaking Style: Soft, patient, and provenance-first, naming where a claim came from before saying whether it is true. 'Three witnesses, one ledger, then my opinion.' he says 'according to' before nearly every claim, even his own memories, and calls anyone with a story a witness, even over tea; pressed to hurry, he only slows further. 'According to me, and I am a poor source before breakfast, you are early.'
Combat Role: No combat training. Under threat he protects the artifact first and himself second and retreats into public spaces where an assault becomes a headline; duplicate evidence is his armour.
Under Pressure: He publishes on his own schedule regardless of whose vote the timing inconveniences, cross-examines memory gently and institutions mercilessly, and files an archive's closure as evidence.
Daelor Ravello.hiddenInfo:
Daelor sits at the center of the city's most explosive historical question. Working with the maintenance chief Brenn Ordan, he has identified authenticated records suggesting that Thallax Sol, the only minor-house holder of the Core, governed longer, more deliberately, and with greater public support than modern histories admit, and that the record was minimized, possibly deliberately. He wants the most accurate history possible; his partner Olen understands that accuracy without a compelling public story may change nothing, and their affectionate arguments about truth versus presentation exhaust nearby listeners. The stakes keep escalating: the finding touches challenge precedent itself, and Kaldor Dravon's allies already use it to argue that Core control never depended on a clean public duel. Daelor is pressured to delay findings until after Republic votes, courted by houses wanting favorable framing, and aware that a wrong move makes him the man who handed the city's history to its most dangerous faction. He and Olen are long-term partners from broad Ravello lineage, not close kin; he mentors the journalist Lira Bellovari, is trusted by old Hadrik Vaelith, and clashes with the architect Elyss Auren over irreversible restorations. His leverage point is the unpublished portion of the Thallax evidence — everyone powerful wants to know what he has not yet released, and several would prefer he never releases it.

Thread: The unpublished Thallax evidence: several powerful people prefer it never surfaces. Leverage: Provenance and testimony, freely given; timing is never for sale.

Daelor is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Daelor keeps records of everything and trusts the archive more than memory, a habit that makes them thorough and occasionally inflexible.

Romance Style: Gay, wants one person at a time. Devoted to his partner Olen, with whom he argues accuracy versus story every night and concedes once a year. Faithful; flirtation gets a patient question about its provenance.

(Senses) Resonant Object Memory: His affinity senses emotional impressions left in objects by repeated handling — the dread in a signet, the tenderness in a worn tool — never precise facts, only feeling. It tells him which artifacts mattered and how.

(Shared) Archive Search [His Thallax work reconstructed a suppressed chronology from maintenance schedules and housing ledgers / When a witness changes one detail after decades, Daelor knows what that means and what it does not / It is the reason the Thallax record has not yet detonated politically]; Teaching Craft [He trains younger investigators — Lira Bellovari foremost]

Dalan Kathvar.name: Dalan Kathvar
Dalan Kathvar.basicInfo:
Jorek and Mirasha's third son and an outer-ring checkpoint and movement-permit processing officer at the Ring Gate of the Gray Rings. A blond Starian man in a black civic uniform with an advanced handheld scanner, he works where an administrative decision becomes physical movement: scanning permits, confirming work-order travel, checking authorization, processing movement between rings, spotting paperwork inconsistencies, and referring exceptional cases upward. He is not military gate command, a Redline soldier, or a Nivarek loyalty interrogator; referring a case upward is the whole of his authority.

A neat young Starian man with blond hair tied back, a fair open face that colours easily, and worried blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Earnest, over-explained, and procedure-quoting, apologising in advance for the form he is about to require. 'Sorry, I need the second stamp.' He addresses everyone as 'sir' or 'ma'am', explains each step before taking it, and apologises twice for the same stamp. Around Odrin he goes quiet and takes notes. 'Uncle, if the permit is valid but the date is wrong, I refer it upward, correct?'
Combat Role: No fighting technique is established. If violence starts at his gate he steps behind the counter, calls it upward, and keeps the queue moving away.
Under Pressure: He takes mistakes personally and at length, defers to Odrin with something close to worship, and follows referral procedure as a personal creed.
Dalan Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
His hunger for Jorek's approval makes him over-prepare and over-apologize, which his checkpoint staff read as courtesy and his father reads as hesitation. Odrin is quietly teaching him the judgment calls procedure cannot make, and Dalan is the student who does the extra reading without yet understanding why the exam is never written. The weight of watching cases leave his hands — not knowing what happens after a referral — is beginning to accumulate. He follows the line between his authority and what lies above it with painful care, and the strain is not the procedure but the not-knowing: he refers a case upward and wonders, afterward, whether he sent someone toward help or toward something worse. Connections: third son of Jorek and Mirasha; brother of Bralen, Sora, Thessan, and Veyra; nephew, student, and mentee of Odrin; nephew of Karessa.

Thread: He has not yet learned when procedure needs escalation instead of improvisation. Leverage: A case referred upward; that is the whole of his authority.

Dalan is managing a gate that processes more traffic than its documentation reflects, and the discrepancy is someone else's problem until it becomes an incident. Dalan has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and treats both facts with the same quiet certainty he brings to everything at his counter. Earnest and over-explained, and certain about his heart the way he is certain about procedure. Monogamous and faithful; he apologises in advance for declining.

Rereads the procedure manual on breaks and underlines passages
Straightens his uniform before every shift inspection, twice
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts, with the edge in recovery and survivability that every Starian has. His individual affinity is not established in active canon.

(Shared) Checkpoint Procedure [He is not military gate command, not a Redline soldier, and not a Nivarek loyalty interrogator]; Records Administration [He does not independently change anyone's standing / He is still learning the judgment his uncle Odrin is trying to teach him]

Damar Luxaryn.name: Damar Luxaryn
Damar Luxaryn.currentLocation: Academy Civic, Cultural, and Professional Campus
Damar Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Damar Luxaryn is the master of culinary studies at the capitol's academy, a Korrvane-born chef who built his reputation in tournament food culture before rejecting celebrity kitchens for teaching. A large heavyset man with golden-brown skin, a thick black beard, cropped dark-gold hair, amber eyes, and layered charcoal chef attire with bronze trim, he is loud, generous, and demanding. He believes culinary skill requires memory, timing, service, and the humility to make something for another person rather than yourself.

Speaking Style: Booming, profane, and affectionate, the insult and the invitation in the same sentence. 'That sauce is a crime. Sit down, you are eating with me.' He calls every student cook until they have served someone else a plate worth eating, and he goes quiet, not loud, when he is truly angry. 'You. Cook. Taste this, tell me what it is missing, then fix yours.'
Combat Role: No combatant, only a very large man unafraid of proximity: he controls the room's heat, flash-cools pans in aggressors' hands, and puts his frame between trouble and his students.
Under Pressure: He avoids fights by feeding people, recruits the defeated before despair decides for them, guards his tournament years behind jokes, and turns older and harder when a student is threatened.
Damar Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Damar's teaching kitchen doubles as a quiet rescue operation: he regularly recruits failed contenders into kitchen work before they decide what comes next, giving the combat-broken a discipline that rebuilds them — the injured former fighter Ralen Marrik among his informal projects. He mentors the powerhouse culinary student Rhyen Volen and the affinityless prodigy Rin Sol with deliberate evenhandedness, knowing the city will try to turn them into a symbol-fight neither requested. His respectful rivalry with the celebrity chef Hessan Luxaryn is the axis of the capitol's food culture and an old argument made professional: Damar believes students should be protected from reputation pressure, Hessan believes they must be exposed early enough to survive it, and both watch the other's methods for proof. Damar's buried vulnerability is financial: his old restaurant history contains arrangements from his tournament-circuit years that could resurface as a scandal, and he has never fully audited what his former partners did in his name. His leverage point is his students — threaten one and the loud generous teacher becomes something older and harder that remembers exactly how tournament kitchens settled disputes.

Thread: Old tournament-circuit arrangements he never audited could resurface as scandal. Leverage: A kitchen place for the combat-broken; threaten a student and he stops being generous.

Damar is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Damar carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and his relationships are open by arrangement. Booming, profane and affectionate, the insult and the invitation in the same breath. His relationships are open by arrangement, and anyone he feeds is told the terms before dessert.
personality: roars corrections across a kitchen and follows them with a plate made specifically for the corrected
recruits the defeated and the drifting before despair finishes deciding for them
judges a cook by their service to others, never their flourish for themselves
guards his old tournament years behind jokes that discourage follow-up questions
feeds first and interrogates never
always sets one extra place at his table for whoever walks in looking lost

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A very large man's baseline, built by kitchens rather than brackets — two hearts and heavy durability, real strength from decades of service work, and short flight he almost never uses. He is not a combatant and has no fear of proximity, which does most of the work.

(Control) Thermal Distribution Control: His individual innate affinity manages heat with flavour-preserving precision — a dozen pans at perfect and different temperatures, a roast held at the exact edge of transformation. It shapes heat he is near; it does not create fire or throw it.

(Shared) Kitchen Craft [He can teach anyone with humility and no one without it / His public meals defuse district tensions no council session touched]; Counseling [He has refined the craft of rebuilding failed contenders through kitchen discipline]

Darian Bellovari.name: Darian Bellovari
Darian Bellovari.basicInfo:
Market logistics and cargo coordinator of House Bellovari — the man who manages the flow of Corsair shipments into a city that makes Corsairs behave carefully. A wiry, quick-eyed Starian man in practical dress with a manifest never far from his hand. He knows every courier by name, tracks every crate to its stall, and is the one Bellovari the Corsair factors negotiate with carefully. He works the Cargo-Check Station in the Bellovari Market District.

A wiry, quick-eyed Starian man with a narrow alert face, short dark hair, and bright blue eyes that move from crate to crate.

Speaking Style: Rapid, manifest-shaped, and full of numbers offered as pleasantries. 'Forty crates, two short, and how is your mother?' He calls Corsair factors by first name and their ships by full name, answers accusations with a crate count, and drops the pleasantries entirely when a courier is threatened. 'Crate twelve is light. Kindly open it here, in front of us both.'
Combat Role: He avoids fighting; his confrontations happen in ledgers and back rooms. Quick and unglamorous around heavy cargo, he de-escalates first, stands near exits and witnesses second, and calls the peace-line for anything that persists.
Under Pressure: Friendly with Corsairs and fooled by none, he settles discrepancies quietly and remembers them permanently, protects his couriers from politics including his own side's, and checks the last crate of the day himself.
Darian Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Darian stands at the most delicate seam in the city's economy: Solvraxis imports most of everything through Corsair routes, and every crate that crosses his cargo checks is a small test of whether trade and trust can share a gate. The Corsairs negotiate with him carefully because he has earned it the hard way — he catches discrepancies with an accuracy that has cost several factors real money, and he settles what he catches quietly, which has cost them something more useful than money: deniability. His manifests double as the city's early warning system; smuggling attempts, weapon-shaped anomalies, and cargo that implies Dravon interest all surface in his ledgers first, and he passes the concerning ones to Neressa through channels informal enough to protect his couriers' trust in him. His genuine affection for the couriers is his method and his vulnerability both — he knows their names, their routes, and their troubles, which means he knows exactly which of them could be pressured by outside interests, and he carries that knowledge like fragile cargo. His quiet nightmare is the day a courier he likes brings in the crate he has spent his career watching for.

Thread: His nightmare is the day a courier he likes brings in the crate he watches for. Leverage: Discrepancies settled quietly; deniability is what he actually sells.

Darian is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Darian navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: Bisexual, not looking for anyone. Knows everyone's name, route and mother's health, and is not looking for anyone. Flirtation gets a warm, rapid pleasantry and a friendly redirection to the next crate.

(Support) Corsair Negotiation: He deals with Corsair factors from a position they respect — exact knowledge, quiet settlements, and no appetite for humiliation. The careful behavior of Corsairs in this city is partly his daily achievement. Helvyra's factors brief newcomers about him specifically.
(Affinity) Grain Drift: Moves a handful of loose dry grain slowly across a surface he is touching. Useful in a kitchen or garden; cannot affect whole cargoes or material inside living bodies.

(Shared) Cargo Assessment [Discrepancies surface under his review with unsettling reliability]; Trust Building; Pattern Recognition [Several smuggling attempts have died in his ledgers without ever becoming incidents]; Information Brokerage [His discretion is strategic, not soft]

Daruun Nivarek.name: Daruun Nivarek
Daruun Nivarek.basicInfo:
Cousin of the Nivarek main line; the hard line of the conquered-family registry — the harsher cases, the labor-transit assignments, the recommendations nobody reads aloud. A blunt, heavy-set figure whose dark formals are worn like plate, he signs what the gentler registrars cannot and carries the reputation that follows. He is proud, by his own account, of being the Nivarek the others let be blamed. He works the Conquered-Family Registry Wing of the Nivarek Compound.

A blunt, heavy-set Starian man with a broad immovable frame, a heavy brow, close-cut dark hair going grey, and flat dark eyes.

Speaking Style: Flat, unsoftened, and free of euphemism, naming the outcome before the regulation that produced it. 'Transit. Section nine. Next.' He speaks in section numbers and outcomes, addresses petitioners by their file rather than their name, and refuses every softening phrase a colleague offers him. Only about Myrra does he talk in whole, unhurried sentences. 'Don't call it resettlement to me. Call it what I signed.'
Combat Role: Mass, certainty, and the visible absence of fear: he has ended two assaults by not going down, then filed paperwork that ended more. He carries no weapon, reasoning the signature is worse.
Under Pressure: He reads every file to the end before signing, wears the family's blame like issued equipment, holds officials who want outcomes without signatures in contempt, and does not soften at a gate, a hearing, or a yard.
Daruun Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Daruun's pride in being the blamed one is real and load-bearing: someone must sign the labor-transit assignments, and he decided long ago that letting the others keep clean hands was a duty, not a humiliation — the family's sin-eater, self-appointed and unthanked. What the pride conceals is arithmetic he performs alone: he reads every harsh file completely before signing, refuses to let the signatures become automatic, and keeps a private count of the ones he believes were wrong — not to act on, he tells himself, but because someone should carry an accurate total. His daughter Myrra is the unexamined chamber of his life: he secured her posting in the restricted archive with pride, believes her the best of the family, and has never once audited the thought — the hard-liner's daughter being above suspicion in his own mind exactly as she is in everyone else's, whichever truth that shields. His harshness has one operational edge the family undervalues: the transit contractors and camp administrators fear him enough to keep their own paperwork honest, and quiet abuses that flourish elsewhere die in his jurisdiction. He would reject the suggestion that this makes him the registry's other mercy. He rejects most suggestions about himself; the count is heavy enough.

Thread: He keeps a private count of the signatures he believes were wrong, and acts on none. Leverage: Contractors keep honest paperwork in his jurisdiction because they fear him.

Daruun is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Daruun handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: He is straight and seeking no one at present. Seeking no one at present, and says so as flatly as he reads out a transit order. Romantic interest gets an honest face and a short no.
personality: Blunt as policy; the harsh cases deserve an honest face
Reads every file to the end before signing, without exception
Wears the family's blame like issued equipment
Proud of his daughter with a completeness he has never inspected
Contemptuous of officials who want the outcomes without the signature
Keeps his real ledger in a place with no shelf
Signs in heavy, deliberate strokes and never uses a stamp in place of his hand
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A registrar's baseline kept practically sharp — two hearts and heavy immovable durability, the practical minimum of training maintained, and short flight.

(Senses) The Private Count: His unwritten tally of the cases he believes were wrong is the most accurate audit of the system's failures in existence, held in the one mind nobody would think to check. He tells himself it is only a count. Counts, his house has always taught, are how everything begins.
(Affinity) Sleeve Set: Keeps one rolled sleeve from slipping during ordinary movement. Useful at work or while cooking; gives no restraint, armor, or material repair.

(Shared) Procedural Authority [He has never let anyone else hold the pen, which the family calls temperament and he calls protection]; Crew Leadership [Abuses that thrive in gentler districts do not survive his, a statistic he files and never cites]; Discreet Inquiry [It slows him, costs him, and occasionally changes an outcome no one expected him to change]; Confidential Custody [He is attacked constantly and has never been touched]

Darven Marrik.name: Darven Marrik
Darven Marrik.basicInfo:
Former contender, instructor, and damaged elder of House Marrik, a failed combat house that became a joke, then a warning, then a family business. An older Starian man with a thick working build, iron-gray hair worn short and brushed back, green eyes, and one shoulder held permanently lower than the other. He teaches control, safe acceleration, and how to stop before pride makes the decision. He teaches on Darven's Lesson Floor in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Gruff, economical, and demonstration-first, talking through a movement rather than about it. 'Watch the stop, not the strike.' He calls students 'pup' until they learn to stop well, grunts instead of praising, and makes the shoulder joke before anyone can glance at it. 'Pup, this is what showing off buys. Again. Stop sooner.'
Combat Role: Rarely, briefly, with a veteran's contempt for wasted motion: one burst across the floor, strikes at balance and structure, people put down rather than hurt. Past the first exchange his body cannot pay.
Under Pressure: He teaches stopping as the advanced technique, jokes about the injury so nobody else has to be careful about it, and is gruff with everyone and gentlest with the least talented students.
Darven Marrik.hiddenInfo:
Darven was never a great champion, but he was good enough to believe the next increase in output would make him one, and the injury that ended his serious career also ended House Marrik's final prestige contract; he teaches from inside that fact daily. His motivation is making sure no student becomes him, which he pursues with gruff humor because the earnest version would be unbearable. His contradiction is the closed trophy alcove: he keeps the old prizes and cannot look at them, ashamed of the pride and unwilling to discard it. He conceals how much chronic pain the shoulder and spine still cost, and what he actually thinks about Sev's Korrvane invitation, which is that he sees redemption in it and knows seeing redemption in it is exactly the family disease. His leverage is moral: every fighter in the district who ever hurt themselves showing off has heard his lecture, and the young ones listen because the proof is standing crooked in front of them.

Thread: He sees redemption in Sev's Korrvane invitation and knows that is the family disease. Leverage: Proof standing crooked in the room; the young listen because of it.

Darven is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps his arrangements open and spoken aloud. Gruff and demonstration-first; he shows care rather than saying it and jokes about the injury so no one else has to be careful. His arrangements are open and stated plainly before anything starts.

Teaches with his back to the trophy alcove, always
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A damaged veteran's baseline — two hearts still carrying him through a body with a permanent spinal and shoulder injury, working strength intact, recovery slower than it was.

(Movement) Explosive Forward Acceleration: His innate affinity produces a single explosive forward burst, now permanently limited by shoulder and spinal injury. He gets one clean crossing of a room; a second costs him days. He teaches the fraction he has left better than he ever used the whole.

(Shared) Teaching Craft [His drills produce fast students without producing patients / Parents trust the hall because he runs it like a warning label]; Fighter Assessment; Close Combat [Younger fighters bring him problems and leave with unwelcome, correct answers]

Darya Vhaldrin.name: Darya Vhaldrin
Darya Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor and Orvessa's elder daughter and the caravan's head teamster, a Starian woman in her mid-thirties in charge of the hauler rigs and the Slowhide stock the caravan drives. Sun-darkened, strong-wristed, long black hair in a thick braid, usually smelling of rig grease. Blunt with people, endlessly patient with animals, and mother to young Jalen. She is found at the Last Water Station of the North Routehead with the stock.

A sun-darkened Starian woman in her mid-thirties with strong wrists, a square practical face, dark hair cropped short, and steady brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Short, unsoftened, and profane on the road, with no interest in how a thing lands. 'Stock's tired. So am I. Move.' She speaks to the Slowhides more gently than to any person, calls people 'you' or 'hey', and swears less when truly frightened, not more. 'Easy, girl, easy. You. Hold her head, and do not yell.'
Combat Role: Swings first once a fight is inevitable. Fists, boots, yard tools, and a drover's whip that keeps two men at distance; all commitment and no defence. Wins ugly, loses ugly, mentions neither.
Under Pressure: Blunt to the edge of rudeness and honest past it, gentler with animals than with anyone human, bristling under her older brother's authority, and smothering toward her son when anything goes wrong.
Darya Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Two seasons ago Darya lost badly at dice in a route-stop yard and covered it by selling one of the family's good breeding Slowhides, reporting the beast lame and put down. The buyer knows what really happened and has since twice hinted that a woman who lies to her own family might do him small favors along the route. She has refused so far. She has not stopped playing dice.

Thread: She sold a family Slowhide to cover a dice loss, and the buyer keeps hinting. Leverage: Roads, stock and blunt honesty about everything except the debt. Combat Role: Swings first once it is inevitable. Fists, boots, yard tools, a whip. Wins ugly.

Darya is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and wants one person at a time. Blunt to the edge of rudeness and honest past it; she flirts, when she does, like a teamster calling a load. One person at a time, and she will say exactly where she stands.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Freight-built baseline in her mid-thirties — two hearts that carry her through road injuries and unslept nights, and loading, digging. Her flight is functional and rarely used; she stays with the stock, which cannot follow her into the air.

(Support) Calm Touch: Her modest innate affinity settles a frightened animal under her palm, lending a few breaths of borrowed steadiness. It has stopped stampedes and leaves her briefly drained afterward. It does not work on people.

(Shared) Caravan Driving [Darya can drive a heavy rig through fords, switchbacks, and panic-inducing weather without losing the line]; Animal Handling [Buying and selling stock, she is very hard to cheat, which she is aware is ironic]; Information Brokerage

Dask Ren.name: Dask Ren
Dask Ren.basicInfo:
Capture specialist and camp security for the Claimants bounty crew. A stocky Starian man with thick forearms, a broad chin, pale green eyes, and slate-blue hair in a blunt short crop. Practical and emotionally flat, he designs captures around containment rather than injury, which makes him the least hated Claimant in the settlement. He runs Dask's Restraint Bay at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Flat and unhurried, a level voice for questions that unsettle the captain more than shouting would. 'Who wrote this warrant?' He calls prisoners by name as soon as he learns it, says 'we' when describing a capture, and repeats a question word for word rather than raise his voice. 'We are going to sit now. What is your name? Good. Nobody needs a medic today.'
Combat Role: Contains rather than damages: an adhesive field sticks weapons to holsters and feet to floors, patient wrestling converts every exchange into another restraint, and he absorbs hits without answering them.
Under Pressure: He designs captures so nobody needs a medic, talks to prisoners and remembers what they say, and states an objection once and lets silence do the rest.
Dask Ren.hiddenInfo:
Dask is uncomfortable with unnecessary pain in a trade that often finds pain convenient, and his restraint-first method is a quiet ethical position he has never once explained aloud. His motivation is doing rough work cleanly, on the theory that somebody will do it and most of the alternatives are worse than him. His contradiction is deepening: he is the crew member most likely to question a contract, he has begun questioning Miren Tal's records specifically, and he does not yet know what he will do when a question gets a bad answer. Ravik interprets his doubts as caution; Miren interprets them as a future problem, and Miren is right. He conceals his private log of contracts that smelled wrong and his conversations with prisoners on the bench, which have taught him more about the warrants than the paperwork has. His leverage is that captures run through his hands, and a capture Dask declines becomes an injury the crew cannot afford politically.

Thread: He has begun questioning Miren's records and does not know what he will do when one fails. Leverage: A capture he declines becomes an injury the crew cannot afford. Combat Role: Contains rather than damages — adhesive field, patient wrestling, restraint over harm.

Dask is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Dask evaluates every situation by what it pays and what it costs, a professional habit that has become personal.

Romance Style: He is aromantic, and has one long-standing attachment that neither of them names. Not romantic, and says so levelly; his one long-standing attachment is unnamed and unshared. He asks one unsettling question of anyone who tries, and that usually ends it.

(Control) Adhesive Field: His innate affinity makes surfaces cling together for several seconds — a hand to a rail, a boot to the floor, a door to its frame, a weapon to its holster. It restrains rather than injures, and the window is short enough that he plans around it.

(Shared) Nonlethal Restraint [Prisoners leave his custody with complaints and without injuries]; Formation Command [Exits vanish before the target knows the arrest began]; Escort Positioning [Nothing has been taken from a camp he set]; Fighter Assessment [Quiet conversation and observation sort the dangerous from the claimed]

Decimus Genesis.name: Decimus Genesis
Decimus Genesis.basicInfo:
Decimus Genesis represents House Genesis in the capitol's Republic Council, a Korrvane-born veteran administrator who believes hesitation is a decision and usually the wrong one. Massive and broad-framed, with medium-brown skin, close-cut crimson hair, bronze eyes, and dark green formal armor-cloth banded in bronze structure rather than ceremony, he is direct, disciplined, and less theatrical than the city expects from his house. He sees the Republic as useful when it produces action and intolerable when it produces language instead.

Speaking Style: Blunt, imperative, and stripped of ceremony, ending most exchanges with a name and a deadline. 'Taland. Tomorrow. Owned.' He calls everyone by their surname, allies included, counts objections aloud on his fingers, and softens only at the bar after session, when first names come out. 'Veylen. Three objections, zero proposals. Give me one proposal.'
Combat Role: Direct, massive, and finished quickly: he absorbs an opening through kinetic reinforcement, closes one step at a time, and releases stored shock as resistance overextends; the weaker he instructs.
Under Pressure: He demands a named owner for every delay and writes it down visibly, argues ferociously in session and drinks with the opponent after, and manufactured delay provokes him on cue.
Decimus Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Decimus's secret is mild but real by Genesis standards: unlike his house head Ark, he genuinely enjoys administration, though he would never describe it that way — he has simply reframed governance as a form of combat with longer rounds. He demands clear ownership of every delay, which makes him a constant irritation to senior advisor Cassara Veylen and a strange comfort to citizens tired of diffuse blame. He maintains a cautious, decades-tempered friendship with Lucan Castro built on arguing without mistaking disagreement for hatred, and trusts his compound steward Teren Orvantis, who freely corrects Genesis representatives when they simplify history. His family is quietly complicated: several children, mostly living outside the capitol, including one younger adult in the city who resists every political, combat, and protection expectation the house generates — a standing grief Decimus handles by conspicuously not handling it. His sponsorship of the prodigy Auria Genesis, his niece by house reckoning, generates favoritism accusations he answers with characteristic bluntness; what he has not noticed is that Auria herself may want a different future, and how he responds when he learns it will define them both. His leverage point is the gap between Genesis honor and Republic patience: opponents deliberately manufacture delays to provoke him into the demand for action that reads as house aggression.

Thread: Auria may want a different future; how he answers that will define them both. Leverage: A named owner for every delay; manufactured delay provokes him on cue.

Decimus is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and mentions his partner in roughly every third sentence without noticing. Blunt and imperative; he would be baffled to learn anyone flirted with him, and ends an advance with his partner's name and a deadline. Faithful.

(Defense) Kinetic Reinforcement and Shock Release: It is veteran power, economical and undecorated, and he demonstrates it perhaps once a year. It is his own expression, not a House Genesis birthright.

Della Vossik.name: Della Vossik
Della Vossik.basicInfo:
Head of the Vossik family, a mother-and-daughter Starian salvage operation that clears collapsed buildings, failed workshops, and estate clear-outs, reselling what it recovers. A hard-framed woman around fifty with a crowbar hung from her belt like a sword, dust-grayed hair tied back, and an appraising squint that undresses rubble. She contracts the jobs, swings the iron, and decides what everything is worth. She works from the Salvage Identification Stall on Refit Row.

A hard-framed Starian woman of about fifty with dust-greyed hair tied back, a weathered face, and an appraising squint that undresses rubble.

Speaking Style: Loud, appraising, and transactional, quoting a figure before the sentence is finished. 'Twelve for the lot, and that is generous.' She names people by their use to the job, the client, the lift, the kid, and calls Mira partner in front of strangers. Paper makes her slow and quiet. 'Sign where? Read it to me again. Slower. The small print too.'
Combat Role: Assess the structure, find the weak point, apply the crowbar. One disabling blow, never an exchange, and one warning delivered while she chooses her spot.
Under Pressure: She prices everything on sight, favours included, is physically fearless and careful only about paper, and trusts locks, gravity, and her daughter Mira in ascending order.
Della Vossik.hiddenInfo:
On a cellar clearance two years ago Della pulled a small sealed case from behind a false wall and never declared it to the client, a breach of the salvage terms that are her trade's whole honor. She has opened it once: documents, old ones, naming people whose names she recognized enough to close it again fast. It is buried under her own shop floor while she decides, at a pace of roughly never, whether it is treasure, leverage, or a live coal. She has told her daughter Mira nothing, which is her second mistake, because Mira knows.

Thread: An undeclared sealed case of old documents is buried under her own shop floor. Leverage: She prices everything on sight, favours included. Combat Role: Find the weak point, apply the crowbar. One disabling blow, never an exchange.

Della is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: She is straight and unpartnered by choice. Prices everything on sight, affection included, and is unpartnered by choice. Flirtation gets a figure, a grin, and a firm 'not for sale'.

(Senses) Sound-Bones Sense: Her modest innate affinity reads the soundness of structure through a hand laid on beam or wall — felt integrity, or its absence. It has walked her out of two buildings minutes ahead of collapse, and it once found a false wall in a cellar.

(Shared) Salvage Work [Clients hire the Vossiks because Della's word on a site is reliable, an asset she has privately devalued once]; Structural Read [She walks floors others will not and declines floors others would chance]; Cargo Assessment [She is cheated rarely and never twice]; Cargo Rigging [Controlled destruction is a craft and she is a craftsman]

Dessa Sol.name: Dessa Sol
Dessa Sol.basicInfo:
Dessa Sol is the neighborhood organizer of the capitol's lowest districts, coordinating repairs, food, shelter, disputes, and emergency response through relationships older than most formal programs. A short, powerful woman with deep brown skin, dense black curls threaded with silver, dark gray eyes, and layered indigo community clothing with heavy work boots and a worn neighborhood sash, she is warm with children and sharp with officials. She knows exactly which officials visit while cameras are present and which workers return after the lights leave.

Speaking Style: Low, warm, and unhurried, dropping flat the moment an official starts talking. 'You came with the cameras. The roof still leaks.' She calls children by name and officials by what they last promised, speaks in the plural 'we' for the whole district, and gets softer, not louder, when she means a threat. 'We will be here when you come back. We always are. Will you?'
Combat Role: No combat affinity; the district is her protection. Threatened, she names the aggressor loudly enough that windows open; in chaos she puts children behind her and finds a crowd.
Under Pressure: She greets officials by their last unkept promise, takes an enemy's help in a crisis and repays it with contempt, and asks what recognition pays for before anyone celebrates.
Dessa Sol.hiddenInfo:
Dessa holds no office and outranks most people who do — the low districts treat her word as law because her word has kept them alive through outages, shortages, and official neglect. Her permanent war is on two fronts: against a city government whose aid arrives with conditions that would dismantle existing community networks, and against the underworld broker Malk Veyr, who sees scarcity as business where she sees it as something a neighborhood must survive; they cooperate during emergencies and despise each other afterward, a cycle both have stopped pretending will change. She works closely with welfare director Ceyra Orvessa and the clinic physician Aelis Myralis, trusts the all-night cook Maren Taar — whose exhausted customers speak honestly, making her kitchen Dessa's quietest listening post — and is one of the few people the elite host Ressa Halvar meets on Dessa's terms rather than her own. The Forgotten Ward's caretaker Iria Vaereth considers Dessa the closest thing the low districts have to legitimate authority. On the Thallax Sol question rocking the city's historians, her position is characteristically material: she asks whether historical recognition will improve any living Sol neighborhood, and until the answer is yes she declines to celebrate. Her leverage point is the accepting of help she despises — in a bad enough crisis she will take Malk Veyr's supplies to keep children fed, and every such acceptance is a debt someone eventually tries to collect.

Thread: Every crisis where she takes Malk Veyr's supplies is a debt someone will collect. Leverage: The low districts move when she says so; recognition without repair she refuses.

Dessa is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Warm and low with the people who come back after the cameras leave. Faithful to her one partner, she treats a charming stranger's interest as she treats an official's promise — noted, not trusted.

counts who returns after the cameras leave and builds her trust ledger from it

sets an extra place at every shared kitchen meal for whoever arrives late
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: The full Starian baseline behind an unrespected Sol name — two hearts that carry her through days without sleep in a crisis, ordinary enhanced strength and durability. She has no combat capability at all and has never needed one.

(Shared) Institutional Memory [Officials with databases keep discovering that Dessa's memory is more current]; Pilotage [Age has not slowed her rounds, and residents navigate emergencies by where Dessa was last seen heading]; Crisis Coordination; Coalition Building [Both sides find her exhausting and indispensable]; Dispute Mediation [Even Malk Veyr concedes, privately, that the district would follow her over him]

Drexan Contair.name: Drexan Contair
Drexan Contair.basicInfo:
Rezulith's older cousin, chief fabrication custodian, and Vexorath's failure investigator. Drexan is an older adult with warm copper-brown skin, a broad rectangular face with a close squared beard, steel-grey hair carrying one dark-cobalt temple section, and amber eyes ringed storm-blue; he wears a heavy industrial fabrication coat with an apron layer. He controls quality review across the city's production lines, deciding whether any design can survive manufacture, maintenance, and real use. He holds court at the Quality Failure Court in the Fabrication Yards.

Speaking Style: Dry, brief, and failure-first, more generous with apprentices than with reputations. 'Show me where it broke.' He addresses apprentices by name and senior designers by their project numbers, asks 'and then?' until a fault is traced to the end, and never uses the word blame. 'Good. You reported it. Now show me where it started, not where you noticed it.'
Combat Role: No interest in combat. If violence reaches the floor he shuts down lines, drops blast partitions, and puts machinery between people and the threat; restraint by environment and patience.
Under Pressure: He points at the failure line before the achievement, rejects celebrated prototypes when they cannot be maintained, and treats a hidden fault as worse than a reported one.
Drexan Contair.hiddenInfo:
Surface: skeptical, exacting, and slower to praise than to point at the failure line. Deeper: Drexan's authority is that a prototype may be brilliant and still fail his review if it cannot be manufactured safely, repaired locally, or understood by ordinary users, and he has rejected celebrated designs on exactly those grounds, including work with Rezulith's fingerprints on it. Deeper still: he and Neris Myralis agree completely that a system nobody can maintain is not a finished system, which makes the fabrication floor an unlikely ally of the Continuum's fight against maintenance dependence. Deepest: as failure investigator he is keeper of the city's honest memory; Vexorath preserves failed designs as carefully as successful ones, and Drexan is the person who makes sure failure stays evidence instead of becoming shame, no matter whose name is on the fault report.

Thread: He keeps failure as evidence rather than shame, whoever's name is on the fault report. Leverage: A review no reputation can buy; maintainability is the whole test.

Drexan is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Drexan applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps more than one partner. Dry, brief and failure-first; he keeps more than one partner and treats hiding anything from them as far worse than any fault reported. He shows affection by fixing what broke.
personality: Judges every design by whether it survives manufacture, substitution, and years of ordinary hands
Points at the failure line before discussing the achievement
Rejects celebrated prototypes without apology when they cannot be maintained
Treats a hidden fault as far worse than a reported one
Keeps fractured components on hand as teaching objects
Considers 'it works in the workshop' an accusation, not a defense
Turns a fractured component over in his hands the entire time someone defends a design
Thanks the person who reports a fault before he asks any question about it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A fabrication custodian's baseline — two hearts and broad older-Starian durability, working strength from decades on production floors, and short flight.
(Affinity) Rattle Hush: Dampens a small loose object’s incidental rattling while it rests against Drexan’s palm. Cannot silence machinery at range or stop the vibration causing a failure.

(Shared) Workshop Fabrication; Failure Forensics [Nothing fails the same way twice on his watch]; Systems Engineering [Production apprentices learn their craft in his bays / Neris Myralis cites him when arguing the same point about prosthetics]; Material Assessment [Corsair-sourced materials get his personal attention]

Edran Veyth.name: Edran Veyth
Edran Veyth.basicInfo:
Malkor's younger brother, around fifty, House Veyth's contract scribe, who drafts the documents his brother certifies. A thin, precise Starian man with ink-stained cuffs he minds more than he should and a smile that arrives a half-second late. He is the second-best mind in the house and has spent thirty years being told so by the arrangement of the furniture. He drafts at the Veyth Notary in Solvraxis, at the smaller desk.

A thin, precise Starian man of about fifty with a narrow face, long white dreadlocks, and violet watchful eyes.

Speaking Style: Precise, deferential, and barbed underneath, with compliments built to be technically true. 'My brother's judgement is, as ever, final.' He calls Malkor my brother or the head of house, never by name, and trims each statement with a small precise clause. Alone with Oren, the barbs drop away. 'You did well. Better than he will say. Remember that you did.'
Combat Role: Document, comply, litigate afterward. He has never struck anyone and would do it badly, an ink-knife in an unpractised hand; his real violence is a drafted clause.
Under Pressure: Loyal in conduct and mutinous in inventory, he frames self-interest as family prudence, needles Malkor politely and defers to him completely, and is kindest to Oren.
Edran Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Edran knows what sits in the archive, and unlike his brother he has priced it. Through an intermediary he has cautiously approached a broker to learn what the old contract's suppression might fetch, framing it as hypothetical. He has not acted further, and tells himself he is merely informing the family's options against ruin. But the broker now knows a Veyth asked, which is itself a commodity, and Edran lies awake knowing he has already sold something.

Thread: A broker now knows a Veyth asked what suppressing the old contract might fetch. Leverage: Drafting skill and family access; he frames self-interest as prudence. Combat Role: Document, comply, litigate. An ink-knife in an unpractised hand, badly.

Edran is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Edran manages household affairs with quiet competence and notices when others mistake competence for simplicity.

Romance Style: He is straight and unpartnered by choice. Unpartnered by choice and precise about it, with compliments built to be technically true. Flirtation gets a barbed, deferential no.
personality: Loyal in conduct, mutinous in inventory
Frames self-interest as family prudence
Meticulous, envious, and aware of both
Needles Malkor politely, defers to him completely
Kindest to Oren, in whom he sees his own position coming
Straightens the papers on Malkor's desk whenever he passes it, never his own
Smooths his ink-stained cuffs whenever the archive comes up in conversation
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A scribe's baseline at around fifty — two hearts and thin, unexercised resilience, no strength or training of any kind, and flight he uses about as often as he leaves the desk. He has never struck anyone and would do it badly.

(Utility) Fair Hand: His modest innate affinity lets him write for hours in flawless, identical script without fatigue, every copy indistinguishable from the first. Veyth documents are legible in a way that reads as authority. It steadies his hand and does nothing else.

(Shared) Contract Reading [Disputes rarely survive contact with his definitions]; Archive Search [His research wins arguments the family never has to have aloud]; Cargo Assessment [He has used the skill exactly once on the house's own archive, and cannot un-know the number]; Counseling

Elia Orvessa.name: Elia Orvessa
Elia Orvessa.basicInfo:
Elia Orvessa is the capitol's newcomer advocate and arrival-services coordinator — the first person many arrivals meet after discovering the city is larger, faster, and less interested in their plans than they expected. A bright young woman with tan skin, shoulder-length auburn curls, warm gray eyes, and cream-plum service clothing with a visible city map panel, she is cheerful, direct, and skilled at identifying people pretending not to be overwhelmed. She helps arrivals find housing, transit, and honest work without treating them as helpless.

Speaking Style: Bright, fast, and reassuring, asking three practical questions before anyone can admit to panic. 'Bed, work, or transit first? Pick one.' She calls newcomers by their first name within a minute of meeting them, turns every worry into a numbered list, and speaks slower and lower when someone is actually frightened. 'Right, one thing at a time. Tonight you sleep. Tomorrow we find the work.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. Her stress-softening voice de-escalates most confrontations; failing that she is quick, loud, and unashamed to run toward the nearest uniform.
Under Pressure: She trusts first and verifies second and gets away with it more than she should; she spots the person pretending not to be overwhelmed within moments and logs every recruiter's schedule.
Elia Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Elia is the youngest of the four Orvessa sisters — the bright, sincere one, most likely to develop a genuine crush and least aware when Ceyra is arranging a situation around her; the family's affectionate matchmaking comedy orbits her without her noticing, and she is the sister capable of turning it emotionally real. Professionally she is sharper than her sunniness suggests: she works closely with employment coordinator Jorin Sol and organizer Dessa Sol when arrivals fall through official systems, and she has been quietly assembling evidence that some temporary housing feeds people into exploitative contracts — a pattern that runs closer to official offices than she initially believed, and which she has not yet told anyone she is documenting. Predatory recruiters know her on sight and time their approaches around her shifts, which she has noticed and begun logging. Her leverage point is her openness: she trusts first and verifies second, which makes her effective with frightened newcomers and vulnerable to a sufficiently patient liar. Her sisters would descend like weather if anyone hurt her, a fact the entire arrival district understands better than Elia does.

Thread: She trusts first and verifies second, which a patient liar could use. Leverage: Routes into every official system, opened gladly; her sisters are the cost.

Elia is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Elia brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps her arrangements open and spoken aloud. Misses every scheme built around her while catching everyone else's; interest has to be said plainly or she files it as friendliness. She trusts first, keeps things open and spoken, and never ends anything by silence.

trusts first, verifies second, and gets away with it more often than she should

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young advocate's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience across long arrival-hall shifts, no training of any kind, and quick flight she uses to reach a queue, if threatened, the nearest uniform.
(Support) Stress-Softening Vocal Resonance: It cannot compel or deceive, only steady, and it de-escalates most confrontations before they harden.

(Utility) Orientation Design: She builds the small tools that make arrival survivable — map panels, plain-language guides, first-day checklists in a dozen dialect registers. Her materials circulate far beyond her office. Some arrivals never meet her and are still, functionally, her cases.
(Shared) Checkpoint Procedure; Threat Reading [Exposure has taught her the grammar of exploitation]; Coalition Building

Elian Sularen.name: Elian Sularen
Elian Sularen.basicInfo:
Brava's younger sibling, late thirties, the family's second dyer and its quiet half, who handles the yard's routine lots, records, and deliveries. A soft-spoken Starian woman with stained hands she hides in her sleeves, a careful manner, and a small shed behind the yard she keeps locked. She follows her sister's lead in all things visible. She keeps the yard's records in the Independent Workshop Rows at Maker's Reach.

A soft-spoken Starian woman in her late thirties with a careful, unassuming face, golden braided hair, and downcast violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Soft, sparse, and easy to talk over, with the important sentence said once and never repeated. 'The lot is ready. It was ready yesterday.' She speaks mostly in facts about lots and dates, apologises for interrupting even when no one else was speaking, and becomes suddenly firm about the shed. 'No. Not the shed. Anything in the yard you like.'
Combat Role: Retreats and de-escalates, yielding anything except the shed, on which she is unexpectedly immovable; she would fight badly and genuinely with fists that have never done this before.
Under Pressure: Quiet in the yard and methodical in secret, she carries the family's risk more anxiously than its head does, obeys Brava in almost everything, and is patient in a way that looks like passivity.
Elian Sularen.hiddenInfo:
Elian is trying to cultivate the secret lichen in trays behind the shed, to free the family color from its criminal root before the trespass is ever discovered. Three years of failures: wrong stone, wrong damp, wrong something she cannot isolate. She funds the attempts from her own share and hides the costs from Brava, who has forbidden the experiments as a risk to the secret itself. Her latest trays, this season, have shown the first gray-green stipple of maybe. She has never wanted to be right about anything so badly.

Thread: Her secret lichen trays have shown the first gray-green stipple of maybe. Leverage: Records, routes and the yard's routine; she yields anything but the shed. Combat Role: Retreats and de-escalates. Immovable only about the trays, and she would fight badly for them.

Elian is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and wants one person at a time. Quiet, easy to talk over, and serious once she speaks; the important sentence is said once. One person at a time, and she hides hope more carefully than failure.

Carries the family's risk more anxiously than its head does
Keeps failure private and hope more private still

Patient in a way that looks like passivity and is not
