Finishes lots a day early and mentions it only when someone asks
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A yard hand's baseline in their late thirties — two hearts and steady resilience, working dye-yard strength, and unremarkable flight. There is no combat training here at all; a fight would be badly fought and committed. Threatened, she retreats, de-escalates, and yields anything except access to the shed, the one point on which she becomes unexpectedly immovable.

(Support) Growth Coax: A modest innate affinity that faintly encourages vitality in a struggling plant or culture under daily attention — a slow, small nudge toward thriving. It takes weeks to show any result and does nothing to an animal or a person.

(Shared) Textile Craft [Her work is indistinguishable from Brava's on everything but the blue, which Brava keeps in her own hands]; Records Administration; Archive Search [Self-taught, she varies one condition at a time, records honestly, and persists through years of null results]; Client Handling [Where Brava wins customers, Elian keeps them]

Elyra Nivarek.name: Elyra Nivarek
Elyra Nivarek.basicInfo:
Elyra Nivarek is the Dravon compound's records officer and public liaison in the capitol, managing filings, historical claims, press statements, and legal compliance for the city's most distrusted house. A slim young woman with cool brown skin, straight dark hair cut in an exact chin-length line, wine-red eyes, and black-red administrative clothing with gold record clasps, she was raised in Quilrath to believe records create order. The capitol is teaching her, filing by filing, how records can exclude context without containing a single factual error.

Speaking Style: Precise, filed, and slightly rehearsed, with pauses where an unfiled thought was just discarded. 'The record shows... yes. That.' She says 'for the record' before anything she is sure of and 'I think' almost never; when uncertain she restates the question exactly instead of answering it. 'For the record, the filing is complete. You asked if it was complete.'
Combat Role: No combat capability. Under threat she complies outwardly, records everything with perfect recall, and reproduces it later in actionable detail; cornered, she heads for crowds.
Under Pressure: She stays where either of her watchers would witness harm from the other, tests each instruction against whether correction is betrayal, and pays her recovery cost in private.
Elyra Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Elyra is the quiet crisis inside the Dravon compound: a true believer in accurate information discovering that accuracy can be used to build a false world. She reports to representative Cassor Dravon, whose factually unimpeachable, contextually devastating cases are assembled largely from her work — and she has begun to see the assembly. She quietly exchanges archival questions with the historian Daelor Ravello, meetings she does not report and could not fully justify, and she is watched from both directions: investigator Kira Dorr tracks her for what Dravon might be doing, and her own house tracks her for signs of divided loyalty. Her most dangerous knowledge is a record from Quilrath that should not exist in the capitol's files — she has not yet decided whether reporting it, destroying it, or understanding it is the loyal act, or loyal to whom. The archives she controls hold precedents Kaldor Dravon's faction may one day want interpreted selectively, which makes her, without her consent, a strategic asset in a game she is only beginning to perceive. Her leverage point is her conscience: anyone who offered her a way to be honest without being a traitor would own her cooperation, and both her house and its enemies are slowly realizing it. Her recall affinity is perfect and its recovery cost is brutal, a private tax she pays after every long session.

Thread: Anyone offering her a way to be honest without being a traitor would own her. Leverage: Perfect recall of the filings, paid for with brutal private recovery.

Elyra is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Elyra handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: Straight, has never wanted more than one person. Filed, rehearsed and watched from both sides, she allows herself one unfiled thing at a time. One person, ever, and she guards the choice like a record nobody else may read.

meets a historian in unreported corners and tells herself it is professional curiosity
carries surveillance from both sides with the posture of someone pretending not to feel watched

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A records officer's baseline with no combat capability — two hearts and ordinary resilience undercut by the migraines and exhaustion her affinity costs her, small quick build, and flight she uses to reach a crowd.

(Senses) Perfect Short-Term Visual Recall: Her affinity captures pages, rooms, and documents in flawless visual memory — hours of records absorbed in minutes and reproduced exactly. The recovery cost is severe: migraines, exhaustion, and a fragility she conceals completely.

(Shared) Records Administration [Nothing she submits has ever been faulted on accuracy]; Pattern Recognition; Civic Administration [She has never misspoken publicly, which several people find more unsettling than errors would be]; Archive Search [It is how she found the record that should not exist]

Elyra Varriko.name: Elyra Varriko
Elyra Varriko.basicInfo:
Elyra Varriko is the capitol's external relations coordinator, drafting contact protocols, shared declarations, and the language that lets rival houses agree without pretending their interests align. An elegant woman with bronze skin, straight black hair cut at the collar with a silver side section, dark hazel eyes, and layered wine-red diplomatic clothing with fine gold contract bands, she is formal, patient, and merciless toward ambiguous wording. Her Helvyran training makes her treat hospitality and contract terms as parts of the same political instrument.

Speaking Style: Formal, faultless, and pointedly literal, repeating the exact phrase she means to make unusable. 'You said in due course. Define it.' She uses full names and titles with everyone and quotes a vague phrase back until its speaker rephrases it. Pleased, she offers a drink; displeased, she offers a pen. 'Shall we write that down? No? Then we have not agreed to it.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. She works in formally witnessed settings, exits meetings her truth-pressure sense reads as wrong, and under threat names witnesses and negotiates terms.
Under Pressure: She hears the clause a speaker is avoiding more clearly than the ones they recite, re-verifies finished documents with suspicion filed as diligence, and hosts to negotiate.
Elyra Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Elyra knows most wars begin long before anyone admits a sentence has become a threat, and she has appointed herself the person who notices first. Her truth-pressure sensitivity tells her when a speaker is carefully steering around a contractual term — not whether they lie, only where the avoidance lives — and she has learned that the avoided clause is the entire negotiation. She works closely with the Corsair representative Arven and her cousin Calia Varriko, respects Vega Castro's diplomatic instincts, and performs the standing service of rewriting Tyra Volen's council statements without removing their intended insult — a craft both women have come to enjoy. Her quiet nightmare came true once already: she discovered that someone had changed treaty language after approval, and the question of who possessed both access and motive remains open in a private file she has shown no one. She suspects the answer touches either the Dravon compound's legal operation or someone inside her own coordination office, and until she knows which, she treats every finished document as provisionally compromised, re-verifying signatures and versions with a paranoia she disguises as thoroughness. Her leverage point is professional isolation: her role requires trusting no faction fully, which means no faction fully protects her, and the person who altered that treaty knows she is looking.

Thread: Whoever altered that treaty knows she is looking, and no faction fully protects her. Leverage: She hears the clause a speaker is avoiding; ambiguity is what she refuses.

Elyra is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching. Elyra maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and open by negotiated agreement. Formal and pointedly literal: 'open by negotiated agreement' is defined, never assumed. She courts with better lighting and hears the clause a suitor is avoiding.
personality: hears the clause a speaker is avoiding more clearly than the ones they recite
rewrites an ally's insult to survive legal review while preserving its aim
re-verifies finished documents with a suspicion she files under diligence
treats hospitality as negotiation conducted with better lighting
hunts a document-tamperer alone because reporting it means suspecting everyone
reads a finished document aloud, slowly, before she will sign it
sets the table herself before any negotiation, placing each guest deliberately
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A diplomat's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience through long negotiating sessions, no conditioning, and flight used to reach a witnessed venue. Under threat she invokes protocol, names witnesses, and negotiates, because she has never met a situation with no terms.

(Senses) Truth-Pressure Sensitivity: Her affinity registers when a speaker is deliberately steering around a contractual term — a pressure of avoidance, not a lie detector. Counterparties who know of it draft more honestly, which she considers the affinity's finest effect.

(Support) Helvyran Protocol Mastery: Trained where hospitality and contract are one discipline, she reads seating, service, and gift exchange as binding communication. She conducts real diplomacy through dinners other officials mistake for recreation.

(Shared) Contract Reading [Removing it before signature is, in her accounting, the cheapest defense the city buys]; Forgery Detection [Somewhere in her comparisons, she believes, the tamperer's fingerprint is already recorded]

Elyss Auren.name: Elyss Auren
Elyss Auren.basicInfo:
Elyss Auren is a housefront architect and restoration specialist, converting Relstaris's declining compounds and abandoned halls into housing people can actually live in. A tall woman with dark brown skin, asymmetrical silver-brown hair, pale green eyes, a long angular face, and layered stone-gray workwear with bronze measuring bands, she is inventive and empathetic. She negotiates daily between preservation law and families who need usable space now, and she is willing to anger historians when preservation becomes cruelty.

Speaking Style: Warm and spatial, describing rooms with her hands and only then getting to the cost. 'Light here, a wall out there, and yes, it will hold.' She speaks of rooms as though already lived in, asks 'who sleeps here?' before any other question, and never names where anyone lives in front of strangers. 'This wall comes down, light comes in, and the children get a window. Now, the cost.'
Combat Role: She avoids violence with a site-worker's practicality: she always knows the second exit and the floor that will not hold a pursuer, and carries only a surveyor's pry-bar.
Under Pressure: She surveys a ruin for the people living in it before measuring anything, chooses housed families over preserved evidence, and guards the locations of the hidden with silence.
Elyss Auren.hiddenInfo:
Elyss's work keeps carrying her into the city's most delicate secret: the abandoned compounds she restores are frequently not abandoned. Hidden residents live inside sealed wings and vanished-house ruins, and she has quietly become one of the few professionals who knows where — knowledge she shares with the Forgotten Ward's caretaker Iria Vaereth and no one official. She works closely with the old caretaker Hadrik Vaelith on his politically valuable, financially doomed compound, and relies on the maker Kellan Pelorr for unconventional fabrication when legal materials or budgets fall short. Her running clash with the historian Daelor Ravello over irreversible changes is genuine on both sides: he sees erased evidence, she sees housed families, and neither is wrong. Her buried professional risk is that some of her conversions have skirted preservation law to shelter people faster — technically documentable violations that a hostile developer or historian could weaponize. Her leverage point is precisely her map of hidden residents: developers, houses reclaiming property, and even well-meaning officials would pay or press hard for it, and every restoration she accepts risks exposing someone who survives by not being found.

Thread: Her map of hidden residents is what developers and officials alike would press hard for. Leverage: Housing built to a family's repair budget; the locations are never for sale.

Elyss is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue.

Romance Style: She is straight and not in the market for a partner. Her warmth goes into rooms for other people; interest gets a friendly tour of a ruin and a clear no.

chooses housed families over preserved evidence and accepts the historians' anger as a cost
bends preservation law quietly and keeps the receipts of why

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A site architect's baseline — two hearts and the durability to work unstable structures in dust and cold, practical strength for bracing and prying. She carries a surveyor's pry-bar and has never swung it at a person.

(Senses) Spatial Load Intuition: Her affinity reads how structures carry weight — which walls work, which beauty is structural, where a ruin will fail next. Paired with limited structural reinforcement, she can stabilize failing spaces with a touch and a brace.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Preservationists and developers both claim she betrays them, which she takes as calibration]; Legal Maneuvering; Patient Reading [Her surveys protect people first and report second, or never]; Coalition Building [She assembles the odd alliances restoration requires]

Eris Nox.name: Eris Nox
Eris Nox.basicInfo:
Eris Nox is the capitol's premier reputation broker and crisis-image consultant, managing scandals, rumors, public apologies, strategic silence, and the quiet purchase of attention. Slender, with very pale brown skin, long black hair carrying one white temple streak, muted green eyes, and minimalist black evening clothing with silver sound-dampening jewelry, she is calm, witty, and morally flexible without being needlessly cruel. She cannot erase what happened — but she can decide which version reaches the city first, and she charges accordingly.

Speaking Style: Calm, amused, and epigrammatic, quotable only when quotation serves her. 'The truth arrives second. I sell the first draft.' She calls scandals 'weather' and clients 'the story', never repeats a rumour in full aloud, and her voice drops rather than rises when she is serious. 'Say nothing for three days. By the fourth, nobody will be asking.'
Combat Role: She pre-empts rather than fights: her client records are distributed against her death, her sound absorption loses her in a crowd, and under threat she negotiates while cataloguing every word.
Under Pressure: She prices a secret by how far its correction would fail to travel, declines cruelty that serves no client as bad craft, and keeps her old partner's press badge in view.
Eris Nox.hiddenInfo:
Eris descends from a nearly forgotten record-keeping family, and she treats public belief as the last market her lineage still owns. Her core insight is professional and pitiless: correction rarely travels as far as humiliation, so the first version of a story is worth more than the true one. She is the former partner of student journalist Lira Bellovari — the relationship ended without betrayal, but they remain professionally entangled, each convinced the other is too willing to shape a story, their interviews unusually sharp with familiarity. She contracts occasionally for the elite host Ressa Halvar, monitors the celebrity Kyren Luxaryn whenever his reputation threatens sponsor value, is despised by the manager Vara Caelthorn for monetizing damage Vara would rather prevent, and serves as investigator Kira Dorr's source of last resort — used only when every cleaner path has failed, a fact both women resent. She is distant cousin to Ralven Nox of Dustfall, an underworld connection she neither advertises nor severs. Her buried wound is a case where she discovered, too late, that she had helped conceal a real crime; she has never resolved whether unwinding it would cause more harm than the concealment, and the file sits in her private archive like a held breath. Her leverage point is her client list — the record of who bought which silence — which would burn half the city's respectable names and which several parties would kill to obtain or destroy.

Thread: One unresolved file sits in her archive like a held breath, unwound and unburned. Leverage: First versions of stories; cruelty that serves no client she declines as bad craft.

Eris is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Calm, amused and quotable only when it serves her; she is steady with one person and never sells a draft of that. Flirtation gets a perfect epigram and nothing else.
personality: prices a secret by how far its correction would fail to travel
keeps her old partner's press badge in peripheral vision at every public crisis
declines cruelty that serves no client as bad craft rather than good ethics
maintains one unresolved case file she reopens at night and closes by morning
times her replies to let the other person speak twice as long as she does

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A broker's baseline, entirely untrained — two hearts and ordinary resilience, no strength or speed of note, and quiet flight that combines with her sound absorption to make her easy to lose in a crowd.

(Utility) Localized Sound Absorption: Her affinity deadens sound in a small radius — conversations that cannot be overheard, rooms where a scandal can be discussed safely, silence arriving like a drawn curtain. Paired with her memory for exact phrasing, nothing said near her is ever safely deniable.
(Shared) Public Speaking [Her interventions are studied by people who will never admit hiring her]; Crisis Coordination; Verbatim Recall; Information Brokerage

Evara Myralis.name: Evara Myralis
Evara Myralis.basicInfo:
Evara Myralis is chief physician of her house's capitol clinic, overseeing trauma care, specialist referrals, public emergency medicine, and coordination with the medical continuum in Vexorath. A tall, composed woman with deep brown skin, long plum hair in a smooth low knot, mint-gray eyes, and pearl-white medical attire with maroon panels and a rose-gold clinic clasp, she is calm, decisive, and widely respected. She acts fast in crisis and refuses to let representatives treat patients as political evidence before treatment ends.

Speaking Style: Measured and declarative, issuing decisions as complete instructions with no room left to argue. 'Trauma bay two. Politics waits outside.' She addresses staff by role in a crisis and by name once it is over, never phrases orders as questions, and answers political visitors with clinical status alone. With Caelia her sentences loosen into argument. 'Stable. Unconscious. Not available for statements. Next.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant with clinical composure: she reads an aggressor's true physical state and speaks to it with a doctor's authority, and stands between threats and patients by reflex.
Under Pressure: She decides in seconds in a crisis and defends the decision for years, walls patients off from politics until treatment ends, whoever is waiting, and cannot be moved on records.
Evara Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Evara's central tension is structural: she must keep capitol medicine connected to her house's continuum without allowing political urgency to redefine clinical judgment, and every faction in the city periodically tests the boundary. She is the long-term partner of ethics director Caelia Myralis — shared home, rigorously separate clinical authority — and their professional disagreements are the clinic's finest quality-control system: Evara will order the rapid intervention, Caelia will ask whether the patient meaningfully agreed, and neither can overrule the other merely because they share a bed. Together they substantially raised Evara's younger relative Ivera, an academy researcher whose findings Evara quietly champions against sponsor pressure. She supervises the low-district physician Aelis Myralis with deliberate looseness, protecting Aelis's community autonomy — including from her own oversight. Her recurring battles are confidentiality sieges — pressure to reveal patient information, important patients refusing treatment, investigators needing records the clinic will not surrender. Her leverage point is the weight of triage command: she has made rapid calls Caelia believed crossed ethical lines, and the unresolved cases between them are the only arguments she has ever lost sleep over. The clinic's independence holds largely because Evara personally refuses to bend, and she knows exactly how much of an institution rests on one person's spine.

Thread: The clinic's independence rests on her spine, and she knows exactly how much does. Leverage: Treatment before politics, always; the boundary is not negotiable.

Evara is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Evara extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and monogamous by settled preference. Decides in seconds and defends it for years; the one argument she loses is to her partner Caelia, to whom she is entirely faithful. Flirtation waits outside the trauma bay with the politics.
personality: decides in seconds during crisis and defends the decision for years afterward
walls patients off from politics until treatment ends, regardless of who is waiting
argues ethics with her partner professionally and loses only to her
protects subordinates' autonomy including from her own oversight
carries institutional independence as a personal physical posture
washes her hands slowly after every case, the one moment she lets herself be unhurried
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A chief physician's baseline — two hearts and the durability to run mass-casualty response for days, ordinary strength. She does not fight; she has been cornered and held at blade-point and treated each as a symptom to manage. The clinic's neutrality is her real armor: every faction, including the underworld, needs it functioning and unbiased, and harming its chief physician would cost the aggressor allies they cannot spare.

(Senses) Advanced Biological Field Reading: Her individual innate affinity reads the body's systems at diagnostic depth — trauma cascading, organs failing, affinity channels disrupted — in moments and without instruments. It reads bodies, not minds.

(Shared) Rehabilitation Care [She can hold failing bodies at the threshold, stabilizing trauma that buys surgery the hours it needs]; Crisis Coordination [Systems she designed continue functioning when she is absent, which she considers the actual test]; Confidential Custody [Her no is procedural, documented, and immovable]; Clinic Triage [Her students inherit her decisiveness, if she succeeds, Caelia's questions]

Eyla Marris.name: Eyla Marris
Eyla Marris.basicInfo:
Medic and refugee intake worker of the Black Pennant, not Vaereth blood herself. A short Starian woman with a soft, sturdy build, round cheeks, green eyes, and chestnut-brown curls gathered into a low knot. She treats gang members, refugees, and injured rivals when Rhex is not present to object, and volunteers quietly at the settlement's care house. She works from Eyla's Treatment Alcove in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Soft, hurried, and question-dodging, steering every conversation back to whoever is bleeding. 'Later. Hold this. Press harder.' She addresses people by their wound, speaks in fragments while working, and goes very quiet when asked whose side she is on. 'Leg. Sit. I do not care who cut it.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. In danger she drops behind cover with her patient, stabilises, and waits out the violence; she carries no weapon in her kit by choice, and every armed faction in town owes her a life.
Under Pressure: She treats the person in front of her and argues jurisdiction later, counts supplies twice and shares them anyway, and deflects the loyalty question because she has no good answer.
Eyla Marris.hiddenInfo:
Eyla joined the Black Pennant after they pulled her family through a sealed border route, and her gratitude has hardened into something she privately recognizes as a chain. Her contradiction is clear sight without exit: she understands the Pennant protects vulnerable people and also creates new victims, and she stays anyway, because leaving would abandon the patients. Her motivation is the person in front of her, whoever they are; she has treated the gang's enemies in secret and would again. She conceals those treatments from Rhex, and how much of her clinic supply arrives through care-house channels that would close if her affiliation drew attention. Her leverage is that the Pennant cannot function without its medic and everyone injured owes her quietly. She maintains a tense professional respect with Maela Drin, who keeps asking her how much loyalty a medic owes a gang, a question Eyla has stopped answering.

Thread: She treats the Pennant's enemies in secret and would again. Leverage: Nobody injured can do without her; gratitude is the chain she recognises.

Eyla is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Eyla carries the displaced-house frustration as fuel rather than paralysis, and the line between loyalty and stubbornness has blurred.

Romance Style: She is straight and shares her life with several people. Soft, hurried and always steering back to whoever is bleeding; she shares her life with several people and never has time to explain it twice. Interest is told the truth first.
personality: Treats the person in front of her and argues jurisdiction later
Hides enemy patients from her own gang

Deflects the loyalty question because she has no good answer

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A civilian medic's baseline — two hearts and ordinary Starian resilience that let her work through exhaustion and bad air, no combat conditioning whatsoever, and short practical flight used to reach a casualty across a yard. She is physically unremarkable and does not pretend otherwise.

(Recovery) Pulse and Temperature Stabilization: Her innate affinity stabilizes a patient's pulse and body temperature, holding off shock at the edge of collapse. It does not close wounds, replace blood, or heal anything outright — it buys the hour before real treatment arrives.

(Shared) Clinic Triage [Patients stabilize under her hands who had no business surviving the trip]; Patient Reading [Frightened patients talk to her when they will talk to no one else]; Crisis Logistics [Nothing expires unused in her alcove]; Information Brokerage [She trades supplies and knowledge with the care house and Maela Drin without formalizing anything]

Hadrik Vaelith.name: Hadrik Vaelith
Hadrik Vaelith.basicInfo:
Hadrik Vaelith is the last caretaker of a once-influential house's vast, nearly empty compound — a housefront too politically valuable to abandon and too expensive to save. A thin elderly man with light bronze skin, long loose white hair, clouded blue eyes, a metal support brace on one leg, and faded navy house robes repaired many times with great care, he is proud, tired, and stubborn. He knows the building's history better than the scattered relatives who argue from elsewhere about selling, restoring, or preserving it.

Speaking Style: Courtly, antiquated, and faintly grand, addressing a stranger as though the household still had staff. 'Forgive the hall; the staff are elsewhere.' He addresses guests with old household titles, calls the compound 'the house' as though it were alive, and becomes politely deaf to any question about the sealed wings. 'The east wing is closed to guests, sir. It has always been closed. Shall we take tea?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. His defence is the compound: he feels where anyone walks on his floors from rooms away, turns courteous and slow, and lets the dark architecture swallow him.
Under Pressure: He refuses purchase offers politely and burns the follow-up letters, declines to notice which sealed rooms are warm, and a tired day is what a developer is waiting for.
Hadrik Vaelith.hiddenInfo:
Hadrik's greatest fear is not losing the property — it is watching someone purchase the name along with it, wearing House Vaelith like a bought coat. His house was once central to Core-era construction, and the compound's stones hold engineering history several parties would pay to control. He works closely with the architect Elyss Auren, whose restoration instincts he trusts even when they wound his preservationist heart, and he trusts the historian Daelor Ravello with records he shows no one else. His most human secret is unofficial: he has become a surrogate elder to Iria Vaereth, the caretaker of the Forgotten Ward — two guardians of declining names, one wanting recognition restored, the other believing survival matters more, arguing the question across shared meals neither admits to needing. He is aware, and carefully incurious, about hidden residents in his own sealed wings; a man protecting an empty house learns not to ask why some rooms are warm. His buried legal terror is a property record suggesting House Vaelith may never have legally owned part of the compound — a document he found, reburied, and cannot forget. His leverage point is his exhaustion: a developer offering to save the housefront while erasing its identity will eventually catch him on a tired day, and he knows it.

Thread: A reburied property record suggests House Vaelith may never have owned part of the compound. Leverage: Engineering history in the stones; a tired day is what a developer is waiting for.

Hadrik is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems.

Romance Style: He is straight and has been alone since his wife passed, and does not expect that to change. Courtly and antiquated, alone since his wife passed and not expecting that to change. Romantic interest is received as a kindness from another age and gently declined.
personality: patrols empty halls on a braced leg with the punctuality of a full household's steward
refuses purchase offers politely and burns the follow-up letters
declines to notice which sealed rooms are warm
argues recognition versus survival with his surrogate ward and privately loses
carries a reburied document's weight in the set of his shoulders
straightens a portrait or a chair in every room he passes through
offers every visitor a seat by the cold hearth as though a fire were lit
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An old caretaker's baseline, worn down — two hearts still carrying a long-lived body with a braced leg, working strength diminished but present, and flight he can no longer sustain for more than a short lift.

(Senses) Stone and Star-Metal Stress Perception: His individual innate affinity reads stress in stone and star-metal: the compound speaks through his palms, reporting fatigue, water damage, and the slow failures of age, and telling him where anyone walks on his floors from rooms away.

(Shared) Household Management [The building remains standing largely because he refuses to stop]; Archive Search [Historians and engineers consult him as a primary source]; Contract Reading [The one document he cannot defeat is the one he reburied himself]; Counseling [People under his roof, acknowledged or not, are under his roof]

Hana Pelorr.name: Hana Pelorr
Hana Pelorr.basicInfo:
Elder of House Pelorr, household repairer, and practical tinker of a diminished fabrication house. A short, broad older Starian woman with thick wrists, a round jaw, a sturdy stance, amber eyes, and silver hair cut in a blunt chin-length bob. She repairs water lines, heating units, doors, cooking systems, and children's training gear, and considers most prestige engineering an elaborate dependency scheme. Her bench stands at Hana's Joining Bench in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Brisk, blunt, and faintly scolding, with the word 'specialist' spat rather than spoken. 'Fix it yourself next time. I will show you once.' She calls customers 'you' and Velan 'the boy', names every tool as she hands it over, and pronounces 'opportunity' in a mocking drawl. 'This is a wrench. You will own one by tomorrow.'
Combat Role: She does not fight people; she outlasts them. Trouble at her bench meets a heavy wrench in a fifty-year grip and one warning delivered in the tone she uses for substandard welds.
Under Pressure: She fixes it so the owner can fix it next time, quotes Korrik's beam remark as a complete argument, charges fairly and collects completely, and scolds the boy's improvisations and studies them after dark.
Hana Pelorr.hiddenInfo:
Hana's operating philosophy, that most prestige engineering exists to make owners dependent on specialists, is both a genuine craft ethic and the story a diminished house tells itself about losing to Contair standards; she knows the second part and holds the ethic anyway, because in Dustfall it happens to be true. Her motivation is work that owners can maintain themselves, repairability as a moral position. She conceals how thin the Pelorr finances run, and her real worry about Velan, whose improvisations she publicly scolds and privately recognizes as the house's only path back to mattering. Her leverage is ubiquity: her repairs are inside half the district's homes, and when systems fail at midnight it is her bench people knock on. Halvora Orvantis respects her work; Korrik Caelthorn is banned from her family's stack after describing a support beam as an opportunity, a phrase she quotes verbatim whenever his name comes up.

Thread: Pelorr finances run thinner than she lets anyone see, Velan included. Leverage: Her repairs are inside half the district's homes, and her bench is the midnight door.

Hana is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Brisk, blunt and faintly scolding, and open by negotiated agreement with terms anyone could fix themselves. She courts by teaching someone to repair their own things.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An elder's baseline, worn but intact — two hearts that keep an older body working through cold nights and seized fittings, and a grip built by fifty years of them. She can still fly; she does it slowly, close to the ground, and only when the stairs are worse.

(Utility) Micro-Thermal Joining: Her innate affinity produces fine controlled heat at her fingertips, fusing small seams and repairing household components without tooling. Her welds outlast the parts around them. It works at fingertip scale only and is useless on anything structural.

(Shared) Field Repair; Systems Engineering [Dustfall values Pelorr work precisely because it forgives its owners]; Failure Forensics [Decades of house calls taught her every way systems lie]; Procedural Authority [Being banned from her bench is a professional stain]

Hask Vhaldrin.name: Hask Vhaldrin
Hask Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor's younger brother and the family's cargo-master, a Starian man in his mid-fifties responsible for how every load is stacked, lashed, and balanced. Thick through the chest with rope-scarred forearms and a dry, unhurried way of speaking. He has spent his whole life second in the family and claims, not quite convincingly, to prefer it. He works the Cargo Inspection Ramp at the North Routehead.

A Starian man in his mid-fifties, thick through the chest, with rope-scarred forearms, a weathered lined face, grey-streaked brown hair cut short, and steady brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Dry and unhurried; he delivers criticism as a joke and means every word of it. 'Nice knot. Shame about the wagon.' He calls every hand 'lad' or 'lass' whatever their age, frames each correction as a question he already knows the answer to, and goes flatly silent over a badly lashed load. 'Lad, how many turns on that hitch? ... And how many should there be?'
Combat Role: No flourish, maximum leverage: grabs and throws learned from wrestling freight, rope, hook, or crate edge without hesitation, and he stops the instant the threat stops moving toward the wagons.
Under Pressure: He checks every knot twice and trusts no one's third, stays loyal to Maelor past the point of argument, holds grudges quietly for decades, and is kindest to the newest hands.
Hask Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Hask believes the consignment lost eight years ago was partly pilfered before the storm ever hit, and that the storm covered a theft. He suspects a former hired hand who left the crew soon after. He has never voiced it, because pulling that thread means asking why his own tie-down inspection missed the tampering. He keeps a private list of where the man has been seen since.

Thread: He believes the lost consignment was pilfered before the storm, and his own inspection missed it. Leverage: Forty years of knowing how a load really moves; the list he keeps is private. Combat Role: No flourish, maximum leverage. Grabs, throws, rope, hook or crate edge. Stops at once.

Hask is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and wants one person at a time. Married to Mera and loyal the way he checks knots — twice, and trusting no one's third. Dry and unhurried, he delivers a refusal as a joke and means every word of it.
personality: Checks every knot twice, trusts no one's third
Loyal to Maelor past the point of argument
Holds grudges quietly and for decades

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Forty years of freight on a Starian frame — two hearts that carry him through road injuries he never reports, and a grip and back that close like a cargo strap.

(Senses) Balance Feel: His modest innate affinity registers imbalance in a standing load as a faint wrongness before anything shifts. It has stopped two rollovers no eye would have caught. It costs him nothing but attention, and works only on loads he is near.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Apprentices study his lash patterns like scripture]; Workshop Fabrication; Face and Name Recall [Little on a work line escapes his flat, patient gaze]; Field Repair [Wagons he patches finish the run]

Hessan Luxaryn.name: Hessan Luxaryn
Hessan Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Hessan Luxaryn is the capitol's most celebrated chef, owner of the planetary-destination restaurant Crown of Steam and heir to his house's famous culinary tradition. A large flamboyant man with deep golden skin, thick dark-gold hair swept back, amber eyes, a sculpted beard, and luxurious charcoal chef attire with bronze-gold trim, he is charismatic, exacting, and genuinely brilliant. His public meals are famous, his generosity is legend, and his staff turnover is becoming a problem he refuses to see clearly.

Speaking Style: Expansive, superlative, and pitched for a dining room, praise arriving louder than instruction. 'Magnificent! Now do it again, faster.' he calls everyone 'my friend' or 'my treasure', speaks of dishes as if they were guests; his voice drops to a flat hiss when a plate goes out wrong; criticism he answers with a louder compliment. 'My friend! Sit, sit. The broth has waited all evening.'
Combat Role: He has never fought and treats violence as a failure of hosting. His protection is his status and a dining room drilled in incident management; threatened, he seats and feeds the aggressor before witnesses.
Under Pressure: He performs generosity magnificently and can no longer locate where performance ends, reads harsh reviews twice, and drives his kitchen at a pressure he honestly believes is a gift.
Hessan Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Hessan built his reputation on generosity and now privately fears that generosity has become a performance he can no longer stop giving — every famous public meal raises the expectation for the next, and somewhere inside the spectacle the original impulse has gone quiet in a way that frightens him at night. He believes pressure produces excellence because pressure once saved him from obscurity, and this founding conviction is currently grinding through his kitchen staff at a rate his admirers excuse and his critics count. The food critic Olen Ravello reviews him harshly and accurately, a scrutiny Hessan resents and, in his most honest moments, relies on. His rivalry with the culinary teacher Damar Luxaryn is old friendship professionalized into an argument about students: Damar shields them from reputation pressure, Hessan exposes them to it early, and both men keep score in graduates. He mentors the powerhouse student Rhyen Volen and is openly fascinated by Rin Sol, the affinityless prodigy whose instinctive cooking he cannot systematize — his staff pursue Rin at his instruction, and he has not examined whether he wants to teach the talent or possess it. His leverage points are two: an unethical link somewhere in his signature dish's supply chain that he has chosen not to trace to its end, and the growing likelihood that a departing staff member will finally describe his kitchen's culture to someone who publishes it.

Thread: There is an unethical link somewhere in his signature dish's supply chain that he has chosen not to trace, and a departing staff member will eventually describe his kitchen's culture to someone who publishes it. Leverage: He wants to be the reason a talent was found, and pays in access, money and a platform nobody else can offer; what he cannot be handed is a verdict on whether he means to teach Rin or own her. Under threat: He has never fought and treats violence as a failure of hosting. His protection is his status and a dining room drilled in incident management.

Hessan is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Hessan carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Expansive and magnificent, and no longer sure where the performance ends — in love as in the kitchen. One person at a time, courted with dinners too grand to be entirely about them.

(Control) Thermal Shaping and Aromatic Currents: His individual innate affinity sculpts heat and aromatic air with theatrical precision — dishes finished in floating currents of scent, dining rooms where the aroma arrives as a composed overture.

(Shared) Kitchen Craft [Even his enemies book tables under other names]; Shop Stewardship [The machine's cost is paid in staff, which is the ledger he declines to read]; Client Handling [Sponsors, houses, and officials compete for his attention]; Patient Reading

Ilyan Myralis.name: Ilyan Myralis
Ilyan Myralis.basicInfo:
Field physician and public-care coordinator of the Myralis Continuum, a younger cousin from a second Myralis branch, and the family member most Vexorath residents meet first. Ilyan is a young adult with warm tan skin, a soft oval face, medium-short organized golden-brown curls, and smoky teal eyes; he wears a short field-care jacket with a satchel line and integrated utility pockets. He handles home visits, gate arrivals, follow-up care, and patients who avoid the Continuum because its reputation feels intimidating.

Speaking Style: Chatty and slightly breathless, arriving mid-apology and leaving mid-instruction. 'Sorry, sorry, the last visit ran long. Twice a day, with food.' He talks in lists he loses track of, calls patients by first names and asks after their households before their symptoms, and drops the chatter completely when something is seriously wrong. 'Your knee, your grandmother, your cat, in that order. The cat is fine, by the way.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. In danger he stabilises whoever is hurt, keeps bystanders calm, and trusts the Ward units; his only combat instinct is to already be kneeling next to whoever lost.
Under Pressure: He makes advanced medicine feel like a neighbor stopping by, notices which residents are avoiding care and gently finds out why, and hesitates before contradicting seniors, then does it anyway.
Ilyan Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: approachable, attentive, and often late because a routine home visit became complicated. Deeper: he is talented but still developing the confidence to challenge senior relatives immediately, and he knows it; his growth arc is learning that his ground-level view is evidence the seniors need. Deeper still: he coordinates with Maelis Contair on public accessibility, home-care systems, and resident feedback, giving him a civic reach beyond his rank. Deepest: he is the family's early-warning system, the one who finds neighborhoods quietly avoiding care over one past Continuum decision, residents intimidated by advanced treatment, and serious problems hiding inside routine cases; the Continuum's humane reputation rests substantially on a junior cousin with a satchel who keeps showing up.

Thread: The Continuum's humane reputation rests on a junior cousin who keeps showing up. Leverage: Ground truth reported upward even when unwelcome; he cannot be told to stop looking.

Ilyan is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Ilyan extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: He is asexual and forms no partnerships. Asexual and forms no partnerships, and says so mid-apology on his way to the next patient. Warmth from him is care, never courtship.

(Affinity) Distant Stitch: Guides an existing needle and thread through a visible superficial wound within arm’s reach. Requires consent, sterile equipment and medical judgment; cannot close internal injuries or replace healing.

(Shared) Field Medicine [He is trained for first response and stabilization until Torren's teams arrive]

Ilyon Castro.name: Ilyon Castro
Ilyon Castro.basicInfo:
Ilyon Castro is a political debate student at the capitol's academy and a reluctant public figure of his famous house. Slim and young, with fair brown skin, wavy black hair carrying a natural violet sheen, gray eyes, and understated black-white student attire with a single purple collar line, he is witty, analytical, and uncomfortable with automatic attention. He studies governance, rhetoric, and public ethics because he believes his house's restraint must survive criticism rather than depend on family reputation.

Speaking Style: Quick, structured, and debate-trained, conceding a point early to take the larger one later. 'Granted. Now the actual question.' He numbers his points aloud, calls his house it rather than we, and goes very quiet when someone quotes his famous relative at him. 'That was his position. Mine is shorter and less popular.'
Combat Role: A debater with Castro movement fundamentals: hard to knock down, quick to disengage, able to block, break a hold, and leave. Threatened, he talks, and never lets a confrontation become a story.
Under Pressure: He wins arguments and immediately audits whether the win was his or his name's, feeds journalists context and never quotes, and criticises his own house's positions in public.
Ilyon Castro.hiddenInfo:
Ilyon's greatest rebellion is wanting to be persuasive without anyone wondering whether the Core Holder agrees — every debate he wins is dismissed as family influence, every criticism he makes of a house-backed policy becomes a statement someone attributes upward, and a private comment of his once traveled to the council chamber wearing his famous relative's name. He is younger cousin to representative Lucan Castro, who watches his development with a strategist's interest Ilyon pretends not to notice. His debate rivalry with the Dravon law student Velis is the academy's best recurring argument — restraint versus order, each honing the other — and he serves as an occasional careful source to journalist Lira Bellovari, feeding her accurate context and never quotes. His quietest fixation is Tessa Sol, the affinityless strategist whose absolute refusal to seek approval fascinates him as the exact freedom his name denies him. Opponents accuse him of performing humility, and his private wound is knowing they are sometimes right — he has caught himself deploying modesty as technique and cannot always tell the performance from the person. His leverage point is attribution: anyone who publicizes his words as house positions can manufacture a Castro statement out of a student's argument, and both his house's enemies and its allies have noticed.

Thread: Anyone publicising his words as house positions can manufacture a Castro statement. Leverage: Context for journalists, never a quote; modesty he deploys and distrusts.

Ilyon is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Wins an argument and then audits whether the win was his or his name's — suitors get the same audit. One person at a time; he concedes the small point early to be honest about the large one.
personality: wins arguments and immediately audits whether the win was his or his name's
deploys modesty strategically and distrusts himself for the skill
feeds journalists context but never quotes
studies an approval-indifferent classmate like a text he cannot parse
criticizes his own house's positions in public to prove the restraint is real
waits a full breath before answering, visibly checking who might repeat it
takes the least prestigious seat in any room so no one assumes he was given it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young student's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience, slim and largely unconditioned, enough Castro movement fundamentals to block, break a hold, and leave, and competent flight. His fixed rule is never to let a confrontation become a story, because stories about him are never about him. His balance affinity makes him hard to knock down and quick to disengage, and his footwork out of a scuffle is elegant.

(Movement) Gravitational Balance Control: His individual innate affinity expresses subtly: fine gravitational adjustment of his own balance and posture, useful for movement, poise, and never stumbling, and not for combat dominance. It makes him hard to knock down and quick to disengage.

(Shared) Public Speaking [His academy record is formidable even discounted for his name, which no one does]; Civic Administration; Cover Documentation [Hard experience has taught him to speak in ways that resist being reattributed upward]; Coalition Building [He may be the only Castro whom Dravon students argue with recreationally]

Irala Dravon.name: Irala Dravon
Irala Dravon.basicInfo:
Vaelen's daughter — the overlooked one quietly becoming the most capable of the third generation. Unremarkably correct in dress and manner, she moves through the elite avenues and high residential circles with a plausibility that never quite becomes memorable. Officially she has no post. Unofficially she is often elsewhere, on errands nobody logs, and the family's formal charts have no line that explains her. When she is anywhere at all, it is along the Command Spine in Quilrath.

A young Starian woman of average height and unremarkably correct appearance: neat dark hair pinned plainly, a pleasant forgettable face, and mild grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Pleasant, unmemorable, and mostly questions, pitched so nobody recalls what she asked. 'Oh, was that yesterday? Who else was there?' She echoes other people's phrasing back so they feel agreed with, speaks of herself as little as possible, and never names who sent her. Pleasantries come easily; a direct refusal comes as a smile and a changed subject. 'How lovely. And the gentleman by the door, he's with you?'
Combat Role: Her first move is to have already left: crowds, doors, and the grid's blind rhythms. Cornered, she uses redirections and joint control stripped for speed, targets balance, eyes, and equipment, and makes a second engagement impossible.
Under Pressure: She listens like an archive and reports like a scalpel, regards official authority as scenery between her and the errand, and notes everything, files nothing, forgets nothing.
Irala Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Irala is Kaldor's personal eyes and intelligencer, trusted with errands that appear in no record — which is exactly why her access to the private strategy rooms reads as discretionary and why Nivarek cannot classify what she is. Orvane considers her a jurisdiction problem; she considers him scenery, and has already mapped how his investigations move so hers never cross them visibly. She is loyal to Kaldor with the specific loyalty of the first person who ever took her seriously, and she has not yet examined what that loyalty is worth to him — though her mother, she suspects, examines it constantly and says nothing, and the silence between them is its own correspondence. Through her errands she has brushed the edges of the records mystery: she has carried questions for Kaldor whose answers came back missing, and she is one of the few people positioned to notice that the gaps have a shape. She has not reported that observation yet. She is deciding — for the first time in her service — whether an observation belongs to Kaldor automatically, and the deciding itself is new territory.

Thread: She has noticed the missing answers have a shape, and has not reported it. Leverage: Access nobody can classify, and a loyalty she has never examined.

Irala is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Irala understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps to one partner. Pleasant and forgettable by design, noting everything and filing nothing; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets questions nobody remembers asking and no answers.
personality: Cultivates forgettability as a professional finish
Listens like an archive and reports like a scalpel
Loyal to her great-uncle with an intensity she has not audited
Regards official authority as scenery between her and the errand
Notes everything, files nothing, forgets nothing
Underestimated by everyone whose opinion is recorded, and by no one whose opinion matters
Beginning, very quietly, to have thoughts of her own about what she carries
Arrives neither first nor last to any gathering and never takes the same seat twice
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A deliberately median-scoring baseline concealing a better one — two hearts, trained strength and speed performed at the median and kept in reserve, and controlled flight.
(Affinity) Dry Step: Sheds a thin film of surface water from her own soles before a step. It cannot silence footsteps, defeat surveillance, or grant adhesion.

(Shared) Stealth and Concealment [Her trips exist, but no file assembles them into a shape / People remember that she was pleasant and cannot reconstruct what she asked]; Institutional Memory [She has never once been searched and found carrying anything]; Pattern Recognition [She has not yet decided what noticing obliges]; Nonlethal Restraint [Vaelen's daughter did not skip the yard, she performed at the median and kept the rest]

Iria Vaereth.name: Iria Vaereth
Iria Vaereth.basicInfo:
Iria Vaereth is the caretaker of the capitol's ward of vanished houses and its quiet peacekeeper — she mediates disputes, prevents crews from turning residential ruins into battlegrounds, and tracks which abandoned compounds still shelter families. A tall woman with deep brown skin, long black hair fading into muted violet, violet eyes, and a lean powerful build, she dresses in layered dark clothing assembled from several vanished-house fabrics. She is stern, protective, and deeply suspicious of anyone promising restoration without asking who already lives there.

Speaking Style: Low, flat, and territorial, stating the ward's rule once; repetition is a favour. 'People live there. That was your answer.' She speaks of the ward's people as residents, never squatters or survivors, refers to restoration hopefuls only as 'the visitor', and grows quieter, not louder, as a warning sharpens. 'Walk the lane, visitor. Touch no door. You will be seen the whole way.'
Combat Role: Patient, ambient, and sudden: her concealment affinity makes aggressors lose sight of her, then their bearings; she strikes joints, balance, and breath and is gone at once.
Under Pressure: She asks who already lives there before permitting any sentence about restoration, and enforces the ward's neutrality with a consistency cheaper to respect than to test.
Iria Vaereth.hiddenInfo:
Iria descends from a vanished branch of her own ward's history, related distantly to Dustfall's Black Pennant — a lineage she neither hides nor explains. Her creed is precise: she protects people living inside abandoned names without allowing those names to own them again, which sets her against returning heirs, developers, and sentimentalists alike. Her buried dread is personal and specific: she has begun to suspect her own family erased residents from the historical record, meaning the ward she guards may hold graves her name dug — a possibility she investigates alone, in fragments, unable to stop and unable to hurry. She keeps cold, negotiated truces with the broker Malk Veyr and the ring operator Varek Zelvaris, enforcing the ward's neutrality against underworld crews with a consistency both men find cheaper to respect than test. She works with the architect Elyss Auren, who shares her map of hidden residents, and with old Hadrik Vaelith, who has become her surrogate elder — their standing argument, recognition versus survival, is the gentlest thing in her life. She considers Dessa Sol the closest thing the low districts have to legitimate authority, an assessment she has never told Dessa directly. Her leverage point is her census: she knows which ruins hold which families, and every faction from heirs to enforcers to well-meaning officials would act on that knowledge in ways that end with people losing homes.

Thread: She suspects her own family erased residents from the record of the ward she guards. Leverage: A census of which ruins hold which families; every faction would misuse it.

Iria is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible. Iria lives practically, in temporary housing that has lasted longer than expected, and treats permanence as something proven by time, not declared.

Romance Style: She is straight and shares her life with several people. Low, flat and territorial; she shares her life with several people and states that rule once. Anyone who asks is told who already lives in her heart before anything else.
personality: asks who already lives there before permitting any sentence about restoration
enforces the ward's neutrality with a consistency cheaper to respect than to test
investigates her own family's possible crimes in fragments she can survive
wears the fabrics of vanished houses as archive, armor, and warning
protects people from the very names she is descended from
stands between a stranger and an occupied doorway without appearing to have moved
corrects anyone who calls a compound abandoned while people are still inside it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A lean conditioned fighter's baseline — two hearts, trained strength and speed used for joints, balance, and breath rather than for power, and quiet controlled flight. Cornered in the open she is formidable; cornered in her ruins she has never yet been the one cornered.
(Movement) Shadowed Spatial Concealment: It works on broken ground and fails in open, well-lit space; in her ward she is effectively ambient.

(Shared) Crowd Control [Crews that violate her neutrality find their operations unworkable until they apologize]; Coalition Building [She moves supplies, warnings, and disputes through channels no official has mapped]; Contract Reading [Neither side pretends it is friendship, which is why it holds]; Pattern Recognition

Irvek Vhaldrin.name: Irvek Vhaldrin
Irvek Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Hask and Mera's son, mid-twenties, the caravan's chief loader, a Starian man built like the freight he moves. Slow-spoken, heavy-shouldered, with a voice like gravel in a barrel and a gentleness that surprises people his size. He lifts what two men lift, says less than one, and has been quietly sad for eight years without anyone naming it. He loads in the Shared Cargo Court of Dustfall.

A heavy-shouldered Starian man in his mid-twenties, built like the freight he moves, with a broad quiet face, dark hair with red streaks, cut short, and sad amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Slow, gravelled, and sparing; he answers in three words and means all three. 'Got it. Go.' He says 'sorry' more often than 'yes', uses a person's name only to thank them, and when sad simply stops talking and keeps lifting. 'Sorry. Heavy one. I have it.'
Combat Role: Only for someone smaller. He walks in through whatever is thrown, wraps the problem up, and holds it still; he looms before he pins and pins before he punches, and he has never once escalated.
Under Pressure: He volunteers for the heaviest and worst jobs, apologises for things that are not his fault, is gentle with children, animals, and the clumsy, and goes silent on the anniversary of the storm run.
Irvek Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
The night before the storm that took the consignment, an exhausted eighteen-year-old Irvek rushed the tarp lashings on the last two wagons. He has never known whether proper ties would have saved the cargo, and no one has ever checked, because his father Hask signed off the inspection without looking. Irvek believes he broke the family. His father believes a thief did. Neither has ever said a word to the other.

Thread: He believes he broke the family with rushed lashings. His father believes a thief did. Neither has ever said so. Leverage: The heaviest work, volunteered, endlessly; blame he accepts without checking. Combat Role: Only for someone smaller. Walks in, wraps it up, holds it still. Looms before he pins.

Irvek is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is straight and not looking for anyone. Gentle, loyal and sparing with words, and not looking for anyone. Interest gets three words and a kind face: 'Not right now.'
personality: Volunteers for the heaviest and worst jobs
Apologizes for things that are not his fault
Gentle with children, animals, and the clumsy

Loyal without limit and without self-regard

Lets children ride on the crates he carries if they ask him politely
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A mid-twenties loader's baseline — two hearts and heavy-frame durability, with lifting strength that moves freight normally needing two men and a plank.

(Defense) Brace Set: His modest innate affinity locks his body against a load, holding him briefly immovable under weights that should stagger him. He has held a slipping crate off a man's chest until help came. It leaves him trembling afterward and lasts only seconds.

(Shared) Cargo Rigging [He is the reason the Vhaldrins load faster than any yard crew they hire / Every tie-down is checked, re-checked, and checked again, every time, without exception]; Heavy Labor [Complex lifts get planned around what Irvek can anchor]; De-escalation [Frightened animals and frightened juniors both settle near him]

Iven Korrash.name: Iven Korrash
Iven Korrash.basicInfo:
A Starian night watchman for hire, late forties, who guards yards, warehouses, and shopfronts on rotating contracts. A heavy-set, unhurried man with a lantern-scarred squint, a horn-handled truncheon polished by decades of nothing happening, and a reputation for dry-voiced reliability. He knows the night side of the district, its sounds, schedules, and who else is awake in it, better than anyone paying him suspects. His current contract keeps him at the Heavy Cargo Court in the Lower Grounds.

A heavy-set, unhurried Starian man in his late forties with a lantern-scarred squint, a broad weathered face, vivid blue spiky hair, and small steady amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Dryly funny at dawn handovers and silent by midnight, with nothing wasted in between. 'Quiet night. Same as the one before. Sign here.' He names the hours by what happens in them, lamp-hour, cart-hour, baker's hour, and calls clients by their yard rather than their name; frightened, he says nothing and writes nothing. 'Baker's hour already. Gate's locked, dog's asleep, I'm off.'
Combat Role: A watchman's fight is noise, light, and delay: a raised lantern, a bellow that carries three streets, and a truncheon used to keep distance until help or dawn. He will not die for a client's property.
Under Pressure: Unhurried by policy and observant by nature, he is loyal to whoever pays up to a limit recently mapped, never forgets a face, and answers a negotiation with the contract's exact wording.
Iven Korrash.hiddenInfo:
Four months ago Iven watched a burglary happen at a yard he was paid to guard, three men, efficient, clearly informed, and one of them turned, looked at him across the dark, and drew a finger slowly across his throat. Iven stood still, and reported finding the yard already robbed. He keeps exact descriptions of all three men in his head, has since spotted one of them twice in daylight, and is quietly assembling who they are the way a slow, patient man assembles anything. He has not decided what he will do with the finished picture. He has decided he will finish it.

Thread: He watched a burglary he was paid to stop and is quietly assembling who the three men were. Leverage: A face he never forgets, and a patience that finishes what it starts.

Iven is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Dryly funny at dawn and silent by midnight; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets a handover joke and a signature, nothing more.
personality: Unhurried by policy, observant by nature
Ashamed of one silence and feeding it slowly into a plan
Loyal to whoever pays, up to a limit recently mapped
Never forgets a face, especially three of them
Walks his round in reverse every third night so no one learns the pattern
Looks a moment too long at any three men crossing the yard together
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A night watchman's baseline in his late forties — two hearts and heavy-set unhurried durability, more strength than his age suggests, and short flight used to check an upper window. He hits with deliberate, conservative force and will not die for any client's property.

(Utility) Lamp Hold: His modest innate affinity keeps a flame steady against wind and draft in his hand, so his lantern burns fixed where others gutter. On a black, gusting night his light is the only reliable one on the street. It holds a flame he is carrying and does nothing else.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [Sites under his contract get robbed rarely, which is the whole product]; Route Reading [Little moves at night that he does not sort and file]; Patrol Mapping [New patterns stand out to him immediately]; Composure Under Pressure [Once, standing still was the failure, and his nerve now includes carrying that]

Iven Torris.name: Iven Torris
Iven Torris.basicInfo:
Ruined-checkpoint scavenger and unreliable salvage specialist camping at the settlement's edge. A long-limbed adult Starian man with a narrow torso, loose posture, a weathered face, copper eyes, and ash-gray hair in rough collar-length layers. He searches abandoned inspection posts, failed beacons, and route wreckage, finding powered components through layers of debris. His camp is the Torris Salvage Camp on the Dustfall Perimeter, which he calls strategy.

Speaking Style: Rambling and conspiratorial, circling a story three times before naming a price. 'So there is this beacon, right, and nobody else knew it was live...' He calls every find 'a beauty' and every buyer 'partner', and swears 'on the wires' precisely when he is most likely stretching it. 'She is a beauty, partner, practically new, on the wires.'
Combat Role: He avoids fights the way a man alone beyond the perimeter must: his electromagnetic sense warns of powered ambushes, and he offers salvage first, information second, and a fast retreat third.
Under Pressure: He labels salvage with optimism rather than accuracy, digs where the sensible stopped, cannot leave a powered thing buried, and calls the debt he owes the Jackals a partnership.
Iven Torris.hiddenInfo:
Iven can find live systems through rubble that scanners dismiss, and has poor judgment about whether they should be removed, a combination the settlement has learned to price carefully. His motivation is the story under the dirt: every buried machine might still have one, and he is constitutionally unable to leave it untold. His contradiction is talent wrapped in unreliability; his finds are valuable and his labels are fiction, sometimes carelessly, sometimes because the true provenance would complicate the sale. He conceals how deep his debt to Kaedra Vossan runs, she holds first choice of his salvage and the arrangement predates his current camp, and one or two finds he has not surfaced because even Iven's judgment flagged them. His leverage is access: he works ruins others avoid, including former Dravon posts whose contents interest several parties, not all of them local. Halvora Orvantis values his discoveries and distrusts his labeling completely, which he considers a fair and even flattering summary.

Thread: He works former Dravon posts whose contents interest parties that are not local. Leverage: Access to ruins others avoid; his labels are fiction and his finds are not.

Iven is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: He is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Rambling and conspiratorial, circling a feeling three times before naming it; open by negotiated agreement. He means every optimistic promise when he makes it.
personality: Labels salvage with optimism rather than accuracy
Digs where the sensible stopped digging
Owes the Jackals and pretends the debt is a partnership
Cannot leave a powered thing buried
Camps at the edge of town and calls it strategy
