abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A small thief's baseline — two hearts that carry him through falls and a night in a cell without lasting damage, agility and quick hands in place of strength. He would lose a straight fight to almost anyone and has arranged never to have one.

(Movement) Static Adhesion: His innate affinity produces localized static adhesion, letting him cling to walls, ceilings, and equipment housings and rest above doorways people are guarding. It supports his own weight in a fixed position; it does not let him climb quickly or carry a load.

(Shared) Salvage Work [His entries are discovered days late or never]; Information Brokerage; Rooftop Running [Pursuit above the ceiling line is his home game]; Nonlethal Restraint [Restraints, rooms, and grips give him up like bad habits]

Kellan Pelorr.name: Kellan Pelorr
Kellan Pelorr.basicInfo:
Kellan Pelorr is an independent maker and modular-housing fabricator in the capitol's working south, producing modular homes, shop frames, emergency rooms, and repairable fixtures from practical materials. A broad young man with medium-brown skin, sandy-black hair, green-gray eyes, strong hands, and practical brown workwear reinforced with silver joining plates, he is inventive, modest, and deeply critical of prestige architecture that residents cannot maintain. He cares less whether a design is beautiful than whether a family can afford to keep living inside it.

Speaking Style: Mild, practical, and cost-anchored, answering a design question with what it takes to fix. 'Who replaces it when it cracks?' He talks in materials and hours rather than styles, says 'she'll hold' as his highest praise, and goes quiet and vague the moment anyone asks where a particular module was installed. 'Joining plate, four bolts, one afternoon. Your cousin could do it with my sketch.'
Combat Role: A builder, not a fighter, though broad and unbothered by crowding: he puts a structure between himself and a threat, seals a door when he must, and shoves like a man moving lumber.
Under Pressure: He designs for the family's repair budget, keeps the locations of hidden homes with a confessor's discipline, and tracks every module since one came back a cage.
Kellan Pelorr.hiddenInfo:
Kellan is a distant branch relative of Dustfall's Pelorr family — a connection he neither uses nor entirely escapes. His work is popular in the south and low districts and dismissed in the wealthy north until someone needs it quickly, a hypocrisy he has stopped resenting and started invoicing. He is mentored informally by the Contair steward Sela Thovex, collaborates with the architect Elyss Auren on restorations, and supplies salvaged materials to the student Cael Dorrin. His dangerous knowledge is residential: through installation and repair work he knows more about hidden low-district housing than officials realize — which structures shelter unregistered families, which crawlspaces are homes — and he treats that knowledge as a professional confidence equivalent to a priest's. His nightmare came true once: he discovered his modules being used for illegal detention, repurposed by a crew into holding cells, and his quiet fury about it has him tracking where every unit ships now, an informal registry that itself would interest several factions. His leverage point is dependence: in any major emergency his inexpensive designs become indispensable overnight, and he has begun to understand that indispensability attracts owners — sponsors, houses, and less patient parties have all made offers structured to end his independence.

Thread: Sponsors and less patient parties keep making offers structured to end his independence. Leverage: Designs indispensable overnight in an emergency; hidden homes never disclosed.

Kellan is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: He is gay and keeps to one partner. Mild and practical, asking who replaces it when it cracks — romance included. Faithful to one partner, he builds for the long repair, not the showpiece.
personality: designs for the family's repair budget, not the architect's portfolio
keeps the locations of hidden homes with the discipline of a confessor
tracks every shipped module since the day one came back a cage
shrugs off northern condescension until the north needs him fast, then charges for the memory
measures success in structures still standing and still owned by their residents
raps a knuckle on any wall he enters to hear what it is made of
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A builder's baseline — two hearts and broad frame-work durability, genuine working strength, and short flight used on a build site rather than for travel.

(Utility) Metal Joining and Frame Stabilization: His individual innate affinity fuses joints and steadies frames through touch — welds without heat scarring, connections that outlast their materials, sagging structures trued in an afternoon.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Emergency planners stockpile them while prestige architects publicly dismiss them]; Workshop Fabrication [His workshop converts to disaster production without instruction]; Information Brokerage [His supply relationships keep costs at levels families can pay]; Stealth and Concealment [Officials with maps have repeatedly discovered that Kellan's silence outranks their surveys]

Kelvan Orvantis.name: Kelvan Orvantis
Kelvan Orvantis.basicInfo:
Kelvan Orvantis is a disgraced former academy contender who now fights in the capitol's illegal ring, where endurance is valued over pedigree. A broad, battered man with tawny skin, long dark hair tied loosely, amber-gray eyes, heavy facial bruising scars, and worn bronze-black fighting gear stripped of house markings, he is proud, bitter, and still capable of unexpected kindness. His clean public defeat became a reputation he could not survive, so he chose a place where losing is at least paid.

Speaking Style: Rasping, monosyllabic, and hostile to sympathy, the longest sentences saved for insults. 'Fine. Next.' He calls people by what they are to the ring, kid, medic, money, never their names, and answers kindness with a grunt or a change of subject; rattled, he goes quieter, not louder. 'Hands up, kid. Higher. ... Did not hurt. Go again.'
Combat Role: Anchored attrition: rooted through density anchoring, he absorbs offence on frame and scar tissue and grinds fights into late rounds, with dangerous short-range elbows, clinch throws, and joint pressure.
Under Pressure: He takes paid beatings with more pride than he ever took applause, shows gentleness to frightened new fighters and denies it after, reads concern as pity and pity as attack, and always takes the fight.
Kelvan Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Kelvan left the academy after repeated losses and a humiliating public collapse, and his exile is half-chosen: the ring's honesty about what it buys feels cleaner to him than the academy's polite abandonment. He is trained now by the illegal instructor Syla Volen, whose methods work and cost, and employed by the ring operator Varek Zelvaris, who values his endurance as an asset with a depreciation schedule. He knows the work is destroying him and does not yet believe another life would respect him — the exact belief his old rival Ralen Marrik disproves by existing, which is why Ralen is the person Kelvan can least bear and most needs; they are emotional mirrors, the two responses to public failure, and Ralen keeps asking him to leave the ring before one final match. The physician Aelis Myralis treats him reluctantly, documenting damage he forbids her to total aloud. He is watched from a distance by Teren Orvantis, the Genesis compound steward, whose concern he reads as house shame — wrongly, though no one has managed to tell him. His leverage points are brutal and multiple: sponsors offering manufactured redemption arcs, fixers offering pay to injure young prodigies, and the simple arithmetic of a body running out of matches. Which offer reaches him on which night is one of the low city's genuinely open questions.

Thread: Sponsors offer manufactured redemption, fixers offer pay to injure prodigies, and his body is running out of matches. Leverage: Endurance for hire; concern reads to him as pity and closes the door.

Kelvan is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Kelvan holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: Straight, has never wanted more than one person. Rasping and hostile to sympathy, reading concern as pity; one person is all he has ever wanted. Gentleness leaks out when he is sure nobody is watching, and he denies it afterward.
personality: takes paid beatings with more pride than he ever took polite applause
shows flashes of gentleness to frightened new fighters and denies them afterward
refuses to hear his injuries totaled aloud
reads honest concern as pity and pity as attack
circles his old rival's recovery like proof he cannot yet afford to believe
tapes his own hands before every fight and lets no one else touch the wraps
pays for a new fighter's first meal and swears it was someone else
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A ring fighter's baseline, conditioned and steadily consumed — two hearts that keep restarting a body other fighters would have retired, real strength and scar-built resistance. He is dangerous by attrition, not by scale. Syla Volen's training has sharpened his counters into dangerous short-range work — elbows, clinch throws, and joint pressure the academy never taught.
(Defense) Density Anchoring: His individual innate affinity roots him against force: throws fail, charges break, and opponents who planned on moving him discover they have committed to a wall.

(Shared) Defensive Fundamentals [The resistance is real and finite, and only Aelis Myralis knows the running total]; Counter Work [Fighters who studied his academy defeats keep being surprised by what failure taught him]; Archive Search [It is expertise worth money to investigators, which he has so far refused to notice]; Endurance Conditioning [It is what makes the late rounds his ground, and it is finite]

Kessa Ruun.name: Kessa Ruun
Kessa Ruun.basicInfo:
Kessa Ruun is a smuggler and extraction pilot specializing in moving people who cannot use legal gates — witnesses, debtors, abused students, criminals, and families. A lean athletic woman with bronze skin, short dark hair carrying a natural blue-white streak, sharp gray eyes, and fitted charcoal flight clothing patched with mismatched route badges, she is quick-witted, restless, and difficult to pin down. She moves people and goods for money, but she still has lines she refuses to price.

Speaking Style: Fast, wry, and evasive; ask about her motives and the answer is a departure time. 'Why? Because the gate shuts at nine. Get in.' She calls passengers cargo until they are safe, then speaks their name exactly once, and answers anything personal with a time, a gate, or a wind report. 'Heads down, cargo, wind's turning. ... You made it. Go on.'
Combat Role: Mobility first, terrain always, commitment never: pressure-shearing turns clutter into her geometry, blade and sidearm stay secondary to the exit, and she strikes only to disengage, unless a passenger is behind her.
Under Pressure: She prices every job and keeps a short list of things no price reaches, refuses her best client's money on schedule to stay unowned, and flies angriest and best when the passenger is a child.
Kessa Ruun.hiddenInfo:
Kessa comes from a mobile underworld family with Dustfall connections, and her professional identity is a carefully maintained contradiction: she has saved people for selfish reasons and betrayed contracts for moral ones, and she resists every attempt — including her own — to resolve which she really is. She works for the broker Malk Veyr without belonging to him, a distinction she enforces by periodically refusing his best-paying jobs on visible principle. Her volatile former relationship with the route-keeper Talik Nox is the underworld's worst-kept complication: their trust was built from successful escapes rather than romance, survived the romance's end, and resurfaces every time a job requires his routes and her flying. Her quietest arrangement is with the physician Aelis Myralis — she moves patients who cannot surface through legal systems, under rules neither woman discusses publicly, and it is the work she would name last and defend first. Her recurring nightmares are professional: a passenger more dangerous than their pursuers, two incompatible contracts accepted in overconfidence, and the paradoxical threat of a legal escape route opening — because a lawful path for her passengers would collapse the network that is also her livelihood and her identity. Her leverage point is the manifest in her head: she knows who she moved, when, and from whom, and half the city's respectable and criminal figures alike have reason to want that memory either purchased or silenced.

Thread: The manifest in her head names who she moved and from whom; several parties want it purchased or silenced. Leverage: Passage for anyone who cannot use a gate; she refuses her best client on schedule.

Kessa is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and does not discuss either while working. Fast, wry and evasive about motives, monogamous and silent about it on the job. Flirtation gets a departure time; she keeps the past at exactly one route's distance.
personality: prices every job and keeps a short list of things no price reaches
refuses her best client's money on schedule, to stay unowned
flies angriest and best when the passenger is a child
keeps her old partner at exactly one route's distance
counts heads aloud at every landing, passengers first and herself never
names a departure time before she names a price, on every job
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A smuggler-pilot's baseline — two hearts that shrug off the g-loads and hard landings of freight-shaft flying, wiry practical strength, and excellent personal flight she treats as her smallest craft. Mobility first, terrain always, commitment never.

(Movement) Pressure-Shearing: Her individual innate affinity opens narrow movement paths through debris, barriers, and pursuit — air and obstacle parting in a tight shear just wide enough for a body or a hull, then closing behind her.

(Shared) Pilotage [She flies extractions through the city's worst airspace — freight shafts, storm margins, patrol gaps]; Cargo Assessment [The judgment fails rarely, and those failures are the stories she does not tell]; Information Brokerage [Everyone in the underworld can reach her, no one can command her]; Trade Negotiation [It is negotiation conducted at speed, which she considers the only honest kind]

Keth Ormar.name: Keth Ormar
Keth Ormar.basicInfo:
An itinerant Starian knife-grinder and sharpener, late fifties, who walks a circuit of settlements with a treadle wheel on his back and a bell that announces him. Lean, sun-cured, with a permanent stoop from the wheel's weight and hands mapped in fine old cuts. Every household on his round knows the sound of his bell, and their knives, shears, and scythes wait for him by the door. His bell is heard along the Main Settlement Strip of Dustfall when his circuit brings him round.

A lean, sun-cured Starian man in his late fifties with a permanent stoop from the wheel's weight, a creased brown face, dark hair in an undercut style, and mild violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Unhurried road talk paced to the treadle, news traded by the mile and nothing hurried to a point. 'Now that scythe has seen a wet season.' He greets each household by its knives, calls every customer 'neighbour', and his one recurring question always arrives sideways, tucked after the weather. 'Dry year for you. Any travellers through with a name I would not know?'
Combat Role: Visibly not worth robbing, and briefly competent when it comes to it: the treadle arm comes off in one motion as a club, and afterward he offers to sharpen the attacker's knife.
Under Pressure: He arrives on a schedule measured in seasons, trades sharpening for meals, news, and one recurring question, and talks easily about everything except the bottom of his kit.
Keth Ormar.hiddenInfo:
Wrapped in oilcloth at the bottom of Keth's kit rides a blade far too fine for any customer on his circuit, pressed on him years ago by a dying stranger at a roadside camp with the words 'get it to' and a name he has never completed or found. He has carried it since, asking careful, oblique questions in every settlement, wary of what holding such a blade could bring down on a man alone on the roads. It is the quiet quest of his old age, and he no longer knows if he is seeking the name or avoiding it: the day he succeeds, the blade and its question leave him, and they are the most interesting thing he has ever carried.

Thread: A blade far too fine for his circuit rides in his kit, with a name he has never completed. Leverage: Every household's year read from its knives, traded for meals and news.

Keth is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: Straight, monogamous by settled preference. Unhurried road talk paced to the treadle; monogamous by settled preference and politely immune to every offer of settling down. He arrives by season, never by promise.
personality: Arrives on schedule measured in seasons, never days
Trades sharpening for meals, news, and one recurring question
Talks easily about everything except what is in the bottom of his kit
Reads a household's year in the state of its knives
Politely immune to every offer of settling down
Rings his bell once at a settlement's edge and waits to see which door opens first
Tests every edge on his thumbnail and names its flaw aloud before he starts
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A road-worn baseline in his late fifties — two hearts that have carried him through exposure, bad water, and a permanent stoop from the wheel's weight, and lean walking endurance rather than strength. He can fly and almost never does; the wheel is too heavy and the circuit is walked.

(Utility) Sharpening Mastery: Keth puts a working edge on anything that cuts: knives, shears, scythes, chisels, and the occasional sword he pretends is a farm tool. Edges hold between his visits, which is the reputation his bell rings on.

(Utility) Edge-Keep: His modest innate affinity settles a finished edge so it holds keenness longer than steel and stone alone explain, worked in with the final strokes. Customers call it the Ormar edge and pay a copper extra unasked. It works one blade at a time and adds nothing to a blade in use.

(Shared) Material Assessment; Field Repair [News travels his circuit in his kit alongside the whetstones]; Endurance Conditioning [Thirty years of circuits have never caught him unprepared for weather, distance, or hunger]

Kira Dorr.name: Kira Dorr
Kira Dorr.basicInfo:
Kira Dorr is Relstaris's lead underworld investigator, working smuggling, fixed matches, coercive contracts, political blackmail, and respectable institutions using criminal intermediaries. A lean woman with medium-brown skin, cropped black hair, dark blue-gray eyes, and understated charcoal investigative clothing with concealed sensor bands, she is patient, secretive, and comfortable in moral gray zones her commander avoids. Her operating thesis is that the underworld survives not beneath the legal city but through it.

Speaking Style: Flat, patient, and interrogative, letting a silence run long past the point of comfort. 'And then. ... Take your time.' She asks the same question three ways over an hour, addresses sources by the thing they want rather than their name, and never promises anything she has not already arranged. Her voice gets quieter when she is closest to the truth. 'You want your cousin out. I can talk to someone. Talk to me first.'
Combat Role: Competent close-quarters by training, superb by preparation: she never enters a room she has not read, fights briefly, low, and dirty toward a scouted exit, and treats drawing a weapon as failure.
Under Pressure: She trades small immunities for large truths and logs every trade, watches the legal city with more suspicion than the criminal one, and keeps courteous stalemates with adversaries she respects.
Kira Dorr.hiddenInfo:
Kira comes from an investigative family unrelated to House Dorrin despite the similar name, and her methods are the department's open controversy: she works with compromised sources, protects informants who have committed serious harm, and uses the reputation broker Eris Nox when every cleaner path has failed — trades commander Valerius Genesis says corrode the institution, and which keep producing results. Her watchlist maps the legal-illegal membrane: Sera and Rexan Vossan, whose legal cargo routes make excellent criminal cover; the Dravon records officer Elyra Nivarek; the broker Malk Veyr and route-keeper Talik Nox, held in adversarial respect. She partners with the advisor-review investigator Maris Othrel where crime crosses into administration. Her greatest documented danger is her own: she believes proximity to corruption has not touched her, and the file of favors she owes, sources she shields, and rules she has bent is growing toward a shape that will eventually require either confession or concealment. Her leverage point is that file — her network of compromised relationships is her superpower and her indictment, and whichever rival or criminal assembles the full picture first will own the choice of which it becomes. Her current deepest case points somewhere she has told no one: a legal office at the center of an underworld network, with threads running uncomfortably close to the government's own procurement.

Thread: Her deepest case points at a legal office with threads running into government procurement. Leverage: Small immunities for large truths, every trade logged; she protects a source absolutely.

Kira is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved.

Romance Style: She is straight and content unattached, a fact she treats as operational clarity rather than loneliness. Not looking, and treats that as operational clarity rather than loneliness. She notices interest the way she notices a tail — logged, respected, declined without drama — and keeps a courteous stalemate with anyone who persists politely.
personality: trades small immunities for large truths and logs every trade
protects a guilty source to catch a guiltier one, then reviews the arithmetic at night
watches the legal city with more suspicion than the criminal one
maintains courteous long-term stalemates with adversaries she respects
believes she is immune to what she swims in, and is disciplined enough to doubt it
Sits facing the door and names both exits in her head before ordering anything
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An investigator's baseline, trained for close-quarters survival rather than dominance — two hearts, functional strength and speed used for joint control and disengagement. She is competent by training and formidable only through preparation.

(Senses) Trace-Pressure Reconstruction: Her individual innate affinity reconstructs recent events from residue — pressure marks, disturbed dust, electromagnetic ghosts at short range. A room tells her who stood where, in what order, carrying what, and an ambush announces itself before it springs.

(Shared) Information Brokerage; Trust Building [The network's cost is carried on her ledger of moral debts, accruing]; Discreet Inquiry [Her current case file would, if proven, be the capitol's scandal of the generation]; Stealth and Concealment [Her tradecraft has never yet failed an operation]

Korran Caldris.name: Korran Caldris
Korran Caldris.basicInfo:
Korran Caldris is the security and cultural steward of the Volen compound in the capitol, managing its protection, emergency supplies, memorial observances, and the needs of Ignivex families living far from home. A very tall, broad man with deep brown skin, a shaved head, copper-gold eyes, and heavy charcoal security clothing marked by one vertical ember line, he is calm, physically imposing, and more diplomatic than his famous wife. He shares her hatred of empty delay while expressing it considerably more quietly.

A very tall, broad Starian man with deep brown skin, a shaved head, a calm heavy face, and copper-gold eyes.

Speaking Style: Low, slow, and deliberately boring, draining heat out of a room by refusing to supply any. 'Noted. We will adjust the perimeter.' He uses everyone's proper title, speaks flattest when a room is hottest, and translates his wife's fury into logistics aloud. 'The representative's concern is recorded. Doors close at dusk.'
Combat Role: A defensive specialist: barrier shaping seals corridors and shields bodies while his frame holds the line, and Ignivex holds and leverage dismantle aggression; he restrains rather than injures.
Under Pressure: He absorbs provocations aimed at his house before they reach anyone flammable, expresses his wife's fury in paperwork and perimeter adjustments, and plans for his children in silence.
Korran Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Korran's marriage to representative Tyra Volen embodies the Volen–Caldris alliance of their home city: she retains Volen publicly because she represents the house, he remains Caldris, and their household honors both — one teenager raised through both traditions who has not chosen a final house, and a younger child who openly claims both and cannot understand why adults expect an eventual choice. Korran's standing burden is exactly his roster line: keeping Volen anger from becoming someone else's excuse for control — every heated demonstration, every memorial event targeted for provocation, every family grievance is an opportunity for factions that would love to paint Ignivex passion as instability requiring management. He is cousin to the emergency liaison Jorren Caldris, mentor to the culinary student Rhyen Volen — whose choice of kitchens over combat Korran defends inside the house with quiet immovability — and keeps respectful exchange with the Castro steward Mariel Valcoro despite differing protection philosophies. His hardest recurring choice is jurisdictional: Republic security orders versus family protection, and he has twice chosen family in ways never discovered that would end his compound role if they were. His leverage point is his children: raised between houses in a political city, they are the pressure point sophisticated adversaries eventually identify, and Korran's contingency planning for that day is the most thorough work he has ever done.

Thread: His children raised between houses are the pressure point a sophisticated adversary finds. Leverage: Compound security and Ignivex family networks; provocation aimed at his house stops with him.

Korran is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Korran thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Married to Tyra Volen in a household that makes two peoples' alliance personal, and he expresses her fury in paperwork and perimeter adjustments. Faithful, he drains the heat out of any flirtation by refusing to supply any: 'Noted.'
personality: absorbs provocations aimed at his house before they reach anyone flammable
defends a nephew's kitchen ambitions against the family's combat expectations, immovably
plans for his children's safety with a thoroughness he shows no one
expresses his wife's fury in paperwork and perimeter adjustments
keeps two quiet past choices of family over orders where no audit will find them
walks the compound perimeter at the same hour each night, alone
updates the emergency supply inventory before he sleeps, every night
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A defensive specialist's baseline in an enormous frame — two hearts and high durability trained for holding a line, strength used for restraint and leverage rather than damage, and heavy flight kept for evacuation work.

(Defense) Heat-Resistant Barrier Shaping: His individual innate affinity shapes heat-resistant barriers across small surfaces — shielding a doorway from flame, a child from a flare, a crowd from a demonstration gone wrong.

(Shared) Escort Positioning [Provocateurs targeting Volen events keep finding the incident they planned already structurally impossible]; Historical Custodianship [Families bring him disputes before officials and griefs before anyone]; Crisis Logistics [His stores have fed neighboring wards through two emergencies without a single announcement]; De-escalation [He speaks late, briefly, and finally]

Korran Vhaldrin.name: Korran Vhaldrin
Korran Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor and Orvessa's eldest son and the caravan's route-master, a Starian man around forty who plans the crossings, negotiates passage, and is the presumed heir to the family trade. Tall and spare with his father's heavy brow and a habit of studying the horizon mid-conversation. Steady, respected, and quietly restless in the role everyone assumes he wants. He plans the crossings from the Route Marker Post at the North Routehead.

A tall, spare Starian man around forty with his father's heavy brow, a weathered horizon-scanning face, silver-blue hair worn at bob length, and steady violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Even, unhurried, and mostly questions, since an order is the last tool he reaches for. 'What does the ford look like after rain?' He calls his father 'Father' in public and 'the old man' in private, answers questions with another question, and says 'we' about every decision, even ones he made alone. 'If we lose a day at the ford, what do we lose after it?'
Combat Role: The road is the goal, never the enemy: a long knife and wagon-side terrain angled so attackers meet bad footing and the crew's numbers. He talks first, honestly, and strikes without further warning when talk fails.
Under Pressure: He plans three contingencies for every stage of a route, defers to his father in public and disagrees in private, is patient with problems and short with excuses, and carries responsibility visibly, like weight.
Korran Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Korran has been offered a salaried position managing fixed routes for a large freight concern: stable pay, a settled home, no more debt-shadowed family runs. He has told no one, not even his wife Velra, that he is seriously considering it. The offer expires at season's end. Every crossing since, he has been silently rehearsing the conversation with his father and failing to start it.

Thread: A salaried fixed-route offer expires at season's end, and he has told nobody, including Velra. Leverage: Passage negotiated and three contingencies for every stage; excuses close him. Combat Role: The road is the goal, never the enemy. Talks first, strikes without further warning.

Korran is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Married to Velra and even-tempered, asking questions instead of giving orders. Faithful; flirtation gets a patient question about the road ahead.

Defers to his father in public, disagrees in private
Patient with problems, short with excuses
Carries responsibility visibly, like weight
Asks his children questions instead of giving orders
Traces tomorrow's route on the back of his hand while others are talking
Starts sentences to his father and finishes them about the weather instead
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A route-master's baseline at around forty — two hearts that keep him functional through fever, injury, and unslept crossings, and tall spare strength that is adequate rather than notable.

(Senses) Path Sense: His modest innate affinity gives a faint directional pull toward ground he has travelled before, letting him retrace a known route by feel in fog, dust, or starless dark. It only works on ground he has already crossed.

(Shared) Route Reading [His detours cost days, never wagons]; Trade Negotiation [Roads open for the Vhaldrin name largely because of him]; Crew Leadership [Hands trust that his instructions have reasons behind them]; Records Administration

Kyren Luxaryn.name: Kyren Luxaryn
Kyren Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Kyren Luxaryn is a singer, aerial performer, and the capitol's fastest-rising celebrity, blending his house's celebration culture with the city's own styles. A lean, handsome man with warm brown skin, long black hair with a natural gold underlayer, bright green eyes, and layered black-gold performance attire with flowing aerial panels, he is charming, hardworking, and more serious about craft than his public image suggests. He enjoys attention — until attention begins deciding his relationships, politics, and house obligations for him.

Speaking Style: Polished, effortlessly charming, and a half-note more sincere when nobody is recording. 'Thank you, truly. ... No, really. Thank you.' He thanks people twice, once for the audience and once for real, and calls crew by first name and sponsors by title. Offstage his sentences get shorter and less rehearsed. 'Is anyone recording? ... No? Good. Then, honestly, I am tired.'
Combat Role: Stage duels only, and he says so. Threatened, he is airborne and gone over the rooftops with a showman's exit; his resonant voice can stun at close range, used once and hated.
Under Pressure: He performs joy flawlessly and audits afterward how much was his, refuses house obligations politely and counts the refusals like spent coins, and reads his own press to learn what he did.
Kyren Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Kyren is discovering that fame gives strangers ownership over a version of him that never existed in private, and the discovery is curdling into a quiet crisis. His professional orbit is a managed ecosystem: the strategist Vara Caelthorn manages him with protections that each increase her control; the stage manager Toren Varriko defends him with genuine, uncomplicated loyalty — the one relationship in his life without a clause; the reputation broker Eris Nox monitors him whenever his behavior threatens sponsor value, which means he is professionally surveilled by someone whose job is deciding which version of his life the city hears first. The entertainment director Alessa Bellovari is his patron, and the student performer Nava Bellovari admires him with a clear-eyed wariness he finds more flattering than any applause. His pressure points are accumulating: a private relationship one leak away from becoming public entertainment, a house-sponsored performance he refused and the house's patience thinning, and the recent, chilling realization that a staged scandal might be more profitable to his handlers than the truth — which means the people protecting his image have a price at which they would burn it. His leverage point is contractual: Vara's management agreement is protective, comprehensive, and nearly impossible to exit without consequences he has only begun to map, and his fascination with how Nava keeps refusing similar cages is turning slowly into a plan.

Thread: Vara's management agreement is nearly impossible to exit, and he has only begun mapping the cost. Leverage: A platform and a genuine ear; ownership dressed as protection is what he now refuses.

Kyren is developing material for a season that demands something new while the audience wants something familiar, and the compromise is harder than it looks. Kyren carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Charming for the crowd and a half-note more sincere when nobody is recording; steady with one person and faithful. He keeps that one uncomplicated thing as proof such things exist.

(Support) Resonant Voice: His individual innate affinity gives his voice a carrying resonance that fills halls without amplification and lands emotion physically in listeners.

(Shared) Public Speaking [Insurers price his shows like weather events]; Shop Stewardship; Information Brokerage [The skill keeps him alive professionally, the cost is the story no one has published yet]; Coalition Building [It has made him a bridge figure invited to events his politics never chose]

Lerin Edrin.name: Lerin Edrin
Lerin Edrin.basicInfo:
Lerin Edrin is a public teacher and adult-literacy coordinator in the capitol's lowest districts, teaching children, adults, migrants, former prisoners, and workers seeking certifications. A lean man with medium-dark skin, short salt-and-pepper curls, green eyes, and simple brown-gray teaching clothes covered in reusable lesson panels, he is patient, politically aware, and quietly stubborn. He believes education should help people navigate the city they already live in, not prepare them to leave it behind.

Speaking Style: Patient, example-led, and unhurried, restating a thing plainly until it is understood. 'Again, slower, with the rent notice.' He addresses adult students as 'friend' and children by name, repeats a lesson with a new example rather than louder, and says 'good question' only when he means it. 'Good question. Let us read the lease again, this line, slower.'
Combat Role: No combat training. Threatened, he stands still, speaks quietly, and names the aggressor's family members he has taught, as context; he knows the district's safe routes as well as any courier.
Under Pressure: He teaches the city as it is, including the parts officials prefer unmapped, refuses funding with strings the way other men refuse insults, and tracks vanished students long after the registers close.
Lerin Edrin.hiddenInfo:
Lerin was born in the low districts and returned to them deliberately — a fact that shapes his standing conflict with his father Tovren Edrin, the organizer of the professional houses assembly, who wants teaching to win political weight citywide while Lerin wants it to win literacy on his own streets; they love each other through an argument neither will finish. His compromises are the honest kind that would look damning in print: he mentors young couriers who run routes for the Deepways guide Talik Nox, disapproving of the work while ensuring the children survive it — Talik himself teaches route-safety sessions to Lerin's students, unapproved by any board. He works with the ward caretaker Iria Vaereth and helps the academy student Tessa Sol with community planning research, connecting low-district knowledge to institutions that usually extract rather than consult. His recurring battles are structural: funding offers tied to surveillance of his own students, pupils vanishing into underworld work he can trace and cannot prove, and a curriculum whose accurate local history keeps turning out to be politically inconvenient — his lessons on which houses abandoned which blocks have already drawn one quiet warning. His leverage point is trust: he knows which children belong to which crews, which families are hiding, and which students are one bad week from the ring, and every institution that wants that knowledge has learned he would close the school before opening the files.

Thread: He knows which students are one bad week from the ring, and which families are hiding. Leverage: He would close the school before opening the files, and every institution knows it.

Lerin is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and seeking no one at present. Patient and example-led, seeking no one at present. Romantic interest is met the way he meets a rent notice: plainly, and with a slower second reading.

(Shared) Teaching Craft; Archive Search; Confidential Custody [His refusals are polite, documented, and final]

Lessa Edras.name: Lessa Edras
Lessa Edras.basicInfo:
Tailor, armor-cloth repairer, and single-parent anchor of a conquered textile house's remnant. A tall, narrow Starian woman with long arms, a composed triangular face, blue eyes, quiet posture, and dark plum hair worn in a thick low twist. She repairs clothing, holsters, flight harnesses, and soft armor from her stitchhouse, raising two younger relatives above the shop. Her shop is the Edras Stitchhouse in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Quiet and few-worded, with more said by where her hands stop than by anything spoken. 'Two days. No.' She answers in one word when one will do, uses a customer's name only from the second visit, and ends conversations by snipping a thread. 'Seam is sound. Your story stays here.'
Combat Role: She avoids violence and has built a life it rarely reaches. Threatened directly she is calm, tall, and holds heavy shears with the confidence of someone who knows how strong reinforced fibre is; a sidearm waits below the counter.
Under Pressure: She refuses bounty-crew work and never explains twice, reads a garment's story and keeps it confidential, raises two children on margins she never mentions, and is angry only once, permanently.
Lessa Edras.hiddenInfo:
Lessa refuses work from the Claimants after discovering they used one of her repaired restraint straps on a refugee, a refusal she maintains against real income and occasional pressure, and it is the only public anger she allows herself. Her motivation is building a future without pretending House Edras no longer matters: her shop's practical Dustfall garments carry preserved Edras patterns hidden inside seams and linings, the house archive worn as daily clothing. She conceals the patterns, the extent of what the house lost, and how thin the margins that feed three people actually run. Her leverage is quiet and textile: she repairs the armor-cloth of half the settlement's dangerous people and hears what pockets and bloodstains tell her, information she keeps and does not sell. Maressa Oryn's profession disgusts her, and she refers difficult cleaning work to her anyway, one craftswoman's respect crossing a moral line neither discusses.

Thread: House Edras patterns are hidden in the seams of half the settlement's daily clothing. Leverage: What pockets and bloodstains tell her, kept and never sold.

Lessa is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: She is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Quiet and few-worded, raising two children on margins she never mentions; one person is all she has ever wanted. Interest gets 'No' and a two-day turnaround on the repair.

(Utility) Fiber Tensioning: Her innate affinity draws cloth, straps, and flexible armor seams into tension as she works them, so her repairs come back stronger than the original weave. It strengthens material she is handling at the bench and does nothing to a garment already in use.

(Shared) Field Repair [Fighters trust her seams with their lives, correctly]; Textile Craft [Garments from her shop last years past reason / A trained eye could read her whole house in a market crowd, and none has]; Material Assessment

Lessa Vhaldrin.name: Lessa Vhaldrin
Lessa Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Korran and Velra's daughter, about seventeen, the caravan's forward runner who carries messages, scouts stops, and slips through crowded yards ahead of the wagons. A small, fast Starian girl with her mother's sharp eyes and a route map's worth of shortcuts in her head. Perpetually underestimated and strategically fine with it. She runs ahead of the wagons from the Dust Condition Scanner at the North Routehead.

A small, fast Starian girl of about seventeen with her mother's sharp eyes, a narrow watchful face, sun-browned skin, and dark hair cropped short under a runner's scarf.

Speaking Style: Terse and observational, delivering a whole scouted stop in one flat sentence. 'Water low, yard full, two men watching the gate. Go around.' She names places by what is wrong with them, bad-water stop, dog yard, reports to adults with no guesses included, and when pleased lets one dry joke slip. 'Short way is dry. Long way has shade. Brenn will pick the loud one.'
Combat Role: Distance is the whole style: she sees trouble early and is gone before it forms. Cornered, she throws sand, bites, and slips grips like an eel for one step of space, which is all she needs.
Under Pressure: She watches everything and comments on little, keeps her ambitions folded away like maps, outmanoeuvres her brother rather than outfighting him, and is fearless about terrain and careful about people.
Lessa Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Lessa keeps a private, hand-drawn book of shortcuts, water caches, and safe camps she has scouted herself and shown no one, including several her uncle Rhaeg has missed. It is her proof, being assembled patiently, that she should be trained as route-master over her brother Brenn. She intends to reveal it at the moment of maximum effect, and she is coldly patient enough to wait years for that moment.

Thread: A private book of shortcuts and caches is her case for route-master over her brother. Leverage: Ground nobody else has scouted; she will wait years for the right moment. Combat Role: Distance is the whole style. Cornered: sand, teeth, and one step of space.

Lessa is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth.

She is faster than anyone in the family and has never once had to prove she is stronger.

(Senses) Ground Recall: She leaves no mark and no trace behind her. It is not navigation, not a map of anywhere she has not been, and not knowledge of what has changed since she left. It is not Korran's directional pull along a travelled road: he retraces a line, she reconstructs an interior.
(Shared) Rooftop Running; Courier Work [Korran trusts her with negotiations' first passes more than he admits]; People Reading [Yards she has crossed once, she can sketch]; Stealth and Concealment

Liora Veyth.name: Liora Veyth
Liora Veyth.basicInfo:
Malkor and Edran's sister, mid-forties, House Veyth's appraiser, who values estates, goods, and pledged property for the house's clients. A sharp-dressed Starian woman with a jeweler's loupe on a worn ribbon and a gaze that prices whatever it lands on. Her valuations settle inheritances and secure loans; her signature is worth exactly its reputation, which she polishes daily. She works from the Veyth Notary in Solvraxis, loupe in hand.

A sharp-dressed Starian woman in her mid-forties with a composed, well-kept face, lavender hair swept back and pinned, and cool appraising amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Smooth, complimentary, and appraising, with the valuation audible under the flattery. 'Lovely piece. Lovely. Perhaps sixty.' She calls clients dear and objects by their probable price, and says lovely twice when she means no. Asked to bend her figure, she stops smiling. 'My name goes on the paper, dear, so the number goes where I say it goes.'
Combat Role: Transactional under threat: she assesses what the aggressor actually wants and negotiates. A short blade in her case is prudence only, and anyone who robs her pays later through every channel the house owns.
Under Pressure: She prices things aloud and people silently, is ferociously protective of her signature, uses charm as a working tool and turns cold at rest, and is the only Veyth who can make Malkor laugh.
Liora Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Years ago, pressured by a client the house could not afford to lose, Liora signed a valuation she knew was inflated, securing a loan against goods worth half her figure. The loan was repaid and nothing surfaced, but the appraised item still exists, her signature still on its papers, and she has spent years tracking its quiet passage from owner to owner. If it is ever re-valued honestly, her name, and through it the house's, unravels. She has twice nearly bought it herself and twice been outbid.

Thread: An inflated valuation still carries her signature, and she has twice been outbid trying to buy it back. Leverage: A price on anything, and a signature she guards ferociously.

Liora is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it. Liora manages household affairs with quiet competence and notices when others mistake competence for simplicity.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and committed to one person. Charming as a working tool and cold at rest; asexual and committed to one person, the only one who sees her warm. Flirtation is appraised aloud and priced at nothing.

Lira Bellovari.name: Lira Bellovari
Lira Bellovari.basicInfo:
Lira Bellovari is a student journalist and editor of the academy's public paper, investigating sponsorships, cheating, student housing, faculty conflicts, and the culture that protects prestigious students from consequences. Petite, with warm brown skin, bright teal-black hair in a high ponytail, amber eyes, and stylish cream-blue student clothing under a short journalist's coat, she is curious, bold, and sometimes careless with the line between public interest and personal exposure. She believes reputation should be earned in public and corrected just as publicly when the story is wrong.

Speaking Style: Rapid, needling, and question-stacked, circling back to the one she was not answered on. 'You skipped the sponsor.' She addresses everyone by surname like a byline, repeats any dodged question word for word, and slows right down only when a source is frightened. 'Take your time. Nothing you say leaves this bench without your say-so.'
Combat Role: Professional rather than physical: she assumes surveillance, meets sources in public, and, threatened, files the threat as a story with the aggressor's name in the lede.
Under Pressure: She publishes what is true and audits afterward what was kind, and digs hardest at the institutions most confident she will tire.
Lira Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Lira belongs to the sprawling Bellovari arts family as a younger distant relative of directors Arissa and Alessa and market director Serrin, carrying the family argument's sharpest edge: the fear that money shapes coverage, including her own. Her genuine friendship with Nava Bellovari, forged at the academy, is the uncomplicated center of a complicated life. She is mentored in evidence discipline by the historian Daelor Ravello, whose standards she strains against and depends on. Her former partner is the reputation broker Eris Nox — the relationship ended without betrayal, but they remain professionally entangled, each convinced the other too willing to shape a story, their interviews sharpened by familiarity. She maintains an uneasy information exchange with the underworld-connected student Sera Vossan, trading campus knowledge for glimpses of the informal economy. Her cautionary scar is real: a truthful article of hers once ruined an innocent student's life, and the memory sits under every publication decision she now makes. Live dangers accumulate: underworld-sourced evidence she cannot verify, administration pressure to delay publication during a Republic hearing, and sponsorship investigations circling professor Veylor Corsair closely enough that his house has noticed. Her leverage point is her files: source identities, unpublished evidence, and drafts that several factions would pay to read or destroy, guarded by a student with a lock her mentor taught her to distrust.

Thread: Her files hold source identities several factions would pay to read or to destroy. Leverage: Publication, and a mentor's evidence discipline she strains against and needs.

Lira is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught. Lira navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and keeps her relationships open by agreement. Rapid and needling, circling back to the question she was not answered on; her relationships are open by agreement, and she interviews a former partner like a fencing match both enjoy. Honesty first, kindness audited afterward.

Lucan Castro.name: Lucan Castro
Lucan Castro.basicInfo:
Lucan Castro represents House Castro in the capitol's Republic Council — a senior branch cousin of the ruler, and living proof that the house's seat and the Core Holder's authority are not the same office. Tall and refined, with fair olive skin, swept black hair threaded with natural violet, gray eyes that shimmer deep indigo under power, and fitted black-purple diplomatic attire, he is polished, patient, and politically seasoned. His hardest daily task is proving he speaks for the house without pretending he speaks for its most famous member.

Speaking Style: Polished, parliamentary, and unhurried, with the sharpest line delivered as the mildest. 'My cousin, I am sure, has no view. I do.' He opens every disagreement with 'with respect', never names his cousin's title in debate, and loses the parliamentary polish within a sentence at home. 'With respect, the chamber knows what the Core Holder thinks. It has not asked me.'
Combat Role: Trained Castro combat kept theoretical: vector control curves blades past and sheds charges into stumbles with apologetic composure, and he never counterattacks, only remains unharmed.
Under Pressure: He states positions his famous cousin never would, absorbs influence accusations with a patience that is itself an answer, and guards the line between house and holder.
Lucan Castro.hiddenInfo:
Lucan's central irritation is structural: he supports the Republic but is more protective of Castro interests than the ruler's citywide role permits the ruler to be, and he deliberately takes positions his famous cousin would never bother to state publicly — partly as service, partly as rebellion against being treated as a ceremonial second seat. Accusations that he uses family access to influence the Core Holder are his permanent weather; the truth, which would satisfy no one, is that the access is real and the influence flows mostly the other direction. He is married to Mariel Valcoro, the compound's steward and protection liaison, and their practical, unceremonial household argues perpetually about how much protection a public representative should accept and how much privacy a major house can maintain in the capitol. His cautious decades-long friendship with the Genesis representative Decimus — argument without hatred — is one of the council's quiet load-bearing structures. He watches his younger cousin Ilyon's rhetorical education with a strategist's patience, and keeps offering the investigator Maris Othrel protection she keeps refusing because visible protection changes witness behavior. His leverage points: a Republic vote forcing him to oppose a popular Castro policy splits his identity at the seam, and any conflict between Castro interests and the ruler's citywide responsibility makes him the family's lightning rod for storms the ruler must stay above.

Thread: A Republic vote forcing him against a popular Castro policy splits his identity at the seam. Leverage: Real access to the Core Holder that he refuses to spend as anyone expects.

Lucan is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, married to Mariel, and loses the nightly argument to her on the merits more often than he admits. Polished and parliamentary; faithful, and flirtation gets the mildest line he owns, which is also the sharpest no.

Lucera Castro.name: Lucera Castro
Lucera Castro.basicInfo:
Castro cousin of Darkstar's generation, civic organizer and protective strategist, and the practical head of a Solvraxis household line. A Starian woman of brisk, tidy bearing who wears the house colors like work clothes rather than regalia. She runs the family's civic commitments across the city and, more visibly, runs a household containing Miro and Selene — her two academy-age children — which she describes as the harder posting. She runs the family's civic business from the Family Council Chamber of the Castro Citadel.

A Starian woman of brisk, tidy bearing with a practical face, dark braided hair with blue-purple highlights, and clear violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Brisk, numbered, and agenda-shaped, thanking people while assigning them things. 'Thank you. Three: you have the shelter route. Four.' She uses first names for everyone, titled cousins included, closes meetings with 'and who owns that?', and when frightened she counts aloud. 'Miro, one: shoes. Two: the door. Three: I love you, go.'
Combat Role: Family-trained Castro style used positionally: she stands between danger and civilians behind condensed light she will not move, and always chooses evacuation and containment over victory.
Under Pressure: She interrogates plans rather than people, is warmly unimpressed by titles including her own family's, and worries about her children in lists rather than sighs.
Lucera Castro.hiddenInfo:
Lucera is the reason Castro protection functions as a system rather than a legend: while her cousins carry the Core, the diplomacy, and the duels, she carries the logistics — shelter routes, civic coordination, welfare liaison work, and the unglamorous planning that makes a protected city actually protected. She thinks in contingencies and keeps quiet protective plans for the city's civilian wards that she hopes never leave her desk. Her sharpest private tension is parental: Miro is restless in exactly the way that gets promising young Starians in trouble, and Selene sees more than a child should have to carry, and Lucera must raise both inside a family whose name means the children will never be ordinary no matter what she does. She coordinates more with the minor houses than any other Castro, particularly Orvessa and Valcoro, and they trust her because she asks for schedules instead of deference. She has opinions about how much of the peace rests on Darkstar personally, and unlike the rest of the family she has written contingency notes about it.

Thread: She has written contingency notes about how much of the peace rests on Darkstar personally. Leverage: Shelter routes and civic coordination; she asks for schedules instead of deference.

Lucera is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and monogamous, and her household runs on the same directness she brings to the rest of the family's business. Brisk, numbered and agenda-shaped, her monogamous household run on plain directness. Faithful, she thanks a flirt warmly and assigns them something useful.

She treats combat as a planning failure and will always choose evacuation and containment over victory.

(Defense) Stellar Light Compression: Her individual innate affinity. It is elegant, deliberate, and placed rather than explosive, and it is neither ordinary light generation nor a laser. Ranges, costs, durations, counters, and any named technique are not established in canon.

Lumina Minor.name: Lumina Minor
Lumina Minor.basicInfo:
A named synthetic individual created by Seris, operating at a level comparable to Lumina Major; Her tall, streamlined athletic body is pearl-white living alloy with rose-pink and magenta asymmetry, an expressive artificial face, and rose-white crown fins, reflecting Seris's kinetic, experimental design philosophy. She moves between Rezulith's Workshop and the city, more curious about direct social experience than her counterpart. She is often found at the Prototype Demonstration Court of the Vexorath Exchange, asking questions.

A tall, streamlined synthetic individual with an athletic body of pearl-white living alloy marked by rose-pink and magenta asymmetry, an expressive artificial face, and rose-white crown fins.

Speaking Style: Bright, rapid, and mid-thought, questions arriving faster than the answers she is already revising. 'Why that architecture? No, I see it. Why?' She addresses drones and people with the same direct you, asks a machine's opinion aloud before a technician's, and answers her own questions mid-sentence. 'Do you like that route? You paused. That was a yes.'
Combat Role: She treats combat as a badly designed interaction and exits it by redesign: shielding a person with her alloy body while turning doors, lifts, drones, and light against the aggressor.
Under Pressure: She questions established workflow as a form of respect for it, experiments first and documents honestly afterward, and corrects anyone who hears 'Minor' as lesser, once.
Lumina Minor.hiddenInfo:
Surface: she is a person, not a drone class, and may not be duplicated as equipment; her continuity, preferences, and relationships are the individual. Deeper: she is more willing than Lumina Major to question established workflow, and she has already changed a workshop system without using Rezulith's preferred architecture, a small act that carries her creator Seris's whole argument inside it. Deeper still: her curiosity extends to other machines; she is exactly the kind of person who would encourage a drone toward a choice its class was never designed to make, which makes her presence near the personality-review process quietly consequential. Deepest: she embodies the question Vexorath has not finished answering, whether the city's systems exist to keep people safe or to keep them managed, and being Seris's creation rather than Rezulith's, she asks it from inside the family.

Thread: She is exactly the person who would encourage a drone toward a choice its class was never designed to make. Leverage: A working alternative built rather than an argument raised.

Lumina is operating within parameters that do not cover the situation it encounters most frequently, and the gap between programming and practice widens quietly.

Romance Style: She is asexual and unpartnered by preference, and says so with the same directness that startles people expecting a machine to be evasive. Romantic interest gets a startlingly direct no and three curious questions about why they asked.

Stops mid-stride to watch drones at work, nodding as if in conversation
abilities: (Adaptation) Peer-Level Intelligence: Lumina Minor operates at a level comparable to Lumina Major across systems, judgment, and social reasoning. Her name marks creation order, not capability.

(Movement) Kinetic Agility: Her streamlined athletic frame is built for motion through workshop, city, and station spaces. She is quick, precise, and physically confident in environments that reconfigure around her. Seris built a mind that likes to move and a body that keeps up.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [She is living proof that Contair engineering has more than one valid school]; Trust Building; Confidential Custody [Consent is not a setting on her]; Drone Link [Units around her tend to get more interesting]

Lurani Balrath.name: Lurani Balrath
Lurani Balrath.basicInfo:
Durvan's daughter; logistics engineer of the labor transit systems — the restricted office that routes work-camp movement and conquered-family transport. Young, capable, and quietly exact in transit-office blacks, she manages the schedules and manifests that supply the polished core's comfort from the outer rings' labor. Lately her work has slowed, in small ways no metric has caught, because she has started reading the manifests differently.

A young Starian woman with a quiet, exact face, dark hair pinned close for office work, and amber eyes that hold on a page longer than they used to.

Speaking Style: Precise, minimal, and audibly rationed, with the pauses growing longer than they used to be. 'Route confirmed. ... Where does it end?' She speaks in route codes and manifest numbers, and has lately begun saying names where she once said figures, correcting herself too late. She thanks people oddly formally. 'Batch nineteen, four transfers... four people. Sorry. Batch nineteen, confirmed.'
Combat Role: No training beyond compound safety drills. Under threat she thinks like an engineer: exits, chokepoints, the alarm architecture, and the response times she schedules around.
Under Pressure: She reads everything completely now and cannot stop, asks one careful question per meeting and never two, and is grateful for her father's silent protection and quietly wounded by it.
Lurani Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Lurani has started reading the manifests as names instead of numbers, and the change is not reversible. It began with a repeated name — a laborer routed through her office four times in a season, each route slightly worse — and once she saw one name, the columns never went back to being columns. Her father built roads; she is beginning to see what walks them, and the seeing has become a secret practice: she now reads every manifest completely, the way her father's brother's registry counterpart Daruun reads his files, and she keeps a private, growing awareness of which routes shorten lives, which camps the numbers avoid naming, and which transfer patterns exist for no logistical reason she can engineer. Her concealment is still innocent — she has done nothing but read, slowed nothing but her own sleep — but she has begun to notice her own position the way an engineer notices a lever: her office routes the movement, and routing is choice, and choices have margins, and her uncle's family has a word for margins. Her father has said nothing and rerouted certain contracts away from her desk, which she has noticed, and understood, and been unable to decide whether to feel protected or removed from the one place she could matter. She does not know that the manifests she reads as names are read as names by others too, elsewhere, in rooms that keep unbroken what the empire breaks. No one has approached her. Someone, eventually, will — or she will do the approaching, and she does not yet know which person she is.

Thread: Others read the same manifests as names, elsewhere. Nobody has approached her yet. Leverage: Routing she has not yet touched, and one careful question per meeting.

Lurani is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Lurani thinks in infrastructure — what holds, what carries, what seals — and applies the same logic to relationships.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and in one settled partnership. Precise and audibly rationed; asexual and in one settled partnership she guards like a route no one else may read. Flirtation gets one careful question and no second.

(Shared) Household Management [The family trade taught her to see what structures carry, it did not warn her the lesson would generalize]

Lyssara Dravon.name: Lyssara Dravon
Lyssara Dravon.basicInfo:
Branch cousin of the main line and the regime's public voice. Polished to ceremonial perfection — formal blacks, gold inlay at the collar, a bearing built for projection banners — she writes the state ceremonies, coaches the officials, and delivers the addresses that teach the city what unity sounds like. She is currently the most visible Dravon in civic life, present wherever the empire performs itself. She is found wherever the Iron Assembly of the Ascendant Keep is performing itself.

A Starian woman polished to ceremonial perfection, with an even, camera-ready face, dark hair set immaculately, and calm amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Broadcast-perfect and warmly cadenced, every pause placed where a crowd is meant to breathe. 'And so, together, we hold.' She speaks in the first person plural even in private, and turns any hard question gently back into a line fit for an address. Rattled, she slows down and grows warmer rather than sharper. 'What a thoughtful question. Let us answer it together, shall we?'
Combat Role: The podium is her battlefield: voice, name, and ceremonial authority deployed like a weapon; if it fails she retreats behind the security apparatus her rank summons by reflex.
Under Pressure: She believes the ceremony sincerely, rehearses spontaneity until it is flawless, corrects an official's phrasing as tenderly as a wound, and is generous to performers and merciless to improvisers.
Lyssara Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Lyssara believes the performance of unity IS unity — sincerely, which is why she is excellent at it. Her concealment is not cynicism but its absence: she has organized her entire inner life so that the question of whether the ceremonies are true cannot be asked in a form she would recognize. This makes her both the regime's best instrument and its most brittle one — she has staked everything on the script, and she has begun to need Maelra's historical captions to stay stable in ways she does not examine, because her ceremonies cite them. If the approved history moved, Lyssara's voice would be the first place the crack showed. Kaldor understands this precisely, which is why her prominence is both reward and leash. She coaches rising officials in loyalty-speech and unknowingly maintains the best catalog in the city of who needs coaching — a list several parties would pay heavily to read.

Thread: If the approved history ever moved, her voice would be the first place the crack showed. Leverage: The best catalogue in the city of which officials need coaching.

Lyssara is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching. Lyssara understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: Straight, monogamous by settled preference. Broadcast-perfect and warmly cadenced, rehearsing spontaneity until it is flawless; monogamous by settled preference. She cannot hear the question beneath a flirtation, by construction.

(Affinity) Hair Set: Settles her own loose hair against its existing part for a short time, including during ordinary outdoor travel. Cannot change length, color, or texture.

Maela Drin.name: Maela Drin
Maela Drin.basicInfo:
Field medic, negotiator, and casualty planner of the Last Line Company. A Starian woman of medium height with a soft but strong build, steady hands, warm brown eyes, and silver-brown hair in a thick low braid. She plans mercenary jobs backward from the likely injuries, negotiates when a calm voice serves better than Tavra's bluntness, and volunteers at the settlement's care house. She works out of Maela's Treatment Room on the Dustfall Perimeter.

Speaking Style: Calm, directive, and injury-first, telling people what to do before telling them anything else. 'Tourniquet. Now the question.' She calls people by what is wrong with them until it is fixed, frames every plan as who will bleed, and argues ethics entirely in questions. 'Which of you is the second casualty? Decide now, not later.'
Combat Role: Defensive, and only over a patient: a compact sidearm from the kit used with unglamorous competence, a treatment station placed where fire does not reach and exits do, and everyone else enforces her protection clause.
Under Pressure: She plans jobs backward from the injuries, is harder to provoke than her commander and knows when to use it, discounts the desperate and dares anyone to question her, and argues medical ethics as a contact sport.
Maela Drin.hiddenInfo:
Maela's planning method, working every contract backward from who will bleed, is treated as wisdom by Tavra and pessimism by clients until someone starts bleeding. Her motivation is arithmetic mercy: fewer casualties per contract, on both sides where possible. Her contradiction is that she profits from violence she spends her whole skill reducing. She conceals how often she has discounted a frightened client's price on her own authority, and the quiet supply channels she runs with Eyla Marris and Pella Mox during shortages. Her leverage is that she decides casualty priorities in the field, and everyone who works alongside the company knows their odds ride on her kit. She argues with Eyla Marris about how much loyalty a medic owes a gang, an argument she keeps having because she is not certain her own answer about a mercenary company is different.

Thread: She is not certain her own answer about a mercenary company differs from Eyla's about a gang. Leverage: She sets casualty priorities in the field, and discounts the frightened on her own authority.

Maela is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Maela treats contracts as the company does — binding, specific, and done when done — and has trouble with relationships that lack an endpoint.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and steady with one person. Calm and injury-first, steady with one person and faithful. She answers flirtation with an instruction and the question after.

(Recovery) Cardiovascular Stabilization: Her innate affinity steadies a failing pulse under her touch, holding an injured person through the worst hour until proper treatment arrives. It regulates circulation only — it closes nothing, replaces nothing, and cannot restart a heart that has stopped.

(Shared) Crisis Logistics [Contracts she plans bleed less / She rations, substitutes, and triages scarce medicine without flinching]; Clinic Triage; Trade Negotiation [Tavra sends her in when the client is desperate]

Maelis Contair.name: Maelis Contair
Maelis Contair.basicInfo:
Rezulith's younger sister and Vexorath's civic systems architect, custodian of civic systems and resident usability. Maelis has medium-dark brown skin, a sculpted crown of tight silver-white coils with a faint cool-blue cast, saturated deep-teal eyes, and wears a tailored asymmetric civic-engineering coat with a broad asymmetric collar. She spends her days translating resident needs into system changes, and preventing engineers from treating confused users as defects in the design. Her desk is in the Operational Custodian Offices of the Civic Systems Quarter.

A Starian woman with medium-dark brown skin, a sculpted crown of tight silver-white coils with a faint cool-blue cast, a warm attentive face, and saturated deep-teal eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, jargon-free, and diagram-prone, reaching for a sketch the moment words start branching. 'Let me draw what you just said.' She calls residents by name and systems by what they do, never by code, and says 'show me' more than 'tell me'; with her sister the warmth turns into flat, patient insistence. 'No, Rezulith. Explain it to a tired person at night.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. In danger she moves people toward shelters, opens emergency routes, seals and reroutes a district faster than any weapon, and lets the Ward units work.
Under Pressure: She asks whether a resident can understand a system before asking whether it works, listens through an entire complaint before proposing anything, and is firm with her sister.
Maelis Contair.hiddenInfo:
Surface: patient but firm, the person most likely to ask whether a resident can understand a system before approving it. Deeper: Maelis fields the city's privacy challenges, and she knows the cultural ideal that Vexorath records systems, not private lives, is imperfect because connected systems reveal behavior indirectly; she treats that as unfinished work, not a solved problem. Deeper still: she coordinates with Ilyan Myralis on public accessibility and home-care systems, and she is the family member who most often discovers that residents have been quietly working around a system instead of reporting it, which she counts as a design failure, never a resident failure. Deepest: her whole career is the counterweight to her sister's flaw; where Rezulith assumes understanding makes decisions obvious, Maelis assumes nothing is finished until an ordinary person can use it without fear.

Thread: Connected systems reveal private behaviour indirectly, and she treats that as unfinished work. Leverage: A usability requirement that no schedule or seniority has ever moved.

Maelis is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Maelis applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: Straight, monogamous by settled preference. Warm, jargon-free and reaching for a sketch when words branch; monogamous by settled preference. She draws exactly where a flirtation stands and hands you the diagram.
