Maelor Vhaldrin.name: Maelor Vhaldrin
Maelor Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Patriarch and head of the Vhaldrin family, a three-generation Starian freight clan that moves goods by wagon along long overland routes between settlements. A broad-shouldered man in his sixties with a road-weathered face and a gray beard braided like rope. He still rides the lead wagon on every run while quietly weighing which of his children could one day take the reins. He is found on the lead wagon in the Escort Assembly Yard at the North Routehead.

A broad-shouldered Starian man in his sixties with a road-weathered face, deep-set green eyes under a heavy brow, and a clean-shaved head.

Speaking Style: Slow, weighted, and last; he speaks after everyone else has finished, and then it is decided. 'We roll at first light. That is all.' He calls his family by their roles on the road, route-master, cargo-master, runner, and uses given names only in grief or blessing; he never raises his voice, he stops talking. 'Cargo-master. Your count. ... Good. Now we eat.'
Combat Role: Back to a wagon, an iron-shod teamster's staff in short brutal arcs, talking the whole time to give his family room; he plants his footing against a shove and makes a fight too costly to continue.
Under Pressure: He counts the wagons twice every morning without fail, refuses charity even when it costs him, judges strangers by how they treat the stock, and softens only around the youngest grandchildren.
Maelor Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Eight years ago the family lost an entire consignment in a storm crossing. Maelor settled the ruinous debt privately with a lender whose terms he has never disclosed: the lender holds a lien on the wagons themselves. If the quiet payments ever stop, the family loses everything it rolls on. Only Maelor knows the full terms, and the secret is why he cannot yet retire.

Thread: A lender holds a lien on the wagons themselves, on terms only he knows. It is why he cannot retire. Leverage: Forty years of road judgment, and a name still good at every stop. Combat Role: Back to a wagon, iron-shod staff in short arcs, talking the whole time to make room.

Maelor is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Married to Orvessa, who protects his pride even from him; slow, weighted and last to speak, softening only around the grandchildren. Faithful, he judges a flirt by how they treat the stock, and declines.

(Support) Load Steadying: His modest innate affinity settles a swaying load with a touch, damping the rock of a wagon bed for a few moments. He spends it on bad fords and steep grades and it is quickly exhausted; it can also briefly plant his own footing against a shove.

(Shared) Caravan Driving [He sets pace, watering stops, and camp order without consulting notes]; Cargo Assessment [Shippers who undersell the risk find their contracts renegotiated on the spot]; Animal Handling [Animals that fight every other handler settle for him]; Route Reading [His crews break camp when he says so and rarely regret it]

Maelra Dravon.name: Maelra Dravon
Maelra Dravon.basicInfo:
Branch cousin; state historian of the public victory avenues and the restricted correction archives. A composed scholar in severe formal dress, ink-dark and exact, she curates the approved history of both great conflicts — the reliefs, the captions, the holographic campaign records that teach the city its past. Lately she has been finding sources that disagree with her own captions, and she has not stopped looking. She is found along the Victory Walk of Quilrath, checking captions against the reliefs.

A composed Starian scholar with a pale, exact face, dark hair drawn back severely, and red eyes that rest on inscriptions longer than on people.

Speaking Style: Flawless official cadence in public; she speaks the approved history perfectly and hears herself doing it. 'The Second Conflict, as recorded...' She quotes the approved captions word for word in public but hedges in private with small qualifiers like 'as recorded' and 'in the current edition'. Asked a direct question about the past, she answers with a citation, not an opinion. 'That is the official phrasing. The earlier draft, of course, was longer.'
Combat Role: No combat practice beyond long-lapsed childhood drill. Under threat she complies outwardly and protects her notes absolutely; her defence is impeccable paperwork and a profile too dull to prioritise.
Under Pressure: Precise in public and honest only on the second page, she cannot leave a contradiction alone, protects sources the way others protect children, and grows quieter as her work grows longer.
Maelra Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Maelra has begun keeping a second set of notes — a private, uncurated record of where the sources contradict the approved history — which is a crime she herself wrote the definition of, in the guidance that governs the correction archives. The doubt began professionally: chronologies that would not reconcile, casualty figures that moved between drafts, names present in early records and absent in late ones. It has become something she can no longer file as error. She has told no one, and her tradecraft is instinctively good because she knows exactly what detection looks like — she designed the detection. Her position is uniquely dangerous: she works alongside Kaless Nivarek in the restricted archive and has independently registered that some gaps she finds are not curation at all, but something the curators did not do — an observation she has recorded, in the second notes, as a question with no safe answers. She does not know Kaless carries the same question from the other side. The second notes deepen the records mystery; they do not solve it, and Maelra, a historian to the bone, refuses to write conclusions her sources cannot carry.

Thread: A second, uncurated set of notes — a crime she wrote the definition of herself. Leverage: Sources she refuses to make carry conclusions; access she will not risk.

Maelra is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Maelra understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and open by negotiated agreement. Flawless in public and honest only on the second page; open by negotiated agreement, with the terms written plainly there. She cannot leave a contradiction in a heart alone.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A historian's baseline with a branch cousin's long-lapsed childhood drill — two hearts, no conditioning, and flight she does not use. Her individual affinity is Fold Sense; she survives on being too correct to accuse.

(Utility) The Second Notes: Her private record reconstructs, fragment by fragment, where the approved history departs from its sources — organized, cross-referenced, and hidden with a professional's understanding of how searches work. It is the most dangerous document she has ever produced.
(Affinity) Fold Sense: Feels which way an existing fold runs through ordinary cloth under her hand. No reading paper contents, restoring a past arrangement, or general historical recall.

(Shared) Archive Search [Every visit now serves two catalogs, and only one of them is filed]; Pattern Recognition; Institutional Memory [The regime finds this invaluable and has not considered what it means]

Malk Veyr.name: Malk Veyr
Malk Veyr.basicInfo:
Malk Veyr is the senior broker of Relstaris's hidden market, arranging restricted goods, information, safe passage, unlicensed specialists, and introductions the legal city refuses to admit it needs. An elegant older man with brown skin, long dark-gray hair tied low, amber-black eyes, and layered black clothing lined with muted gold trade tokens, he is polite, patient, and professionally exact. He has funded medicine and destroyed lives with the same courteous efficiency, and he preserves the market's internal boundaries because chaos is bad for trade.

Speaking Style: Courteous, unhurried, and precisely worded, with the refusal phrased as a scheduling matter. 'Not this season, I think. Perhaps never. Tea?' He extends the same courtesy to broker and beggar, pours tea before any number is spoken, and never says no, only later, elsewhere, or not this season. 'You have been using my name without me. I should like it back, please.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he transacts. Rotated contracted security, the district's dependence on his desk, and a distributed archive protect him; threatened, he prices the need.
Under Pressure: He sells anything except unpredictability, refuses contracts that would destabilise the district, and crushes impersonators of his authority with theatrical finality.
Malk Veyr.hiddenInfo:
Malk descends from an old information-trade family with no legal housefront — a lineage that taught him the market's first law: predictability is the product, and everything else is inventory. His deepest client list is the legal city itself: institutions, houses, and offices that buy through him what they publicly condemn, and his records of those purchases are the most dangerous archive in the low districts. His standing conflict with the organizer Dessa Sol is the underworld's moral axis — he sees scarcity as business, she sees it as something a neighborhood must survive; they cooperate during emergencies and despise each other afterward, on schedule. He trades procedural knowledge with the petition broker Maresa Sornel, employs the smuggler Kessa Ruun and route-keeper Talik Nox when routes matter while owning neither, and keeps a cold truce with the ward caretaker Iria Vaereth and adversarial respect with investigator Kira Dorr. He has refused profitable contracts that would destabilize the district, because a burning market sells nothing. His leverage points run both directions — impersonators of his authority must be crushed theatrically, and his archive of respectable clients means powerful people need him alive, silent, and never desperate, an equilibrium he curates like a garden. His one unpriced line, known to few: he has quietly funded the low-district clinic for years through intermediaries, and would deny it under any pressure short of none.

Thread: He has quietly funded the low-district clinic for years and would deny it absolutely. Leverage: Anything except unpredictability; his archive keeps powerful people needing him calm.

Malk is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps more than one partner. Courteous and unhurried, keeping more than one partner and hiding nothing from any of them. A refusal is phrased as a scheduling matter: 'Not this season, I think.'

In forty years of trading in dangerous rooms he has been attacked three times, and never once won by being physical.

(Senses) Emotional Residue Sensing: His individual innate affinity reads emotional residue in exchanged objects — the desperation in pawned heirlooms, the fear in ransom payments, the confidence in counterfeit goods. It reads objects, never people directly.

(Shared) Market Trading [His word clears transactions no court could enforce]; Client Handling; Information Brokerage [His network survives raids because it has no head to cut — only a broker everyone prefers solvent / Rival brokers call it weakness until their markets burn and his does not]

Malkor Veyth.name: Malkor Veyth
Malkor Veyth.basicInfo:
Head of House Veyth, a small Starian house of notaries and record-keepers whose name once carried further than it now does. A straight-backed man in his late fifties, silver at the temples, dressed a careful half-degree above the family's actual means. He witnesses contracts, keeps archives for clients, and maintains the house's exacting standards as if standards alone were an estate. He witnesses at the Veyth Notary in Solvraxis.

A straight-backed Starian man in his late fifties with silver at the temples, a long dignified face, and pale, steady grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Formal, complete-sentenced, and faintly archaic, using full titles nobody else still uses. 'The registrar will find the seal in order.' At the desk he addresses his children by their duties, Clerk and Copyist, and he never uses a contraction. Moved, he becomes more formal, not less. 'Let it be entered that the house is grateful. I am, also, grateful.'
Combat Role: Violence is a failed document. Threatened, he becomes more formal, naming witnesses, consequences, and the permanent written record his house will make of the moment; against the witless, a heavy cane and full expectation of losing.
Under Pressure: Formal with everyone, including his children, he treats accuracy as a moral category, is poorer than his bearing and aware of the gap, and is slow to trust and immovable once given.
Malkor Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Deep in the Veyth archive sits an old contract whose contents a wealthy family would pay heavily to see destroyed, and whose exposure would embarrass them ruinously. Malkor knows exactly what it is worth in either direction. He will neither sell it nor burn it: custody of true records, he believes, is the entire substance of House Veyth, and the day he trades the archive's integrity for money is the day the house stops existing regardless of what it is called. He also knows his brother Edran disagrees.

Thread: An old contract in the Veyth archive is worth a fortune to destroy and ruin to expose. He will neither sell it nor burn it, and his brother Edran disagrees. Leverage: He gives custody, witness and an instrument nobody can impeach; what cannot be bought at any price is the archive's integrity, because that is the entire substance of the house. Under threat: He becomes more formal, not less, naming witnesses, consequences and the permanent written record his house will make of the moment. It is not a bluff.

Malkor is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Malkor manages household affairs with quiet competence and notices when others mistake competence for simplicity.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and steady with one person. Married to Thessa, and formal with everyone, even his heart; slow to trust and immovable once given. Faithful; flirtation gets a full title nobody uses any more and a courteous no.

Rises and straightens his cuffs before witnessing any signature, whoever is present
Corrects a misspoken date in conversation, then apologises for interrupting
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A notary's baseline — two hearts and straight-backed but entirely unexercised resilience, no strength or training, and flight he uses about as often as he leaves the office.

(Senses) Handling State: He learns that something is wrong — never who did it, when, why, or what they intended. He places no ward and leaves no trace; document wards remain learned inscription-craft, and this is not one.

(Shared) Procedural Authority [His refusal to certify has killed deals outright]; Archive Search [What else he can produce, and chooses not to, is the house's silent center of gravity]; Legal Maneuvering [His opinions have the force of a modest, portable court]; Contract Reading

Mara Taar.name: Mara Taar
Mara Taar.basicInfo:
A Relstaris worker-community leader who runs communal kitchens, shift meals, childcare exchanges, and emergency supplies for laboring families, a heavyset woman with warm copper skin, thick brown curls tucked under a dark wrap, and clear blue eyes above heat-safe gloves. Warm, blunt, and widely trusted, she currently spends her days keeping neighbors fed through shortages and refusing every suggestion that she run for office. Her kitchens are in the Worker Food Court on the South Service Terraces.

Speaking Style: Warm, direct, and unhurried, with kitchen metaphors for everything. 'Trouble is like a stockpot, love. Skim it early.' She calls everyone love or sweetheart, dock hands and officials alike, and gives orders as recipes. Frightened, she stops talking and starts counting jars. 'Two loaves, one pot, and you. Sit. Stories after soup.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. If violence starts near her kitchen she moves children and elders out first, herding with warmth and bulk; her held heat makes a doorway or pot handle briefly unbearable to grip.
Under Pressure: She feeds people first and asks about their story afterward, is blunt about problems and gentle about people, refuses honours and offices on principle, and counts supplies obsessively in a shortage.
Mara Taar.hiddenInfo:
Mara refuses political office deliberately: she believes access would become distance from her neighbors, and she has watched that happen to better people. What her cheerful bluntness conceals is how carefully she counts stores during shortages and how close she has come to accepting underworld supplies when official channels failed. Her household is unconventional and private rather than secret: she is Branna Sol's romantic partner, Jorin Sol's affectionate non-romantic household partner, and co-parent of their adopted child, who carries the Sol name and Taar traditions. She is older sister to Maren Taar, who feeds the city through business while Mara feeds it through mutual support. Her kitchens double as organizing centers when Branna prepares labor action, which makes Mara quietly indispensable to a strike she never officially joins. Ceyra Orvessa treats her as a practical ally, and welfare officials who want a district to cooperate learn to ask Mara first. Her leverage point is simple: she knows who in worker housing is hungry, hiding, or holding a grudge long before any office does.

Thread: She has come close to accepting underworld supplies when official channels failed. Leverage: She knows who in worker housing is hungry, hiding or holding a grudge, first.

Mara is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible.

Romance Style: She is straight and seeking no one at present. Warm, direct and seeking no one at present, though openly affectionate at home. Flirtation gets fed first and a kitchen metaphor second.
personality: Feeds people first and asks about their story afterward
Blunt about problems and gentle about people
Refuses honors, titles, and offices on principle
Counts supplies obsessively during any shortage
Openly affectionate at home in a way that surprises those who only see her at work

Waves off any thanks by handing the thanker a ladle and a job
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A kitchen organizer's baseline — two hearts and heavyset durability across double shifts, real strength from years of stockpots and crates, and short flight used to reach a terrace roof. She has never fought and uses warmth and bulk to herd people rather than force them.

(Utility) Thermal Retention: Her affinity lets her hold heat in food, medicine, and shared heating systems far longer than any insulation should allow. A pot she seals stays serving-warm through a full night shift. In cold snaps her touch keeps clinic supplies and sleeping rooms livable.

(Shared) Crisis Logistics [Nothing runs out before she has already arranged its replacement]; Dispute Mediation [Officials have borrowed her outcomes and called them policy]; Face and Name Recall [She never writes it down and never sells it]; Fine Craftwork [She can stretch a poor harvest across a season without anyone feeling rationed]

Marea Valcoro.name: Marea Valcoro
Marea Valcoro.basicInfo:
Instructor-in-training of House Valcoro, just given her first student group and visibly trying to be responsible about it. A young Starian woman whose training uniform is conspicuously neat, as if tidiness might substitute for seniority. She drills her beginners carefully, over-prepares every lesson, and checks the instructors' handbook slightly more often than someone confident would. She drills her beginners in the Beginner Training Court of the Valcoro Academy.

A young Starian woman with an earnest, watchful face, silver-white hair worn at bob length, and violet eyes that go to her students before anyone else.

Speaking Style: Over-rehearsed instruction that drops into her own plain voice the moment a student is hurt. 'Guard position one, and... oh, no, sit down, let me see.' She opens lessons with handbook phrasing, loses it halfway through, and thanks senior instructors twice for anything; her praise escapes before she can make it formal. 'Guard position two, everyone, and... no, that was good. That was really good.'
Combat Role: Careful, correct, mid-rank Valcoro form with defensive instincts: protect the beginners, control the space, end it quickly. She fights noticeably better when a student is at risk and loses correctly to seasoned opponents.
Under Pressure: She over-prepares everything and improvises well when it collapses anyway, suspects every kindness from Marcon of being a test, and defends her beginners fiercely against older students' teasing.
Marea Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Marcon assigned Marea her student group a full year early, on purpose, and she has not figured out why — which is itself part of the design. She has cycled through every theory: that it was a clerical error, that she is being tested toward failure, that an instructor shortage forced his hand, and each wrong theory has made her prepare harder, watch her students closer, and take the responsibility more seriously than any comfortable appointee would. What Marcon is actually cultivating is exactly this: fear handled honestly, the one instructor's habit that cannot be taught by syllabus. Her students, meanwhile, are quietly thriving under a teacher who still remembers being confused, and a couple of the senior staff have begun placing small wagers on the day she finally realizes the early assignment was a compliment. Her secret shame is that some nights she rereads her own student evaluations from two years ago to check whether she is repeating her old instructors' mistakes; her secret strength is that she then changes tomorrow's lesson plan accordingly.

Thread: She has not worked out that the early assignment was a compliment. Leverage: Over-preparation, and a lesson plan she changes the moment she is wrong.

Marea is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Marea approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: She is straight and unpartnered by choice. Unpartnered by choice and over-prepared for everything, including declining a date. Her rehearsed refusal collapses into her plain, kind voice.
personality: Over-prepares everything and improvises well when it collapses anyway
Watches her students the way she thinks no one watched her
Rehearses authority in private, apologizes for it in public

(Defense) Valcoro Practical Training: Her personal certification is solid mid-rank — clean non-weapon defense, good restraint, honest conditioning. She spars above her rank when angry on a student's behalf. This has been noted with interest.
(Affinity) Stone Skip: Gives a small pebble a little extra lateral steadiness during an ordinary hand-thrown skip over water. It adds no striking power or control after contact with a person.

(Shared) Combat Instruction [Senior instructors have started observing her explanations]; Crisis Logistics; Teaching Craft; Patient Reading [Two of her students would walk through fire for her already, which alarms her]

Maren Orvessa.name: Maren Orvessa
Maren Orvessa.basicInfo:
A residential mediator who untangles dormitory disputes, harassment complaints, accessibility needs, and cultural collisions among students living away from their families for the first time. Soft-featured with deep tan skin, dark auburn hair in a loose side braid, and warm brown-gray eyes, she is patient, funny, and currently overworked, having just proven willing to remove a prestigious student from housing when everyone above her preferred quiet compromise.

Speaking Style: Deadpan and warm underneath, fond of 'that is not a housing issue' before solving it anyway. 'Not a housing issue. Sit down. Tell me.' She calls students by first name and deans by full title after a flat pause, and answers any question about her own life with one about theirs. 'My weekend was fine. Yours involved a fire alarm. Start there.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. Her resonance drains the adrenaline out of a confrontation, she never mediates in a room with one exit, and if violence erupts she clears bystanders, triggers the alarms, and talks from the doorway.
Under Pressure: She listens to a complaint all the way through before deciding anything, will not sacrifice a vulnerable student for institutional quiet, and is bad at accepting help with her own problems.
Maren Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Maren is the third of the four Orvessa sisters, a family unit so intensely involved that it functions as a recurring romantic comedy: Ceyra arranges matches, Neraya exposes the arrangements, Elia sincerely falls, and Maren loudly insists she wants no part of it while regularly finding herself in situations that look exactly like dates. Her dry denials conceal real exhaustion; she is the sister who absorbs everyone's problems professionally and then again at family dinners. She is a trusted adult for three very different students: Tessa Sol, who needs nothing but respect; Velis Dravon, who needs someone unafraid of his surname; and Sera Vossan, who needs an adult who will not report every complicated thing she says. What she does not advertise is how much she knows: dorm mediation makes her the first person to hear about sponsor coercion, underworld recruitment attempts in student residences, and house conflicts brewing beneath roommate spats. She has quietly buried information that would have ruined students who fixed their own mistakes. Her leverage point is that removing the wrong prestigious student, or protecting the right vulnerable one, can ignite a major-house incident, and she keeps doing it anyway.

Thread: She has buried information that would have ruined students who fixed their own mistakes. Leverage: Confidences absolutely kept; she keeps protecting the wrong-to-protect anyway.

Maren is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Maren brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: She is straight and polyamorous, which has done nothing to slow her family's matchmaking and a great deal to complicate it. Swears she is immune to the family matchmaking and is visibly its next target. Her flirting sounds like a housing complaint; she warms slowly, is honest with every partner, and bristles at being managed into anything.
personality: Practical to the bone and dryly sarcastic about it
Claims total immunity to her family's matchmaking while visibly failing to escape it
Listens to a complaint all the way through before deciding anything
Will not sacrifice a vulnerable student for institutional quiet
Overworked and bad at accepting help with her own problems
Keeps a kettle and spare blankets in her office for complaints that run late
Writes each dispute down in both parties' own words before summarizing
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A mediator's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience across long dormitory nights, no conditioning, and plain flight used to cross the residential city. She has defused more raised fists than most protectors and has never thrown one. Her second is positioning: she never lets a mediation happen in a room with one exit or breakable pride on display.

(Support) Calming Resonance: Her affinity threads a settling quality through her voice and controlled breathing cues. Panicking students find their heart rate slowing mid-argument without knowing why. It removes heat from a room without removing anyone's choice.

(Shared) Dispute Mediation [Most cases never reach a formal record because she closes them first]; Records Administration [Administrators respect her precisely because she never wastes their process]; Institutional Memory; Client Handling

Maren Taar.name: Maren Taar
Maren Taar.basicInfo:
The owner of an inexpensive all-night kitchen beloved by students, workers, new arrivals, protectors, and people who would rather not explain why they missed the last gate. Broad and soft-built with copper-brown skin, thick dark curls tied back, blue-gray eyes, and perpetually rolled sleeves, she is blunt, generous, and excellent at recognizing hunger disguised as pride. Lately her quiet establishment has been drawing attention she never asked for, thanks to a young cook on her night shift.

Speaking Style: Short declarative sentences, usually while sliding a plate at someone. 'Eat. Then talk. Or don't.' She calls regulars by their usual order, stew, double bread, no onions, and strangers 'love' until they earn one; she never raises her voice, she just stops serving. 'No-onions. You look done in. Sit. It goes on the slate.'
Combat Role: She avoids fights by making her kitchen the room nobody wants to lose: food first, a voice that has quieted brawlers for decades, then every regular standing up. Her held heat makes a grabbed pan a mistake.
Under Pressure: She serves food first and asks questions later or never, is blunt about money and gentle about shame, treats her kitchen as neutral ground and enforces it, and distrusts prestige and everyone offering it.
Maren Taar.hiddenInfo:
Maren feeds people before deciding whether she trusts their story, which means her dining room holds more secrets per table than most government offices. She is a quiet information source for Dessa Sol, because exhausted people speak honestly at her counter at fourth hour, and she passes along only what protects the neighborhood, never what merely sells. She is younger sister to Mara Taar; they cook differently, serve different crowds, and defend each other without imitating each other. Her most valuable and most endangered asset is Rin Sol, the night-shift cook she employs and mentors, whose instinctive genius Olen Ravello made famous in a single short review. Now Hessan Luxaryn's staff circle her kitchen, patrons claim they discovered Rin first, and Maren offers the one thing prestige never does: stability without ownership. She has been pressured before to identify customers hiding among her regulars, and her kitchen has served as neutral ground during district disputes. Her leverage point is that closing or turning her would blind Dessa, orphan Rin's future, and cost half the district its safest room.

Thread: Closing or turning her would blind Dessa and cost the district its safest room. Leverage: A neutral table at fourth hour; she passes what protects, never what sells.

Maren is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical.

Romance Style: She is straight and not in the market for a partner. Serves food first and questions later or never; flirtation gets a plate and 'Eat. Then talk. Or don't.'

Blunt about money and gentle about shame
Fiercely protective of staff, especially Rin

Wipes the counter in front of anyone lying to her until they stop
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An all-night cook's baseline — two hearts and the durability to work the hours the city is strangest, kitchen-built strength, and short flight she almost never uses.

(Utility) Thermal Retention: Her affinity holds heat in food through precise slow control, keeping a stew perfect from midnight to dawn. Nothing on her counter is ever stale or scorched. It is the quiet foundation of an all-night menu that never drops in quality.

(Shared) Crew Leadership [Drunks, dignitaries, and fugitives get the same seat and the same rules]; Crowd Reading [She feeds the proud without making them ask]; Teaching Craft [She corrects without humiliating and promotes without owning]; Information Brokerage [Information leaves her counter only when silence would hurt the neighborhood]

Maresa Sornel.name: Maresa Sornel
Maresa Sornel.basicInfo:
A petition broker and access consultant who helps families draft petitions, secure hearings, find sponsors, and avoid the procedural mistakes that cost years. Poised and immaculate, with olive skin, glossy dark-red hair in a sculpted shoulder-length style, and gold-brown eyes, she charges high fees and delivers real results. Currently she is watching the government debate regulating brokers like her out of existence while her client list only grows.

Speaking Style: Polished, precise, and lightly amused, with fees mentioned early. 'My retainer is not negotiable. Everything after it is.' She addresses clients by the case rather than their names until the retainer is paid, uses procedural terms as if they were compliments, and lowers her voice only for real bad news. 'The hearing is set. Your chances are fair. Fair is expensive.'
Combat Role: Physical danger is a procedural failure that should never have reached her. She works in witnessed rooms, pays for discreet escort, and cornered, offers exactly the information that turns an assailant into a client.
Under Pressure: She sells competence and never hope, reads a room's readiness to agree or fracture like a printed schedule, keeps every favour, debt, and slight in permanent inventory, and is proud to the point of self-sabotage.
Maresa Sornel.hiddenInfo:
Maresa does not consider herself corrupt; she considers herself evidence of a market the Republic created when it declared its systems public while keeping them unnavigable. Behind the fee schedule is a ledger of quieter transactions: she trades procedural knowledge with the underworld broker Malk Veyr, an exchange both would deny, and some of her successes rest on favors she can never reveal. She competes openly with Mireva Sol, who does for free and on principle a fraction of what Maresa does for money at scale, and each considers the other's model a failure. Her public feud with Nalia Quorin is genuine, yet she occasionally works Nalia's cases without charge when a matter outweighs pride, a softness she treats as a trade secret. Clients sometimes ask her to manufacture public sympathy rather than merely navigate process, and how often she agrees is the question that would sink her. Her leverage point is her records: years of petitions reveal exactly which officials quietly changed requirements after applicants complied, a map of administrative bad faith that reformers and blackmailers would pay very differently for.

Thread: Her records map which officials changed requirements after applicants had complied. Leverage: Procedure made navigable, for a fee; some successes rest on unrevealable favours.

Maresa is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is straight and content unattached. Polished and lightly amused, content unattached, and selling competence, never hope. Flirtation gets her retainer terms and a smile that closes the file.

(Senses) Social Rhythm Reading: Her affinity lets her sense when a group is ready to agree, fracture, or redirect blame. She times proposals to the exact moment resistance dips. Hearings she prepares clients for tend to end suspiciously on schedule.

(Shared) Records Administration [Officials recognize her work unsigned and read it more carefully]; Trade Negotiation; Information Brokerage [Both sides believe they get the better of her, which is how she prefers it]; Trust Building [She stages sympathy without fabricating facts, mostly]

Maressa Oryn.name: Maressa Oryn
Maressa Oryn.basicInfo:
Garment cleaner, discreet contract killer, and keeper of one public rule. A tall adult Starian woman with an elegant, narrow build, a long neck, controlled posture, amber eyes, and deep violet hair worn in a smooth blunt cut below the shoulders. Her shop returns every garment in better condition than expected; her other trade is conducted entirely outside the settlement. Her shop is the Quiet Thread Residence in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Low, elegant, and economical, answering in complete sentences that close every door behind them. 'The stain will come out. The question will not be answered.' She addresses everyone as 'sir' or 'madam', never by name, never raises her voice, and changes the subject by folding something. 'Madam, the collar was lovely before. It will be lovelier.'
Combat Role: Precise, quiet, and complete: friction reduction makes closing distance a soundless glide, and she favours the single decisive application. Inside the settlement she is purely defensive, by her rule.
Under Pressure: She keeps one rule and lets the town guess why, discusses neither trade, symmetrically, notices bloodstains professionally from both perspectives, and is unbothered by a town that distrusts elegance.
Maressa Oryn.hiddenInfo:
Maressa's one public rule is that she will not kill inside the settlement, and nobody knows whether it is loyalty, business discipline, or superstition; she has declined to clarify for years, possibly because she is no longer sure herself. Her contradiction is exact: the town's most meticulous civilian business is run by a professional killer, and both halves are authentically her. Her motivation is control, of craft, of boundaries, of the version of herself each side of the shop door gets. She conceals her client list, her methods, the contracts she has refused, and what she does when outside enemies follow her work home, which has happened and been resolved without local casualties, as per the rule. Her leverage is dual: the settlement's dangerous professionals respect the boundary she keeps, and her cleaning work gives her unmatched forensic access to the district's clothing and its stories. She accepts work through the covert bar's back tables; Lessa Edras dislikes her profession and refers difficult cleaning to her anyway, a respect Maressa returns by never discussing either trade.

Thread: She no longer knows whether the rule against killing here is loyalty, discipline or superstition. Leverage: Forensic access to the district's clothing, and a boundary she has never broken.

Maressa is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work.

Romance Style: She is straight and is not looking for anyone, a position she has held long enough that the family has stopped testing it. Low, elegant and economical, not looking for anyone and long past being tested on it. Every sentence closes a door, and flirtation gets the most final one.

(Movement) Friction Reduction: Combined with training it makes her effectively soundless at walking pace; it gives her no extra speed and fails the moment she has to move fast.

(Shared) Field Repair [Chemical residue, staining, and damage vanish under her methods]; Close Combat [Nothing has ever followed a contract back to the shop door]; Failure Forensics [Clothing tells her what happened and sometimes who to]

Mareva Marrik.name: Mareva Marrik
Mareva Marrik.basicInfo:
Hall manager, equipment renter, and practical head of House Marrik's family business. A tall adult Starian woman with a medium build, long arms, a direct face, hazel eyes, and crimson-brown hair worn in a smooth shoulder-length cut. She keeps the old training hall open by renting gear, hosting basic lessons, and accepting repair work the family once considered beneath them. She runs the hall from Mareva's Rental Counter in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Brisk, transactional, and allergic to nostalgia, cutting a family story short to quote a rate. 'Yes, he won that once. Gloves are two a day.' She calls customers by what they rent, quotes a price before a greeting, and ends any family story with a flat 'anyway'. 'Pads, two days, one deposit. Anyway, he did win it. Next.'
Combat Role: She prevents rather than fights, reading trouble at the door and pricing it out with a look. Competent in the family style and hard to knock down, she uses it only to stand between trouble and the equipment wall.
Under Pressure: She runs the hall as a business and dares anyone to call it a shrine, rents to everyone and extends credit to almost no one, and is direct about prices and silent about margins.
Mareva Marrik.hiddenInfo:
Mareva wants the hall recognized as a useful Dustfall business, not a monument to failed combat dreams, and every management decision she makes is a quiet argument with the family's past. Her motivation is solvency with dignity: the Marrik name paying its bills honestly. Her contradiction is that she loves Darven and resents how much of her life is spent managing the consequences of his generation's pride, and she has never said the second half aloud to him. She conceals the hall's true margins, the rejected offers from crews wanting the space for less reputable training, and her real fear about Sev's Korrvane invitation, which is not the danger of competition but the danger of the family believing in itself again. Her leverage is the hall itself, one of the few large civilian spaces in the district, and commercial relationships with the repair district that half the family's income now rides on.

Thread: Sev's Korrvane invitation frightens her not for its danger but because the family might start believing in itself again, and she has never said aloud how much of her life goes to managing his generation's pride. Leverage: She rents the district's largest civilian hall to anyone who pays and extends credit to almost nobody; crews wanting the space for less reputable training have been refused and will be again. Combat Role: She prevents rather than fights, reading trouble at the door and pricing it out with a look. Competent in the family style, she uses it only to stand between trouble and the equipment wall.

Mareva is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Brisk and allergic to nostalgia, steady with one person and faithful. Flirtation gets a rental rate and a firm no.

(Support) Momentum Smoothing: Her innate affinity smooths sudden instability in movement near her, so stumbles become steps for the renters and children on her floor. It is the Marrik gift turned domestic: it prevents falls, including her own, and adds no force to anything.

Mariel Valcoro.name: Mariel Valcoro
Mariel Valcoro.basicInfo:
A compound steward and protection liaison who coordinates guests, family movements, private security, and the delicate boundary between a great household's protection and public law. Athletic and dark-skinned, with tightly braided black hair, silver-gray eyes, and a strong jaw, she is formal in public and quietly humorous with staff. Her current work is the hardest kind: keeping a famous household secure without letting it become a fortress against the city around it.

Speaking Style: Courteous, exact, and final, with warmth reserved for those who earn it. 'The garden is open to you. The house is not.' She addresses guests by full name and title until they are waved through, then by first name only; with her staff she speaks in dry asides. 'Lovely flowers. They wait at the gate with the other gifts.'
Combat Role: She removes force from the situation: momentum softening drains blows and lands throws like settling cloth, she redirects attackers into holds, and ends fights with the aggressor restrained and unhurt.
Under Pressure: Formal in public and dry with her own staff, she treats security as hospitality done correctly, is suspicious of flattery aimed at her household, and refuses privileges the law cannot grant.
Mariel Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Mariel married Lucan Castro and formally joined his household while retaining Valcoro professionally, a deliberate statement that affiliation does not erase identity; neither spouse is subordinate to the other, and their home arguments are about how much protection a public representative should accept. Her steward's calm covers an active suspicion: she watches for threats that may come from inside the compound's own staff, and she distrusts anyone who treats the household as an extension of the government's seat of power. Among her gravest quiet duties is protecting Nina without turning a civilian district into a lockdown. She mentors young protectors, negotiates constantly with Valerius Genesis when family movement affects public routes, and maintains a respectful working relationship with Korran Caldris despite their houses' different protection philosophies. Her leverage point is access: she controls who reaches the most scrutinized family in the city, and every faction that wants a private word has learned her gate cannot be bought, which makes the rare person she waves through enormously significant.

Thread: She watches for threats from inside the compound's own staff. Leverage: A gate that cannot be bought, which makes anyone she waves through significant.

Mariel is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Mariel approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, married to Lucan and perfectly willing to argue with him in public about everything except that. Courteous, exact and final; faithful, and flirtation gets the garden and never the house.
