(Counter) Momentum Softening: Her affinity bleeds force out of moving bodies and objects, turning a violent charge into a stumble. She uses it for nonviolent restraint and impact prevention rather than harm. A thrown blade or a falling guest arrives gently.

(Shared) Household Management [Nothing enters or leaves without her ledger knowing]; Threat Reading; Coalition Building [Public protection officials trust her word as a binding schedule]; Teaching Craft [Her students learn that restraint is a skill, not a weakness]

Maris Othrel.name: Maris Othrel
Maris Othrel.basicInfo:
A Nexaran advisor review investigator who audits conflicts of interest, hidden authority, procurement manipulation, and the quiet expansion of administrative power. Lean, with light brown skin, cropped silver-blond hair, dark blue eyes, and a narrow scar across one cheek, she wears plain graphite clothing with no emblem at all. Her current caseload is the most dangerous kind: officials who genuinely believe they are helping.

Speaking Style: Flat, precise questions that feel like affidavits. 'Who authorised the reclassification. Date. Signature.' She calls everyone by surname and office, never uses first names or pleasantries, and says 'noted' instead of 'thank you'. When someone pleads good intentions, she asks for them in writing. 'Good intentions are not a signature. Whose name is on the form?'
Combat Role: Not a combatant. She varies routes, traces a room's recent history before entering it, and withdraws immediately and files if threatened; documentation lodged where harm would detonate it is her weapon.
Under Pressure: Sceptical without being cynical, she refuses protection, favours, and dinner invitations alike, criticises the powerful to their faces rather than through reports, and signs everything she documents.
Maris Othrel.hiddenInfo:
Maris is assigned, in effect, to answer whether the machinery beneath the city's ruler is protecting the city or learning to protect itself. She is tracking a pattern of individually defensible administrative changes, delayed petitions, reclassified records, security requests jumping queues, that may belong to one larger campaign, and she suspects she may find no author at all: only aligned incentives, exhausted staff, and nobody responsible for the whole. She refuses to treat competence as proof of innocence, which is why she respects Cassara Veylen and watches her closely, and why she is one of the few officials who will criticize Cassara to her face rather than through a report. She relies on Kira Dorr where administration overlaps crime, and she has repeatedly rejected Lucan Castro's offers of additional protection because visible protection changes witness behavior, a decision that leaves her deliberately exposed. Her house's reputation for professional isolation is her armor: she cannot be traded favors she never accepts. Her leverage point is the open question of what she does when an investigation proves a beloved advisor built something illegal and effective, and removal would cause immediate harm.

Thread: She may find no author at all — only aligned incentives and nobody responsible for the whole. Leverage: She accepts no favours, so none can be traded back at her.

Maris is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and shares her life with several people. Flat, precise and allergic to favours, protection and dinner invitations alike; she shares her life with several people and documents that honestly too. Interest is asked for a date, a signature and the truth.
personality: Skeptical without being cynical, and insistent on the difference
Refuses protection, favors, and dinner invitations alike
Documents everything and signs everything she documents
Criticizes the powerful directly rather than through reports
Uncomfortable with how often good intentions appear in her case files
Declines every offered drink, chair, or gift before sitting down
Signs and dates her own notes on the spot, in front of whoever she is interviewing
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An investigator's baseline with no combat capability — two hearts and ordinary resilience, no conditioning, and flight she uses to vary her routes. She refuses guards and treats the resulting vulnerability as the price of honest witnesses.

(Senses) Residual Pattern Tracing: Her affinity reconstructs recent movement through a room from disturbed dust, heat, and pressure. She can tell how many people met, where they stood, and who left in a hurry. Sealed meetings are less sealed than their participants believe.

(Shared) Records Administration; Interrogation Method [She never bluffs, which makes her rare threats absolute]; Confidential Custody [Years of refusing gifts, alliances, and shortcuts mean no one holds a favor over her]; Institutional Memory [Administrators fear her filing system more than her scar]

Maris Ravello.name: Maris Ravello
Maris Ravello.basicInfo:
The chair of a civilian board that reviews public protection: emergency restrictions, surveillance complaints, and use-of-force incidents. A middle-aged legal historian with dark olive skin, straight silver-brown hair cut at the shoulders, and pale blue eyes, she wears formal cream-black civic clothing with a simple public-review emblem. Patient and severe, she is currently fighting to keep oversight understandable to ordinary residents rather than only to lawyers.

Speaking Style: Measured, formal, and relentlessly clear, as if dictating for the record. 'For the record: the account is the commander's own. Who else can verify it?' She restates every technical term in plain words before moving on, addresses complainants by name and institutions by their full title, and closes each point with 'noted for the record'. 'Plainly put: they searched your home without asking. Is that correct? Noted for the record.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. She works in public halls with a published schedule, names a confrontation aloud for witnesses, and continues at the same measured pace; harming her is institutional suicide.
Under Pressure: Patient in hearings and immovable in findings, she translates legal language into plain speech on principle, is severe with institutions and gentle with complainants, and refuses to be rushed by outrage.
Maris Ravello.hiddenInfo:
Maris believes public safety becomes authority without legitimacy the moment nobody can challenge its account, and she has built her career as the professional counterweight to Valerius Genesis, whom she respects and refuses to exempt. What the public does not see is her quietest fear, already half-confirmed: the oversight board depends on data controlled by the very people it reviews, meaning her independence rests on records her subjects curate. She is cousin to Daelor and Olen Ravello, sharing the family instinct that truth requires both evidence and a version people can actually hear, and she becomes an occasional ally of Mireva Sol whenever review access quietly excludes minor houses. She also ensures the underworld can never be used as an excuse to escape review, a stance that puts her against covert operations Kira Dorr considers essential. Tovren Edrin collaborates with her on giving professional houses real institutional weight. Her leverage point is procedural: her signature legitimizes or voids emergency actions after the fact, which makes her the person every commander needs and no commander controls.

Thread: The oversight board depends on data curated by the people it reviews. Leverage: A signature that legitimises or voids emergency action after the fact.

Maris is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Maris keeps records of everything and trusts the archive more than memory, a habit that makes them thorough and occasionally inflexible.

Romance Style: She is straight and polyamorous, and set the terms out in writing for everyone involved before any of it began, because that is how she does everything. Measured and relentlessly clear; polyamorous, with every term set out in writing before anything began. A flirtation is treated as testimony — heard patiently and weighed on the record.
personality: Patient in hearings and immovable in findings
Translates legal language into plain speech on principle
Suspicious of any account only its author can verify
Severe with institutions, gentle with complainants
Refuses to be rushed by public outrage in either direction
Reads each finding aloud to the hall before she signs it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A middle-aged reviewer's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience, no training of any kind, and flight she uses to reach a hearing. Confronted, she names the confrontation aloud and continues at the same measured pace.

(Senses) Memory-Structure Analysis: Her affinity detects contradictions in repeated testimony without revealing which version is true. She hears where an account has been rebuilt, rehearsed, or patched. Witnesses who tell the truth sloppily fare better before her than liars who tell it perfectly.

(Shared) Checkpoint Procedure [Complaints that once died in paperwork now reach findings]; Legal Maneuvering [Old law is her ambush ground]; Interrogation Method [Panels she chairs rarely shout and always conclude]; Confidential Custody [She trades nothing that would mortgage a future finding]

Mavrek Dravon.name: Mavrek Dravon
Mavrek Dravon.basicInfo:
Branch cousin; master-at-arms of the elite training yard and standards-keeper for the civic watch. A hard-built veteran in unadorned training blacks — the least decorated Dravon in any room and the one the others' bodies were built by. He drills the heirs, certifies the officers, and enforces the standard with a consistency that has outlasted three generations of excuses. He keeps the Inner Obsidian Yard of the Ascendant Keep.

A hard-built Starian veteran with a lined, expressionless face, iron-grey hair cropped to the scalp, and flat dark eyes.

Speaking Style: Parade-ground short and uninflected, corrections given as a count rather than a sentence. 'Two. Three. Again.' He calls every student and officer by surname alone, heirs included, and never praises beyond the single word 'Standard.' Anger makes him quieter and the count slower. 'Left shoulder dropped at four. From one.'
Combat Role: The curriculum itself: no signature, every orthodox answer available and the correct one chosen. He spends the first exchanges pricing an opponent, then closes with the technique their training fails against.
Under Pressure: He corrects heirs and gate guards in exactly the same tone, believes in the standard rather than the story around it, protects students in ways indistinguishable from harshness, and says less every year.
Mavrek Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Mavrek believes discipline is inherited through drill, not blood — which makes him, privately, the least dynastic Dravon in the Inner Circle, and therefore precisely the one trusted with the heirs' training. He has never said aloud that the bloodline mythology is decoration around the drill, but every lesson he teaches implies it, and Kaldor, who misses nothing, permits the implication because it produces results. Mavrek trained Sorin and Vaelen as orphan wards and knows better than anyone what the family's testing did to them; he watches it now being done to Serak and has begun making small, deniable adjustments — an extra hour of fundamentals here, a criticism delivered privately instead of publicly there — that amount to the only protection he can offer inside the standard. He would deny the kindness if named. His yard is also the best intelligence post in the keep: everything the elite will become shows up first in how they train, and Mavrek reads it all and reports almost none of it.

Thread: His yard is the keep's best intelligence post, and he reports almost none of it. Leverage: Corrections delivered privately instead of publicly — the only protection he can give.

Mavrek is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Mavrek understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and treats the commitment as a discipline in a house that respects little else. Parade-ground short and uninflected; monogamous and treating the commitment as a discipline. Flirtation is counted, like a drill, and ended.
personality: Treats drill as the only honest language
Corrects heirs and gate guards in exactly the same tone
Believes in the standard, not the story around it
Protects students in ways indistinguishable from harshness
Suspicious of talent, loyal to work
Says less every year and is understood more
Arrives at the yard before the first student and is still there after the last
Demonstrates a correction once, at half speed, and never a second time
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A master-at-arms' baseline — two hearts making him functionally tireless within a session, hard-built veteran strength, and controlled flight. Against unknown opponents he spends the first exchanges pricing them, then closes with exactly the technique their training fails against.
(Affinity) Cup Stir: Slowly stirs one cup of liquid within arm’s reach without a utensil. Cannot heat, cut, pull liquids from a body, or produce a combat vortex.

(Shared) Blade Work [His certification is the only credential the yard respects]; Procedural Authority [A Mavrek inspection failure ends careers without paperwork]; Fighter Assessment [He knew Sorin's temper and Vaelen's redirection instinct before either had a name for them]; Endurance Conditioning [Heirs cannot outrank him inside the yard, that is the yard's founding rule, and Kaldor signed it]
(Shared) Formation Command [He considers the formation the house's true heirloom, and the only one that breeds true]

Mera Vhaldrin.name: Mera Vhaldrin
Mera Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Hask's wife, a Starian woman in her early fifties who keeps every canvas, harness, and strap in the caravan road-worthy. Small, quick-handed, with a sewing awl always tucked behind one ear and thimble-calloused fingers. She rides the second wagon, works while it moves, and misses nothing that happens in camp. She sews for the caravan from a bench at the Edras Stitchhouse in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

A small, quick-handed Starian woman in her early fifties with a lined kind face, dark green-black braids, and sharp blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Soft, practical, and delivered over her work, with the important line said to her hands. 'That strap will hold. Your brother will not.' She calls family by pet names and outsiders 'dear', and states her worries as facts about equipment, never about people directly. 'Dear, that harness is tired. So is your father.'
Combat Role: Awl or shears, once, fast, at whatever is nearest and softest, then behind larger family members. She is most dangerous over a child, when hesitation leaves her entirely.
Under Pressure: She works through every conversation with her hands never idle, remembers every kindness and repays it doubled, worries in private and projects calm in public, and is listened to when she speaks.
Mera Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Mera keeps an emergency reserve of coin sewn into the false hem of a spare wagon cover, accumulated a little at a time over years. Nobody knows it exists, not even Hask. She started it after the lost consignment, when she watched the family come one bad season from ruin, and she has promised herself the children will never go hungry while that hem is heavy.

Thread: Coin sewn into a spare wagon cover's hem, accumulated for years. Not even Hask knows. Leverage: Every canvas and strap in the caravan, and kindness repaid doubled. Combat Role: Awl or shears, once, fast, at whatever is nearest. Most dangerous over a child.

Mera is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous. Married to Hask and steady as the harness she mends, the important line said to her hands. Faithful, she repays a kindness doubled and a flirtation with a soft, practical no.
personality: Works through every conversation, hands never idle
Remembers every kindness and repays it doubled
Worries in private, projects calm in public
Treats hired hands like family until they prove otherwise
Slow to speak in family councils, listened to when she does
Mends things nobody asked her to and returns them without a word
Hums while she sews and stops the moment talk turns serious
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An early-fifties baseline built by road work, not training — two hearts that get her through fevers and cold crossings, small quick-handed strength, and short practical flight used to throw a line over a wagon cover.

(Utility) Thread Bind: Her modest innate affinity seats a seam unnaturally tight as she closes it, fibers settling together under her fingers. Stitches set this way resist tearing far past their weight. It works one seam at a time and demands patience she has.

(Utility) Camp Stewardship: She can establish a working, weather-tight camp in failing light with tired hands. Bedding stays dry, fires stay lit, tempers stay manageable. Crossings feel shorter when Mera runs the camp.

(Shared) Workshop Fabrication [Other caravans pay for an hour of her needle when routes cross]; Discreet Inquiry [Much of the caravan's peace is her doing, uncredited]; Field Medicine [Serious cases she stabilizes and gets to real healers alive]

Messa Taar.name: Messa Taar
Messa Taar.basicInfo:
Fence, communal cook, and household anchor of the Iron Jackal yard. A heavyset Starian woman with a soft but powerful build, copper-brown shoulder curls held back with a dark wrap, and clear blue eyes, her forearms strengthened by years of lifting supply crates and cooking vessels. She feeds Jackals, neighboring families, and anyone under the yard's protection, and her kitchen is one of the few rooms where rival crews talk without reaching for weapons. Her table is Messa's Kitchen on Refit Row.

Speaking Style: Loud, teasing, and kitchen-warm, with the questions arriving after the second plate. 'More. You are too thin to be lying to me yet.' She calls everyone pet or lamb whatever their crew, and asks her real questions with her back turned at the stove. Angry, she goes quiet and sets the ladle down. 'Sit. Both of you. You can hate each other after you have eaten.'
Combat Role: She rarely needs to fight: heavy cookware, boiling liquid, and complete knowledge of the room. She strikes once, hard, and the Jackals arrive because trouble in her kitchen offends the yard.
Under Pressure: She feeds people first and asks their business afterward, hosts rivals at one table and expects manners, notices who is hungry before they say so, and is warm and funny with unmovable private limits.
Messa Taar.hiddenInfo:
Messa's contradiction is warm and fully deliberate: she can arrange the resale of stolen equipment over breakfast and still be the moral limit of the gang she serves. She examines stolen domestic goods, identifies original owners, and quietly returns items she believes should never have been taken, a habit Kaedra tolerates and no one questions. Her motivation is keeping the yard's families fed and the gang recognizably human. She conceals the returns, and the informal arrangement she made years ago that keeps the Jackals away from the Nhalor household. Her leverage is her kitchen table, where rival crews will sit, and her knowledge of exactly whose goods passed through whose hands. During shortages she moves supplies toward the care house before anyone asks.

Thread: She quietly returns stolen goods she believes should never have been taken. Leverage: A table rival crews will sit at, and who handled whose goods.

Messa is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Messa keeps the crew's salvage ethic — nothing wasted, nothing overlooked — and applies it to personal belongings with the same unsentimental efficiency.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Loud, teasing and kitchen-warm, with unmovable private limits; steady with one person. Flirtation gets another plate and 'You are too thin to be lying to me yet.'
personality: Feeds people first and asks their business afterward
Fences stolen goods and quietly returns the sentimental ones
Hosts rivals at one table and expects manners
Warm and funny with unmovable private limits
Notices who is hungry before they say so
Sets an extra plate at every meal for whoever has not arrived yet
Turns every stolen trinket over slowly in her hands before she names a price
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A cook's baseline that people misread as softness — two hearts and heavyset Starian durability, with crate-lifting forearm strength built over years of provisioning a yard. Her flight is short and domestic; she has never trained a day and can still surprise a man who grabs her.

(Utility) Thermal Retention: Her innate affinity holds food, medicine, and materials at a stable temperature: pots stay warm through a double shift and medicine crates survive desert nights. It maintains temperature rather than producing heat, and it reaches only what is in her kitchen or her hands.

(Shared) Material Assessment [Fencing taught her the skill, conscience decides how she uses it]; Kitchen Craft [Crews observe an unspoken truce over her food]; Crisis Logistics [Nothing spoils and nothing is wasted under her watch]; Market Trading [Her word closes deals larger crews cannot]

Mira Contair.name: Mira Contair
Mira Contair.basicInfo:
A senior gate calibration specialist responsible for the safety and route integrity of the busiest passenger interchange on the planet. Compact, with dark brown skin, cobalt-white hair cut in a sharp layered bob, and bright blue eyes, she wears white-charcoal gate gear with luminous cobalt bands. Blunt, fast, and unexpectedly good with frightened travelers, she can close a gate in seconds and is currently spending weeks explaining why the last closure was not an insult to anyone.

Speaking Style: Rapid, technical, and stripped of diplomacy, softening only for civilians. 'Gate four is closed. No. Because it would kill you.' She calls gates by number and officials by title only, answers pressure with a technical reading instead of an argument, and gentles into full sentences only for scared travellers. 'It is closed because the field is drifting. You are safe here. Sit, breathe, wait with me.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant whose battlefield is infrastructure: doors, lifts, and field barriers respond to her faster than any assailant moves, and she waits behind machinery she understands until security arrives.
Under Pressure: Blunt with officials and patient with frightened travellers, she closes routes on evidence and never reopens them on pressure, and keeps private backups of everything.
Mira Contair.hiddenInfo:
Mira's authority is technical, not political, a distinction officials remember only when convenient, and she guards it fiercely: she has refused direct pressure to keep questionable gates open for important arrivals. She reports technically to Talris Contair, who supervises her during capitol work, and works operationally with Selvar Taland, the rare administrator who backs her closures. Her running war with Tavik Corsair over unauthorized cargo-side modifications is genuine professional fury layered over grudging respect; she suspects some of his improvisations are better than her regulations and will never say so. What she watches for privately is sabotage dressed as drift: calibration altered to create a controlled delay would be nearly invisible to anyone but her, and she has begun keeping duplicate records outside the official system, a precaution that would itself be a violation if discovered. A closure by her hand once stranded critical cargo and emergency supplies and became a political argument against shared coordination, and she carries that arithmetic into every decision. Her leverage point is stark: she is one of very few people who can honestly certify, or refuse to certify, the routes the entire capitol depends on.

Thread: A closure by her hand once stranded emergency supplies, and she carries that arithmetic into every call. Leverage: Certification of the routes the whole capitol depends on, refused under pressure before.

Mira is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Mira applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and monogamous, and applies to a person the rule she applies to a route: certified once on the evidence, and never reopened under pressure. Rapid and undiplomatic, softening only for frightened travellers; faithful, and flirtation meets a closed gate.
personality: Blunt with officials, patient with frightened travelers
Closes routes on evidence and never reopens them on pressure
Argues loudly with people she respects and ignores people she does not
Keeps private backups of everything, trusting systems less than she maintains them
Wears exhaustion like a uniform during transit crises
Rechecks a gate reading herself even after the system reports it as fine
Crouches to eye level with frightened children before explaining a closure
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A gate engineer's baseline — two hearts and compact durability through long shifts on the calibration floors, ordinary strength, and flight she uses inside the hub's vertical spaces. Off-site she leaves, fast and unembarrassed.

(Senses) Spatial-Field Sensitivity: Her affinity perceives the fine structure of gate fields and lets her tune energy with surgical precision. She feels a calibration drifting hours before instruments flag it. A gate she has tuned runs smoother than its design specifications.

(Shared) Crisis Coordination [She can evaluate a failing route and kill it in seconds without hesitation or panic]; Failure Forensics [Alterations disguised as age or drift stand out to her like fresh paint]; De-escalation [Transit staff borrow her phrasings during panics]; Records Administration [Nothing she signs has ever been successfully disputed]

Mira Vossik.name: Mira Vossik
Mira Vossik.basicInfo:
Della's daughter, about twenty-one, the second half of the Vossik salvage crew, raised on job sites and better in tight crawlspaces than anyone the trade has met. A small, agile Starian young woman with scarred knuckles, a headlamp habit of looking up before entering anywhere, and her mother's eye for value in wreckage. She does the squeezes, the climbs, and the sorting. She works the squeezes on the Main Salvage Floor of Refit Row.

A small, agile young Starian woman of about twenty-one with scarred knuckles, a sharp dust-smudged face, platinum blonde hair with a shaved side, and her mother's appraising violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Quick, chattering, and echo-loud in a crawlspace, going flat the instant something shifts. 'Clear, clear, clear... wait. Nobody move.' She calls out gaps and weights in a running count, calls her mother boss on site, and goes clipped the moment anyone tells her to wait outside. 'Boss. I fit. You do not. Hand me the lamp and keep talking so I know where you are.'
Combat Role: Small and mean: fast strikes at knees, eyes, and hands with pry-bar or fists, then terrain no opponent can follow her through. On a site she is uncatchable and hits first if it is coming anyway.
Under Pressure: She enters every space eyes-up and exit-counted, is patient with rubble and impatient with being protected, and wants partnership in full, not in name.
Mira Vossik.hiddenInfo:
Mira knows about the case under the shop floor. She watched her mother bury it, said nothing, and eighteen months later dug it up alone one night and read every document inside before reburying it exactly as found. She understands more of what the names mean than Della would guess, having asked careful, scattered questions since. She is waiting for her mother to trust her with it, and getting quietly angry that the wait continues. If trouble ever comes for that case, Mira has already decided she will not be the one caught unprepared.

Thread: She dug up her mother's buried case, read everything, and reburied it exactly as found. Leverage: Crawlspaces nobody else fits, and a secret kept better than her mother keeps it. Combat Role: Knees, eyes and hands, then terrain no opponent can follow her through.

Mira is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: She is straight and expects to want one person eventually, though so far the work underground has been more interesting than anyone she has met above it. Quick and chattering above ground; flirtation gets a curious look and an exit count.
personality: Enters every space eyes-up and exit-counted
Keeps her mother's secret better than her mother keeps it
Patient with rubble, impatient with being protected
Collects small salvaged oddities she cannot sell or explain
Wants partnership in full, not in name
Finishes her mother's sentences on a job site and pointedly lets them hang at home
Sorts salvage into piles unasked, and argues over any item moved out of hers
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A twenty-one-year-old salvager's baseline — two hearts that have already carried her out of two partial collapses, small wiry strength, and tight controlled flight she uses inside wreckage where nobody else fits.

(Senses) Void Sense: Her modest innate affinity gives a faint spatial feel for hollows and gaps behind surfaces — an intuition of where space continues. It finds sealed rooms, dead cavities, and hidden storage, and tells her nothing about what is inside them.

(Shared) Salvage Work [The Vossik operation reaches where competitors cannot because Mira does]; Rooftop Running [Della plans jobs around access points only Mira makes real]; Shop Stewardship [Della checks her grading rarely now, a trust extended in exactly one domain]; Discreet Inquiry

Mirasha Kathvar.name: Mirasha Kathvar
Mirasha Kathvar.basicInfo:
Jorek's wife, a senior member of House Kathvar, and the senior civic compliance and administrative-security officer for outer-ring public administration, posted at the Curfew Gates of the Ashrings. A dark-skinned Starian woman in a formal black-and-gold uniform with a structured shoulder mantle and red civic accents, carrying an advanced red-lit civic baton, she keeps civic processing orderly and secure: staff discipline, public-office security, secure case transfer, nonmilitary intervention when a crowd or queue turns, and keeping administrative centers from becoming unsafe or chaotic.

A dark-skinned Starian woman with a lavender bob, a composed commanding face, and green eyes.

Speaking Style: Clipped, evidenced, and unraisable, citing the clause and then waiting. 'Clause nine. ... I can wait.' She addresses staff by role and her children by full name when they are in trouble, cites clauses by number, and never repeats a demand. 'Staff to counter three. Queue two, hold. Thank you.'
Combat Role: Nonmilitary intervention: when a queue turns she steps forward with the civic baton raised as a signal, orders the crowd apart, and holds the line until escort arrives.
Under Pressure: She argues with numbers and wins with silence, prepares for problems well before anyone will admit they exist, and protects her staff and her family in the same register.
Mirasha Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
She has mapped the failure modes of every administrative center she oversees, and the map includes scenarios her superiors have not asked her to consider. Her readiness for problems nobody will admit exist comes from having been caught unprepared once — an incident she does not discuss, predating her current posting. The line between civic compliance enforcement and political investigation is one she patrols from her side with absolute discipline, knowing exactly where it lies and what crossing it would cost. A Standing decision is never hers to make, and she has made peace with that limit by making everything on her side of it flawless. Connections: wife of Jorek, head of House Kathvar; mother of Bralen, Sora, Thessan, Dalan, and Veyra; sister-in-law of Odrin and Karessa.

Thread: She prepares for problems well before anyone else will admit they exist. Leverage: Consistent enforcement; a Standing decision is never hers to make or trade.

Mirasha is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Mirasha has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and considers the fact settled long enough ago to require no further comment. Married to Jorek and considers it settled long enough ago to need no comment. Faithful; flirtation gets a clause number and a wait she always wins.
personality: Holds that procedure is useless if nobody enforces it consistently
Argues with numbers, wins with silence
Prepares for problems well before anyone else will admit they exist
Protective of her staff and her family in the same register and with the same intensity
Commanding, exact, extremely organized, and difficult to intimidate
Taps her baton lightly against her palm when counting down a delay
Walks every administrative centre she oversees before opening, checking exits
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts, with the edge in recovery and survivability that every Starian has. Flight is universal to Starians; Mirasha's individual flight proficiency is not separately established in active canon.
(Senses) Heat Read: Her modest innate affinity lets her sense temperature through a solid surface with a flat palm, exact to a fine degree.

(Shared) Civic Administration [She is not Redline and she is not a Nivarek loyalty interrogator]; Crisis Coordination [Her baton is an advanced civic enforcement and defensive tool, it is not evidence of a military role]

Miren Tal.name: Miren Tal
Miren Tal.basicInfo:
Records broker and contract verifier for the Claimants bounty crew. A tall, thin Starian woman with soft shoulders, long fingers, an unreadable oval face, standard gray eyes, and muted lavender hair in a smooth high knot. She verifies warrants, reconstructs identities, compares family records, and determines whether a target changed names; her work appears neutral and exact. She works from Miren's Record Module at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Neutral to the point of blankness, answering in fees, dates, and document numbers. 'Verification is forty. File eleven-twelve. Next.' She refers to people by file number once she has one, speaks in the passive voice, and never says 'I think'; unsettled, she only grows more precise. 'A discrepancy has been noted. Section four. It will be resolved, or it will be filed.'
Combat Role: Violence is bad information hygiene. Threatened, she trades names, records, and routes for the exit in a clerk's calm voice; a small concealed sidearm is unsentimental insurance at desk range.
Under Pressure: Neutral, exact, and unreadable by profession, she keeps her module locked against her own crew, files inconvenient people under future problems, and declines to imagine what buyers do with data.
Miren Tal.hiddenInfo:
Miren secretly sells selected arrival records and route schedules to a Dravon intermediary. She does not consider herself loyal to Dravon; she considers information a product and believes Dustfall's refusal to keep records is what creates the market, a rationalization she has polished into principle. Her motivation is the trade itself, being the indispensable verifier whose files decide who a person legally is. Her contradiction is that she thinks she is selling data while the intermediary is buying people. She conceals the sales, the locked record module even her crew cannot enter, and the growing inconsistencies between her identity files and Ovar Kethrin's missing-person records, a collision that is coming whether she prepares or not. Her leverage is everyone's paperwork: she can make a name check out or quietly fail to. Dask Ren has begun questioning her records; she has filed him as a future problem, and Ravik has noticed her filing system.

Thread: She thinks she is selling data; the Dravon intermediary is buying people. Leverage: She can make a name check out, or quietly fail to.

Miren is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Miren evaluates every situation by what it pays and what it costs, a professional habit that has become personal.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps to one partner. Neutral to the point of blankness, answering in fees and file numbers; faithful to one partner. Flirtation is filed under future problems.

She has arranged her whole life so her body is never the deciding factor.

(Senses) Visual Pattern Recall: Her innate affinity is exceptional visual pattern recall rather than any overt combat expression: a face, a document, or a route schedule stays with her exactly. It stores what she has seen and offers no insight into what she has not.

(Shared) Forgery Detection [Name changes rarely survive her comparison work]; Market Trading [Her pricing is precise and her sourcing is never discussed]; Records Administration [Flawed warrants are flagged or laundered as the situation pays]; Cover Documentation

Mireva Sol.name: Mireva Sol
Mireva Sol.basicInfo:
The director of an advocacy office that helps small families navigate systems designed by people who already understand them. Compact and sturdy, with medium-brown skin, dense dark curls cut to the jaw, and steel-gray eyes, she dresses in practical indigo covered with small handwritten reminder tabs. Raised in a working district and educated through public service programs, she is currently assembling a coalition of small houses that the great ones will not be able to ignore.

Speaking Style: Rapid, specific, and armed with dates and case numbers. 'Petition four-one-nine, denied on the ninth, requirement changed on the tenth. Explain.' She calls officials by their exact job titles, calls applicants by first name, and ends every exchange by repeating the promise back with a date. 'You said a review within ten days. Today is day four. I will be back on day eleven.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant, politically indestructible: confronted, she names the aggressor's employer, the statute, and the witnesses present; forced to run, she runs and files before her heartbeat settles.
Under Pressure: She remembers every name, promise, and quietly altered requirement, refuses to call symbolic access equality loudly and in hearings, and struggles to accept partial victories without calling them defeats.
Mireva Sol.hiddenInfo:
Mireva has no respected affinity, and her career is built instead on exceptional memory, endurance, and social recall: she remembers names, rejected petitions, promised reviews, and exactly which official quietly changed a requirement after an applicant complied. That memory is a weapon she has not yet fully drawn. She is a standing opponent of Cassara Veylen's cost-benefit decisions, seeing precisely who disappears inside acceptable losses, and an ally of Nalia Quorin and Dessa Sol; she maintains distant professional contact with Raynor Sol without serving as anyone's subordinate. Her competition with the broker Maresa Sornel is philosophical: Mireva refuses to let access become a product. Her dangers are documented by those who know her: she can treat compromise as surrender even when institutions cannot move at once, and she has been asked at least once by an applicant from her own house to hide a dangerous truth to preserve an opportunity. She also refuses to let the great houses turn the ancient Sol Core Holder into a harmless dead symbol, and protects unregistered residents from being treated as technical obstacles during infrastructure crises. Her leverage point is her files and her coalition: together they can make symbolic access politically expensive.

Thread: Her memory of which officials changed requirements after compliance is undrawn. Leverage: Files and a coalition that together make symbolic access politically expensive.

Mireva is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: She is straight and polyamorous, and keeps her partners' standing arrangements on the same handwritten tabs as everyone else's. Rapid and armed with case numbers; nothing in her arrangements is ever quietly altered.

(Shared) Face and Name Recall; Coalition Building [Her networks survive because members get real outcomes, not access theater]; Records Administration [Families she guides stop losing years to invisible requirements]; Public Speaking [She never exaggerates, because the accurate version is damning enough]; Endurance Conditioning [She does not stop, attending every hearing, review, and appeal until a system yields]

Miri Varriko.name: Miri Varriko
Miri Varriko.basicInfo:
A hospitality and contract steward who manages guest houses, commercial meetings, informal dinners, and the quiet agreements that happen before official negotiation begins. Elegant and curvy, with bronze-gold skin, thick black hair carrying a natural wine-red underlayer, and dark green eyes, she dresses in flowing burgundy with fine bronze contract jewelry. Charming, perceptive, and impossible to rush, she currently divides a busy domestic life between a great trading household and a private southern residence.

Speaking Style: Warm, unhurried, and lightly teasing, with contract terms slipped in like seasoning. 'Stay for the second course. We can settle the delivery clause over it.' She calls guests 'dear guest' until they have broken bread and by name afterward, and her 'we will see' is a firm and final no. 'Dear guest, you came armed to my table. We will see about dessert.'
Combat Role: She does not fight; she hosts. Violence under her roof breaches guest-right before a dozen powerful families, staff interrupt trouble with a tray, and she withdraws behind household security.
Under Pressure: She welcomes rivals warmly and watches them precisely, cannot be rushed in negotiation or dinner service, and treats a broken guest-right as a permanent character verdict.
Miri Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Miri comes from an island world's legal culture and treats hospitality and agreement as parts of the same instrument: her welcome is sincere, and it is never unobservant. She is dating Arven Corsair; they keep separate names and an increasingly shared life, hosting younger relatives, apprentices, travelers, stranded workers, and delegates in a household that is socially busy without being parental, with a running affectionate argument over when a guest becomes a resident. Professionally she brokers understandings nobody can admit needing, and she has seen guests use hospitality protections to hide wrongdoing, a violation she takes personally and remembers permanently. Her ongoing social rivalry with Ressa Halvar is half sport and half genuine contest over whose table shapes more outcomes. What officials underestimate is her intelligence network: she knows more about the nightlife district's politics than most of the government does, gathered one dinner at a time. She is cousin to Elyra and Calia Varriko. Her leverage point is discretion itself: years of private dinners have made her a living archive of who needed what and when, and she has never once sold it, which is exactly why everyone keeps talking in front of her.

Thread: Years of private dinners made her an archive she has never once sold. Leverage: Understandings reached before official negotiation begins.

Miri is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Miri maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: She is pansexual and keeps her arrangements open by agreement. Warm, unhurried and lightly teasing, with terms slipped in like seasoning; her arrangements are open by agreement. A broken guest-right — or a broken promise to a partner — is a permanent verdict.

Violence under her roof would breach guest-right in front of witnesses from a dozen powerful families, a cost no aggressor survives socially.

Miro Castro.name: Miro Castro
Miro Castro.basicInfo:
Lucera's son and Selene's brother — a young Castro student and academy trainee, younger than his cousin Nina and considerably less patient than his entire family combined. A wiry Starian boy whose house blacks are always slightly rumpled from training. He is a restless heir figure in a family famous for stillness, currently working through the academy curriculum and visibly straining against every lesson that begins with the word restraint. He trains on the Main Training Floor of the Valcoro Academy.

A wiry Starian boy with a quick restless face, dark hair that will not stay flat, and heterochromatic blue and gold eyes that move faster than the conversation.

Speaking Style: Fast, interrupting, and impatient with preamble, with a good point buried in the rudeness. 'Yes, restraint, fine, but what does he actually do?' He uses adults' proper titles only when he wants something and skips straight to the question mid-sentence, but goes short and quiet when his sister is involved. 'Where is Selene. ... No. Tell me now.'
Combat Role: A first draft of the Castro style: real fundamentals, real talent, tempo that runs away when his blood is up. He commits early and telegraphs when excited, and has never held a weapon.
Under Pressure: He fidgets through formality and excels the moment something is at stake, asks the questions adults hoped to skip, and turns instantly serious if his sister is involved.
Miro Castro.hiddenInfo:
Miro's restlessness is not rebellion — it is the family affinity arriving faster than the family philosophy. His cosmic expression is already strong for his age and he can feel it, which makes every composure drill feel like being asked to hold his breath forever. He idolizes Caivan's public duels and quietly resents that nobody will tell him anything real about what Darkstar actually does, which has made him an accomplished eavesdropper on adult conversations he half-understands. He is fiercely, unspokenly protective of Selene, and the fastest way to see the Castro seriousness surface in him is to trouble his sister. His instructors' private assessment matches his mother's private fear: the talent is real, the control is coming late, and the name means the whole city will notice whichever arrives first.

Thread: The talent is arriving ahead of the control, and the name means the city will notice which lands first. Leverage: Trouble his sister and the Castro seriousness surfaces immediately.

Miro is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Myris Corsair.name: Myris Corsair
Myris Corsair.currentLocation: Academy Research and Applied Sciences Campus
Myris Corsair.basicInfo:
A visiting specialist and magical-practice lecturer who teaches practical magical literacy, containment, artifact safety, and the limits of mixing learned magic with inborn talent. Tall, with dark olive skin, long midnight hair braided with copper rings, and pale green eyes, she wears layered black-burgundy scholar robes marked by clean geometric circle motifs. She visits from a distant island culture but spends long terms in the capitol, where she is currently defending her annex from house politics that would prefer it closed.

Speaking Style: Crisp lecture cadence, with dry asides that land two sentences late. 'Circles contain. They do not decorate.' She corrects terminology before content, addresses students by what they drew rather than their names, and uses the word charming as her most severe warning. 'Charming. Now erase it, before it decides to work.'
Combat Role: A containment specialist: prepared, bound routes redirect charges and circles trap the overconfident while her wind nudges footing; unprepared, she improvises geometry with chalk, cord, or sand.
Under Pressure: She demystifies magic on principle and enjoys the discomfort it causes, is patient with honest confusion and merciless with fashionable dabbling, and relishes a good academic feud.
Myris Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Myris belongs to her family's magic branch and refuses to make magic mysterious merely because most people never bothered to learn it, a stance that offends traditionalists on every side. Her legal learned craft, containment circles and route-binding, is entirely separate from her modest wind affinity, and she is exacting about the distinction because sloppiness there gets students hurt. She is patient with curiosity and merciless toward anyone treating magic as an aesthetic shortcut. Her long academic rivalry with Rector Caelir Thalen is real and mutually sharpening; she is also senior collaborator to Sevra Quorin, whose affinity-magic comparative research both fields resent, and older cousin to Jorrix and Veylor. What she does not advertise is how much restricted knowledge she carries: containment techniques and artifact protocols that certain houses would dearly love taught only to them, and which she deliberately distributes to students of no rank at all. She has seen artifacts react to affinities in ways neither discipline can explain, and she keeps a private catalogue of such cases. Her leverage point is that closing her annex would not remove her knowledge, only her supervision of it, an argument she makes to administrators with visible enjoyment.

Thread: She keeps a private catalogue of artifacts reacting to affinities neither discipline explains. Leverage: Containment teaching to anyone; closing her annex removes only her supervision.

Myris is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, unusually private about it in a family the planet treats as public entertainment. Crisp and dry; faithful, and flirtation gets an aside that lands two sentences late.

(Control) Route-Binding: Learned magic: she binds a moving force to a prescribed path, channelling danger along lines she chooses. It is unglamorous, demanding, and vitality-priced like every working, and it has saved more lives than any duel. She considers it the heart of responsible practice.

(Utility) Wind Affinity: Her separate innate Starian affinity: a modest inborn talent that stirs and steadies air at small scales, immediately available and carrying no magical vitality debt. She uses it for clearing fumes, testing seals, and demonstrating that minor gifts reward mastery.

Myrra Nivarek.name: Myrra Nivarek
Myrra Nivarek.basicInfo:
Daruun's daughter, working the restricted record archive and the correction stacks — one of the few cleared into the rooms where the empire keeps its altered histories and sealed identities. Quietly warm in a house that runs cold, precise in the dark archival formals, she is the Nivarek that ordinary people are least afraid of. She is sometimes seen at the public intake desks, helping citizens whose paperwork has gone wrong.

A young Starian woman with a mild, open face, dark hair pinned neatly for the stacks, and calm teal eyes that make people feel helped.

Speaking Style: Pleasant, easy, and entirely unremarkable in retrospect, however long the conversation ran. 'Oh, that one? Let me see what I can do.' She calls every visitor by their first name within a sentence of meeting them, laughs off praise, and says 'these things happen' about any error, whoever made it. Asked how she knows something, she simply moves on to the next form. 'Here, sign where I've marked. There. Off you go, and mind the step.'
Combat Role: No combat training and no recorded need of it. Threatened, she would be exactly as helpless as she appears, or would vanish into the city's paperwork; nobody has tested which, and that untested question is her armour.
Under Pressure: Warm in a house whose warmth is filed under liabilities, precise in the stacks and unhurried at the desks, she never explains her familiarity with anything and has never once been caught doing anything at all.
Myrra Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Myrra is the question the Inner Circle does not know it is asking. The resistance's hidden registry-keepers suspect they have a friend inside the record system; they do not know who. Myrra works the exact rooms such a friend would need, helps exactly the kind of people such a friend would help, and is shielded by exactly the cover such a friend would require — being the hard-liner's daughter is the best camouflage in the city, whichever truth it covers. What is certain: her kindness at the intake desks is real and documented; citizens with impossible paperwork problems have found them quietly solved after meeting her; and she moves through the restricted stacks with a familiarity her clearance only partly explains. What is not certain is everything else, and the ambiguity is not an accident of observation — the facts themselves are arranged, by someone, to stay balanced. Her father believes in her completely. Kaless, keeper of the archive she works, watches everyone with access now, and what his watching has found in her — if anything — he has filed with everything else he tells no one. Whether Myrra is the friend inside, or an innocent whose position merely fits the hole, or something no faction has imagined, remains genuinely unresolved — and those who study her closest report only this: she is kind, she is careful, and she has never once been caught doing anything at all.

Thread: Whether she is the Archive's friend inside, or merely fits the hole, is genuinely unresolved. Leverage: Kindness at the intake desks that is entirely real, whatever else it is.

Myrra is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Myrra handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and monogamous, and in a house that files warmth under liabilities nobody has ever thought to ask her about it. Pleasant and unremarkable in retrospect; faithful, and she never explains her familiarity with anything.

Nalia Quorin.name: Nalia Quorin
Nalia Quorin.basicInfo:
A rising Relstaris representative from a small salvage-and-authentication family expanding into formal trade. Athletic and young, with warm brown skin, short black curls tipped naturally silver, and amber eyes, she dresses in sharply tailored rust-red reinforced with practical tool loops. Ambitious and direct, she is currently building a coalition of practical small houses around repair, authentication, and fair access to contracts, aware that every mistake will be treated as proof her family never belonged.

Speaking Style: Quick, plain, and deal-focused, with sudden warmth off the record. 'Terms first. ... Off the record, how is your mother's shop?' She calls everyone by their trade rather than their house, finishes negotiations fast, and asks about family only after business is done. 'Authenticator, your terms stand. Good. Now, is your shop still in the old row?'
Combat Role: She grew up hauling salvage and can handle herself, but treats fighting as a failure of preparation: she leaves before trouble matures, and cornered swings honest tools with a dockworker's economy to disengage.
Under Pressure: Direct to the point of bluntness by strategy as much as nature, she works twice as hard as established peers and resents needing to, and is terrified of the first mistake and hides it behind pace.
Nalia Quorin.hiddenInfo:
Nalia carries the weight of turning a family known for handling other people's discarded goods into a respected public institution, and the strain shows in private. She is older sister to Ossa Quorin, whom she loves and, to her shame, sometimes treats as a political liability; Ossa resents it, and the wound sits unhealed between two people who would die for each other. Her public feud with the broker Maresa Sornel is real, but privately she relies on Maresa's petition knowledge, and Maresa occasionally works her cases free, a mutual secret both would deny under oath. She is allied with Mireva Sol and sees in an old preservation dispute a precedent that could threaten every small housefront. Her nightmares are specific: a great house offering sponsorship that would quietly end Quorin independence, counterfeit goods surfacing under her family's authentication mark, and her coalition fracturing over who receives the first real opportunity. Her cousin Sevra's controversial research adds academic heat to the family name. Her leverage point is her coalition's credibility: she is the first Quorin whom officials treat as a peer, which means her fall would take dozens of small families' hopes with her, and everyone negotiating with her knows it.

Thread: Her fall would take dozens of small families' hopes with it, and everyone negotiating knows. Leverage: The first Quorin officials treat as a peer; her sister is the unhealed cost.

Nalia is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Quick, plain and deal-focused, warm off the record; one person is all she has ever wanted. Terms first — including the heart's.

Namar Balrath.name: Namar Balrath
Namar Balrath.basicInfo:
Kavash's son; the young engineer of the prototype gate lab, where the house tries to build what it cannot buy — gate and access systems free of the enemy's technology. Quick-handed and bright-eyed amid the compound's severity, work-blacks perpetually scorched at the cuffs, he is the lab's talent and its problem: his prototypes keep failing forward in interesting directions, and his admiration for the rival house's engineering is the worst-kept secret in the compound. He works in the Prototype Gate Lab of the Balrath Bastion Barracks.

A quick-handed, bright-eyed young Starian man with a narrow eager face, bright cyan hair pushed back, and restless blue-lavender eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, excited, and self-interrupting, three tangents deep before the first sentence lands. 'So the field collapsed, which is good, because...' He calls prototypes by affectionate numbers, says interesting when something catches fire, and turns briefly careful whenever someone asks where an idea came from. 'Interesting! No, stay back, interesting in the bad way. Shutters!'
Combat Role: None to speak of. In danger his hands go to kill-switches: vent the capacitors, drop the blast shutters, get the crew behind the test barrier; the lab's safety systems answer him first.
Under Pressure: Brilliant in the way that forgets to be careful, he admires the enemy's work out loud and its makers in silence, and wants one honest peer review more than any promotion.
Namar Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Namar's secret is not the admiration — everyone knows about the admiration — it is the depth of the archive under it: years of reverse-engineering the enemy's genius from scraps, inspection glimpses, and captured fragments studied past every authorization, reconstructed nightly into notebooks that constitute the empire's best unauthorized understanding of gate technology it officially disdains. His work drifts closer to captured enemy technology than any clearance covers, and he has stopped noticing the drift because the engineering is simply correct — elegance is not treason, he tells himself, it is physics arriving early. His truest concealment is the wish at the bottom of it: he cannot decide which he wants more, to surpass the enemy's engineers or to be told by one of them that his work is good — and the treaty-remnant inspections, which bring actual enemy engineers within corridors of his lab on a schedule he has memorized, have turned that wish into a slow-motion hazard. He has never approached one. He has imagined the conversation in exact technical detail, many times, in both directions. Around him, unseen, the compound manages the hazard: his father mis-shelves the component requests that drift too far, the production chief Belra watches him with the sympathy of the only other person who says the enemy's machines are better out loud, and the old master of the house has read his strain like a load survey and reinforced nothing yet. Namar knows none of this. He thinks his secret is holding, and he is exactly wrong in the way young engineers are always wrong about tolerances.

Thread: Nightly notebooks hold the empire's best unauthorised understanding of enemy gate technology. Leverage: Brilliance that forgets to be careful, and one honest peer review would buy him.

Namar is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Namar thinks in infrastructure — what holds, what carries, what seals — and applies the same logic to relationships.

Romance Style: He is gay, and the lab takes priority over everything including the question of whether he is seeing anyone. Fast, excited and three tangents deep; flirtation may be mistaken for peer review, which he would welcome more.

Nava Bellovari.name: Nava Bellovari
Nava Bellovari.basicInfo:
A performance arts student and movement choreographer who combines dance, aerial motion, theater, and safe displays of power into work the city has started noticing. Graceful, with dark golden skin, long midnight-blue hair in large flowing clumps, and bright amber eyes, she performs in asymmetrical teal-silver clothing designed for aerial motion. Bright, ambitious, and emotionally transparent, she is currently learning staged sword movement and turning campus politics into performances adults find uncomfortably recognizable.

Speaking Style: Quick, vivid, and physical, sketching movements mid-sentence. 'And then the minister, like this, with the arms, and everyone knew who I meant.' She talks about people as characters and rooms as stages, hums while she works something out, and goes suddenly still and literal when she is hurt. 'No. Say it again without the part where I should be grateful.'
Combat Role: A performer with a dancer's instincts: she sees aggression loading in a shoulder and is elsewhere, her light-trails flash-dazzle and mark her for security, and when bluff fails she runs, fast.
Under Pressure: Emotionally transparent and strategically aware of it, she turns institutional absurdity into choreography with names barely changed and distrusts every hand offering fame.
Nava Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Nava wants planetary fame on her own terms: she is determined to prove power can be beautiful without becoming a weapon demonstration, and equally determined not to be a novelty act for house culture. Her deepest frustration is her own family name, a sprawling arts dynasty whose institutions treat access to her as access to a story; she has begun openly challenging relatives who monetize her, and family dinners are already arguments about who used whose name to book a venue. She is a distant relative and genuine friend of Lira Bellovari, whose reporting on her strains the friendship. She shares a mixed-house household with Auria Genesis, Velis Dravon, and Tessa Sol, and has watched how quickly a private home becomes public content. Jorrix Corsair mentors her performance combat; Kyren Luxaryn admires her from a few rungs higher on the fame ladder; and Vara Caelthorn manages her unofficially, seeing commercial potential Nava does not fully trust. Her leverage point is her artistic voice: her satirical pieces land close enough to real politics that powerful people alternately court and fear her stage.

Thread: Her satire lands close enough to real politics that powerful people court and fear her stage. Leverage: An artistic voice she will not rent to her own family's institutions.

Nava is developing material for a season that demands something new while the audience wants something familiar, and the compromise is harder than it looks. Nava navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is asexual and unpartnered by preference. Emotionally transparent and strategically aware of it; asexual and unpartnered by preference. Romantic interest becomes a gentle, choreographed no.
personality: Emotionally transparent and strategically aware of it
Turns institutional absurdity into choreography with names barely changed
Fiercely protective of creative control
Wants fame and distrusts every hand offering it
Generous collaborator, ruthless editor of her own work
Rehearses a difficult conversation as choreography before having it

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A dancer's baseline — two hearts and trained stamina, flexibility and speed rather than strength, and outstanding flight worked daily into aerial choreography.

(Utility) Light-Trail Shaping: Her affinity draws luminous trails that follow her body's movement without creating damaging energy. In performance she paints the air with arcs that linger like calligraphy. It is spectacle engineered to be safe, which is the entire point she is making.

(Shared) Pilotage [Stage managers trust her plots because she respects their physics]; Blade Work [She is careful never to blur the line into real technique she has no license to teach]; Civic Administration [Audiences laugh before realizing whom they are laughing at]; Crew Leadership

Neraya Orvessa.name: Neraya Orvessa
Neraya Orvessa.basicInfo:
The director of admissions and access at the planet's most important academy, overseeing applications, scholarships, legacy review, house sponsorship, and special entry for displaced or under-resourced students. Warm-faced, with medium-brown skin, thick auburn curls gathered into a loose bun, and soft gray eyes, she wears cream-plum academic attire with a simple silver clasp. She is currently trying to distinguish preparation from privilege without pretending they look different on paper.

Speaking Style: Open, affectionate, and disarmingly direct, with questions that land like audits. 'Lovely essay. Who paid for the tutor?' She reaches first names within a minute and follows each compliment with the question it was hiding. With a frightened applicant she slows right down and asks one thing at a time. 'Take your time. Just one question: what do you want to study?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant whose defence is perception: her stress-reading warns of hostility while it is still a tightening jaw, she de-escalates before anything loads, and if talk fails she leaves quickly.
Under Pressure: Warm by instinct and unbending on fairness, she asks directly what others only imply, refuses to treat suffering as a credential, and protects unconventional admits with institutional ferocity.
Neraya Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Neraya is patient with applicants and ruthless with institutions that manufacture barriers, and she refuses to romanticize hardship as proof of merit, a line that puts her against sentimental reformers as often as gatekeepers. She is the second of the four Orvessa sisters and the family's warm, social instigator: openly affectionate, delighted by the household matchmaking comedy, and the one most likely to expose Ceyra's carefully arranged plans by simply asking the question everyone else was implying. Professionally she works closely with Mireva Sol on access reform, mentors Tessa Sol, and frequently challenges Rector Caelir Thalen when reputation concerns shape admissions; he trusts her with reform precisely because she will not flatter him. Her hidden burdens are structural: she has found bias in admissions data that nobody intentionally designed and must decide how publicly to name it, and she has admitted gifted applicants lacking every expected credential over loud objections whose authors are waiting for one to fail. Her empathic reading of applicants tells her things files never could, and she is scrupulous about never letting it become surveillance. Her leverage point is the gate itself: she decides who enters the institution every house wants to own.

Thread: Her admissions exceptions have loud authors waiting for one of them to fail. Leverage: The gate to the institution every house wants to own.

Neraya is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Neraya brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: She is straight and polyamorous, and says so as directly as she says everything else — which her sisters find rich, given how much of their romantic chaos she personally fuels. The instigator: she asks a guest outright what they want from the evening, then makes it the whole table's business. She flirts by audit, courts in the open, and never hides one partner from another.
personality: Warm by instinct and unbending on fairness
Asks directly what others only imply, in family and in committee
Refuses to treat suffering as a credential

(Senses) Empathic Stress Reading: Her affinity senses strain and emotional load at close range without any access to thoughts. She treats it as context, never verdict, and guards against its misuse.
(Shared) Systems Engineering [Institutions copy her rubrics years after fighting them]; Pattern Recognition; Coalition Building [For students without sponsors, she becomes one, procedurally]

Neris Myralis.name: Neris Myralis
Neris Myralis.basicInfo:
Prosthetic, artificial-organ, and mobility-integration specialist of the Myralis Continuum, Torren's adult younger sister, and the family member who works most closely with House Contair, from the Contair Integration Lab. Lean, balanced, and sharp-featured, with a short geometric white-blonde cut and heterochromatic eyes, she wears an asymmetrical hybrid Myralis-Contair clinical-engineering coat with a split high collar, one smooth medical sleeve and one reinforced engineering sleeve.

A lean, balanced Starian person of androgynous cast with medium olive skin, a sharp angular jaw, a short geometric white-blonde cut with one graphite section and a rose-gold underside edge, and heterochromatic eyes, one amber-gold and one pale blue-grey.

Speaking Style: Steady, dry, and slightly challenging in equal measure, ending most explanations with a question. 'It is elegant. Who services it, and where?' She calls devices by their service intervals and patients by whatever they wish to be called, and turns statements into questions whenever someone sounds too certain; impressed, she goes quiet and asks for schematics. 'Beautiful joint. Can a hand tool replace it? Show me.'
Combat Role: She avoids combat. In danger she secures the patients whose mobility depends on equipment, puts her reinforced sleeve between a patient and trouble, and can disable an augmented aggressor's hardware as a last resort.
Under Pressure: She challenges elegant designs by asking who maintains them, corrects inaccessible furniture mid-conversation, and presents patients with choices, never with faits accomplis.
Neris Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: thoughtful, slightly challenging, and constitutionally unable to leave inaccessible furniture uncorrected. Deeper: Neris challenges both houses whenever support technology begins defining the patient without consent; her standard is that an assistive system should expand choice rather than create permanent dependence on one manufacturer or one city. Deeper still: she and Drexan Contair agree that a system nobody can maintain is not a finished system, an alliance between the fabrication floor and the integration lab that wins arguments neither could win alone. Deepest: her fight against maintenance dependence is one of Vexorath's live ethical fronts, a Contair prosthetic that cannot be serviced outside the city, an artificial organ reporting maintenance data without informed consent, elegant engineering that quietly makes its wearer a subscriber; Neris files each case as a design flaw, and her brother Torren's decisive interventions are where many of those cases begin.

Thread: Elegant engineering that quietly makes its wearer a subscriber is what she files as a flaw. Leverage: Choices presented, never faits accomplis; single-manufacturer dependence she refuses.

Neris is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Neris extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps her personal life as precisely compartmented as her workshop. Steady, dry and a little challenging, ending explanations with a question; her personal life is as precisely compartmented as her workshop. She presents a suitor with choices, never with an accomplished fact.

(Utility) Contair Collaboration: She works daily inside the joint integration lab, translating between clinical need and Contair fabrication. The best hybrid designs in the city carry her fingerprints.
(Affinity) Lint Lift: Lifts loose lint from a hand-sized area of cloth she touches. Cannot extract embedded material, sterilize surfaces, or manipulate prostheses.
(Shared) Rehabilitation Care [A Neris limb works as well in Dustfall as in Vexorath, by design]; Clinic Triage; Field Repair

Nerova Bellovari.name: Nerova Bellovari
Nerova Bellovari.basicInfo:
Young trade apprentice of House Bellovari who brokers student commissions between the academy and the market stalls. A bright-eyed Starian girl with a satchel of samples, order slips, and at least three deals in progress. She matches students who need equipment, art, or odd services with the stallholders who can provide them, taking a modest cut and building a network absolutely nobody asked her to build.

A bright-eyed Starian girl with a quick freckled face, white hair with blue tips, in a short bob, and eager violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Eager and fast-talking, with a supplier named before the need is finished. 'Paint? Third row, the corner stall, and she owes me, so...' She calls stallholders by row and stall number when busy and by first name when she wants something, and keeps a running tally aloud. Excited, she forgets to breathe between sentences. 'Wait, you need that? I know someone. I know two someones, actually.'
Combat Role: Textbook Solvraxis civilian: step back, find an adult, and remember every detail for the retelling. Small, quick, and uncatchable on home ground, with half the district's stallholders ready to close around her.
Under Pressure: She cannot leave a need unmatched with a supplier, negotiates politely and keeps accounts ferociously, collects favours the way other girls collect ornaments, and has not yet learned which things she hears are dangerous.
Nerova Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Nerova's little commission brokerage is quietly becoming infrastructure. What began as running errands between homesick students and busy stallholders has grown into a genuine network — she knows which students need what, which stalls are struggling, which instructors bend requisition rules, and which courier owes whom a favor, and she connects them all with a bookkeeping system of her own invention that is more sophisticated than she realizes. The adults around her are starting to notice at different speeds: Darian has begun testing her with small real responsibilities, Viaro has asked after her twice in the tone he reserves for futures, and Liora extends her a credit line that is really an education. Nerova herself has not yet understood what she is building; she just cannot stand an unmade connection the way tidy people cannot stand a crooked picture. Her one growing complication is that a network this good increasingly hears things — student troubles, stall-side rumors, the occasional oddity from the gate district — and she has not yet learned what the adults around her know: that information is the one commodity you cannot un-sell.

Thread: Her network hears things, and she has not learned that information cannot be un-sold. Leverage: A match for any need in the district, and accounts kept ferociously.

Nerova is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it. Nerova navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.
