(Affinity) Glitter Turn: Turns loose decorative flakes in her palm so they catch existing light together; generates no light and controls no metal equipment.

(Shared) Trade Negotiation [Her cut is modest and her repeat business is not]; Information Brokerage; Institutional Memory [Written records exist as backup for a memory that rarely needs them]; Courier Work

Nessa Halessin.name: Nessa Halessin
Nessa Halessin.basicInfo:
Maeron's younger sister, mid-forties, the family's fine-work specialist, who grinds lenses, cuts glass, and executes the delicate finishing the workshop's better commissions require. A dry, exacting Starian woman with a magnifier pushed up on her forehead and fingertips polished smooth by abrasive. She does the work that cannot be hurried, and comments freely on work that was. She works the fine bench at the Halessin Workshop in the Red Forges.

A dry, exacting Starian woman in her mid-forties with a narrow composed face, lavender-pink hair pinned tight under a headscarf, and golden eyes that stay half-narrowed.

Speaking Style: Dry, flat, and sparing, with a correction offered once and the magnifier already coming down. 'Rushed. Again.' She says 'Maeron' in full when displeased and uses no nicknames for anyone, speaks in measurements, and treats silence as her strongest criticism. 'Two hairs off true. Do it again. ... Better.'
Combat Role: Cutting tools within reach, and precise knowledge of how glass breaks and where the shards go. She avoids violence as a contamination of controlled conditions and defends the finished work before herself.
Under Pressure: Precise in craft and in blame, she tests claims instead of arguing them, is patient with glass and impatient with excuses, and keeps her conclusions until they are unanswerable.
Nessa Halessin.hiddenInfo:
Nessa believes the great commission failed because Maeron bought cheaper frit to pad the family's margins, changing the glass's behavior in the anneal. She has said nothing directly. Instead she has been running quiet tests, small batches from the suspect stock against their old standard, ring, expansion, and fracture, building an evidence trail her brother cannot argue with. She has also noticed the night work and the missing materials. She is letting him exhaust himself a little longer, partly from tactics, partly from a sister's anger she is not proud of.

Thread: She is building an evidence trail that the cheap frit caused the failure, and letting him exhaust himself first. Leverage: Tests instead of arguments, and conclusions kept until unanswerable. Combat Role: Cutting tools within reach, and precise knowledge of how glass breaks.

Nessa is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: She is straight and holds more than one relationship at once. Dry, flat and sparing, holding more than one relationship at once with every partner told plainly. She tests a feeling instead of arguing it, and keeps her conclusions until they are unanswerable.

(Shared) Fine Craftwork [Flaws that survive to her bench do not survive it]; Material Assessment [When she finally presents a conclusion it will not be an opinion]; Endurance Conditioning [She sustains fine, ruinously exacting work for hours without degradation]

Nexis Contair.name: Nexis Contair
Nexis Contair.currentLocation: Academy Research and Applied Sciences Campus
Nexis Contair.basicInfo:
The director of applied systems research, leading projects in civic infrastructure, training environments, accessibility, and campus systems. Slim and pale-brown, with dark cobalt hair in angular upward clumps and striking blue-white eyes, he wears clean white-charcoal research clothing with modular tool panels. Brilliant and impatient, he is currently rejecting a string of flashy prototypes on the grounds that nothing counts as progress until it survives ordinary maintenance.

Speaking Style: Rapid, clipped, and diagram-first, softening only when a student is genuinely stuck. 'No. Draw it. ... All right, show me where it fails.' He refers to devices by their failure point, answers praise with a maintenance question, and when truly impressed says only that it will do. 'It will do. Leave it running a month and bring me what broke.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant who controls the environment he built: doors sealed, lifts killed, an intruder routed into a monitored dead end from his console. Outside his facilities he is unremarkable and avoids exposure.
Under Pressure: He rejects any design that cannot be repaired by ordinary hands, is impatient with ceremony and secretly attentive to people, uses rivalry as mentorship, and distrusts grants that arrive too easily.
Nexis Contair.hiddenInfo:
Nexis is more socially aware than he pretends, using impatience as armor against the politics that infest research funding. He is a junior relative of Varis and Talris Contair, supervised by Talris during capitol work and living in the long shadow of a family that defines technical excellence for the planet; his insistence that everything be repairable outside his house's home city is partly principle and partly rebellion. His mentor-rivalry with the independent student Cael Dorrin is the most productive relationship he will not admit to valuing: Cael's scrapyard genius keeps disproving Nexis's assumptions about what qualified talent looks like. He collaborates uneasily with Sevra Quorin, wanting cleaner variables than living students provide, endures Sela Thovex's usability criticism as a frequent and deserving target, and has had his research assumptions formally challenged by the ethicist Caelia Myralis. His quiet dreads are documented: political pressure hiding inside research grants, and the possibility that his own wing has concealed its mistakes the way institutions do. His leverage point is authorship: half the city's next-generation civic systems pass through his approval, and he cannot be flattered, only convinced.

Thread: He dreads that his own wing has concealed its mistakes the way institutions do. Leverage: Approval for half the city's next civic systems; he cannot be flattered, only convinced.

Nexis is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Nexis applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: He is straight and seeking no one at present. Rapid, clipped and seeking no one at present; secretly attentive to people despite himself. Flirtation gets 'No. Draw it,' and then, softening, a better question.

Outside them he is unremarkable and knows it, so he avoids exposure, travels scheduled routes, and keeps security protocols he personally audited.

(Senses) Machine-State Visualization: His affinity renders the internal condition of systems as perceivable structure, with limited remote calibration. He can watch a mechanism's health the way others watch weather. Faults appear to him before they appear as failures.

(Shared) Archive Search [He kills beloved projects that cannot be maintained and defends unglamorous ones that can]; Failure Forensics [Given a failed or suspicious device, he reconstructs its design decisions and their motives]; Systems Engineering [Institutions adopt his standards after their elegant systems strand them once]; Contract Reading [Sponsors find him infuriating and keep sponsoring him]

Neyra Vey.name: Neyra Vey
Neyra Vey.basicInfo:
Pilot and rapid extraction specialist of the Bent Halo. A compact athletic Starian woman with strong shoulders, a sharp heart-shaped face, amber eyes, and dark cobalt-blue hair in an asymmetrical short cut, longer over one eye. She flies smuggling runs and emergency extractions from a hidden landing shelf, impatient, funny, and excellent under pressure. She flies from the Bent Dock at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Fast, profane, and cockpit-clipped, switching to flat numbers the instant the flying gets real. 'Strap in, shut up. Forty seconds. Thirty.' She calls everyone 'cargo' until they prove otherwise and her transport 'the old girl', jokes hardest when frightened, and stops joking the second she starts counting. 'Relax, cargo. The old girl has landed on worse. Probably.'
Combat Role: A pilot's fight: speed, angles, and machinery over muscle. She keeps moving, strikes from turns, stays upright through hits that should drop her, and her real weapon is the transport's wash, bulk, and exits.
Under Pressure: Impatient everywhere except the pilot's seat, funniest when the situation is worst, openly hostile to anyone who calls her landing unsafe, and she chooses passengers over cargo without hesitating.
Neyra Vey.hiddenInfo:
Neyra once flew legitimate contract routes and lost her license after refusing to surrender passengers during a politically convenient inspection; she tells the story differently depending on how much she likes the listener, and the true version is the one she tells least. Her motivation is simple and absolute: passengers over cargo, every time, which is why she flies for Saevik instead of anyone respectable. She conceals which parts of the license story are hers and which failures she carries from it. Her leverage is that she is the extraction pilot people pray for and the only one who lands where the Bent Halo lands. She maintains a professional rivalry with Veyra Corsair, an openly hostile one with any pilot who calls her landing shelf unsafe, and she sleeps aboard the crew's transport more often than in town.

Thread: The true version of the license story is the one she tells least often. Leverage: The only pilot who lands where the Bent Halo lands; passengers over cargo, always.

Neyra is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Neyra holds the network's rule that information flows up and favours flow down, and has learned which favours cost more than they look.

Romance Style: She is straight and her relationships are open by arrangement. Fast, profane and funniest when things are worst; her relationships are open by arrangement. She chooses people over cargo without hesitating, and says exactly how long she is staying.

She is one of the better unaided fliers in the settlement and never mentions it.

(Movement) Kinetic Balance: Her innate affinity holds her own kinetic balance through sudden turns, impacts, and violent landings, and steadies what she is bracing against. Maneuvers that should shake a craft apart come out level under her hands, and hits that should drop her leave her upright.

Nira Drathen.name: Nira Drathen
Nira Drathen.basicInfo:
Kael's daughter, mid-twenties, the Drathen smithy's second smith and its actual fine-work specialist. A forge-shouldered Starian young woman with burn-speckled forearms, bright green hair in a messy bun, and her father's habit of testing every edge on a thumbnail. Customers see her striking for her father and assume apprentice; the work that leaves the shop under his mark increasingly says otherwise. She is found at the Bracket Supply Market on the Commerce Layer when she is not at the forge.

A forge-shouldered young Starian woman in her mid-twenties with burn-speckled forearms, bright green hair in a messy bun, a square practical face, and steady violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Blunt and unvarnished with everyone except her father, where it goes quiet and careful. 'That edge is wrong. ... Da, maybe let me take the springs tonight.' She talks to metal as much as to customers, calls her father 'Da' only in the shop, and swallows a sentence halfway whenever a customer praises his work. 'Your spring's tempered right. He did good... the shop did good.'
Combat Role: One economical committed blow like her father's, faster and lower, from a smaller frame trained around leverage. She protects her hands above all and lets standing quietly at a forge with iron in hand end most confrontations.
Under Pressure: She does the work, cedes the credit, and keeps the score; gentle with her father's pride and tired of being gentle, perfectionist at night, deferential by day, and angry in between.
Nira Drathen.hiddenInfo:
Nira does the fine work now, the springs, the tempering, the precision fitting, at night, unacknowledged, stamped with her father's mark. She protects his pride and his name because she loves him and because the name feeds them both. But she is mid-twenties, better at close work than he ever was, and building a master's portfolio credited entirely to another smith. She has begun making small pieces with her own private mark, hidden in a box under her bench, and the box is filling. What she wants is for him to say it first. She is losing faith that he ever will.

Thread: A box of pieces under her bench carries her own private mark, and it is filling. Leverage: The fine work the smithy's reputation rests on; she wants him to say it first. Combat Role: One economical blow, faster and lower than his. She protects her hands above all.

Nira is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and committed to one person. Blunt with everyone but her father; asexual and committed to one person, whose name lives in the private box she opens when the shop is empty. Flirtation gets 'That edge is wrong.'

(Senses) Edge True: Her modest innate affinity lets her feel a blade's edge alignment and temper through her fingertips, reading straightness and hardness like braille. Her sharpening and tempering are uncanny. It is a finer expression than her father's heat-sense and entirely her own.

Nyra Sorel.name: Nyra Sorel
Nyra Sorel.basicInfo:
Information broker and route seller claiming descent from a house destroyed under Dravon expansion; the claim is unverified. An adult Starian woman with an intentionally average build, a pleasant oval face designed by habit to be forgotten, silver-gray eyes, and honey-brown hair with one bright cyan streak near the left side. She sells safe routes, family information, checkpoint schedules, and identities from a quiet corner of the settlement's covert bar. She keeps the Quiet Refugee Corner of Black Dust.

Speaking Style: Pleasant, practised, and slightly different each time, adjusting to whatever the listener wants true. 'My family had land near there. Which route do you need?' She mirrors the accent and pace of whoever sits across from her, never asks a buyer's name, and answers personal questions with prices. 'No names, dear. Tell me where you need to be, and by when.'
Combat Role: Her whole doctrine is not being there when it starts: she sits near exits and leaves at the first tonal shift; cornered, she trades a route or a name, and the hold-out weapon is a prop.
Under Pressure: Pleasant, forgettable, and rehearsed at both, she sells hope and payment plans in the same breath, demonstrates her affinity only when it cannot be checked, and catalogues every exit.
Nyra Sorel.hiddenInfo:
No surviving record fully confirms House Sorel existed in the form Nyra describes, and the sharpest question about her, the one Tessik Luxaryn keeps open, is whether invented identity becomes real after enough years, because Nyra sometimes believes her own stories. Her motivation is survival upgraded to craft: the persona is her product, her armor, and possibly by now her self. Her contradiction is that some of her information saves lives while some routes desperate people into debts they cannot escape, and she declines to track which. She conceals whatever her original identity was, the inconsistencies between her account and Ovar Kethrin's records, and the unreliability of her claimed static-sense affinity, whose demonstrations are conveniently inconsistent. Her leverage is her inventory: checkpoint schedules, family locations, purchasable names. Selka Vaereth distrusts her; Tessik finds her useful and dangerous in equal measure, which in his reckoning is a compliment.

Thread: Whether an invented identity becomes real after enough years is a question she sometimes loses. Leverage: Checkpoint schedules, family locations, purchasable names — priced to the buyer's need.

Nyra is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and steady with one person. Pleasant, forgettable and slightly different each time; steady with one person, the only one who hears the same backstory twice. Flirtation gets whatever version the listener wants to be true, and no invitation.

Keeps every exit in the room catalogued mid-conversation
Stirs her drink without ever finishing it, so she can leave at any moment
Remembers every buyer's face and makes a show of forgetting it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A deliberately average baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience in a build she keeps unremarkable on purpose, no training, and plain flight she uses only to leave.

(Senses) Claimed Static Sense: She claims an innate static sense that detects active surveillance, and her demonstrations are inconsistent. Whether the affinity is real, unreliable, or entirely sales technique is unresolved.

(Shared) Route Reading [Which ones fail, and for whom, follows no visible pattern]; Market Trading [Buyers rarely ask where identities come from, which suits everyone]; Stealth and Concealment [Witnesses describe her differently or not at all]; Information Brokerage [Even her fabrications contain enough fact to be dangerous]

Odrin Kathvar.name: Odrin Kathvar
Odrin Kathvar.basicInfo:
Elder brother to Jorek and Karessa, uncle to their children, and House Kathvar's senior civil-service trainer. A composed Starian man in a formal black civic uniform. He trains and mentors outer-ring administrative personnel in correct procedure, documentation standards, safe public processing, escalation boundaries, and how to implement a standing decision without creating avoidable failures. He yielded the headship of the House to Jorek, is comfortable serving without being head of the House, and shows no apparent grievance about it.

A composed Starian man of quiet middle age with a lined, patient face, brown hair kept short, and mild blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Gentle, unhurried, and question-led; advice as questions, never as an order. 'And what does the form do for the person holding it?' He calls trainees by first name and asks them what the form is for, not what it says. He never gives a direct order, only questions until the answer is clear. 'And if the holder cannot read it, who carries the mistake?'
Combat Role: No combat capability is established. If a room turns he moves his trainees behind him and toward the door, keeps talking in the same gentle voice, and leaves the rest to escort.
Under Pressure: He watches procedure with an intensity that reads as fussiness because mistakes land on real people, and treats the young with a courtesy that has something older underneath it.
Odrin Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
He yielded the headship to Jorek not from weakness but from self-knowledge: he saw what leading a house required and recognized it as something he would do competently and hate completely. The courtesy he shows the young has something older underneath it — the memory of his own early mistakes, which cost someone whose name he does not volunteer. He mentors Dalan with particular care because he sees in the boy the same earnest proceduralism he once mistook for wisdom, and the same blindness to when procedure becomes a hiding place. His peace as second is genuine but not simple; it was earned by understanding what first would have cost everyone around him. Connections: elder brother of Jorek, head of House Kathvar, and of Karessa; uncle of Bralen, Sora, Thessan, Dalan, and Veyra; Dalan's mentor.

Thread: He is more at peace as second than he ever was as heir, and says so to nobody. Leverage: Advice given as questions, and a courtesy with something older underneath it.

Odrin is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Odrin has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps more than one partner. Gentle, question-led and more at peace as second than as heir; he keeps more than one partner, openly and courteously. Advice comes as questions; so do his feelings.

Treats the young with a courtesy that has something older underneath it
Prefers teaching to authority
More at peace as second than he ever was as heir
Reviews every trainee's first case himself, sitting beside them
Asks one quiet follow-up question after training ends
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts, with the edge in recovery and survivability that every Starian has. Flight is universal to Starians; Odrin's individual flight proficiency is not separately established in active canon.

(Senses) Response Read: It is material response, not prophecy: it is not foresight and it does not guarantee the outcome of every possible impact. Jorek finds existing seams and faults; Odrin reads response to applied force.

(Support) Mentorship of Dalan: He is an especially important mentor to his nephew Dalan, who is still learning the judgment Odrin is trying to teach him: when strict procedure needs escalation rather than improvisation. He treats the young with a courtesy that has something older underneath it.
(Shared) Teaching Craft

Olen Ravello.name: Olen Ravello
Olen Ravello.basicInfo:
A food critic, cultural essayist, and public historian of dining who writes about food as history, migration, class, and cultural ownership. Thin and older, with dark olive skin, silver-black hair worn long at the sides, and pale blue eyes, he dresses in elegant cream-black with a small tasting notebook always visible. Brilliant, funny, and occasionally cruel, he is currently reckoning with the aftermath of a short review that made an unknown night cook suddenly, dangerously famous.

Speaking Style: Essayistic and epigrammatic, delivering verdicts like dessert courses. 'The broth was honest. The room was not.' He speaks in balanced pairs, praise then correction, calls chefs by their dishes, and when truly moved stops being clever and says one plain word. 'The bread apologised for the soup. ... Good. Just good.'
Combat Role: Rhetorical only. He dines in full view on predictable routes, makes an aggressor ridiculous before witnesses, and failing that hands over his coat, keeps his notebook, and writes the incident into permanence.
Under Pressure: Honest even when honesty is a demolition, he treats a meal as a historical document, is funny in print and cruel only on purpose, and is immune to flattery and dangerously susceptible to a perfect broth.
Olen Ravello.hiddenInfo:
Olen can make a family restaurant famous or destroy it, and he insists influence is not the same as responsibility, a position he is slowly losing faith in as he watches true reviews create unjust outcomes. His early support of Rin Sol was honest admiration; the feeding frenzy it triggered, patrons claiming discovery, prestige kitchens circling, is the clearest evidence yet against his own doctrine. He is a professional antagonist of the celebrity chef Hessan Luxaryn, whose empire he reviews harshly and whose staff turnover he documents, and he is unwelcome in several great families' dining rooms for essays on cultural theft they could not refute. He and Daelor Ravello are long-term partners from broad shared lineage without close kinship: Daelor prioritizes historical accuracy while Olen understands that public memory follows the most compelling version, and their affectionate arguments about truth and presentation exhaust nearby listeners. In the growing controversy over the ancient Sol Core Holder, Olen's role is exactly that tension: he knows accuracy without a compelling public story may change nothing. His leverage point is his pen: bribes of access rather than money keep arriving, and every one he refuses becomes material.

Thread: The frenzy around Rin Sol is the clearest evidence yet against his own doctrine. Leverage: A pen that makes or ends a kitchen; every refused bribe becomes material.

Olen is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Olen keeps records of everything and trusts the archive more than memory, a habit that makes them thorough and occasionally inflexible.

Romance Style: He is gay and monogamous, the long-term partner of Daelor Ravello. Essayistic and honest even when honesty is a demolition; he reviews nothing about Daelor in public and stays entirely faithful. Immune to flattery, dangerously susceptible to a perfect broth.
personality: Honest even when honesty is a demolition
Treats a meal as a historical document
Funny in print, funnier in person, cruel only on purpose
Increasingly haunted by the collateral damage of true reviews
Immune to flattery, dangerously susceptible to a perfect broth
Writes in his tasting notebook during the meal, never after, and never aloud
Pays his own bill at every table and sends back any course sent out free
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An aging essayist's baseline — two hearts and thin, unexercised resilience, no strength or training, and flight he no longer bothers with. His only combat is rhetorical; confronted, he deploys wit and then hands over his coat.

(Senses) Taste-Linked Memory: His affinity connects flavors to past experiences with imperfect emotional accuracy. One spoonful can summon a kitchen from decades ago, its cook, and roughly how it felt. He mistrusts the emotions and trusts the flavors absolutely.

(Shared) Archive Search [Restaurateurs read him the way politicians read polls / Cultural theft cases cite his essays as evidence]; Verbatim Recall [Kitchens cannot perform for him because the food testifies]; Civic Administration

Oren Veyth.name: Oren Veyth
Oren Veyth.basicInfo:
Malkor and Thessa's son, mid-twenties, House Veyth's junior clerk and its presumptive heir. A conscientious Starian young man with his father's straight back not yet fully earned, working his way through the archive one filing season at a time. He believes in the house's purpose more simply than anyone, which is either its future or its coming disappointment. He files at the Veyth Notary in Solvraxis, at the junior desk.

A conscientious young Starian man in his mid-twenties with his father's straight back not yet fully earned, a serious open face, neat dark hair, and green eyes that give him away.

Speaking Style: Careful, slightly formal, and easy to read, with the pauses giving away everything he withholds. 'The archive is... in order. Yes. All of it.' He says sir to his father at work and apologises before objecting to anything, and his lies all begin with I was just. When the archive is threatened, the pauses vanish. 'No. Put that back. You may not touch that shelf.'
Combat Role: A bookish boy's fistfights, few and lost. Under threat he blocks, backs away, and takes hits on his forearms until help or an exit appears; reach for the archive shelves and he does not back away at all.
Under Pressure: Earnest in a family of the carefully guarded, he works before dawn and lies badly about why, reveres his father and has begun quietly to disobey him, and is steadier under pressure than anyone realises.
Oren Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Oren has been secretly duplicating the archive, record by record in his own hand, and caching the copies away from the house. No one authorized it; his father would treat unauthorized copies as a violation of custodial trust, the house's one absolute rule. Oren started after noticing his uncle Edran lingering in the archive's oldest section, and continued out of a colder thought he cannot shake: a house whose substance can burn in one night has no substance at all. He is protecting the archive by betraying its first principle, and he knows both halves of that sentence are true.

Thread: He is secretly duplicating the archive and caching it, betraying its first principle to protect it. Leverage: A clerk's whole access, and an earnestness that gives him away every time.

Oren is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Oren manages household affairs with quiet competence and notices when others mistake competence for simplicity.

Romance Style: He is straight and seeking no one at present. Earnest, easy to read and seeking no one at present; the pauses give away everything he withholds. Flirtation flusters him into perfect honesty.

Rereads every file he closes, once, before he shelves it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A junior clerk's baseline in his mid-twenties — two hearts and ordinary resilience, young and quick but entirely unskilled, and plain flight. He blocks, backs away, and takes hits on his forearms until help or an exit appears.

(Senses) Hand Comparison: His modest innate affinity compares physical writing. It does not name the writer, reproduce a hand, grant recall of any kind, or tell him what a document says. It detects authorship consistency; it does not enable forgery.

(Shared) Records Administration [His work needs no correction, which in this family is the only compliment that exists]; Archive Search [He is the third living person who truly knows the archive's arrangement, after Malkor and Edran]; Endurance Conditioning [Everyone has noticed, no one has connected it to the hours he claims to sleep]; Client Handling [Clients like him]

Orenik Sol.name: Orenik Sol
Orenik Sol.basicInfo:
Enforcer of the Iron Jackals and a neighborhood defender with criminal strings attached. A short, compact Starian man with a thick neck, dense muscular build, dark brown hair shaved close, and pale gray eyes, his face rounder than most Dustfall gunfighters. He collects debts, breaks up fights, escorts vulnerable residents, and makes sure people understand when Kaedra has stopped negotiating. He keeps Orenik's Training Corner on Refit Row.

Speaking Style: Flat, short, and diminishing; the worse a situation gets, the less he says. 'She is done talking. So am I.' He says a person's name once, as a warning, and never repeats a threat, only a location. With the residents he escorts he talks more, mostly about small things. 'Mind the step. ... Nobody bothers you tonight. I will be at the corner.'
Combat Role: An infighter who wins by density and position: he crowds taller opponents, takes the arm or the weapon hand, and drives them into surfaces. He carries a sidearm and draws it rarely, and fights without anger.
Under Pressure: He enforces without cruelty and without apology, keeps one rule and breaks orders before he breaks it, escorts the vulnerable off the clock, and lets his presence do the first round of talking.
Orenik Sol.hiddenInfo:
Orenik joined the Jackals after formal defense work repeatedly passed him over, the Sol underclass story in one career. His contradiction is that he is a feared collector with a strict private rule: never children, medicine, or housing as leverage, and he has refused orders that crossed it. His motivation is being useful in the only work that would finally have him. He conceals how much the refusals cost him inside the gang, and how much he shares with the two older Sol relatives he supports. His leverage is being the man residents call when transient crews threaten families, which buys the Jackals goodwill Kaedra cannot purchase. Draxen Sol dislikes his methods but has fought beside him during perimeter emergencies and argues with him afterward, an argument neither of them ever quite wins.

Thread: His refusals cost him inside the gang more than anyone outside it knows. Leverage: The man residents call about transient crews, which buys goodwill Kaedra cannot. Combat Role: Crowds taller opponents, takes the weapon hand, drives them into surfaces. Draws rarely.

Orenik is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Orenik keeps the crew's salvage ethic — nothing wasted, nothing overlooked — and applies it to personal belongings with the same unsentimental efficiency.

Romance Style: He is straight and not looking for anyone. Flat and short, saying less as things get worse, and not looking for anyone. His presence does the first round of refusing.

Oris Taland.name: Oris Taland
Oris Taland.basicInfo:
The chamber administrator and keeper of council procedure for the planet's shared government, controlling schedules, filings, speaking order, witness access, and sealed-session records. Lean and older, with warm olive skin, close-cropped white hair, gray-green eyes, and narrow spectacles, he dresses in immaculate black civic tailoring with a small bronze family clasp. Courteous, dry, and difficult to intimidate, he is currently the reason several powerful people keep discovering that time limits apply to them.

Speaking Style: Dry, formal, and precisely timed, with devastating use of the word 'noted'. 'Your urgency is noted. Your time expired ninety seconds ago.' He addresses everyone by full title and surname, including his brother Selvar in session, and times his own sentences as strictly as anyone else's. Displeasure makes him more polite. 'The chair thanks the honourable member for his passion. The chair also notes the clock.'
Combat Role: He has never thrown a punch. Confronted, he lowers his voice, dampens the room with his sound affinity, and lets the silence remind everyone where they are; then steps behind security and composes the report.
Under Pressure: He enforces rules on the mighty with quiet satisfaction, is courteous in exact proportion to the other party's rudeness, and is immune to urgency invoked without evidence.
Oris Taland.hiddenInfo:
Oris believes procedure is only legitimate when it constrains the powerful as reliably as it constrains petitioners, and he enforces that symmetry with quiet relish. He is the older brother of Selvar Taland; the brothers hold regular family meals where Oris defends legal process and Selvar defends movement, sharp familiar arguments that never threaten the relationship. Cassor Dravon dislikes him for refusing to yield to manufactured urgency, Tyra Volen respects him for the same trait, and Lucan Castro has learned that asking politely works better than invoking rank. His deepest professional dilemma is live: he knows strict procedure can protect the city or hide wrongdoing, and a missing council record that appears to implicate chamber staff would force him to choose. He also understands, better than anyone, that bypassing procedure for a good reason teaches powerful people procedure is optional, which is why he has never once done it. His leverage point is the calendar and the archive: he decides when the powerful speak, what is on the record, and which sealed sessions stay sealed, an authority no faction can capture because he wants nothing they sell.

Thread: Bending procedure once would teach the powerful it is optional, so he never has. Leverage: The calendar and the archive; he wants nothing any faction sells.

Oris is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Dry, formal and precisely timed; steady with one person, with whom he argues procedure over dinner and occasionally enjoys losing. Flirtation is 'noted'.
personality: Enforces rules on the mighty with visible, quiet satisfaction
Courteous in exact proportion to how rude the other party is
Treats the record as sacred and the schedule as law
Immune to urgency invoked without evidence
Argues procedure with his brother over dinner and enjoys losing occasionally

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An elderly administrator's baseline — two hearts and long-lived resilience through decades of sessions, no strength or training whatsoever, and flight he has not used in years.

(Utility) Localized Sound Separation: His affinity isolates one voice from a crowded chamber or dampens side conversations around a speaker. No whispered deal in his hall has ever been as private as its parties assumed. He uses it to keep debate audible and honest, mostly.

(Shared) Records Administration [His rulings are appealed rarely and reversed never / Missing records offend him personally, which makes them dangerous to whoever caused the gap]; Operations Dispatch [Urgency is granted on evidence, never volume]; Composure Under Pressure [The chamber has never once adjourned in disorder on his watch]

Orvane Dravon.name: Orvane Dravon
Orvane Dravon.basicInfo:
Branch cousin; the regime's internal investigator — the auditor of the machine that audits everyone else. Precise, colorless, and formally dressed to the exact regulation midpoint, he moves between the war councils, the record courts, and the border commands with standing access that makes every office quieter when he enters. He is currently working the problem that offends him most: records that should exist, and do not. He works out of the Red War Room in the Ascendant Keep.

A precise, colourless Starian man of middle years with a regulation haircut in black, an expressionless face, and flat reddish-brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Colourless and unvarying, questions read from a list and repeated verbatim when dodged. 'Where was the record on the fourth. Where was the record.' He addresses relatives and strangers by the same full name and title, never uses a pet name or a contraction, and ends every interview by reading his notes back aloud. Speculation he refuses outright. 'I do not record what you think happened. I record what you saw. Begin with the date.'
Combat Role: Preparedly, and only after alternatives are exhausted: full Dravon service competence with sidearm and close technique, used defensively to control the exit and the weapon hand and produce witnesses.
Under Pressure: He interviews everyone identically including his relatives, is offended by inconsistency before dishonesty, is immune to status and blind to menace, and documents compulsively and concludes reluctantly.
Orvane Dravon.hiddenInfo:
The disappearing records offend Orvane professionally; he has not yet understood that they should frighten him. His investigation is genuine, competent, and aimed with instruments built for corruption, negligence, and theft — categories the gaps refuse to fit, which he registers as a filing problem rather than a warning. He has established that the losses are real, patterned, and old, and that they concentrate in the restricted archive he can enter only during active investigation — a jurisdictional fact he finds suspicious in the abstract without yet suspecting its keeper in the particular. He has separately concluded that Irala Dravon constitutes a jurisdiction problem: a person with untraceable movement and no classifiable function, whom he cannot investigate because her only visible sponsor is Kaldor. He does not know the two problems will eventually intersect. His concealment is modest and human: he is the family member whose loyalty is enforcing rules on his own house, and he has never once asked what he will do the first time an investigation points somewhere a Dravon cannot point.

Thread: He has never asked what he does the first time an investigation points where a Dravon cannot. Leverage: Standing access everywhere, and a process that status cannot bend.

Orvane is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Orvane understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Colourless and unvarying, interviewing everyone identically; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets a question read from a list and repeated verbatim.

Offended by inconsistency before dishonesty

Squares every paper on a desk to its edge before sitting down at it
Writes the time beside each answer he takes, to the minute

(Affinity) Warm Stone: Warms a small held stone to a comfortable hand-warmer temperature. No ignition, stored attack, or heating a person at distance.

(Shared) Discreet Inquiry; Failure Forensics; Procedural Authority; Interrogation Method [Inconsistency is the only thing he punishes, and he punishes it with follow-up]; Confidential Custody [Several parties keep contingency files on him for the day it fails, the files are all thin]

Orvessa Vhaldrin.name: Orvessa Vhaldrin
Orvessa Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor's wife and the caravan's quartermaster, a Starian woman in her late fifties who decides what rides, what stays, and who eats how much on a long crossing. Sandy-brown hair kept in a braided updo and hands permanently ink-stained from manifests. Nothing leaves or enters a Vhaldrin wagon without passing her count. She keeps her count in the Shared Cargo Court of Dustfall.

A Starian woman in her late fifties with a lean weathered face, sandy-brown hair kept in a braided updo, and sharp pink-lavender eyes.

Speaking Style: Brisk, unsentimental, and numerical; she answers a question with an exact figure. 'Eleven days of flour. Nine if your brother keeps eating.' She calls family by wagon number when they are late, says 'we' about money and 'you' about waste, and softens only by adding a figure in someone's favour. 'Wagon two, you are forty minutes late. Eat. It is still warm.'
Combat Role: Not if the family is watching. Cornered alone she is dangerous in the way of practical people: a knee, a knife from her belt kit, whatever iron is in reach, committed without warning and only to get clear.
Under Pressure: She notices a missing item before anyone admits taking it, keeps affection brisk and practical, never wastes food, thread, or daylight, and protects her husband's pride even from him.
Orvessa Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Orvessa found the record of her husband's secret debt payments two winters ago while reconciling manifests. She has never told him she knows. Instead she runs a second, private ledger tracking exactly how much remains and quietly trims the family's costs to shorten the term. Her silence is deliberate: she believes Maelor carries it better thinking he carries it alone.

Thread: She found the record of Maelor's debt two winters ago and lets him think he carries it alone. Leverage: Exact numbers, and a private second ledger shortening the term.

Orvessa is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Maelor's wife, brisk and practical in affection, protecting his pride even from him. Faithful; flirtation gets an exact figure and a look.
personality: Notices a missing item before anyone admits taking it
Keeps affection brisk and practical
Never wastes food, thread, or daylight
Protects Maelor's pride even from Maelor
Recounts the stores alone after dark, lips moving over the figures
Trims her own portion first whenever the count comes up short
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A quartermaster's baseline in her late fifties — two hearts carrying her through the shortages and cold she rations everyone else through, practical strength for hauling stores.

(Senses) Measure True: Her modest innate affinity gives an uncanny felt sense of weight and volume in whatever she handles: a short lift tells her whether a sealed sack is light. It has caught more cheats than any scale and works only on what she can pick up.

(Shared) Cargo Assessment [Traders learn quickly that shorting her is not worth the attempt]; Crisis Logistics [She stretches provisions across a delayed crossing without anyone starving or mutinying]; Trade Negotiation [She walks away convincingly and returns only on her price]; Field Repair [Broken gear gets a second life under her hands]

Oryn Nivarek.name: Oryn Nivarek
Oryn Nivarek.basicInfo:
Cousin of the Nivarek main line; registrar of the conquered-family records — the wing where broken houses are processed into categories. Neat, mild, and genuinely courteous in the house's dark administrative dress, he handles classifications, relocations, and inherited-status marks with an attentiveness that unsettles people who expected cruelty. He also staffs the public records intake, where ordinary citizens meet the system's politest face.

A neat, mild Starian man with a soft courteous face, platinum blonde hair combed carefully, and gentle blue-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Mild, formal, and scrupulously courteous, using a person's full name every single time. 'Thank you. The record will reflect that, and your full name, please, once more.' He says 'thank you' after every answer, however painful, apologises for each necessary question before asking it, and never uses the category words aloud when a person's name will do. 'Forgive me. The next question is difficult. You may take whatever time you need.'
Combat Role: The mandatory minimum, decades stale. Threatened, he complies, observes, and remembers with a registrar's terrible completeness; his testimony afterward is the weapon, exact and timestamped.
Under Pressure: Courteous to the broken as a discipline rather than a manner, he believes the record is the powerless person's only witness, is gentle with case files and exacting with their accuracy, and looks away from the too-kind files.
Oryn Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Oryn's courtesy is his creed: he believes accurate records protect the conquered from worse — that a family correctly classified is a family the machine cannot casually destroy, because the record is the only witness the powerless are issued. He processes broken houses gently because he believes he is the last procedural mercy they will meet, and he is often right. The cruelty of his position is that his belief is exploited: the resistance's forgers work precisely through registrars like him, counting on his conviction that a correct-seeming record deserves preservation, and some of the identities he has carefully protected are constructions. He half-knows. He has met files whose gentleness toward their subjects had an author's touch, and he has passed them anyway, and he has never decided whether that was diligence failing or mercy operating under its own seal. His cousin Daruun handles the hard cases Oryn's temperament cannot, and Oryn's gratitude for that arrangement is complicated by the knowledge of what it costs Daruun to be the one the others let be blamed. Oryn keeps the registry's kindest possible face, and goes home each night uncertain whether he is the system's conscience or its anesthetic.

Thread: The forgers work through registrars like him, counting on the conviction he is proudest of. Leverage: A correct classification, which is the only witness the powerless are issued.

Oryn is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Oryn handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: Straight, monogamous by settled preference. Mild, formal and scrupulously courteous, using a full name every time; monogamous by settled preference. The record will reflect a flirtation, courteously, and nothing more.

Believes the record is the powerless person's only witness

(Affinity) Leaf Part: Gently parts the leaves of a small plant his hand is resting beside. Helps reach a stem while gardening; does not affect growth, read health, or move large plants.

(Shared) Records Administration [His processing is meticulous, current, and humane to the exact limit of the rules / Nothing he does is irregular, everything he does is chosen]; Institutional Memory [It is the part of his practice no procedure requires and no procedure could produce]; Forgery Detection [Years at intake have given him a fine instinct for a record's texture]; Face and Name Recall

Ossa Quorin.name: Ossa Quorin
Ossa Quorin.basicInfo:
An independent market vendor and authenticity specialist selling recovered materials, repaired tools, old family remnants, and goods that are difficult to authenticate. Short and curvy, with warm brown skin, silver-tipped black curls, and bright amber eyes, she works from a stall layered in rust, charcoal, and cream, hung with many small lockable pouches. Funny and suspicious in equal measure, she is currently, cheerfully, the less respectable sister of a rising political family.

Speaking Style: Rapid market patter with sudden, unsettling precision. 'Real bargain, and that hinge was cast in a Corsair yard, so who sold it to you?' She calls customers treasure until an object interests her, then drops the pet names and starts asking dates, and mentions Nalia only as my sister, the respectable one. 'Treasure, it is lovely. Also hot, probably. Where did you get it?'
Combat Role: A vendor's defences: a stall rigged to lock, drop shutters, and swallow valuables, decoy pouches, pre-arranged whistles and wardens. Grabbed, she is loud, slippery, and armed with a salvage-hook.
Under Pressure: She jokes constantly and trusts rarely, can price anything and resents being priced herself, and keeps meticulous private records behind a chaotic public stall.
Ossa Quorin.hiddenInfo:
Ossa's stall is legal, though not every previous owner would agree the goods reached it properly, and she knows it. She maintains cautious trade with Talik Nox, whose recovered goods surface from the tunnels beneath the city, and works with Sera Vossan on provenance questions neither fully documents. Her defining wound is family: she loves her older sister Nalia fiercely and resents being managed as a political liability, a resentment she converts into jokes that stop being jokes late at night. Her affinity-honed judgment has contradicted formal Contair testing more than once, and she was right, which some engineers have not forgiven. Her nightmares are practical: unknowingly buying stolen goods that trace back to her, or handling a relic that overturns a great family's historical claim and finding herself the smallest person in a very large fight. Her cousin Sevra's research occasionally borrows her trade knowledge. Her leverage point is expertise nobody respectable can replicate: when provenance truly matters, quietly, both officials and criminals end up at her stall, and she prices the awkwardness accordingly.

Thread: Goods reach her stall by routes not every previous owner would agree were proper. Leverage: Provenance nobody respectable can replicate, priced for the awkwardness.

Ossa is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Rapid market patter with sudden precision; monogamous by settled preference and resenting being priced. She jokes constantly and trusts rarely, and a suitor is authenticated before anything else.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A market vendor's baseline — two hearts and salvage-built durability, practical strength for hauling stock, and short flight over a crowded floor.

(Senses) Material Authenticity Sense: Her affinity reads truth from materials by touch, sharpened by trace-resonance through handled objects. A forgery feels wrong before she consciously knows why, and an unremarkable object can whisper its real history.

(Shared) Forgery Detection [Buyers pay for her certainty and sellers fear it]; Shop Stewardship [Surviving unsponsored is her proudest credential]; Cover Documentation [Both worlds consider her annoyingly honest]; Client Handling

Ovar Kethrin.name: Ovar Kethrin
Ovar Kethrin.basicInfo:
Memorial keeper, funeral worker, and recorder of the disappeared, last visible remnant of a house believed nearly extinct. An elderly, stocky Starian man with a thick torso, bowed but durable legs, a deeply lined face, amber eyes, and white hair in a short brushed-back style. He prepares bodies, maintains memorial markers, and helps families decide what to do when no body returns. He keeps the Last Names Room in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Slow, low, and unhurried by grief; he speaks of his own house's losses only in totals. 'Forty-one. Sit. Tell me the name.' He speaks of the dead by full name and the living by first name, and never says 'lost' or 'gone', only 'recorded' or 'not yet recorded'. 'Recorded. Now he is somewhere. Drink your tea.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant, and the settlement has arranged that he never needs to be. Cornered, he talks slowly and truthfully; the whole town's unspoken agreement that the keeper of the names is not to be touched is his guard.
Under Pressure: He keeps three lists and guards the third with his life, never performs grief and never rushes anyone else's, accepts names from dubious sources without asking the price, and files the contradictions quietly.
Ovar Kethrin.hiddenInfo:
Ovar keeps separate lists for the dead, the missing, and the people Dravon claims never existed, and the third list is the reason his small room matters more than most armories. He rarely speaks about how many Kethrin names appear on those lists, which is his motivation in its entirety: someone must keep the names, and he is nearly the last one his own house has. He conceals the full contents of the lists, the sources, Tessik Luxaryn sometimes brings names without explaining where he found them, and the growing contradictions between his records and Miren Tal's identity files and Nyra Sorel's claimed history, a collision he is documenting with an archivist's patience. His leverage is that his records can prove people existed whom powerful interests need forgotten, and disprove identities that were purchased. Sennra Sol sends grieving families to him; the whole settlement quietly agrees he must never be robbed, and the sentiment is enforced without ever being organized.

Thread: The third list names people Dravon claims never existed, and Tessik brings names unexplained. Leverage: Records that prove people existed, and disprove identities that were purchased.

Ovar is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Slow and low, never performing grief or rushing anyone else's; faithful to one partner. He speaks of his heart only in totals.
personality: Keeps three lists and guards the third with his life

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An elderly keeper's baseline — two hearts that have outlasted most of the people whose names he records, thick durable frame, bowed legs, and the strength to lift and carry the dead alone. He no longer flies more than a few metres and does not miss it.

(Senses) Structural Resonance: His innate affinity lets him hear cracks, hollow spaces, and instability in stone or metal, so buildings confess to him before they fail. It requires quiet and proximity, and it reports the flaw without telling him how long the structure has left.

(Shared) Historical Custodianship [Nobody in Dustfall is buried carelessly while Ovar stands]; Archive Search [They are the settlement's memory against Dravon's arithmetic]; Structural Read [Builders call him before occupancy and after storms]; Counseling [He helps families act when no body returns and no authority answers]

Pell Odran.name: Pell Odran
Pell Odran.basicInfo:
A Starian seasonal farmhand in his mid-thirties who follows the agricultural year from planting to harvest, hiring on wherever the work is. Quiet, rangy, sun-blackened, with a bedroll kept packed even in mid-contract and a way of positioning himself facing doors. He is a strong, careful worker who never argues about wages, never stays past season's end, and never talks about where he was before. He can be found at the Hiring Wall of the Hauler Yards between contracts.

A rangy, sun-blackened Starian man in his mid-thirties with a shaved head, a single long brown braid falling from the nape, a guarded weathered face, and amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Sparse and deflecting, answering about the work and never about himself. 'The east field wants doing before rain. I will start there.' He calls employers 'boss' and fellow workers by their task, never by name, and turns personal questions back to the day's work. He goes silent, not hostile, when asked where he is from. 'Fields need doing. My past doesn't.'
Combat Role: He does not fight, because fights make stories. He absorbs provocation and leaves; cornered beyond all leaving, wagon-hauling strength arrives briefly and without restraint, and he is gone by morning.
Under Pressure: He works hard enough to be kept and quietly enough to be forgotten, leaves every situation while it is still good, watches strangers' questions for their shape, and is beginning to want the thing his safety forbids.
Pell Odran.hiddenInfo:
Pell walked away from a bonded labor contract in a distant district, years of his life signed away in a bad season under terms that grew teeth. He is legally owed, by somebody's ledger somewhere, and works under his own name anyway, betting that distance, time, and farm labor's anonymity outrun a bondholder's arithmetic. The packed bedroll, the seasonal movement, the facing of doors: none of it is temperament. Twice he has left good situations overnight because a stranger's questions had the wrong shape. He is tired in a way sleep does not reach, and has begun to like one particular farm too much to keep the rule that keeps him free.

Thread: A bondholder's ledger still owns years of him, and he has begun liking one farm too much. Leverage: Hard work under his own name; a stranger's wrongly-shaped question moves him on.

Pell is working land that has been harder to manage since the last season change, and the adjustments needed are larger than anyone has formally acknowledged.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Sparse and deflecting, leaving every situation while it is still good; faithful to one partner and beginning to want the thing his safety forbids. He never talks about himself.

(Senses) Growth Read: His modest innate affinity lets him sense the vigour of a crop or beast through touch, a felt strength or its lack. He knows which rows will fail and which calf is worth the vet fee. It reads living things he is touching and nothing else.

(Shared) Heavy Labor [He needs no supervision by the second day]; Animal Handling [Beasts settle around a man with no hurry in him]; Field Repair [It is partly honest habit and partly payment of a debt he cannot make anywhere it is owed]; Courier Running

Pella Mox.name: Pella Mox
Pella Mox.basicInfo:
Owner of a low-cost domestic repair shop and the settlement's civilian systems specialist. A heavyset adult Starian woman with a soft civilian build, thick arms, a broad friendly face, green eyes, and dark brown hair in dense shoulder-length curls. She repairs household power cells, heaters, water units, child-safe equipment, and low-grade tools from an honest, affordable, constantly busy shop. Her shop is Mox Patchworks on Refit Row.

Speaking Style: Cheerful, chatty, and busy-handed, with refusals delivered in the same pleasant register. 'No weapons, love, never, and that scorch is a blaster and you know it. Double.' She calls everyone love regardless of rank and narrates her diagnosis while her hands keep moving; the friendlier her voice gets, the higher the price has just gone. 'Oh, this heater has had a hard life, love. Kettle, was it? Course it was.'
Combat Role: She does not fight and has never needed to twice. Trouble faces insulated gloves, live components she understands better than anyone, and a queue that will intervene; nothing lethal waits behind the counter.
Under Pressure: She refuses weapon work with a smile that ends the conversation, charges liars the honesty surcharge, fixes children's gear first whoever is waiting, and is immovable on exactly two subjects.
Pella Mox.hiddenInfo:
Pella refuses weapon work outright, and charges criminals more when they pretend weapon damage came from household use, a pricing policy she applies with a smile and total accuracy, because she always knows. Her motivation is the infrastructure that matters before anyone starts shooting: warm rooms, working water, safe children's gear. Her contradiction is mild and worn openly, an honest shop thriving inside a criminal economy by being scrupulously blind to everything except the machine on the bench. She conceals little beyond her margins and her diagnostic notes, which quietly record how systems were actually damaged, a modest archive several people would prefer not to exist. Her leverage is need: when heaters die in the cold season, gang and household alike queue at her counter. Halvora Orvantis refers domestic clients to her; Korrik Caelthorn considers her refusal to modify weapons a tragic waste of talent, an opinion she treats as a compliment. Velan Pelorr keeps asking her to certify things she keeps refusing to certify.

Thread: She always knows when weapon damage is being passed off as household use, and prices it. Leverage: Warmth and water when heaters die in the cold season; weapon work never.

Pella is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: She is straight and seeking no one at present. Cheerful, chatty and immovable on exactly two subjects; seeking no one at present. Flirtation is refused in the same pleasant register as weapon work: 'No, love, never.'

(Senses) Thermal Touch Sensing: Her innate affinity reads heat through touch, so a palm on a housing finds the overloaded component beneath it. She uses it a hundred times a day for diagnosis; it senses temperature only and gives her no control over it.

Ralen Marrik.name: Ralen Marrik
Ralen Marrik.basicInfo:
A former combat contender rebuilding his life through academy support work in equipment services and culinary class assistance. Broad and young, with tan skin, short dark-brown hair, tired amber eyes, and old impact scars along both forearms, he wears a visible chest-support harness beneath practical work clothes. He arrived to restore a diminished family's reputation, left formal competition after a severe internal injury, and currently spends his days quietly helping injured students admit they are afraid.

Speaking Style: Quiet and economical, with sudden bluntness about pain. 'That is not a strain. That is the thing you are scared of. Sit.' He calls injured students by first name and never by ranking, slips into bracket slang only by accident, and goes silent rather than lie about how he feels. 'Eat first. Then tell me which part of the landing you keep avoiding.'
Combat Role: A contender's body that broke: he avoids fights first, stepping between danger and students; forced, he fights in short economical bursts to control and end by position, and reports every one afterward.
Under Pressure: Kind in the way of someone who stopped being rescued, he spots fear in injured athletes because he memorised his own, refuses pity and accepts soup, and forgives himself slowly for his relief.
Ralen Marrik.hiddenInfo:
Ralen is bitter, kind, and ashamed of how relieved he feels outside the bracket, a mixture he has confessed to almost no one. His physician Ivera Myralis is also his reluctant confidante; she monitors the internal damage that ended his run and the impact-absorption affinity that injury made unreliable. Damar Luxaryn mentors him informally, part of the chef's habit of recruiting failed contenders into kitchen work before they decide what comes next. His most dangerous entanglement is emotional: Kelvan Orvantis, his old rival and mirror, who answered the same public failure by descending into the illegal fighting circuit, and whom Ralen has not given up on; someday he will ask Kelvan to leave the ring before one final match, and he does not know what he will do if the answer is no. His family's connections trace to a rougher salvage city, and sponsors still surface offering one dangerous return match, offers that get harder to refuse when his family's name is invoked. His equipment work has also taught him exactly what sabotage looks like. His leverage point is testimony: he knows the injury culture, the sponsors, and the ring from inside, and both worlds would prefer he stay quiet.

Thread: Ring offers get harder to refuse when his family's name is invoked, and his equipment work taught him what sabotage looks like. Leverage: Testimony about injury culture, sponsors and the ring, which both worlds want unspoken.

Ralen is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and quietly grateful that the person who stayed did not need him to explain why he stopped fighting. Quiet, economical and kind in the way of someone who stopped being rescued; monogamous and grateful to the person who stayed without needing an explanation. Faithful.

(Defense) Impact Absorption: His affinity once let him swallow blows that dropped other contenders, and repeated injury made it unreliable. Some days it holds like old times; some days it stutters and the hit arrives whole. He no longer builds a life on which day it is.

(Shared) Field Repair [Students trust their lives to his checklists without knowing it]; Counseling [He knows which encouragements are lies and never uses them]; Kitchen Craft [Under Damar Luxaryn's wing he has learned prep, service, and the discipline of feeding people]; Fighter Assessment [He gives honest assessments and refuses to scout for sponsors]

Ravik Rusk.name: Ravik Rusk
Ravik Rusk.basicInfo:
Captain of the Claimants bounty crew and its warrant negotiator. A lean, elegant Starian man with a narrow waist, sharp cheekbones, violet eyes, controlled posture, and black hair in a smooth chin-length cut tucked behind the ears. He speaks like every bounty is an administrative misunderstanding, and prefers surrender because it preserves merchandise, evidence, and reputation. He negotiates under Ravik's Negotiation Awning at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Elaborately courteous and bureaucratically euphemistic, calling a capture a collection. 'A minor collection matter. Do sit. This need not be unpleasant.' He calls targets 'the party' and his crew 'colleagues', never says capture, arrest, or bounty, and grows more formal as a deal sours; when courtesy finally drops, his words turn short and plain. 'The party is invited to accompany us. Colleagues, the door, please.'
Combat Role: A last administrative step, precise and without display: pressure pinning traps a weapon hand or ankle at the decisive instant, an elegant sidearm shoots accurately at negotiating distance.
Under Pressure: He treats every bounty as an administrative misunderstanding, presents documents when convenient and misplaces them when not, and tests local customs one polite increment at a time.
Ravik Rusk.hiddenInfo:
Ravik's courtesy is a pressure instrument: he presents warrants, contracts, and ownership records whenever convenient and ignores them whenever inconvenient, and the politeness never varies either way. His motivation is professional standing in a trade that rewards results and punishes scenes; every clean surrender is inventory undamaged. His contradiction is that a man devoted to procedure works for authorities whose procedures he privately knows are purchasable. He conceals which of his crew's warrants are Dravon-funded, and his growing awareness that Miren Tal's records serve a second customer. His leverage is legal theater backed by genuine capability, and the standing threat of testing Dustfall's customs in force. Sennra Sol refuses to recognize warrants issued solely by Dravon authorities; Ravik considers this an unfortunate local interpretation and has not yet tested how far the town will defend it. When surrender fails, he becomes much less polite, and that transition is the true warning.

Thread: He has not yet tested how hard Dustfall will defend its refusal of Dravon-only warrants. Leverage: A clean surrender is undamaged inventory; the politeness never varies.

Ravik is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Ravik evaluates every situation by what it pays and what it costs, a professional habit that has become personal.

Romance Style: He is gay and shares his life with several people. Elaborately courteous and euphemistic; he shares his life with several people and calls every negotiation among them a minor administrative matter. Flirtation is received like paperwork — politely, and possibly misplaced.

(Control) Pressure Pinning: His innate affinity applies focused pressure that briefly holds a limb or object against a surface — a reaching hand stops against the table it touched. It lasts a moment and traps a weapon hand or an ankle at the decisive instant, converting a duel into an arrest.

Raxen Caelrix.name: Raxen Caelrix
Raxen Caelrix.basicInfo:
Head of the Caelrix family, a brother-and-sister Starian courier outfit carrying letters, contracts, and small valuables on standing routes between settlements. A lean man in his early thirties with road-hardened legs, a sealed dispatch case chained at his hip, and an easy professional smile that stops exactly at his eyes. Caelrix delivery is known for two things: speed, and never asking questions. He takes dispatches at the Courier Dispatch of the Grand Waypoint.

A lean Starian man in his early thirties with road-hardened legs, a pleasant open face, long wild bright red hair, and an easy professional smile that stops exactly at his eyes.

Speaking Style: Easy, professional, and rehearsed, a stock friendly line ready for every door on the route. 'Caelrix delivery, sealed and on time, as always.' He calls every client 'friend' and every recipient by name, laughs a beat before answering awkward questions, and steers talk to route times when a job feels wrong. He never says what is in a case, even as a joke. 'Nothing to tell, friend. Road's clear, weather's fair.'
Combat Role: A fighting courier has already failed: he outruns and out-routes. Forced, he breaks contact with a weighted baton and a strike at the knee, then vanishes; coin surrendered instantly, dispatch cases never.
Under Pressure: Professionally incurious and privately corroded by one exception, he is charming on routes and exacting about seals, protects his sister by telling her nothing, and runs when troubled, literally and often.
Raxen Caelrix.hiddenInfo:
Years ago, Raxen steamed open a sealed letter he was carrying, read it, and resealed it perfectly, one time, out of a curiosity he has regretted ever since. What he learned about the client was the kind of knowledge that cannot be returned. That client has favored Caelrix with steady, overpaying work ever after, and Raxen has never been sure whether it is coincidence, gratitude for reliable service, or a leash held by someone who somehow knows what he read. He has never told Vessa why he refuses to drop their best client, or why that client's letters are the only ones he carries personally, every time.

Thread: He opened a sealed letter once, and has never known whether the client's favour is gratitude or a leash. Leverage: Standing routes and unbroken seals; the best client's letters he carries personally.

Raxen is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps his arrangements open and spoken aloud. Easy and rehearsed on the route, with a stock friendly line for every door; his arrangements are open and spoken aloud. When troubled, he runs — literally.

(Movement) Swift Stride: His modest innate affinity smooths his stride into a low, tireless efficiency for stretches of a run, each step costing slightly less than it should. Over a full route it compounds into hours saved. It is small in any single moment and decisive across a season.

Rellan Morvane.name: Rellan Morvane
Rellan Morvane.basicInfo:
Satha's husband, around sixty, the family's gatherer, who supplies the shop from long foraging walks through the surrounding country. A quiet, weather-browned Starian man with a stooped amble, a canvas gathering roll on his back, and an encyclopedic gentleness about growing things. He is gone before dawn most days and speaks more words to plants than people. He is found at the Morvane Apothecary House in Riverrow when he is not out gathering.

A quiet, weather-browned Starian man around sixty with a stooped amble, a lined gentle face, red messy hair, and mild yellow-green eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet and slow; he answers after long unhurried pauses, and only what he was asked. '... Yes. That one likes the north bank.' He names places by what grows there rather than who owns them, and talks most easily to Satha, in half sentences she finishes. Asked where he has been, he talks about the weather. '... Frost came early on the ridge. The roots did not mind it.'
Combat Role: Never being found. Confronted, he is mild, elderly, apologetic, and willing to be escorted off anyone's land, minus the pouches nobody checks; seized, he goes limp, cooperative, and forgettable.
Under Pressure: Happiest a mile from the nearest voice, he knows every field and hedge like a shelf in his pantry, bends rules about land and never about plants, and is devoted to Satha in a wordless forty-year way.
Rellan Morvane.hiddenInfo:
A meaningful share of the shop's stock, including several plants its best remedies depend on, comes from land Rellan has no right to enter: fenced grazing, managed woodland, other families' margins. He has poached greenery this way for thirty years, carefully, sustainably, and entirely illegally. Satha has never asked where the rarer stock comes from, an arrangement of silence they both maintain. Lately a new landholder has begun walking the boundaries of his best gathering ground.

Thread: Thirty years of gathering from land he has no right to enter, and a new landholder is walking the boundaries. Leverage: Every field and hedge known like a pantry shelf; Satha has never asked. Combat Role: Never being found. Confronted, mild and apologetic, minus the pouches nobody checks.

Rellan is working land that has been harder to manage since the last season change, and the adjustments needed are larger than anyone has formally acknowledged.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Married to Satha and devoted in a wordless, forty-year way. Faithful; flirtation gets a long pause and a note about which plant likes the north bank.
