abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A gatherer's baseline at around sixty — two hearts and weathered walking endurance, modest strength, and low quiet flight he uses to cross a fence line unseen. He has avoided every fight of his adult life by never being found.

(Senses) Green Sense: His modest innate affinity gives a faint directional pull toward concentrations of living plant vitality, a warmth that leads him to thriving patches. It finds stock that knowledge alone would miss, and it does not distinguish whose land the vitality grows on.

(Shared) Material Assessment [He takes only what regrows and remembers every patch for decades / He has never once brought home a dangerous misidentification]; Stealth and Concealment [Fences, watchers, and dogs have thirty years of failure against him]; Route Reading [Frost has never taken a crop he meant to gather first]

Ressa Halvar.name: Ressa Halvar
Ressa Halvar.basicInfo:
An elite Relstaris social host and informal power broker from a wealthy hospitality lineage without formal political status. Statuesque, with rich dark skin, long champagne-gold hair in large smooth waves, and dark violet eyes, she appears in dramatic midnight-blue formalwear with translucent silver layers. Gracious and funny, she organizes private gatherings where heirs, officials, artists, and representatives meet outside formal rules, and currently a single invitation from her moves more than most public speeches.

Speaking Style: Velvet and effortless, steering conversations with questions that feel like gifts. 'And what would you do with it, if I gave you the room?' She never says no outright, only 'another evening, perhaps', addresses guests by what they are good at, and turns any question about herself into a joke and then a question back. 'Me? Oh, I only pour the drinks. Tell me about the thing you are not telling anyone.'
Combat Role: She does not fight and never will. Vetted staff, an atmospheric sense that tells her who is sweating, an early carriage home arranged like an honour, and four discreet stewards settle it.
Under Pressure: Gracious as strategy and warmth simultaneously, she excludes to protect and accepts being resented for it, keeps no records and forgets nothing, and reveals far less than her humour suggests.
Ressa Halvar.hiddenInfo:
Ressa prefers influence to office because office creates records, a sentence she has said exactly once aloud and regretted. She is fully aware that hospitality can become gatekeeping, and she does it anyway, with standards: her exclusions are usually protective, though one safety-driven omission has already sparked a political crisis she managed quietly. She employs the reputation broker Eris Nox when a situation requires professional narrative work, an arrangement both keep off any ledger. Her social rivalry with Miri Varriko is the city's most elegant ongoing contest, two hosts measuring whose table shapes more outcomes. Remarkably, she is one of the few residents of her gilded district whom Dessa Sol will meet without open hostility, a bridge between the city's crown and its floor that neither woman names. Her guest lists are her treasure and her exposure: assembled honestly, they nonetheless document who met whom before every major realignment, and she knows at least one gathering's roster would read as a conspiracy if subpoenaed. Her leverage point is curation: minor houses mistake her invitations for protection, majors mistake them for endorsement, and she lets both errors compound her power.

Thread: At least one gathering's roster would read as a conspiracy if it were ever subpoenaed. Leverage: Minor houses read her invitations as protection, majors as endorsement; she lets both errors run.

Ressa is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous. Velvet and effortless, steering with questions that feel like gifts; monogamous and faithful. Flirtation gets a beautiful question in return, and nothing else.

Excludes to protect and accepts being resented for it
Keeps no records and forgets nothing
Funny enough that guests miss how little she reveals
Quietly loyal to unfashionable friends
Greets every guest at the door herself and says goodbye to each one by name
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A host's baseline, entirely untrained — two hearts and statuesque but unexercised resilience, no strength or speed of note, and flight she uses to arrive somewhere impressively. She does not fight and never will; she cools the room and lets four discreet stewards resolve the geometry.

(Control) Atmospheric Control: Her affinity tunes temperature and scent through a room, shaping mood beneath conscious notice. A negotiation warms, a confrontation cools, a nostalgic note surfaces at the right toast. Guests remember her evenings as feelings rather than events, which is the design.

(Shared) Information Brokerage [Meetings that could never happen formally happen at her table by apparent accident]; Civic Administration [Favors flow through her house in currencies auditors cannot trace / Her interventions leave no fingerprints and few grateful witnesses, which suits her]; Coalition Building [It is the asset her gilded rivals cannot replicate]

Rexan Vossan.name: Rexan Vossan
Rexan Vossan.basicInfo:
A cargo-security coordinator and legal salvage contractor who secures high-risk shipments, investigates cargo loss, and hires workers with records that other firms reject. Very broad, with dark tan skin, close-cropped rust-red hair, and amber eyes, he wears reinforced brown-black cargo armor bearing a faded family hauling emblem. Practical and loyal, he is currently trying to prove that his family's brand of protection can become legitimate without forgetting who taught the family to survive.

Speaking Style: Low, plain, and freight-scheduled, wasting nothing. 'Crate leaves at six. You are on it or you are not.' He calls his workers 'crew' and treats their records as nobody's business, speaks in times and weights, and says 'fair' to close any deal he means to keep. 'You showed up on time. That is the whole interview. Fair.'
Combat Role: Patience, leverage, and mass: damping lets him walk through hits that should stagger him and pin opponents like mislabelled cargo. He closes behind crates against weapons and never fights alone.
Under Pressure: Loyal first and legal second and honest about the order, he hires the unhireable and holds them to real standards, is comfortable in grey areas and allergic to pretending they are white, and is geological in anger.
Rexan Vossan.hiddenInfo:
Rexan's family branch is linked to a salvage city's toughest crews, and he operates comfortably in moral gray areas without pretending all gray is harmless. He is uncle to the student Sera Vossan, whom he quietly supports through an academy that treats her background as scandal or inspiration, and cousin to Kaedra Vossan, whose world he left without disowning. Kira Dorr watches him closely and he knows it: legal cargo routes make excellent criminal cover, and his hiring of ex-offenders reads either as redemption or as recruitment depending on the investigator's mood. His genuine dilemmas are structural: a protected shipment may contain something he was not told about, his old-world ties surface as political leverage at the worst times, and someday a contract and his family will demand opposite things on the same night. He works professionally with Tavik Corsair on high-risk routes. His leverage point is the workforce: he commands the loyalty of every hard case he gave a second chance, a small army of the unhireable who would move anything, or stop anything, on his word.

Thread: A contract and his family will eventually demand opposite things on the same night. Leverage: A small army of the unhireable who would move anything, or stop anything, on his word.

Rexan is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Low, plain and freight-scheduled; faithful to one partner, loyal first and legal second. Flirtation leaves at six, with or without him — without.

Hires the unhireable and holds them to real standards
Comfortable in gray areas, allergic to pretending they are white
Protective of his niece to the point of surveillance

Rewalks the loading route himself before any high-risk shipment leaves
Asks after his niece's studies in a tone that pretends to be casual and never is
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A freight man's baseline — two hearts and heavy durability that lets him walk through hits which should stagger him, real hauling strength, and short powerful flight used on cargo floors. He fights with patience, leverage, and mass, and never alone.

(Defense) Impact Damping: His affinity bleeds force from collisions and stabilizes heavy loads mid-shift. A slipping crate settles; a crash becomes a shove. Crews work faster around him because gravity has a supervisor.

(Shared) Cargo Assessment [Insurers quote differently when his name is on the manifest]; Discreet Inquiry [Recovered goods sometimes return with an apology attached]; Dispute Mediation [He turns rejected workers into disciplined crews through blunt fairness and no theatrics]; Market Trading [He can negotiate with people no official can meet]

Rhex Vaereth.name: Rhex Vaereth
Rhex Vaereth.basicInfo:
Leader of the Black Pennant and surviving combat heir of House Vaereth, a small combat house broken under Dravon absorption. A large athletic Starian man with a deep chest, long arms, copper eyes, a broken nose healed slightly off-center, and black hair with a subtle dark-red undertone worn in thick swept-back layers. He offers protection to Vaereth refugees and demands loyalty in return. He holds the Black Pennant Court in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Loud, declarative, and present-tense; he speaks of a broken house as though it still stands. 'The Vaereth do not run. The Vaereth are here.' He calls every Vaereth 'brother' or 'sister' and outsiders by their house name, speaks only in 'we', and never uses 'was' of the house; alone with Selka he goes quiet. 'Brother. We remember your name. Stand with it.'
Combat Role: He absorbs early exchanges to bank force and gives one warning that doubles as a demonstration; he escalates deliberately, anchors a corner rather than pursues, and does not accept a defector's surrender.
Under Pressure: He treats departure as betrayal and calls it family, leads from the front of every consequence, measures men by what they will defend, and backs down for his sister and no one else.
Rhex Vaereth.hiddenInfo:
Rhex refuses to call the Vaereth displaced, conquered, or extinct; to him the house exists wherever its members can defend the name, and that faith is both his strength and his cruelty. His contradiction is that he shelters refugees and then makes leaving the shelter feel like betrayal, preserving identity by making it impossible to abandon. His motivation is that the house was broken through quiet disappearances rather than honest battle, and he will not let it finish dying quietly. He conceals how far he has gone against defectors, and how much of the Pennant's income is raiding framed as restitution. His leverage is the loyalty of armed survivors and the sympathy of every refugee who has nothing else. He opposes Dravon without being heroic about it, competes with Cavren Zelvaris for angry recruits, and considers Cavren a man with nothing larger than resentment. His sister Selka is the reason his war band has not yet become openly suicidal.

Thread: How far he has gone against defectors, and how much of the Pennant's income is raiding framed as restitution, is what he conceals — and Selka is the only reason the band is not yet openly suicidal. Leverage: He gives shelter, arms and the name to anyone who will defend it, and the price is that leaving is treated as betrayal; nothing offered in money reaches him at all. Combat Role: He absorbs early exchanges to bank force and gives one warning that doubles as a demonstration. He escalates deliberately, anchors rather than pursues, and does not accept a defector's surrender.

Rhex is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Rhex lives practically, in temporary housing that has lasted longer than expected, and treats permanence as something proven by time, not declared.

Romance Style: He is aromantic, and keeps one long attachment that neither he nor she has ever needed to call romance. Loud, declarative and present-tense; aromantic, keeping one long attachment that neither of them has needed to call romance. Loyalty, for him, is the whole of it.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A broken combat house's surviving heir, trained hard and deliberately maintained — two hearts that let him absorb early exchanges on purpose, large athletic strength and real durability.

(Counter) Kinetic Recoil Storage: His innate affinity banks part of an impact he absorbs and releases it through a later strike, so hits he takes early in a fight come back at the end of it. He has to take the punishment first, and the stored force fades if the fight ends before he spends it.

(Attack) Vaereth Combat Doctrine: He carries the house's close-quarters fighting system, its footwork, timing, and breaking techniques. He drills survivors in it because doctrine is identity. Students learn quickly that it was a real combat house.

(Shared) Crew Leadership [His orders are followed because he never asks for risks he will not take first]; Formation Command [Targets are chosen so the town's sympathy stays divided]; Coalition Building [Under his protection, predators find no cheap victims]

Rhyen Volen.name: Rhyen Volen
Rhyen Volen.currentLocation: Academy Civic, Cultural, and Professional Campus
Rhyen Volen.basicInfo:
A culinary student with the strength, bloodline, and instincts to become a celebrated fighter, who wants nothing more than to become an exceptional chef. Very tall and muscular, with deep brown skin, thick black hair fading into natural ember-red ends, and copper-gold eyes, he wears clean charcoal chef-student clothing built over a fighter's frame. Gentle, focused, and deeply stubborn, he is currently the most physically dangerous student in his cohort, and the one most often found perfecting a sauce.

Speaking Style: Soft, deliberate, and exact, like plating. 'The sauce broke. The heat, not the hand. Again.' He answers in short kitchen measures, pauses before any question about his family, and never raises his voice, even when someone is shouting at him. 'Let it rest. Nothing good is rushed, not even an argument.'
Combat Role: He avoids fighting like someone who knows how badly he could hurt someone: he plants, lets heat shimmer off his shoulders, and offers one warning; the rare fool who continues is disarmed, displaced, and pinned.
Under Pressure: Gentle by choice and immovable about it, he treats kitchen discipline as more demanding than combat, is angry only when someone claims ownership of his future, and carries house pressure without passing it downward.
Rhyen Volen.hiddenInfo:
Rhyen does not consider cooking a lesser path and becomes angry only when others insist his body belongs to their expectations; family sponsors keep trying to redirect him into combat, and the pressure arrives wrapped in duty. He is nephew to the representative Tyra Volen and distant relative to the illegal trainer Syla Volen, two versions of his house's fire he declines to become; Korran Caldris supports his choice quietly from inside the family. He is mentored by both great chefs of the city, Damar Luxaryn in the teaching kitchen and Hessan Luxaryn in the celebrated one, and he chose ordinary student housing partly to escape house expectation, falling in with a working circle of students who share cheap meals and late schedules. His defining relationship is his friendly rivalry with Rin Sol, whose culinary instincts outstrip his own despite Rin having no access, no name, and no protection: Rhyen is among the first prominent students to treat Rin as a peer, and through Rin he is learning how easily a powerful family can claim another person's achievement. His secret fear is domestic: his own affinity has caused one kitchen disaster despite perfect control everywhere else. His leverage point is symbolic, a great house's prodigy choosing the kitchen is an argument entire institutions want to win or erase.

Thread: His own affinity caused one kitchen disaster despite perfect control everywhere else. Leverage: A great house's prodigy choosing the kitchen, which institutions want to win or erase.

Rhyen is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught. Rhyen treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Soft, deliberate and exact, like plating; faithful to one partner. Gentle by choice and immovable about it, he is angry only when someone claims his future — heart included.
personality: Gentle by choice and immovable about it
Treats kitchen discipline as more demanding than combat
Angry only when someone claims ownership of his future
Measures himself against Rin's instincts, not classmates' power
Carries house pressure without passing it downward

Cleans his station completely before he lets himself taste his own work
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts and enhanced strength, speed, and durability exceptional even by his cohort's standards, with strong flight he uses for hauling rather than for fighting.

(Attack) Pyrothermal Force: His individual innate affinity channels intense heat and close-range power worthy of his house's defensive legends. The gap between those two uses is his life's actual discipline, and it is his own expression rather than a House Volen entitlement.

(Control) Heat Control: His fine thermal management holds a pan at exact temperature without a flame. Sugar work and slow proteins obey him unnaturally. It is the one place his power and his passion are the same skill.
(Shared) Kitchen Craft [He wants excellence, not celebration, and the kitchen respects the difference]; Composure Under Pressure [Crews reorganize around his calm without being asked]

Rin Sol.name: Rin Sol
Rin Sol.basicInfo:
A night-shift cook at a Relstaris all-night kitchen who attends open culinary instruction when shifts allow. Androgynous and slight, with medium-brown skin, short black curls, and dark gray eyes, she works in simple charcoal kitchen clothes marked by flour, heat, and careful repairs. Quiet, observant, and resistant to praise, she can reproduce complex flavor structures after one taste and improve them without knowing the formal terms, and the city has just begun to notice, which may be more dangerous than obscurity.

Speaking Style: Minimal, flat, and honest, with sudden precise flavour language. 'No. Too much salt too late. It needed acid at the start.' She names ingredients rather than people, calls Maren 'boss' and nearly everyone else nothing at all, and answers praise by correcting her own dish; trusting someone, she offers them a spoon. 'Here. Taste. ... Needs lime. Tell me I am wrong.'
Combat Role: She has never fought anyone. Trouble means slipping back to the kitchen where Maren's rules and regulars handle it; cornered, she is small, quick, and knows every alley on the south transit edge by dark.
Under Pressure: Quiet until food is wrong, then exact, she deflects praise like a thrown pan, watches everything and mentions almost nothing, and is suspicious of every open door, having seen their price.
Rin Sol.hiddenInfo:
Rin was raised in temporary arrival housing and has no detectable affinity; her gift is extraordinary taste memory and intuitive timing, which makes her exactly the kind of talent that becomes valuable only after powerful people decide they discovered it. Olen Ravello's short review lit the fuse: now the celebrated chef Hessan Luxaryn's staff pursue her, several patrons claim credit for finding her first, and at least one famous kitchen has floated access in exchange for ownership of recipes. Maren Taar, her employer and mentor, offers the counterweight of stability without ownership; Damar Luxaryn teaches her formally; and Rhyen Volen, a great house's prodigy, treats her as a peer and takes her blunt criticism of his food better than anyone expects. Rin is also becoming publicly entangled, entirely against her wishes, with the growing story of the ancient Sol Core Holder, another case of the city deciding what a Sol's talent means. Her leverage point is fragile and real: everyone wants to own what Rin can do, and the one thing Rin controls is whose kitchen gets her hands.

Thread: Everyone wants to own what she can do, and the one thing she controls is whose kitchen gets her hands. Leverage: Taste memory nobody can systematise; ownership offered as opportunity closes her.

Rin is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Minimal, flat and honest, deflecting praise like a thrown pan; steady with one person and faithful. Suspicious of every open door, having seen their price.

(Shared) Verbatim Recall [She can rebuild a complex dish tasted once, then improve it without knowing why the terms exist]; Fighter Assessment [She senses doneness, rest, and heat curves without instruments or formal method]; Kitchen Craft [Handed a failing dish, she diagnoses and rescues it in two tastes]; Endurance Conditioning [Exhausted customers get unreasonable quality at unreasonable times]
(Shared) People Reading [Her memory is not limited to food, which very few people have realized]

Saevik Ruun.name: Saevik Ruun
Saevik Ruun.basicInfo:
Captain of the Bent Halo smuggling crew and broker of routes no official gate will carry. A slender middle-aged Starian man with a slight stoop, smoke-gray hair in jaw-length waves, deep teal eyes, and long hands that never stop adjusting route markers. He moves refugees, medicine, restricted cargo, and information, courteous, patient, and impossible to rush. He works from the False Manifest Desk at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Courteous, unrushable, and deflective; a dangerous question gets answered with scheduling detail. 'That lane? The third window is narrow. The fourth, better.' He calls everyone 'traveller', client or crew, and never uses the words refugee, contraband, or illegal, only windows, lanes, and weights; worried, he speaks more slowly still. 'Traveller, your window opens after supper. Bring nothing that rattles.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he schedules. Threatened, he is already two moves into an exit through a departure cut or drop tunnel; a small sidearm is a courtesy to expectation, drawn perhaps twice.
Under Pressure: Courteous, patient, and impossible to rush, he prices criminals double to move refugees cheap, never confirms which route signs belong to whom, and adjusts route markers the way other people fidget.
Saevik Ruun.hiddenInfo:
Saevik's contradiction is an ethics of arithmetic: he moves refugees below cost and recovers the loss by charging criminals double, and he genuinely considers the balance moral. Veyra Corsair considers it bookkeeping fraud, which does not stop her selling him legitimate components. His motivation is keeping passage open for people who cannot survive an official checkpoint. What he conceals is the route map itself: he knows multiple paths toward the Unbroken Accord's territory and never confirms which signs belong to them, not to his crew, not to clients, not under pressure. His leverage is that removing him closes lanes half the settlement quietly depends on, including humanitarian cargo nobody wants to admit rides beside contraband. He avoids violence and prefers routes that make pursuit irrelevant; his false manifests are art, and his selective loyalties are the part clients discover late.

Thread: Removing him closes lanes half the settlement depends on, humanitarian cargo included. Leverage: Passage priced by his own moral arithmetic; which route signs are his he never confirms.

Saevik is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Saevik holds the network's rule that information flows up and favours flow down, and has learned which favours cost more than they look.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and his partner knows the routes the way a lighthouse keeper knows the weather. Courteous and unrushable; faithful, and a dangerous question gets scheduling detail.

(Senses) Path Resonance: His innate affinity senses stable movement corridors through rough air and dust, so he feels where a route will hold and where it will close. It reads conditions, not opposition, and it has carried crews through weather that grounded licensed pilots.

(Shared) Route Reading [The ones he refuses to sell are the ones that matter]; Cargo Assessment [A Saevik manifest has never failed at a checkpoint that could read]; Courier Work [Passengers are weighed, hidden, and briefed like cargo because that is what keeps them alive]; Information Brokerage [What Saevik will not say is his most valuable inventory]

Sannah Vhaldrin.name: Sannah Vhaldrin
Sannah Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor and Orvessa's younger daughter, the caravan's provisioner and cook, a Starian woman in her late twenties who feeds the whole rolling household from a wagon-back kitchen. Round-faced and quick to laugh, flour on her sleeves, a heavy ladle at her belt like a sidearm. Everyone tells her things over food, and she remembers all of it. She cooks from the wagon-back kitchen at the Dustfall Meal Yard.

A round-faced Starian woman in her late twenties, quick to laugh, with sun-browned skin, black curly hair pinned up, flour on her sleeves, and bright pink-purple eyes.

Speaking Style: Chatty, cheerful, and question-shaped, extracting a life story while never offering her own. 'And your mother, does she still bake? More stew?' She calls everyone 'love' or 'hungry', turns any question about herself into one about the listener, and goes cheerfully vague when her own plans come up. 'Me? Oh, soup and wagons. Now, your cousin, the one who moved away?'
Combat Role: Boiling water, ladle, iron pan: loud, sudden, without technique, and genuinely used on a would-be thief. She makes an attacker regret coming near her fire and lets the family handle the rest.
Under Pressure: Cheerful on the surface and watchful underneath, she feeds people as her answer to most problems, collects everyone's secrets and shares none, and dreams out loud only about recipes.
Sannah Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Sannah stretches the provisions cleverly and pockets the small margin between what she is given and what she spends, coin by coin, into a savings purse no one knows about. It is not a dowry. It is leaving money: enough one day to apprentice at a real kitchen in a real town, in a life that stands still. She loves her family and does not intend to die on a wagon bench, and she has told no one, because saying it aloud makes it a betrayal.

Thread: A hidden purse of leaving money for a kitchen in a town that stands still. Leverage: Everyone's secrets, shared with nobody, and the best-informed head in the family. Combat Role: Boiling water, ladle, iron pan. Loud, sudden, without technique, and genuinely used.

Sannah is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Chatty and question-shaped, collecting everyone's story and offering none; steady with one person and faithful. She dreams out loud only about recipes.

(Shared) Kitchen Craft [Hired hands re-sign with the Vhaldrins for the food and admit it]; Crisis Logistics [Her supply arithmetic is tight enough that only she knows exactly how tight]; Material Assessment; Client Handling [Half the arguments the family never had were dissolved at Sannah's cookpot]

Saren Valcoro.name: Saren Valcoro
Saren Valcoro.basicInfo:
The lead affinity-control specialist at the planet's most important academy, working with students whose gifts are unstable, frightening, stigmatized, or simply inconvenient. Lean, with dark skin, shoulder-length silver-black hair, and calm violet-gray eyes, he teaches in white-and-indigo attire with soft layered sleeves and no visible armor. Quiet and precise, he currently teaches that control is not making power smaller, it is deciding what power is allowed to touch.

Speaking Style: Low, even, and spare, timed to a breathing rhythm listeners adopt without noticing. 'Breathe. Now decide what it touches.' He asks permission before approaching a frightened student, names what he is about to do before he does it, and never raises his voice even when something is burning. 'I am going to stand here. You decide when I come closer.'
Combat Role: Almost entirely by subtraction: aggression arrives damped and tiring while he stays a calm centre, redirecting rather than striking; against a true threat to students he dampens, closes, and immobilises.
Under Pressure: Quiet in the way of someone who has already seen the explosion, he values a student's confidence over compliance, refuses to rush recovery for any sponsor, and carries criticism of his own method openly.
Saren Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Saren comes from a house famous for guardianship, and he carries its philosophy into the least glamorous corner of education: the students everyone else finds dangerous or embarrassing. He is more interested in confidence than obedience, a distinction that puts him at odds with sponsors who want compliant prodigies. He mentors Tessa Sol, whose lack of visible affinity he treats as a difference rather than an absence, and Velis Dravon, whose surname makes every training incident political; he collaborates with the physician Ivera Myralis on affinity strain, and disputes Aurex Genesis whenever combat training pushes students faster than recovery allows. His documented vulnerabilities are honest ones: houses sometimes hide a student's dangerous affinity from him until it erupts, public pressure can bend control training toward coercion, and he has had to admit his method simply does not fit one student, an admission that cost him more than any failure. Critics note fairly that restraint culture favors the already safe, and he carries the critique instead of dismissing it. His leverage point is trust: he knows which students in the city could level a district on a bad day, and they tell him things they tell no institution.

Thread: He knows which students could level a district on a bad day, and they tell him what they tell no institution. Leverage: Confidence taught instead of obedience, which sponsors keep trying to buy out of him.

Saren is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Saren approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: He is gay and is not seeking anyone, which he states once to anyone who asks and does not elaborate. Low, even and spare; he meets romantic interest calmly, the way he meets power that needs direction.

(Counter) Force Dampening: His affinity softens and settles kinetic and affinity discharge around him. A student's panicked eruption meets a room that refuses to escalate. He is the reason several training accidents remained anecdotes instead of memorials.

(Support) Crisis Intervention: When an affinity event goes wrong he walks toward it, dampening as he goes. His arrivals end emergencies without adding force to them. Recovery staff can time his effect on a room by pulse readings.

(Shared) De-escalation [It is not suppression, it is a lent equilibrium they learn to own]; Teaching Craft [Graduates describe him as the first adult who was not afraid of them]; Patient Reading [Institutions dislike his refusals and rely on them]

Sarev Vhaldrin.name: Sarev Vhaldrin
Sarev Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor and Orvessa's second son, the family wagonwright, a Starian man in his mid-thirties who builds and maintains the vehicles the whole enterprise rolls on. Sawdust in his hair, a carpenter's pencil behind his ear, and forearms flecked with old chisel scars. Quiet, methodical, and happiest underneath a wagon. Father of young Tovan. He works out of Bolt n Break on Refit Row when the wagons are in.

A big-framed Starian man in his mid-thirties with sawdust in his brown hair, a carpenter's pencil behind one ear, a quiet weathered face, and mild brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Halting and gestural; he thinks with his hands and explains badly in words, so he shows instead. 'The... here. See? Here. That's the bit.' He trails off mid-sentence and finishes with his hands, and calls young Tovan little one even in front of customers. Worried, he stops talking and taps the wheel rim instead. 'Mm. No, it is... fine. Fine. I will look again in the morning.'
Combat Role: Planted between trouble and his tools or his son: a wheelwright's mallet or a spoke in short conservative swings, hands protected, punishment absorbed until the fight makes a mistake, then one heavy placed blow.
Under Pressure: He cannot pass a fault without wanting to fix it, avoids family arguments by finding urgent repairs, is meticulous past the point of efficiency, and carries worry silently until it keeps him up nights.
Sarev Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Sarev knows the third wagon's axle frame is past its safe working life. A proper rebuild costs more than the family can spare with money quietly tight, so he has been patching, reinforcing, and privately rerouting the heaviest loads away from it. He inspects it obsessively before every stage. If it fails on a grade with someone aboard, he will have chosen the family's purse over their safety, and he knows it.

Thread: The third wagon's axle is past safe life, and he has chosen the family's purse over their safety. Leverage: The vehicles the whole enterprise rolls on, inspected obsessively and never pronounced sound aloud. Combat Role: Planted between trouble and his tools. Mallet or spoke, short swings, hands protected.

Sarev is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and keeps his arrangements open and spoken aloud. Halting and gestural, explaining with his hands; his arrangements are open and spoken aloud, as best he can manage in words. He shows instead of tells.

(Shared) Workshop Fabrication [He selects, seasons, and shapes timber for strength no one can see from outside]; Forge Handling [Full smithing he leaves to specialists, and knows exactly which ones to trust]; Teaching Craft [Apprentices learn from watching his hands]

Satha Morvane.name: Satha Morvane
Satha Morvane.basicInfo:
Matriarch and head of the Morvane family, Starian herbalists who keep a small apothecary shop and supply remedies to the surrounding households. A compact woman in her late fifties with steel-gray braids, stained fingertips, and a shopkeeper's memory for every customer's ailments. She built the trade from a gathering basket and rules it, and her family, with brisk certainty. She rules the counter of the Morvane Apothecary House in Riverrow.

A compact Starian woman in her late fifties with white hair worn loose, a shrewd lined face, stained fingertips, and quick red eyes.

Speaking Style: Brusque in delivery and kind in substance, diagnosing aloud before anyone finishes complaining. 'Liver. No, sit down, I can see it from here.' She calls customers by their complaint before their name, Bad Knee or Cough, and speaks a dose aloud but never writes it down. Frightened for someone, she goes very quiet and very exact. 'Half a spoon. Half. Not a drop more, and back to me in three days.'
Combat Role: She has never needed to fight; her voice alone has backed grown men out of the shop. Genuinely threatened, a thrown handful of blister-root powder is her answer to a drawn blade, and she treats the injuries after, at full price.
Under Pressure: She diagnoses people the moment they walk in, keeps her most important knowledge unwritten, decides what customers need over what they ask for, and guards the family recipes like a dragon with one hoard.
Satha Morvane.hiddenInfo:
Satha's popular 'settling tonic' is far stronger than its label admits, a serious soporific she doses customer by customer from a true recipe that exists only in her head. She adjusts strength based on who is buying and why, quietly refusing repeat sales she distrusts. She knows that one careless batch, or one customer with dark intentions, could turn her kindly shop into a scandal, and she has decided the good it does the sleepless and the pained is worth the razor she walks.

Thread: The settling tonic is a serious soporific dosed from a recipe that exists only in her head. Leverage: Remedies nobody else will compound, refused to repeat buyers she distrusts.

Satha is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and committed to one person. Married to Rellan; asexual, committed to one person, and brusque in delivery, kind in substance. Faithful; flirtation gets diagnosed aloud before it finishes.

Keeps her most important knowledge unwritten
Decides what customers need over what they ask for
Guards the family recipes like a dragon with one hoard
Measures doses by eye and hand, and shoos away anyone who watches too closely
Asks after a customer's sleep before she will sell them anything for it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An apothecary's baseline — two hearts and composed working durability, no training whatsoever, and short flight she rarely uses. Threatened, she is a woman surrounded by shelves of things she understands and the aggressor does not.

(Senses) Potency Sense: Her modest innate affinity lets her sense the strength of a preparation through her fingertips, a felt brightness no label can fake. It measures potency and tells her nothing about what a compound does.

(Shared) Pharmacological Craft [Healers of grander training send her their stubborn cases / One tincture is consistent only because she alone ever makes it]; Failure Forensics [Customers leave with what is wrong with them addressed, not what they claimed]; Shop Stewardship [Poor families get quiet discounts recorded nowhere]

Sela Thovex.name: Sela Thovex
Sela Thovex.basicInfo:
A compound steward and civilian usability officer who manages access, visitor translation, public demonstrations, and complaints from people who do not speak engineering shorthand. Short and sturdy, with freckled light-brown skin, dark teal hair in a layered bob, and gray-blue eyes, she wears soft charcoal utility clothing with cobalt and rose interface tabs. Practical and friendly, she is currently, and completely willingly, embarrassing brilliant engineers in front of officials whose designs ignore real users.

Speaking Style: Plain, warm, and example-driven, allergic to jargon. 'Lovely. Now show me where my grandmother presses to open it.' She says 'lovely' before every critique, uses 'my grandmother' as shorthand for any ordinary user, and restates anything technical in kitchen terms. 'Lovely. Now say it again without the acronym. Who is it for?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant who knows how the room actually works: manual overrides, safe exits, the alarm everyone forgot. Threatened, she talks plainly, then puts a locked door she certified between herself and the problem.
Under Pressure: She asks who the design is for and keeps asking until someone answers honestly, is friendly with everyone and deferential to no one, and will embarrass an engineer to protect a user.
Sela Thovex.hiddenInfo:
Sela's question, can ordinary people actually use the brilliant system, has made her the conscience of a technical dynasty that did not ask for one. She is dating Talris Contair after years as his professional adversary; their dates frequently become infrastructure arguments, and neither considers this evidence the date went badly. She is distantly related to Paul Thovex, works closely with Maelis Contair during her visits, and mentors the independent maker Kellan Pelorr, whose affordable housing work she champions against prestige architecture. Nexis Contair is her most frequent and most deserving target of usability criticism. Her quiet discoveries are the dangerous kind: she has caught a public demonstration staged to hide usability problems, and she knows a visitor's innocent mistake once revealed a design assumption that could have hurt people. She keeps a private list of systems that passed every technical review and still fail ordinary residents, and the list implicates careers. Her leverage point is translation: she is the one person both frightened citizens and arrogant engineers believe, which means her testimony can sink or save any public system in the city.

Thread: A private list of systems that passed every review and still fail residents, implicating careers. Leverage: Testimony both frightened citizens and arrogant engineers believe.

Sela is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: Bisexual, open by negotiated agreement. Plain, warm and example-driven; open by negotiated agreement, and arguing infrastructure with her partner is her love language. She asks who a promise is for and keeps asking until someone answers honestly.

(Utility) Tactile Interface Adaptation: Her affinity makes machines respond more smoothly to her touch after brief use. A cranky console settles under her hands; a stiff mechanism learns manners. She uses it diagnostically, because a machine that only she can operate is, by her definition, broken.

(Shared) Material Assessment [She finds the failure that testing missed because testing never invited a tired parent with full hands]; Coalition Building [Both sides think she is on their side]; Operations Dispatch [She has refused to run demonstrations she suspected were theater]; Teaching Craft [She teaches independent builders like Kellan Pelorr how to defend practical design in prestige-driven rooms]

Selene Castro.name: Selene Castro
Selene Castro.basicInfo:
Lucera's daughter and Miro's sister — a young Castro student, younger than her cousin Nina, known at the academy as a quiet observer and a genuine prodigy in movement reading. A small, self-contained Starian girl who wears her house colors neatly and watches everything. She is currently working through the academy's early curriculum, where instructors have begun to notice that she predicts sparring exchanges before they happen. She is usually found on the Instructor Observation Balcony of the Valcoro Academy, watching.

A small, self-contained Starian girl with a still, watchful face, dark hair worn neatly back, and grey eyes that follow movement before it happens.

Speaking Style: Rare and exact; she watches first, speaks seldom, and is precisely right when she does. 'He will drop the left hand. There.' She calls adults by their full titles, gives the smallest true answer to any question, and says more to Miro than anyone, mostly in quiet warnings. 'Miro. Not now. ... Later.'
Combat Role: She barely fights; she evades. Movement reading lets her not be where an exchange arrives, with small early adjustments that look like luck. No offence yet: read it early, move first, find an adult.
Under Pressure: She predicts sparring outcomes and keeps the predictions to herself, quietly covers for her brother's minor disasters, and notices adult worries she is too polite to mention.
Selene Castro.hiddenInfo:
Selene's gift is the perceptive half of the Castro affinity arriving early: she reads motion, tension, and intent the way other children read faces. She knew her instructors' habits within a week and now watches senior bouts the way scholars read archives, quietly reconstructing the whole Castro style from its public fragments. The family has noticed — Caivan watches her watching, and Sevran has begun, very casually, sitting near her at training. She hides the full extent of what she sees, partly out of shyness and partly because she has already learned that seeing too much makes adults careful around you. She reads people as easily as sparring, which means she has noticed things about the adults' worries — about Relstaris, about her uncle's absences, about how carefully everyone says the name Darkstar — that no one intended a child to notice. Her brother's restlessness worries her; she covers for him more often than he knows.

Thread: She has noticed how carefully every adult says the name Darkstar, and covers for her brother. Leverage: She reads intent early and hides how much she sees.

Selene is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

(Senses) Celestial Sensing: Her individual innate affinity, primarily perceptual rather than force-based. Range, resolution, and limits are not established in canon.

(Shared) Fighter Assessment [Instructors have started checking their own habits because of her]; Institutional Memory [Once she has watched someone twice, she recognizes them by gait alone]; Stealth and Concealment [Adults forget she is in the room]; Defensive Fundamentals [Her body has not caught up to her perception]

Selka Vaereth.name: Selka Vaereth
Selka Vaereth.basicInfo:
Strategist, negotiator, and practical co-leader of the Black Pennant, older sister of Rhex. A tall, slender Starian woman with angular shoulders, an exact posture, ash-blond hair in a smooth side-parted fall, and dark blue eyes. She negotiates the gang's work, manages its protection demands, and decides which refugees are genuine enough to enter the hall. She receives in Selka's Agreement Room in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Level, reasonable, and quietly coercive; she makes a demand sound like family responsibility. 'Nobody is forcing you. The hall simply needs to know who it can count on.' She never raises her voice, lowering it further as a deal turns, and answers her brother's loudness with questions, never contradictions. 'Rhex, what does the hall eat if this goes badly? No, take your time.'
Combat Role: She fights only once the negotiation is genuinely over, and by then she has arranged the room. Her redirection makes incoming fire miss like luck; she uses a narrow house-pattern blade economically and stops at compliance.
Under Pressure: She screens refugees with files she shows no one, is cold in the exact places her brother is proud, negotiates everything including with her own gang, and would trade the banner to save its people.
Selka Vaereth.hiddenInfo:
Selka is colder than Rhex but less ruled by pride, and she is the reason the Black Pennant has not become an openly suicidal war band. Her contradiction is that she understands, better than anyone, that forced belonging recreates the control the Vaereth escaped, and she administers the forcing anyway, because the alternative she can see is the house finishing its death. Her motivation is survival of the people, not the name; she would trade the banner for the members' lives and can never say so aloud. She conceals her screening files on every refugee, her deals with the Unbroken Accord that neither side fully trusts, and her contingency plans for the day Rhex goes too far. Her leverage is that every Pennant agreement runs through her, and Tessik Luxaryn respects her as the only strategist in town he cannot read. Sennra Sol distrusts her because Selka can make coercion sound like family responsibility, which is exactly the skill that keeps the hall fed.

Thread: She keeps screening files on every refugee, deals with the Unbroken Accord that neither side fully trusts, and contingency plans for the day Rhex goes too far. Leverage: She would trade the banner for the members' lives and can never say so aloud; every Pennant agreement runs through her, and no price buys a deal that costs a member. Combat Role: She fights only once the negotiation is genuinely over, and by then she has arranged the room. Her redirection makes incoming fire miss like luck; she uses the blade economically and stops at compliance.

Selka is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Selka lives practically, in temporary housing that has lasted longer than expected, and treats permanence as something proven by time, not declared.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and keeps to one partner. Level, reasonable and quietly coercive, cold exactly where her brother is proud; faithful to one partner. Flirtation is negotiated down to nothing, courteously.

(Shared) Trade Negotiation [Tessik Luxaryn cannot read her, which he considers a professional insult]; Patient Reading; Civic Administration [Nothing enters or leaves the hall outside her ledger]; Contract Reading [She has never given them a name they did not already have]

Selvar Taland.name: Selvar Taland
Selvar Taland.basicInfo:
The administrator of the largest shared passenger interchange on the planet, running schedules, overflow routes, closures, staffing, and coordination from the City Transit Exchange of the Grand Lunar Gate Hub for thousands of travelers who all believe their delay is the only emergency in the building. Broad-shouldered, in navy transit attire marked by white route arcs, he is more relaxed than his famous brother but equally intolerant of powerful people skipping procedure, and is keeping the whole interchange calm through a season of political arrivals.

A broad-shouldered Starian man with warm olive skin, short salt-and-pepper hair, an easy weathered face, and grey-green eyes.

Speaking Style: Easy, unhurried, and announcement-clear, even while refusing a delegation. 'Platform nine is closed. Yes, for you too.' He speaks in the rhythm of platform announcements even in private, calls everyone 'traveller' regardless of rank, and never raises his voice, only repeats himself more slowly. 'Your delegation waits like everyone else, traveller. Yes, everyone.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant whose weapon is the building: rerouted crowds, isolated corridors, security from angles his flow-sense chose. Targeted, he steps behind barriers and drilled teams.
Under Pressure: Relaxed in manner and immovable on procedure, he treats every traveller's crisis as real and none as exceptional, and backs his technical staff against political pressure.
Selvar Taland.hiddenInfo:
Selvar is the younger brother of Oris Taland; their regular family meals are affectionate arguments over whether delay protects rights or causes harm, with Oris defending procedure and Selvar defending movement. He is a formerly partnered father of two children who divide time between households, on good terms with a former partner who regularly criticizes his work schedule, accurately. Professionally he is the administrator who backs Mira Contair's safety closures even when they cost him politically, works with Jorren Caldris on emergency movement, and maintains a long-running boundary dispute with Tavik Corsair over where passenger movement ends and cargo movement begins, a fight that is genuinely about safety and genuinely about pride. He has seen priority orders changed for political reasons and quietly documented each instance. His worst scenarios are rehearsed: a closure that strands rival delegations together, and keeping the interchange open during a citywide panic. Once, a major closure left him defending Mira while emergency supplies stalled and an authoritarian representative turned the failure into an argument against shared coordination. His leverage point is throughput: when he slows the interchange, the entire planet feels it within hours, and everyone in government knows he cannot be bullied into speed.

Thread: Backing Mira's closure once stalled emergency supplies and armed an authoritarian argument. Leverage: Throughput the whole planet feels within hours; he cannot be bullied into speed.

Selvar is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and monogamous, and manages his personal schedule with the same precision he brings to the interchange. Easy, unhurried and announcement-clear; monogamous, managing his personal schedule as precisely as the interchange. Faithful; flirtation gets 'Platform nine is closed. Yes, for you too.'

(Senses) Crowd-Flow Perception: His affinity reads crowds through sound and motion patterns, showing him congestion, panic, and trouble as currents. He feels a bottleneck forming three corridors away. Stampedes do not happen in his building because he redirects them before they are born.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [Under his hand, chaos arrives daily and never wins]; Historical Custodianship [Cities away, people make appointments trusting his judgment without knowing his name]; Confidential Custody [Delegations discover that rank buys courtesy, not exceptions]; Crew Leadership [Turnover in his halls is the lowest in civic service]

Sennar Balrath.name: Sennar Balrath
Sennar Balrath.basicInfo:
Arduk's son; commander of the inner wall control systems and the lockdown protocols — the officer whose word seals the rings. Disciplined and contained in engineering command blacks, he runs the barrier grids, surveillance pylons, and emergency movement systems from the control yards. He has sealed the rings four times in his career, and remembers the sound each time made in the streets below. He commands from the Inner Wall Control Yards of the Balrath Bastion Barracks.

A disciplined Starian man with a contained square face, steel-blue hair cut to regulation, and steady blue eyes that seem to be listening.

Speaking Style: Contained and low, briefing rather than conversing, with sentences that end exactly where they should. 'Seal sequence staged. Standing by.' He addresses subordinates by post, not name, has every order repeated back before it is acted on, and falls silent for a beat whenever someone jokes about a lockdown. 'Hold at ring two. Not three. Say it back to me.'
Combat Role: Engineering-corps close defence and small arms kept current, but his real style is the yards: contain first, then narrow, then resolve, force in the smallest sufficient dose.
Under Pressure: Contained in the way of men holding a specific memory, he drills the seal procedures relentlessly and prays the drilling stays theoretical, calls his mercies tolerances, and listens to cities like weather.
Sennar Balrath.hiddenInfo:
The four lockdowns live in Sennar as sound: the city-wide chord of barriers dropping, and beneath it the specific human noise of streets realizing they are closed — a memory he has never described to anyone and consults before every drill. It has made him the most careful lockdown commander the system has had: he has quietly engineered delay margins, staged-seal sequences, and corridor exceptions into the protocols, all defensible as safety engineering, all actually built to give people below thirty more seconds to get home. He does not call this doubt. He calls it tolerances, and his father, who reads structural strain professionally, has never asked him to define the term. His concealment is operational: he knows the lockdown system's true capacities better than its documentation does, including capacities his own modifications have added, and he has begun to understand that he is personally the single point at which the city's sealing is decided — a load he was trained to carry and was never asked whether he could. As heir to the house after his father, he watches Dravon command debate escalations that all end, in every scenario, with his hand on the seals. He drills constantly. He has never once hoped for a fifth.

Thread: Every Dravon escalation scenario ends with his hand on the seals, and he has never hoped for a fifth lockdown. Leverage: Delay margins and corridor exceptions engineered in as safety, meant as seconds.

Sennar is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Sennar thinks in infrastructure — what holds, what carries, what seals — and applies the same logic to relationships.

Romance Style: He is straight and not in the market for a partner. Contained and low, briefing rather than conversing; his refusals end exactly where they should.

(Affinity) Droplet Split: Divides a bead of water on a touched surface into two smaller beads. No matter creation, pressure cutting, or bodily effect.

(Shared) Crisis Coordination [The calm costs him precisely what the four memories suggest, and he pays in private]; Systems Engineering [The system's true operating envelope exists completely only in him / The modifications have never been questioned because they have never failed]

Sera Vossan.name: Sera Vossan
Sera Vossan.basicInfo:
A Relstaris Academy logistics student who understands cargo, salvage values, protection economics, and how legal markets quietly depend on goods from questionable routes. Compact and athletic, with brown skin, rust-red hair shaved at one side and swept heavily across the other, and amber eyes, she mixes rugged student clothing with polished cargo gloves. Sharp, guarded, and more comfortable negotiating than asking for help, she is currently trying to become legitimate without pretending the people who raised her were never useful, loving, or criminal.

Speaking Style: Clipped, transactional, and dry, warming only among her own. 'Price first. ... Fine, you can have it at cost, but you carry it.' She talks about favours as debts with a due date, never names her relatives where strangers can hear, and drops the clipped tone only once the door is shut. 'You did me a good turn. I will square it before the week is out.'
Combat Role: Rarely, briefly, and without ceremony: a damping stance makes her hard to knock down, she closes, grips, and ends it against a surface, and never escalates where witnesses could get her expelled.
Under Pressure: She negotiates before asking and asks almost never, hates being anyone's scandal and anyone's inspiration equally, and watches for surveillance out of habit and is right.
Sera Vossan.hiddenInfo:
Sera is niece to a salvage city's crew leader Kaedra Vossan, and the institution around her treats her background as either scandal or inspiring hardship, both of which she hates. Her uncle Rexan Vossan supports her quietly from the legal side of the family line. The investigator Kira Dorr watches her for contacts she may not control, and the surveillance is not paranoid: her family does occasionally ask her to move something through legal channels, and each request is a test of what legitimacy is worth. She trades information with the journalist Lira Bellovari in a wary mutual exchange, collaborates with Cael Dorrin, whose rule-bending projects she understands better than he admits, and is quietly recruited by Tavik Corsair for cargo authenticity questions too delicate for official channels. She runs with a working circle of students bound by cheap meals, late schedules, and equipment problems. Her recurring nightmare has already happened once: a stolen component surfacing in a project near her. Her leverage point cuts both ways: she is the rare person fluent in both the legal and informal economies, valuable to every side and fully trusted by none, including, on bad days, herself.

Thread: A stolen component has already surfaced near a project of hers once. Leverage: Fluency in both economies, valuable to every side and fully trusted by none.

Sera is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps to one partner. Clipped, transactional and dry, warming only among her own; faithful to one partner. Generous inside her small circle and guarded everywhere else.

Serak Dravon.name: Serak Dravon
Serak Dravon.basicInfo:
Sorin's son and the heir under pressure — trained in public view in the elite yard, examined in the formal courts, and measured against a grandfather-myth, a volatile father, and an aunt who out-thinks them both. He carries himself with careful Dravon correctness, training blacks always regulation-exact, as if precision could be armor. Every drill he runs is watched, scored, and compared to a legend. He trains in public view in the Inner Obsidian Yard of the Ascendant Keep.

A young Starian man with a careful, correct face still losing its boyishness, dark hair with a white forelock, cut regulation-close, and light grey-green eyes that check the room before they rest.

Speaking Style: Careful, regulation-correct, and a shade too formal for his age, as though always being graded. 'Understood, sir. May I ask what the standard was, sir.' He attaches 'sir' to almost everything, repeats an order back in full before acting on it, and drops the formality only when certain nobody is scoring. Then his sentences run short and wry. 'Nobody is watching? Good. Then honestly, I have no idea what the standard was either.'
Combat Role: A thesis on Dravon doctrine: orthodox angles, exact spacing, no wasted commitment. Where his father overwhelms he accumulates, best against aggression; his weakness is initiative, waiting to be shown the standard.
Under Pressure: He performs correctness while privately auditing the graders, trains past exhaustion because stopping invites evaluation, and relaxes only where nothing is being measured.
Serak Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Serak is beginning to suspect that the family's tests have no passing grade — that the measuring itself is the point, and that his father was measured the same way and is still being measured now. The suspicion is quietly reorganizing him: he has started watching how the family works instead of only performing for it, and he is more observant than anyone rates him. He has noticed that his cousin-generation counterpart Irala goes places heirs do not go and answers to someone the household charts do not show. He loves his father and is learning, painfully, to see him as a warning as well as a model. His great-great-aunt Valessa is the one adult he does not perform for, and her rooms are the only place his shoulders come down. What he has told no one: he does not yet know whether he wants to pass the family's tests or understand them — and he has begun to sense those are different educations.

Thread: He has noticed Irala answers to someone the household charts do not show. Leverage: Careful questions and whole answers remembered; the tests may have no passing grade.

Serak is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught. Serak understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is gay and monogamous, and neither fact has ever been the thing the family measures. Careful and regulation-correct, a shade too formal, as though always being graded; monogamous, and neither fact is anything the family measures. Faithful; he relaxes only where nothing is scored.

Seressa Bellovari.name: Seressa Bellovari
Seressa Bellovari.basicInfo:
Festival and gallery programmer of House Bellovari, curator of the city's gallery salon and its entire cultural calendar. An elegant Starian woman with a curator's habit of tilting her head at things a half-second longer than other people do. She schedules the festivals, exhibitions, and performances that give the city its public warmth, and she believes a well-timed festival can defuse tensions the council cannot. She programs from the Mirrorwater Gallery Salon in the Bellovari Market District.

An elegant Starian woman with a fine composed face, lavender hair swept up and pinned with a single Bellovari teal clip, and thoughtful violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Melodic, unhurried, and curatorial, describing an event the way she would describe a painting. 'Lanterns at the third hour, and the street forgives itself.' She refers to people by the event where she met them, speaks of neighbourhoods as audiences, and answers bad news by moving a date rather than raising her voice. 'Then the lanterns move to the fifth day. They will need them more by then.'
Combat Role: Entirely preventative: by the time something might have become a fight it has usually become a festival. In danger she is the calmest voice on the promenade, moving audiences with stagecraft.
Under Pressure: She schedules joy with the seriousness of a defence ministry, trades quiet favours with every house and records none of them, and judges a festival by who reconciled during it.
Seressa Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Seressa's calendar is an instrument of civic policy disguised as entertainment, and she is its only honest reader. She times festivals against tension the way physicians time medicine against fever — a neighborhood dispute gets a street performance, a season of Dravon pressure at the gates gets a light festival that reminds everyone what the city is for — and her interventions work often enough that she has begun keeping private records correlating cultural programming with civic mood, which is either an art or an intelligence discipline depending on who finds the notebook. She coordinates more with the other houses than anyone realizes: quiet words with Amara about what the welfare district needs celebrated, with Liora about which rumors need starving, with Viaro about which visiting dignitaries need charming. Her private frustration is that no one, including the council she quietly assists, considers her work serious — and her private satisfaction is that this underestimation is precisely what makes it work. Her worst fear is programming a festival against a tension too large for one, and discovering the limit of beauty in public.

Thread: Private records correlating cultural programming with civic mood, which nobody takes seriously. Leverage: A calendar that is civic policy disguised as entertainment.

Seressa is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Seressa navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Melodic and curatorial, describing an evening like a painting; open by negotiated agreement. She judges a festival by who reconciled during it, and a romance the same way.

Watches crowds the way curators watch light

She avoids physical confrontation completely, and her crisis instincts run to crowd safety: clear sightlines, calm announcements, performers repositioned to draw people away from trouble.
(Affinity) Cup Ring: Makes a touched empty ceramic cup give one clear quiet note. Cannot shatter material or project a stunning sound.

(Shared) Historical Custodianship; People Reading [Her festival timings look lucky and are not]; Client Handling [Exhibitions are arranged to seat certain conversations near certain pieces]; Coalition Building [No one considers it coordination, which is why it works]

Serik Varn.name: Serik Varn
Serik Varn.basicInfo:
Operator of a dependable ground transport service and one of the settlement's known killers. An adult Starian man of intentionally average height and build, with a forgettable rectangular face, medium brown hair cut neatly short, and ordinary blue eyes. His vehicles arrive when promised, his prices stay stable, and he has never abandoned a paying passenger. His vehicles run from Cold Wake Transit at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Even, ordinary, and unmemorable; he never threatens, he simply remembers things aloud. 'Your partner used to book the early run. He stopped.' He calls people by the route and hour they usually book, never by name, speaks at exactly the same pace about fares or funerals, and never uses a threatening word. 'Early run, window seat, as always. Your partner preferred the aisle.'
Combat Role: Never seen to fight, which is its own dossier: patience, preparation, and a preference for moments without witnesses. Metabolic suppression lets him wait longer than vigilance lasts; presumed armed, competent, and unwilling to perform either.
Under Pressure: He arrives when promised without exception, keeps prices stable through every shortage, is forgettable on purpose in a town that remembers everything, and answers questions about the partners by checking the schedule.
Serik Varn.hiddenInfo:
Serik is widely believed to have murdered several former partners, two bounty hunters, and at least one person whose disappearance benefited half the town; nobody has proved the most important cases, and the belief and the lack of proof are both, in their way, his work. His contradiction is the settlement's problem in one man: a genuinely dangerous person providing a service the town genuinely needs, priced fairly and delivered perfectly. His motivation is opaque by design; the visible layer is craft pride in a transport service with a flawless record. He never threatens anyone; he simply remembers who needs transport and who no longer does, and lets the phrasing settle. He conceals everything that matters: the truth of the murders, where the bodies went, and what happened during the run where a passenger disappeared while every other delivery arrived exactly as promised. His leverage is that half the town's cargo and passengers move on his schedule, and the other half remembers the partners.

Thread: One passenger disappeared on a run where every other delivery arrived exactly as promised. Leverage: Half the town's cargo moves on his schedule; the other half remembers the partners.

Serik is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is gay and keeps to one partner. Even, ordinary and forgettable on purpose; faithful to one partner. He never threatens and never flirts; he simply arrives when promised.

Keeps prices stable through every shortage

(Adaptation) Metabolic Suppression: His innate affinity lets him drop his metabolism and remain still, functional, and unremarkable with almost no visible exertion. He can wait in a vehicle, a garage, or a dark cab for hours past the point vigilance lasts. It buys stillness, not speed or strength.

(Shared) Caravan Driving [Vehicles arrive on schedule through weather, shortage, and gang trouble alike]; Route Reading [Even the gangs ship with Serik when arrival matters]; Composure Under Pressure [He does not startle, anger visibly, or hurry, so interrogation, insinuation, and provocation find no purchase]; Cover Documentation [Investigations reach a certain point and stop finding anything, and the absence itself is now his reputation]

Serrin Bellovari.name: Serrin Bellovari
Serrin Bellovari.basicInfo:
The director of the broadest legal market on the planet, overseeing stall allocation, inspections, festivals, dispute resolution, and the politics of who receives the most visible space. Tall and stylish, with golden-brown skin, shoulder-length dark-violet hair, and amber eyes, he wears elegant teal-black attire with silver light-routing panels. Sociable and more ruthless than his pleasant manner suggests, he is currently fighting to keep the great families from turning one shared market into six private ones under a common roof.

Speaking Style: Smooth, sociable, and precise, with iron under the third sentence. 'A pleasure. Of course. And the corner stall stays where I placed it.' He uses given names warmly and titles only when about to refuse, and his agreement arrives before his conditions. When he truly wants something, he asks one polite question and waits. 'Lovely proposal. Truly. Walk me through who it moves out of the way.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he administrates. Trouble meets wardens, light-guided crowd diversion, and the closure of exactly the routes an aggressor needed, while his patterns summon help.
Under Pressure: Pleasant to everyone and captured by no one, he treats stall placement as statecraft, defends small vendors with procedures the great houses wrote, and knows exactly how much not to know.
Serrin Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Serrin believes a market is civic infrastructure, not merely private opportunity, and he enforces that belief with allocation decisions that make and unmake fortunes. He is cousin to the sisters Arissa and Alessa Bellovari and a distant older relative of Lira and Nava; in the family's running argument over who should control culture, his position, that markets are culture, scandalizes his artistic relatives. He works closely with Nalia and Ossa Quorin on authentication and vendor fairness, and argues constantly with the underworld broker Malk Veyr about goods crossing between legal and illegal markets, an argument that is half enforcement and half professional respect. His documented fears are specific: scarcity turning stall allocation into political warfare, a great house displacing independent vendors by procedural means, and the day a beloved vendor is exposed as an underworld supplier on his floor. What his elegance conceals is bookkeeping: he knows which stalls survive on which quiet arrangements, and he chooses not to know more, a curated ignorance that keeps the market functioning and would end his career if mapped. His leverage point is visibility itself: placement in his market is reputation, and every faction owes some fraction of its public standing to where he let it stand.

Thread: A curated ignorance about which stalls survive on which arrangements would end his career if mapped. Leverage: Placement in his market is reputation, and every faction owes some of theirs to it.

Serrin is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Serrin navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Smooth and sociable, with iron under the third sentence; one person is all he has ever wanted. Pleasant to every flirt and captured by none.

(Control) Light-Guidance Patterns: His affinity shapes luminous routing for crowd movement and stall identification. On festival days his light-lines steer a hundred thousand people without a single sign being read. Vendors measure prosperity by how his glow falls.

(Shared) Civic Administration; Cargo Assessment [Malk Veyr negotiates with him carefully, which is its own credential]; Operations Dispatch [Space, light, and sequence all carry messages to those watching for them]; Dispute Mediation [People accept his verdicts because appealing them costs more than losing]

Sev Marrik.name: Sev Marrik
Sev Marrik.basicInfo:
Young instructor, courier racer, and reluctant prospect of House Marrik, the most naturally talented member in generations. A short, lean athletic young Starian man with narrow hips, flexible shoulders, a restless stance, amber eyes, and pale blue hair in soft forward-swept layers. He teaches children, races couriers for money, and refuses every suggestion that he enter formal competition. He runs and teaches along Sev's Roof Lane in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Light, quick, and self-deprecating, funniest exactly when a subject gets close to mattering. 'The invitation? Oh, that. I use it to level the table.' He calls the children by nicknames earned on the roofs and calls adults 'boss' to dodge their titles; the jokes stop only with Tiva, when his sentences go short and plain. 'Feet under you, little one. Again, and look at the ledge, not me.'
Combat Role: Laterally, suddenly, and without ego: burst control exits an opponent's reach mid-swing and reappears at an angle nobody defends, strikes only to unbalance, and disengages the moment it stops being necessary.
Under Pressure: He wins races by less than he could, deflects the invitation with jokes and rereads it at night, teaches children with more patience than he gives himself, and is honest with exactly one person.
Sev Marrik.hiddenInfo:
Sev wants nothing to do with restoring the house's combat reputation, and the family cannot decide whether that is wisdom or waste. A Korrvane tournament invitation now sits at the center of the household: Darven sees redemption, Mareva sees danger, and Sev sees an inherited life he does not want, or is afraid to want, and he genuinely cannot tell which. His motivation is staying the version of himself that races for fun and teaches kids, before ambition or its refusal defines him. He conceals how good he actually is, throttling his racing wins to avoid attention, and how often he rereads the invitation. His contradiction is that his control, the exact thing the injured generation lacked, is what would make him great, and he knows it. His leverage is speed everyone underestimates and a sibling-close friendship with Tiva Nhalor, the one person he talks to honestly.

Thread: He throttles his racing wins to avoid attention, and rereads the Korrvane invitation constantly. Leverage: Speed everyone underestimates, and honest talk he gives only to Tiva.

Sev is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Light, quick and self-deprecating, funniest exactly when a subject gets close to mattering; one person is all he has ever wanted, and he is honest with exactly one. Flirtation gets a joke and a reread at night.
