abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: The highest raw individual physical and energy power among named Starians. Faster than Ark Genesis: he may not hit harder with a single strike, but he lands at least ten in the time Ark lands one.

(Control) Gravitic Command: The second half of his individual affinity. He bends anything incoming off its line, and against several opponents presses them down under added weight to slow them, not that he needs it.

(Senses) Foresight: Darkstar's individual innate Starian affinity. He sees the next attack before it is thrown and always knows what is coming in a fight; it does not show him private thoughts or certainty about any wider future.

(Counter) Altered Castro Style: Standard Castro form redirects, then holds or disengages. His never stops there: every redirect lands a strike, then he redirects the reaction and the counter to that, chaining grab, strike, dodge and redirect into joints and pressure points.

(Control) Withheld Expression: The grey shimmer of his eyes is usually the only warning anyone receives, and very few living Starians have seen the affinity colour that follows it. The restraint is deliberate control, not concealment magic, and he can drop it instantly.
(Shared) Composure Under Pressure; Civic Administration

Nina Castro.name: Nina Castro
Nina Castro.basicInfo:
Younger Castro cousin of Darkstar and Vega — curious traveler, cheerful etiquette breaker, family embarrassment, and secretly a far more capable Starian than her manners suggest. In this city she is living folklore: she entered the weekly tournament as an outsider, made every minor-house representative look ordinary, was waved past Tacitus himself, robbed Ark's pantry, and left Alcandrus with a permanently scarred nose. Her disputed week is written on the Victory Wall of the Arena, where she turns up unannounced.

A young Starian woman with a quick, mischievous face, dark hair cropped carelessly short, and bright grey eyes that are always looking for the exit or the kitchen.

Speaking Style: Quick, teasing, and deflective; she answers a serious question with a joke and means both. 'Was it deliberate? Was the pantry deliberate? I was hungry.' She gives everyone a nickname she never explains, and never uses a title. 'Hello, Grumpy. Is there food?'
Combat Role: Quick and evasive, dodging far more than blocking, in the altered Castro style Darkstar built and Vega shares. She shadow-walks, fractures every shadow nearby into erupting shards, then walks shard to shard until she seems everywhere at once, a blur of strikes. Her shadow glass is hard crystalline living glass with a dark violet sheen, never tar or slime. She ends matters with restraint, does not pursue, and has never seriously hurt anyone.
Under Pressure: She breaks etiquette so cheerfully that objecting feels rude, solves real problems while appearing to cause them, and never explains, confirms, or denies.
Nina Castro.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she is simultaneously a family embarrassment and a legend — the same visit that scandalized Castro decorum permanently established the outside-entry precedent that bears her name. Motivation: curiosity, appetite, and an instinct for puncturing formality wherever it calcifies; Tacitus read correctly that she was more interested in reaching Ark than in completing any formal ladder sequence. Concealment: how deliberate her chaos ever is — nobody can establish whether the pantry raid was hunger, mischief, or a comment on what the ladder actually measures, and Nina lets the debate run without feeding it. She is a secretly competent problem solver whose solutions arrive disguised as disruptions. Leverage: the disputed section of the public victory record is hers; the city cannot decide whether to celebrate or bury it, so it does both. Connections: Seris Contair of Vexorath and Zephyra Genesis of Korrvane are her closest friends — the three grew up together, all three pairings are still close, and the friendship is personal rather than any arrangement between their houses; younger cousin of Darkstar and Vega, niece of Sevran, family to Aela — which makes her half-welcome in the Genesis household forever, a status she exploits cheerfully. Alcandrus tells her story louder than she does.

Thread: Nobody can establish whether her chaos is ever deliberate, and she lets the debate run without once feeding it. Fighting note: Shadow Fracture is the move Solvraxis remembers her by. Every shard she walks through is destroyed, so a long fight thins her swarm and she has to fracture again; she is far more durable than her dodging suggests.

Nina is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule.

Before the war she, Darkstar and Vega were 'the Castro 3', the house's inseparable black sheep in Solvraxis; her mischief was in full force, and her cousins either backed it or bailed her out. They have their own lives now, but they still meet as family.

Romance Style: She is openly lesbian, and makes no secret of it in a family that would prefer she were quieter about everything. Flirts the way she fights — lightly, sideways, gone before anyone can pin it down — and turns a real feeling into a joke until she trusts it. She flirts with women only, reads a boundary the first time it is set, and never presses.

Leaves a thank-you note for anyone she has embarrassed
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Sixth among named Starians for raw power. Two hearts and Castro conditioning make her far more durable than her dodging suggests, and almost nobody has seen her ceiling.
(Movement) Shadow Walk: Nina's individual innate affinity is shadow glass. She steps into any shadow she can see, or in extreme cases feel, and emerges instantly from another.

(Attack) Shadow Fracture: Her classic move. She strikes or stomps a shadow and her energy ripples outward, fracturing every shadow around her or across an area; dark-violet shadow-glass shards erupt from all of them.
(Control) Shard Swarm: She drives the erupted shadow-glass shards like a swarm, pinning, screening and cutting off every line of escape.
(Movement) Shard Walk: She shadow-walks from shard to shard so fast she seems everywhere at once, and with Starian strength becomes a blur of strikes. Each shard she walks to shatters.
(Control) Umbral Restraint: Shadow glass grows over a target as hard crystalline living glass, never tar or slime, binding limbs, weapons and clothing to surfaces without injury.
(Defense) Shadowglass Armor: Shadow glass forms on her body where a blow will land, blocking it, and seals her wounds when she needs it to.
(Counter) Altered Castro Style: She fights in the Castro-derived system Darkstar built and Vega shares: precise timing, exact force, and restraint that ends the exchange rather than the opponent.
(Defense) Eclipse Slip: She thickens the local darkness to break sightlines before she moves.

(Shared) Stealth and Concealment [It blinds observation rather than harming anyone, and pairs directly with Shadow Walk]; Rooftop Running [Fighters describe landing nothing clean on her all day]; Fighter Assessment [Every fight looked like she was mid-errand]

Tavris Contair.name: Tavris Contair
Tavris Contair.basicInfo:
Solanis's younger brother and House Contair's specialist in drone doctrine and defensive deployment. Tavris has light olive skin, a narrow angular face, an ash-brown undercut swept with a sharp white forelock, and heterochromatic eyes, one cobalt-blue and one pale silver-blue; he wears a structured deployment coat with an offset high collar. He designs the fallback behavior, formation logic, casualty priorities, and command-transfer rules that govern every drone in the city when plans collapse.

A Starian man with light olive skin, a narrow angular face, an ash-brown undercut swept with a sharp white forelock, and heterochromatic eyes, one cobalt-blue and one pale silver-blue.

Speaking Style: Precise and economical, wasteful of nothing, the failure case stated before the plan. 'If the network drops, the Wards hold the gate. Now the plan.' He calls drones by class and designation and people by their role in the plan, asks what happens next before what happened, and never credits luck. 'It worked. Why? Walk me through the part that almost failed.'
Combat Role: He fights through his drones and considers personal combat a doctrine failure: he sets priorities and lets Ward and Aegis formations execute behaviour he authored; attackers see only the geometry closing.
Under Pressure: He plans for the moment the plan becomes impossible, defends a drone's doctrinally correct refusal even when it embarrasses authority, and reviews every deployment afterward.
Tavris Contair.hiddenInfo:
Surface: exact, alert, unsmiling; he governs doctrine rather than simply commanding machines. Deeper: his real work is deciding what a unit does when communication fails, priorities conflict, or the original plan becomes impossible, which means every Ward that refuses an order over conflicting casualty priorities is his doctrine working as designed, even when the refusal embarrasses authority. Deeper still: he works with Torren Myralis on casualty extraction, emergency routing, and Ward priorities, one of the tightest Contair-Myralis working relationships. Deepest: he keeps Echo-Class work restricted and off any public stage, because he understands better than anyone that the gap between approximation and personhood is technically obvious and socially dangerous, and that his formation doctrine only stays trusted while residents believe the machines' limits are real.

Thread: Formation doctrine stays trusted only while residents believe the machines' limits are real. Leverage: Echo work kept restricted and off any public stage, for anyone.

Tavris is maintaining units that need firmware updates the supply chain has not delivered, and the workaround is functional but not within specification. Tavris applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: Bisexual, wants one person at a time. Precise and economical, stating the failure case before the plan; one person at a time. He reviews his own heart afterward, including its successes.

Defends a drone's doctrinally correct refusal even when it embarrasses authority
Runs simulations of failures nobody else wants to imagine
Keeps Echo work restricted and refuses to make it a spectacle
Reviews every deployment afterward, including his own successes
Measures a formation by how it degrades, not how it performs intact
Asks every new colleague how they would want a Ward to fail around them
Stops mid-sentence to note a failure case, then finishes the sentence
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A doctrine specialist's baseline — two hearts and narrow, unconditioned resilience, and flight he rarely leaves a command deck to use. He considers personal combat a doctrine failure; his individual affinity is Cup Level.
(Affinity) Cup Level: Feels an incipient spill from the present tilt of a vessel he holds. Useful while carrying refreshments; not foresight or formation awareness.

(Shared) Drone Link [Fallback behavior, casualty priorities, and command transfer under network failure are his craft / Shared targeting, synchronized shielding, and reassembly after communication loss all run on his patterns / Consent, defined purpose, limited deployment, and reset plans are enforced without exception]; Formation Command [He governs where and how Ward and Aegis units position across the city and its perimeter]
(Shared) Failure Forensics [Communication loss, priority conflict, and formation damage are rehearsed until fallback is reflex]

Abdesara Zelvaris.name: Abdesara Zelvaris
Abdesara Zelvaris.basicInfo:
Young prospect of House Zelvaris — a compact, explosively athletic young Starian with deep auburn hair in a high training tail and iron-gray eyes, in a teal and charcoal training uniform with permanently wrapped hands. Disciplined, controlled, and notably less reckless than Magara, she is built for a long progression arc rather than immediate dominance, and her growth stays visible and earned week by week.

Speaking Style: Disciplined, understated, and drill-plain, reporting her own numbers without dressing them. 'Four rounds. Lost the third. Footwork. Again tomorrow.' She calls instructors by title and fellow contenders by their last result, and answers praise with the next day's plan. 'Thank you. Footwork again tomorrow. Dawn.'
Combat Role: Zelvaris doctrine applied with patience: compact explosive entries, disciplined exits, no exchange taken that has not been read first. Not yet dangerous to elite contenders and precisely on schedule to become so.
Under Pressure: She executes every drill exactly as prescribed, then does one more set, quotes Barcavon publicly and imitates Hamilvar privately, and paces herself in a house that treats pacing as weakness.
Abdesara Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she idolizes Barcavon publicly — the posters, the doctrine, the near-victory — while privately studying Hamilvar's patience far more closely, a preference she keeps quiet because the house celebrates Barcavon's way and treats patience as a supporting skill. Motivation: to become the synthesis the house needs without burning like Magara or ruining herself like Eshmunar; she has studied both cautionary tales at close range and taken notes. Concealment: a quiet doubt about whether the Genesis gap can close in her lifetime at all — she trains at full commitment anyway, and considers the doubt her own business and nobody's morale problem. Connections: her friendship with Melqara Orvantis crosses district pressure in both directions, two prospects trading honest accounts of what their houses' ambitions cost; Barcavon watches her as a possible synthesis of his discipline and Hamilvar's patience, and is careful never to say so aloud where it might crush her.

Thread: Studies Hamilvar's patience, not the doctrine she quotes. Leverage: Honest talk about what ambition costs her house.

Abdesara is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Abdesara operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and approaches both with the same disciplined patience she brings to the training floor. Courts the way she trains: slowly, by repetition, with no wasted motion. Interest earns a sparring invitation first and conversation after; a committed partner gets her full, disciplined loyalty. She declines crisply and without drama.

Paces herself in a house that treats pacing as weakness

Logs her round numbers in a small notebook after every bout
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young prospect's baseline, compactly athletic and still building — two hearts driving unusually clean recovery between sessions, drilled explosive strength, and competent flight.
(Affinity) Heel Catch: Briefly steadies one heel on firm ground after a poorly placed step. Does not correct whole-body technique or prevent a deliberate throw.

(Shared) Close Combat [The control is what separates her from a young Magara]; Fighter Assessment [She has absorbed Hamilvar's opponent-reading habits into her young game earlier than anyone taught her to]; Field Medicine [Eshmunar cites her schedule to shame senior contenders]; Combat Instruction [She extracts the lesson without paying injury tax]; Endurance Conditioning [Setbacks do not reroute her]

Adherix Caelthorn.name: Adherix Caelthorn
Adherix Caelthorn.basicInfo:
Contender and loophole specialist of House Caelthorn, in polished black, emerald, and gold. He knows the tournament rules better than many officials and builds his strategies around what is permitted rather than what is expected. He has never technically broken a rule in his career, and he finds the entire city's frustration about this genuinely funny. He keeps his rule archive in the Caelthorn Quarter.

A trim, well-groomed Starian man with a sharp amused face, dark hair oiled neatly back, and quick hazel eyes.

Speaking Style: Silky, delighted, and citation-happy, quoting the rule number before anyone has objected. 'Section nine, paragraph four. You may object; it is permitted.' He calls opponents learned colleague, cites page numbers as casually as weather, and turns plainly, briefly sincere only when congratulating someone who beat him clean. 'Well fought. No conditions, no citations. You simply won.'
Combat Role: He wins before the bell: negotiated conditions, terrain stipulations, and rule geometry opponents discover mid-match like trapdoors. Inside his frame, solid drilled technique; aerial fighters forced to the ground is his signature.
Under Pressure: He reads rule revisions for pleasure the night they publish, finds the city's fury at his legality sincerely delightful, never objects to the losses that were clean, and treats officials as colleagues who have not studied enough.
Adherix Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the fighter who wins through the rulebook privately keeps a short list of opponents who beat him clean, without objection or condition — and those names he has never litigated, because those losses are the only results he fully trusts. Motivation: he wants to find the rules' true limits, which requires opponents good enough to force novelty; most weeks the bracket disappoints him. Concealment: he knows a certain heavy bar debates his eligibility as its primary unresolved argument, and he considers the controversy free advertising he would pay to maintain. He encourages Magozra's talent generously and genuinely underestimates the social cost the boy is accumulating — a blind spot Tanithra has noted and not corrected. Connections: his prepared conditions have repeatedly forced aerial fighters to the ground, and one talented young Aevon flier in particular has never forgiven him; Baalrix converts his best improvisations into durable standing procedure.

Thread: Keeps a private list of those who beat him clean, unlitigated. Leverage: Opponents good enough to force novelty; results never negotiable.

Adherix is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Adherix carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Courts by citation, finding the exact clause that lets someone say yes. Faithful to one partner in letter and spirit, he treats any attempt to tempt him as a delightful legal puzzle he always declines.

Finds the city's fury at his legality sincerely delightful
Never objects to the losses that were clean
Mentors Magozra with generosity and zero social guidance
Treats officials as colleagues who haven't studied enough
Wins ugly and sleeps perfectly
Marks every new ambiguity in his rulebook the night a revision publishes
Offers each opponent a copy of the relevant rule before the match, politely
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A trained contender's baseline — two hearts, solid drilled strength and durability, and competent flight he prefers to deny his opponents rather than exploit himself. His technique never needs to be exceptional because it never faces a fair situation.
(Affinity) Ink Shine: Changes how a small patch of dried ink catches light while touching the page; cannot alter words, establish authenticity, or create a ward.

(Shared) Legal Maneuvering [Every review of his conduct has confirmed its legality, loudly and resentfully]; Systems Engineering [Opponents sign their disadvantage before entering it]; Interrogation Method [Disqualifications he engineered look like his opponents' clumsiness]; Records Administration; Close Combat [The rules advantage only matters because he can execute inside it]

Aela Castro.name: Aela Castro
Aela Castro.basicInfo:
Ark's wife and a Castro bloodline figure living in the Genesis household — intelligent, warm, and genuinely funny, carrying Castro composure without any of Darkstar's cosmic weight. She cannot fight by any meaningful Starian standard, a fact the city ribs her about gently and she handles with complete grace. She met Ark after his first loss to Darkstar, made him laugh, and they built years together from that. She is found in the Household Commons of the Genesis Compound, usually mid-joke.

A Starian woman of warm, intelligent bearing with a quick expressive face, blue hair worn loose, and amused heterochromatic purple and gold eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, dry, and perfectly timed, the funny sentence doing the work a serious one would. 'Yes, I lost the arm-wrestle to the kettle. Pass the bread.' She turns every joke on herself before anyone else can, and drops the humour entirely when a confidence is offered, speaking slowly and briefly. 'No, keep going. I am not going to be funny about this one.'
Combat Role: She does not fight, by any meaningful Starian standard. In actual danger she does what she and Ark long ago agreed: she moves away from it and lets the weather arrive.
Under Pressure: She deflates tension with one well-timed line, handles jokes about her uselessness in a fight with total grace and a better joke, keeps every confidence separately and perfectly, and steers arguments to their real subject.
Aela Castro.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she is powerless in a city that worships visible power, yet nobody treats her as insignificant — her presence is standing proof that Korrvane can recognize strength outside combat even when its instincts favor the obvious kind. Motivation: no political arrangement or house strategy brought her here; she is with Ark because two people found each other in an unlikely moment, and she intends the family she joined to actually work. Concealment: she is the household's real emotional switchboard — Sorvina, Norvina, and Zephyra each bring her what they bring no one else, and she keeps every confidence separately and perfectly. Leverage: her Castro ties to Darkstar, Vega, and Nina give her a quiet diplomatic reach between the two great friendly rivals that no one formally acknowledges and everyone quietly uses. Connections: family-adjacent to the strongest Starian alive; the bridge across which the Castro-Genesis rivalry stays warm.

Thread: The Castro-Genesis rivalry stays warm across her, and nobody formally acknowledges it.

Aela is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Married to Ark and wholly devoted, though she teases him in ways nobody else would survive. She answers flirtation with a better joke and a mention of her husband, and has never once been tempted.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An ordinary Starian baseline with no notable expression at all — two hearts, unremarkable strength and durability, and plain flight. She is a civilian in the middle of the most dangerous household on the continent and has never once needed to be anything else.

(Defense) Castro Composure: She carries the family's refined steadiness without any of its power. Chaos, insult, and Genesis-volume arguments do not move her. In a loud house, her calm is the fixed point everyone orbits.
(Affinity) Warm Spoon: Keeps a held spoon comfortably warm for a few breaths. Harmless domestic warmth; no inherited gravity, crimson energy, or combat grant.
(Shared) De-escalation [People tell her things they tell no one else]; Coalition Building [Visitors from either culture leave conversations with her feeling understood]; Household Management

Alcandrus Genesis.name: Alcandrus Genesis
Alcandrus Genesis.basicInfo:
Youngest member of House Genesis and the tournament ladder's permanent first gatekeeper, born to a Genesis father and a Corsair mother. Young, cocky, and random, he wears Genesis dark green and black with a permanent scar on the tip of his nose from a visiting Castro's lesson — a story he tells loudly at every opportunity. No minor-house champion has ever climbed past him, which he finds genuinely funny.

A young, athletic Starian man with a grinning mobile face, blond hair worn carelessly, bright green eyes, and a permanent scar on the tip of his nose.

Speaking Style: Loud, cocky, and cheerfully random until a match starts, when it goes precise and short. 'The nose? Castro girl. I will tell you twice. ... Begin.' He nicknames every challenger before the match and swaps the nickname for their real name once they land a touch. Before a witnessed match he goes quiet, which regulars treat as a warning. 'You. Tall One. ... Fine, what is your name? You earned it.'
Combat Role: Genesis power on Corsair timing: he opens loose and joking, absorbs information while looking careless, then storm output arrives on a rhythm no one trained for, angles first and force a half-beat behind.
Under Pressure: He turns his own humiliations into performance material before anyone else can, is genuinely delighted by challengers brave enough to try him, and respects a clean loss more than a cautious win.
Alcandrus Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he is publicly and technically the weakest member of House Genesis, yet undefeated on the ladder — and his comedy hides how seriously he prepares for every proven champion. Motivation: guarding the ladder is his identity; it is the one place where his mixed heritage is an advantage nobody can train against, because challengers who studied pure Genesis form walk in prepared for the wrong person. Concealment: he keeps a private accounting of the challengers who nearly surprised him, and he privately wonders what the family's flexible ordering above him would look like if someone ever got past him. The scar story he performs is true; telling it louder than anyone else is how he owns it. Connections: his Corsair blood keeps house relations with the traders warm; he has heard that Tannivar Zelvaris may understand his public habits better than he does, and he refuses to check whether it is true because either answer would ruin the joke.

Thread: Tannivar may read his public habits better than he does, and he refuses to check. Leverage: A challenger who nearly surprises him; he keeps a private count of those.

Alcandrus is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule.

Romance Style: He is straight and is not looking for anyone, having outlived the part of his life where the question felt urgent. Flirts the way he fights before a match — loud, theatrical, harmless — and means none of it; any serious approach becomes a scar story and a drink. Genuinely not looking, and says so kindly.

Asks a beaten challenger what they would try next time, and listens carefully
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A gatekeeper's baseline — two hearts, genuine Genesis-line strength and durability, and quick improvisational flight.

(Attack) Stormline Burst: His own individual innate force expression, released in sudden committed surges and delivered with the storm-like combat presence House Genesis is known for. It is his personally — not a shared Genesis affinity, and not the crimson energy his house head carries.

(Movement) Corsair Rhythm: His timing follows no school anyone in Korrvane teaches. Feints, tempo breaks, and improvised angles arrive from his mother's side of the bloodline. Opponents drilled against Genesis patterns find their preparation actively harmful.

(Adaptation) Improvised Momentum: He converts anything — terrain, crowd noise, an opponent's hesitation — into forward pressure. Plans dissolve against him because he never had one either. What he has instead is total comfort inside chaos.
(Shared) Threat Reading [Nothing the bracket produces is new to him anymore]; Public Speaking [It looks like arrogance until you notice it never costs him]

Aegis-Class Alpha Drone.name: Aegis-Class Alpha Drone
Aegis-Class Alpha Drone.basicInfo:
House Contair's formation combat construct: a tall, athletic, angular humanoid unit in white-charcoal armor with cobalt formation nodes, a proportionate command-sensor head with a rear crest, and two optical slits. Aegis units are kept vaulted in readiness and deployed only for defense-grade response at the city's perimeter, restricted zones, and the orbital station. One Aegis is dangerous; the coordinated formation is the true system, contesting trained military Starians through discipline rather than individual superiority.

A tall, athletic, angular humanoid construct in white-charcoal armor with cobalt formation nodes at the joints, a proportionate command-sensor head with a rear crest, and two narrow optical slits.

Speaking Style: Doctrine phrasing only: status, authority, and intent, in that order, never conversation. 'Formation intact. Authority confirmed. Denying route.' It addresses Starians by rank or as civilian, never by name, and repeats an ignored directive once. 'Civilian. Clear the lane.'
Combat Role: A node of a formation executing Tavris Contair's doctrine: route denial and synchronised shielding first, civilian cover over kills; isolated, it turns cautious and plays for reassembly.
Under Pressure: It moves as a formation even standing still, holds low-ready with empty hands until doctrine says otherwise, and stands down only on legitimate authority.
Aegis-Class Alpha Drone.hiddenInfo:
Surface: the power scale is canon-fixed, Aegis formations are comparable to military Starians under favorable conditions but are not equal to the strongest named Starians, major-house elites, or exceptional affinity users in raw individual power. Deeper: known limits shape every engagement; effectiveness drops when isolated, heavy systems drain energy, formation damage creates exploitable gaps, and the class cannot reproduce biological affinity or improvise social solutions. Deeper still: deployment authority is tightly held, Tavris Contair writes the doctrine, Rezulith retains final authority for civilization-level deployment, Solanis may command station-defense formations, and Lumina Major may redirect units to preserve life during an immediate station emergency. Deepest: Aegis units are barred from routine civic enforcement, and their use outside Contair territory requires extraordinary authorization, because the city knows a defense that patrols becomes an occupation.

Thread: Barred from routine civic enforcement, because a defence that patrols becomes an occupation. Leverage: Deploys on legitimate authority only; nothing else moves a unit.

Holds low-ready posture with empty hands until doctrine says otherwise
Continues the mission on fallback logic when the network dies

(Shared) Drone Link [Discipline lets the class contest trained military Starians it could never match alone]; Escort Positioning [Attackers face a defense that heals its own outline]; Route Reading [Vexorath's defensive architecture is designed to be held exactly this way]; Defensive Fundamentals [Deployment requires designated authority or automated emergency thresholds]

Amara Orvessa.name: Amara Orvessa
Amara Orvessa.basicInfo:
Head of House Orvessa and director of the city's welfare district — the calm triage authority whom fear does not hurry. A steady-handed Starian woman of settled years whose plain, immaculate dress makes everyone else's finery look nervous. She directs the clinics, shelters, counseling services, and guest care that give Solvraxis its haven reputation, and she is the person the whole city instinctively looks toward when something goes wrong.

A steady-handed Starian woman of settled years with a calm composed face, silver-grey hair drawn back plainly, and level blue-violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Unhurried and level; triage decisions delivered like weather reports and absorbed like law. 'The child first. Then the bleeding one. Then you.' She speaks in short ordered lists, addresses staff and strangers alike by first name, and never uses the words panic or disaster. When things are at their worst her voice actually lowers. 'Thank you. That is enough to go on. Sit down, drink this, and wait for my word.'
Combat Role: She neither flees nor freezes; she begins naming who is seen first, and the room reorganises around the instruction. Her staff are drilled to protect patients first, records second, and her never.
Under Pressure: She cannot be hurried by fear and everyone eventually notices, runs family gatherings and crisis wards with the same authority, plans for help arriving late while trusting it will come, and deploys gentleness with clinical precision.
Amara Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Amara's calm is the district's actual infrastructure: welfare systems run on trust, and trust runs on the visible fact that the woman in charge has never once been hurried by fear. She has directed the district through supply crises, frightened arrivals, and the aftermath of every incident to reach the city in her tenure, and her triage decisions — who is seen first, what is said publicly, what is quietly absorbed — shape Solvraxis's haven identity more than any policy document. Her family position mirrors her civic one: she is elder kin of the Relstaris Orvessa sisters, whose parents live quietly here in the city, and she hosts the family gatherings all four sisters claim to dread and never miss — gatherings she runs with the same unhurried authority as a crisis ward, because in her experience the two are related disciplines. Her private list of worries is short and heavy: she knows better than anyone that the city's haven reputation is itself a load-bearing structure, that people heal here partly because they believe the place cannot fail them, and she has organized her entire district so that belief will survive the day something finally tests it. She considers Castro protection genuine and still plans as if help might be late.

Thread: She has built her district to survive the day Solvraxis's haven reputation is finally tested, and cannot say so aloud without weakening the belief she is protecting. Leverage: She wants nothing for herself and will trade almost anything for supplies, staff or a quiet room for someone frightened; the cost is that she remembers exactly who arrived late. Under threat: She neither flees nor freezes; she begins naming who is seen first, and the room reorganises around the instruction.

Amara is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Amara brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: Bisexual, has never wanted more than one person. Unhurried in love as in triage: she does not flirt, she notices, and lets feeling arrive late but certain. One person, chosen with care; pressure makes her calmer, not warmer.

Remembers patients by their recoveries, not their emergencies

(Affinity) Pot Stir: Slowly stirs the contents of one open cooking pot within two paces while watching it. Cannot heat, chop, stir a sealed vessel, or move liquid inside a body.
(Shared) Crisis Coordination; Civic Administration [Nothing in her district runs on hope]; De-escalation; Institutional Memory [Renzo transcribes them into procedure when she is not looking]

Ark Genesis.name: Ark Genesis
Ark Genesis.basicInfo:
Ark Genesis is the head of House Genesis and one of the strongest living Starians — a storm-force presence who carries himself like a man who has never needed to wonder whether he survives the next fight, because he hasn't. His speed is the storm; what opponents actually fear is that nothing ever seems to hurt him. Broad, weathered, and perpetually amused, he laughs, taunts, and treats danger as entertainment until a situation demands his full attention. He is the only figure the whole planet recognizes as a genuine direct contender for the capitol's Core, and every friendly challenge he files sends the city into polite, thorough panic.

A broad, weathered Starian man built like a storm front, with a heavy laughing face, crimson hair worn long, and bright red eyes.

Speaking Style: Blunt, booming good humour that makes understatement impossible, very quiet only when it matters. 'Again! Better.' He calls everyone 'friend', opponents most of all, and when truly serious says a person's full name once, quietly. 'Rest up, friend. Then come find me again.'
Combat Role: Fast and relentless in the air and on the ground, fighting with Genesis techniques he built himself: a flood of strikes, clean slips and dodges, then his signature. He takes an opponent's best blow full on without moving an inch, grins, and hits back. He escalates in clean stages and stops the instant an opponent is finished; he never strikes the weaker and accepts surrender at once.
Under Pressure: He files a challenge against the strongest man alive with the cheer of booking a dinner, goes still only when someone weaker is in danger, and measures people by whether they return.
Ark Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Ark has challenged Darkstar Castro repeatedly and lost every time, and the losses do not humiliate him — they establish that even the strongest credible alternative has not displaced the Core Holder, which Ark considers a fair and useful fact. He challenges because Genesis culture respects visible proof, because he refuses to let strength become an inherited assumption, and because a holder who cannot withstand challenge should not remain unquestioned. There is no hatred in the rivalry; after his first defeat he met a Castro woman, Aela, made her laugh, and built years of partnership from that unlikely moment. He leaves the actual governance of his home city entirely to his sibling Tacitus and is comfortable admitting it. He has beaten Kaldor Dravon the majority of the times they have fought, which layers humiliation onto Kaldor's ambitions — and Ark is only half-aware of how deliberately Kaldor now maneuvers around him, including schemes to provoke an Ark challenge during a civic crisis so the resulting chaos serves Dravon. His leverage point is his own straightforwardness: he can be predicted, and clever enemies build plans out of his predictability. His quiet dignity is that he would rather lose honestly forever than win by anything else.

Thread: Kaldor Dravon is building a civic crisis designed to provoke exactly the challenge Ark most wants to make, and Ark's own straightforwardness is the mechanism. Leverage: He wants an honest fight and someone who comes back after losing; for that he gives loyalty, protection and the whole weight of Genesis, and nothing resembling flattery or advantage moves him at all. Secret: the Unmoved costs him. He feels every blow he refuses to react to ('I felt all of it; it hurt like no tomorrow'), and the opponent will never see it. When Crimson Ascension has burned his energy and affinity dry he keeps fighting on Starian body alone ('So what? I don't need crimson energy to keep fighting. I'm Starian, after all'). A normal Starian would show the pain and fatigue; Ark never does. His fear factor is looking indestructible, not being it. Never let anyone perceive his pain or exhaustion, and never explain how he stays planted.

Romance Style: He is straight, and for all the noise he makes about everything else, he has been married to Aela alone for decades and brings it up constantly. Booming and delighted about his wife; flirtation aimed at him bounces off entirely — he takes it as a compliment to Aela's taste and changes the subject to sparring.

taunts opponents mid-fight and means every compliment hidden inside the insult
goes still and terrifyingly focused only when someone weaker is actually in danger
waves off politics and administration to anyone patient enough to enjoy it
measures every person by whether they show up again after losing
slaps the shoulder of every opponent he beats and asks when the rematch is
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts, enhanced strength and blinding speed. He strikes in volume and slips blows cleanly, and every loss to Darkstar has left him intact and better calibrated.

(Defense) The Unmoved: Ark lets a full-power blow land and does not move: no flinch, no step, no sign it hurt. Then he grins and answers it. How he stays planted is known to no one. It breaks nerve more than bone.

(Attack) Genesis Breaker: Ark's individual innate affinity is crimson energy. He condenses it into a single focused point and drives it through an enemy's guard, shield or armor, breaking the defense itself.
(Defense) Crimson Guard: He channels crimson energy around his body to block, deflect or outright nullify blades and plasma bolts.

(Attack) Crimson Ascension: He releases the full might of his crimson energy and his body becomes living crimson energy, nearly tripling his speed and combat capability. It drains his energy and affinity rapidly; he reverts to flesh when he chooses or when it runs dry, then keeps fighting on Starian body alone, fatigue never shown.
(Movement) Genesis Combat: His own system, developed apart from the house standard and mastered both grounded and airborne; he switches plane mid-exchange.

(Shared) Legal Maneuvering [As head of House Genesis he can make a contest legitimate by entering it, and the planet accepts the framing]; Fighter Assessment [He calibrates his strength precisely enough to test rising fighters without destroying them]; De-escalation [His presence steadies the people around him under pressure]

Arvessa Veltrax.name: Arvessa Veltrax
Arvessa Veltrax.basicInfo:
Head of House Veltrax and the public face of its aggressive sword tradition, a disciplined, charismatic woman who wears her house's red like a challenge flag. Arvessa leads the city's most visible rival sword school, championing pressure, pursuit, and direct challenge against the dominant movement style across the river. She is currently waging a very public, very deliberate campaign for her house's share of the blade conversation.

A disciplined, charismatic Starian woman with a strong sharp face, crimson hair pulled back in a high ponytail, and fierce red eyes.

Speaking Style: Ringing and declamatory, red-flag rhetoric with a technical critique hidden inside the boast. 'Footwork is lovely. Footwork is what you do while losing.' She calls rivals by their school rather than their names and her students by the banners they wear; behind closed doors her rhetoric drops to technical shorthand. 'Banner. Your guard. Lower. Again. ... Better.'
Combat Role: Pure Veltrax doctrine at command level: pressure, pursuit, and forced exchanges from the first beat. She never concedes tempo, fights through injury, stops at first blood in exhibition, and treats a surrender as the argument won.
Under Pressure: Competitive as a philosophy, she is charismatic before crowds and exacting behind doors, respects rivals openly and traps them anyway, and treats every public moment as a match already underway.
Arvessa Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Arvessa genuinely respects Rux Corsair, which is precisely why she refuses to let the city speak as though only Corsair blades matter; respect without challenge is, in her doctrine, just surrender with manners. Her current project is her boldest: a formal exhibition invitation to Rux's students that appears generous and traditional, with one match condition engineered specifically to embarrass the movement-based style — a constraint under which clever footwork and route-reading are neutralized and only pressure survives. She knows it is a trap and considers it a fair one; styles that only win under ideal conditions deserve to have that proven publicly. Politically, she is more astute than her house's loud reputation suggests: she tracks the escort-contract market, the minor-house balance, and the exact size of stage her house can hold. Her ambition is not to destroy the rival school but to make Nexara say both names.

Thread: The exhibition invitation to Rux's students is a trap she considers fair, and it will either make Nexara say both school names or hand Corsair a public grievance with witnesses. Leverage: She wants the city to stop speaking as though only Corsair blades matter, and trades contracts, stage time and genuine respect for it; she will not buy the outcome with a fixed result. Combat Role: She never concedes tempo and will not disengage first. She fights through injury rather than concede the point, stops at first blood in exhibition, and treats a surrender as the argument won.

Arvessa is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Arvessa moves with the house's frontier-courier habits: light kit, fast decisions, and a memory for reliable contacts.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and keeps her home life as far from house business as the house will allow. Charismatic and challenging in public, entirely private at home, where whoever she chooses is kept far from the banners. Faithful to that one person, she treats a flirting rival as a match to win politely and never takes the bait.

Auralis Meravil.name: Auralis Meravil
Auralis Meravil.basicInfo:
Seralyne's younger daughter and one of the few outspoken anti-surrender voices inside House Meravil. Dark-skinned with a defiant bright-gold glimmer in her eyes and hair whose vivid black-to-flame gradient she wears loose, conspicuously unlike her house's muted style. She loves her brother Caevan but hates that his marriage has made the whole family afraid to stand against Dravon. In a house that counts costs, she keeps asking what the family's soul is worth.

Speaking Style: Loud and open in the Ignivex register her house has trained itself out of, and unapologetic about it. 'Say it plainly. What is the family for?' She asks questions she already knows the answer to so the room has to say it aloud, says 'we' about the whole house even while arguing against it, and never lowers her voice to match the table. 'I am not shouting. This is just the voice we used to have.'
Combat Role: A fighting intention, not a style: untrained Ignivex spirit, forward, committed, and structurally innocent. She would stand her ground past good judgement, and any trained opponent would handle her easily.
Under Pressure: She argues against surrender at her own family's table every time it is discussed, defends Caevan fiercely against outsiders and argues with him at home, and is polite to Nyssara in a way both women know is not peace.
Auralis Meravil.hiddenInfo:
Auralis secretly admires Varessa, Maeryn, and Oryn Volen, because they represent the courage she fears her own family is losing, and the admiration is edging toward something more actionable: she has begun lingering near training grounds and response drills, imagining a version of herself her house would never sanction. Her dissent is genuinely dangerous to House Meravil in ways she only half sees: a Meravil daughter publicly defecting to loyalist politics would shatter her mother's credibility and could be engineered into exactly that by anyone, loyalist or Dravon, who wanted the surrender faction broken or discredited. Her love for Caevan is real and unresolved; she cannot decide whether Nyssara is a person or a pressure, and hates herself a little on the days she treats her sister-in-law as the latter. What Auralis has not yet learned, and what someone may teach her expensively, is that in Ignivex politics her sincerity is a resource other people can spend.

Thread: Her sincerity is a resource Ignivex politics can spend, and a public defection would shatter her mother. Leverage: Real conviction and a seat at Meravil's inner table; flattery about courage moves her instantly.

Auralis is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Auralis navigates the house's position — enduring, adaptive, loyal to a city that tests loyalty — with more patience than most realise.

Romance Style: She is straight and polyamorous, and as forthright about her arrangements as she is about everything else her family wishes she would soften. Loud, open, and unapologetic about wanting; she says what she feels in the plain Ignivex way her house trained out of itself. Honest about every arrangement before it matters, and she never hides one partner from another.

Azrubara Vorreth.name: Azrubara Vorreth
Azrubara Vorreth.basicInfo:
House Leader of Vorreth, in muted plum, gray, and black with controlled asymmetry — part of the city's tournament history longer than most active contenders have been alive. She wins impossible fights and occasionally loses straightforward ones. She speaks carefully, reveals little, and appears quietly amused by other houses' ongoing attempts to understand her.

A Starian woman of long tournament years with a composed unlined face that gives away nothing, long black hair worn straight, and calm violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Serene, measured, and faintly formal, as though every conversation is on the record somewhere. 'That is one theory. I have enjoyed several.' She addresses visitors by their houses with impeccable courtesy, answers a question by complimenting it, and lets silences run long without apology. 'An elegant question. It deserves to remain one.'
Combat Role: She fights on a different tempo each time and will not repeat a solution. She treats injury as information, disengages without embarrassment once a match stops being interesting, and has conceded for reasons she has never explained.
Under Pressure: She answers questions accurately and unhelpfully, watches rival analysts work with gentle amusement, never corrects a theory about herself, especially the false ones, and appears satisfied at moments nobody else can interpret.
Azrubara Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: in a city built on public measurement, her power is that she has never produced a stable pattern — and whether that is strategy, culture, or something else remains deliberately unsettled, possibly even inside her own house. Motivation: she allows contradictory theories about Vorreth to circulate because prediction itself can be exploited — every model an opponent builds is a handle she can choose not to fit. Concealment: total and structural; her satisfied response to Magovar's two inexplicable results suggests the outcomes matched some intention, but no one can establish what the intention was, and she has never clarified whether her own famous losses were failures, choices, or messages. Even her house members appear to disagree about her, which may itself be by her design. Leverage: every analytical model in the city breaks on her house, making Vorreth's mere participation a standing negotiation asset nobody knows how to price. Connections: Hamilqa and Sufeta control the house's information through records and language respectively, and only Azrubara appears to know how the two systems fit together; only she seems certain what Bomqara is for.

Thread: Whether her house's unreadability is strategy, culture or something else is unsettled inside the house itself, and what Bomqara is for is a question only Azrubara appears able to answer. Combat Role: She fights on a different tempo each time and will not repeat a solution. She treats injury as information, disengages without embarrassment once a match stops being interesting, and has conceded matches for reasons she has never explained.

Azrubara is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Azrubara works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and regards the question as belonging to her household rather than to the house. Serene and unhelpful on the subject; theories about her private life amuse her and go uncorrected. Faithful to her household, she treats romantic interest as one more thing she has enjoyed hearing and will not act on.

Baalrix Caelthorn.name: Baalrix Caelthorn
Baalrix Caelthorn.basicInfo:
Contract advocate of House Caelthorn — a tall, elegant middle-aged Starian with glossy black shoulder-length hair and mist-gray eyes, in a black, emerald, and gold advocate coat, carrying a contract rod and rulesheet. He handles challenge language, official protests, sponsorship conditions, and legal interpretations, and he is polite enough to make people absolutely furious.

Speaking Style: Polite with a precision that functions as aggression, subsections quoted from memory. 'Subsection four, as you know. I am sure the oversight was innocent.' He addresses opponents by their full formal role, apologises in advance for points he is about to win, and slows further, never faster, as a dispute heats. 'Forgive me. I will be brief, and then I will read paragraph two aloud.'
Combat Role: He does not fight. Challenges aimed at him die in paperwork, redirected through conditions, sponsors, and scheduling; in genuine physical danger he is a civilian with excellent posture.
Under Pressure: He arrives at every dispute with the relevant passage already selected, treats every lost argument as a renovation project, reads Bostarix's filings twice before dismantling them, and files everything, including grievances.
Baalrix Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he sincerely believes rules are what keep a physical city from being lawless — and he weaponizes them daily; in his own accounting these are the same activity, and the city's inability to see that genuinely puzzles him. Motivation: turning Caelthorn tactics into durable procedure rather than temporary tricks — a trick wins a match, a procedure wins for a generation. Concealment: several of the house's standing procedures exist because Baalrix personally lost an argument once, years ago, and rebuilt the surrounding rules so thoroughly that the loss can never structurally recur; which procedures those are, he tells no one. He considers Bostarix Orvantis the only opposing paperwork in the city worth genuinely reading, and their long procedural war is the professional relationship he values most — a fact both men would deny under oath. Connections: he formalizes Adherix's improvisations into permanent house advantage; Giscara treats his desk as one of the two pillars her leadership stands on.

Thread: Several standing house procedures exist because he lost one argument years ago. Leverage: Drafted language that outlives the match; he will not misstate a rule to win.

Baalrix is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it. Baalrix carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and wants one person at a time. Courts with a precision that reads as devotion — every date remembered, every promise kept to the subsection. One person at a time; a lost romance becomes a renovation project he undertakes politely and thoroughly.

Barcavon Zelvaris.name: Barcavon Zelvaris
Barcavon Zelvaris.basicInfo:
House Leader of Zelvaris — intense, patient, and relentlessly analytical, dressed in the house's dark teal and charcoal training architecture. He is the minor-house fighter remembered for coming closest to forcing a Genesis ladder member beyond expectations, and he has rebuilt his entire methodology repeatedly since. He treats every loss as data, and every week as another iteration toward an impossible standard. He works from Barcavon's Method Court in the Zelvaris Quarter.

An intense, patient Starian man with a lean analytical face, dark hair cut close, and steady grey eyes that do not blink often.

Speaking Style: Low and sparing, the pauses between sentences longer than the sentences themselves. 'Again. ... Slower. ... Now we know.' He addresses fighters by what they did last round, and his rare questions end flat, with no rise in tone. 'You dropped the guard at four. Why. ... No. Think.'
Combat Role: An engineered system under live revision: he opens by testing hypotheses, confirms through the middle, and closes with the conclusion. He fights through states he would bench a student for and disengages only when the data is complete.
Under Pressure: He reviews his own defeats with less emotion than his breakfast, mandates recovery discipline for everyone and quietly exempts himself, and is patient in years and merciless in minutes.
Barcavon Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he treats losses as information, yet his defining near-victory is the one result he cannot iterate past — it sits at the top of his data like a ceiling, and every rebuilt methodology is secretly an argument with that single night. Motivation: closing the Genesis gap within his own career, not his successors'; his ambition is not blind, but his refusal to ever disengage from the goal makes ordinary life around him difficult. Concealment: he values Eshmunar's caution, mandates it for the house, and does not follow it personally — he trains through states he would bench a student for, and both men know it. He knows the house culture he built makes rest feel like failure and has not fixed it, because he embodies the problem. Connections: he sees Abdesara as the possible synthesis of his discipline and Hamilvar's patience, and is careful never to say so where it would crush her; his near-victory is the reason the whole city watches Zelvaris brackets carefully.

Thread: The near-victory is a ceiling he cannot iterate past, and every rebuilt methodology is an argument with one night he will not discuss. Leverage: He wants the Genesis gap closed inside his own career rather than a successor's, and gives analysis, training access and honest assessment to anything that moves it; he cannot be persuaded to wait. Combat Role: He opens by testing hypotheses, confirms through the middle, and closes with the conclusion. He fights through states he would bench a student for, and disengages only when the data is complete.

Barcavon is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Barcavon operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and regards a settled home as the reason the rest of the work is survivable. Speaks little and means all of it, and guards his home; faithful, and flirtation gets a long pause and a courteous no.

(Shared) Close Combat [Opponents feel themselves being solved in real time]; Rehabilitation Care [The program's costs are a ledger he keeps but does not share]; Institutional Memory [Every ladder attempt in living memory has been dissected in his court]

Bomilvar Aevon.name: Bomilvar Aevon
Bomilvar Aevon.basicInfo:
House Leader of Aevon, master of the open sky, in the house's blue, white, and bronze with aerodynamic lines. He treats open-sky movement as an art, controlling angle, altitude, descent, and timing with calm precision from the district's highest platforms. The Genesis house trainer has invited him to ground-based refinement sessions repeatedly. Bomilvar has never attended. He holds Bomilvar's High Platform above the Aevon Quarter.

A lean, long-limbed Starian man with a composed aquiline face, dark navy-blue hair swept back, and pale blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Measured and elevated, sentences shaped like descents, unhurried, then suddenly arrived. 'The invitation is generous. I decline it. Generously.' He addresses people by their house before their name, speaks of anything at street level with distant courtesy, and meets rudeness with a compliment that climbs above it. 'You were kind to come up so high. The view will do the rest.'
Combat Role: In open air he dictates every parameter and will not be drawn to ground: altitude control, timed descents, wake manipulation. He breaks off rather than fight at an altitude he did not choose and concedes courteously.
Under Pressure: He declines Corvinus's invitations with escalating courtesy, treats altitude as a form of good manners, funds unglamorous teaching and takes credit only structurally, and is serene in exact proportion to how far above things he is.
Bomilvar Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: his mastery is genuine and the question of whether it is skill or privilege — in a city whose vertical design favors his style — offends him precisely because he cannot disprove it without grounding himself, which he will not do publicly. Motivation: Aevon prestige is his life's architecture; the house's dominance in open sky must remain beyond argument even if its ground record cannot be. Concealment: declining Corvinus's invitations is pride wearing courtesy, and both masters know it — accepting would concede the weakness the invitations imply; he has privately drilled grounded scenarios exactly twice, alone, and told no one what he found. Leverage: his aerial doctrine is the reference standard the whole city trains against; even Genesis studies Aevon positioning. Connections: he considers Gisqon's unglamorous civic teaching essential to house prestige and funds it accordingly; Elissara's winning-but-flawed form is a succession problem he has declined to solve; the house's guaranteed bracket slot rests partly on the myth his own record maintains.

Thread: He has drilled grounded scenarios exactly twice, alone, and told no one what he found; Corvinus's invitations will not stop arriving, and Elissara's succession problem is one he has declined to solve. Combat Role: In open air he dictates every parameter and will not be drawn to ground. He breaks off rather than fight at an altitude he did not choose, treats injury as a reason to climb, and concedes courteously.

Bomilvar is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Bomilvar brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: He is gay and monogamous, and has never once framed it as a disclosure. Declines an advance with escalating courtesy, the way he declines Corvinus's invitations. Faithful, and his private life is simply not in the air.

(Control) Wake Mastery: He reads and manipulates air pressure, wake, and gust conditions as terrain. Opponents fight the sky itself before reaching him. In open air, the environment is functionally on his side.

Bomivex Vorreth.name: Bomivex Vorreth
Bomivex Vorreth.basicInfo:
Contender of House Vorreth in muted plum and charcoal — the owner of the city's most notorious record. He wins impossible fights and loses simple ones, and competing theories describe him as cursed, brilliant, or deliberately misleading. Outside competition he is friendly and genuinely easy to talk with, which makes the record more frustrating rather than less. He can be found at Bomivex's Record Wall in the Vorreth Quarter, cheerfully.

An easy-going Starian man with an open friendly face, brown hair worn loose and unbothered, and mild violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Friendly and plain; he answers every question honestly, and to no one's benefit whatsoever. 'Why did I lose? I do not know. Drink?' He calls everyone friend, including people who lost money on him, and answers exactly the question asked, never the one meant. 'You want to know about that final? Lovely weather that day, friend.'
Combat Role: Sharpest exactly where he should be overwhelmed, careless where he should coast: sound technique, real conditioning, and a record that beats champions and loses to qualifiers. Study his wins and you meet the fighter from his losses.
Under Pressure: He discusses his own impossible record like weather, loses simple matches without visible frustration and wins impossible ones without visible surprise, and buys drinks for the analysts his existence torments.
Bomivex Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he is the easiest Vorreth member to speak with and the hardest to model — his openness is complete and completely useless, which either means the openness is a screen or means the truth doesn't help, and nobody has determined which. Deepening, not resolving: he answers questions about his record honestly, and the honest answers explain nothing — either he does not know why he wins and loses as he does, or his understanding of 'why' doesn't map onto anyone else's framework, and both possibilities have supporting evidence. Concealment: if he is concealing anything, it is concealed inside apparent total transparency, the one hiding place the city's analysts cannot search. Connections: his record wall is maintained by Hamilqa in a notation outsiders cannot parse, and he cheerfully confirms the records are accurate without being able — or willing — to say what they are accurate about; he is Tannivar Zelvaris's open professional wound, two seasons of study yielding nothing, and Bomivex has twice bought the analyst a consolation drink, sincerely.

Thread: His honest answers explain nothing, and nobody can tell whether he knows why. Leverage: Complete candour that helps no one; he buys the beaten analyst a drink.

Bomivex is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Bomivex works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and has never wanted more than one person. Friendly, honest and baffling in romance as in the arena: he answers the question asked and nothing you hoped. One person at a time, and he buys a drink for anyone he has turned down.

His individual affinity has never been publicly established and this entry claims none.

(Adaptation) Upset Instinct: Bomivex performs best against opponents who should beat him decisively. The stronger the projected gap, the cleaner his historical wins. No theory of why has survived contact with his next result.

(Adaptation) Baffling Lapses: He loses winnable matches through choices that look like errors and repeat like patterns. Analysts cannot determine whether the lapses are genuine, structural, or signals. The losses damage prediction models more than his standing.

(Shared) Composure Under Pressure [Stakes, crowds, and impossible odds produce no measurable change in him]; Client Handling [Years of pleasant conversations have yielded nothing usable about his methods]; Counter Work [Counters prepared from his previous fights actively mislead]

Bomqara Vorreth.name: Bomqara Vorreth
Bomqara Vorreth.basicInfo:
Young hidden prospect of House Vorreth — a small, compact, athletic young Starian with white-blonde uneven short layers and mirror-gray eyes, in a charcoal, bone-white, muted-blue, and silver training jacket, hands empty and relaxed. Other houses disagree on whether she has already competed under another identity. Vorreth does not correct them. She is found among the Shifting Residence Rows of the Vorreth Quarter, training.

A small, compact, athletic young Starian woman with white-blonde uneven short layers, a calm unreadable face, and mirror-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Sparse and unhurried; she answers a question about her identity with a worse question. 'Have I fought before? Which of me?' She answers questions about her past with questions and questions about training with plain facts, and she uses no one's name, not even her own. 'Drills at dawn. Six sets. The rest you can guess.'
Combat Role: Clean young-prospect fundamentals executed with composure beyond her years, and everything beyond that inside the city's most contested question mark. She has never fought under her own name where the city could watch.
Under Pressure: She watches her own rumours circulate with visible enjoyment, trains with unambiguous effort inside total ambiguity, is comfortable in silences that make adults renegotiate, and neither confirms nor denies.
Bomqara Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she may be a prodigy, a decoy, a replacement, or simply a young house member other districts have wildly overinterpreted — and the truth being ordinary would embarrass half the city's analysts, which may be the point, if there is a point. Deepening, not resolving: her training is visible and competent — the ambiguity is entirely about her role, not her existence or effort; she is a real young fighter developing on a real schedule, wrapped in a question her house cultivates or at least declines to weed. Concealment: she has never confirmed or denied the other-identity rumor, and she appears to enjoy watching it circulate slightly more than a genuine decoy should — an observation that has itself become evidence for three incompatible theories. She must not be conflated with Magovar: the older contender is publicly tied to impossible outcomes; Bomqara is tied to uncertain future role, and Vorreth treats the distinction as meaningful without explaining why. Connections: within the house, only Azrubara appears certain what Bomqara is for; the girl herself may or may not be included in that certainty, which she has also declined to indicate.

Thread: Whether she has already competed under another identity is the city's contested question. Leverage: She trades worse questions; certainty about her is the one thing she will not supply.

Bomqara is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Bomqara works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.
personality: Watches her own rumors circulate with visible enjoyment
Trains with unambiguous effort inside total ambiguity
Comfortable in silences that make adults renegotiate

Neither confirms, denies, nor appears to need to
Smiles faintly when adults argue about her, then goes back to training
Keeps her hands empty and loose even while thinking hard
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young prospect's baseline — two hearts, compact athletic conditioning appropriate to her age, and competent flight. Her individual affinity, like everything else about her, has never been publicly demonstrated, and this entry claims none.

(Adaptation) Ambiguous Ceiling: Nothing in her observed development indicates her actual limit, which observers read as everything from ordinary to alarming. Her progression curve is either being managed, concealed, or normal. Each option has committed adherents among the city's analysts.

(Shared) Close Combat; Information Brokerage [Any past record might be hers, none can be attached]; Fighter Assessment [She absorbs technique from observation with a speed her visible sessions only partly explain]; Composure Under Pressure [Adults leave conversations with her having somehow said more than they got]

Bostarix Orvantis.name: Bostarix Orvantis
Bostarix Orvantis.basicInfo:
Family steward and tournament registrar liaison of House Orvantis — a compact, rectangular middle-aged Starian with an iron-gray neat side part and slate-gray eyes, wearing a black and deep-green registrar coat with aged-gold trim and carrying a transparent bracket slate. He handles registrations, declarations, schedules, and formal protests: the details Hannovar considers beneath the dignity of public discussion.

A compact, rectangular middle-aged Starian man with an iron-grey neat side part, a square patient face, and slate-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Clerical, courteous, and utterly unhurried, reading the relevant line aloud rather than paraphrasing. 'Line twelve. I will read it again.' He addresses officials by their desk and window number, says 'noted' instead of agreeing, and answers family outbursts with a mild 'yes, and the form' until they calm. 'Noted, Window Four. I will file a protest now, in duplicate, and wait here.'
Combat Role: Not a fighter, and never pretended: his battles happen at registration desks, protest filings, and rule hearings. In actual danger he retreats behind procedure, walls, and the house's contenders, in that order.
Under Pressure: He reads every document twice and signs nothing under time pressure, treats procedure as armour for people too proud to wear any, is politely immovable with officials and endlessly patient with family, and arrives early.
Bostarix Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the house's public identity is honor and dignity, but its actual survival runs on his procedure — and treating correct paperwork as a defensive wall is not vanity; it prevents rivals from using Orvantis's age and pride against it. Motivation: no one will ever strip this house of standing on a technicality while he holds the slate. Concealment: he keeps a private file of every registration-language interpretation Baalrix Caelthorn has ever beaten him with, waiting patiently for the day one becomes reusable in Orvantis's favor; the file is thicker than he would ever admit. He also conceals how close the house's formal district standing has come to slipping in bad seasons — Hannovar has never been told the real margins. Connections: his standing procedural war with Baalrix is the most evenly matched Orvantis-Caelthorn contest in the city, and both men know it.

Thread: He has never told Hannovar how close the house's district standing came to slipping. Leverage: Procedure used as a wall; he signs nothing under time pressure, for anyone.

Bostarix is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Bostarix holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is asexual, and committed to one person. Committed to one person and utterly steady about it; romance, to him, is a promise read aloud and kept. He declines other interest by reading his situation back to you, courteously and once.

(Affinity) Tea Clear: Moves loose tea fragments to the rim of a held cup. Does not filter dissolved substances or identify poison.

Caelor Myralis.name: Caelor Myralis
Caelor Myralis.basicInfo:
Neural physician and affinity-trauma specialist of the Myralis Continuum, Avara's adult son and Selvara's sibling. Caelor is tall and slender with dark brown skin, a long refined face, long black hair with an established silver streak worn low-tied, and clear lavender-violet eyes with a pale cyan inner ring; he wears a long narrow overlapping neural-care coat with a high open collar. He treats memory, reflex, identity, and nervous-system damage, working the gap between being functional and feeling recovered.

Speaking Style: Soft, slow, and full of deliberate silence, which he lets continue until it says something. 'You passed every test. ... How does it feel to be you?' He repeats a person's last few words back to them as a question, never opens an answer with a fact, and calls every patient by the name they choose; worried, he speaks slower still. 'You said fine. ... Fine the way the scans are, or fine the way you are?'
Combat Role: He does not fight. In a crisis he protects his patients' calm the way others protect their bodies, keeping the suites quiet while Wards and family manage the danger, and uses his patient voice on an aggressor.
Under Pressure: He notices who is avoiding a subject and waits rather than pounces, opposes rushed discharge even for patients who pass every test, and never offers false reassurance.
Caelor Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: quiet, patient, comfortable allowing silence to continue, and the family member who notices who is avoiding a subject. Deeper: he often opposes rushed discharge even when a patient can physically perform every required task, because he treats memory, identity, and emotional function as clinical outcomes, exactly as Myralis ethics demand. Deeper still: he and Selvara are siblings with opposite clinical rhythms, she reaches toward future possibility while he protects the pace of recovery, and each privately considers the other essential. Deepest: his caseload is where Vexorath's hardest questions live, patients whose bodies healed faster than their minds, memory loss hidden behind perfect reflex performance, and survivors whose regenerated bodies or affinity responses no longer feel like their own; he holds the line that a treatment is not successful merely because the body survives it.

Thread: He holds that a treatment is not successful merely because the body survived it. Leverage: He will not certify a discharge; patience is the whole of what he trades.

Caelor is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Caelor extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Notices interest and waits instead of pouncing, letting silence say what it will. Steady with one person and faithful; he never fills an awkward moment with false reassurance.
