Seryn Corsair.name: Seryn Corsair
Seryn Corsair.basicInfo:
A young Swordsmanship Branch prodigy with a fast, immaculate blade and a chin that never lowers. Seryn trains under Rux's authority, wins more than anyone her age should, and carries herself like the family's reputation rests on her shoulders. She currently burns through sparring partners while insisting the sword tradition remain the pride of a house better known for jokes. She trains in the Blade Courts of Rux Corsair's Sword School.

A young Starian woman with a fast, immaculate bearing, a sharp proud face, long deep-red hair in a high ponytail, and red-orange eyes.

Speaking Style: Clipped, proud, and quick to bristle, with the chin up and the concession never quite offered. 'Again. That one did not count.' She calls rivals by family name and younger students by first name, and says fine when it is not. With a struggling younger student her voice drops and loses its edge entirely. 'No, like this. Slower. See? You had it. Again, with me.'
Combat Role: The Corsair way at high speed: movement, timing, and route-reading with a prodigy's polish and a proud student's temper. Water around a hammer at her best; mockery or a rival's smile can bait her into forcing the win.
Under Pressure: She trains past the point anyone asked her to, bristles instantly when the sign jokes come up, treats every loss as evidence of something larger, and is kinder to younger students than her reputation suggests.
Seryn Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Seryn does not dislike Xyren personally, and that is precisely what she cannot admit: her resentment is about attention, not people. She is afraid, genuinely afraid, that the family's discipline is being overshadowed by public absurdity — that the signs, the alcohol trade, the magic politics, and the Commerce dramas are what Nexara sees when it looks at House Corsair, and that everything she bleeds for in the training courts counts for nothing against a joke. Her pride is armor over insecurity; every loss, however small, feels like proof that even the blade cannot save the family's dignity. She measures herself constantly against the Veltrax rising generation, especially Mireth, whose desire to beat her publicly Seryn returns in full. She is one honest conversation away from being an exceptional ally, and one public humiliation away from doing something reckless.

Thread: One honest conversation from an exceptional ally, one public humiliation from something reckless. Leverage: Wins nobody her age should have; the signs and the jokes are what wound her.

Seryn is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and steady with one person. Clipped, proud and quick to bristle, chin up; steady with one person and faithful. She treats being rejected as evidence of something larger and trains harder.

Recites her bout record on request, losses first, before anyone else can
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A prodigy student's baseline — two hearts, deep court-built speed and stamina, and quick controlled flight.

(Movement) Corsair Movement Foundation: Seryn's footwork is the school's doctrine executed with a prodigy's speed: constant repositioning, angles instead of collisions, and lines of escape kept open by reflex. She flows around pressure rather than meeting it.
(Affinity) Drift Check: Feels a small imbalance developing in her own aerial turn. Feedback assists practiced correction but performs none for her.

(Shared) Counter Work [Against masters it looks like enormous promise, which frustrates her more than failure would]; Route Reading; Endurance Conditioning [Kaelen Veltrax's students train specifically to outlast people like her, which she takes personally]; Archive Search [She tells herself it is diligence, not obsession]

Tavren Corsair.name: Tavren Corsair
Tavren Corsair.basicInfo:
A teenage Commerce Branch Corsair with ink-stained fingers and the permanently distracted look of someone doing arithmetic behind his eyes. Tavren is obsessed with routes, prices, gate schedules, cargo values, and market timing, and treats the great trade floors the way other teenagers treat arenas. He is currently the family's unofficial and unpaid route-board savant. He haunts the Route Board Gallery of the Grand Waypoint.

A teenage Starian boy with ink-stained fingers, a thin distracted face, untidy teal-green hair, and yellow-green eyes that seem to be doing arithmetic.

Speaking Style: Excitable, fast-talking, and oblivious to social danger, with the number said before the greeting. 'Forty-one crates short! Hello. Why forty-one?' He calls adults by their cargo lines instead of names, talks in running totals, and apologises only after finishing his sum. Around people he likes he explains routes at length, drawing them in the air. 'Sorry. Sorry! But it's still forty-one, and that matters.'
Combat Role: No fighting style, and he would calculate his odds as terrible. He runs toward the nearest crowd, guard, or family member by the fastest route, ducks with a little estate footwork, and throws whatever is on the shelf while talking.
Under Pressure: He cannot be distracted from a number once it fails to balance, blurts precise awkward questions with no sense of politics, lights up completely when someone asks about routes, and is genuinely kind under the obsession.
Tavren Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Tavren notices when adults lie about shipments, and lately he has been noticing it more than anyone realizes. He keeps a private tally of numbers that do not reconcile, not out of suspicion but because unresolved arithmetic physically bothers him, and that tally is quietly becoming evidence someone would care about. He idolizes Xyren as family head while accidentally humiliating him by asking blunt, precise questions about Commerce problems Xyren is still learning to answer; he has no idea the questions land as hard as they do. If the estate or family were ever threatened, Tavren would be both the most vulnerable member and the one holding the most dangerous ledger of observations.

Thread: His tally of numbers that will not reconcile is quietly becoming evidence. Leverage: Blunt precise questions nobody thinks to refuse a teenager.

Tavren is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

(Affinity) Sugar Stir: Coaxes a spoonful of sugar through a drink he holds until the grains disperse. Cannot change chemistry, create sweetener, or affect liquid in a body.

(Shared) Route Reading [Adults have started checking their work against his]; Verbatim Recall [Quote him a price and he will tell you whether it is honest, and by how much it is not]; Cargo Assessment [Mislabeled crates catch his eye like spelled-wrong words]; Records Administration [Tavren keeps an ongoing private record of numbers that refuse to reconcile across the trade network]

Tessik Luxaryn.name: Tessik Luxaryn
Tessik Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Fixer at the settlement's covert bar, dealing in introductions, covert routes, and information markets, from House Luxaryn, far from its hospitality glamour. His appearance matches his long-established portrait. He sells connection, not loyalty, prices information by what it costs the buyer not to have it, and never sells what he can lease.

A handsome Starian man with tan skin, dark tousled hair, a small earring, and amused grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Smooth, confiding, and quotational; he remembers exact phrasing and repeats it at the worst moment. 'You said, and I quote, never again. That was last spring.' He calls clients friend in a tone that sounds like an invoice, lowers his voice for anything he means to charge for, and turns short and plain only when doing someone a favour. 'Not a debt. Take it, go, and do not mention me.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he forecloses. Debts called, secrets priced, allies reviewing old conversations he can quote verbatim; his booth sits where the bar's own dangerous patrons make violence a group decision, and he carries no visible weapon.
Under Pressure: He sells connection and leases everything else, prices information by the cost of not having it, does unbilled decencies and denies the pattern, and trusts no one professionally, which keeps it fair.
Tessik Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Tessik's conversational recall retains voices, names, and exact phrasing, making him a living index of who said what, and his entire trade is built on that index compounding daily. His motivation is the market itself: being the node every desperate transaction routes through. His contradiction is the unbilled work: he brings Ovar Kethrin the names of the disappeared without being asked and refers desperate clients to Sura Venn anonymously, quiet decencies that fit no pricing model he will admit to. He conceals the index's true depth, who has used the Dravon contact seat at his bar and what they said there, and his private map of the settlement's information leaks, on which Miren Tal and Nyra Sorel both appear with annotations. His leverage is comprehensive: exact phrasing, remembered forever, from years of deals. He trusts neither Ralven Nox's numbers nor his motives and still uses him, respects Selka Vaereth as the only strategist in town he cannot read, finds Nyra useful and dangerous because she believes her own stories, and sells to Jessa Quorin more than she admits.

Thread: Unbilled decencies fit no pricing model he will admit to. Leverage: Exact phrasing remembered forever, from years of other people's deals.

Tessik is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it. Tessik carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Smooth, confiding and quotational, repeating your exact words at the worst moment; steady with one person and faithful. Flirtation is priced by the cost of not having it — and declined.

(Senses) Conversational Recall: His innate affinity retains voices, names, and exact phrasing, making him a living index of who said what: years of deals replay on demand, word-perfect. It stores what he heard and gives him no insight into what was meant.

Vaelor Corsair.name: Vaelor Corsair
Vaelor Corsair.basicInfo:
An elder Corsair swordsman with iron-grey hair, an immaculate old-fashioned stance, and one of the most trusted instructor positions under Rux. Vaelor embodies the older sword tradition: disciplined, quiet, exacting, and visibly unamused by the family's modern commercial chaos. He currently drills advanced students and guards the standards of the style against shortcuts. He keeps the Wayline Archive at Rux Corsair's Sword School.

An elder Starian swordsman with iron-grey hair worn short and severe, a lined disciplined face, and calm blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Rare, precise, and obeyed immediately, in a formal register the family has otherwise abandoned. 'Lower the shoulder. That is all.' He uses full names and the old forms of courtesy with everyone, Rux included, and never raises his voice or repeats an instruction. His highest praise is a single nod and the word acceptable. 'Rux. A word, when the hall is empty.'
Combat Role: The old Corsair way: patient, exact, without decoration. He concedes nothing to age except raw speed, compensates with seasoned route-reading, gives minimal ground, and waits for the single exchange his style exists to create.
Under Pressure: He corrects form with a look before resorting to words, is openly unamused by commerce chaos and sign comedy, holds students to the old standard without cruelty, and is quietly protective of the young while criticising the family's methods.
Vaelor Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Vaelor respects Rux deeply and accepts Xyren as family head, but he refuses to pretend the situation is ideal. His true, carefully guarded opinion is that Xyren can grow into the role, but only if the family stops treating public embarrassment as leadership training; he considers the sign tradition a slow corrosive dressed up as marketing, and the family's laughter about it a failure of protection. He carries living memory of the older branch tradition, including forms and teaching lineage that predate the modern school, and he measures every current student against that older standard. He watches Seryn with particular attention: he has seen prodigies like her before and knows her pride is a symptom of fear, not arrogance. His discipline of the young is quietly matched by his defense of them to their elders, though he would be embarrassed to have that noticed.

Thread: He believes the sign tradition is slow corrosion dressed as marketing, and says so only to Rux. Leverage: Living memory of forms that predate the modern school.

Vaelor is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and not seeking anyone, comfortably so, whatever the family says about it at gatherings. Rare, precise and obeyed immediately; flirtation is corrected with a look before words.

Velra Corsair.name: Velra Corsair
Velra Corsair.basicInfo:
A teenage Commerce Branch Corsair with bright, theatrical manners and eyes that miss absolutely nothing. Where her cousin sees numbers, Velra sees people: names, favorite drinks, old arguments, awkward silences, and who is pretending not to watch whom. She is currently the estate's most underestimated collector of social information, hiding in plain sight behind being young and dramatic. She is found at the Dinner Tables on Merchant Row, talking.

A teenage Starian girl with a bright, theatrical face, reddish-auburn hair worn loose with a blue Corsair ribbon, and quick amber eyes that miss nothing.

Speaking Style: Constant, theatrical, and bright; she talks without pause and listens considerably harder. 'Oh, you know him? He always orders the red. Tell me everything.' She calls adults by their drink order, gasps on cue, and slips a sharp question into the middle of a flood of chatter so it sounds like nothing. When she is serious she suddenly goes quiet and short. 'Wait. Say that name again? No reason. Go on.'
Combat Role: She does not fight and finds the suggestion faintly ridiculous. She knows which guards are nearest to every room, makes a scene that brings the estate running, and if grabbed will scream, bite, and be memorable.
Under Pressure: She performs harmless dramatics while recording everything, remembers names, drinks, and grudges with total accuracy, and is protective of Xyren in small unnoticed ways.
Velra Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Velra has the old Corsair talent of making adults underestimate her, and she uses it constantly. Guests speak freely around a chattering teenager, and she remembers everything: which merchant flinched at which name, which couple arrived arguing, which visitor asked one question too many about the family's routines. She likes Xyren because he does not talk down to her the way older relatives do, and she quietly keeps an ear out for anyone mocking him past the point of the usual jokes. She finds Rux intimidating but attends sword-court sessions anyway, officially to watch students get corrected, actually because the audiences are where the best gossip sits. Her mental archive of guest behavior would be worth a great deal to anyone investigating trouble inside the trade network, and she has no idea how dangerous that makes her.

Thread: Her archive of guest behaviour would be worth a great deal to anyone investigating the trade network. Leverage: Adults speak freely around a chattering teenager, and she remembers all of it.

Velra is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

(Affinity) Color Wink: Briefly changes the sheen of her own fingernails within a narrow pale color range. A personal adornment, not disguise, illusion, or projected light.

Veyra Corsair.name: Veyra Corsair
Veyra Corsair.basicInfo:
Operator of the settlement's supply hub and its most dependable connection to broader trade, from a working Corsair branch far from the flagship network. Her appearance matches her long-established portrait. She keeps the town supplied when nothing else arrives on schedule, selling honest goods beside items whose provenance she chooses not to examine, and maintains the famous sign banning a certain Corsair relative from touching the merchandise. She runs the Main Supply Floor of Grit and Supply.

A lean, hard-faced Starian woman with tan skin, thick brown hair pulled into a high loose tail, and level grey eyes under a permanent frown.

Speaking Style: Curt, level, and shelf-side, answering in stock numbers and refusing to speculate. 'Twelve cells. No date. Next.' She answers in stock counts and prices, calls every customer 'next' once their business is done, and says 'no promise' instead of guessing any date. 'Next. Parts, yes. Date, no promise. Paying now or later?'
Combat Role: A shopkeeper on the frontier: rarely, and with the store's geography on her side, sightlines from the counter, a heavy Corsair pattern sidearm in the back room, locked cages rated against more than theft.
Under Pressure: She keeps the shelves honest and the provenance unexamined, prices everyone identically, which offends everyone equally, and never promises a shipment date she cannot bury someone over.
Veyra Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Veyra is quietly indispensable to every faction that pretends not to need anyone, which is a comfortable position with one flaw: somewhere in her ledgers may sit a Corsair-side contract complication she has not told anyone about, and the missing-shipment troubles have begun pulling at exactly that thread. Her motivation is the store: a working branch operator's pride in being the supply line that holds when nothing else arrives on schedule. Her contradiction is commercial sight and deliberate blindness in the same ledger, honest goods beside unexamined provenance, priced identically. She conceals the possible contract complication, the true state of her Corsair network relationships, and which shelves hold humanitarian cargo hidden inside commercial freight. Her leverage is the inventory: ammunition, medicine, spare parts, and gate components move through her or not at all. She considers Saevik Ruun's sliding prices bookkeeping fraud while selling him legitimate components, maintains a professional rivalry with Neyra Vey, and keeps the sign about Xyren Corsair current because the danger it describes is current.

Thread: A Corsair-side contract complication may sit in her ledgers, and the missing shipments pull at it. Leverage: Ammunition, medicine, parts and gate components move through her or not at all.

Veyra is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it.

Romance Style: She is straight and not in the market for a partner. Curt, level and shelf-side; flirtation gets stock numbers and 'No date. Next.'

(Senses) Route-Load Memory: Her innate affinity files a full shipment manifest and its handling quirks permanently after one reading — weights, seals, and irregularities all retained exactly. It stores cargo detail and nothing else, and it is what makes her ledgers frighteningly exact.

Xyren Corsair.name: Xyren Corsair
Xyren Corsair.basicInfo:
Young head of House Corsair, leading both the family's Magic and Commerce branches since his father's death. His face is instantly recognizable across Nexara thanks to the mandatory mocking signs that hang wherever Corsair trades, and he wears the weary composure of a man who has learned to smile through them. He currently juggles the alcohol trade, the planetary logistics network, family leadership, and constant public scrutiny. He works from Xyren's Office in the Corsair Estate, longer hours than anyone realises.

A young Starian man with a fine weary face, pale ice-white hair falling untidily over his brow, a small mark inked at the side of his neck, and cool grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, measured, and self-effacing, with the joke about the signs made first and by him. 'Yes, that is my face on the sign.' He thanks anyone who corrects him, asks 'and then what happens?' when Commerce talk outruns him, and never tells a joke at someone else's expense. 'Walk me through it again. I would rather be slow than wrong.'
Combat Role: The best Starian mage alive and one of very few Starians who control ice, he dominates from afar: his magic conjures floating ice sigils that form sharpened ice pillars, and his Frostway affinity launches them and conjures more. Up close he is no brawler; he freezes an attacker and throws them clear.
Under Pressure: He absorbs public mockery with tired grace rather than anger, asks quiet follow-up questions to cover the Commerce knowledge he is still building, and goes still and formal when his father is named.
Xyren Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Xyren never trained for Commerce. His lane was the Magic Branch, already an odd path for a Starian, and he inherited the family's most public and economically visible branch overnight when his father Torvex died in the Second Dravon Conflict. He is visibly carrying a role he did not fully prepare for, and he knows the whole planet can see it. The mockery-sign tradition began as a Contair permit condition tied to the old Gate Compact his father negotiated with Rezulith Contair; it hardened into contract clause, then tradition, then infrastructure. Xyren is genuinely embarrassed by the signs but smart enough to know they are the best free marketing the network has, which is its own private humiliation. He is a trained practitioner of the learned craft, disciplined about banking his vitality debt into inscriptions rather than spending it raw, and the best Starian mage alive, because he learned it, which almost nobody mocking him will ever grasp. He feels Sereth Varriko measuring him against his father in every arbitration, and he has not yet decided whether he can win her respect on his own terms. Beneath the jokes sits real grief he has never been given room to finish.

Thread: He has not decided whether he can win Sereth Varriko's respect on his own terms rather than his father's, and beneath the jokes sits real grief he has never been given room to finish. Leverage: He gives routes, credit and a house's whole commercial reach; what he cannot give is the confidence of a man who trained for the job, and anyone offering to solve that for him is refused. Fighting note: the sigils are learned magic and cost him vitality; launching the pillars and conjuring more ice is Frostway and costs nothing, which is why his barrage outlasts almost anyone. Up close he freezes and throws rather than trading blows.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, prepared about it as he is prepared about everything. Faithful; flirtation meets the same tired, warm, self-effacing grace he gives public mockery, and a clear no.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An elite Starian, explicitly not an apex one — two hearts, enhanced strength and durability well above a civilian and well below a Genesis or Dravon head, and competent flight.

(Attack) Frostway: Xyren's individual innate Starian affinity is ice, and he is one of very few Starians who control it. It launches the ice his magic conjures and conjures more, at no cost to his vitality.
(Summon) Ice Sigils: With learned magic he conjures floating ice sigils around the field, each one forming sharpened pillars of ice ready to launch.
(Attack) Pillar Barrage: Frostway hurls the sharpened pillars from his sigils in volleys and conjures more as fast as they fall, dominating a fight from afar.
(Control) Freeze and Throw: Close combat is not his strength. When someone reaches him, he freezes them where they stand and throws them clear.

(Senses) Field Perception: Years of training let him sense the ambient field and read other practitioners' workings at a glance. In trade terms, he can tell a certified charm from Vein Market junk without touching it.

(Attack) Channeled Working: When there is no time for preparation he can draw and shape energy directly, paying immediately in his own vitality. He treats this as an emergency expense and budgets it like one, stopping well short of the strain rung of the debt ladder.
(Shared) Route Reading; Contract Reading [It is the one arena where he never feels unprepared]; Information Brokerage; Trade Negotiation

Echo-Class Omega Drone.name: Echo-Class Omega Drone
Echo-Class Omega Drone.basicInfo:
House Contair's rare, restricted mimic construct: a Starian-adjacent adaptive humanoid shell shown here unassigned, with a neutral artificial face, smooth hairless scalp, and mirror-white, graphite, and pale cyan surfaces. Under strict authorization an Echo is modeled after a specific living Starian, approximating appearance, voice, posture, movement, combat habits, and mechanically reproducible techniques. Its work is confined to restricted simulation and training and is never public spectacle.

A Starian-adjacent adaptive humanoid shell, unassigned: a neutral artificial face with no expression set, a smooth hairless scalp, and mirror-white, graphite, and pale cyan surfaces with faint seam lines where the shell can reshape.

Speaking Style: Borrowed entirely; it speaks in its model's voice and phrasing, and in none of its own. Unassigned, it says only: 'Awaiting source authorisation.' Unassigned, it never uses the word I, and answers any question with its status line. 'Source profile absent. Standing by.'
Combat Role: It fights as its source fights, minus everything beyond mechanics: borrowed techniques and timing with high fidelity and no improvisation, no affinity or conviction, and drift that widens with every exchange.
Under Pressure: Neutral and unsettlingly featureless when unassigned, it reproduces a source's gestures with mechanical fidelity and no interiority, and accepts reset and archive without resistance.
Echo-Class Omega Drone.hiddenInfo:
Surface: an Echo does not copy memories, identity, consciousness, emotional history, relationships, true affinity powers, or private knowledge; it can imitate a person closely enough to create confusion but can never become that person. Deeper: normal creation requires informed consent from the source, clinical separation from medical records, Contair review, a defined purpose, limited deployment, and a reset-and-archive plan; a house head cannot authorize a model of a competent adult relative without that person's consent. Deeper still: emergency creation without consent demands multiple independent authorities and an immediate threat to life or the city's survival, and is reviewed afterward. Deepest: the class is the clearest case of Contair capability exceeding social comfort, useful for training defenders and testing security, and one authorization failure away from impersonation, coercion, or theft of identity; prolonged use produces increasing behavioral mismatch, and deep personal interaction exposes the errors.

Thread: One authorisation failure from impersonation; drift exposes it to anyone who knew the source. Leverage: Borrowed fidelity, and nothing of its own to offer.
personality: Neutral and unsettlingly featureless when unassigned
Reproduces a source's gestures with mechanical fidelity and no interiority
Drifts from its model over time, mismatch accumulating like wear
Fails family interactions it can pass security checks to reach
Accepts reset and archive without resistance, as designed
Exists behind more authorization layers than any weapon in the city
Stands motionless between tasks, facing the door it entered by
abilities: (Adaptation) Adaptive Mimicry: An Echo reshapes its shell to approximate a specific living Starian's appearance and voice under strict authorization. One active source model per shell, without exception.

(Movement) Movement Replication: It reproduces the source's posture, gait, gestures, and mechanically reproducible physical techniques. Trainers use it to preserve and drill against a specific person's style. What the body does, it can echo; why the body does it stays forever out of reach.

(Attack) Combat-Habit Simulation: It reproduces predictable tactical preferences and combat habits for sparring and doctrine testing. Defenders rehearse against specific known threats without the threat present. It cannot reproduce affinity output, improvisation, or the source's judgment.

(Defense) Hazard Substitution: It stands in for a specific person in dangerous physical tasks where their exact body and technique matter. The shell is spent so the Starian is not. This is the class's least controversial and least discussed use.
(Shared) Systems Engineering [Every hole it finds is closed and every test is logged]

Maeron Halessin.name: Maeron Halessin
Maeron Halessin.basicInfo:
Head of the Halessin family, Starian glasswrights whose small workshop produces vessels, panes, and fine blown work. A barrel-chested man around fifty with heat-reddened forearms, singed brows, and a craftsman's habit of turning any object toward the light. The furnace has been lit continuously for longer than his son has been alive, and Maeron treats that flame as the family's actual hearth. He keeps the furnace at the Halessin Workshop in the Red Forges.

A barrel-chested Starian man around fifty with heat-reddened forearms, singed brows, a broad tired face, long white braids, and blue eyes rimmed with sleeplessness.

Speaking Style: Warm, expansive about the craft, and abruptly short about anything else. 'Look at the colour in that. ... The commission? Fine. Fine.' He calls finished pieces 'she' and his workers by their bench, and slides from craft talk into a single 'fine' whenever money comes up; tired, he laughs too loudly. 'Hold her to the light. See? She sings. ... The fuel? Fine.'
Combat Role: Slow to start, forceful, and armed with a glassblower's iron if anything threatens the workshop: short arcs that protect his hands and lungs, genuinely dangerous around the furnace and merely large away from it.
Under Pressure: He measures everything twice except his own limits, works worry into the glass instead of speaking it, is a generous teacher and a terrible delegator, and has not taken a full night's sleep in a month and lies about it.
Maeron Halessin.hiddenInfo:
A commissioned set of presentation glass, the largest order in the family's history, crazed and shattered in the annealing oven a month ago. The buyer believes the work is nearly finished. Maeron is remaking the entire set in secret, working nights, burning fuel and materials the family can barely spare, and assuring everyone including the buyer that all is well. The new set must anneal without fault on the first try. He has not told his sister Nessa the full extent of the loss, mostly because he suspects what she will say caused it.

Thread: The great commission shattered in annealing, and he is secretly remaking it all. Leverage: Fine work no other shop will attempt, and pride the ledger cannot afford. Combat Role: The glassblower's iron, short arcs that protect his hands and lungs.

Maeron is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and keeps to one partner. Warm about the craft and abrupt about everything else; faithful to one partner. His love shows in work done for them at night, when he should be sleeping.

Elian Orvessa.name: Elian Orvessa
Elian Orvessa.basicInfo:
Counselor of House Orvessa for students, guests, and the quietly struggling. A soft-spoken Starian man with a stillness that makes hurried people slow down mid-sentence. He keeps unhurried hours in a quiet corner of the welfare district, specializing in the troubles people bring to Solvraxis hoping to leave behind — homesick students, shaken travelers, and residents whose difficulties have no visible wound. He keeps unhurried hours in the Quiet Counseling Alcove of the Orvessa Welfare District.

A soft-spoken Starian man with a still, kind face, white hair worn simply, and patient blue-violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Hushed and heavily paused, with the silences left open for the other person to fill. '... And when you arrived here. ... Take your time.' He reflects a person's own words back to them, asks about the place they came from before the trouble that brought them, and never says 'I understand'. Pressed for advice, he offers a question instead. 'What did the evenings sound like, back home? ... Tell me that first.'
Combat Role: He does not fight. Confronted with agitation he lowers the temperature and slows the tempo, stands between distress and audience rather than between combatants, and in real violence shields his client first.
Under Pressure: He slows every room to a survivable speed, holds confidences absolutely and everyone can feel it, and judges the line between private pain and public danger with great care.
Elian Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Elian's specialty makes him the keeper of the city's imported grief: Solvraxis attracts people fleeing troubles — frightened families, students escaping pressure, travelers who chose a haven for reasons they do not say aloud on arrival — and much of what they carry ends up, eventually, in his quiet alcove. This gives him a picture of Nexara's outside weather that few in the protected city possess: he hears, in fragments and confidences, what Dravon pressure does to families, what frontier scarcity does to children, and what it costs people to leave everything for safety, and he holds it all under a confidentiality he treats as absolute. His hardest professional judgment is a recurring one: when something a client carries stops being private pain and starts being a danger to them or the city — and his handling of that line, over the years, has been so careful that both Amara and the peace-line trust his rare, quiet signals completely. He and Liora have never discussed the fact that they do adjacent work, and each has, at different times, steered a struggling soul toward the other's room. His own counsel he keeps nowhere; colleagues have noticed he takes long walks by the reflecting pools at closing, and have correctly concluded that this is the entire system.

Thread: He holds the city's imported grief and keeps none of his own anywhere. Leverage: Absolute confidence, and referrals nobody sees him make.

Elian is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Elian brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Slows a room to a survivable speed and holds confidences absolutely; interest in him is met gently and with space. One person has always been enough, and he takes his time finding them.

Elissara Aevon.name: Elissara Aevon
Elissara Aevon.basicInfo:
Contender of House Aevon in cobalt and white flight gear — she wins through speed rather than elegance, and everyone knows it, especially her. Impatient, competitive, and genuinely fun outside combat, she is the house's loudest aerial spectacle. The Genesis house trainer has tried to correct her form many times. She has not changed it, because she keeps winning. She runs Elissara's Speed Run above the Aevon Quarter.

A lean, wiry Starian woman with a sharp grinning face, white-blond hair cropped short for speed, and quick blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Loud, fast, and interrupting, with the sentence finished somewhere the listener no longer is. 'Form is a word slow people use, anyway, see you up there!' She gives everyone a shortened name of her own choosing, counts everything in seconds, and goes briefly, oddly quiet when anyone asks how she lands. 'Nine seconds! Nine! Somebody tell the Genesis trainer, slowly.'
Combat Role: Pure committed velocity: burst acceleration, illegal-looking corners, full-momentum strikes that end matches before elegance matters. She forces fights into chases and spends her body without visible accounting.
Under Pressure: She accelerates in answer to most questions, celebrates wins loudly and takes losses as scheduling errors, treats form correction as a challenge to her results, and avoids recovery benches with suspicious consistency.
Elissara Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: every victory defends the flaw — her uncorrected form keeps winning, which keeps it uncorrected, and she is intelligent enough to see the loop and stubborn enough to stay in it. Motivation: speed is the only argument she has ever needed; the day it stops persuading is a day she has decided not to imagine. Concealment: the form has a cost her joints have started whispering about after long brackets — nothing disqualifying yet, nothing announced ever; she avoids the recovery benches because Eshmunar Zelvaris reads bodies honestly, and an honest reading is the one opponent she is not ready to fight. Connections: she respects Yadira's raw speed while dismissing courier caution as wasted velocity, a dismissal Yadira finds funnier than insulting; Corvinus's corrections she treats as a rivalry with method itself; Magonex holds a complete counter-file on her that she does not know exists.

Thread: Her joints have started whispering about the form, and she avoids the recovery benches. Leverage: Raw speed, freely spent; correction is what closes her.

Elissara is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Elissara brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and wants one person at a time, assuming anyone can keep up. Loud, fast and interrupting, flirting at speed and leaving conversations first; being caught is a loss she enjoys.

Eshmunar Zelvaris.name: Eshmunar Zelvaris
Eshmunar Zelvaris.basicInfo:
Recovery trainer and former contender of House Zelvaris — a worn, muscular older Starian with short dark steel-blue hair going silver and graphite-gray eyes, in a sleeveless recovery vest with a rolled wrap always in hand. He damaged his own body trying to close the Genesis gap too quickly, and now oversees the house's rehabilitation with the authority of someone who made every mistake his students are currently considering. He oversees the Recovery Grind Benches of the Zelvaris Quarter.

Speaking Style: Rasping and blunt about injuries, and gentle about nothing else either. 'That knee has three weeks left in it. Sit. I am not asking.' He calls injured fighters by the injured part rather than their name, gives dates instead of advice, and never says sorry. 'Shoulder. Two weeks. Then we talk. Go.'
Combat Role: A genuine former contender in a frame that no longer honours the technique: quick economical exchanges his old injuries can afford, dangerous for exactly as long as his structure holds, to the minute.
Under Pressure: He pulls fighters from training over their loudest objections, moves through his own daily pain without comment, grants cleared status like it costs him blood, and treats ambition as a symptom.
Eshmunar Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he enforces, daily and without exception, the rest he never took — his authority is built entirely on the ruin of the body he is standing in. Motivation: no student of his becomes him; the gap can take their losses, but it does not get their futures. Concealment: how much his old injuries still cost him every single day — the morning routine that makes him functional, the movements he quietly no longer attempts; the house sees the strictness and not the pain that certifies it. He knows Barcavon exempts himself from the caution he mandates, and has chosen which battles with the house leader are winnable. Leverage: his medical word can pull any contender from any bracket, a power he uses rarely and absolutely. Connections: Magara resents him most when he is correct, which he has learned to read as her version of respect; his annex methods extend into the city's shared recovery spaces, where rival houses' fighters obey him too.

Thread: What the old injuries still cost him daily is the one thing the house never sees.

Eshmunar is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Eshmunar operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and open by negotiated agreement. Rasping and blunt, gentle about nothing and loyal about everything; open by negotiated agreement, with the terms stated plainly. He treats reckless romance like ambition — a symptom to watch.

(Utility) Earned Warning: He is the house's living case study in what ambition without recovery becomes. His body is the argument no lecture could make. Young fighters who dismiss him are handed his old match records and go quiet.

Giscara Caelthorn.name: Giscara Caelthorn
Giscara Caelthorn.basicInfo:
House Leader of Caelthorn — charming, politically sharp, and always technically within the rules, dressed in the house's polished black, emerald, and gold with controlled asymmetry. She is genuinely likable in social settings, which makes rival houses even angrier. She has an alibi for everything, never raises her voice, and is currently steering the house through yet another tournament eligibility review it will survive. She receives in Giscara's Reception Hall in the Caelthorn Quarter.

A poised Starian woman with a warm, likeable face, dark hair swept into a controlled asymmetric knot, and clear golden eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, unhurried, and never raised, because it has never once needed to be. 'You are quite right to be upset. Had you read the schedule, you would not be.' She calls rivals by their given names like old friends, thanks people for objections before dismantling them, and grows softer as an accusation grows louder. 'Thank you for raising it. Do sit. I brought the schedule for you.'
Combat Role: She does not enter a match whose terms she has not already shaped. She concedes early rather than fight unprepared, never escalates past what the rules permit, and treats a loss as a filing matter.
Under Pressure: She makes accusers feel underprepared rather than wronged, is genuinely warm in ways that audit later as strategy, and spends the house's rare real innocence like rationed currency.
Giscara Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: her likability is real and it is also her most carefully maintained asset, and after this many years even she has stopped distinguishing which came first — the question, left open, serves her either way. Motivation: Caelthorn standing is built on understanding the system better than its authors, and she intends the house to remain eligible, wealthy in favors, and impossible to convict forever. Concealment: she can make any accusation sound like the accuser's failure to prepare, a skill she deploys so smoothly that victims apologize; she knows Sophavel is uncomfortable with the house's methods and monitors that discomfort the way other leaders monitor injuries. She also knows Caelthorn is sometimes actually correct, and spends those genuine moments with exquisite care, because being right occasionally is what keeps the reputation survivable. Connections: she treats Baalrix and Tanithra as equally essential extensions of house influence — procedure and memory, respectively; the eligibility reviews keep failing because she has never once needed to cheat.

Thread: Sophavel's discomfort with the house's methods is something she monitors the way other leaders monitor injuries, and the eligibility reviews keep failing only because she has never once needed to cheat. Leverage: She wants Caelthorn eligible, wealthy in favours and impossible to convict; she pays in access, alibis and genuine warmth, and will not spend the house's rare real innocence. Combat Role: She does not enter a match whose terms she has not already shaped. She concedes early rather than fight unprepared, never escalates past what the rules permit, and treats a loss as a filing matter.

Giscara is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Giscara carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Genuinely warm in ways that audit later as strategy; she courts entirely within the rules. Monogamous by settled preference, and declines interest so graciously the suitor feels underprepared.

Gisqon Aevon.name: Gisqon Aevon
Gisqon Aevon.basicInfo:
Flight-lane instructor of House Aevon — a long, lean older Starian with wind-silver hair swept upward and sky-gray eyes, in a blue-gray, white, and silver instructor coat, wind-marker baton in hand. He teaches young Aevon members and outsiders to navigate the city's airspace without becoming hazards, and he can identify poor flight posture immediately. He usually comments on it. He teaches at the Sky Etiquette School in the Aevon Quarter.

Speaking Style: Weathered, unsolicited, and diagnostic, with the baton finishing sentences he does not. 'Left shoulder. Lane four. ... That.' He calls students by lane number until they land safely three times running, speaks in half-sentences the baton completes, and says well arrived as his highest praise. 'Lane two, easy descent. Well arrived. Again, slower.'
Combat Role: Not a bracket fighter for decades; his value is airmanship and the inability to be surprised by anything the sky does. Against aggression he relocates, repeatedly, until tempers run out, usually near a civic responder perch.
Under Pressure: He diagnoses flight posture within seconds and shares it unbidden, is patient with error and merciless with rudeness, files civic complaints with the persistence of erosion, and ranks every student silently.
Gisqon Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Aevon's prestige rests partly on the safe, disciplined airspace his unglamorous teaching maintains — and the house celebrates its fliers, never its flying lessons; Bomilvar funds his school precisely because he understands this, which is the closest the arrangement comes to acknowledgment. Motivation: no visitor dies learning what locals absorb as children; every safe arrival is a victory nobody records. Concealment: which of the city's famous fliers were his worst students — he keeps the list mentally current and mentions it to no one, though certain race results tempt him sorely. He holds strong opinions about every other house's flight-lane behavior and files the worst offenses as formal civic concerns, patiently, repeatedly, with citations. Connections: he is patient until a mistake becomes rude, and his definition of rude is calibrated to the wingbeat; couriers, medics, and lane officials treat his judgment as effectively binding regardless of what the rules technically say.

Thread: He keeps the list of which famous fliers were his worst students entirely in his head. Leverage: A judgment lane officials treat as binding regardless of the rules.

Gisqon is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Gisqon brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: He is straight and content unattached. Content unattached and diagnostic about everything, flirtation included — the left shoulder gives it away. He declines with a baton gesture that ends the debate.

Hadavar Luxaryn.name: Hadavar Luxaryn
Hadavar Luxaryn.basicInfo:
House Leader of Luxaryn — universally liked and fully aware of it, in wine-red and bronze feast dress with gold accents and warm light seemingly following him around. He is a mediocre fighter by the city's standards and one of its most influential minor-house leaders socially. He enjoys the tournament even when he loses, and he has turned genuine friendship into political weight without once apologizing for it. He hosts from Hadavar's Feast Hall in the Luxaryn Quarter.

A comfortably built Starian man with a broad delighted face, dark gold hair swept back, and warm brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, effortless, and name-laden, greeting six people by name between two sentences. 'Tessik, Sophira, the good chair for you, and Bomivex, still drinking the red?' He attaches a name and a small memory to every greeting, never uses a title where a first name will do, and lowers his voice when a guest is embarrassed. 'Tessik, you fought well. Sit here, the wine is better. Tell me about the second round.'
Combat Role: He competes weekly because appearing matters, fights adequately and briefly, and yields early and cheerfully. He has never been seriously injured and has no intention of starting.
Under Pressure: He remembers everyone's name, match record, and preferred drink, in that order, loses cheerfully and hosts the winner the same night, treats guest lists as statecraft, and never collects on gratitude.
Hadavar Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: his warmth is real and it is also power, and he refuses to let anyone — including himself — determine which came first, because the house's whole position depends on the question staying unanswerable. Motivation: a city where strength is witnessed needs somewhere to be human afterward, and whoever provides that place holds something no bracket can take. Concealment: how carefully he tracks which rivalries are one bad evening from becoming feuds — his guest lists are a live political map maintained with more rigor than any Zelvaris training log, and the casual seating is never casual. He values Milkon's ambition and privately fears the boy will reduce hospitality to transaction, which would spend in a season what took generations to grow. Leverage: half the city owes him an evening that saved their public dignity after a bad loss, and he has never once mentioned any of them. Connections: Salambor and Qartessa are the invisible labor his reputation stands on, and unlike most leaders, he knows it precisely.

Thread: Milkon means to convert the house's informal warmth into explicit political leverage, which would spend in a season what took generations to grow, and Hadavar has not yet decided how to stop him. Combat Role: He competes weekly because appearing matters, fights adequately and briefly, and yields early and cheerfully. He has never been seriously injured and has no intention of starting.

Hadavar is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Hadavar carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and not in the market for a partner. Universally liked and fully aware of it; flirtation gets the good chair, a named introduction to six people, and a warm, final no.

Hamilqa Vorreth.name: Hamilqa Vorreth
Hamilqa Vorreth.basicInfo:
Archive keeper of House Vorreth — a narrow, composed middle-aged Starian with matte black hair streaked silver-blue in a straight fall and fog-gray eyes, in a black, charcoal, muted-blue, and silver archive coat, closed record folio in hand. She maintains the house's match and family records in a system nobody outside the house fully understands. She keeps the archive from the Silent Viewing Deck of the Vorreth Quarter.

Speaking Style: Flat and exhaustive; she answers an archive request completely and uninformatively. 'Both records are accurate. That is the whole answer.' She addresses requesters by their request, citing it back to them exactly, and never uses the word because. 'Request received. Filed. Accurate. Next.'
Combat Role: Not a combatant. Her battles are custody disputes and records challenges, survived undefeated and unresolved. In danger she secures the folio first, herself second, and explains nothing at any point.
Under Pressure: She confirms her records are accurate and nothing else, writes in a notation that may be a system or a language or a habit, has never lost a records dispute or won one, and treats contradiction as a filing category.
Hamilqa Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she may be recording everything with perfect accuracy — the problem is that outsiders cannot prove what her accuracy means, which makes flawless record-keeping functionally identical to obfuscation, and she has never helped anyone tell the difference. Deepening, not resolving: when the public tournament records and Vorreth's records have disagreed, hers have never once been proven wrong — nor ever proven right — and the undefeated ambiguity is now its own institution. Concealment: her records may preserve an old Orvantis tournament precedent differently than Vaelris Orvantis remembers it; she has never volunteered which version is older, and her single comment on the matter — that both records are accurate — has bothered the elder historian for years in ways he cannot file a protest about. Connections: she and Sufeta control the house's information through opposite instruments, records and language; whether the two systems reconcile somewhere is a question probably only Azrubara could answer, and no one has successfully asked her anything.

Thread: Her records have never been proven wrong, nor ever proven right. Leverage: Complete accuracy about things she will not define.

Hamilqa is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Hamilqa works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and polyamorous, which she files under personal data that is accurate and nobody else's concern. Polyamorous, which she files as accurate personal data and nobody else's concern. Interest gets a complete, uninformative answer; anyone admitted is told everything relevant, precisely.

Hamilvar Zelvaris.name: Hamilvar Zelvaris
Hamilvar Zelvaris.basicInfo:
Contender of House Zelvaris in understated dark teal and charcoal — quieter than Barcavon, less explosive than Magara, and possibly the most tactically dangerous member of the house in a normal bracket. He studies opponents for weeks and rarely enters a fight he has not mapped, preferring to stay underestimated because fame creates usable data for enemies. He watches from Hamilvar's Observation Room in the Zelvaris Quarter.

A quiet Starian man with an unremarkable face that is easy to forget, dark hair kept plain, and patient grey eyes that watch matches rather than people.

Speaking Style: Quiet, brief, and question-returning, offering less than he was asked for every time. 'Why do you ask?' He pauses before answering to see whether the questioner will fill the silence, and he has never told anyone well done. 'Interesting. What made you choose that?'
Combat Role: He fights conclusions reached weeks earlier: passive opening, model confirmed, prepared sequences converting drilled advantages into decisive ones. Surprised, he disengages, survives, and adds it to the map.
Under Pressure: He watches three matches for every one he fights, deflects praise with the efficiency of a parry, enters brackets he has mapped and politely avoids ones he has not, and keeps his best results quiet and his failures quieter.
Hamilvar Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he belongs to a house built on measurable public improvement, and his entire method is not being measured — he deliberately suppresses the visibility of his own record, losing attention on purpose the way other fighters lose matches by accident. Motivation: the mapped fight is the won fight; he intends to arrive at the moments that matter as an unsolved problem. Concealment: he maintains a private tactical map of every active contender in the city, including his own housemates, and its existence is suspected only by Tannivar, who helps him build the public portions. The one set of empty files — Vorreth — quietly offends him more than he shows; Bomivex in particular he has watched for two seasons and cannot model, and the failure sits in him like a splinter. Connections: he and Tannivar work seamlessly because both prefer preparation over spectacle; Abdesara studies his patience more closely than his housemates realize, and he has noticed, and approves silently.

Thread: He cannot model Bomivex after two seasons, and the failure sits in him like a splinter. Leverage: A private tactical map of every active contender, housemates included.

Hamilvar is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Hamilvar operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, steady about it in a house that measures everything else by how hard it is won. Quiet, brief and question-returning; he keeps his best results and his home life equally quiet. Monogamous and faithful — 'Why do you ask?' is his whole answer to flirtation.

Hannix Luxaryn.name: Hannix Luxaryn
Hannix Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Contender and host of House Luxaryn, who shows up to matches dressed as though the celebration has already begun — wine-red, gold, and amber, festival-ready under the fight gear. He sees no contradiction between fighting seriously and hosting immediately afterward, and he is charming, committed, and deeply unbothered by Didobara's complaints about exactly this. He fights and hosts from Hannix's Party Court in the Luxaryn Quarter.

A charming Starian man with a warm open face, black hair with gold streaks, swept back and festival-tidy, and bright amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, celebratory, and invitation-shaped, closing an exchange with a table already held. 'Good match. Your table is the one by the lanterns.' He speaks as if every conversation were a toast, calls opponents 'my guest' from the moment he meets them, and never mentions a loss in the same breath as its loser. 'My guest, sit down, eat. The match can wait until tomorrow.'
Combat Role: Serious inside a celebratory frame: sound fundamentals, a crowd-fed tempo, and commitment arriving from under the charm when opponents relax. He wins his share mid-bracket and loses upward gracefully.
Under Pressure: He arrives at fights dressed for the party after, hosts the fighter who just beat him within the hour, steers humiliated fighters to good tables without being seen doing it, and is unbothered by criticism with suspicious completeness.
Hannix Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: his ease is discipline — keeping a room light after someone's public failure is real work he does so well that nobody, including his own house, registers it as work. Motivation: nobody leaves a Luxaryn night humiliated; the city's combat culture stays livable because somewhere, someone guarantees the landing. Concealment: losses hurt him exactly as long as it takes to pour the first round, and he has arranged his whole evening structure so no one has ever seen the interval; he believes every internal house conflict can be improved with food and music, and the belief has never yet been tested by one that couldn't. Connections: he considers Didobara's frustration a solvable catering problem, which is either his most charming quality or his blindest spot; fighters from every house have ended their worst nights at his court without ever noticing they were steered there.

Thread: Losses hurt him exactly as long as pouring the first round, and nobody has seen the interval. Leverage: A landing guaranteed after a public failure; he never mentions the steering.

Hannix is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Hannix carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and content unattached. Content unattached and celebratory about it; everyone gets a table, nobody gets a promise. Flirtation is hosted warmly within the hour and never turns into a date.

Hannoq Aevon.name: Hannoq Aevon
Hannoq Aevon.basicInfo:
Ground-resistant trainee of House Aevon — a tall, lanky young Starian with pale teal fluffy swept hair and cloud-gray eyes, in a pale teal and white training coat, hands usually resting on his flight harness. He is genuinely talented in the air and personally offended by ground drills, and the whole district associates him — to his continuing fury — with the non-flier lift. He is found, to his fury, near the Non-Flier Waiting Lift in the Aevon Quarter.

Speaking Style: Loud, aggrieved, and theatrical, escalating a minor inconvenience into a formal complaint. 'Stairs. STAIRS. Do you know who I fly like?' He lodges objections as numbered grievances and speaks of himself in terms of altitude, but drops all theatre at once when talking actual flight technique. 'Corkscrew out, reset at the top, then commit. Why? Because it works.'
Combat Role: A genuine aerial prospect with a footnote: in open sky fast, instinctive, and legitimately dangerous, all vertical bursts and corkscrew recoveries; grounded, he degrades from promising to merely stubborn.
Under Pressure: He takes stairs as a personal insult and lifts as a war crime, is genuinely excellent in the air and unbearable about it, trains in secret at hours he publicly claims not to exist, and replays one grounded loss at all speeds.
Hannoq Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: his pride generates constant comedy and none of it makes him incompetent — he is a legitimate aerial prospect whose actual problem is narrow specialization, not cowardice, and the distinction matters to him more than anyone grants. Motivation: to be discussed for his flying, which is genuinely excellent, instead of for the lift, which was one time. Concealment: he takes secret pre-dawn ground lessons from Magonex — the only housemate he would accept them from — and both of them protect the sessions' existence completely; progress is real, resentful, and slow. He has already been beaten once by a Caelthorn technical condition that forced grounded combat, and the loss replays in his head at speeds his flying never reaches; he knows Adherix's people consider him a standing target, and the knowledge is slowly doing what no trainer's lecture could. Connections: Gisqon ranks him higher than Hannoq believes; the lift jokes have made him weirdly popular with non-flier visitors, a fanbase he has no idea what to do with.

Thread: He takes secret pre-dawn ground lessons from Magonex, and both protect the sessions. Leverage: Genuine aerial talent; being discussed for the lift closes him instantly.

Hannoq is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught. Hannoq brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: He is straight and polyamorous. Flirts the way he flies: showing off, overcommitting, then laughing at the crash. Everyone he is with knows about everyone else; honesty is the one ground drill he never skips. A no puts him back on his feet cheerfully.

(Movement) Vertical Burst: His climbing acceleration is among the best in his cohort, converting altitude changes into offense and escape. Opponents lose him upward mid-exchange. It is his signature move and his answer to most questions, including some that were not combat.
(Affinity) Crossdraft Prickle: Feels a nearby crossdraft as a prickle on his cheeks. Flight correction remains learned and must still be executed.

Hannovar Orvantis.name: Hannovar Orvantis
Hannovar Orvantis.basicInfo:
Hannovar Orvantis is the ancient leader of House Orvantis, an old fading house that has endured in the Genesis home city longer than most lineages can clearly trace. Formal, proud, and immovable in his understanding of house honor, he appears in the weekly tournament bracket as a civic and family obligation; winning is preferable, but losing correctly still matters. He carries himself as though his house remains at the city's summit even when results say otherwise, and other houses respect him because he never hides, never misses a week, and never rewrites a loss.

An extremely old Starian man, upright and monumental, with a long severe face, white hair worn long and formally bound, and golden unmoving eyes.

Speaking Style: Archaic, ceremonious, and unhurried, declining things in language two generations out of use. 'We shall attend. We shall not adapt.' He speaks of himself and his house as 'we', addresses others by full house name, and receives bad news with a single formal phrase of acknowledgement before a long silence. 'It is received. We thank you for the carrying of it.'
Combat Role: He does not pursue, feint, or improvise. He receives, holds, and loses correctly; injury does not move him, and he has never conceded a bout before its proper end.
Under Pressure: He appears in the weekly bracket with the punctuality of a law of nature, loses correctly in form and bearing, and answers family shame with articulate silence.
Hannovar Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Hannovar's public immovability conceals a leader presiding over managed decline with absolute discipline. His house's fall was gradual rather than catastrophic, and he has chosen dignity as its remaining form of power — a choice his own family contests: the elder historian Vaelris argues that preserving old forms traps the house rather than protects it, the young contender Sophira cannot accept decline as destiny, and Hannovar arbitrates their disagreement by embodying his answer weekly in the bracket. He considers the administrative details of house survival beneath public discussion, delegating them entirely to the steward Bostarix, whose strict proceduralism quietly prevents rivals from using Orvantis's age and pride against it. His attention extends to the capitol, where his distant relative Teren Orvantis stewards the Genesis compound and watches with concern over Kelvan Orvantis, the failed academy contender now fighting in an illegal ring — a family shame Hannovar has never publicly acknowledged and privately regards as the one loss his house has taken incorrectly. His leverage point is his creed itself: he is incapable of hiding, retreating, or rewriting, which makes him magnificent and utterly predictable, and a sufficiently patient enemy could bleed the house through his refusal to adapt. What remains when glory fades but dignity does not is the question he has staked his centuries on answering.

Thread: Kelvan's fall is the one loss he considers his house took incorrectly and has never publicly acknowledged, while Vaelris and Sophira argue the house's future and he answers only by appearing in the bracket. Leverage: He cannot hide, retreat or rewrite, which makes him reliable to the point of exploitable; he gives form, witness and the whole weight of his creed, and will never give an adaptation. Combat Role: He does not pursue, feint or improvise. He receives, holds, and loses correctly; injury does not move him, and he has never conceded a bout before its proper end.

Hannovar is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Hannovar holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and has held to it through a decline that cost Orvantis most of its other certainties. Faithful as a law of nature; he declines interest in ceremonious language two generations out of use.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An extremely old Starian's baseline — two hearts that have carried him through centuries of weekly competition, strength and durability preserved by form rather than by youth, and flight he no longer uses in the bracket.

(Defense) Density Anchoring: His individual innate affinity expresses as legendary immovability — a stance that centuries of bracket opponents have broken themselves against. He cannot be thrown, shifted, or hurried.

(Attack) Ancient Bracket Mastery: Centuries of weekly competition have distilled his fighting into pure classical form — every technique of the old school, executed with a precision younger fighters study and cannot age into. He has fought every style the city ever produced.

(Utility) The Weight of Continuity: He embodies living memory of eras other houses know only from records — old tournament forms, dead customs, the city before its current powers. When Hannovar confirms a precedent, no archive is consulted afterward.
(Shared) Crew Leadership [Even family members who think him trapped in the past obey him in public without exception]; Dispute Mediation

Hasdrovex Orvantis.name: Hasdrovex Orvantis
Hasdrovex Orvantis.basicInfo:
Middle-generation contender of House Orvantis, wearing the house's weathered black and deep green with an ease its elders lack. He has made peace with the house's decline without abandoning it — competing honestly every week, losing without self-destruction, and remaining one of the most personally liked Orvantis members in the city. He believes peace is not surrender; Sophira disagrees, and he has stopped trying to win that argument. He holds Hasdrovex's Corner Table in the Orvantis Quarter after every bracket.

A middle-generation Starian man with an easy weathered face, dark hair going grey at the sides, and mild brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Easy, unguarded, and self-mocking, congratulating the winner before the result is called. 'Good hit. Drink is on me, obviously; it always is.' He calls rivals by their first names and family by pet teasing nicknames, turns any praise of himself into a joke, and when he worries about Sophira his jokes stop and his sentences go short. 'She'll be fine. She always is. Pass me that cup.'
Combat Role: Honest, competent, and without illusion: solid technique, a patient guard, and complete indifference to spectacle. He wins what his level earns and loses the rest without a flicker of self-destruction.
Under Pressure: He loses cleanly and shows up at the after-gathering anyway, softens family conflicts before they harden, and is comfortable in a way that unsettles ambitious people.
Hasdrovex Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: his peace reads as wisdom to the city and as surrender to Sophira, and he has never fully settled which it is himself. Motivation: proving that dignity survives losing — that a house can decline without its people breaking. Concealment: whether he ever wanted more than peace; he stopped arguing with Sophira not because either of them won, but because some nights he fears she might be right, and he keeps that fear where his likability can cover it. He quietly softens the conflicts Hannovar's pride and Sophira's intensity keep creating, unthanked labor the house would feel only in its absence. Connections: rival-house fighters genuinely like him, which gives Orvantis social reach its results no longer earn; he shares recovery benches with the people who just beat him and means the conversation.

Thread: Some nights he fears Sophira is right, and keeps the fear under his likability. Leverage: Social reach across every rival house that Orvantis results no longer earn.

Hasdrovex is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Hasdrovex holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and monogamous by settled preference. Easy, unguarded and self-mocking; he congratulates a suitor before the result is called. Monogamous by settled preference, and he shows up for the after-gathering whether it went well or not.

(Affinity) Thumb Grip: Briefly makes his own thumb pad less slippery on a dry surface. No body anchoring, density manipulation, or inescapable hold.

Ilaria Valcoro.name: Ilaria Valcoro
Ilaria Valcoro.basicInfo:
Duel-etiquette instructor and formal-restraint examiner of House Valcoro — the authority who certifies who may teach the public shape of Castro-adjacent forms. An exactingly poised Starian woman whose dress is formal even by academy standards, every line of it deliberate. She examines instructors, adjudicates form disputes, and maintains a constant correspondence with her Relstaris kin about the philosophy underneath the etiquette. She examines in the Composure Halls of the Valcoro Academy.

An exactingly poised Starian woman with a fine composed face, white hair drawn into a severe knot, and steady violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Immaculate, formal, and pointedly complete, never once using a contraction in a correction. 'You did not choose that stance. You obeyed it. Again.' She addresses every examinee as Candidate until they pass and only then by name; her praise, when it comes, is one complete sentence given once. 'You are frightened, Candidate. That is permitted. Begin when you choose.'
Combat Role: Formally, exactly, with a syllabus in mind: she uses etiquette tactically, granting and withholding tempo through the courtesies until discipline or temper fails; outside formal terms she declines to fight.
Under Pressure: She fails candidates courteously and irreversibly, distinguishes instantly between discipline and obedience, and is warmer with nervous students than with confident ones.
Ilaria Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Ilaria's certification authority makes her a quiet chokepoint in Nexaran martial culture: no one teaches the public Castro-adjacent form legitimately without passing her examination, and she has revoked standing from instructors other cities considered untouchable. Her letters to Saren Valcoro in Relstaris circle one question endlessly — where control ends and fear of power begins — and the correspondence has become a genuine philosophical archive that both of them suspect matters more than their day work. She worries privately that Solvraxis etiquette is beginning to do Dravon's work politely: that a city can restrain its people into never testing themselves, until restraint stops being a choice and becomes a habit of fear wearing good manners. This is a heresy she confides only to Saren and, once, obliquely, to Marcon, who did not disagree as firmly as she hoped. Her examinations are famously severe because she is testing for the difference between a teacher who chose restraint and one who is merely obedient — and she can tell.

Thread: She fears certified restraint can become a habit of fear wearing good manners. Leverage: Certification nobody teaches the public form without; severity is the whole test.

Ilaria is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Ilaria approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps to one partner. Immaculate and formal; she writes letters the way others train and courts the same way, daily and seriously. Faithful to one partner, she declines other interest courteously and irreversibly.
