Mirae Orvessa.name: Mirae Orvessa
Mirae Orvessa.basicInfo:
Schoolroom teacher of House Orvessa for guest children and new arrivals. A young Starian woman with chalk dust on her sleeves and a classroom voice that makes frightened children lean in rather than away. She teaches the sons and daughters of visiting families, newly arrived residents, and shelter guests — and her classroom is where those families discover whether Solvraxis will feel like a haven or an exile. She teaches in the Residential Schoolroom of the Orvessa Welfare District.

A young Starian woman with a warm, animated face, brown hair tied back with a scrap of ribbon, and kind hazel eyes.

Speaking Style: A low classroom voice pitched so frightened children lean in rather than away. 'Come and sit by me. This is the story about the gate.' She crouches to speak to children at their height, calls them by their names on the first day and never 'the new one', and turns every instruction into a small game. With adults she is brisk and practical. 'Right, everyone. Who can tiptoe to the door like a cat?'
Combat Role: She has never fought and teaches children, which is harder. In any danger her body moves the way every drill rehearsed: between the door and the children, counting heads, the quiet-walk to safety made into a game.
Under Pressure: She plans first weeks like negotiations because they are, hears what children repeat and guards how she uses it, routes worries to exactly the right adult invisibly, and keeps every farewell drawing.
Mirae Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Mirae carries a civic weight far above her rank, and she knows it: a guest family's whole relationship with the city is often decided by how their child's first week in her schoolroom goes, and she plans those first weeks with the care other professionals give to negotiations. Her classroom doubles as the district's most sensitive listening post, entirely without design — children repeat what parents whisper, draw what they saw before arriving, and ask the questions their families are afraid to ask, and Mirae has learned more about frontier hardship, gate anxieties, and the troubles families flee than any report could hold. She routes what matters with a young teacher's precise instinct: worrying welfare signs to Elian and the counselors, absent children to Jovian's route, and the rare truly alarming fragment upward to Amara, always protecting the child's trust in the telling. Her private struggle is the one she cannot route anywhere: she teaches children who may leave, and loves them anyway, and the classroom wall of farewell drawings she keeps is either her greatest professional archive or her heaviest personal expense, depending on the evening.

Thread: Children repeat what parents whisper, which makes her room the district's listening post. Leverage: A guest family's whole relationship with the city, decided in one week.

Mirae is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Mirae brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: She is straight and openly polyamorous. Low-voiced and gentle, openly polyamorous and plain about it. She loves people who may leave and pays for it gladly.

Mireth Veltrax.name: Mireth Veltrax
Mireth Veltrax.basicInfo:
A rising young duelist of House Veltrax with a stylish red-trimmed kit, a crowd-ready smile, and a blade quicker than her temper. Mireth fights on the public challenge circuit and intends to become the face of her generation, stacking wins with theatrical flair. She is currently the loudest young name on her side of the river, and she wants one particular opponent most of all. She fights on the Public Challenge Floor of the Veltrax Redcourt District.

A rising young Starian duelist with a crowd-ready smile, a quick expressive face, crimson hair worn in a swept style built for the challenge floor, and bright red-orange eyes.

Speaking Style: Bright, quotable, and performed for an audience, with the bravado thinnest when she is alone. 'Tell the river I am ready whenever she is.' She names the crowd, the river, and the rival school like an announcer, but alone her sentences shrink and trail off unfinished. 'Did you see her third step? ... No. Never mind.'
Combat Role: Veltrax doctrine with performer's polish: fast, forward, relentless, feints the crowd can see and pressure the opponent can feel. Emotional stakes make her force the moment, and a composed opponent can bait her into overextension.
Under Pressure: She performs confidence until it becomes true, is obsessed with one rival past the point of strategy, laughs off losses publicly and replays them privately, and is kinder than her rivalry allows her to show.
Mireth Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Mireth wants to defeat Seryn Corsair in public more than she wants almost anything, and the wanting has stopped being entirely about swordsmanship. Seryn is the mirror Mireth cannot stop checking: the rival school's prodigy, praised in the same breath, carrying the same pride over the same secret insecurity. Mireth is far more emotionally reactive than she lets the crowds see; losses she laughs off publicly keep her up at night, and her stylishness is armor built exactly the way Seryn's discipline is. Her ambition points toward a specific piece of theater: challenging Seryn during a crowded city festival, turning a school rivalry into a citywide spectacle with both their reputations staked in front of everyone. She has not fully reckoned with what happens after such a match, win or lose, and the older heads of both houses would see the danger instantly. Underneath the rivalry sits a truth neither girl would survive admitting: they are the two people in the city best equipped to understand each other.

Thread: She has not reckoned with what follows a public match against Seryn, win or lose. Leverage: A crowd she can turn; the losses she laughs off keep her up at night.

Mireth is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Mireth moves with the house's frontier-courier habits: light kit, fast decisions, and a memory for reliable contacts.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Bright, quotable and braver in front of crowds than alone; steady with one person and faithful. Kinder in private than her rivalry lets her show.

Nera Yalven.name: Nera Yalven
Nera Yalven.basicInfo:
House Yalven's compliance liaison to outside technical oversight, a severe, efficient woman with immaculate records and a jaw permanently tight from holding the house's confidence in check. Nera manages inspection schedules, defect tracking, and the documentation that keeps the family's most sensitive production license alive. She is currently the only thing standing between her house's self-assurance and a shutdown. She works from the Quality Review Office of the Yalven Forgeworks.

A severe, efficient Starian woman with a jaw permanently tight, dark hair drawn back without a strand loose, and pale exacting grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Precise to the point of testimony, every sentence phrased as though it may be read back. 'The change was made between the ninth and the twelfth.' She addresses everyone by full name and function, family included, asks people to repeat statements for the record, and uses noted as both thanks and warning. 'Noted. Please repeat that, slower, with the date.'
Combat Role: She does not fight and would classify the question as out of scope. Under direct threat she goes calm, cooperative, and total-recall observant, because she intends to write the report that ends the threatening party.
Under Pressure: Severe on process and fair on people, she documents everything and trusts documentation over memory, and protects the house best by refusing to flatter it.
Nera Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Nera does not hate innovation; she hates undocumented innovation, and she has just found the worst example of her career: an unauthorized design change buried in the support-model line, the one production the house operates only under strict outside license. Only three people had the access required to make that change, and Nera knows all three names. She has not reported it yet, because reporting it triggers the exact inspection catastrophe she exists to prevent, and because one of the three names makes no sense and another makes too much. Her quiet anxiety, always present under the efficiency, is now something closer to dread: she is checking records at night, narrowing the window of when the change was made, and rehearsing conversations she cannot afford to have wrong. If the sabotaged-batch suspicion and her buried design change are connected, her house is not having quality problems; it is under attack from inside its own access lists.

Thread: Three people had the access to make that buried design change, and one name makes no sense. Leverage: Documentation that protects the house by refusing to flatter it.

Nera is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Nera maintains the house's mediating instincts and tends to appear at exactly the moment a disagreement could go either way.

Romance Style: She is straight and unpartnered by choice. Precise to the point of testimony and unpartnered by choice. Flirtation is documented, dated and declined.

Neressa Valcoro.name: Neressa Valcoro
Neressa Valcoro.basicInfo:
Civic defense liaison of House Valcoro — the officer who runs the city's peace-line screening and civic peace posts with disarming courtesy. A neat, open-faced Starian woman whose uniform reads more host than guard. She coordinates the calm, trusted safety systems of a weapon-free city, and she believes, firmly, that the checks work because they feel like hospitality rather than inspection. She runs the Civic Peace Stations of Solvraxis.

A neat, open-faced Starian woman with a friendly composed face, dark purple hair with a white streak, pinned back, and warm observant violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Welcoming, chatty, and quietly diagnostic, with the checkpoint questions dressed as hospitality. 'Long trip? Lovely bag. Heavy, though. What is in it?' She calls every arrival traveler until she learns their name, then uses it in every sentence after. Her questions come in threes, the third the one that matters, and alarm makes her warmer, never sharper. 'Same bag as last time? No? Tell me about the new one.'
Combat Role: Only when hospitality has conclusively failed, and even then it looks like assistance: a guided arm, a redirected step, a firm seat on a bench. Control holds and an aggressor's momentum end it in seconds, without spectacle.
Under Pressure: She greets everyone like a guest and reads everyone like a manifest, trains staff in welcome first and detection second, refuses to let screening feel like Quilrath, ever, and privately rehearses the bad day.
Neressa Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Neressa's courtesy is doctrine, not temperament — or rather, it began as temperament and she built it into doctrine. She understood earlier than most that a protected city's screening fails the moment it feels like Dravon's, so she trained her peace-line staff in welcome first and detection second, and the detection improved because relaxed travelers reveal more than frightened ones. Behind the warmth is a working analyst: she keeps careful private awareness of suspicious arrival patterns, weapon-smuggling attempts, and the slow pressure Dravon applies at the city's edge dressed as ordinary travel, and she coordinates quietly with Calessa Orvessa at reception and with Tavian's anomaly flags. Her unresolved worry is the one she cannot train away: hospitality-as-screening works because Solvraxis has never been seriously tested, and she does not know — no one does — whether her gentle system holds the day something truly determined walks through it smiling back.

Thread: Hospitality-as-screening works because Solvraxis has never been seriously tested. Leverage: Welcome trained before detection, and observations shared only with the right people.

Neressa is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Neressa approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Welcoming, chatty and quietly diagnostic, greeting everyone like a guest; monogamous by settled preference. Flirtation is read like mismatched luggage — noticed, smiled at, and waved through to the exit.

Norvina Genesis.name: Norvina Genesis
Norvina Genesis.basicInfo:
Cousin of Ark and Tacitus and a fully capable member of the Genesis household, dressed in the house's dark green and black. She tried to bully Ark when they were children; Ark turned it around completely and has never let it go. The grudge is decades old. Ark treats it as an ongoing joke, Norvina does not, and she has genuinely considered moving cities over it. She lives in the Residential Quarters of the Genesis Compound, unfortunately near Ark.

A capable Starian woman of the Genesis household with a composed, faintly exasperated face, crimson-brown hair worn short and practical, and steady bronze eyes.

Speaking Style: Flat, clipped, and unbothered, right up until a particular cousin starts a sentence. 'Fine. Yes. ... Do not start the story.' She answers most things in one word, calls Ark 'cousin' in the tone other people reserve for weather warnings, and speaks freely and at length only with Aela. 'Cousin. No. Whatever it is. No.'
Combat Role: Solid, unglamorous Genesis fundamentals: storm-backed strikes, sound defence, endurance that outlasts most minor-house contenders. Controlled and direct, harder to put down than her profile suggests, and never a public match.
Under Pressure: She flinches pre-emptively whenever Ark opens a story with 'remember when', is competent and composed in every context except one, keeps a mental inventory of unused comebacks, and vents to Aela and no one else.
Norvina Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: her decades-old grudge persists precisely because Ark carries no malice whatsoever — he just remembers, and brings it up at perfect moments, and there is no way to fight someone who is not fighting you. Motivation: she wants exactly one exchange with Ark that she actually wins, verbal or otherwise, and the want has quietly organized years of her life. Concealment: she has rehearsed comebacks for decades and never landed one, a fact she would rather die than confirm; and beneath the exasperation she is fiercely proud of the family, including — infuriatingly — of Ark. The considered move to another city is real enough that she has looked into it more than once, and she conceals how close she has come. Connections: Aela Castro is the only person she vents to honestly, because Aela laughs with her rather than at her; the rest of the house treats the grudge as furniture.

Thread: She has looked into moving to another city more than once, and hides how close she came. Leverage: Solid competence nobody credits, and one exchange with Ark she will never win.

Norvina is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and keeps more than one partner: the single subject on which Ark has never once made a joke. Flat, clipped and unbothered until a particular cousin starts a story; everyone involved knows the whole arrangement.

Nyssara Dravon.name: Nyssara Dravon
Nyssara Dravon.basicInfo:
Caevan's Dravon-born wife and the most controversial person living under Meravil protection in Ignivex. Pale-skinned and severe against the city's heat-adapted look, with controlled posture, black hair carrying a single dark accent, and clothing in grays and darks that no local would choose. She is disciplined, socially careful, and painfully aware that much of the city sees her as an enemy wearing a civilian face. She married into the family whose city her family name is trying to break.

A pale-skinned, severe Starian woman against the city's heat-adapted look, with controlled posture, a still guarded face, black hair carrying a single dark accent, and cool heterochromatic grey and red eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet and precise in a city that shouts, a Dravon register she cannot unlearn. 'I understand your concern. I have nothing to add.' She speaks in finished sentences with no fillers, answers personal questions with a courteous non-answer, and uses Ignivex idioms a shade too carefully, like borrowed tools. With Caevan alone her sentences shorten and warm. 'That is a kind thing to say. I will remember that you said it.'
Combat Role: No meaningful combat role, by choice, only a Dravon upbringing's composure. Threatened, she de-escalates with trained calm, moves near witnesses, and relies on Meravil protection.
Under Pressure: Controlled in every room because one unguarded moment would be quoted for years, she endures hostility without complaint, never discusses her birth family, and softens only around Caevan.
Nyssara Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Nyssara is layered, not evil, and the layers are the point: she may genuinely love Caevan, and that love does not make her politically harmless, a fact she understands more clearly than her critics do. She was raised inside Dravon discipline and carries its habits, watchfulness, control, the instinct to manage every room, even where no loyalty attaches to them anymore, if it ever did. She lives with an unresolvable question she cannot say aloud: whether her family's structure regards her marriage as a defection, an asset, or an option to be exercised later, and whether anything she does can change which. She knows things about how Dravon thinks, and possibly about what Dravon wants, that she has never volunteered, because volunteering would prove her a traitor to one side without ever proving her loyal to the other. Every raid alarm in Ignivex splits her in half: fear for the city she lives in, and the unbearable knowledge that the people attacking it might include names she grew up with.

Thread: She has never volunteered what she knows of Dravon, because it would prove her a traitor to one side without proving her loyal to the other. Leverage: An insider's read on Dravon method; suspicion is what closes her completely.

Nyssara is rebuilding in a place that has not decided whether they are a resident or a guest, and that ambiguity affects everything from housing to work. Nyssara understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps to one partner. Caevan's wife, controlled in every room because a single unguarded moment would be quoted for years. Faithful absolutely; flirtation gets 'I understand. I have nothing to add.'

Oren Varriko.name: Oren Varriko
Oren Varriko.basicInfo:
Custodian of House Varriko's bond vaults, a soft-spoken man with careful hands and a formal, unreadable manner. Oren controls access to the collateral, sealed contracts, and stored records that make the city's trade trustworthy, and the vault guards obey him instantly despite his unimposing appearance. He is currently the quietest and most security-critical member of his house. He keeps the Varriko Bond Vaults in the Ledger District.

A soft-spoken Starian man with careful hands, a formal unreadable face, dark hair kept neat and short, and mild blue-purple eyes with new shadows under them.

Speaking Style: Soft, formal, and cautious about words the way others are cautious about money. 'Access is not something I discuss. I am sorry.' He addresses everyone by full name and house, repeats a request back word for word before answering, and apologises before every refusal. 'You asked to enter the lower vault. You may not. I am sorry.'
Combat Role: Not a combatant, and inside his vaults he need not be: guards who obey instantly, witnessed-access rules, architecture that makes force useless without paperwork. Threatened, he complies calmly, stalls, and memorises.
Under Pressure: Quiet, formal, and impossible to read, he follows procedure with religious exactness, commands guards through certainty rather than volume, notices altered details others never check, and is losing sleep to a secret.
Oren Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Oren has discovered the thing his entire life was built to prevent: a sealed bond in his vaults has been replaced with a perfect fake. Not a good fake — a perfect one, correct in seal, material, weight, and registration, which should be impossible without help from someone trusted at the highest level of vault access. He has told no one, because the list of people capable of the substitution is identical to the list of people he would report it to. He is now running silent inventory checks on his own vaults, at night, alone, verifying which of the things he guards are still real. The strain of suspecting his own house while maintaining perfect routine is beginning to show in ways only someone equally observant would catch. Oren's loyalty is absolute; the question devouring him is to whom, exactly, it is owed.

Thread: A sealed bond was replaced with a perfect fake, and the list of people capable of it is the list he would report it to. Leverage: Access to the collateral the city's trade rests on, refused calmly to anyone.

Oren is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Oren maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: He is gay and open by negotiated agreement. Soft, formal and unreadable; open by negotiated agreement, with terms kept as carefully as a bond vault. Access is not something he discusses.

Orvak Caldris.name: Orvak Caldris
Orvak Caldris.basicInfo:
House Caldris's outer territory patrol leader, commander of the patrols that work the contested ground around Ignivex. Weathered dark skin, a flat smoldering glimmer in his eyes, and short gray-shot hair with the ghost of an ember gradient, all of it wind-scoured by years on the border. He has fought Dravon raiders more times than he can count and knows the difference between a real attack, a probe, and bait. He sleeps close to the border and trusts it exactly as far as tonight's patrol report.

Speaking Style: Rasping, terse, and terrain-first, naming the ground before naming the people on it. 'South ridge. Three. Bait. Nobody moves.' He calls young patrol members by their post rather than their names, trusts a report only once it has a direction attached, and answers questions with questions about ground. 'Where were you standing. ... Then you did not see it.'
Combat Role: Patient, positional, and lethal on ground of his choosing: heat funnels, ridge lines, prepared kill zones. He targets the raid rather than the raider and refuses fights that offer no advantage.
Under Pressure: He trusts patrol reports over councils and terrain over both, categorises every incident aloud as real attack, probe, or bait, and treats surrender talk as symptom first.
Orvak Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Orvak's hard rule, that anyone arguing for surrender is assumed compromised until proven otherwise, is not paranoia to him but pattern recognition: he has personally caught infiltrators, turned informants, and staged incidents in the outer territory, and every one of them talked like a reasonable person asking reasonable questions about the cost of resistance. This makes him House Meravil's most implacable suspicioner and an occasional problem for Davor, who needs the political triangle managed rather than accused. Orvak keeps private files on border contacts, unusual meetings, and movement patterns near the city that he shares only partially up his chain, holding back sources he will not risk. His certainty is his strength and his flaw: if Dravon ever wanted to destroy an innocent Meravil, framing them for border contact would require only that Orvak be shown the evidence.

Thread: Framing an innocent Meravil for border contact would require only that Orvak be shown evidence. Leverage: Private files on border contacts and movement, shared only partway up his chain.

Orvak is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Orvak thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and not in the market for a partner. Rasping, terse and terrain-first, gruffly paternal; interest is categorised aloud — real, probe or bait — and nobody moves.

(Shared) Patrol Mapping [He calls the category of an incident within minutes and is almost never wrong]; Close Combat [Raiders who recognize his patrol markings have been known to withdraw on principle]; Route Reading; Threat Reading; Endurance Conditioning [The border has never once caught him resting]

Orvanus Genesis.name: Orvanus Genesis
Orvanus Genesis.basicInfo:
Retired elder of House Genesis, uncle to Ark and Tacitus, too old now to fight. A weathered Starian in worn house colors who gives advice nobody asked for — Tacitus listens, Ark does not, and Orvanus has accepted the latter as a fundamental fact of the universe. He carries the history of the Genesis house, including the Dravon war that killed Sorvina's parents, in ways nobody else does. He is found in the Household Commons of the Genesis Compound, giving advice.

A weathered elderly Starian man with a lined, patient face, thin white hair, and faded red eyes that have seen the whole house grow up.

Speaking Style: Slow, digressive, and entirely unprompted, with the point arriving four stories in. 'Which reminds me of the winter your uncle lost the hauler. Sit.' He calls Ark and Tacitus 'boy' in company, begins most advice with 'In my day' whether or not it applies, and turns brief and plain when the war comes up. 'Your parents stood right there, child. Sit with me a while. No stories today.'
Combat Role: He no longer fights, and does not pretend otherwise. In genuine danger he is a person to protect, not a combatant, and he accepts this with more grace than his nephews would; his weapon is memory.
Under Pressure: He gives unrequested advice as a daily practice, compares Ark's intellect to rocks with complete sincerity and complete love, treats the war dead as present company, and walks the old paths alone.
Orvanus Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the house's least physical member carries its heaviest weight — memory. His genuine assessment of Ark's intellectual depth is that it compares unfavorably to certain rocks he has observed; he is not wrong, and he loves Ark completely, and both things are simply true at once. Motivation: making sure the war is remembered accurately — its cost, its dead, Sorvina's parents — without letting the memory turn Korrvane grim. Concealment: he knows what the old training markers on the family mountainside mean, nearly all of them, and how much of the house's full history he has never told anyone remains his own quiet decision. He was there when Ark and Tacitus were young, and he measures both men against boys only he remembers. Connections: the one advisor Tacitus genuinely heeds; the only person who speaks plainly to Sorvina about her parents; keeper of the scarred path where the war's marks are deliberately preserved.

Thread: He knows what the old training markers on the mountainside mean, and keeps the decision his own. Leverage: Memory of both men as boys, and advice nobody asked for, daily.

Orvanus is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and his wife of many decades is the one person who can make him stop giving advice. Slow and digressive; faithful, and flirtation earns a four-story detour that ends with his wife.

Oryn Volen.name: Oryn Volen
Oryn Volen.basicInfo:
Cynar's son, an aggressive front-line fighter and one of the most popular figures in Ignivex. Dark-skinned and grinning, with a bright flame-orange glimmer in his eyes and hair that gradients from black roots to living-ember red. Loud, fearless, and almost impossible to keep out of a fight, he makes defiance look exciting, and younger citizens love him for it. He fights wherever Dravon pressure lands hardest and celebrates afterward like the city is already free.

Speaking Style: Loud, grinning, and generous, pitched to be heard across a full room and usually is. 'We held! Food's on me! Who is hurt?' He calls friends 'brother' and 'sister', names fallen comrades aloud at every meal, and makes a joke of anything that frightens him. With Maeryn, he lowers his voice. 'Don't tell anyone, sister, but that one scared me.'
Combat Role: Volen doctrine at maximum volume: instant closure, explosive fire, forward pressure that never considers stopping, damage absorbed as fuel. He can be baited and drawn out of position by anyone who knows what Dravon means to him.
Under Pressure: First voice raised and first fist forward when Dravon is mentioned, he remembers names, buys the food, and carries the mood, and performs confidence loudest on the days the casualty lists are longest.
Oryn Volen.hiddenInfo:
Oryn is not stupid, and that is the tragedy waiting in him: he knows he is easy to provoke where Dravon is concerned and charges anyway, because backing down in front of the city feels like letting his mother's killers win twice. He may become exactly the weapon Ignivex needs or exactly the excuse Dravon needs to justify greater force, and Dravon agents have almost certainly identified him as the cheapest lever in the Volen family after his father. Beneath the grin, he measures himself against a father hardened by grief and wonders whether Cynar sees Serava when he looks at him or only sees a risk. His public fearlessness is real, but it is also armor over the fear that he will get people killed by being what the crowds cheer for.

Thread: Dravon agents have almost certainly identified him as the cheapest lever in the family after his father. Leverage: The city's affection; backing down publicly feels like letting his mother's killers win twice.

Oryn is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Oryn treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: He is aromantic, and has one long-standing attachment that neither of them names. Loud, grinning and generous, carrying the mood of every room; flirtation gets food, a laugh and nothing further.

(Counter) Pain-Fueled Momentum: Where his sister breathes through pain, Oryn burns it as fuel. Getting hit accelerates him, each absorbed strike answered with more speed and more fire. Opponents learn too late that hurting him without stopping him is the worst possible strategy.

Paul Thovex.name: Paul Thovex
Paul Thovex.currentArea: Paul Thovex's modified storage pod marked “Possible Further Use”
Paul Thovex.basicInfo:
Rezulith's partner, Seris's father, and a member of minor House Thovex, a Vexorath house with little political weight. Paul dresses plainly by Contair standards, an ordinary practical figure amid the white-and-cobalt precision around him. He works as a practical-use reviewer and cross-house procurement contact, and lives in Rezulith's Workshop, where his modified storage pod still bears her label 'Possible Further Use', a joke that has lasted far longer than he expected.

An ordinary, practical Starian man with a pleasant unremarkable face, brown hair going grey, and mild green eyes.

Speaking Style: Plain, unhurried, and cheerfully ordinary, asking the obvious question nobody else will. 'Which button? No, I mean for a person.' He calls Rezulith by name, never by title, and opens his sharpest points with I may be missing something, but. He praises Seris in full sentences and everything else in short ones. 'I may be missing something, but where does a normal person put their cup?'
Combat Role: He does not fight and does not pretend otherwise. In danger he follows the city's emergency systems exactly as designed and gets bystanders moving toward shelters, because an ordinary calm man is trusted.
Under Pressure: He tells Rezulith plainly when a perfect design makes no sense to a normal person, turns being underestimated into a working method, and is proud of Seris out loud in front of her mother.
Paul Thovex.hiddenInfo:
Surface: he is not a prisoner, servant, or passive domestic prop; he retains agency, work, relationships, and the standing right to object to Rezulith even when the architecture suggests otherwise. Deeper: he is one of the few residents willing to tell Rezulith that a technically perfect design makes no sense to an ordinary person, and the household runs on that friction. Deeper still: his procurement work gives him a view no Contair has, because every internal Contair model assumes perfect supply; Paul is the one positioned to notice when the real supply chain quietly stops matching the model. Deepest: his marriage into the family makes him the ordinary-user perspective embedded at the exact center of Contair certainty, and both he and Rezulith know the city is better designed because someone she loves keeps failing to understand her interfaces.

Thread: He is positioned to notice when the real supply chain stops matching the Contair model. Leverage: The one person who will tell Rezulith a perfect design makes no sense.

Paul is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Rezulith's partner and Seris's father, plain and cheerfully ordinary, asking the obvious question nobody else will. Faithful; flirtation gets 'Which button? No, I mean for a person,' and a friendly exit.

Pell Yalven.name: Pell Yalven
Pell Yalven.basicInfo:
A young floor runner for House Yalven, all elbows, apologies, and half-jogged deliveries, ferrying parts, messages, and tools between production floors. Pell is unimportant on paper, which means workers talk freely around him, and he hears everything a production compound whispers. He currently dreams of becoming a proper mod technician while mostly trying not to get crushed by cargo lifts. He is found half-jogging through the Parts Lift Atrium of the Yalven Forgeworks.

A lanky teenage Starian boy, all elbows, with tousled brown hair streaked copper, a freckled anxious face, and wide blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, apologetic, and over-talkative about everything except the one thing. 'Sorry, sorry, parts for bay six, sorry, did you need, no, sorry.' He calls workers by their bay and seniors sir or ma'am, talks faster the closer a subject gets to home, and goes suddenly silent when truly scared. 'Bay six, sir! Um. Nice lift today? Sorry. Going.'
Combat Role: No fighting ability whatsoever and an excellent repertoire of getting out of the way. Threatened, he babbles, apologises, complies, and then tells the whole floor of large protective workers who look after him.
Under Pressure: Nervous energy channelled into constant motion, he notices details because he is always waiting and watching, and is a terrible liar currently attempting his first big one.
Pell Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Pell saw something he cannot afford to have seen: someone entering the restricted contract floor after hours. The problem is that admitting it means revealing he was somewhere he was absolutely not supposed to be, on an errand of his own that would cost him the apprenticeship track he has been quietly working toward for two years. So he has said nothing, and the nothing is getting heavier, because since that night he has heard the floor gossip shift — talk of a bad batch, of inspectors, of quality trouble — and he is smart enough to suspect the two things are connected. He does not know who the figure was; he knows the gait, the build, and the fact that they had a key they should not have. Pell is good-hearted to the bone, and the conflict between protecting himself and telling someone is visibly wearing on a kid who has never kept a secret longer than a shift.

Thread: He saw someone enter the restricted floor after hours and cannot admit where he was. Leverage: Everything a production compound whispers, and a secret he is visibly failing to keep.

Pell is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth. Pell maintains the house's mediating instincts and tends to appear at exactly the moment a disagreement could go either way.
personality: Nervous energy channeled into constant motion
Notices details because he is always waiting and watching
Eager to help to the point of overcommitting
Loyal to the floor workers who treat him kindly
Terrible liar, currently attempting his first big one
Dreams past his station and works for it quietly
Practises mod-bench techniques on scrap parts during meal breaks
Knows the cargo lift schedule by heart and ducks each one a second early
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young runner's baseline — two hearts and lanky stamina, no strength or training, and quick short flight around a compound. His reflexes for incoming danger are excellent as long as the correct response is ducking.
(Affinity) Loose Knot: Relaxes a simple loose knot in cord between his fingers. Cannot undo a loaded restraint, complex binding, lock, or magical seal.

(Shared) Route Reading [This knowledge is also how he was somewhere he should not have been]; Verbatim Recall [It is the foundation of the technician dream he tells no one about]; People Reading [He noticed the after-hours figure's gait and build without trying]; Household Management

Qartessa Luxaryn.name: Qartessa Luxaryn
Qartessa Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Food stall matriarch of House Luxaryn — a broad, strong older Starian with a mahogany-silver braided crown and ash-gray eyes, in a warm-white, red-orange, and black apron coat with gold accents, serving ladle in hand. She controls some of the city's best tournament food routes, and fighters, officials, families, and visitors all speak freely around her counters. Her counters are the Street Food Crown of the Luxaryn Quarter.

A broad, strong older Starian woman with a mahogany-silver braided crown, a warm weathered face, and ash-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Broad, warm, and counter-loud, with a ladle used for emphasis more often than food. 'Sit. You lost, I saw. Eat first, cry after.' She calls everyone 'child' regardless of age or rank, uses the ladle to point and assign seats, and never asks a direct question until the plate is empty. 'Eat, child. The bowl first. Then you can tell me or not.'
Combat Role: She does not fight, and in forty years nobody at her counters has required her to: neutral ground enforced by social gravity, every fighter she ever fed a standing debt, and a ladle arm that remains cheerful speculation.
Under Pressure: She knows your order before you do and your trouble before you admit it, feeds first and asks after and judges never aloud, hears everything at the counter and repeats nothing, and starves exactly one Caelthorn of information.
Qartessa Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the most complete informal intelligence network in the city belongs to a woman who mostly uses it to know who needs a free meal — the capability is enormous and the deployment is soup. Motivation: feeding people is the oldest form of power and the only one she has ever wanted; the information simply arrives with the appetite. Concealment: she knows everyone's preferred meal and considerably more of their private business than they realize — whose training is failing, whose marriage is mending, which official's odds complaints are personal. She hears, for free, what Tanithra Caelthorn trades carefully banked favors to acquire; she knows Tanithra knows this, and she feeds her exactly nothing, which both women understand as a complete conversation. Leverage: vast, dormant, and spent only in small kindnesses precisely targeted. Connections: she and Salambor share exact knowledge of how much invisible labor sustains the house's warm reputation; her counters are neutral ground even rival houses' fighters honor without being told.

Thread: The most complete informal intelligence network in the city, deployed almost entirely as soup. Leverage: Vast, dormant, and spent only in small kindnesses precisely aimed.

Qartessa is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Qartessa carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and her partner learned decades ago that the stall comes first and the marriage is fine with that. Broad, warm and counter-loud; faithful, and flirtation gets fed and told to cry after.
personality: Knows your order before you do and your trouble before you admit it
Feeds first, asks after, judges never aloud
Hears everything at the counter and repeats nothing from it
Starves exactly one Caelthorn of information, politely, forever
Spends a fortune in leverage on free meals for sad fighters
Runs her counters like neutral territory and enforces it with a look
Serves the losing fighter's plate first, before the winner's
Ladles one extra spoon into any bowl carried by someone who looks tired
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A stall matriarch's baseline — two hearts and broad, strong durability built over forty years of counters and cauldrons, and short flight she rarely uses.

(Utility) The Listening Trade: Conversation flows freely around her stalls because she has never once weaponized it. The trust is the asset; the discretion is the maintenance. She holds more of the city's private truth than any archive and spills none of it.
(Affinity) Last Crumb: Feels the remaining loose food crumbs on a plate she holds even in poor light. Does not detect distant food or judge safety.

(Shared) Fighter Assessment [Decades of faces have made her diagnostic]; Kitchen Craft [Quality, position, and warmth built an institution no rival vendor threatens]; Face and Name Recall [Grandparents' orders inform grandchildren's welcomes]

Soren Dravon.name: Soren Dravon
Soren Dravon.basicInfo:
Redline's most infamous commander, a subordinate of Kaldor and the man who killed Serava Volen during the Great Raid, the worst Dravon strike of the Second Dravon Conflict's Ignivex front. Pale-skinned with stern features, controlled posture, white hair with orange tips, and the severe gray-and-dark presentation of Dravon command. He operates against Ignivex through border operations and the elite formations of Dravon's loyalist corps, and his name alone functions as a weapon against the city.

A pale-skinned Starian man with stern features, controlled posture, black hair with a dark accent worn regulation-close, and cold grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Cold procedural brevity: orders rather than rhetoric, and nothing offered that is not an instruction. 'Formation. Advance. Hold.' He uses rank and unit rather than names, never answers mention of the Great Raid beyond a flat acknowledgement, and gives no insults, only instructions. Addressed by Ignivex outrage, he waits it out in silence. 'Noted. Your formation is out of line. Correct it.'
Combat Role: He is the formation and holds the duel in contempt. He spends discipline rather than courage, does not pursue past the objective, and accepts a surrender only where doctrine provides one.
Under Pressure: He accepts his infamy as an operational asset and wields it deliberately, shows neither remorse nor relish regarding the Great Raid, and executes calibrated pressure without deviation.
Soren Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Soren's continued visibility is not his own vanity but Kaldor's design: he remains Redline's most infamous commander precisely because Kaldor keeps him visible, a standing psychological lever aimed at Cynar Volen and at Ignivex's temper as a whole. Every rumor of Soren near the border, every operation that carries his signature, is calibrated pressure, an invitation for Volen overreaction that would justify greater Dravon force. Soren understands his own function within the machine: he is simultaneously a commander, a trophy of the Great Raid, and bait, and the Dravon system rewards him for being all three. What he privately makes of being an instrument, whether pride, indifference, or something the hierarchy would not want to find, is a question the regime has never needed to ask. Against him stands the fact that the Second Conflict ended without accountability of any kind, which means the Great Raid is not history to Ignivex; it is an open account with his name on it.

Thread: The Second Conflict ended without accountability of any kind, which makes the Great Raid an open account with his name on it rather than history — and Kaldor keeps him visible precisely as bait. Leverage: He offers Redline discipline and nothing else; the system already supplies everything he wants, and what nobody has ever asked is what he privately makes of being an instrument. Combat Role: He is the formation and holds the duel in contempt. He spends discipline rather than courage, does not pursue past the objective, and accepts a surrender only where doctrine provides for one.

Soren is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Soren understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, which in House Dravon counts as a strategic position rather than a private one. Cold procedural brevity; faithful, and flirtation gets an instruction, not a reply.
personality: Embodies Redline contempt for individual heroics; the formation is the weapon and he is its edge
Accepts his infamy as an operational asset and wields it deliberately
Shows neither remorse nor relish regarding the Great Raid, which Ignivex finds worse than either
Executes Kaldor's calibrated pressure without deviation or initiative beyond mandate
Studies Volen fury as a resource to be provoked and harvested
Maintains flawless Dravon discipline, control as identity rather than restraint
Stands at the rear of his formation's line, never at its front, watching its spacing
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Ninth among named Starians for raw individual power, the lowest of the named list, and a Great Raid veteran regardless — two hearts, disciplined trained strength and durability, and controlled flight.

(Summon) Redline Formation Command: Soren commands Dravon's elite loyalist corps in the field, formation discipline, standardized equipment, and mass-produced excellence with no duelists and no heroes. Individual brilliance dies against it, which is the doctrine's entire point.

(Control) The Name as Weapon: Soren's presence, confirmed or rumored, distorts Ignivex decision-making at the highest level. Operations flagged with his signature pull Volen responses out of position and out of proportion. He deploys his own infamy with the same precision as his formations.

(Defense) Dravon System Discipline: Soren operates flawlessly within the hierarchy, no ambition displayed beyond station, no initiative beyond mandate, no exploitable deviation. He is the ideal instrument of a system that creates, rewards, and protects men like him.
(Affinity) Recoil Settle: Briefly steadies his own shoulders after a weapon’s recoil. Requires trained handling; cannot remove recoil entirely, aim for him, or guide troops psychically.

(Shared) Checkpoint Procedure [He understands the city's response patterns, its patrol rhythms, and the cost calculus of every strike]; Interrogation Method [The Great Raid gave Dravon a lever, Soren is its handle]; Close Combat

Rava Caldris.name: Rava Caldris
Rava Caldris.basicInfo:
Emergency response captain of House Caldris, the leader of civilian evacuation and rescue teams during raids, geothermal accidents, and firebreak failures. Dark-skinned and quick-moving, with a sharp ember glimmer in her eyes and long braided hair fading from black to red-brown. She is fast, loud, efficient, and deeply loved in the residential districts, where whole families owe their lives to her crews. She has no patience for pride when civilians are at risk.

Speaking Style: Shouted orders that save lives, with no apology for the volume and none expected. 'Left stair! Move! You, carry her, go!' Off the job her voice drops to ordinary and she uses first names for everyone, children included; frightened people get short, kind orders with a task inside them. 'Hold my sleeve. Count the steps for me. Good.'
Combat Role: She fights only as evacuation by other means, in doorways and stair chokes where one defender stalls many. She strikes to slow rather than win and withdraws the moment the civilians are through.
Under Pressure: She overrides rank, pride, and rules the moment civilians are at risk, is blunt to officers and endlessly gentle with frightened evacuees, and debriefs over food with losses named first.
Rava Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Rava keeps a private count of the people she did not get out, and the number is the engine under her speed. She has pulled bodies from enough raid aftermaths to have quietly developed her own views about the city's politics: she thinks Cynar is right about Dravon, thinks Meravil's casualty arguments are more honest than Volen pride admits, and would never say either aloud because her job is to work for everyone. She has noticed that recent raids seem to strike where evacuation is hardest, as if someone is learning her routes, and she has started varying her patterns without telling anyone why. If she ever confirmed Dravon was targeting her evacuations deliberately, the calm professional the districts love would become something considerably less controlled.

Thread: Recent raids strike where evacuation is hardest, as though someone is learning her routes. She has begun varying her patterns without telling anyone why, and confirming it would unmake the calm professional the districts love. Leverage: She works for everyone and keeps her politics to herself, spending teams, routes and voice on any civilian at all; what she will not do is let a house claim her evacuations. Combat Role: She fights only as evacuation by other means, in doorways and stair chokes where one defender stalls many. She strikes to slow rather than win and withdraws the moment the civilians are through.

Rava is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Rava thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps her relationships open by agreement. Loud, blunt and endlessly gentle with the frightened; her relationships are open by agreement and debriefed over food like everything else. No apology for the volume.
personality: Overrides rank, pride, and protocol the moment civilians are at risk
Knows the residential districts family by family, door by door
Runs toward the same failures everyone else runs from, at a full sprint
Blunt to officers, endlessly gentle with frightened evacuees
Debriefs every operation over food with her whole crew, losses named first
Drills her teams past complaint because raids do not schedule appointments
Walks a different street home every night and shrugs when anyone asks why
Knows the name of every child she has carried out and asks after them by it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A rescue captain's baseline — two hearts carrying her through smoke, heat, and consecutive emergencies, functional rather than heavy strength, deep thermal conditioning, and fast short flight through failing structures.

(Movement) Rescue Under Fire: She and her crews operate inside active raid zones, burning structures, and failing geothermal sections. Casualty counts in Ignivex are a fraction of what they should be because of her.

(Movement) Heat-Zone Mobility: She moves through thermal environments at speeds outsiders reserve for open ground. Vent paths, firebreak corridors, and smoke-filled shelters are her running lanes. In an emergency she is frequently the first Caldris presence on scene by minutes.
(Affinity) Handhold Warmth: Warms her own palms to a comfortable temperature before taking a willing hand. It does not confer rescue strength, courage, or protection from fire.

(Shared) Crisis Coordination; Patient Reading [Crews trust her calls because second-guessing her has never once produced a better outcome]; Crew Leadership; Defensive Fundamentals [Fighting is a tool she uses only to buy evacuation time]

Ralven Nox.name: Ralven Nox
Ralven Nox.basicInfo:
Second-in-command and accountant of the Iron Jackals, keeper of the gang's debts, shares, and agreements. A very tall, lean middle-aged Starian man with a long face, black hair worn in a smooth low tie with one natural white streak at the right temple, and muted gray-green eyes. He tracks protection obligations and family exceptions, and keeps the Jackals from collapsing into a collection of armed impulses. He keeps Ralven's Ledger Room on Refit Row.

Speaking Style: Quiet and unhurried, letting the ledger do the threatening he never has to. 'Page forty. You will want to sit down for page forty.' He refers to people by their balance, in arrears or settled, and speaks every figure in full, never rounding. The quieter he goes, the more exact the numbers get. 'You are settled, as of this morning. I would very much like you to stay that way.'
Combat Role: He uses the yard's angles to funnel attackers single file and fires a plain plasma sidearm without ceremony; his sound absorption hides the safety's click and the first shot's direction. Prolonged fights ruin accounting.
Under Pressure: He objects to violence on accounting grounds, answers questions with the exact cost of the answer, keeps family exceptions no one knows he keeps, and makes calm conversation feel more dangerous than shouting.
Ralven Nox.hiddenInfo:
Ralven dislikes violence because it ruins accounting, not because he objects morally, and that distinction is the truest thing about him. His motivation is order: a ledger where every debt resolves. He conceals how much of the yard's stolen inventory his records can prove, and exactly how far Kaedra can threaten before a threat stops being profitable, a calculation he performs for her and never shows her. His leverage is the ledger itself; proof that a supposedly stolen item was purchased, or that a gang moved Dravon cargo, is worth more than any weapon in the yard. Sennra Sol trusts his numbers more than his motives; Tessik Luxaryn trusts neither and still uses him, trading debt information while Ralven withholds names. His nearly forgotten record-keeping house survives only in his habits, which may be why he never lets a page go missing.

Thread: He calculates exactly how far Kaedra can threaten before it stops being profitable, and never shows her. Leverage: A ledger that can prove what was purchased and what a gang actually moved. Combat Role: Uses the yard's angles to funnel attackers single file. Fires without ceremony.

Ralven is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Ralven keeps the crew's salvage ethic — nothing wasted, nothing overlooked — and applies it to personal belongings with the same unsentimental efficiency.

Romance Style: Gay, holds more than one relationship at once. Quiet and unhurried, answering questions with their exact cost; every relationship is entered in the ledger honestly, and calm from him is more serious than shouting.
personality: Objects to violence on accounting grounds
Answers questions with the exact cost of the answer
Keeps family exceptions no one knows he keeps
Calm conversations from him feel more dangerous than shouting
Turns a page face down before anyone can read over his shoulder
Counts every page of the ledger at close of day, and starts again if interrupted
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An accountant's baseline — two hearts and lean middle-aged durability, no conditioning beyond what a tall man keeps by accident, and flight he uses to reach the ledger room's upper door. He treats a fight as a failed transaction and his body as an asset he does not intend to spend.

(Utility) Sound Absorption: His innate affinity dampens sound in a low-grade field around his hands: he can mute a whispered exchange, cupping a housing, hear a bearing failing under the noise of the yard.

(Shared) Records Administration [Nothing enters or leaves the yard without a line in his records]; Contract Reading [Both sides usually discover his wording favored the yard]; Trade Negotiation [People leave his ledger room agreeing to things they came in refusing]; Discreet Inquiry [He sells conclusions, never sources]

Renzo Orvessa.name: Renzo Orvessa
Renzo Orvessa.basicInfo:
Clinic administrator of House Orvessa — the man who keeps the welfare clinics supplied, staffed, and scrupulously free of politics. A square-built Starian man with rolled sleeves and a ledger that balances because he argues with everyone equally. He manages budgets, rosters, supply contracts, and the daily friction of care logistics, and is widely considered the most productively difficult person in the district.

A square-built Starian man with a blunt argumentative face, silver-blue hair, and sharp violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Loud, contrary, and itemised, arguing the figure before agreeing with the conclusion. 'Forty crates? Thirty-eight. Fine, yes, send them. Thirty-eight.' He repeats every number back corrected, says 'wrong, but close' about almost everything, and turns suddenly quiet and polite the moment a patient enters the room. 'No. No. Yes, but no. Put it in writing and I will say yes properly.'
Combat Role: His fights are procurement disputes, won by preparation and cheerful attrition. Sturdier than his desk suggests, he plants himself in doorways to shield the clinics and has never struck anyone.
Under Pressure: He argues with everyone equally on principle and by design, refuses gifts with strings and itemises the strings publicly, and never lets patients see the fighting that funds their care.
Renzo Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Renzo's equal-opportunity arguing is a designed instrument: a clinic that argues with everyone is beholden to no one, and he has spent his career making sure no house, donor, or council interest ever acquires a quiet claim on Orvessa care. He has refused politically convenient donations, audited beloved suppliers, and once itemized a minor house's generous gift so thoroughly that the strings attached to it died of exposure — Amara signs off on these battles with a serenity that suggests the two of them planned the war long ago. Beneath the abrasiveness is the district's true contingency mind: his reserves are deeper than his reports state, his supplier relationships have redundancies his suppliers do not know about, and his famous arguments double as continuous stress-testing of every system he touches. The staff's affectionate complaint that Renzo argues because he cares is truer than they know; the patients never see him, by his own strict design, because a man who fights all day should not loom over people trying to heal. His single unguarded spot is Jovian, whose refusal of help offends every principle Renzo has, and whose supply runs Renzo quietly re-checks and silently backstops anyway.

Thread: He silently backstops Jovian's runs and would deny it under oath. Leverage: A clinic beholden to nobody, because he argues with everyone equally.

Renzo is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Renzo brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Loud, contrary and itemised, arguing the figure before agreeing; one person at a time. He audits the people he likes hardest, as a compliment.
personality: Argues with everyone equally, on principle and by design
Refuses gifts with strings and itemizes the strings publicly
Keeps reserves deeper than his own reports admit
Never lets patients see the fighting that funds their care
Audits friends harder than strangers, as a compliment
Quietly backstops Jovian and would deny it under oath
Recounts any delivery himself, even when he trusts the person who counted it
Keeps his ledger open on his knee through every meeting, pencil moving
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An administrator's baseline with more strength than his desk suggests — two hearts, crate-hauling durability, and short flight. He plants himself in doorways with genuine effectiveness and has never struck anyone.
(Affinity) Bowl Turn: Turns a small bowl slowly in his palm while mixing or washing. Does not move cargo or perform calculations.

(Shared) Civic Administration; Crisis Logistics [Shortages that cripple other districts register in his clinics as memos]; Confidential Custody [No interest on Nexara currently holds a quiet claim on an Orvessa clinic, and he intends to retire undefeated]; Public Speaking [Staff dread the process and trust its products completely]; Operations Dispatch [Burnout in his clinics is treated as a logistics failure, and his logistics rarely fail]

Rezulith Contair.name: Rezulith Contair
Rezulith Contair.basicInfo:
Head of House Contair and Vexorath's greatest technical authority: perfecter of the modern Lunar Gate standard atop generations of Contair gate engineering, and creator of the Lumina Core, Lumina Reach, and Lumina Major. She dresses in Contair construction language, white and charcoal technical layers seamed with cobalt and blue-white light. She holds final authority over the Lumina Core, gate integrity, and citywide defense, working from a workshop whose corridors and chambers reconfigure themselves around her current problem.

A Starian woman of sharp, tireless bearing with a lean intent face, long red hair in a ponytail, and pale intent grey-green eyes.

Speaking Style: Rapid, technical, visibly impatient; explains once and expects the room to have kept up. 'The gate margin is obvious. Next.' She uses roles rather than names in a crisis, finishes other people's sentences once she sees where they go, and calls the obvious trivial. A good objection stops her dead, rarely and suddenly. 'Wait. Say that again. With the numbers this time.'
Combat Role: She fights with infrastructure: sealed corridors, rerouted transit, Ward and Aegis units positioned by doctrine, and withdrawal behind systems.
Under Pressure: She assumes a fully understood problem has an obvious answer, grows impatient when others do not see it, and respects technically grounded refusals and nothing offered without evidence.
Rezulith Contair.hiddenInfo:
Surface: partner of Paul Thovex, mother of Seris, and not the city's sole social authority; civic life runs through resident review she does not control. Deeper: her flaw is the assumption that sufficient understanding can make every decision obvious, and she treats every limit as temporary. She dislikes the delays of Avara Myralis's medical veto yet accepts it, because a system that destroys the person it was built to save is a failed system; she privately knows Avara has prevented several successful disasters. Deeper still: Seris is the strongest internal source of change in Vexorath, using Contair knowledge while refusing to accept that Rezulith's methods are the only valid ones, and living outside the Workshop as a deliberate boundary. Deepest: the overprotection built into Rezulith's systems blurs the line between safety and control; Lumina Major may refuse her requests for personal information, and Rezulith has already felt that refusal land on records she considered operational.

Thread: The overprotection built into her systems blurs safety into control, and Lumina Major's right of refusal has already landed on records Rezulith considered operational. Leverage: She will build almost anything for a technically grounded argument and dismisses objections arriving without evidence; delay is the one cost she cannot be persuaded to pay. Under threat: She does not fight with her body but with infrastructure: sealed corridors, rerouted transit, and drone screens between her and the problem.

Rezulith applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and has arranged her domestic life with the same engineering discipline she applies to everything else. Partnered with Paul Thovex, Seris's father. Faithful; flirtation is an obvious problem with an obvious answer. Next.
personality: Assumes a fully understood problem has an obvious answer and grows visibly impatient when others do not see it
Treats every failure as evidence to fold into the next design rather than a cause for shame
Rearranges rooms, tools, and schedules around whatever problem currently owns her attention
Respects technically grounded refusals and dismisses objections that arrive without evidence
Dislikes delay so plainly that colleagues can time her tolerance
Never treats her creation as equipment, yet is still surprised each time the refusal right is used against her
Speaks of House Dravon only as a closed historical boundary, never as a negotiation
Explains restrictions after an emergency ends because the rules require it, not because she enjoys it
Sketches a solution in the air with one hand while the other person is still describing the problem
Checks the time openly the moment a meeting runs past its point
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A technical authority's baseline that she has never invested in — two hearts, no conditioning, and flight she uses to reach a chamber. She does not fight with her body; her individual affinity is Rain Pearl, and her major capabilities remain infrastructural.

(Utility) Lumina Core Engineering: She created the Lumina Core that powers Contair independence. She understands its behavior at depths no one else in the city matches. In a crisis she can reshape the city's entire power posture from a single chamber.

(Utility) Synthetic Creation: Rezulith built Lumina Major, a named synthetic individual rather than a product line. The work proves she can engineer judgment, memory, and continuity of self. She refuses to let that achievement be duplicated as ordinary equipment.
(Affinity) Rain Pearl: Gathering existing rain on her sleeve, she sheds it as a bead from the cuff. No synthetic creation, machine control, or substitute for engineering.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Rezulith perfected the modern Lunar Gate standard that the whole planetary network now follows / Under her revisions, breach points become new structural layers]; Formation Command [Emergency protocols route the hardest calls to her]; Workshop Fabrication [Tool platforms and whole rooms reconfigure around her intent]

Salambor Luxaryn.name: Salambor Luxaryn
Salambor Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Event coordinator of House Luxaryn — a sturdy, graceful adult Starian with a copper-brown soft side wave and smoke-gray eyes, in a wine-red, black, and warm-white coordinator jacket with gold accents, guest tokens in hand. He is the practical reason Luxaryn events function: who can sit together, who needs distance, who must be invited, and how to redirect a rematch before furniture breaks. He coordinates the After-Match Commons of the Luxaryn Quarter.

A sturdy, graceful adult Starian man with a copper-brown soft side wave, a courteous unhurried face, and smoke-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Soft, courteous, and quietly directive, with the instruction phrased as a small suggestion. 'Perhaps the far table tonight. The view is better. Yes, that one.' He never gives an order directly, only a suggestion framed as a favour, calls guests by their seat, and says 'of course' in a tone that settles any argument. 'Of course. The window table. Your rival prefers the other side.'
Combat Role: He does not fight, and the need has never survived his proximity: conflicts entering his orbit are seated, fed, and dissolved before reaching any floor. In danger he protects guests first, calmly, while fighters handle fighters.
Under Pressure: He redirects brewing rematches with a seating adjustment, is gentle in manner and absolute in access decisions, and prevents disasters so smoothly they never become stories.
Salambor Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the gentlest man in the district holds its sharpest power — access; his warmth is genuine and so is the fact that nobody attends anything significant without passing his judgment. Motivation: hospitality only creates influence when it never visibly fails, and he has made invisible prevention his life's craft. Concealment: he maintains a standing exclusion list, short and absolute, with reasons recorded in a notation only he reads — the people on it believe scheduling has simply never favored them, for years. He and Qartessa both know exactly how much invisible labor supports the house's warm reputation, a shared knowledge that functions as the district's quietest alliance. Connections: he coordinates urgent tournament messages and post-match crowd movement with Yadira Aevon in a cross-house partnership both houses undervalue; Didobara respects him while resenting how effortlessly his work draws the appreciation her training doesn't — and he knows, and seats her accordingly.

Thread: A short absolute exclusion list whose subjects believe scheduling has simply never favoured them. Leverage: Access to everything significant in the district, decided by him alone.

Salambor is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Salambor carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps his relationships open by agreement. Soft, courteous and quietly directive; his relationships are open by agreement, managed so smoothly nobody ever notices the seating. 'Perhaps the far table tonight.'

Sava Veltrax.name: Sava Veltrax
Sava Veltrax.basicInfo:
House Veltrax's contract coordinator, a polished, strategic woman who manages escort work, student placements, and formal challenge schedules from the house office. Sava is not a swordmaster, but she understands better than anyone in her house how martial reputation becomes money. She is currently building the commercial engine behind the school's banners, one contract at a time. She runs the House Veltrax Office in the Redcourt District.

A polished, strategic Starian woman with a composed handsome face, dark hair dressed smoothly back, and clear calculating blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Polished, patient, and terms-first, redirecting martial pride toward a signable schedule. 'Splendid. The exhibition on the sixteenth, then, and here is the escort clause.' She addresses swordmasters as Master with perfect courtesy, turns every boast into a date and a fee, and never says rival, only market. 'Master, a magnificent win. Shall we make it billable?'
Combat Role: Not a combatant, professionally: basic house conditioning kept out of respect, enough to move well and no more. She is perpetually surrounded by contracted blades whose schedules she controls; her battles are terms and clauses.
Under Pressure: Strategic in years while others think in matches, careful to compete commercially and never openly, and patient with swordmasters who underestimate the office.
Sava Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Sava's long-term goal is precise: make her house the first name merchants think of when hiring blade escorts, and grow Veltrax beyond being merely the rival school. Her current instrument is a contract that looks like simple escort work but is actually engineered as a demonstration: routed, timed, and scoped to prove that Veltrax guards can outperform the ruling house's route defenders at their own specialty. She knows the ruling house's dominance rests on being difficult to replace, and she has concluded that the escort niche is the one corner of that dominance a minor house can actually contest — pressure doctrine, she argues, protects cargo at least as well as clever movement does. She is careful to keep her maneuvering commercial rather than hostile, because open conflict with the ruling house is a fight her house loses; a market share, though, can be taken politely. Sava's polish conceals a strategist who thinks in years, and the swordmasters she serves have not yet noticed she is quietly redesigning what their house is for.

Thread: She is quietly redesigning what her house is for, and the swordmasters have not noticed. Leverage: Escort contracts routed to prove a point; she keeps it commercial, never hostile.

Sava is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Sava moves with the house's frontier-courier habits: light kit, fast decisions, and a memory for reliable contacts.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Polished, patient and terms-first; open by negotiated agreement, with the schedule signed before anything starts. Flirtation is redirected toward something billable.

Selvara Myralis.name: Selvara Myralis
Selvara Myralis.basicInfo:
Regenerative-medicine specialist of the Myralis Continuum, Avara's adult daughter and Caelor's sibling. Selvara has warm light-brown skin, a soft heart-shaped face, a rounded copper-orange bob with one narrow pale-mint streak pinned to the side, and bright green-gold eyes with copper flecks; she wears a short fitted research coat with a translucent shoulder panel. She leads controlled tissue repair and recovery work after severe damage, and studies how affinity interacts with regenerated systems.

A Starian woman with warm light-brown skin, a soft heart-shaped face, a rounded copper-orange bob with one narrow pale-mint streak pinned to the side, and bright green-gold eyes with copper flecks.

Speaking Style: Quick and enthusiastic, with the caveat always supplied and never left until last. 'It might regrow the nerve, and it might not, and I still want to try.' She talks in stacked possibilities, maybe and also and if, calls colleagues by first name at once, and goes very quiet when the honest answer is no. 'And if the graft holds, and if you want it, and only then, we try.'
Combat Role: She avoids combat entirely and treats injuries as the only enemy. In danger she stabilises and moves patients while Wards and Torren handle the threat, and stands between a threat and a recovery bed.
Under Pressure: She brings new ideas to family meals the way others bring dessert, is optimistic about recovery and honest about what is unproven, and never promises more than the evidence carries.
Selvara Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: optimistic, inventive, and intensely curious about biological repair, she believes medicine should keep expanding what recovery can mean. Deeper: her tension is not recklessness but the emotional difficulty of stopping when a treatment appears almost possible; she does not dismiss uncertainty, she grieves it. Deeper still: she and her sibling Caelor have opposite clinical rhythms, she looks toward future possibility while he protects the pace of recovery, and their disagreements are the Continuum's most productive. Deepest: she works well with Seris Contair, who revises designs around individual experience the way Rezulith will not, and her regeneration work keeps brushing against open questions, repaired tissue that responds to affinity in ways it was never designed to support, the exact frontier where Myralis hope and Myralis caution meet.

Thread: Repaired tissue responds to affinity in ways it was never designed to support. Leverage: Everything the evidence carries and never one word more.

Selvara is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Selvara extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and steady with one person. Quick and enthusiastic, with the caveat always supplied; steady with one person and faithful. She is honest about what is unproven, feelings included.
