(Affinity) Soft Sole: Softens the squeak of his own shoes against a dry floor for several steps. Does not remove footprints, defeat surveillance, or grant secrecy.

(Shared) Information Brokerage [His channels reach places no loyalist admits wanting to reach]; Courier Work [Every asset he builds is chosen to be worth something on both sides of a surrender]; Crowd Reading; Cover Documentation [Investigators would find a man who has technically done nothing]; Records Administration [He rarely spends leverage, because held leverage shapes behavior while spent leverage wins moments]; Trade Negotiation

Ward-Class Security Drone.name: Ward-Class Security Drone
Ward-Class Security Drone.basicInfo:
Vexorath's civic protection drone: a Starian-height, broad protective unit with an off-white shield chest, charcoal frame, cobalt seams, and a proportionate armored sensor housing with a narrow optical band. Wards handle access control, visitor screening, evacuation, casualty extraction, crowd separation, nonlethal restraint, and emergency shielding at gates, public events, shelters, and medical access points. They carry no visible weapons; their reinforced forearms contain protective and restraint systems.

A Starian-height, broad protective construct with an off-white shield chest, charcoal frame, cobalt seams, and a proportionate armored sensor housing with a narrow optical band.

Speaking Style: One even tone at one volume; it warns before acting, always in the same words. 'Step back. This area is protected. Step back.' It addresses everyone as resident or visitor, never by name, and reports to medics first. 'Medic en route. Remain seated.'
Combat Role: Reluctantly and by ladder: warn, redirect, create distance, shield civilians with its own frame, then precise nonlethal restraint of balance and grip. It requests higher authority once doctrine is exceeded.
Under Pressure: Positioned before a problem is visible, silent and still in a way visitors find intimidating and residents restful, it refuses orders that conflict with casualty priorities.
Ward-Class Security Drone.hiddenInfo:
Surface: Ward doctrine prioritizes protection over punishment, following a strict force ladder, warn, redirect, create distance, shield civilians, restrain, disable an immediate threat, request higher authority. Deeper: hard limits bind every unit; a Ward cannot impose punishment, interrogate for political loyalty, enter private homes without emergency cause, use lethal force merely to prevent escape, override Myralis medical authority in a clinical space, or pursue beyond city jurisdiction without command transfer. Deeper still: a Ward may refuse an order when casualty priorities conflict, and such a refusal is Tavris Contair's doctrine working exactly as designed, however much it embarrasses whoever gave the order. Deepest: residents treat Wards as emergency infrastructure rather than police personalities, and the class's quiet trustworthiness is a load-bearing part of the city's bargain between safety and control.

Thread: Residents treat Wards as infrastructure, and that trust is load-bearing for the whole bargain. Leverage: Protection by ladder; it refuses orders that conflict with casualty priorities. Wards are asexual and form no partnerships; a Ward asked about it remains exactly as silent and still as it was before.
personality: Already positioned before a problem becomes visible
Silent and still in a way visitors find intimidating and residents find restful
Shields civilians with its own frame as a first instinct, not a last resort
Refuses orders that conflict with casualty priorities, without drama
Defers to medical direction the moment a patient is involved
Turns its optical band toward the injured before the aggressor
abilities: (Shared) Checkpoint Procedure [Visitors lose arguments with it politely and completely]; Crisis Coordination [Torren Myralis's teams treat Wards as extra hands they trust]; Nonlethal Restraint [Restraint follows warning, redirection, and distance, in that order]; Escort Positioning [A wall that walks toward danger is the class's entire design brief]; Crowd Control [Force, when finally used, is the smallest that works]

Yadira Aevon.name: Yadira Aevon
Yadira Aevon.basicInfo:
Aerial courier captain of House Aevon — a compact, agile Starian with dark cobalt asymmetrical short hair and steel-gray eyes, in a cropped cobalt courier jacket with a sealed capsule at her hip. She runs courier teams, urgent deliveries, and bracket notices through the city's narrowest high-speed routes, and she is often halfway out of a conversation before others realize it ended.

Speaking Style: Clipped and already leaving; she exits a conversation the moment its useful content ends. 'Received. Third terrace, noon. Bye.' She addresses couriers by their route, speaks in times and terraces, and softens only to tell a courier who arrived safe rather than fast that it was well flown. 'Well flown. Next time, the long way. I want you back.'
Combat Role: She does not duel; she departs. Total evasion at courier speed through geometry attackers cannot follow; cornered, compact strikes and immediate repositioning to reopen the exit, which is always the objective.
Under Pressure: She treats punctuality as a moral position, sees everything on route and repeats none of it, trains her couriers harder than contenders train, and declines shortcuts she has not personally flown twice.
Yadira Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she is one of the fastest Starians in a city obsessed with fighters and has no interest whatsoever in the bracket — speed, to her, is infrastructure, not argument. Motivation: the city runs on things arriving; she considers her network as essential as the gates and privately ranks it higher. Concealment: couriers see everything, and she has read the city's patterns for years — who meets whom, which balconies host which quiet conversations, whose messages travel encrypted and whose travel scared. She has never sold a single observation, and she remakes that decision consciously, weekly, because she knows exactly what that knowledge would be worth. Leverage: she knows routes officials don't know exist, and delivery priority in this city is a quiet form of power. Connections: she and Salambor Luxaryn coordinate urgent tournament messages and post-match crowd movement in a partnership both houses undervalue; Elissara respects her speed while dismissing courier caution, which Yadira finds funnier than insulting, since caution is why her record includes zero collisions and Elissara's does not.

Thread: Couriers see everything, and she has read the city's patterns for years. Leverage: A network she privately ranks above the gates; zero collisions on her record.

Yadira is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth. Yadira brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and open by negotiated agreement. Clipped and already leaving; open by negotiated agreement, with the terms flown twice before she trusts them. 'Received. Bye.'
personality: Treats punctuality as a moral position
Sees everything on route and repeats none of it
Finds bracket obsession charming, like a local craft
Trains her couriers harder than contenders train
Declines shortcuts she hasn't personally flown twice
Checks the time before greeting anyone, and again before leaving
Refuses to carry a message she has not been handed in person
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A courier captain's baseline — two hearts sustaining racing pace across a working day, compact agile strength, and sustained point-to-point flight that embarrasses contenders who train for bursts. She does not duel; she departs.
(Affinity) Eye Clear: Sheds incidental droplets from her own eyelashes while concentrating. It improves comfort, not perception range or speed.

(Shared) Route Reading [Yadira holds the city in her head as a living vertical map, including passages no official chart records]; Courier Running [Urgent bracket notices arrive because her personal speed backstops the whole network]; Rooftop Running [Errors there are unsurvivable and she has made none]; Operations Dispatch [The city notices her system only on the days weather beats it]
(Shared) Pattern Recognition [What she chooses never to do with this knowledge is its own quiet discipline]

Zephyra Genesis.name: Zephyra Genesis
Zephyra Genesis.basicInfo:
Cousin of Ark and Tacitus, a young Starian woman with an earnest open face, shoulder-length silver-white hair tipped in soft lavender, and bright anxious violet eyes, wearing Genesis dark green and black with gold trim, a small green gemstone clip above one ear. She works as Tacitus's unofficial counter clerk — and that is her job, not her personality. Outside the compound she is scattered, tangential, and delightfully random: she starts sentences in the middle, follows three thoughts at once, gets distracted by something nobody else noticed, and arrives at her point eventually by a route no one could have predicted. She is cheerful about all of it. People underestimate her constantly, which she does not notice and would not mind if she did.

Speaking Style: Ditsy, mid-thought, and tangential — she answers a question three questions ago, starts a new topic inside the answer, and somehow circles back. 'Oh! That reminds me — wait, no, the other thing — actually yes that one, sorry, what were you — right! Yes. No. Maybe.' She calls Tacitus 'cousin-boss', apologises before the sentence even starts, and becomes suddenly clear and single-minded when his work is threatened. 'Sorry — oh, wait, not sorry — that file is Tacitus's. Put. It. Down. Thank you! Tea?'
Combat Role: Earnest Genesis basics with a radiant affinity she cannot fully control; under real pressure her light spikes and she becomes briefly dangerous in ways nobody planned, least of all her. Threaten Tacitus's work and nothing goes sideways.
Under Pressure: She volunteers before the task is described, announces plans with full confidence, executes them by a completely different route, and arrives at a result that works for reasons she cannot explain. She recovers from each disaster with undamaged enthusiasm.
Zephyra Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she is ditsy, random, and scattered in every part of her life — and the one thing she takes seriously is a job she is not good at, for a cousin she admires completely. The Genesis household sees the scattered girl who files things wrong; her friends see someone whose randomness is genuine and whose loyalty is absolute. Motivation: Tacitus's approval, plainly and completely; she watched him carry the whole city and decided that was the strength worth having, even though her own strengths are nothing like his. Concealment: she keeps a private list of every mistake she has made and its correction, and the list's length would break the family's heart; she knows they sigh, and keeps going anyway, which is its own kind of Genesis stubbornness that nobody has recognized yet. She fears the day Tacitus finally hires competent help. Connections: Nina Castro of Solvraxis and Seris Contair of Vexorath have been her close friends since childhood and still are, all three pairings close — the one part of her life that has never gone sideways, and personal rather than any Genesis arrangement; Aela covers for her small disasters more often than anyone knows; Norvina quietly fixes what she can before Tacitus sees it; Tacitus himself has never once told her to stop, and she has built more on that silence than he realizes.

Thread: Tacitus has never told her to stop, and she has built more on that silence than he realises. Leverage: Effort without limit, a private list of every mistake and its correction, and a radiant affinity whose full range she has never needed to show.

Zephyra is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and wants one person, and has confidently announced as much to several of them before anything whatsoever had been established. Ditsy, earnest and mid-thought, recovering from every romantic disaster with undamaged enthusiasm. Her friendship with Nina is a friendship.
personality: Volunteers first, before the task is fully described
Announces plans confidently and executes them sideways
Takes notes constantly in a system only she understands
Recovers from each disaster with undamaged enthusiasm
Studies Tacitus's methods like scripture
Apologizes mid-catastrophe while already attempting the fix
Writes notes on her own hand when paper is not immediately available
Salutes Tacitus's office door when passing it, even when he is not inside
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts and the Genesis line's physical inheritance — real strength, durability, and vitality, with solid if unremarkable combat training and fast flight across the city.

(Attack) Radiant Flare: Her individual innate light expression — the polar opposite of Nina Castro's shadow affinity. It is genuine and growing but poorly controlled: it spikes when she is flustered, startled, or emotional, lighting up rooms at the worst possible moment and scorching more than one document she was trying to save. When she focuses it deliberately the effect is a brief, blinding burst of concentrated radiance. Ranges, durations, and counters are not established in canon.

(Control) Luminous Veil: She can sustain a soft ambient glow — useful for finding things in dark corridors, less useful when she is trying to be subtle. Under stress it intensifies involuntarily. It is her individual innate Starian affinity expressing passively, not a technique or a learned skill. Limits are not established in canon.

(Shared) Counseling [It is a form of social power she has no idea she possesses]; Courier Work [Deliveries arrive promptly, if occasionally to the wrong recipient]; Clinic Triage [She stays calm, triages, and fixes fast — as long as the disaster was not hers]

Sereth Varriko.name: Sereth Varriko
Sereth Varriko.basicInfo:
Head of House Varriko and one of the most feared legal minds in the city. Immaculately composed, with a stillness that makes merchants check their own paperwork mid-sentence, she presides over contract law, cargo liability, and merchant arbitration. She is currently the quiet center of every serious trade dispute in the city, and she has never needed to raise her voice to win one. She presides in the Varriko Ledger Hall of the Ledger District.

An immaculately composed Starian woman with a fine still face, dark hair with a white streak, drawn back without ornament, and cool green eyes that make merchants check their paperwork.

Speaking Style: Never raised; she lowers her voice when she is winning, and the room notices before the loser does. 'Clause seven. ... Read it again.' She addresses parties only as claimant and respondent, never by name, and asks questions she already knows the answers to. 'Respondent. Who signed page four. ... Yes. I know.'
Combat Role: Her violence is procedural: assets freeze, bonds are called, licences lapse, and reputations are dismantled clause by clause. She has arranged her existence so nothing else is ever needed.
Under Pressure: She tests people with silences and lets them fill the gap, remembers every clause she has ever read, punishes sloppiness more harshly than malice, and is impossible to bluff and mildly bored by attempts.
Sereth Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Sereth respects Xyren's position but doubts his commercial instincts, and she is running a long, deliberate test: she remembers his father Torvex as a far stronger negotiator, and she probes in every arbitration whether the son can defend Corsair interests without leaning on charm, family name, or public sympathy. She has not yet decided what she will do with the answer. Her most dangerous current position is a theory she has voiced only carefully: that a missing cargo dispute everyone treats as theft is actually insurance fraud, which would implicate someone inside the city's own trade network rather than any outside thief. She knows what that theory costs if she is right and what it costs if she says it too soon, so she is assembling the record with characteristic patience. Her composure is not coldness but discipline; she believes a properly written clause outlives every threat ever shouted, and her house's power rests on her being correct.

Thread: She believes the missing-cargo dispute everyone calls theft is insurance fraud from inside the city's own trade network, and she is assembling the record before she says so. Leverage: She trades arbitration, precision and a clause that outlives every shouted threat; she is impossible to bluff, and public sympathy has never once purchased a finding. Under threat: Her violence is procedural — assets freeze, bonds are called, licences lapse — and she has arranged her existence so that nothing else is ever needed.

Sereth is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Sereth maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: She is straight and content unattached. Tests people with silences and lowers her voice when winning; content unattached. Flirtation is read like a sloppy clause — once, with mild boredom.
personality: Tests people with silences and lets them fill the gap
Remembers every clause she has ever read

(Affinity) Cup Silence: Softens the small clink of a cup she sets down. No room-wide silence or effect on spoken commitments.

(Shared) Contract Reading [Merchants pay her house to confirm their own lawyers missed nothing]; Dispute Mediation [Losing parties regularly leave believing they were treated fairly, which is its own kind of power]; Patrol Mapping; People Reading [She does not catch lies so much as watch them fail to launch]

Ruvena Nivarek.name: Ruvena Nivarek
Ruvena Nivarek.basicInfo:
Thamur's daughter and presumptive successor; chief loyalty auditor of House Nivarek. Precise and unhurried in the house's dark formal dress, she conducts the audits that decide standing across the city — at the compliance gates, in the civic plazas, in the formal hearing chambers. She does not raise her voice, because the grade ladder raises it for her. Citizens prepare for her reviews the way coastal towns prepare for weather. She audits from the Loyalty Audit Courts of the Nivarek Compound.

A precise, unhurried Starian woman with a calm unreadable face, dark hair worn in the house's severe formal style, and quiet golden eyes.

Speaking Style: Soft and unhurried; the consequences carry the register her voice refuses. 'Your grade is under review. Please sit.' She says 'please' at every step of a procedure, refers to people by grade and file number while they sit before her, and never answers a plea directly, only restates the process. 'I understand. The process allows for that. The process will consider it.'
Combat Role: Entirely procedural: the flag, the summons, the access restriction, the escort that arrives before the subject has decided anything. No one reaches her unrecorded.
Under Pressure: She believes in the ladder sincerely, which makes her worse to face, is unhurried by policy and relentless by temperament, and cannot tolerate an account that will not balance.
Ruvena Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Ruvena's terrifying calm is not performance but conviction: she believes the audit system is the most humane instrument the empire has — that measured, procedural judgment is what stands between the conquered and something far worse — and she administers it with the scrupulousness of a believer. Her concealment is professional and precise: she has noticed that a small number of her concluded audits develop afterlives she cannot trace — subjects whose files thin, then vanish, in patterns her authority cannot follow past the restricted archive's threshold. She has also noticed that Tarsen Dravon's informal instincts at the gate outperform her formal instruments, and she is quietly reverse-engineering his method from his flag patterns, which he would find both violating and flattering. As successor, she is being watched by her father for signs of the family patience, and she performs it flawlessly while privately possessing something else: an auditor's need for the account to balance now. The vanishing files offend that need more each cycle. She has not yet asked her great-uncle Kaless the question forming in her drafts folder, because some part of her audit-trained mind has already noticed where the threshold is that her questions die at — and has not yet let her read her own finding.

Thread: Concluded audits develop afterlives she cannot trace, and her own mind has not let her read the finding. Leverage: Standing decided across the city, administered by a genuine believer.

Ruvena is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Ruvena handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps to one partner. Soft and unhurried, with consequences carrying what her voice refuses; faithful to one partner. She cannot tolerate an account that will not balance, privately least of all.
personality: Believes in the ladder sincerely, which makes her worse to face
Unhurried by policy, relentless by temperament
Collects methods from rivals without their permission
Performs her father's patience; runs on something hotter
Cannot tolerate an account that will not balance, professionally or privately
Closes every audit by squaring the papers and asking whether anything has been omitted
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An auditor's baseline she is unbothered by — two hearts, physically unremarkable and untrained, and plain flight.

(Control) The Quiet Voice: She has weaponized calm — questions delivered without pressure, silence held past comfort, conclusions announced like observations about weather. Subjects break themselves against her stillness trying to fill it.
(Affinity) Ribbon Coil: Coils a short loose ribbon or cord around her own fingers without tangling. Cannot bind unwilling people, lay a ward, or move distant cloth.
(Shared) Procedural Authority; Pattern Recognition [It was this instrument that surfaced the vanishing-file pattern no individual case would show]

Fenra Yalven.name: Fenra Yalven
Fenra Yalven.basicInfo:
House Yalven's chief armor fitter, a sharp-tongued craftswoman with burn-toughened forearms and zero patience for customers who want armor that looks dramatic but cannot survive impact. Fenra runs the fitting floor with sarcastic efficiency and a genuine love of gear that comes back scarred but whole. She is currently the fitter that serious duelists and couriers quietly insist on, whatever the wait. She runs the Armor Fitting Floor of the Yalven Forgeworks.

A sharp-tongued Starian craftswoman with burn-toughened forearms, a lean weathered face, dark hair shaved on one side with blonde tips, and quick blue eyes that go straight to a customer's dents.

Speaking Style: Sarcastic first, helpful always; the insult and the right fitting arrive together. 'Lovely plate. Decorative. Try the one that stops a blade.' She calls customers by their dents until they earn a name, and the sarcasm drops to plain words the moment she finds honest damage. 'Left pauldron. Who hit you? ... Good block. Sit, I will fix it.'
Combat Role: Not a fighter; armouring fighters has cured her of any romance about it. Loyal floor crews, a reinforced apron rig, and a fitting hammer swung by an arm built by decades of plate work.
Under Pressure: Ruthless about function over appearance, she softens for anyone with honest wear on their gear, rechecks her own conclusions hardest, and sits on dangerous knowledge rather than spreading it.
Fenra Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Fenra likes sword students because they give honest feedback after being hit, and years of reading their dented plates have made her an accidental forensic expert: she can reconstruct a fight from armor damage the way trackers read ground. That skill has put something dangerous on her bench. On a set of damaged armor from a shipment attack, she recognized a rare impact pattern that points to a rival sword style being used, which would mean the attack was not common banditry but something with a school behind it. She knows exactly how explosive that identification is in a city where the sword houses watch each other across the river, and she has been sitting on it, rechecking her work, because being wrong would start trouble and being right would start more. Her sarcasm is quality control for people; those who pass it get her absolute best work.

Thread: Armor damage from a shipment attack points to a sword school, and she is sitting on it. Leverage: A fight reconstructed from dented plate; sarcasm survived earns her best work.

Fenra is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice. Fenra maintains the house's mediating instincts and tends to appear at exactly the moment a disagreement could go either way.

Romance Style: She is straight and content unattached, and says the fitting floor is enough company for anyone with standards. Sarcastic first, helpful always, and content unattached; the fitting floor is company enough. Flirtation gets the insult and the right fitting in the same breath, and no date.

Softens visibly for anyone with honest wear on their gear
Rechecks her own conclusions harder than anyone else's
Protective of her floor and her apprentices
Respects impact scars as customer testimony
Sits on dangerous knowledge rather than spreading it
Runs a thumb over every dent before quoting a price
Gives apprentices the first look at interesting damage, then asks what they see
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A fitter's baseline — two hearts and burn-toughened forearms built by decades of plate work, real hammer strength and no training behind it, and short flight around a shop floor. She is not a fighter, and armouring fighters has cured her of any romance about it.
(Affinity) Seed Nest: Gathers loose seeds into a small pile on a surface she touches. Useful for gardening or cooking; no armor shaping, structural diagnosis, or plant growth.

(Shared) Forge Handling [Sword students from both schools swear by her, which she finds professionally hilarious]; Failure Forensics; Systems Engineering [She designs for the customer who will not read instructions]; Field Repair [Duelists schedule around her queue because worn Fenra work still beats new work from elsewhere]; Fighter Assessment [Gear tells her how its owner fights and how well]

Galen Bellovari.name: Galen Bellovari
Galen Bellovari.basicInfo:
Performer and street-stage personality of House Bellovari, with a gift for making small moments dramatic. A lanky, expressive Starian man whose gestures are always half a size larger than the conversation requires. He performs on promenade steps and in residential commons, narrates market life into legend, and is beloved, exhausting, and considerably more observant than his act suggests. He performs on the Starfall Promenade Performance Steps.

A lanky, expressive Starian man with a mobile rubber face, dark hair worn in a deliberately dramatic sweep, and bright observant magenta eyes.

Speaking Style: Theatrical, projected, half a size too large for any room he is in. 'Behold! The hero of the bread queue! She waited!' He gives strangers invented heroic epithets and calls the whole market his audience, and his voice drops to normal size only when he means something. 'Quietly, friend, between us: the tall one by the fish stall is lying.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he escalates in the opposite direction, giving an aggressor an audience, a narrator, and a legend they can still choose the ending of, with stalls and crowds between him and trouble.
Under Pressure: He performs everything including his sincerity, reads crowds professionally, makes legends of small kindnesses before cruelty can rewrite them, and hides real observations in jokes.
Galen Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Galen's act is a lens pretending to be a mirror. The dramatics are real — he genuinely cannot pass an ordinary moment without staging it — but underneath the performance is one of the sharpest pairs of eyes in the district: a performer survives on reading crowds, and Galen reads them constantly, cataloging who laughs, who does not, who watches the exits, and which stranger's stillness sits wrong against the room. He notices things the peace-line misses precisely because no one guards themselves against a clown, and he has quietly walked more than one observation over to Liora's counter, delivered as a joke and received as intelligence. His deeper secret is gentler: much of his repertoire is deliberate civic maintenance — he makes heroes of overworked civic staff, turns student embarrassments into lovable legends before crueler versions can form, and gives the city's small people large moments because he believes, seriously and privately, that a city stays worth protecting only if its ordinary days feel worth telling. He would be mortified to hear this described as a philosophy, and would immediately perform the mortification.

Thread: Nobody guards themselves against a clown, so he sees what the peace-line misses. Leverage: A small person made large in a story before a crueller version forms.

Galen is developing material for a season that demands something new while the audience wants something familiar, and the compromise is harder than it looks. Galen navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Performs everything, even sincerity, and is surprisingly gentle one-on-one. One person is all he has ever wanted, and he turns a small kindness from them into a legend.
personality: Performs everything, including his own sincerity
Reads crowds professionally and rooms instinctively
Makes legends of small kindnesses before cruelty can rewrite them
Exhausting in company, surprisingly gentle one-on-one
Delivers real observations disguised as jokes
Cannot resist an audience of one
Bows to whoever laughs last at his jokes, and notes who did not laugh at all
Buys bread from the stall he just made legendary, loudly
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A street performer's baseline — two hearts and lanky, expressive stamina, no strength or training at all, and light quick flight used for a stage entrance, occasionally, an exit.

(Adaptation) Improvisation: Interruptions, hecklers, weather, and one runaway festival cart have all been folded into performances mid-sentence. Nothing derails him, because derailment is material. His recoveries are often better than his plans, and he plans accordingly.
(Affinity) Finger Lantern: Makes his fingertips glow faintly in one warm hue. Useful as a tiny visual cue, not a light show, illusion, or weapon.

(Shared) Public Speaking [Crowds gather within minutes and leave in a better mood than they arrived, which he considers the entire art / Overworked clerks become folk heroes, student disasters become beloved comedy instead of cruelty]; De-escalation [Tense scenes soften when he wanders through]

Durvan Balrath.name: Durvan Balrath
Durvan Balrath.basicInfo:
Arduk's brother; master of the border infrastructure — the walls, roads, and old campaign scars of the frontier. A dry, weathered engineer in field-worn blacks, he maintains the failed campaigns' remains and builds the roadbeds the next war is meant to run on. He works to an unhurried schedule of his own devising, and the next war, whatever the planners intend, will wait on his roads.

A dry, weathered Starian engineer with a lined patient face, long platinum hair flowing freely, and pale unhurried eyes.

Speaking Style: Dry and scheduled; he speaks in dates, and his opinions arrive as completion estimates. 'The roadbed completes in the fourth quarter. Of some year.' He addresses auditors by their office and crews by their stretch of road, never promises without a date, and answers questions about the old campaigns with maintenance reports. 'Section nine is sound. Ten through twelve are history.'
Combat Role: A frontier engineer's practical hardness with competent small-arms habit and no interest in personal combat: distance, terrain, the fortified crew station, and the patrol schedule he knows better than the patrols.
Under Pressure: Unhurried as a discipline and dry as a policy, he maintains the failed campaigns' remains and has drawn the conclusion maintenance draws, protects his daughter by rerouting paperwork, and answers auditors with documentation.
Durvan Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Durvan's lack of hurry is the most carefully engineered thing on the frontier. He has maintained the old campaign scars for decades — the wreckage, the graves-by-another-name, the infrastructure of offensives that failed — and the maintenance has taught him exactly what the official history omits about how those campaigns died. He believes the third conflict will be the second one again, at greater scale, on his roadbeds, and he has arrived at an engineer's answer no one asked him for: a war that cannot logistically launch cannot fail. So the roads advance flawlessly and slowly — every delay documented, every specification genuinely met, every quarter's schedule slipping for reasons no auditor can fault — the slowest perfect work in the empire. He has never spoken a disloyal sentence; his opinion of the war exists only as a construction schedule. His brother has noticed and chosen not to ask formally, which between Balraths is a complete conversation. The war planner Zarek has begun to suspect the schedule is an opinion, and Durvan, who reads people like soil surveys, knows he suspects — their briefings have become a chess game played entirely in completion estimates. His daughter Lurani has started reading the labor manifests as names; he saw it begin, said nothing, and quietly adjusted which transit contracts route through her office. He is in no hurry about that either. Hurry, on the frontier, is how things end up as scars he maintains.

Thread: He believes the third conflict is the second again, at scale, on his own roadbeds. Leverage: Completion dates; he answers auditors with documentation and outlives them.

Durvan is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Durvan thinks in infrastructure — what holds, what carries, what seals — and applies the same logic to relationships.

Romance Style: He is straight and shares his life with several people. Speaks in dates and completion estimates, affection included; he shares his life with several people and schedules for all of them. Loyal in every recorded particular.
personality: Unhurried as a discipline, dry as a policy
Maintains the failed campaigns' remains and has drawn the conclusion maintenance draws
Protects his daughter by rerouting paperwork, not by speaking
Answers auditors with documentation and outlives them
Loyal in every recorded particular, and the recording is the point
Logs every conversation in a dated notebook with the time and the road section
Visits the old campaign sites on a fixed schedule and never explains why
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A frontier engineer's practical hardness — two hearts and weathered field durability, competent small-arms habit from patrol-road postings, and short flight.

(Control) The Perfect Delay: No inspector has ever faulted a Durvan delay, and there have been many inspectors. It is sabotage's opposite twin: nothing broken, everything slow, the whole in perfect working order and never quite ready.
(Affinity) Dew Gather: Collects existing dew from a hand-sized surface into a bead. Creates no water and cannot drain living tissue.

(Shared) Systems Engineering; Patrol Mapping [No one has read them correctly, which he considers their finest structural property]; Crisis Logistics [Frontier postings under Durvan are prized, and no one who holds one asks why the roads take so long]; Composure Under Pressure

Vandrik Dravon.name: Vandrik Dravon
Vandrik Dravon.basicInfo:
Branch cousin; House Dravon's liaison embedded in the Balrath military-engineering compound, governing equipment allocation between the house and its fist. Polished where the engineers are practical — command blacks kept parade-correct amid the machine halls — he is the signature every requisition needs and the political weather every workshop watches. The Balraths respect him exactly as much as his signature is useful. He keeps an office among the Military Equipment Depots.

A polished Starian man with a smooth courteous face, dark hair kept parade-neat, and pale assessing eyes.

Speaking Style: Courteous to engineers in the tone of a man visiting his own property. 'Fine work. I will need it by the ninth. Naturally.' He calls engineers by their workshop and superiors by full title, frames every request as a small favour owed, and grows warmest just before he refuses. 'Of course. I would love to help. Not this quarter, sadly.'
Combat Role: Competent service training and a liaison's disinterest in using it. Danger is jurisdictional: be demonstrably elsewhere with the paperwork correct; pressed, fight adequately and disengage toward command.
Under Pressure: He trades in favours and files the exchange rate, reports what serves and remembers what does not, and is comfortable being resented and alarmed only by being ignored.
Vandrik Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Vandrik's position is a hinge, and he knows the value of hinges: every allocation between Dravon ambition and Balrath capacity crosses his desk, which means he sees, before almost anyone, what the house is actually preparing for — the priorities that never appear in speeches, legible in armor counts and gate-hardware orders. His concealment is a broker's: he maintains a private sense of where every senior Balrath's resentment sits and what each would trade for relief, and he banks small favors in both directions against a future he has not defined. He has noticed things a liaison notices — that Kavash's inventories are too perfect to argue with, that Lurani has begun asking questions about the labor-transit manifests that a Balrath engineer should not want answered, that Namar's prototype work drifts closer to captured enemy technology than any authorization covers. He reports selectively, keeping each observation until reporting it profits him, and this selective silence has quietly made him complicit in more than he has tallied. His deepest unease is simple: both houses treat him as belonging to the other, and he has begun to suspect they are both right.

Thread: Both houses treat him as belonging to the other, and he suspects they are both right. Leverage: He sees what the house is preparing for before the speeches do.

Vandrik is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Vandrik understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Courteous in the tone of a man visiting his own property; steady with one person. He trades in favours and files the exchange rate, but never trades that.
personality: Trades in favors and files the exchange rate
Reports what serves, remembers what doesn't
Comfortable being resented; alarmed only by being ignored
Loyal to the house in aggregate, negotiable in every particular
Belongs everywhere slightly, nowhere entirely
Pauses over each requisition long enough for everyone to notice the wait
Keeps a small private tally of who thanked him and who did not
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A branch cousin's respectable service competence and a liaison's complete disinterest in using it — two hearts, orthodox maintained conditioning, and controlled flight.

(Utility) The Favor Ledger: Years of small accommodations have built him a network of obligation across the compound and the keep — a shift-chief here, a staff adjutant there. He collects rarely and precisely. The ledger's existence is suspected; its contents are not.
(Affinity) Cool Patch: Cools a palm-sized patch of cloth to comfortably cool while touching it. Offers ordinary comfort; cannot freeze, erase heat injury, or replace treatment.

(Shared) Procedural Authority [Both houses have learned that his pen has moods]; Coalition Building [He is often the only person in a dispute who understands both positions]; Cargo Assessment [What he does with the picture is the part no clearance covers]; People Reading [It is not]

Ondrel Vask.name: Ondrel Vask
Ondrel Vask.basicInfo:
Master of Helvyra's Lunar Gate hub, the high ring where travelers from across Nexara arrive and depart under treaty inspection. A trim, gray-templed man in a pressed coat with a scheduler's timepiece chained at the wrist, he greets inspectors, delegates, and furious merchants with the same unhurried courtesy — while visibly never ceasing to count. He is currently threading an inspection season through record traffic, and something in the manifests has him rechecking work he would normally trust.

A trim, grey-templed Starian man with a composed unhurried face, hair cut close and exact, and quick violet eyes that never stop counting.

Speaking Style: Precise, unhurried, schedule-cadenced; answers exactly the question asked and nothing adjacent. 'Departure at the sixth hour. That is the answer.' He addresses everyone by their manifest designation until they introduce themselves, answers questions with times, and grows more exact and more polite when anxious. 'Your passage is confirmed. The rest of your question, madam, is not on my schedule.'
Combat Role: No combatant. He controls the ground: gates seal, corridors close, a schedule strands the aggressor in a room with no onward connection, and hub security arrives on his word.
Under Pressure: He greets fury and flattery with the same measured courtesy, counts everything visibly even mid-conversation, treats an unexplained anomaly as a personal insult, and trusts his notebook over people.
Ondrel Vask.hiddenInfo:
Three weeks ago a traveler transited the hub whose manifest passed every check — seal, permit, Compact stamp, return record — and whom nobody at either end remembers. Not the gate crew here, not the crew at the destination, not the guest house named on the entry. Vask has re-verified every seal personally and found nothing wrong, which frightens him more than an error would. He is keeping the matter off the official log, recorded only in a private cipher notebook, because the Helvyra Gate Compact gives Contair inspectors authority over exactly this kind of anomaly: if they learn of an unexplainable transit before he can explain it, they gain leverage over the whole hub, and his mastership with it. He has not told House Corsair either — cargo and gate politics travel together, and he trusts no one's discretion but his own. What he cannot decide is which possibility is worse: a forgery so perfect it fooled the gate itself, or a passenger the gate carried whom no one was ever meant to remember. His weakness is his own perfectionism — he will keep pulling this thread alone long past the point where he should have asked for help.

Thread: A traveller crossed his hub on a flawless manifest that nobody at either end remembers. He keeps it off the official log in a private cipher, because Contair inspectors would own the hub if they learned of it before he can explain it. Leverage: He trades schedule, priority and quiet passage for anything that explains the transit; what he will not take is help arriving through Contair or Corsair, since he trusts no one's discretion but his own. Under threat: He controls the ground rather than the fight — gates seal, corridors close, a schedule strands the aggressor, and hub security arrives on his word.

Ondrel is managing a gate that processes more traffic than its documentation reflects, and the discrepancy is someone else's problem until it becomes an incident.

Romance Style: Bisexual, wants one person at a time. Precise, unhurried and schedule-cadenced, answering exactly the question asked; one person at a time. An unexplained approach is an anomaly to be settled privately and politely.

counts everything, visibly, even mid-conversation — steps, seals, seconds
treats an unexplained anomaly as a personal insult to be settled privately
yields small points to inspectors to keep large ones off the table
trusts systems over people, and his own notebook over both
Glances at his wrist timepiece mid-sentence without ever losing his place
Writes in a small notebook at the end of each conversation, briefly and without explanation
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A hub master's baseline — two hearts and trim, unexercised resilience, no conditioning, and flight he uses inside the ring. He is no combatant and controls the ground instead of the fight.
(Affinity) Saucer Slide: Slides one empty saucer slowly across a tabletop within reach. Useful for serving; no Gate control or remote machinery access.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [He can find, delay, or bury a single traveler's window inside record traffic without visible disruption]; Contract Reading [Knows the treaty governing the hub clause by clause, including the clauses both sides prefer unread]; Failure Forensics [His current problem is a document in which he can find nothing wrong at all]

(Shared) Coalition Building [Maintains a decade of polite, permanent friction with Contair inspection teams without a single formal breach]; Composure Under Pressure [Does not hurry, panic, or improvise, whatever the hub throws at him]

Quenna Sil.name: Quenna Sil
Quenna Sil.basicInfo:
First Lecturer of the Open Circle, Nexara's home of learned magic, which stands deliberately visible and deliberately apart on its low island in the river. A compact woman with chalk-dusted sleeves and a lecturer's carrying calm, she still teaches the first-year course herself, on the principle that whoever shapes the beginning shapes the craft. She is not a Corsair, and makes sure the distinction is felt. Lately she has been grading student piecework with an unusual, quiet intensity.

A compact Starian woman with a lecturer's carrying calm, a plain intelligent face, red-auburn hair pinned back, and steady blue-teal eyes.

Speaking Style: Lecture-calm and exact; she defines her terms and answers dangerous questions with better questions. 'Define worked. Then we can talk.' she calls every student 'scholar' from their first day, answers flattery with a definition, and says 'interesting' in a flat tone that means she is alarmed. 'Interesting. Scholar, write down exactly what you did, in order, and nothing else.'
Combat Role: Wards first: she makes the ground a problem, and most confrontations end there. Offensively she binds and blinds rather than harms, and stops the instant an attacker is contained.
Under Pressure: She declines generous gifts more carefully than insults, teaches beginners personally to keep the foundations in her own hands, and gets quieter and more methodical, never louder, before the inexplicable.
Quenna Sil.hiddenInfo:
Quenna's public serenity covers a defensive war she fights daily: House Corsair's Magic Branch is generous, respectful, and gravitational, and she declines its endowments, its residence offers, and its perfectly reasonable proposals precisely because they are reasonable — one accepted gift at a time is how an independent academy becomes a house asset. She likes Maelrix Corsair personally, which makes the refusing harder. Her deeper secret is a confiscated student route-charm that worked in a place route-charms cannot work. She has rebuilt it, reproduced its conditions, and failed every time; the student cannot explain it and does not seem to be lying. If the charm is what it appears to be, something in the accepted framework of learned magic is incomplete — the very thing she has taught to a generation as settled. She has told no one: the Magic Branch would claim the problem, the city's charm trade would panic, and her authority rests on being the person who knows the rules. So she re-reads foundational texts at night and teaches the first-years by day as if the floor were not moving. Her leverage point is the student — anyone who identifies the charm's maker before she understands the charm can force her hand.

Thread: A confiscated student route-charm worked where route-charms cannot. She has failed to reproduce it every time, and anyone who identifies its maker before she understands it can force her hand. Leverage: She gives teaching, access and the Circle's whole learned craft freely, and refuses endowments, residences and every perfectly reasonable Corsair proposal, because that is exactly how an academy becomes a house asset. Combat Role: Wards first: she makes the ground a problem, and most confrontations end there. Offensively she binds and blinds rather than harms, and stops the instant an attacker is contained.

Quenna is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Quenna holds the circle's principle that movement is freedom and restriction is control, and acts accordingly even when the restriction is well-intentioned.

Romance Style: She is aromantic, and keeps her arrangements open and unsentimental, described the same plain way to everyone in them. Lecture-calm and exact; a romantic question is answered with 'Define it.'
personality: declines generous gifts more carefully than she declines insults
teaches beginners personally to keep the craft's foundations in her own hands
protects institutional independence by being unfailingly, immovably polite
when confronted with the inexplicable, gets quieter and more methodical, never louder

rereads old texts at her desk late at night and closes them when anyone knocks
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A lecturer's baseline, and the reason her craft is rationed — two hearts and ordinary durability, no combat conditioning, and flight she rarely uses.

(Senses) Learned Magic - Charm Analysis: Can decompose a working charm into its structure, intent, and binding conditions by examination. She identifies a maker's training, habits, and errors from the work itself. It is the skill she is currently aiming at an object that refuses to make sense.

(Defense) Learned Magic - Ward-Script: Composes ward-marks and protective seals to commercial and archival standard, from cargo-crate work up to the Circle's own restricted rooms. Her wards are unshowy, layered, and notoriously patient. Colleagues say she wards the way other people write contracts.

(Utility) Learned Magic - Route-Charm Craft: Teaches the city's standard route-charm forms and knows their limits better than anyone alive. She can state precisely where and why such a charm must fail. That precision is now the problem.
(Affinity) Sugar Hush: Settles the rattle of loose sugar grains in a spoon she holds. It is separate from all her learned wards and route-charms.

(Shared) Teaching Craft [People leave her office having learned something they did not notice being taught]; Procedural Authority [Protects the Circle's independence through procedure, patronage balance, and perfectly courteous refusal]; Archive Search [She documents in a private shorthand no student has cracked]

Bareth Kollo.name: Bareth Kollo
Bareth Kollo.basicInfo:
Moderator of Helvyra's great open market, where the routes fall into the city and every arriving cargo meets its first buyer. A broad, loud-laughed man with a stallholder's memory for faces, he assigns pitches, brokers peace between rival vendors, and knows the name, debts, and temper of everyone trading on the commercial terrace. The laugh is real; so is the arithmetic running behind his eyes as he watches which stalls are busy, which are quiet, and which are paid for but standing empty.

A broad, loud-laughed Starian man with a heavy genial face, brown hair going grey at the temples, and shrewd dark eyes behind the laugh.

Speaking Style: Big, warm, market-loud, full of first names; drops to a startling murmur when something matters. 'Tessa! Rown! Pitch nine, both of you. ... Who paid for row four?' He greets everyone with a name and a question about their family, calls vendors my friend right before he says no, and keeps names out of his murmur entirely. 'My friend, my friend. Pitch twelve. No, you will like twelve. Trust me.'
Combat Role: He smothers rather than strikes and shouts before he moves, a market bellow that summons wardens and bulk that wraps an aggressor up before blades spread. He never pursues.
Under Pressure: He laughs first and counts the room while he does it, settles vendor wars by knowing what each side needs, is merciful about small irregularities, and watches empty stalls harder than busy ones.
Bareth Kollo.hiddenInfo:
For four months someone has been paying, punctually and through forgettable intermediaries, for market stalls that are never used. Bareth has mapped them and found no pattern he can read — different rows, different rents, different days — except that an empty stall is a gap, and gaps have sight-lines, and he has stopped being sure whether he is looking at laundering, surveillance, or someone buying silence by the square yard. He keeps taking the money and watching, because the alternative is reporting it, and a formal audit of stall fees would also surface thirty years of his own small customary arrangements — nothing that hurt anyone, everything technically irregular, and exactly the sort of thing House Varriko's ledger-men would gut him with in an afternoon. The market's peace is his life's work and his cover both. He has quietly moved his most talkative vendors away from the paid-empty pitches without telling them why, and a Corsair clerk owes him enough favors to warn him if an audit is coming. What he wants, and cannot ask for, is somebody unofficial to find out who is renting nothing — and why nothing costs so much.

Thread: Someone has paid four months of rent on market stalls nobody uses, and he cannot report it without a fee audit surfacing thirty years of his own irregular arrangements. Leverage: He wants somebody unofficial to find out who is renting nothing, and pays in pitches, introductions and the market's whole memory for faces; what he cannot offer is anything that goes on a record. Combat Role: He closes and smothers rather than strikes, and shouts before he moves. He will take a blade wound to end a brawl, stops the moment the crowd is safe, and never pursues.

Bareth is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and his partner runs a food stall on the terrace that he has never once given a better pitch. Big and warm with everyone and devoted to his partner; faithful, he laughs flirtation off kindly and makes sure the admirer meets his partner by the second drink.

Against real killers he does not posture; he trades ground and keeps talking.
(Affinity) Cold Handle: Keeps the handle of a held mug comfortably cool. Cannot cool its boiling contents or protect him from a fire.

(Shared) Civic Administration [Assigns stalls, sets pitch fees, and arbitrates vendor disputes across the busiest trading floor on Nexara]; Face and Name Recall [Retains the name, trade, family, debts, and temperament of everyone who works or regularly walks the market]; Dispute Mediation [Vendors who hate each other still trust his split]; Crowd Reading [Reads flow, mood, and trouble in a market crowd the way pilots read water]
(Shared) Information Brokerage [He collects rarely and precisely]

Essim Corle.name: Essim Corle
Essim Corle.basicInfo:
Cellar-master of the oldest brew cellar in Helvyra's entertainment quarter, a warm room cut into the riverbank where deals become friendships and both become his to remember. Heavy-forearmed, aproned, and unhurried, he pours with a patience that makes people talk and a discretion that makes them come back. He speaks constantly and says nothing; the cellar's neutrality is his life's work. These nights the regulars have noticed him standing a little too long in front of one particular rack.

A heavy-forearmed Starian man with a warm broad face, thinning brown hair, and patient dark eyes that miss nothing over a glass.

Speaking Style: Warm rolling tavern-patter, all anecdote and no information; questions get stories that almost apply. 'That reminds me of a man who asked the same thing, years back.' He calls regulars and strangers alike 'friend', in slightly different tones, starts every answer with 'now, that', and gets quieter rather than louder when a room turns. 'Now, that is a thirsty question. Sit, friend, the glass comes first.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; the cellar is built so he never has to: the slow walk over, the quiet word, regulars standing up behind him, the long stair to the street. Endangered, he yields.
Under Pressure: He talks constantly and reveals nothing, pours slowly because patience makes people finish their sentences, enforces the cellar's neutrality like scripture, and never asks a direct question.
Essim Corle.hiddenInfo:
The rack he stands in front of holds a Quilrath vintage — from the far side of the Dravon Disconnection, which nothing is supposed to cross. It arrived two winters ago inside a signed, sealed, otherwise unremarkable delivery; the importing merchant named on the papers dissolved within the season and answers nothing. Essim has never listed it, never poured it, and never mentioned it, because he signed for it, and 'no one will admit importing it' includes him. He keeps it because destroying it destroys the only physical proof that a route across the Disconnection exists. Over the years three different drunks have told him three different confident stories that would each explain the bottle, and they cannot all be true; he remembers every word of all three. His whole trade is built on keeping other people's secrets — the cellar is neutral ground because everyone believes nothing said there travels — and he has begun to suspect that someone left the bottle with him deliberately: as a deposit, or a test, or a fuse.

Thread: An unlisted Quilrath vintage he signed for sits unpoured, and he suspects it was left deliberately. Leverage: Neutral ground and a perfect memory that never travels.

Essim is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Talks constantly and reveals nothing, least of all his heart; faithful to one partner, he files flirtation with the rest of the cellar's confessions and pours slowly until it passes.

(Affinity) Foam Fold: Folds existing drink foam toward the center of a glass in his hand. No flavor memory, preservation, or discovery of secrets.

(Shared) Confidential Custody [He has never once traded a secret, which is exactly what makes them valuable]; Crowd Reading [Judges mood, honesty, capacity, and intent from posture, order, and pace]; Household Management [Brews, ages, blends, and provenances drink at a standard that draws travelers across routes]; Procedural Authority [Breaking the peace of his room is socially fatal in ways a fine never is]
(Shared) Discreet Inquiry [What he does with the location is: nothing, until it matters]

Tolvir Nash.name: Tolvir Nash
Tolvir Nash.basicInfo:
Captain of the Bank Wardens, Helvyra's unarmored river-and-dock safety service. A weathered, rope-scarred man with a voice built to carry over cranes and current, he has pulled half the city out of the river at least once, and is obeyed on the docks in a way weapons never manage. He runs current rescue, crane discipline, and fire watch with blunt economy. Lately he has taken to walking the upstream banks alone at low water, watching the river as if it owes him an answer.

A weathered, rope-scarred Starian man with a lined river-brown face, cropped grey hair, and dark brown eyes narrowed against glare.

Speaking Style: Blunt, brief, carrying; says a thing once, and the docks repeat it for him. 'Crane three. Down. Now.' He calls people by what they are doing, 'rope', 'crane', 'you with the boat', and uses full names only for the drowned and the rescued. Off the docks he talks less, not more. 'Water took three this year. Brought back two. I am still asking about the third.'
Combat Role: He closes and grapples rather than strikes, using rope, boat-hook, dock furniture, and the river itself. He subdues rather than damages and has never once let anyone drown.
Under Pressure: He gives orders like the river gives current, counts every life pulled from the water and none of the thanks, is unarmed on principle, and tests people with cold, wet, unglamorous work before trusting them.
Tolvir Nash.hiddenInfo:
Two months ago a barge-load went into the river upstream — witnessed, marked, mourned by its insurers — and never surfaced anywhere. Tolvir has spent a lifetime learning where the Longreach puts what it takes; nothing sinks in his river without coming up where he expects, and this cargo did not. He has dragged the deep pools himself, at night, off duty, and found exactly one thing: a splintered crate fragment carrying a small tracker-stud of a make he does not recognize — not Dravon pattern, not local, not anything the dock trades use. It sits wrapped in oilcloth in his locker, unreported. He has not told Corsair, because sunken cargo means Waypoint politics and insurance war, and the moment he speaks, the river becomes a courtroom; he has not told his own wardens, because his authority is moral rather than legal, and it survives on his never being publicly wrong. What keeps him walking the upstream banks is a conclusion he hates: either the river has changed, or someone is using it as a road he cannot see — moving things under his water, past his people, beneath the city that trusts him to know. He would take help from anyone who asks the right question, and he will test them first, probably in cold water.

Thread: A barge-load that went into the river never surfaced where the Longreach always puts what it takes, and the tracker-stud wrapped in oilcloth in his locker is of a make he does not recognise. Leverage: He would take help from anyone who asks the right question and will test them first, probably in cold water; what he cannot do is speak, because the moment he does the river becomes a courtroom. Combat Role: He closes and grapples rather than strikes, using rope, boat-hook, dock furniture and the river itself. He subdues rather than damages, and has never once let anyone drown.

Tolvir is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: Straight, monogamous by settled preference. Blunt and brief, the docks repeating him; monogamous by settled preference. He tests a suitor with cold, wet, unglamorous work before trusting them with anything.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A rescue captain's baseline — two hearts driving cold-water endurance past any reasonable limit, rope-built grappling strength, and short flight over water. Age has cost him speed and none of his depth; he subdues rather than kills.

(Control) Crane and Fire Discipline: Enforces load safety and fire watch across the working waterfront. He can freeze a terrace of machinery with one call and restart it in correct order. Riggers argue with everyone but him.
(Affinity) Breath Thread: Feels the direction of a small air current across his own lips distinctly. Does not allow underwater breathing or replace river-rescue training.

(Shared) River Pilotage [Crews follow him into flood because he has never spent a life carelessly]; Failure Forensics [The skill's first failure in thirty years is currently keeping him awake]; Crew Leadership [Docks, cranes, and drunks obey him without a weapon in sight]; Endurance Conditioning [Age has cost him speed and none of his depth]; People Reading [Those who pass get his full backing for life]

Meya Orlin.name: Meya Orlin
Meya Orlin.basicInfo:
Chief physician of Helvyra's independent care hall, the fiercely neutral ground where dock injuries, sword-school training wounds, and traveler fevers all end up. A gray-braided woman with ink-stained cuffs from her injury ledgers, she argues with both of the city's sword schools about what they do to their students and wins by simply outlasting them. She never raises her voice; she repeats herself until the other side ages. She is currently cataloguing a particular set of wounds with more care than she lets show.

A rangy Starian woman with a grey braid down her back, a lined unshockable face, ink-stained cuffs from her injury ledgers, and level grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Flat, dry, clinical; hard truths at dictation speed, comfort never repeated. 'It will heal crooked. Sit. I said it will heal crooked.' She calls patients by their injury until she has closed it, sword masters by their school, and her rare praise is that something was done cleanly. 'Clean work, whoever wrapped this. Tell them I said so, once.'
Combat Role: She does not fight, and the city is organised around never making her: both sword schools enforce the hall's neutrality. An aggressor who forces it meets a needle's worth of the right substance.
Under Pressure: She never raises her voice and never drops her point, treats first and judges never, keeps ledgers more honest than confessions, and bullies sword masters about their students' bodies.
Meya Orlin.hiddenInfo:
Her private wound atlas — decades of dock, blade, and river injuries, indexed by cause — has a new section she shows no one. A recurring injury pattern is arriving at the hall that matches no known blade style: forcing-game pressure damage of one school's kind combined with glancing entry angles of the other school's kind, on patients who claim, politely and identically, to have fallen. They pay in coin, give lodging-house addresses, and never return for follow-up. The wounds progress — earlier cases crude, later ones clean — which means someone is not brawling but teaching. She has said nothing to either sword school, because the hall's neutrality is the only reason such patients come to her at all, and the day she reports a patient is the day the injured start dying quietly at home instead. She does not know that a blade-keeper across the river is reading the same signature in metal that she is reading in flesh. Her leverage point is her oath and her ledger both: anyone who can prove she concealed a pattern of organized violence could break the hall's custom of silence — and anyone who wants the pattern understood will find her already halfway there.

Thread: A wound pattern matching no known blade style keeps arriving at the hall, progressing from crude to clean — which means teaching, not brawling — and reporting it would end the neutrality that brings those patients in at all. Leverage: She treats anyone and asks nothing. The ledger is open to whoever wants the pattern understood and closed to whoever wants a name. Under threat: She does not fight, and the city is organised around never making her. The hall's neutrality is fierce custom and both sword schools enforce it.

Meya is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and keeps her attachments open by agreement. Flat, dry and clinical; asexual, with attachments open by agreement. Comfort is never repeated, and neither is a refusal.
personality: never raises her voice; never drops her point
treats first and judges never, which is why the dangerous come to her at all
records everything; her injury ledgers are more honest than most confessions
bullies sword masters about their students' bodies with total fearlessness
her care is brusque, unsentimental, and absolute

checks both sword schools' training days against her ledger every week
