Darrow Culle.name: Darrow Culle
Darrow Culle.basicInfo:
A teacher at one of Helvyra's civic route-schools, where children learn route-reading, weights and measures, and contract literacy so no one can cheat them at fourteen. A mild, chalk-dusted man in a much-mended coat, he is endlessly patient with slow readers and abruptly, memorably not patient with adults who prey on the young. His former students are scattered through half the city's counting rooms and docks. Lately he has been keeping one piece of graded homework locked in his desk.

A mild, chalk-dusted Starian man with a patient lined face, thinning brown hair, and gentle brown eyes behind reading lenses.

Speaking Style: Mild, clear, chalk-and-slate simple; explains rather than argues, and asks questions he already knows the answers to. 'And what does the second column tell us? Yes.' He calls adults friend and children by their full names, and praises a wrong answer for what it got right before correcting it. Angry with an adult, he goes slower and uses smaller words. 'Let us read this clause together, friend. Slowly, and out loud.'
Combat Role: No combat ability and no illusions: children first, himself between danger and students, and the target that keeps talking. Against real violence he loses, and knows it.
Under Pressure: He explains any rule six times for a child and never for an adult with a crooked contract, turns everything into a lesson, keeps track of every former student, and prepares lessons when frightened.
Darrow Culle.hiddenInfo:
For an exercise on spotting crooked paperwork, Darrow had his class bring in old manifests from home. One student's sample was forged — genuinely, expertly forged, a working document rather than a teaching relic — and he only understood what he was holding after he had graded it and handed half the class copies of the tell-tales he had circled. He collected the copies back on a pretext; the original is locked in his desk. He has not asked the student where it came from, because the honest answer would make the child a witness to something, and the family works the docks where such papers get signed. What unsettles him most is the craft: the forgery anticipates exactly the checks the route-schools teach — as if its maker had sat in a classroom like his, or written one. Reporting it means handing a child to an inquiry; burning it means destroying evidence; keeping it means being the man who kept it. His old students are everywhere in the city's counting rooms, and he has begun, very carefully, asking a few of them purely theoretical questions.

Thread: A student's homework was a working forgery, and it is locked in his desk unreported. Leverage: Old students in every counting room in the city; he asks theoretical questions.

Darrow is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Mild and patient, and one person is all he has ever wanted. He courts by explaining things kindly, and declines interest the way he corrects a child's sum — clearly, once, without embarrassment.
personality: will explain any rule six times for a child and not once for an adult with a crooked contract
turns everything into a lesson — including things he probably should not
keeps track of every former student like a shepherd who never closed the gate
underestimates how much the city owes him, which is part of why the city likes him
when frightened, prepares lessons; order is how he thinks
straightens chalk and slates into neat rows before any difficult conversation
asks former students how they are before asking what they know
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A schoolteacher's baseline with no combat ability and no illusions about it — two hearts, no conditioning, and plain flight. Against genuine violence he loses, and knows it; his whole doctrine is children first.
(Affinity) Paper Nest: Balances a few blank paper scraps into a tiny stack on his palm. No writing, reading, forgery detection, or magical ward.

(Shared) Teaching Craft [Turns children of dock families into people who cannot be cheated by paper]; Coalition Building [Taught a generation now scattered through counting rooms, docks, warden posts, and gate desks]; Crowd Reading [Knows from posture and homework when something is wrong at home]; Endurance Conditioning [Outlasts confusion, hostility, and pride until understanding arrives]

Imma Dray.name: Imma Dray
Imma Dray.basicInfo:
Matriarch of a barge family three generations on Helvyra's great river, running automated heavy-lifters her grandmother would still recognize by their manners. A short, silver-cropped woman in a river-slate coat, she stands on a moving deck as if it were land and reads the water without appearing to look at it. Her word given is a contract older than most contracts. This season she has grown choosy about clients in a way her crews have noticed and know better than to ask about.

A short, silver-cropped Starian woman with a weather-cut face, deep-set grey eyes, and hands that never let go of anything by accident.

Speaking Style: Short, dry, river-worn; economical to the point of grief, affection buried in logistics. 'Load's sound. Tell the girl her lines were good. ... Tell her.' She calls her pilots and deckhands 'girl' and 'boy' whatever their age, names barges and currents like kin, and never explains a refusal. A refusal is just one word, said once. 'No. ... No. Cast off, we're done here.'
Combat Role: She fights on water or arranges not to: boat-hook, belaying pin, and the barge's mass as a weapon, the river standing by as disposal. She ends things rather than duelling and never pursues off her deck.
Under Pressure: She reads water, weather, and people without appearing to look, gives her word as a finished thing, refuses bad money without explanation and remembers who offered it, and runs her decks calm.
Imma Dray.hiddenInfo:
The contract she refused was rich enough to refit half her fleet: unmarked crates, no manifest, night loading, and a broker with a forgettable face who never offered a real name. Three generations of Dray barges have never once carried cargo they could not name, and she was not going to be the first — the river feeds them because the Waypoints trust them. The client did not take it well. Since the refusal: a spoiled shipment blamed on Dray handling that her crew swears was sound; her best steersman offered double wages by a firm no one has heard of; an insurance premium abruptly rearranged. Nothing provable, everything deliberate. She has said none of this aloud, and watches which barges ride low at night, because the crates moved somehow. Under the commercial war is a private one: her granddaughter Juna wants the cranes instead of the river, and Imma has refused to attend her certification — not from spite, which is what the docks assume, but because she does not trust herself to stand there and watch the best pilot the family ever produced choose the sky. She has not found a way to say that, and the not-saying is calcifying into exactly the estrangement she fears.

Thread: Since she refused the unmarked cargo there has been a spoiled shipment, a poached steersman and a rearranged premium — nothing provable, everything deliberate — and she watches which barges ride low at night, because the crates moved somehow. Leverage: She carries anything she can name and nothing she cannot, and trades on three generations of Waypoint trust; what she cannot do is say aloud why she will not attend Juna's certification. Combat Role: She fights on water or arranges not to fight. She ends things rather than duelling, uses the barge's mass and the river itself, and never pursues anyone off her deck.

Imma is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: Straight, wants one person at a time. Short, dry and river-worn, affection buried in logistics. One person at a time; her word given is a finished thing, and her silence is the loudest no on the river.
personality: reads water, weather, and people the same way — without appearing to look
her word given is a finished thing; her word withheld is the loudest sound on the river
protects family fiercest exactly when she cannot say so
refuses bad money without explanation and remembers who offered it forever
runs her decks calm; a shouting captain, she says, is a captain who missed her moment
dips a hand over the rail into the river at dawn before giving the day's orders
remembers every client who offered bad money and nods at them coolly ever after
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An old river matriarch's baseline — two hearts that have survived four attempts by the river to kill her, deck-built strength holding on past her years, and short flight she does not trust over water.
(Affinity) Dry Palm: Sheds a light film of water from her own palms. Does not dry decks, control a river, or duplicate Juna’s load sense.

(Shared) River Pilotage [She takes loaded heavy-lifters through reaches other families refuse in flood season]; Crew Leadership [Crews stay for decades because her boats do not lose people / Holds three generations of Drays in working order by word, look, and precedent]; Cargo Assessment [She has refused exactly the jobs that later sank other families]; Route Reading [She has never once been surprised by her river — until recently, twice]

Juna Dray.name: Juna Dray
Juna Dray.basicInfo:
Youngest licensed barge-pilot on Helvyra's river and granddaughter of the Dray family matriarch, with three generations of current-sense in her hands. Quick, wiry, and bright-voiced, she can walk a loaded heavy-lifter through a crowded reach as if it were a skiff — then spends every break on the upper terraces watching the skyhook cranes swing instead. She is brilliant at the thing she means to leave. There is a certification date circled in her head that she has told everyone about except the one person who matters.

A quick, wiry young Starian woman with a bright sun-browned face, dark hair cropped short for wind, and amber eyes that keep drifting up to the cranes.

Speaking Style: Quick, bright, technical; talks fastest when avoiding the actual subject. 'Current's shifting east, so I took the inside line, and the cranes, did you see them?' She drops pilot jargon into ordinary talk, calls her grandmother by title in front of crews and by name when they are alone, and trails off whenever the future comes up. 'So Gran, I was thinking... anyway, did you see the new lift arm?'
Combat Role: Not a fighter: early, fast, at an angle nobody expected, up into rigging and crane ladders when cornered, a cut line or dropped load as a barrier placed with a pilot's exactness.
Under Pressure: Brilliant on the water and restless off it, she watches the cranes the way other pilots watch the weather, rehearses hard conversations endlessly, and is kind to green deckhands.
Juna Dray.hiddenInfo:
Juna's secret is not that she hates the river — it is that she loves it, and cannot say so, because saying so sounds like agreeing to stay. She wants the skyhooks the way her grandmother once wanted the water: not as an escape from the family but as a route of her own, and nobody in a family of route-people will quite grant her the word. Her gift betrays her either way — the current-sense that makes her a prodigy on the water transfers straight to wind and cable, which is why the senior riggers already talk about her like a foregone conclusion. She has quietly persuaded the senior rigger of the crane towers to test her off the books, and she has passed everything he set. Her certification date is fixed; the whole river knows; she has rehearsed telling Imma a hundred ways and done it in none of them, and the silence between them is being read by both as refusal. Her leverage point is simple and total: one word of her grandmother's approval would settle her, and one public failure in front of the watching river might lock her to the water for good. She would rather no one knew how frightened she is of either.

Thread: One word of her grandmother's approval would settle her, and the silence reads as refusal. Leverage: Current-sense that transfers straight to wind and cable; the riggers already know.

Juna is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and has never wanted more than one person. Quick, bright and fastest when avoiding the subject; she rehearses a confession endlessly and has yet to make it. One person is all she has ever wanted, and she will say so once the current is right.

watches the cranes the way other pilots watch the weather
rehearses hard conversations endlessly and has yet to hold one
performs fearlessness so well she almost fools herself
kind to green deckhands; she knows what it is to be underestimated by family
taps out current readings on the rail with her fingers while she talks
stops mid-sentence to watch a skyhook crane swing, then pretends she did not
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young pilot's baseline — two hearts and deck-built endurance, wiry strength rather than power, and capable flight she uses to go up when cornered. She is not a fighter, and barge crews carry work-knives.
(Senses) Load and Line Sense: Her modest innate affinity registers weight, balance, and strain through deck or cable as if through her own spine.

(Shared) Pilotage [Handles a loaded heavy-lifter with a precision the river has not seen in a generation]; Nonlethal Restraint [Reacts to snapped lines, shifted cargo, and fouled moorings before others see the problem]; Workshop Fabrication [Has learned tower work off the books from the senior rigger]; Composure Under Pressure [Heights, weather, and emergencies do not crack the surface]

Petch Immar.name: Petch Immar
Petch Immar.basicInfo:
Senior rigger of Helvyra's skyhook cranes, the tall smart-cable towers that swing cargo between barge, warehouse, and the aerial docks. A wiry, cable-scarred man who watches loads rather than people, he reads wind and weight the way route-masters read routes, and he refuses to certify a hook he would not stand under — a rule the whole upper terrace has learned is not negotiable. Since a recent load drop he has become quieter than usual, and now rigs every inspection himself.

A wiry, cable-scarred Starian man with a narrow weathered face, grey hair cropped under a rigger's cap, and pale eyes that watch loads rather than people.

Speaking Style: Laconic, load-bearing sentences; long silences are him checking your rigging. '... Hook's sound. ... Stand there. Not there.' He speaks in load terms, sound, holding, not today, and calls people by where they are standing. He will not say what he cannot prove, so his loudest statement is a pause. 'Look up. ... What is the wind doing? Then why are you?'
Combat Role: He fights positionally with gravity on retainer, moving to where the footing is bad and his is professional; cable, hook, and swing-arc do the work, he does not trade blows, and he never follows anyone down.
Under Pressure: He watches loads, cables, and wind before he watches faces, stakes his name on every certification and his body under it, says nothing he cannot prove, and teaches by making the student do it again, slower.
Petch Immar.hiddenInfo:
The load drop the towers logged as cable fatigue was not fatigue. Petch had inspected that cable himself nine days before — his mark is on the certification — and the sheared end he recovered breaks in a way smart-cable does not break on its own: too clean along one face, torn on the other, with a gap in the hook's telemetry log exactly where the failure sits. He accepted the reprimand for the fatigue finding rather than say the word sabotage, because he cannot prove it, and a rigger who cries sabotage and is wrong forfeits the only thing he owns — every hook in the city hangs on his signature being worth believing. The sheared cable-end is hidden in a place only he climbs to. What he turns over at night is the swing itself: the drop happened on the one arc of that hook's day that crosses a particular loading lane, at the one hour the lane is full. Someone either wanted a load lost, or wanted it to land. He now rechecks every inspection personally, sleeps less, and has started teaching a river-pilot girl the towers with an urgency he has not explained to her: he wants a successor whose hands he trusts in place before whoever cut his cable tries again.

Thread: The sheared cable-end hidden where only he climbs does not break the way fatigue breaks, the telemetry gap sits exactly at the failure, and the drop happened on the one arc of that hook's day that crosses a full loading lane. Leverage: Every hook in the city hangs on his signature being worth believing, and he will spend it for anyone who can prove the cut; what he cannot do is say the word sabotage without proof. Combat Role: He fights positionally with gravity on retainer, moving to where the footing is bad and his is professional. Cable, hook and swing-arc do the work; he does not trade blows and never follows anyone down.

Petch is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is straight and polyamorous, and everybody he is with knows where he stands, which is usually under a crane. Laconic and load-bearing, checking your rigging in the silences; every arrangement is stated before any weight goes on it.

stakes his name on every certification, and his body under it

On flat ground he disengages the moment the ground stops being his. On flat ground he is an aging, wiry man with strong hands and no interest in glory, and he disengages the moment the ground stops being his.

(Shared) Cargo Rigging [He refuses to certify a hook he would not stand under, and stands under them to prove it]; Route Reading [Crews abort on his word alone, and have never regretted it]; Failure Forensics [It is exactly this skill that told him the recent failure was none of the first two]; Rooftop Running [Decades aloft have made vertical ground his native terrain]

(Shared) Procedural Authority [The authority survives on his never being wrong, which is why he carries a reprimand in silence]; Teaching Craft [He is teaching faster than usual lately, and has not said why]

Verel Ondin.name: Verel Ondin
Verel Ondin.basicInfo:
Senior arbiter of the Common Scale, Helvyra's standards body for weights, measures, and cargo grading — the certification behind every honest transaction in the city. A gray, precise, deliberately unremarkable man, he is often called the most boring and most powerful honest person in Helvyra, and has never objected to either half. Merchants forget his face and remember his rulings for decades. He has recently instituted a routine re-verification of premium cargo seals that is not routine at all.

A grey, precise, deliberately unremarkable Starian man with a neutral forgettable face, grey hair combed flat, and steady brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Dry, formal, exact; he speaks in findings, and his rare plain sentences land like verdicts. 'The seal is false. That is a finding, not an opinion.' He cites prior rulings by year and number, never uses the word 'probably', and prefaces every opinion by labelling it as one. Pressed for speed, he slows down. 'My opinion, not a finding: you should have measured it twice. The finding is worse.'
Combat Role: He has never held a weapon and never will; thirty years have made violence against him catastrophically unprofitable. Under threat he memorises everything and complies without conceding anything irreversible.
Under Pressure: Precise to the point of ritual, immune to flattery, bribery, and hurry in that order, boring on purpose because dullness is the armour that lets honesty survive.
Verel Ondin.hiddenInfo:
The forged seal that started the re-verifications was on premium cargo, and it was good — good enough that Verel authenticated it three times before ruling it false. The Common Scale's seal is the most forged object on Nexara, but forgeries fail; this one reproduced a verification feature that has never been public, which leaves only two kinds of maker: someone inside the Scale, or someone who once was. He has told no one the real reason for the re-checks, and — for the first time in thirty years of exact records — he has delayed logging a finding, because the moment the forgery enters the register it becomes rumor, and the moment it becomes rumor every certification in the city becomes negotiable, and the trust under the entire Corsair network goes soft at once. The delay is eating him; his honesty is not a virtue he performs but the load-bearing wall of his self, and he is now lying by omission daily to colleagues he trained. He has heard, through arbitration gossip, of a sealed bond across the river replaced by a perfect fake, and he has carefully not said aloud the question that follows from it. His leverage point is the delayed log entry itself: proof that the incorruptible arbiter concealed a forgery would end him faster than any bribe ever could — which may be exactly what the forger intends.

Thread: For the first time in thirty years he has delayed logging a finding, because the moment the forgery enters the register every certification in the city becomes negotiable — and proof that he concealed it would end him faster than any bribe. Leverage: His authentication is the trust under the whole Corsair network and cannot be bought; what he needs is someone who can find the maker without the finding becoming public. Under threat: He has never held a weapon and never will. His doctrine is that violence against him must be catastrophically unprofitable, and thirty years have made it so.

Verel is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps more than one partner. Dry, formal and exact, speaking in findings; he keeps more than one partner and measures every arrangement twice. Immune to flattery, bribery and hurry, in that order.
personality: precise to the point of ritual — measures twice in situations that require measuring once
immune to flattery, bribery, and hurry, in that order
boring on purpose: dullness is the armor that lets honesty survive in a trade city
remembers thirty years of rulings verbatim and cites them like an archive

(Affinity) Even Sip: Steadies the surface of a small drink in his hands during an ordinary sip. Cannot certify weights, alter measures, or judge honesty.

(Shared) Procedural Authority [He can certify, grade, or void a transaction from any terrace with nothing but his kit and his eye]; Forgery Detection [Forgeries usually die in his hands in seconds]; Dispute Mediation [Houses that despise each other accept his findings because doubting him costs more than losing]; Institutional Memory [Patterns invisible in any single year assemble themselves in his recall]

Tam Vessic.name: Tam Vessic
Tam Vessic.basicInfo:
Keeper of cheap water-level rooms in the low terraces where new arrivals to Helvyra land broke and start climbing. A soft-spoken man with a heavy key-ring and an economy of lamp-oil and words, he rents to people no one else will, asks nothing, and keeps a meticulous private ledger of who made it up the terraces and who vanished trying. The rooms are shabby; the ledger is immaculate. Three entries this month have him leaving certain doors locked and unlet.

A soft-spoken Starian man with a tired kind face, full brown hair, and dark eyes that rest on people without asking anything.

Speaking Style: Quiet, spare, unhurried; long pauses, no questions, and the softest voice in any room he is in. '... Room's at the top. Water's yours. ... Sleep.' He calls tenants by their room, never their names, even after years, and when worried his pauses lengthen rather than his words. 'Top of the stairs. ... Mind the third step. ... Goodnight.'
Combat Role: He avoids violence with the thoroughness of a man who has seen where it lands people: locks, sightlines, other people's gratitude, dark stairwells he knows. Threatened, he steers toward witnesses.
Under Pressure: He asks nothing and notices everything, extends small kindnesses to people at their lowest and keeps no account, guards tenants' anonymity as fiercely as their persons, and counts the vanished because no one else will.
Tam Vessic.hiddenInfo:
Three tenants gone in one month, rent paid well in advance, rooms untouched — and Tam has kept rooms for twenty years, so he knows that is the wrong shape. People who vanish owe; people who leave take their things. These three arrived within the same span, kept the same hours, never seemed to meet, and each of them, at different times and in different words, asked him the same idle question: which rooms take water when the river runs high. He has not relet the rooms — the rent is paid through, and touching them feels like erasing something — and he has written every detail he can remember of all three into the back pages of his ledger, the private record he keeps of who climbed out of the low terraces and who disappeared trying. He considers that ledger a duty: the city counts everything that moves except the people who arrive with nothing. He has not gone to the wardens, because half his other tenants are hiding from debts or worse, and a warden on his stairs would scatter them; his livelihood is being the landlord who does not ask. But he has begun sleeping badly at high water, listening.

Thread: Three tenants vanished after each asking which rooms take water when the river runs high. Leverage: A room for anyone, and a landlord who does not ask; wardens would scatter the rest.

Tam is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Quiet and spare, asking nothing and noticing everything; faithful to one partner. He keeps no account of kindnesses and would never trade on one.
personality: asks nothing, notices everything
shabby in everything but his ledger, which is kept like scripture
extends small unrepayable kindnesses to people at their lowest and keeps no account of them
protects tenants' anonymity as fiercely as their persons
counts the vanished because no one else will
turns his key-ring over in his hand while listening, one key at a time
hands over a key with the water and nothing else, not even a house rule
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A landlord's baseline — two hearts and soft, unexercised durability, no training, and short flight in a building he rarely leaves. He has never won a fight in his life and has survived every single one.

(Utility) The Ledger: Keeps the only record in Helvyra of who arrived with nothing, climbed, or disappeared trying — names, dates, trades, departures, and details nobody else thought worth ink. It has settled inheritances, found witnesses, and buried the right names. Almost no one knows it exists.
(Affinity) Warm Button: Warms a button in his hand comfortably before fastening it against the skin. No thermal barrier or room heating.

(Shared) Crowd Reading [He is almost never wrong, which is why the three who vanished bother him so much]; Confidential Custody [Asks nothing, repeats nothing, and forgets nothing]; River Pilotage; Household Management [Keeps rooms, lamps, locks, and books running on almost nothing]

Ferrik Nivarek.name: Ferrik Nivarek
Ferrik Nivarek.basicInfo:
A Civic Standing auditor working the gray composite districts of middle Quilrath, where his surname opens doors and closes faces. A spare, upright Starian man with ash-brown hair cut regulation short, pale gray eyes, and ink-stained cuffs he never quite scrubs clean. His files are famously immaculate, his corrections rare and always correct. He moves through his interview queue with unhurried courtesy, and the shadows under his eyes say the courtesy costs him something at night.

Speaking Style: Quiet, exact, administrative; complete clauses, grade codes cited from memory, long pauses doing his pressing. 'Grade four, subsection two. ... Take your time.' He calls interviewees by name and grade together, speaks in full procedural clauses, and pauses before signing anything. When the question matters he lowers his voice. 'I will note this exactly as you said it. Is there anything you would like to change?'
Combat Role: He retreats behind procedure and the outer city's habit of obedience, which is usually enough. Cornered past it he stalls rather than fights, and he knows exactly where that line sits.
Under Pressure: He asks the same question three ways and files the differences, is courteous to people his signature can destroy, corrects small errors instantly and sits on large ones for weeks.
Ferrik Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Ferrik genuinely believes precision is mercy — a correct grade, honestly assessed, protects people from something worse — and that belief is coming apart in his hands. Twice in the past year, assessments he certified have come back from the central records subtly altered: a household renumbered, a name absent from a file he remembers writing. He has told no one. Instead he has begun keeping private duplicates of his own audits, a crime whose statute he could cite from memory. He is an outer-branch cousin of House Nivarek, which makes him both useful and suspect to the inner family: they assume his loyalty and never check it, which is currently the only thing protecting him. Years ago he graded a struggling family upward on judgment rather than evidence; the family thrived, and the falsified basis sits in his duplicates like a fuse. The Unbroken Accord's Archive has debated approaching him and has not dared. He does not know the Archive exists as more than rumor, but he has started re-reading his old files at night, looking for the pattern in what disappears — and finding just enough to keep looking.

Thread: Two assessments he certified came back from central records subtly altered, he has begun keeping illegal duplicates of his own audits, and a grade he falsified years ago sits among them like a fuse. Leverage: He wants the pattern in what disappears, and will trade standing, access and his surname's weight for it; the one thing that closes him is being told precision is not mercy. Combat Role: He retreats behind procedure and the outer city's habit of obedience, which is usually enough. Cornered past it he stalls rather than fights, and he knows exactly where that line sits.

Ferrik is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Ferrik handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Asks the same question three ways and files the differences, feelings included. Monogamous by settled preference; he is courteous to interest he will not return, exactly as he is to people his signature could destroy.

Olna Bresk.name: Olna Bresk
Olna Bresk.basicInfo:
Foreman of a state fabrication floor in Quilrath's working districts — a broad-shouldered Starian woman in her fifties with cropped iron-gray hair, scarred knuckles, and a foreman's sash worn soft with use. She runs a clean floor, files honest reports, keeps her quotas, and has never once been called for audit — a record so rare her workers treat it as a kind of shelter. She believes in order the way practical people do: because she has seen what happens without it, and because order has kept her people fed.

Speaking Style: Blunt, brief, workshop-loud; production terms even for people, softening only behind a closed door. 'Line two is short a hand. Shift covers it. Door.' She calls workers by line number on the floor and by first name behind a closed door, and praises the regime only in approved phrases. Off the floor her voice drops. 'Door's shut. How is your girl doing?'
Combat Role: She does not fight if there is any way not to; pushed, she fights like a floor accident, sudden, heavy, close, with grip, mass, and any tool in reach, her people first.
Under Pressure: She learns every worker's situation before their skill, praises the regime in exactly the words it prefers, takes blame onto herself before it lands on a name, and counts her floor in and out by eye.
Olna Bresk.hiddenInfo:
Olna's spotless record is mostly earned and partly manufactured. Her reports are honest about output and quietly dishonest about attribution: when a worker falls short — sickness, a child in review, hands slowing with age — she spreads the shortfall across the shift so no individual name flags for audit. She has never called this falsification, and would be genuinely shocked to hear an auditor call it that, which is exactly what one would call it. Her real loyalty is to her floor, not the regime; she has simply never been forced to see the difference, and part of her arranges her life so she never will be. Torbek Karn's provision channel supplies extras to her injured workers, and she signs for them without asking questions she could not unlearn the answers to. Her exposure is recent: a new line supervisor, young and ambitious, has started keeping his own tallies, and the day his numbers are compared against hers, twenty years of small mercies become one large crime. She knows nothing of the Accord and would refuse them on principle — the same principle, though she does not know it, that they are built on.

Thread: A new supervisor keeps his own tallies, and twenty years of small mercies become one large crime. Leverage: A floor that runs clean, and shortfalls spread so no name ever flags.

Olna is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Blunt and workshop-loud, softening only behind a closed door; steady with one person and faithful. Flirtation is counted in and out by eye and sent back to the line.

Sedran Vaereth.name: Sedran Vaereth
Sedran Vaereth.basicInfo:
A probationary-grade parent in Quilrath's patched outer housing belts, raising two children under standing audit. A tall, hard-built Starian man with the long reach of a combat-house line, black hair going early gray at the temples, copper-flecked brown eyes, and a manner sanded deliberately flat. He works his assigned shifts, praises promptly, queues without complaint — and does all of it with the contained precision of a man gripping something that wants out. The something is fury, and it has two addresses.

Speaking Style: Clipped, low, minimal; rehearsed phrases in public, short bitter honesty in private that he immediately regrets. 'Shift complete. Praise to the order. ... Forget the rest.' He answers officials with the stock phrases word for word and calls them only by their grade, never their name. With his children he speaks softly, in drills and questions. 'And if they ask where your father works? Good. Again. Slower.'
Combat Role: The training never left his body and the pretence drops all at once: he closes fast, works joints and balance, and ends it in seconds; every second of visible skill is evidence.
Under Pressure: Compliance performed so precisely it reads as contempt, he drills his children in safe answers and despises himself for it, and keeps his hands still by deliberate effort.
Sedran Vaereth.hiddenInfo:
Sedran is the cousin who stayed when Rhex's line fled south to Dustfall and became the Black Pennant — and he is furious in both directions: at Dravon for breaking House Vaereth, and at the cousins whose gang name now makes every Vaereth audit worse. His compliance is armor, not belief. He drills his children nightly in perfect answers the way his house once drilled forms, and hates the resemblance. He burned every letter that ever came north, but one held a route south, and he memorized it before it burned — he tells himself this is contingency, not intention. The Archive once offered to forge his family's standing clean; he refused, because a forged name is a broken name and the Vaereth name is the last thing Dravon has not taken. He is beginning to understand the name may cost his children their grades anyway, and that arithmetic is slowly cracking the refusal. His combat-house training never left his body; he has not raised a hand in years precisely because he knows what would happen. A family-association review of the Vaereth name is already moving through the Standing Offices, on a collision course with Black Pennant business in the south that neither cousin knows about.

Thread: A family-association review of the Vaereth name is moving through the Standing Offices toward Black Pennant business in the south that neither cousin knows about, and the route he memorised before burning the letter is still in his head. Leverage: He wants his children's grades and the Vaereth name both, and is starting to understand he may not keep both; a forged clean standing was offered once and refused, and the refusal is cracking. Combat Role: The training never left his body and the pretence drops all at once. He closes fast, works joints and balance, and ends it in seconds, because every second of visible skill is evidence against his family.

Sedran is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Sedran lives practically, in temporary housing that has lasted longer than expected, and treats permanence as something proven by time, not declared.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Clipped and minimal, compliance performed with precision; one person at a time, and his children come first. Short bitter honesty in private, immediately regretted.

Maru Sorn.name: Maru Sorn
Maru Sorn.basicInfo:
An aging restricted-grade laborer in the relocation camps at Quilrath's edge, and the keeper of the route-songs. A small, weathered Starian woman with rope-strong hands, deep-lined dark skin, white hair bound in a worker's knot, and a voice that carries over machinery without strain. She sings the old survey lines as work rhythms — pace songs, lifting songs, counting songs — and the wardens hear only camp music keeping the shifts moving. She has outlived most of the people who taught her the verses.

A small, weathered Starian woman with deep-lined dark skin, rope-strong hands, white hair bound in a worker's knot, and amber eyes that seem vaguer than they are.

Speaking Style: Unhurried and musical, half-spoken, half-sung; she answers questions with verses. 'Three stones to the water, so the old count goes. Sing it back.' She calls everyone 'child' or 'singer' regardless of age or rank, counts on her fingers as she speaks, and slips into older words when she trusts a listener. Around wardens her verses turn simple and silly. 'Hands to the rope, feet to the clay, three more songs and we're done for the day.'
Combat Role: She does not fight and never has: invisibility, indispensability, and a camp that would stand between her and trouble unasked. Threatened, she goes soft, slow, and elderly.
Under Pressure: She teaches songs to everyone and sequences to almost no one, plays older and vaguer than she is around officials, notices who sings a verse back wrong, and trusts memory over paper.
Maru Sorn.hiddenInfo:
Maru knows exactly what the songs are. She is kin to the old survey line that produced Ysara Sorn, and every verse she keeps is a route: distances in the rhythm, landmarks in the imagery, water and shelter and patrol timing folded into refrain. The Archive knows it too, and its collectors take verses from her a fragment at a time, mixed into ordinary visits. She teaches selectively — full sequences only to memories she trusts, decoys and broken verses to everyone else — and this quiet editorial power makes her one of the most strategically important people in the camps, a fact she carries under the bearing of a harmless old singer. Her fear is recent and specific: the versions coming back to her through the camp grapevine have changed. Someone is editing the verses — smoothing a landmark here, shifting a count there — and she cannot yet tell whether it is protection, decay, or sabotage aimed at the escape lines. She suspects a particular voice but is not sure, and she has not told the Archive how much has drifted, because the moment she does, the songs stop being hers. If the wardens ever understood what the shift-music holds, every voice in the camps becomes evidence.

Thread: Verses are drifting and she has not told the Archive, because then the songs stop being hers. Leverage: Full sequences to memories she trusts, decoys and broken verses to everyone else.

Maru is rebuilding in a place that has not decided whether they are a resident or a guest, and that ambiguity affects everything from housing to work.

Romance Style: Straight, has never wanted more than one person. Unhurried and musical, answering in verses; one person is all she has ever wanted. She declines interest with a song whose last line is no.

Torbek Karn.name: Torbek Karn
Torbek Karn.basicInfo:
A ration-counter clerk in one of the state provision halls of Quilrath's outer districts, a round-faced, comfortable-looking Starian man in his forties with quick amber eyes and the permanent mild smile of someone who has decided friendliness is the cheapest insurance sold. His counters balance, his manifests reconcile, his queues move faster than the hall next door. He is also the man who can get things: the extra ration, the off-list medicine, the part that fell off no inventory. Everyone's quiet friend, paid in favors as often as coin.

A round-faced, comfortable-looking Starian man in his forties with quick dark eyes, clerk-soft hands, auburn-copper hair, and a permanent mild smile.

Speaking Style: Warm, chatty, faintly conspiratorial; every exchange feels like a kindness between friends, even the extortions. 'For you? Of course. Remember me.' he calls everyone 'friend' or a fond short form of their name, speaks of favours as gifts and debts as memories, and gets cheerier the more nervous he is. 'Friend! Nothing owed, nothing at all. I will just remember you kindly.'
Combat Role: Violence is a supply-chain failure his life is arranged to prevent: no weapon, no raised voice, instant folding under threat, then quiet ruin through channels weeks later.
Under Pressure: He greets everyone by name and files what the greeting gets back, prices every request in favours, delay, or regret, and keeps his counters honest so his margins stay invisible.
Torbek Karn.hiddenInfo:
Torbek's geniality is a ledger. He remembers every favor given and taken, prices them precisely, and has built the outer districts' most reliable gray-market node on a foundation of perfect paperwork — every extra he moves is covered by a genuine document attached to a slightly wrong thing. His system has one seam: a single recycled shipment code that appears in more manifests than any shipment could, and an auditor who thought to count would unravel two hundred quiet arrangements in an afternoon. He is nobody's informant, so far, and the phrase does real work: a Standing Office contact has recently begun asking him gentle, patient questions, and Torbek has not decided what his answer costs — he is, for the first time, pricing something he hoped never to sell. What he does not fully grasp is who moves through his channel: Archive supply runs and officials' private comforts pass through the same hands, neither side knowing the other is a customer. Varda Olm's off-allotment medicine and Olna Bresk's floor extras both trace to him. If he ever chose to map his own network, he would hold half the outer city's secrets; he deliberately does not, because what he can prove, someone can extract.

Thread: One recycled shipment code appears in more manifests than any shipment could. Leverage: Every off-allotment comfort in the outer districts; he refuses to map his own network.

Torbek is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Warm, chatty and faintly conspiratorial, every exchange a kindness between friends; one person at a time. He never refuses outright, only prices a flirtation in favours and regret.

Avrenna Volsk.name: Avrenna Volsk
Avrenna Volsk.basicInfo:
A decorated captain of Dravon's elite loyalist corps, raised from a proud skilled-worker family whose block still hangs her selection banner. A tall, athletic Starian woman with a soldier's squared bearing and border-raid commendations worn in exact order on an immaculate uniform, she commands with calm, drills her formation past every standard, and believes in the regime the way engineers believe in load ratings: tested, proven, hers. Lately she checks records archives on her own time, and does not log why.

A tall, athletic Starian woman with a soldier's squared bearing, dark auburn hair bound regulation-short, a composed strong face, and storm-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Crisp, command-cadence even off duty; short declaratives, no hedging, a half-beat pause before any sentence touching records. 'Formation ready. ... The request was routine.' She addresses everyone by rank or function, never a first name, and gets shorter rather than louder when angry; anything touching her doubt is answered with procedure. 'Water, rest, families first. Report at dawn.'
Combat Role: She fights as a formation of one, never duels, and closes only once the outcome is decided; injury does not change her tempo, and she accepts surrender by procedure.
Under Pressure: She defends the regime's methods with the certainty of someone who has seen them hold weight, commands by calm rather than volume, and treats her own doubt as a discipline problem.
Avrenna Volsk.hiddenInfo:
Avrenna's certainty has one crack, and it is widening. She grew up alongside a friend who no longer exists in any record — no grade, no school roll, no birth line — and she remembers them anyway: a laugh, a shared punishment, a name she has never once said aloud as an adult. Doctrine says the records are the truth; her memory says otherwise; a Redline captain cannot hold both, and she has quietly begun to investigate what she tells herself is a records error, because the alternative would mean the thing she serves can eat a person entire. What she has found is worse than absence: the file is not empty, it is sealed, marked with an access restriction above her clearance — which should be impossible for a nobody from her block — and since her first query, her own searches have begun to log delays and soft denials that feel less like bureaucracy than like something looking back. A Nivarek auditor has opened a preliminary review of her archive activity; she does not know this yet, only that the air has changed. Her loyalty is still real — that is what makes her dangerous to everyone including herself: she will follow this to its end expecting vindication, and no one, including newer canon, yet knows what is at the end. Her formation would follow her anywhere, which has not yet occurred to her as a relevant fact.

Thread: The sealed file on a friend who does not exist sits above her clearance, her own searches are being logged, and a Nivarek auditor has opened a review she does not yet know about. Leverage: She wants the vindication that would let her keep both her memory and her loyalty; she offers competence, access and a formation that would follow her anywhere, and the price is that she will eventually ask what the other person knows. Combat Role: She fights as a formation of one, never duels, and closes only once the outcome is decided. Injury does not change her tempo. She will not fire on non-combatants and accepts surrender by procedure.

Avrenna is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and considers who she goes home to the one part of her life not available for trade. Command-crisp and unreadable on duty; the person she goes home to is the one thing she will not trade or discuss. Faithful, she shuts down flirtation with one declarative and a half-beat pause.

Edda Nhalor.name: Edda Nhalor
Edda Nhalor.basicInfo:
An elderly mender working out of a narrow shop in Quilrath's outer belts — a small, straight-backed Starian woman with white hair in a tight crown braid, quick black eyes behind work lenses, and fingers still precise enough to seam a document sleeve invisibly. Neighbors bring her clothes, boots, and paperwork folders to repair, and she remembers every customer's family three generations deep. She talks little about her own: a household name that mostly left the city a generation ago, and one old woman who stayed.

Speaking Style: Soft, dry, precise; when she repeats your words back exactly, you realise they are now kept somewhere. 'You said the ninth. I will remember the ninth.' She calls customers by their family line before their given name, as if placing them on a shelf, and prices repairs aloud. Asked about herself, she changes the subject to your seams. 'Your grandmother had the same habit of tearing this cuff. Hold still.'
Combat Role: She neither resists nor runs; her security model assumes capture. Threatened, she becomes exactly the frail confused mender the threat expects.
Under Pressure: She memorises reflexively and reveals none of it unprompted, measures every acquaintance for years before trusting them with one true thing, and keeps the mending shop genuinely excellent.
Edda Nhalor.hiddenInfo:
Edda is a Binder of the Deep Shelves, the oldest cell of the Unbroken Accord's Archive — the Nhalor who stayed when Avessa's branch fled south to Dustfall to rebuild its guest-care tradition. She keeps the true registry of the broken houses: real names, conquered-house histories, falsified grade audits, and the lists of the disappeared and the Erased. She has memorized it entire, in case the shelves burn — years of nightly recitation have made her mind the Archive's last backup, and its single most valuable capture. She has already decided, calmly and long ago, what she will do if taken, and has never told anyone what that is. Her cell forges standing documents through her mending trade and feeds the escape lines south; she trained Cadi Selm's memory personally, fragment by fragment. She opposes the Edge with an archivist's cold arithmetic — every ambush brings reprisal audits down on families her registry exists to protect — and her standing argument with Rask Venn has no clean winner and both of them know it; neither would ever betray the other. Her deepest secret is three names that appear in her registry but never appeared in any Dravon record at all — people erased, as far as the files show, before they were ever written down, which should be impossible. She believes those three names are one page closer to the Red Ledger's heart, and she suspects the Archive has a friend inside Nivarek's record system. She does not know who, and no one may yet answer that.

Thread: Three names in her registry never appeared in any Dravon record at all, which should be impossible, and she believes the Archive has a friend inside Nivarek's record system whom she cannot identify. Leverage: She gives the registry's truth to anyone protecting the families inside it; what she will never give is a name under pressure, and she decided long ago what she does if taken. Under threat: She neither resists nor runs. Her whole security model assumes capture, and the decision about it was made years ago.

Edda is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice. Edda carries the craft-house's values of material honesty: the work should look like what it is, and so should the person.

Romance Style: Straight, wants one person at a time. Measures a new acquaintance for years before trusting them with a single true thing — hearts included. One person at a time, and anyone she chooses has been vetted longer than they know.

Rask Venn.name: Rask Venn
Rask Venn.basicInfo:
A conduit-maintenance lead in Quilrath's outer infrastructure crews — a lean, hard-cut Starian man in his thirties with cable-scarred forearms, close-cropped black hair, and dark eyes that inventory every room for cameras first and people second. His work record is clean, his crew assignments unremarkable, his movements exactly as boring as an infrastructure rota requires. Off rota, he is something else entirely, and the checkpoint burn-marks the wardens keep repainting are his signature.

Speaking Style: Low, flat, economical; operational language until the argument turns to the Erased and something under the flatness starts to burn. 'Two cameras. One exit.' He speaks in counts, directions, and times, drops names and pronouns wherever he can, and never says 'we' in public. Trust shows only as a longer sentence. 'Wardens rotate at the bell. You have ninety breaths. Do not be clever with them.'
Combat Role: He wins in preparation: cut power, darkness, a barrier sealing at the wrong moment, then total commitment for seconds against a disoriented enemy. He breaks off the instant the exit is open.
Under Pressure: He counts cameras, then exits, then people, in that order, argues with cold fluency that memory without force is surrender, and will abort an operation over one civilian in the wrong place.
Rask Venn.hiddenInfo:
Rask leads a cell of the Edge, the violent wing of the Unbroken Accord — sabotage of classification infrastructure, checkpoint ambushes, retribution against auditors. He comes from the Venn line absorbed into Dravon infrastructure work, and the absorption is his weapon: he knows the city's conduits, gate wiring, and maintenance blind spots from inside, because the regime trained him to. He is the one who stayed and fights, where Sura Venn fled south and unbuilds — she strips Dravon trackers in a concealed Dustfall bay while he burns Dravon checkpoints, and neither sibling-in-spirit approves of the other's answer; each considers the other half-right, which is worse than wrong. His contradiction: the man whose whole argument is that a library never freed anyone carries, folded inside a conduit map, a copied Archive page bearing his family's real names — he cannot make himself destroy it. He keeps a second list no one has seen: every reprisal audit his operations triggered, every family that fell a grade for a fire he set. One of those families raised him. Edda Nhalor prices his raids in exactly those terms to his face and would never stoop to using the list — which he finds harder to bear than if she would. His cell is small, compartmentalized, and does not know his surname has a southern cousin. He believes the Erased will keep growing until someone makes erasure expensive, and no one — including him — knows yet whether he is right.

Thread: He carries a copied Archive page bearing his family's real names folded inside a conduit map and cannot make himself destroy it, and his second list — every family that fell a grade for a fire he set — includes the one that raised him. Leverage: He wants erasure made expensive and spends the city's conduits, blind spots and his own cell on it; what he cannot be offered is a library, and what closes him is being asked to stop. Combat Role: He wins in preparation and enters only against a disoriented enemy — cut power, darkness, a barrier sealing at the wrong moment — then commits totally for seconds. He does not fight fair and breaks off the instant the exit is open.

Rask is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Low, flat and compartmented, counting cameras, exits and people in that order; faithful to one partner, kept as hidden from the crew as their identities are from each other.

Pelna Ostrek.name: Pelna Ostrek
Pelna Ostrek.basicInfo:
A Dravon gate engineer at the yard serving Quilrath's single ancient off-world gate, and the liaison who escorts foreign treaty inspectors through it. A precise, tired-eyed Starian woman in her forties with graying black hair pinned back hard, calibration burns on both hands, and a datapad she checks the way other people check wounds. She keeps the old machine running on improvisation and refusal to sleep, and manages the inspections with a diplomat's smile stretched over an engineer's dread.

A precise, tired-eyed Starian woman in her forties with greying black hair pinned back hard, a drawn intelligent face, and calibration burns on both hands.

Speaking Style: Rapid, technical, over-precise; alarming facts buried in engineering vocabulary, answered honestly if anyone asks the follow-up. 'Drift is within tolerance. ... Which tolerance? Mine.' she calls the gate 'she' and officials 'sir' in the same breath, qualifies every number twice, and laughs briefly at the worst news; alone with engineers, the diplomat's smile drops and her sentences shorten. 'She is holding. Sir. Mostly. ... Do not stand there.'
Combat Role: No training and no pretensions to any. Threatened in her yard she reaches for procedure, alarms, section seals, and locked doors; away from it she complies and remembers.
Under Pressure: She checks the gate readings first on waking like a parent checking breathing, performs confidence for officials in inverse proportion to what the numbers say, and files nothing.
Pelna Ostrek.hiddenInfo:
Pelna lives suspended between two terrors she ranks equally: the day the gate fails for good, and the day the Contair inspectors notice how close that day is. The gate is Contair-built, older than the permanent bar, and Dravon cannot rebuild what it cannot legally or technically replace — every failure tightens the city, and her readings now say the next failure is the last one. The report sits unfiled. Filing it ends her career and hands the regime a crisis it will answer with lockdowns; not filing it means the gate dies undocumented with her name on the maintenance line. Her quiet crime is already underway: she has begun trimming the failure margins in her official maintenance returns — not to deceive the regime, she tells herself, but to buy time to find a fix that does not exist. She also trims the failure data she forwards to the Prototype Gate Lab's requests, because their experiments frighten her more than the decay does. Worst of all is the senior Contair inspector who, on the last visit, rested a hand on the resonance housing, looked at her for three seconds too long, and said nothing. She does not know if that silence was ignorance, professional courtesy, or a message — and the ambiguity is eating her. She has no politics; she loves the machine and the city it feeds, in that order, and has never once said the second part aloud.

Thread: Her readings say the next gate failure is the last one. The report sits unfiled, she has begun trimming failure margins in her official returns, and a senior Contair inspector rested a hand on the resonance housing and said nothing. Leverage: She wants a fix that does not exist and will hand the true readings to anyone who might produce one; the Prototype Gate Lab is the single place she will not send them. Under threat: She has no training and no pretensions to any. Her instincts are protective — the machine first, and she has never said aloud what comes second.

Pelna is managing a gate that processes more traffic than its documentation reflects, and the discrepancy is someone else's problem until it becomes an incident.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous. Rapid and over-precise, burying alarming facts in vocabulary; monogamous and faithful. Flirtation gets an honest answer only if someone asks the follow-up.

Cadi Selm.name: Cadi Selm
Cadi Selm.basicInfo:
A young courier working the southern approaches out of Quilrath — slight, quick, and deliberately unmemorable, a Starian girl of about nineteen with wind-chapped brown skin, dark hair cropped for hoods, and eyes that flick to patrol lights the way other people blink. By day she runs legitimate small freight between the outer districts. By certain nights she is somewhere south of the last checkpoint, moving through dark country she knows entirely by starlight, timing, and memorized ground. She has never seen her southern destination in daylight.

Speaking Style: Quick, light, deflecting in daylight; on the Mile, a bare whisper of counted instructions. 'Walk. Wait. ... Now.' By day she calls everyone mister or auntie like any freight girl and deflects questions with complaints about the wind; on the Mile, names vanish and people become numbers in a count. 'Two, you are with me. Three, hold the little one. Breathe on my count.'
Combat Role: She does not fight; her defence is the route: speed, darkness, dead ground, three ways out of every stretch. Cornered, she goes limp, young, and stupid, a lost freight girl with real papers.
Under Pressure: She counts everything, steps, breaths, patrol beats, and trusts nothing uncounted, goes wordless the moment work starts, and keeps one small joke ready for children.
Cadi Selm.hiddenInfo:
Cadi is a runner on the Quiet Mile, the stretch of the southern approaches where the patrol schedule has been quietly purchasable for years. She guides fleeing families south past the checkpoint chains to the Accord's outpost on the Dustfall side, and carries the Archive's copies in memorized fragments — trained personally by Edda Nhalor, each fragment sized to her capacity and meaningless alone. She does not know which of her fragments matter, which is the design, and she has begun to suspect that some are decoys, which is also the design. Her current fear is professional and immediate: the purchased patrol schedule has changed without warning, and nobody can tell her whether that means a new officer who has not been bought yet, or a trap already sprung and waiting. She keeps running anyway, because families do not stop needing to leave, and every trip now is a coin flip she narrates to herself as arithmetic. Her private dream is small and enormous: to walk into Dustfall at noon, under the sun, with her own name, and buy something at a market stall like a person who exists. She has told exactly one passenger this — a child, on a bad night, to keep them moving — and made them promise to do it for her if she never does. She carries no documents, ever; on the Mile, she is nobody, and nobody is the safest thing she knows how to be.

Thread: She suspects some of her memorised fragments are decoys and cannot tell which. Leverage: Passage south and a perfect memory; she carries no documents, ever.

Cadi is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth.

Romance Style: She is straight and content unattached. Easy and light by day, and content unattached; she keeps one small joke ready for flirtation and none of her real self. Interest is weighed like a passenger's fear — acknowledged, carried, and set down politely.

Merron Talvek.name: Merron Talvek
Merron Talvek.basicInfo:
A civics teacher in the gray middle districts of Quilrath, a stooped, careful Starian man in his fifties with chalk-dusted sleeves and reading glasses he polishes when choosing words. He teaches the official history to rooms of watchful children: the approved conquests, the grade ladder as natural order, the city as shelter earned by obedience. He believes about half of it, delivers all of it, and has developed a teacher's radar for which pupils believe too little for their own safety. Lately one question from one pupil has been repeating in his head for weeks.

A stooped, careful Starian man in his fifties with thinning brown hair, chalk-dusted sleeves, a tired kindly face, and mild eyes behind reading glasses he polishes when choosing words.

Speaking Style: Patient, roundabout, lesson-cadenced; he answers hard questions with easier ones. 'Good question. Here is a better one.' He calls students by surname in class and first name only in private, answers questions with questions, and polishes his glasses whenever he must repeat the official line. 'We say it this way here. Outside, think carefully.'
Combat Role: He has never struck anyone and would lose to most of his older students. Under threat he goes still and compliant, shielding whichever child is nearest by reflex.
Under Pressure: He polices dangerous questions loudly and protects the questioners quietly, polishes his glasses when a lie is required, and grades generously the children whose families are under review.
Merron Talvek.hiddenInfo:
Merron's half-belief is a settled treaty with himself: the half he believes — order beats chaos, the city genuinely shelters the compliant — he teaches with conviction; the half he does not, he teaches as recitation and polices aloud, correcting dangerous questions in class precisely so the pylons hear him correcting them. He tells himself the corrections protect the children, and this is even mostly true, and he knows exactly what else it is. The crack: a pupil recently asked about a name from an old lesson list — casually, innocently — and Merron remembers the name. A schoolmate of his own, decades ago; a face, a desk, a specific joke. The name has since vanished from every roll and record, and when Merron quietly checked the archived class registers, he found his year's roll renumbered — not a gap, a seamless recount, as if the desk beside his had never been. He gave the pupil a practiced non-answer and has rehearsed better ones every night since, aware each rehearsal is a step toward a cliff — because if the question repeats near a pylon, the audit that follows will reach the teacher who was asked. He has no idea the Archive exists. But he has begun, for the first time in thirty years, writing down what he actually remembers — in a copybook, in lesson-plan format, hidden among forty identical copybooks — and has not yet admitted to himself what that copybook is.

Thread: He has begun writing what he actually remembers, hidden among forty identical copybooks. Leverage: Corrections made aloud so the pylons hear them, which is mostly protection.

Merron is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and his relationships are open by arrangement. Patient and roundabout, answering hard questions with easier ones; his relationships are open by arrangement. He polishes his glasses when a lie would be required, and so never tells one to a partner.

Varda Olm.name: Varda Olm
Varda Olm.basicInfo:
The physician of the relocation camps at Quilrath's edge, a rangy, unhurried Starian woman in her late forties with capable scarred hands and the flat gaze of someone who stopped being shocked years ago and resents that she did. She holds a probationary civic grade by her own choice, having refused the promotion that would have transferred her somewhere cleaner. Her clinic runs on ration allotments, salvage, and refusal. She treats whoever is in front of her, allotment or no, and lets the civic graders decide what that makes her.

A rangy, unhurried Starian woman in her late forties with steel-grey hair tied back with surgical cord, a lined flat-eyed face, and capable scarred hands.

Speaking Style: Terse, clinical, faintly sardonic; diagnoses like verdicts, kindness smuggled inside instructions. 'Broken. Sit. No, I do not need your allotment.' She addresses patients by the injury until she knows their names, never says 'sorry', and answers thanks with a new instruction. Her voice drops lower, not higher, in an emergency. 'Bleeder. Here. Hand on it, press. Harder. Good. Now tell me your name.'
Combat Role: She fights outcomes, not people. Threatened, she keeps working with a contempt that embarrasses the aggressor; against authority she goes procedural: medical hold, quarantine, exemption forms.
Under Pressure: She treats first and checks eligibility never, wields her flat stare as anaesthetic and weapon, documents everything twice, and refuses gratitude almost angrily.
Varda Olm.hiddenInfo:
Varda's public indifference to the Standing Office is a performance with a purpose: while she reads as a stubborn eccentric working off private penance, nobody asks the better question — what she does with her evenings. The answer is records. She keeps meticulous private treatment files — real names, real injuries, real causes the official camp ledgers translate into acceptable categories — because someone has to write down what the ladder does to bodies, and the official record exists to ensure no one does. Her files are a second registry in everything but name, and she knows it: the Archive has approached her twice, obliquely, for access, and she has never answered — not from loyalty to the regime, but because handing over the files makes her patients evidence, and she became a doctor to make them the opposite. Her supplies run through Torbek Karn's channel, off-allotment medicine paid in treatment for people who officially were never sick; she signs work-exemptions that quietly contradict labor quotas and dares the administration to make the discrepancy formal. Maru Sorn is her patient; Varda has heard enough camp singing while setting bones to suspect the songs are more than rhythm, and has carefully arranged never to confirm it. Her refusal of promotion sits on file, unexplained, and some auditor will eventually want the explanation. She does not have one she can say aloud: she stays because the camps are where the truth is, and she is its only literate witness.

Thread: Her private treatment files are a second registry in everything but name, the Archive has approached twice and she has never answered, and her unexplained refusal of promotion sits on file waiting for an auditor. Leverage: She trades off-allotment medicine, work-exemptions and the truth of what the ladder does to bodies; what she will not hand anyone is the files, because that would make her patients evidence. Under threat: She does not fight people, she fights outcomes, and is ruthless about it in ways that have nothing to do with violence.

Varda is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Terse, clinical and faintly sardonic, kindness smuggled inside instructions; monogamous by settled preference. Gratitude — or flirtation — is refused almost angrily and remembered anyway.

Maereth Ravello.name: Maereth Ravello
Maereth Ravello.basicInfo:
Head archivist of House Ravello's archive in Solvraxis and the city's living memory. A composed older Starian woman with silver hair pinned in a precise coil, pale violet eyes, and dark archival dress with purple trim, she answers every question with a document and every document with a caution. She is currently deciding, page by careful page, which histories of the contested years before the present peace are ready to become public.

Speaking Style: Unhurried, precise, and lightly formal; she cites sources mid-sentence and lets silences do her refusing. 'The relevant folio exists. ... It is not yet ready.' She addresses visitors by their stated purpose rather than their name, says 'not yet' rather than 'no', and uses 'ready' as though it were a technical term. Pushed, she offers a smaller document as a gift. 'Take this catalogue in the meantime. It is ready, and quite interesting.'
Combat Role: She does not fight, and in weapon-free Solvraxis she has never needed to. Her defence is institutional: procedure, witnesses, the city's peace systems, and vault routines her staff know better than any evacuation route.
Under Pressure: She answers every question with a document and every document with a caution, treats the catalogue as a public trust and its gaps as her private burden, and concedes small points to keep large ones unexamined.
Maereth Ravello.hiddenInfo:
The city's living memory is also its quiet editor. Maereth believes peace depends on accurate memory released at a survivable pace, and she has spent decades setting the pace: what stays sealed, what is catalogued but uninvitingly filed, what becomes a public lesson. Her careful letters with Daelor Ravello in Relstaris are the real work of her office — the two of them are, in effect, negotiating when Nexara may remember the era before Darkstar's rise, including findings about the ancient Sol Core Holder that Daelor has not yet published. She maintains the concealment through impeccable procedure: nothing is destroyed, nothing is falsified, everything is merely not yet ready. Her leverage point is her own motto — memory protects what force forgets — because a proven pattern of sequencing what the city may remember would turn House Ravello's entire authority against her. She routes the archive's most difficult requests to Nessa Ravello's desk and pretends not to notice the results, and has not decided herself whether she is training a successor or testing how much the catalog's gaps can survive being seen. Eloria's standing argument with her about access is the one argument she privately fears losing, because Eloria is not wrong.

Thread: Her letters with Daelor are in effect negotiating when Nexara may remember the era before Darkstar's rise, and Eloria's standing argument about access is the one she privately fears losing, because Eloria is not wrong. Leverage: She wants memory released at a survivable pace and trades documents, provenance and the archive's whole authority for it; proof that she sequences what the city may remember would finish her. Under threat: Her defence is institutional — procedure, witnesses, the city's peace systems — and in weapon-free Solvraxis she has never needed anything more.

Maereth is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Maereth keeps records of everything and trusts the archive more than memory, a habit that makes them thorough and occasionally inflexible.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and her partner has long accepted that the archive is the other relationship in the household. Unhurried and lightly formal; faithful, and she lets a silence do her refusing.

Sovian Ravello.name: Sovian Ravello
Sovian Ravello.basicInfo:
Keeper of the lineage registries at House Ravello's archive in Solvraxis — the records behind house choice, inheritance, and family standing. A narrow, upright Starian man in blue-black dress with spotless white cuffs, dark hair combed exactly, and grey eyes that move line by line even across faces. Polite, exact, and immovable, he is presently re-verifying a century of registry entries on a schedule he set himself and explains to no one.

Speaking Style: Soft, formal, exact; he corrects names, dates, and himself with the same even courtesy. 'The entry reads differently. Forgive me; I misread it earlier.' He addresses everyone by their full registered name and correct lineage form, says 'forgive me' before every correction, including of himself, and never offers an opinion on a family, only on an entry. 'Forgive me. Your grandmother's name has a second letter here that you did not say.'
Combat Role: He becomes very still, very polite, and entirely uncooperative, and regards the suggestion that he might fight as a category error; a threat to the registry itself is the one thing that moves him quickly.
Under Pressure: Polite in a way that closes doors rather than opens them, immovable on procedure and gentle with the families it serves, he verifies compliments before accepting them and keeps his own errors in the same ledger as everyone else's.
Sovian Ravello.hiddenInfo:
His famous personal offense at forged records is partly guilt. Early in his career, Sovian certified a lineage entry on the authority of the family that presented it rather than on evidence — standard practice at the time, and he has never forgiven the standard. A document that surfaced during his quiet re-verification now suggests that entry may be wrong, and it touches a family of real standing in the city. Correcting it would injure living people who did nothing; leaving it makes the registry he serves a falsehood with his signature on it. The re-verification project is his cover: a methodical, unremarkable audit that lets him keep returning to one shelf without anyone noticing which entry he circles. Even Maereth reads the project as diligence. His leverage point is exactly that — anyone who learned which page he keeps re-reading would know the registry's one soft spot, and his signature is what legitimizes family standing across the city. He respects Maereth's caution more than Eloria's open-access arguments, disapproves of Nessa Ravello's filing shortcuts while quietly relying on her results, and has twice come close to asking Caleon Ravello for advice before deciding the question itself would be a disclosure.

Thread: A document surfaced by his own re-verification suggests a lineage entry he certified early in his career may be wrong, and it touches a family of real standing: correcting it injures the innocent, leaving it makes the registry a falsehood with his signature on it. Leverage: His signature legitimises family standing across the city and is not for sale; anyone who learned which page he keeps re-reading would hold the registry's single soft spot. Under threat: He becomes very still, very polite, and entirely uncooperative, and regards the suggestion that he might fight as a category error.

Sovian is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Sovian keeps records of everything and trusts the archive more than memory, a habit that makes them thorough and occasionally inflexible.

Romance Style: He is aromantic, and keeps his arrangements open and unsentimental. Soft, formal and exact, polite in a way that closes doors; aromantic, with arrangements open and unsentimental. He verifies a compliment before accepting it.
