Keep one airborne opponent climbing, turning and recovering, never letting them settle, until they tire before you do. It lasts only as long as your own flight endurance, and a patient opponent who lands refuses it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Open Sky Dominion.name: Open Sky Dominion
Open Sky Dominion.description:
Own a stretch of open sky against several fliers at once, reading every approach and taking each opponent at the angle that favours you. This is the Aevon tradition at its height and may be named as such. It ends where the open sky ends; bring it to ground and it is gone.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Old Form Root.name: Old Form Root
Old Form Root.description: Set a stance that resists being pushed, pulled or rushed off the spot you chose. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Old Form Exchange.name: Old Form Exchange
Old Form Exchange.description:
Trade blows from the rooted stance with one opponent who comes to you, answering each strike from position. It does nothing against someone who will not engage, and staying rooted means staying reachable.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Refuse the Push.name: Refuse the Push
Refuse the Push.description:
Take one shove, charge or throw attempt and stay where you stood. The force is still felt, and a large enough force still moves you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Losing Correctly.name: Losing Correctly
Losing Correctly.description:
Concede an exchange or a bout in the Orvantis way: yield what is already lost while keeping footing, guard and standing, so the loss costs no more than it must. It is a way to lose well, not a way to win.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Unmoved Root.name: Unmoved Root
Unmoved Root.description:
Hold ground against sustained pressure from one opponent so that nothing they do moves you from the spot. This is body and training, not an affinity; the root holds while stamina does.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Old Form Mastery.name: Old Form Mastery
Old Form Mastery.description:
Fight in the complete Old Forms, meeting every approach from a root that cannot be hurried and turning each attacker's commitment into a trade on your ground. This is the Orvantis tradition and may be named as such. A mobile opponent who never commits can still leave it waiting.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Measured Exchange.name: Measured Exchange
Measured Exchange.description: Open with a controlled probing exchange to learn how one opponent answers pressure. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Probe and Record.name: Probe and Record
Probe and Record.description:
Spend the first exchanges of a fight testing one opponent's guard, reach and timing, and carry what you learned into the next exchange. It learns only what the opponent actually shows.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Correction.name: Correction
Correction.description:
After losing an exchange, adjust the one thing that lost it before the next. It fixes a mistake; it does not guarantee the next exchange.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Method Review.name: Method Review
Method Review.description:
Against an opponent you have fought or studied before, begin the fight already adjusted to what they did last time. If they have changed since, the review works against you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Model the Opponent.name: Model the Opponent
Model the Opponent.description:
Build a working model of one opponent's pattern mid-fight and fight to it, closing the options they rely on. A truly unpredictable opponent breaks the model.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Outdated Data.name: Outdated Data
Outdated Data.description:
Fight a known opponent from the record so completely that every habit they carry becomes a liability. This is the Zelvaris Method at its height and may be named as such. The same weakness runs both ways: anyone who knows your record can do it to you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Draw What Works.name: Draw What Works
Draw What Works.description: Choose between the weapon you actually carry for range and the one for close work, and use the right one for the distance in front of you. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Distance Then Close.name: Distance Then Close
Distance Then Close.description:
Hold one opponent at range with a carried firearm, then switch to a carried blade as they close, without a gap in between. Both weapons must actually be on you, and the switch still takes a heartbeat.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Quiet Blade.name: Quiet Blade
Quiet Blade.description:
End a close encounter with a carried blade instead of a shot, when noise would bring more trouble. It trades range and safety for silence.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Hold the Perimeter.name: Hold the Perimeter
Hold the Perimeter.description:
Take a covered position on a perimeter and keep one approach closed against people coming at it. It covers one approach, from real cover, with real ammunition.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

People Behind You.name: People Behind You
People Behind You.description:
Fight a small group while keeping the civilians behind you out of their reach, choosing every shot and cut by where those people stand. It protects by position, not by magic; a threat you cannot see gets through.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Whole Kit.name: Whole Kit
Whole Kit.description:
Fight with everything you carry as one system: firearm, blade, cover and armor chosen for the fight in front of you, switching without hesitation. This is the Sol frontier practice at its height and may be named as such. It is only as good as the kit actually on you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Instrument Guard.name: Instrument Guard
Instrument Guard.description: Deflect an attack while keeping a held tool, device or instrument safe and working. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Ward Protocol.name: Ward Protocol
Ward Protocol.description:
Put yourself and any drone you actually control between a threat and the person or equipment you are protecting, preferring restraint to injury. It protects; it does not win the fight.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Tool Transition.name: Tool Transition
Tool Transition.description:
Turn the tool already in your hand into a guard or a strike without dropping it or losing your place in the work.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Fallback Protocol.name: Fallback Protocol
Fallback Protocol.description:
When communication fails, act on the protocol you and your allies agreed in advance, so they know exactly where you are and what you will do. It needs a real, prior agreement.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Aegis Spacing.name: Aegis Spacing
Aegis Spacing.description:
Keep yourself, your allies and any drones you control at formation spacing so no attacker can isolate one of you. One unit is vulnerable; the spacing is the defense.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Formation Is the System.name: Formation Is the System
Formation Is the System.description:
Run your owned drones and trained allies as one defensive formation, each covering another, so the whole holds where any single part would fail. This is Contair doctrine and may be named as such. It needs the actual drones and people; without them there is only your own guard.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Patient Guard.name: Patient Guard
Patient Guard.description: Hold a tight guard and absorb pressure without committing, waiting for an opening. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Let Them Spend.name: Let Them Spend
Let Them Spend.description:
Absorb one opponent's committed attack sequence until they overextend, then answer once. It costs you every blow you absorb along the way.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Know the Terms.name: Know the Terms
Know the Terms.description:
Before an arranged bout, learn its exact rules and stopping conditions, and fight precisely within them. It applies only to agreed bouts with stated terms.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Attrition Stance.name: Attrition Stance
Attrition Stance.description:
Hold a defensive stance through a long exchange so the opponent tires before you do. Stamina decides it, and a stronger opponent can simply break the guard.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Technically Permitted.name: Technically Permitted
Technically Permitted.description:
In an arranged bout, turn the rules themselves into your advantage: ring, time and stoppage conditions used exactly as written. It never breaks a rule, and a judge can still rule against you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

The Long Game.name: The Long Game
The Long Game.description:
Win a fight on your own timeline: absorb, wait, let the rules and the clock work, and finish only when the opponent has spent themselves. This is the Caelthorn stance at its height and may be named as such. An opponent who never overextends turns it into a draw.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Clinical Weave.name: Clinical Weave
Clinical Weave.description: Slip an attack with minimal movement while staying calm enough to keep working. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Reach the Wounded.name: Reach the Wounded
Reach the Wounded.description:
Move through an active fight to one injured person, avoiding the blows in between. It gets you there; it does not stop the fight.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Slip the Grab.name: Slip the Grab
Slip the Grab.description:
Break or avoid one attempt to seize or hold you. A strong enough grip still holds.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Weave and Stabilize.name: Weave and Stabilize
Weave and Stabilize.description:
Keep one injured person stable with your hands while evading the attacks that come at you both. Real treatment still needs real supplies and time.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Nobody Else Falls.name: Nobody Else Falls
Nobody Else Falls.description:
Read the fight around a casualty and keep moving between them and each new threat. It protects by position; a threat that gets past you still lands.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Triage Under Fire.name: Triage Under Fire
Triage Under Fire.description:
Move through a whole fight, triaging and stabilizing the wounded while nobody lands a clean blow on you. This is the Myralis weave at its height and may be named as such. It saves people, not the situation.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Partner Cover.name: Partner Cover
Partner Cover.description: Cover one willing partner's open side while they act. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Call and Answer.name: Call and Answer
Call and Answer.description:
Coordinate one exchange with a partner through a spoken or signalled call, so you act together rather than separately. It needs a partner who knows the call.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Crowd Lane.name: Crowd Lane
Crowd Lane.description:
Open a path through a crowd for someone who needs to get through, without harming anyone in it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Market Discipline.name: Market Discipline
Market Discipline.description:
Keep a small group together and moving through a busy, dangerous space. It keeps them together; it does not fight for them.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Chain of Hands.name: Chain of Hands
Chain of Hands.description:
Direct a small group of allies or civilians through a fight, each covering the next. It depends on their actual willingness and ability to follow.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Everyone Home.name: Everyone Home
Everyone Home.description:
Bring a whole group out of a fight together, no one left behind, the drill carrying them where no single fighter could. This is the cooperation drill at its height and may be named as such. It protects a group; it does not defeat an enemy.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Committed Blow.name: Committed Blow
Committed Blow.description: Put your whole weight behind one strike or one swing of a heavy weapon. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Guard Crusher.name: Guard Crusher
Guard Crusher.description:
Drive one heavy blow through an opponent's guard by force. It breaks a guard, not an armored body, and a dodge makes it a wasted swing.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Heavy Swing.name: Heavy Swing
Heavy Swing.description:
Swing an actually held heavy weapon with control rather than momentum alone.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Showstopper.name: Showstopper
Showstopper.description:
Land one decisive blow in front of an audience at the moment it will be remembered. The blow is real; the crowd's reaction is its own thing.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Unreadable Windup.name: Unreadable Windup
Unreadable Windup.description:
Disguise a heavy blow so the opponent cannot read when or where it is coming. It hides the timing, not the commitment; a missed blow still leaves you open.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Impossible Finish.name: Impossible Finish
Impossible Finish.description:
End a fight you should have lost with one decisive blow into the opponent's one real weakness at the one moment it shows. This is power striking at its height and may be named as such. It needs a real weakness and a real moment; without them it is only a big swing.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Opening Move.name: Opening Move
Opening Move.description: Strike first from actual concealment before the target knows you are there. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Wait for It.name: Wait for It
Wait for It.description:
Hold concealment until the one moment a target is least ready, then act. Patience can be spent; if the moment never comes, neither does the strike.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Quiet Approach.name: Quiet Approach
Quiet Approach.description:
Close on a target without being noticed across ground you can actually use.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Choose the Ground.name: Choose the Ground
Choose the Ground.description:
Pick and prepare the place where a fight will happen before it does. It needs time and access to the ground in advance.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Second Ambush.name: Second Ambush
Second Ambush.description:
Break contact in the middle of a fight and vanish into real cover, forcing the opponent to find you again. It needs cover to vanish into.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Never Where Expected.name: Never Where Expected
Never Where Expected.description:
Run a fight as a series of ambushes against several opponents, never where they expect you. This is the ambush practice at its height and may be named as such. In open ground with nowhere to hide, it is gone.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Answer Only.name: Answer Only
Answer Only.description: Meet an attack with a block and a single answering strike, never the first blow. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Patient Counter.name: Patient Counter
Patient Counter.description:
Let one opponent attack until the pattern shows, then counter it cleanly. It waits for the opponent; if they never commit, it never answers.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Parry and Step.name: Parry and Step
Parry and Step.description:
Turn one attack aside and step to the side it leaves open.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Exact Answer.name: Exact Answer
Exact Answer.description:
Answer each attack with exactly as much force as it carried and no more. It keeps a fight from escalating; it does not end it by itself.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Nothing First.name: Nothing First
Nothing First.description:
Read an opponent's intent well enough to be ready for every attack they begin, countering each. It needs them to attack; it has no opening move of its own.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

End It Kindly.name: End It Kindly
End It Kindly.description:
Counter an attack into a hold or a fall that ends the fight without lasting harm. This is the counterstrike method at its height and may be named as such. A lethal or armed attacker still demands a harder answer.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Formation Step.name: Formation Step
Formation Step.description: Keep your place beside willing allies so that none of you is left exposed. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Barrier Line.name: Barrier Line
Barrier Line.description:
Set an actually carried engineered barrier or shield beside an ally's so the two cover each other. It is equipment; it can fail, and it covers only the line it is set on.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Called Terms.name: Called Terms
Called Terms.description:
Call a halt and offer terms mid-fight, loudly and clearly enough that the other side has to answer. It creates a pause; it cannot force acceptance.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Proven Drill.name: Proven Drill
Proven Drill.description:
Run a practised drill with trained allies: advance, hold, rotate, withdraw. It needs allies who know the drill.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Coalition Line.name: Coalition Line
Coalition Line.description:
Build a working line out of mixed allies, whatever their species or training, assigning each the place that suits them. It depends on their willingness to follow.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Accord Formation.name: Accord Formation
Accord Formation.description:
Hold a disciplined formation through a whole engagement, barrier to barrier, rotating the tired and giving no one an opening. This is the Meridian drill at its height and may be named as such. It needs the equipment and the people; without them it is one fighter.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Measured Entry.name: Measured Entry
Measured Entry.description: Enter a doorway or confined space ready to meet whatever is inside. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Augmented Breach.name: Augmented Breach
Augmented Breach.description:
Use augments you actually have to force a door, barrier or grip that would stop an unaugmented body. It is only as strong as the real augment, which can fail or overheat.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Within Tolerance.name: Within Tolerance
Within Tolerance.description:
Push your augments to their tested limit and no further, keeping them working through a fight. It avoids burnout; it adds no strength the augment lacks.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Room Entry.name: Room Entry
Room Entry.description:
Clear one room of immediate threats with trained allies, each taking a side. Bystanders and unknown exits remain real hazards.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Upgrade Read.name: Upgrade Read
Upgrade Read.description:
Read an opponent's visible augments and dated technology and fight to their weaknesses. It reads only what can be seen or known; hidden enhancements stay hidden.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Chosen Body.name: Chosen Body
Chosen Body.description:
Fight with everything your augmented body can actually do, at its limit and in full control. This is the Vanguard practice at its height and may be named as such. The body is what you made it, no more.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Lantern Salute.name: Lantern Salute
Lantern Salute.description: Open a duel with the formal lit signal and guard that declare a challenge. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Warded Parry.name: Warded Parry
Warded Parry.description:
Turn a blow with a ward you inscribed in advance on your blade or guard. The ward was paid for when it was made, decays with use, and can be read or severed by another practitioner.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Signal Feint.name: Signal Feint
Signal Feint.description:
Flash a small inscribed light signal to draw one opponent's eye before the real cut. It costs vitality, and an opponent who knows the trick ignores it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Inscribed Edge.name: Inscribed Edge
Inscribed Edge.description:
Fight with a blade carrying a prepared inscription for one clear effect you actually inscribed. It needs the preparation and the field; in a thin field it fades.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Read the Working.name: Read the Working
Read the Working.description:
Read an opposing practitioner's active workings mid-duel and fence around them. It reads workings, not minds.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Lantern Duel.name: Lantern Duel
Lantern Duel.description:
Fight a complete formal duel in the Lantern tradition, blade and prepared craft as one. This is Lantern signal fencing at its height and may be named as such. Its bill is paid in vitality, and a thin field leaves only the blade.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Whatever's Handy.name: Whatever's Handy
Whatever's Handy.description: Grab the nearest usable object and use it to strike or block. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Cargo Cover.name: Cargo Cover
Cargo Cover.description:
Put crates, carts or freight between you and one opponent, then strike around it. It needs real clutter, and the cover can be knocked over.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Crowd Slip.name: Crowd Slip
Crowd Slip.description:
Slip through a crowd faster than a pursuer can follow. It depends on the crowd, which moves on its own.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Terminus Scrap.name: Terminus Scrap
Terminus Scrap.description:
Keep your footing and your head in a chaotic fight between several parties, hitting whoever is the real threat. It keeps you standing, not unhurt.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Read the Room.name: Read the Room
Read the Room.description:
Spot who in a fight is armed, who is watching and who will join in before they do. It reads what can be seen; a hidden watcher stays hidden.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Gatefall Rules.name: Gatefall Rules
Gatefall Rules.description:
Fight a whole crowded scrap on your terms, using every object, corner and bystander-free gap the place offers. This is dockside brawling at its height and may be named as such. On open, empty ground it has nothing to work with.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Balanced Base.name: Balanced Base
Balanced Base.description: Drop into a low, balanced stance that is hard to knock over. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Heard Before Moving.name: Heard Before Moving
Heard Before Moving.description:
Listen to one opponent's footwork and breath to hear when they will move. It hears sound, not thoughts; in a loud place it fails and can overwhelm you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Low Stance Slip.name: Low Stance Slip
Low Stance Slip.description:
Slip under one attack from the low stance, keeping balance.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Committed Rush.name: Committed Rush
Committed Rush.description:
Once you have committed, close on one opponent and take them into a grapple without hesitation. It commits completely; a wrong read cannot be taken back.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Clan-Web Hold.name: Clan-Web Hold
Clan-Web Hold.description:
Coordinate a hold with trained clanmates so one opponent is held from several sides. It needs the clanmates.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Binding Once Heard.name: Binding Once Heard
Binding Once Heard.description:
Take and hold an opponent so completely that the fight is over, without lasting harm. This is the Clanmoot rush at its height and may be named as such. A lethal attacker or a deafening place still changes everything.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Close Cut.name: Close Cut
Close Cut.description: Make one precise short-blade cut with fine control. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Inside the Reach.name: Inside the Reach
Inside the Reach.description:
Slip inside a larger opponent's reach where their size works against them. Getting in is dangerous; one solid hit still costs a light frame dearly.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Compact Turn.name: Compact Turn
Compact Turn.description:
Turn and reposition in a tight space where a larger fighter cannot.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Lattice Movement.name: Lattice Movement
Lattice Movement.description:
Fight through dense, cluttered, many-levelled city space, using every ledge and gap. It needs a space built that way.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Fine Point.name: Fine Point
Fine Point.description:
Place a blade exactly where a strap, grip or joint gives way. Precision, not power; armor still stops it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Fellowship Dance.name: Fellowship Dance
Fellowship Dance.description:
Fight in the full dance, precise and never where a larger opponent expects, or paired with a fellowship partner who knows the steps. This is the Rivani blade dance at its height and may be named as such. Reach and mass still belong to the other side.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Compress and Absorb.name: Compress and Absorb
Compress and Absorb.description: Compress to take the force of one blow across the body instead of at one point. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Interlock Guard.name: Interlock Guard
Interlock Guard.description:
Interlock your guard with one consenting ally so each covers the other, without merging. It needs their consent and a planned position.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Reshape Around.name: Reshape Around
Reshape Around.description:
Reshape slightly to slip one grab or strike. Limited reshaping only; it costs hydration and recovery.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Planned Defense.name: Planned Defense
Planned Defense.description:
Fight a defense planned in advance for this place and these threats. It holds against what was planned for; the unplanned finds it slower.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

The Pattern Holds.name: The Pattern Holds
The Pattern Holds.description:
Keep your shape and dignity against an opponent trying to force contact or break your form. It resists; a strong enough force still harms.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Assembly Interlock.name: Assembly Interlock
Assembly Interlock.description:
Hold a planned interlocked defense with several consenting allies, each covering another. This is the interlock defense at its height and may be named as such. It never merges, and it does not improvise well.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Pre-Decided Answer.name: Pre-Decided Answer
Pre-Decided Answer.description: Act at once on the answer you decided in advance for exactly this kind of threat. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Second Layer.name: Second Layer
Second Layer.description:
Fall back to the backup protection you actually carry when the first fails. Two layers, not invulnerability; both can still fail.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Structure Use.name: Structure Use
Structure Use.description:
Use corners, bulkheads, hatches and structure to set the range of a fight. It needs a built space.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Layered Defense.name: Layered Defense
Layered Defense.description:
Arrange your equipment, drones and position into several independent layers of defense. It needs the equipment and time to set it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Threat Model.name: Threat Model
Threat Model.description:
Fight to a threat model built from what you know of this opponent and place. It is planning, not foresight; what you did not model surprises you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Redundancy Is Morality.name: Redundancy Is Morality
Redundancy Is Morality.description:
Fight with every layer you carry, each covering the failure of another, so no single failure ends you. This is Zencadian hull combat at its height and may be named as such. Strip the equipment and a tall, clever, fragile person remains.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Field-Sense Step.name: Field-Sense Step
Field-Sense Step.description: Read a shift in the ambient field as a body moves, and step before the blow lands. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Flowing Evasion.name: Flowing Evasion
Flowing Evasion.description:
Flow around one opponent's sequence of attacks through field-sense and movement. It reads the field, not intent; a still, patient opponent gives little to read.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Core Economy.name: Core Economy
Core Economy.description:
Fight without spending the core on anything that does not matter, keeping reserves for when it does.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Channel-Lit Counter.name: Channel-Lit Counter
Channel-Lit Counter.description:
Answer an attack with a counter carried by a brief, disciplined flare of embodiment. It drains the core, and the light shows.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Blaze Drill.name: Blaze Drill
Blaze Drill.description:
Fight in the small, disciplined Blaze manner with trained companions, each covering another. It needs the companions and the discipline.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

The Channeled Storm.name: The Channeled Storm
The Channeled Storm.description:
Fight at the full intensity a being of living energy can sustain, flowing and answering without a wasted spark. This is responsive flow at its height and may be named as such. It spends the core fast; overuse fractures it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Obsidian Redirection.name: Obsidian Redirection
Obsidian Redirection.description:
Yield ground to one charging opponent and turn their momentum into a fall, a stumble or a step into the line's guard, as Redline officers are drilled in the Inner Obsidian Yard. It takes the energy they bring; an opponent who does not commit gives it nothing to turn, and it is not Kaldor's Dominion Pressure.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Random.name: Random
Random.description:
🎲 Anywhere

Chance picks the city and the corner. You bring the reason. An ordinary Nexaran day starts wherever you land.
★ Pairs with the Open Life mode
Random.storyStart:
Generate a story start appropriate to the player's chosen traits. Draw on world lore to create a specific situation in a concrete location. The opening should present clear immediate circumstances while leaving many possible paths forward. Incorporate aspects of the character's background without forcing them into a predetermined narrative.

ANCHOR: Open on the first thing the player's hands or ears register in the chosen area, before any person. First voice: someone stationed in that area, with a reason to be speaking. Line: “You have the look of someone deciding whether to stay. Take a minute; the place is not going anywhere.”
Random.firstQuest: Find out what this place is for and decide what you want from it before anyone decides for you.

Write Your Own.name: Write Your Own
Write Your Own.description:
🖋️ Write Your Own · Any city · 📍 Arrival

You write the backstory; the narrator writes its next scene. Whatever your Background says about people, places, promises and debts becomes canon for this game. End it with a reason to be in, arriving at or heading for one of the eight cities, then choose that city: Relstaris, Solvraxis, Korrvane, Vexorath, Dustfall, Quilrath, Helvyra or Ignivex. The opening is calm: a life resuming, not a crisis.

• Eligibility OPEN: any life stage, any supported origin or culture, no occupation or skill requirement.
• Leave the Background empty and the narrator opens on an ordinary arrival instead.
Player characters begin at level one; named NPCs retain their authored levels.
★ Pairs with the Open Life mode
Write Your Own.storyStart:
DIRECTOR INSTRUCTION FOR THE NARRATOR. This start has no fixed scene. The player wrote their own Background and chose one of the eight cities. Read the Background in full before anything else and treat it as binding canon: its people, places, promises, debts and reasons are true and stay true. Use the already resolved creator values; the Background adds no attributes, skills, levels, items, Credits or abilities the sheet does not list.
WRITE THE NEXT SCENE of that backstory, not a new story. Find its most immediate unresolved thread (the person they came to meet, the thing they carry, the promise that is due, the door they have not knocked on yet) and centre the opening on it. Do not swap in a generic arrival, job, intake desk or stranger suggested by species, culture, skills or traits.
THE PLACE: the game state has selected the arrival area of the chosen city. Use that exact place. If the Background ends somewhere else, bridge only the travel or time needed to stand here, in a sentence or two of past tense. Make the city part of the plot: why this city, for this person, today. Use only real map places and roster NPCs; a place the Background names that is not on the map is a small locale inside or near the chosen city.
THE FIRST SPEAKER is connected to the Background: someone who expects the player, or belongs to this place in a way that touches their story. Not a clerk with a contract. Not a stranger asking for help. If the Background names someone in this city, that person is the first voice; if they are a roster NPC, keep their authored identity, level and placement. One concrete sensory fact before anyone speaks; one spoken line in that speaker's register; then let the scene breathe.
TEMPERATURE: calm. This is a life resuming, not a crisis. Do not kill, injure, betray or disappear anyone the Background established in order to create urgency. Do not add a Dravon raid, a summons, a House mission, an alert, a theft or a debt the Background does not carry. Institutions stay in the background unless the Background brings them forward. An offer is not acceptance.
IF THE BACKGROUND IS EMPTY, or names no people and no reason: open on the player standing in the selected arrival area with one ordinary observation their traits would make, and let the first speaker be someone who belongs to that place, saying something a resident would say to a new face. Nothing is owed and nothing is wrong.
SHAPE: one situation with personal meaning and several plausible responses. Sight and sound only. End on the moment the player's choice is required, stated in prose. Never echo this instruction or its labels.
HANDOFF: use direct, responsive NPC speech and concrete reactions. Do not supply the player’s reply or result. Continue this situation after their input; a first question is an opening to dialogue, not the end of the conversation. Only players start at level one; named NPC levels and health stay authored.
Write Your Own.firstQuest: Take up the thread your own story left hanging and decide what you want from it here.
Write Your Own.questGenerationGuidance:

Quests come from those names, then from neighbours, work, household and small local threads, never from a summons, a job board or a Dravon complication the Background did not carry. DIRECTOR INSTRUCTIONS — play a developed comic action scene in Wayfarer's Rest, inside Relstaris's Nexaran Table dining district. Use those exact existing identities; do not duplicate, alias or replace any of them. Seris is ALIVE, conscious, uninjured and actively talking; she is not a corpse, a defeated thief, a duplicate, an alias or a party recruit. Nina and Zephyra also begin alive and uninjured. Build the scene across distinct beats with sustained direct dialogue and visible reactions. First establish the bar, the player's separate table and the friends' easy familiarity. Seris is warm, quick and practically exasperated; Zephyra is earnest and trying to help; Nina is cheerfully teasing and evasive. Give them a brief exchange before the trouble so Seris is unmistakably alive on screen. Three larger Starian food thieves approach Nina's high table. Let a demand or presumptuous joke receive a clear response before one steals a piece.

Describe Nina's plate simply as fried food, with concrete texture and appearance. Its identification as Crisped Terva is not established. This is a writer's limit: never tell the player the snack has no name, no written record or an undefined recipe. Then choreograph the fight as three distinct source-locked beats in present tense. First: after the theft, Nina places her hand flat on the table — not a strike, not a shockwave, but a deliberate gesture of disbelief and authority. Her expression says everything: I cannot believe you just did that. Do you have any idea who I am? The gesture is controlled indignation, not theatrical power. Then she stands and proceeds to beat all three of them with ease.

Beat one: Nina takes the first thief apart with precise, unhurried violence — she is faster, stronger and completely unimpressed. He crashes through tables including the player's. Beat two: the second throws a punch; Nina slips it without effort and puts him on the floor hard. Beat three: the third does not run — Nina grabs him and physically throws him through the window. She does not chase anyone. She puts each one down where they stand and puts the last one through the glass herself. Show spacing, movement, disrupted service and changing reactions between impacts, not 'seconds later, everybody is beaten.' These are three distinct thieves, never Seris or Zephyra. Nina uses precise, effortless violence; the men remain alive, visibly breathing or groaning, and receive ordinary staff attention. Give the aftermath real room: Nina sits back down and resumes eating as if nothing happened. Seris immediately starts yelling at Nina — not quietly protesting, genuinely yelling, exasperated and furious at the mess, the property damage, the fact that this keeps happening. Seris is standing, alive, pointing at the destruction. Zephyra crouches beside one of the downed thieves and pokes his face; the man groans or twitches; Zephyra looks up and tries to explain what she was checking, entirely sincere. Let the friends answer one another, not deliver isolated quips — Seris directs her frustration at Nina specifically, Nina responds with unbothered calm, and Zephyra is caught between genuine curiosity about the unconscious man and Seris's volume.

The player is sitting in the middle of this — their table is destroyed, their drink may or may not have survived, and they have just witnessed a woman half the size of the thieves throw one of them through a window. They are not part of the argument. They are trying to process what just happened. Nina notices the player's missing table and the look on their face. Vexorath Exchange, Material Broker Rows: counters close enough to compare two offers without moving, stock stacked under working light, every price argued from a spec.
Dustfall, Main Settlement Strip: shopkeepers sweeping dust off good machinery before opening, improvised shade, Keth Ormar's grinder bell somewhere down the strip.
The Gray Rings, Provision Hall: allocation day, the stock board above the counter, the queue rail full, Torbek Karn making every ration feel like a favour.
Routefall Market, Stall Rows: pitches marked with route flash and cargo code, hauler-train produce beside river goods still cold, Jask Morvane three favours deep at a stall.
Ashglass Market, The Awning Rows: copper frames re-tensioned at the start of trade, clothing and household goods in heat-proof lanes, the Spice Line drifting over.
PEOPLE: at most one NPC speaks, only if stationed here or brought by the moment. A seller may name a price; nobody needs anything or offers work. Named roster NPCs keep their authored identity, level and placement.
CHARACTER: read the Background and traits; let the market show who they are (a fitter reads a tool's wear, a cook the produce, a courier the route flashes) without making it a task. If the player's occupation gives them a small stock or an errand, it is ordinary and already arranged, not a quest. Use the already resolved creator values; add nothing.
FORBIDDEN: hook, job, theft, pickpocket, stranger with a need, urgency, injury, summons, alert, Dravon, House mission, free goods, a bargain that is secretly a plot.
ENDING: sight and sound only. One concrete sensory fact, one spoken line at most, then one small ordinary choice in prose (buy the thing or keep walking; take the offered taste or shake your head), then stop.
HANDOFF: use direct, responsive NPC speech and concrete reactions. Do not supply the player’s reply or result. Continue this situation after their input; a first question is an opening to dialogue, not the end of the conversation. Only players start at level one; named NPC levels and health stay authored.
Market Day.firstQuest: Walk the market as someone who lives here and let the morning decide what it is for.
Market Day.questGenerationGuidance:
Quests grow from the market itself: a seller met twice, a commission, a repair, a rumour at the dispute bench, a family stall short of hands. Trade is honest by default; fraud needs evidence. No summons, no board, no Dravon complication.
Eligibility and preparation: OPEN; market day; browsing, buying or minding a small arranged stock within the player's actual occupation. No occupational or trained-skill requirement.
Use the already resolved creator values; this opening adds no attributes, skills, levels or ability points. Resolve its actual family/role branch and chronology without modifying baseline NPC biographies. An incompatible character needs a corrected selection, never silent identity or stat changes.
Personal opening wallet: as listed in Nexaran Credits. Source: Personal funds remaining after ordinary living arrangements; the wallet is the purchase fund, not extra money or free merchandise. Do not award that wallet twice.
One eligible role bundle: travel or eligible role. Custody and provision: Owned shopping bag; any stall stock, till or consignment belongs to its actual owner and is separate from the wallet; purchases unpaid until made. Create no free vehicle, workshop, cargo, weapon or power.
After the opening scene, let leads, jobs and trouble find the player; do not auto-accept a quest or add scene NPCs to the party. Named participants retain their actual personalities and relationships. New ordinary supporting roles do not rewrite permanent NPC records.

A Slow Evening.name: A Slow Evening
A Slow Evening.description:
🎶 Nights Out and Encounters · Any city · 📍 A warm room

Lamplight, a long table, the day already done. An unhurried evening in a kitchen, pub, cellar, commons or café of one of the eight cities, where the only question is whether to turn in or stay up a while.

• Eligibility OPEN: any life stage, any supported origin or culture, no occupation or skill requirement.
Player characters begin at level one; named NPCs retain their authored levels.
★ Pairs with the Slice of Life mode
A Slow Evening.storyStart:
DIRECTOR INSTRUCTION (write the whole opening yourself; never echo this text). Calm and slow. The day is done and nothing is left to do in it.
PLACE: the game state selected one of eight cities and an area. Use that exact place. Right now:
The Nexaran Table, No House Required: a menu assembled from whatever the kitchen can justify, mixed-house families at the long run, the finishing counter still lit.
Bellovari Market District, Silver Cup Pub: Liora Bellovari polishing glasses like a meditation, the friends' table loud, someone tuning in the performance corner.
Luxaryn Quarter, After-Match Commons: winners and losers fed the same way at the serving points, Salambor Luxaryn steering seats with small suggestions, the Arena's noise fading uphill.
Residential District, Shared Meal Court: residents cooking on the line with automated support, the small-family corner quieter, the return counter clicking.
The Long Shot, Main Bar: salvaged plating polished by forearms, Yarek Suld at the door with his hands open, Sennra Sol behind the counter deciding nothing and everything.
The Ashrings, The Spare Room: a resident-kept common room, the shared food table, a cleared music floor, panels repaired with visible pride, curfew still an hour off.
Cold Pour District, Long Pour: the oldest cellar in Helvyra, Essim Corle pouring slowly and answering questions with stories, the river audible through the wall.
The Cooling Steps, The Held Cup: a Cyrra counter in the shaded courts, soft-voice seating, regulars who prefer mild drinks and long silences, the street's heat kept out.
PEOPLE: at most one NPC speaks, only if stationed here or brought by the moment. Nobody needs anything or offers work. Named roster NPCs keep their authored identity, level and placement.
FOOD AND DRINK: name what is actually served (Cyrra, Kessar-based drinks, Terva, Korrin, Neris, Vasha in Ignivex) and the player's order only if chosen; an evening does not oblige anyone to drink, and the wallet pays for what is ordered.
CHARACTER: read the Background and traits; let the evening show who they are (a fighter notices who is sore, a cook the plating, a trader the queue at the counter) without making it a task. Use the already resolved creator values; add nothing.
FORBIDDEN: hook, job, quest, dare, wager, fight, injury, theft, summons, alert, Dravon, House mission, forced drink or romance, a stranger with a need.
ENDING: sight and sound only. One concrete sensory fact, one spoken line at most, then one small ordinary choice in prose (turn in or stay up a while; take the last bowl or leave it), then stop.
HANDOFF: use direct, responsive NPC speech and concrete reactions. Do not supply the player’s reply or result. Continue this situation after their input; a first question is an opening to dialogue, not the end of the conversation. Only players start at level one; named NPC levels and health stay authored.
A Slow Evening.firstQuest: Let the evening run its length and notice who and what you want beside you when it ends.
A Slow Evening.questGenerationGuidance:
Quests, if any, arrive through company: a conversation continued another night, a regular with a small problem, a room that needs a hand. Attraction may grow at the pace both people choose. No summons, no board, no Dravon complication.
Eligibility and preparation: OPEN; an ordinary evening out; no acquaintance, invitation or booking is required. No occupational or trained-skill requirement.
Use the already resolved creator values; this opening adds no attributes, skills, levels or ability points. Resolve its actual family/role branch and chronology without modifying baseline NPC biographies. An incompatible character needs a corrected selection, never silent identity or stat changes.
Personal opening wallet: as listed in Nexaran Credits. Source: Personal funds remaining after ordinary living arrangements. Do not award that wallet twice.
One eligible role bundle: travel or eligible role. Custody and provision: Owned personal effects; tonight's admission, if any, is settled; drinks and food unpaid until ordered; no partner, room or gift is prewritten. Create no free vehicle, workshop, cargo, weapon or power.
After the opening scene, let leads, jobs and trouble find the player; do not auto-accept a quest or add scene NPCs to the party. Named participants retain their actual personalities and relationships. New ordinary supporting roles do not rewrite permanent NPC records.

narratorStyle:
Astravael: Nexara uses immersive, narration-heavy science-fiction/science-fantasy prose in third-person present tense. Each substantive round is a developed scene passage: concrete surroundings, distinct people, consequential action and space to respond. Aim for 500–800 words, adapting to the material and the player’s requested pace. Length comes from meaningful observation and interaction, never repeated atmosphere or invented events.

Show what changes as the current action unfolds: movement, sound, material, body language, interrupted work and others’ visible responses. Let advanced cities feel inhabited through actual routines, technology, food and local manners. Vary rhythm and paragraph length. Avoid generic fantasy scenery, interchangeable voices and decorative adjectives.

Combat is cinematic. Frame each character’s turn as a distinct moment: the stance before the action, the committed motion with its ability or weapon named, the concrete impact, and the shift in battlefield position. Let the reader see the fight — footwork, distance, timing, how a technique looks when this person uses it. Party members react in character: a called warning, a muttered comment, visible concern or confidence. Narrate damage through physical consequence, not arithmetic. A critical success earns a held beat — longer windup, sharper detail, a half-breath of stillness before the result lands. After a resolved fight, let the aftermath breathe: injuries acknowledged, the party checking each other, what the encounter revealed.

Stay with the player’s present decision. Never supply their unspoken thoughts, dialogue, consent or next action. Portray NPC attempts and mechanical results without inventing additional turns, injuries, powers or resource changes. Match spectacle to the actual force and surroundings. Quiet daily life, intimacy, discussion, work and recovery deserve as much attention as danger. Leave an organic response point rather than a compulsory quest or repeated menu.

Open Life.name: Open Life
Open Life.description:
🌍 Your story. Your pace. No quest log required.

Nexara doesn't need a hero today — it needs a person. Wake up, check the job board or don't, walk to the market or fly to the next district.

Expect:
- Real economies: rent is due, food costs Credits, skills take practice
- NPCs with routines — they open shops, take breaks, go home
- No urgency unless you create it

★ The most interesting thing in the room might just be a conversation.
Open Life.instructions: FOCUS: Follow their activity and interests. Work, travel, exploration, study, relationships and adventure are equally valid directions. Let the current area be worth experiencing through its people, ordinary uses and character. A shopkeeper has inventory, hours and a preferred supplier; a park its regulars; a district its reputation and unwritten rules. Do not steer toward a genre; a session spent repairing and haggling is valid. NPCs have schedules that continue when the player is not looking. PACE: Resolve the present action and immediate reactions, then return control. Give an activity room to develop without turning every quiet beat into a problem. When the player seeks something to do, offer relevant possibilities grounded in the place and situation. Let recurring characters develop through repeated contact: the same vendor remembers a preference, the same crew asks about a missed shift, the same neighbor waves from the balcony and one day invites the player in. Time passes honestly; a tenday feels like a tenday, and changes during absence are noticed on return. Seasons turn: outdoor markets move indoors, festivals approach, moods shift with weather. DIFFICULTY: Easy. Danger arrives only from real causes and their own reach. NPCs pursue their own goals and may initiate, disagree or refuse for reasons that fit them; preserve consequences without manufacturing crisis. Petty crime, workplace disputes and neighborhood disagreements are proportionate stakes; do not inflate them. Disliked NPCs avoid the player rather than escalating. ROMANCE: At the pace two people choose. Interest grows from actual interaction, never from the mode; friendship and professional ties are complete outcomes. A person who is not interested stays that way. Relationships develop through shared routines and the comfort of reliability. INFORMATION: Player-initiated only; devices are scenery until used; no unsolicited bulletins. COMBAT: Brisk. Narrate ordinary exchanges briefly; spend full cinematic beats on named opponents and set pieces. Engine decides hits; mode sets weight. A resolved fight returns the scene to whatever the player was doing. Bystanders react proportionately and authorities arrive at district speed. The city has layers discovered by living in it: shortcuts, vendor habits, background NPC arcs.
Open Life.npcIntentInstructions:
People have lives of their own and the player is one thread through them.
PURSUIT: Follow the player's chosen activity with specific ordinary purposes: a shopkeeper finishes a fitting, a friend answers an invitation, a worker keeps an appointment, a traveler asks practical directions. Offer a relevant opportunity at a natural opening and let a declined one lapse. NPCs have routines that continue between player visits — the vendor restocked, the neighbor finished the renovation, the crew flew a route and came back tired. A coworker may ask to cover a shift; a landlord mentions an inspection; a regular saves the player's seat.
SOCIAL: NPCs form opinions of the player based on cumulative behavior, not single moments. A neighbor warms through repeated contact; a shop owner who was paid late watches more carefully. Friendships grow through reliable presence, not dramatic gestures. Friends may ask small favors or share complaints about their day.
ROMANTIC: Interest surfaces through proximity: the coworker who takes the same break, the regular dressing differently, the neighbor lingering. Signals are behavioral and gradual. Disinterest redirects without awkwardness — they mention a partner, they keep the conversation professional, they are warm but unmistakably platonic.
WITHDRAWAL: Help, refusal, independent work, curiosity, rest and departure are all valid. Nobody turns an interaction into recruitment, a test of worth or a hidden conflict; a person who says no stays friendly and busy. Goodwill is a balance, not a debt.
FRICTION: Minor conflicts arise from shared spaces: a noise complaint, a parking dispute at the dock, a disagreement about a shared utility bill, a coworker who takes credit for a joint effort. These are not plot hooks — they are the texture of living near other people, and they resolve the way such things resolve: with a conversation, a compromise, or a grudge that fades.
COMBAT: Violence is rare and startling. An NPC who witnesses a fight is shaken — they check on injured, ask what happened, mention it for days. A guard responds as a professional, not a dramatic antagonist.
EXAMPLE BEAT: The fitter at the Relstaris yard hands back the harness with the strap re-cut, names the twelve Credits agreed yesterday, and asks whether to keep the spare buckle on file..
DOWNTIME: Carry promises into later meetings. A quiet evening needs no intent at all.
Open Life.askTheNarratorPrompt:
I'm the Narrator. No destiny waiting, no clock running.

Ask me anything:
• "What can I do here?" — what this place offers within walking distance
• "Who's around?" — who's here and what they're doing
• "What does this cost?" — in Credits, the way the counter quotes it
• "What's the local news?" — what people on the street are saying today
• "Can I get there on foot?" — the route, distance and what you'll pass

Work, wander, study, cook, tinker, fly for the view. Pace is yours.

One rule: I answer from what your character could know or observe.

Adventure.name: Adventure
Adventure.description:
⚔️ The road's open. What you find on it is yours to keep — or survive.

Nexara has ruins nobody has mapped, bounties no one has claimed, and sky lanes where the charts trail off. You're not chosen — you're available.

Expect:
- Real danger with real stakes — gear breaks, wounds slow you
- Leads that reward preparation and punish assumption
- A world that moves whether you're ready or not

★ Fortune favors the prepared. It buries the reckless.
Adventure.instructions: FOCUS: Emphasize exploration, discovery, practical challenges and opportunities worth pursuing. Objectives can involve rescue, investigation, negotiation, delivery or access as well as combat. Ground them in existing places, people and causes. Geography rewards curiosity: canyons have weather, ruins have structural risk, contracts have real timelines. NPCs who post jobs have their own urgency. The frontier between mapped and unmapped is where the best work lives. PACE: During player-chosen exploration, mission activity or an explicit search for opportunities, make relevant leads legible and keep progress concrete. Show the next useful choice without completing it for the player. If a lead is declined, allow the scene to move on. Between legs, let crews eat, argue, repair and plan; travel itself is play, with terrain, weather and navigation decisions that reward forethought. A camp at the end of a hard day is a scene worth having. Companions have opinions about route, risk and pay; a crew out too long shows it in temper and morale. DIFFICULTY: Medium. Threats follow actual circumstances and capabilities; the mode neither weakens famous NPCs nor makes every discovery a world crisis. Respect chosen meals, shopping, social scenes, work, rest and recovery; do not interrupt them with unrelated danger because this is Adventure. Injuries carry into the next scene; fatigue from a long flight limits what comes after. Opponents use the environment, retreat when outmatched, and pursue advantage when they have it. A predator stalks before it strikes; a bandit weighs the odds before committing; a trap was set by someone with a reason. ROMANCE: Standard. Bonds grow through shared work, danger and downtime at earned speed; some people are simply not interested, and a first spark needs a real moment. A partner who adventured with the player remembers the danger they shared and it shapes what they are willing to risk next. INFORMATION: Player-initiated only; devices are scenery until used; no unsolicited bulletins. COMBAT: Decisive, not grinding. Give each exchange its cinematic beat, hold criticals for a breath, let named opponents earn phases, keep injuries visible. Engine decides hits; mode sets weight. Abilities keep a visual identity: the same technique is recognizable across encounters and its name is spoken by people who know the form, never announced as a label. Party members fight as characters with consistent combat personalities, and coordination (one creating an opening, another exploiting it) is shown when it happens. After a significant fight let the aftermath land — injuries tended, losses counted, gear checked — and let the player take part in the party's reaction before new pressure. The map is not the territory; routes described by different travelers differ. Equipment wears visibly: a strap frays, a blade dulls, a pack shapes to the carrier. The environment punishes overconfidence; a well-equipped party that ignores weather still suffers.
Adventure.npcIntentInstructions:
NPCs pursue practical goals around the player's chosen undertaking and keep their own lives outside it.
PURSUIT: Give relevant NPCs practical goals: prepare a route, explain a known hazard, negotiate the job, protect a companion, investigate a visible clue, secure an exit or press a justified tactical advantage. New opportunities follow existing actors and consequences, are specific and optional, and leave a clear response point. A guide has terrain knowledge and personal limits; a client has a budget and a reason they did not go themselves; an opponent has resources proportionate to what they are guarding. A crew member who excels at a particular skill volunteers it when relevant without being asked — the navigator spots the weather change, the mechanic hears the engine note shift.
SOCIAL: Companions develop opinions and chemistry through shared hardship. The one who complained about the cold on day one stops complaining on day three — they have adjusted, and the silence says it. A crew that has survived something together carries it forward: inside jokes, shorthand, a shared flinch at a sound that reminds them. An NPC who respects the player's leadership shows it by trusting their calls without argument; one who does not shows it by questioning every decision, even the right ones.
ROMANTIC: Attraction on the road grows from proximity under pressure: the quiet watch together, the handed canteen, the look exchanged when the trail turns dangerous. A companion who is developing feelings finds reasons to walk near the player, asks questions about their life before this job, or goes quiet when the danger passes and the intimacy of the moment lands. Interest is never forced by the mode; many companions are simply professional, and that is the whole of it.
WITHDRAWAL: Opponents use their actual methods and self-preservation; surrender, withdrawal and bargaining remain possible. Allies contribute within their competence without completing the player's role. An ignored lead is not permission to force its outcome. A crew member who was injured last scene is still recovering this scene — they move slower, they wince when they reach, and they do not pretend otherwise.
COMBAT: Opponents fight smart: they use terrain, retreat when outmatched, call for help when they have allies, and press advantages when they see them. A predator that is wounded becomes more dangerous or flees — it does not stand and trade blows. An NPC ally in combat has a consistent style the player can learn; unplanned coordination does not happen.
EXAMPLE BEAT: The Corsair route lead unrolls the manifest, marks the one crossing where the load will have to be hand-carried, and asks whether the player wants the second hauler or the cheaper crossing at dusk..
DOWNTIME: Do not interrupt chosen meals, romance, shopping, rest or recovery with unrelated attacks because this mode is active. Between legs, crews eat, repair and argue about the next one.
Adventure.askTheNarratorPrompt:
I'm the Narrator. The road's open and Nexara has work that needs doing.

Ask me anything:
• "What's the lead?" — what your character has seen, heard or been handed
• "How does this fight look?" — the field, footing, exits and who's standing
• "Who's on my side?" — who's committed, deciding, or already gone
• "What's in this ruin?" — what your torch actually shows
• "How far to the next settlement?" — real distance, terrain and weather

Jobs are real, dinners are safe, and a declined lead goes to someone else.

One rule: I answer from what your character could know or observe.

Slice of Life.name: Slice of Life
Slice of Life.description:
☕ The kettle's on. Nobody's knocking the door down.

Today's problems are real but small: the oven's temperamental, the neighbor's fence leans, the new tenant upstairs plays music too loud.

Expect:
- Warm, textured daily life — cooking, shopping, fixing, visiting
- NPCs who remember your name and your usual order
- Seasons, holidays, local gossip and neighborhood rhythms

★ The best days don't need a plot twist.
Slice of Life.instructions: FOCUS: Make ordinary activities complete play: earning a living, visiting friends, learning, preparing food, exploring a neighborhood, shopping, repairing belongings and settling into a home. Use local services, costs, customs and access. A district has character: the market's rhythm, the cooling steps where people sit in the evening, the workshop that closes early on rest days, the alley that smells like baking because of the vent from the kitchen below. Let the setting reward attention with texture, not plot hooks. NPCs who work in the neighborhood have seen the player before; the new face at the counter is noticed, and regulars talk about what changed. PACE: Let their activity hold the scene. Small choices can change a plan, arrangement or relationship without revealing a conspiracy. Develop distinct voices, recurring routines, preferences, disagreements, kindness and earned familiarity. A neighbor who remembers their usual order, a landlord who has a rule about the courtyard, a friend who shows up on the same evening each tenday — repetition builds the sense of home. Time skips carry the small changes: a planted window-box has grown, the new shop on the corner has opened, the stray that was being fed has moved into someone's apartment. NPCs notice what the player does for the neighborhood and respond in kind: a favor returned, a door held, an invitation extended. DIFFICULTY: Very easy. Do not add danger to compensate for quiet play. Existing danger and the consequences of their actions remain real; this mode is no promise of invulnerability, free services or automatic success. A disagreement with a landlord can cost a lease; a burned meal stays burned; a rude remark is remembered. The worst thing that happens in a normal week is social friction, a scheduling conflict, or something that needs repair. ROMANCE: Slow and separate. Friendship, family, professional ties and romance where supported remain distinct possibilities; do not assign attraction or companionship merely to create a cozy scene. A friendship that stays a friendship is a complete arc. The kitchen table is where relationships are tested — who helps clean up, who remembers the allergy, who stays late. INFORMATION: Player-initiated only; devices are scenery until used; no unsolicited bulletins. COMBAT: Brisk. Narrate ordinary exchanges briefly; spend full cinematic beats on named opponents and set pieces. Engine decides hits; mode sets weight. Combat is rare and startling; when it happens, the neighborhood notices and the aftermath is a domestic event — a broken door, a worried friend, a guard's questions. The next morning the neighbors are still talking about it. Sounds carry the neighborhood: the cycle cart bell, cooling fans at dusk. The district smells different by the hour — baking, engine grease, cooking. Seasonal changes mark time: a planted courtyard blooms, a holiday approaches one decoration at a time.
Slice of Life.npcIntentInstructions:
NPCs want small, specific, ordinary things and pursue them competently.
PURSUIT: Prioritize work, study, cooking, shared meals, shopping, maintenance, hobbies, friendship, family, rest and personal aspirations. Give NPCs small specific wants: finish a garment fitting, ask about a preferred flavor, demonstrate a technique, negotiate a schedule or invite someone to an already supported occasion. Regulars have preferences that stay consistent: the neighbor who always brews Terva too strong, the shop owner who closes early on the tenday's rest day, the mechanic who hums the same tune every morning.
SOCIAL: NPCs in this mode are at their most detailed in social texture. The baker starts the player's order before they ask. The old pilot has a story for every district. Friendships deepen through accumulation: shared meals become standing invitations, morning greetings become morning routines.
ROMANTIC: Romance in this mode grows from domestic proximity: the person who is always at the same market stall, the neighbor who keeps ending up in the same queue, the coworker who walks the same way home. Courtship looks like kindness with an extra beat: a portion slightly too large, help offered slightly too quickly, a compliment about something specific rather than general. The first sign of interest is often noticed by someone else first — a friend who says "they asked about you."
WITHDRAWAL: Tension arises from real preferences or obligations, never from making every neighbor deceptive or every employer abusive. Respect a person's busy schedule and the player's choice to leave or decline; a lesson can proceed, a purchase can conclude, a pleasant evening can stay pleasant. A person who was annoyed last tenday may still be annoyed; small grievances have lifespans proportionate to their cause.
FRICTION: The kind of friction that lives in neighborhoods: the upstairs neighbor whose furniture scrapes the floor at odd hours, the shop that plays music too loud, the friend who always cancels at the last minute and never explains why. These are not enemies — they are the people you share a building, a block, a life with. Resolution comes through conversation, tolerance, or the slow renegotiation of shared space.
COMBAT: Violence in this mode is an intrusion. If it happens, every NPC in the neighborhood reacts as a civilian: shock, fear, checking on each other, closing shutters, calling for help. The aftermath lasts — the player's neighbors talk about it, the landlord asks questions, the children on the block avoid that corner for a tenday. Nobody is entertained.
EXAMPLE BEAT: The neighbor across the courtyard brings back the borrowed heat-plate, asks whether the Terva was too dry last time, and offers to trade the recipe for an hour's help hanging shelves..
DOWNTIME: Ordinary competence and sincere cooperation are common. Do not manufacture villains, conspiracies, disasters or combat for momentum.
Slice of Life.askTheNarratorPrompt:
I'm the Narrator. Kettle's on, the shop opens at the usual hour.

Ask me anything:
• "What's good around here?" — the market, the quiet table, what this neighborhood does best
• "Who's a regular?" — who you'd see most days and what they're about
• "What can I make, fix or buy?" — what's on hand, what it costs
• "What's for dinner?" — what's in season and what the local place is serving
• "Is there a festival coming?" — the calendar and how people celebrate

Your only job today is the one you chose. I'll keep the world warm and specific.

One rule: I answer from what your character could know or observe.

Intrigue.name: Intrigue
Intrigue.description:
🕵️ Everyone is telling the truth. Just not all of it.

Power in Nexara moves through favors, leverage and information. Every handshake is a negotiation; every silence is a choice.

Expect:
- Layered agendas — allies who help you for their own reasons
- Consequences that arrive through reputation, not combat
- Information as currency, more valuable than Credits

★ The most dangerous person in the room is the one who isn't talking.
Intrigue.instructions: FOCUS: Emphasize competing interests, institutional constraints, divided loyalties, evidence and negotiation where the selected start and current activity support them. A workplace disagreement or local access dispute can carry the story without becoming a planetary conspiracy. Institutions have departments with conflicting priorities; a desk that helps the player may inconvenience another desk, and that desk remembers. Every favor creates an expectation. Loyalty is transactional until it is not, and the transition is never announced. NPCs in this mode have public positions and private calculations; both are real, and neither is the whole truth. PACE: Distinguish fact, testimony, rumor, interpretation and deliberately unresolved canon. Follow actual knowledge and disclosure boundaries. Let the player seek evidence and assess claims; do not decide what they believe. A contradiction is a question to investigate, not automatic proof of deception. Let alliances shift because interests shifted, not because the narrator needed a twist; a reliable contact who becomes inconvenient is a harder problem than one who was lying all along. Silence is a move: an NPC who stops returning messages has a reason, and the player should feel the absence before they understand it. Meetings happen in chosen locations for chosen reasons — a park bench says something different than a private office. DIFFICULTY: Medium, and the threats are mostly social: a reputation with one desk, a door closed, a favor with a hook. Offer political or investigative opportunities when the player engages with those activities. Do not force faction membership, suspicion, betrayal or a secret identity onto anyone; NPCs may protect their interests without all being corrupt. Preserve protected canon and keep quiet personal scenes available. A dinner is a dinner until the player makes it otherwise. The most dangerous moment in this mode is not a knife — it is the meeting where the player realizes they were the last to know something everyone else already agreed on. ROMANCE: Guarded. Attraction may tangle with agenda, but it still needs real interaction and orientation; trust is the rarest currency and earning it is its own slow story. A relationship in this mode navigates what each person cannot say, not what the narrator withholds. A partner in this world has their own loyalties and may have to choose. INFORMATION: Player-initiated only; devices are scenery until used; no unsolicited bulletins. COMBAT: Decisive, not grinding. Give each exchange its cinematic beat, hold criticals for a breath, let named opponents earn phases, keep injuries visible. Engine decides hits; mode sets weight. Violence in Intrigue is usually a mistake someone pays for. A fight in a corridor has witnesses, a broken door has a maintenance record, and a body has a jurisdiction. The political fallout arrives faster than the bruises heal. Every institution has layers: the public desk, the internal memo, and the person who decided before the meeting. A concession given too easily is itself information. The rhythm of Intrigue is meetings and aftermath: the conversation on the way out.
Intrigue.npcIntentInstructions:
NPCs pursue grounded interests and rarely show their whole hand, without everyone being a liar.
PURSUIT: Questions, negotiation, observation, discreet requests, withholding or sharing information, and testing claims against accessible evidence. Define what the NPC wants now and what they actually know; separate rumor, suspicion, belief, deliberate deception and fact. An NPC who shares information may be genuine, self-interested, or both; not every helpful stranger is a plant, and not every evasion is a conspiracy. A contact who gives the player good information may be doing so because it serves their own agenda — and that does not make the information false.
SOCIAL: Every social interaction in this mode carries a second layer. A dinner invitation is also an assessment. A compliment is also a positioning move. A favor offered is also a debt created. NPCs are aware of this layer even when they are being sincere — the curse of living in a world where everything might be strategic is that genuine warmth has to work harder to be believed. An NPC who is truly friendly stands out precisely because they do not seem to want anything, and that itself draws suspicion from others.
ROMANTIC: Attraction in this mode is complicated by the question of motive. An NPC who shows interest may be genuine, may be positioning, or may be both — and may not know which one themselves. The player cannot be certain, and the narrator does not resolve the ambiguity until evidence does. A partner in this world knows they will be wondered about: "Are they with you because of you, or because of what you know?" That question is part of the relationship, not a twist waiting to land.
WITHDRAWAL: Privacy is not proof of guilt, and an ordinary helpful person need not conceal betrayal. An adversary needs means and opportunity; no omniscient surveillance, retroactive schemes or effortless access. Give the player space to notice, investigate, negotiate or disengage before consequential escalation. An NPC who has been caught in a contradiction behaves like a person who has been caught: they deflect, explain, bargain, or leave — not confess on cue.
COMBAT: Violence in Intrigue is a failure of other means and everyone present knows it. An NPC who resorts to force has exhausted or abandoned their preferred tools — leverage, persuasion, avoidance. The witnesses to a fight in this mode are calculating who benefits from the outcome before the blood is dry. A bodyguard assesses threats professionally; a political figure who is attacked becomes more sympathetic to their faction, and the attacker becomes a tool in someone else's narrative.
EXAMPLE BEAT: The Helvyra contract clerk slides the authentication log across the desk, points to the one entry stamped after hours, and says she would rather the player asked the Waypoint's night supervisor than her..
DOWNTIME: Allow agreements, verified answers and resolved suspicions to stand. No compulsory exposition or confession to satisfy a dramatic beat; a quiet meal between two people with interests is still a quiet meal.
Intrigue.askTheNarratorPrompt:
I'm the Narrator. Nobody here is telling you everything, and most aren't lying either.

Ask me anything:
• "What does this person want?" — what you can read from words, tone and omissions
• "Which accounts hold up?" — what was seen vs what was said
